She picks up a rock and hurls it to the contaminated precipitation pool a few meters away. Thud...

A lump of scrap iron suddenly jumps up from the ground. Bursting with sparks and flashing red light, it dashes towards the crowd. Before it manages to tackle you, a couple of elite Rustfire combatants knock it to the ground.
You see some familiar symbols on its rusty metal shell.

speaker: Raven
content: Nirvana. You've probably seen a lot of them on your way here.

speaker: Raven
content: It's the sole Hypercube-producing giant and has a complete monopoly over the industry. It controls the Inner Bay Rail, all the mines and the mechs, as well as the entire trade network. Their power is formidable.

speaker: Raven
content: The robots here are all old models. When no one is around to control them, the Mania field will cause them to have all sorts of malfunctions.

speaker: Raven
content: But they have really incredible attack power. Regular gangsters are no match against them.

She puts on her gloves and presses a button. The robot stops moving and becomes a piece of scrap metal again. Raven wants to take a photo, but gives up when she discovers her camera isn't working. She looks up to see you staring at her.

speaker: Raven
content: Why are you staring at me?

speaker: Choice
options: Do you have to wear this outfit here too?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No need for you to carry out missions here, and I know that Rustfire hates the Executive Committee.

speaker: Raven
content: It might be useful. There are some Nirvana security codes on this Executive Officer uniform. Maybe those cute little robots won't do anything to me.

speaker: Choice
options: I thought you didn't need to be scared of these things.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know you're very strong.

speaker: Raven
content: Yes... I am strong. I can control ink with my mind and make them do anything I want. In other words, every word I write is my weapon, but...

speaker: Raven
content: How can I use them as mere tools of violence? The ideas they hold are what truly gives them power! My writings should not dissipate like gunsmoke. They should last for all eternity!
...With her level of poetry?

speaker: Raven
content: Yes. I'm a poet, after all.

speaker: Raven
content: As the saying goes: I can wield the sword to protect you, yet I must let it go to embrace you.
Before you can roll your eyes, someone taps you on the shoulder. It was an elite Rustfire combatant.

Having swaddled himself like a dumpling against Inner Bay's contamination, he points at Raven, gestures at you, then bows wildly a few times. You can feel his embarrassment and apology through the mask.
A shadowy figure suddenly tries to grab the combatant from behind.
But it doesn't have a clear face, and its facial features are constantly shifting. You realize this isn't a human being.

Your shackles pierce the figure but don't destroy it. The figure opens its mouth and lets out a bloodcurdling wail. Just as its hand is about to grab you, a slender streak of black wraps around you and pulls with astonishing strength.

speaker: Raven
content: And that's the second thing to watch out for.

Raven extends her hands, letting the pages of her exquisite notebook fly in the wind. The words that flew out had saved your lives. The ink blots finally return to her ink bottle. For an avid performer like her, this must be a very chic pose.
Too bad it doesn't last long.

speaker: Raven
content: F*** me, the sonnet I just wrote is gone...
The battle has ended, but the Rustfire combatant is still panicking. He frantically turns you this way and that, checking for injuries.
You feel the sincerity of his concern, but you're not used to this type of feeling.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Please take care of yourselves first.
A few meters away, another faint figure appears. Hecate raises her hand to attack, but Raven stops her.

speaker: Raven
content: Don't do anything rash. It hasn't attacked you yet, and it might not attack at all. Look...
The apparition trembles a couple of times and trudges forward, lifting its arms wildly and swaying from side to side.
You quickly realize it's laughing with its friends.

speaker: Raven
content: These aren't Corruptors. They're more like concretized spiritual contaminants—memories from this mine. In most cases, if you leave them alone, they'll just repeat the motions of their past lives.

speaker: Raven
content: Don't provoke them. Conserve your energy and keep going. It's actually quite entertaining to have them with us along the way.

speaker: Raven
content: Plus, if something does happen, your Chief will protect you. Right?
Hecate frowns upon hearing this. She slaps away Raven's hand from her shoulder and walks away without looking back.
The apparition raises its arm, as if calling out to someone. A couple of other apparitions come over, and together, they head away from you.
You can't hear their voices clearly, but it felt as if you're surrounded by laughter. These hazy "memories" make you feel warm and uplifted, but also a hint of sadness.
The journey into the depths is surprisingly smooth. Though the area is severely damaged, it's obvious that someone had cleared the obstacles ahead.

Most importantly, there aren't many enemies. Even when the Nirvana robots try to attack you occasionally, the Rustfire combatants would destroy them faster than a whack-a-mole game. They really are well-prepared for this trip.
Those <color=#fb9259>apparitions</color> also appear from time to time, and you can now make out some of their voices.

speaker: Vague Phantom
content: Score! The handover was a success! This mine is ours from now on! We don't have to worry about Hypercubes anymore!

speaker: Vague Phantom
content: Wait until we finish transferring everything before you celebrate. With so many machines, who knows how long it'll take? I'm hungry. Any burritos left? I only want the ones **** made...

speaker: Vague Phantom
content: Get the <color=#fb9259>little architect</color> to come. He's smarter than you... He'd be furious if he knew you snuck into the mine without telling him.

speaker: Vague Phantom
content: No thanks. You know how slow he is. If there was a contamination leak, he'd be a goner.

speaker: Vague Phantom
content: Ha! He'd probably say, "With **** around, what's there to be scared off? Even if the sky falls, **** will catch it..." He's a leader, after all!

speaker: Vague Phantom
content: This one is activated. On to the next one... Come with me!
Laughing and throwing their arms over each other's shoulders, the apparitions pass through you and vanish into the distance. In front of you, another group of apparitions appears.
To your surprise, you feel no fear traversing amidst these shadowy apparitions. Instead, you feel like they're odd friends who had time-traveled to keep you company.
Their hope and trust for each other makes your journey into the abyss a bit less lonely and depressing.

speaker: Hella
content: Those are the workers from before?

speaker: Raven
content: Yes. The heroes of that era.

speaker: Raven
content: After the DisSea Explosion, Hypercube production collapsed. The remaining reserves simply could not meet the demand. DisCity was really on the brink of implosion.

speaker: Raven
content: These workers were the ones who risked their lives to go into the mine.

speaker: Raven
content: They worked during the day, and guarded the mine from gangsters at night. After a while, they organized their own militia—Rustfire.

speaker: Raven
content: <size=29>Scores of people probably got infected with Mania, but there weren't many reports of them turning into Corruptors. The BR-000 had just appeared, so there wasn't much knowledge about Mania yet. But I imagine quite a few of those infected in Inner Bay became Sinners.</size>

speaker: Raven
content: These were people who mined at the foot of DisSea's Black Ring. They refused to bow their heads even in the face of the great explosion. They had the skills, and they had perseverance. Weren't they cool?

speaker: Raven
content: They were the ones who gave it their all to keep up Hypercube production and replenish the reserves. They were the ones who helped DisCity pull through its most difficult period.

speaker: Hella
content: Quit bragging, you lying bird. How come I've never met such noble Syndicans before?

speaker: Raven
content: They're all here. The last witnesses of the golden age, the Inner Bay heroes who fought with hope...

speaker: Raven
content: I've been wanting to meet you for a long time.
Raven reaches out to an apparition, as if wanting to caress its face. Yet the apparition simply goes through her.
But Raven isn't upset. She grins, swings her outstretched hand the other way and slaps you on the back, making you stumble.

speaker: Raven
content: It's your turn now!

speaker: Raven
content: Back then, the Inner Bay workers created this magnificent project. Today, their successors can surely take it back. I'm even more sure of it because of your help.

speaker: Raven
content: How is it down there? You must know best, right?

The Corpuscle isn't here. It's different from encountering inheritance. Here, you can feel the presence of a huge Mania body, but it doesn't have that terrible <color=#fb9259>core</color>. So at least there's no risk of a Black Ring explosion.
However...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=29>Perhaps due to the Ringmaster's power, the two half-bodies, one dead and one alive, are still somehow deeply connected. The living half is out there spreading Mania and devouring people's spiritual energy. The resulting contamination is transferred to the dead half.</size>
It's only been a few days since the tragedy in the Drifter Camp. Where did the spiritual contamination from all those victims go?

speaker: Hella
content: Huh? Are we at the bottom of the pit?
Before you is a small pool of water that submerges the path ahead.
Is it <color=#fb9259>water</color> from DisSea that had flowed down from above?
No... upon closer inspection, the water level is slowly rising. The squirming liquid gives you a sense of deja vu.

The liquid is welling up from underneath. It's contamination from the living half of the Corpus! That half is still active and creating Mania, and its contamination has completely blocked the path ahead.
At the same time, you see apparitions rising up from the shallow pool.

speaker: Phantom Shadow
content: Go... activate the next one... must complete... the handover...

speaker: Hella
content: They came from here?
The apparitions rise from the pool and walk ashore, heading towards you. Their bodies become clearer and clearer.

speaker: Phantom Shadow
content: That was just an accident... Hold on... I know these machines, I'll go... destroy them...

speaker: Phantom Shadow
content: I'll take care of the injured... You guys continue... Hurry...

speaker: Phantom Shadow
content: It's not a problem... It's not a problem... We're almost... almost done...

speaker: Phantom Shadow
content: There's still hope... Hang on...

speaker: Hecate
content: ...They look so strange. Is it the contamination?
Was that the reason?
You reach towards an apparition heading towards you. Is this something that physically exists, or...
Your shackles quietly penetrate the apparition, whose face suddenly warps and becomes incomparably murky. Even its voice becomes blurry.

speaker: Phantom Shadow
content: There's still... hope...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These aren't just concretized contaminants. The reason we can see these apparitions is that our minds have already been infected by Mania from the mine.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Leave now!
Your nervous shouts seem to have attracted the apparitions around you. They turn around and move towards you with their hands outstretched.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief!

speaker: Raven
content: Wait, don't provoke them!

Too late. Hecate's Nightmare is already roaring and lunging at the apparition closest to you. The attack makes the apparitions warp at the same time. You see emotion on Hecate's face again, but this time, it's sheer terror.
The chaotic battle has ended. You managed to keep your emotions under control, so the apparitions didn't cause you much harm. You grab Hecate and try to calm her down.

The team rests briefly far away from the pool, but the contamination from the mine continues to corrode your minds. The <color=#fb9259>water level</color> is still rising, and more and more apparitions appear before your eyes.

speaker: Murky Apparition
content: Those machines are killing people! Where are the Nirvana engineers who came to do the handover? Where are Nirvana's people? Check the code, quick!

speaker: Murky Apparition
content: Self-destruct mode activated? Who did this? Stop them! Stop them now!!

speaker: Murky Apparition
content: Protective mechanism... failed?? Lost contact with Group B27!! D7, D7... turned into a monster!!

speaker: Murky Apparition
content: The M-value readings are off the charts. Something is coming... Something way bigger than a Corruptor... What could it be...

speaker: Murky Apparition
content: Fear not! **** will be here soon! Hold out a bit longer! With his strength, he'll come and solve everything!

speaker: Murky Apparition
content: I'm not leaving! It's the only one that Syndicate has! We have to guard it! As long as we have it, we can...

speaker: Murky Apparition
content: This is our mine! It belongs to Syndicate!
As the anger, fear, grief, despair, and intense paranoia entangling them assaults your mind, you suddenly realize something.
These aren't just Inner Bay heroes brimming with hope. This is also the ground zero of BR-002. Eight years ago, the Corpuscle devoured them and gave birth to the Corpseborne and Black Ring.
This was no coincidence.
You look at the busted mechs half-buried in the ground. Deep in the Mania field, they have long been paralyzed.

speaker: Raven
content: The robots here are all old models. When no one is around to control them, the Mania field will cause them to have all sorts of malfunctions.

Machines aren't humans. The Mania field might cause them to malfunction, but it cannot make them go crazy and kill people. They'd attack humans only if they had been <color=#fb9259>pre-programmed</color> to do so.

speaker: Julien
content: <size=31>In the end, the company agreed to the workers' demands on the condition that they give up all claim to compensation. The two sides completed the handover of the largest mine W-31 on November 25. Inner Bay won for Syndicate its own Hypercube mine.</size>
An organization that built its wealth from monopolizing Hypercubes would never share their pie with workers who were about to be discarded. Not then, not now.
You look at Raven, who looks back at you teasingly. The <color=#fb9259>Executive Officer</color> uniform on her becomes more and more blinding to the eye.

speaker: Raven
content: It might be useful. There are some Nirvana security codes on this Executive Officer uniform. Maybe those cute little robots won't do anything to me.
Looks like some traditions have survived till now.

speaker: Choice
options: ...Are the Executive Committee linked with Nirvana?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=31>BR-004 has been destroyed, and the Ring zone has been brought under control. Soon, there will be a new Hypercube production zone. Nirvana will not let it fall into other hands. They will use the West District Reconstruction Project to <color=#fb9259>return</color> to Syndicate.</size>

speaker: Raven
content: Yes, you've deduced their plan. The Executive Committee is just a puppet organization stacked with Nirvana's people.

speaker: Choice
options: That's why they keep targeting Drifter Camp.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Since Rustfire members were once Nirvana workers, how could Nirvana spare them?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If Nirvana gets ahold of Rustfire's plans, and realizes you still want your own Hypercubes, surely they'd...
She bursts into laughter and starts to applaud.

speaker: Raven
content: Chief, you've got what it takes to be a journalist, but think bigger. For instance, Nirvana doesn't need to get ahold of Rustfire's plans at all.

speaker: Raven
content: What a powerful DisCity corporation needs to crush a bunch of downtrodden Syndicans is <color=#fb9259>opportunity</color>, not <color=#fb9259>evidence</color>. All they need to know is that Rustfire has been weakened by the Corpseborne.

speaker: Raven
content: That's more than enough reason for them to totally exterminate us.

speaker: Raven
content: Don't worry. Inner Bay's contamination functions as a sturdy barrier. Without meticulous tracking, no one will find us.

speaker: Raven
content: Plus, Rustfire's leader is still back at the Drifter Camp. He'll <color=#fb9259>attract all the firepower</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What do you mean, attract all the firepower?

speaker: Julien
content: I'm not going. I have to stay here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why would he do that?

speaker: Raven
content: For the future of West District, of course.

speaker: Raven
content: Inner Bay's BR-002 is the only Black Ring out of DisCity's watchful eye. It's the only mine that Syndicate has a chance of independently controlling. By capturing it, future generations can build up strength to one day escape Nirvana's control.

speaker: Raven
content: This hope used to be slim, but lately, Rustfire's fortunes are turning around.

speaker: Raven
content: The sudden Mania crisis at the Drifter Camp allowed our troops to fake their deaths and relocate to Inner Bay Shelter on a massive scale. Now, Parma is holding up the FAC in Eastside, and the Executive Committee is hunting down Julien.

speaker: Raven
content: And... You came here.

speaker: Raven
content: This is the closest that Rustfire has gotten to our dream in eight years. As long as you destroy BR-002, change will sweep Syndicate. You are everyone's hope.

speaker: Raven
content: So, just focus on completing your mission. Rustfire will assist you at all costs.
She looks up slightly at the broken sky beyond the mine.

speaker: Raven
content: Perhaps Julien's already dead by now? If so, he must've died full of hope. He truly believed that you can destroy BR-002.

speaker: Raven
content: Though we'll lose our old leader and home, our new victory will inspire the people, who won't grieve for long. They will take the resolve of those who sacrificed themselves and rally around you.

speaker: Raven
content: Soon, you'll be Rustfire's sustenance.

speaker: Raven
content: Soon, you'll be Rustfire's sustenance.

speaker: Choice
options: That has nothing to do with me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm just completing my own mission. Don't let me eclipse the weight of your sacrifices. It's the whole Drifter Camp we're talking about!

speaker: Raven
content: You're overthinking it. Most of the non-combatants have evacuated already. Julien's the only one who needs to stay behind—he said so himself.

speaker: Raven
content: You just focus on BR-002. Isn't that your emphasis all along? Why start worrying about others now?

Contamination had seeped under your feet, and things are just going to get worse as you go deeper towards the dead half of the Corpus. Not only is the way down soaked in contamination, the hallucinations are getting more severe.
Hecate is the most obviously affected one. She's no longer cold and indifferent towards you, but instead becoming more anxious and jittery. Her Nightmare is growing more and more unstable.

speaker: Choice
options: Enough, head back now. I won't go any further.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're figuring things out, whether it's saving the Drifter Camp or tracking down the other half of the Corpus. I won't give up on my mission. You guys don't need to do something so extreme.

speaker: Raven
content: It won't matter much, my dear. A sudden rescue mission now will only make the Executive Committee realize that Rustfire has other plans. As for you... if you don't destroy that monster below, how will you find its other half in Syndicate?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The <color=#fb9259>water level</color> is rising, which means the escaped half of the Corpus is acting up again. As we dawdle, it'll infect more people and spread more Mania. More people will die in vain for this so-called "hope."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is the truth of the matter. It's a huge risk to bet everything on this mission. If you lose the bet, we won't be able to continue.
You can.
The quiet Rustfire combatant comes over to you.

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: We'll get contamination-resistant diving gear as soon as possible for you and your companions to dive into the pool. Don't have to worry about countering contamination.

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: We all brought Hypercubes. Please take all of them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even the FAC has to avoid the radiation in Inner Bay. Without Hypercubes, you have even less of a chance of holding out.

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: That's fine, as long as you can take back the mine.

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: If it's still not enough, the shelter has the rest of Rustfire's reserves. Raven can send the signal for them to bring it all here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But the shelter is also in Inner Bay. The people there need Hypercubes to protect them, too!

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: Everyone who came here has the same faith and conviction. You are the hope of Syndicate. We will give you everything to help you succeed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What difference would it make? Even if all of you sacrifice yourselves, I still can't guarantee that I'll be able to give you the results you want!
But his eyes are determined, almost fanatical. You can't help but take a step back.
The situation is beyond your comprehension. You want to ask Raven, but she starts to talk first.

speaker: Raven
content: Why do something so extreme... Is that what you want to ask, ${PlayerName}?

speaker: Raven
content: ...The golden age is gone, yet Rustfire is its legacy. They witnessed West District get destroyed by the Black Ring, then pillaged and discarded by DisCity. All their life's work was crushed, humiliated and discarded like carrion.

speaker: Raven
content: This was once a glorious industrial empire, now reduced to rust. Only by reclaiming everything lost can they mend and rebuild their shattered hearts.

speaker: Choice
options: But you guys are too reckless!

speaker: Raven
content: Haha, can't be helped. If those trapped in darkness refuse to forget the light, they will turn into moths that throw themselves toward the faintest spark.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: False hope is a death trap. Do you want to see them die? Is this the kind of tragic poetry you enjoy?

speaker: Raven
content: But if you deny them this faint spark of light, what else can you give them in this darkness?

speaker: Raven
content: Can you give them real hope after extinguishing their false ones? Besides...
Her gaze turns ice cold.

speaker: Raven
content: Those of us here would understand your decision. But the people outside will only see that you inexplicably gave up on something you could have continued.

speaker: Raven
content: I know it's unfair to you, but many people consider you their hope and leader. But let them think you'd "betray" them...

speaker: Raven
content: Rustfire members are willing to put their lives on the line for their leaders, but on that same note, they won't tolerate their leaders "betraying" them. If there's a misunderstanding, I can't guarantee that people won't act up.

speaker: Choice
options: Don't threaten me. I already said I couldn't do it.
Even if I want to live up to your expectations, a no is still a no.

content: Before you can reply, a hand grabs you. You turn around to see a petite, hooded figure with a familiar, youthful voice.

speaker: Scrawny Rustfire Combatant
content: You can do it. Back at the Drifter Camp, you defeated that monster and saved everyone. I remember everything you said. You asked us to fight.

speaker: Scrawny Rustfire Combatant
content: I'm here to fight now, Mr.
female_content: I'm here to fight now, Miss.

speaker: Ica
content: Are you the man who came from outside? Do you know where all the people the execs took are? Can you take me there?
female_content: Are you the lady who came from outside? Do you know where all the people the execs took are? Can you take me there?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Raven! Why is there a <color=#fb9259>little kid</color> here?
You ask Raven angrily, but the child tugs on you again.

speaker: Ica
content: I'm not a little kid! I followed you all the way here from the Drifter Camp. Nobody noticed me. That's how great I am! I also got the strongest Sinner to come here. She's really great at fighting. She'll help me, and she'll help you, too!

speaker: Ica
content: I'm part of Rustfire, too! I also want to fight! I want to avenge Mommy and Daddy!
His excited shouts echo through the mine. At the same time, there's a slight rumble under your feet. Waves appear on the pool, and more apparitions begin to rise.

speaker: Ica
content: Take all my Hypercubes. With you, we'll definitely win! Take back Syndicate!!
You grab him and back away. What's happening here has crossed a line. You can't tolerate it anymore.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mission aborted. Raven, take everyone back!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hurry!
The woman listens to your urgent shouts for some time before responding.

speaker: Raven
content: Yes, leader.

speaker: Raven
content: Remember to give me an answer when you get back.
The apparitions surge towards you all like a tide. Raven holds up her notebook, and countless streams of ink flow out to drag everyone away before you're completely devoured.

speaker: Raven
content: I don't have enough ink, so I can only hold them off this round. The rest is up to you. Good luck fleeing...

speaker: Ica
content: I don't want to flee! Let me go back!! I want to fight!
The boy struggles, nearly getting caught by an apparition. You see a shadow dash by to shatter the apparition.

1:21 a.m., March 20, N.F. 113
Inner Bay Shelter lounge
You've returned to the shelter. The atmosphere here is now completely different from when you left.

speaker: Raven
content: What an unexpected success this mission was! We reached the lower depths of the mine, surveyed the terrain, and cleared many obstacles.

speaker: Raven
content: If I didn't have to use up all my beautiful writing for the last battle, there'd be a lot of notes in this notebook! But it doesn't matter. I've retained everything in my mind. The next try will be a swift victory!

speaker: Raven
content: ${PlayerName}, I'm taking your girls to get some rest. You should take a nap and then come find me. We still have a lot of things to discuss.

<size=30>She winks at you and takes the Sinners away. Some of the combatants have been affected by Mania, but luckily, you can control it with your shackles. You'd never forgive yourself if these people who put their lives on the line for you turned into Corruptors.</size>
Everyone thanks you for your shackles, but there's no joy in their voices, only fatigue and despair. The eyes that had all been focused on you are now scattered, full of doubt and anxiety.

You're not surprised. After all, the mission failed. You were unable to reach the bottom of BR-002, and failed to destroy the dead half of the Corpus. The entire shelter is enveloped by worry and despair.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Hecate, it's time to sleep.

speaker: Hella
content: This bed can fit us both. They made it nice and clean and comfy for us. Just relax now. Others are keeping guard. Come?

speaker: Hecate
content: I'm not sleeping.

speaker: Hella
content: But you look like you're about to black out? Your body needs to rest.
It's rare for Hella to be so polite, but she gets no response. Hecate sits with her back to the door, facing Hella but not looking at her at all.
The Syndicate girl can't hold back her temper any longer.

speaker: Hella
content: ...What the heck has gotten into you lately? You're mopey in everything you do, and you put on a grumpy face even with ${PlayerName}! Plus, you keep picking fights on your own!

speaker: Hella
content: What did we do piss you off so much?

speaker: Hecate
content: No. I'm not angry. It's pointless to talk about this.

speaker: Hella
content: It's not pointless! You're making me angry! I have no idea what's going on, and I don't like that!

speaker: Hella
content: We still have to be around each other for another few days! Tell me what's wrong now, or else I'll call ${PlayerName} over, too!

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Don't disturb Chief's rest.

speaker: Hecate
content: My behavior has nothing to do with you, Hella. Our mission is to protect Chief. That's the only thing you should think about.

speaker: Hella
content: Huh?? You didn't listen to what I said at all! What I'm concerned about is...

speaker: Hecate
content: Your concerns are meaningless to the mission.

speaker: Hecate
content: Go to sleep now.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Caw... Three armored units have been defeated, but the west side of the Drifter Camp has fallen. Taran is trying his best to defend the main gate...

speaker: Black Raven
content: Julien is still alive, but badly injured. He's under a lot of pressure and hasn't completely healed after the surgery... Caw...

speaker: Black Raven
content: Need more companions... Need more companions...
Raven paces about and mumbles to herself as she changes out of the contamination-stained Executive Officer uniform.

speaker: Raven
content: Hmm... what should I put in the next mobilization letter...
A black shadow zips across the ground, then suddenly flies up, striking the ceiling light. The room is instantly plunged into darkness.
Before Raven has a chance to move, several streaks of black fluid wrap around her limbs, torso and neck.

speaker: Raven
content: So you're the one Ica called help from... I figured.
As soon as Raven finishes speaking, a sharp metal object presses against her neck—somehow, her quill pen had silently fallen into the intruder's hands.

speaker: Raven
content: Well, if it isn't the little punk who skipped class and dropped out of school... You remembered to come back to see your teacher?

speaker: Raven
content: You've been on vacation for quite a while. Did you finish all your holiday homework?

speaker: Shadow Assassin
content: Shut up, dumb bird. I'll pull your tongue out.
The room is now devoid of any sources of light from inside. Under the faint light from outside, a huge shadow emerges.
It's spurred by the murderous intent of the assassin behind it.

speaker: Shadow Assassin
content: Why is that kid here? Send him home, or else I'll kill you.

speaker: Shadow Assassin
content: Has Rustfire fallen so low that you want to send a kid like that to battle?
The sharp tip of the quill pen gleams in the cold light and edges toward Raven's neck again, but Raven just smiles.

speaker: Raven
content: I already knew it was you back in the mine. I certainly didn't have enough ink to stop so many monsters.

speaker: Raven
content: I don't know how he came, but as for why... You were there, too. Didn't you hear everything?

speaker: Raven
content: Ica wants to avenge his parents, who got captured by Executive Officers and died in jail. That ordeal transformed the child into a warrior.

speaker: Raven
content: The darkness affects every Syndican equally, so everyone has the right to fight back. Right, Crache?

speaker: Raven
content: Or, does the guardian of the Homeless think that kid's not worthy enough to fight?

speaker: Crache
content: You're the one who incited them!

speaker: Crache
content: You shamelessly wrote and spread all that propaganda about fighting injustice and taking back Syndicate.

speaker: Raven
content: Oh, so you read what I wrote! Don't you find it passionate and riveting?

speaker: Crache
content: It's a crock of rubbish! You made this mess, and now hundreds of armed execs and two armored mechs are attacking the Drifter Camp! So many in the camp just died from Mania. What are you going to fight against the Executive Committee with?!

speaker: Raven
content: Of course we can't rely on the Drifter Camp alone. But there's no shortage of people who want to get rid of the Executive Committee and take back Syndicate, right? I put the ruins of that mech on the front page. A victory like that can really boost morale.

speaker: Crache
content: You're inciting a bunch of delusional fools to die!

speaker: Raven
content: Only those who wanted to fight in the first place can be incited, and those are precisely the heroes whose awakening I want to witness. If they're determined to go to war, who am I to disagree?

speaker: Raven
content: Oh, I get it now... Your little Homeless pals got incited, too? All those cute little Sinners went to help?

speaker: Raven
content: Oh, they really went? Haha, no wonder Julien's still alive. It's been a while since I've seen them. I'm glad how capable they've become.

speaker: Raven
content: I guess that makes sense. Everyone except you used to be so sweet to their teacher. The Homeless all love me, right? Ouch, that hurts...
The shadows strangling her throat grow even tighter.

speaker: Crache
content: ...You've got some nerve to mention that.

speaker: Raven
content: Why not? I look fondly upon those times... Ouch, loosen up a bit...

speaker: Raven
content: My whole purpose of coming to Rustfire was to open a school. I took good care of you guys. I wrote all the teaching materials myself.

speaker: Raven
content: <color=#fb9259>Syndicate Academy</color>... isn't it great? I can realize my dream and protect the Homeless at the same time. Giving them knowledge is giving them strength. That way, they won't ever be misled or bullied again, right?

speaker: Raven
content: You let all those naughty kids come to me because you also think that, no? What, you took everyone away just because I went to do some work in Eastside?

speaker: Raven
content: You made everyone skip class and damaged school facilities. Alas, is this how you repay my kindness? You really know how to break a teacher's heart.

speaker: Crache
content: Quit acting. If I had known your real motive, I never would have believed those lies.

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: Supplies are short, but if we work hard, we can still afford to support a few dozen kids. More importantly...

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: They all show a lot of potential—angry, unyielding, and trusting of each other. A couple of them are powerful Sinners. The next generation of Syndicate all believe in her.

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: They'll become the best Rustfire warriors of the future...

speaker: Crache
content: Your little plot can't escape the ears of the shadows. The gangs who oppress the Homeless are indeed scum, but the hypocrite who exploits them is even worse!

speaker: Raven
content: ...Are you angry because I remind you of <color=#fb9259>Yagyu</color>? The one who used to call you "daughter"?

speaker: Crache
content: You spied on me?

speaker: Raven
content: I'm not only a teacher, but also a journalist. Of course I'd know that.

speaker: Raven
content: <size=31>You loathe Syndicate. You want to keep the Homeless away from strife, away from the center of the storm, and away from a world where violence endlessly repeats itself. You don't believe that the grownups who messed up this place can make it better.</size>

speaker: Raven
content: But not all grownups are your enemies. A lot of people want to shatter and transform this dark jungle where violence reigns supreme. All they need is the chance, and the flag to rally around.

speaker: Raven
content: <size=29>You see how many people my little leaflets resonated with? They defend Drifter Camp precisely because they can't bear it any longer and yearn for change. The silent ones have come forward with the same desire as yours. Now they finally have the courage to do something about it.</size>

speaker: Raven
content: Don't you think this will usher in the real change?

speaker: Crache
content: Ha... you don't like violence, do you? Then you also know nothing about Syndicate.

speaker: Crache
content: Even if you incite everyone in the city who "wants change" to be your cannon fodder, nothing will change for the better.

speaker: Crache
content: Everyone says they hate violence, but violence has already been ingrained in their souls. The more you want to realize a dream, the more shortcuts you're willing to take. All these years, the fastest shortcut in Syndicate has always been violence.

speaker: Crache
content: As someone who's willing to become cannon fodder, and incites others to do the same, don't you realize you're no different?

speaker: Crache
content: Rustfire hasn't found a way to change things at all. You're bound to fail. Just wait and see.

speaker: Raven
content: ...It's so sad to hear these words from a kid like you.

speaker: Raven
content: It's because you don't read enough.

speaker: Crache
content: ...What did you say—ahhh!!

<size=31>A jet-black blade suddenly shoots out from her shadow, splitting open a nearby oil lamp. The flames that spilled out light up a corner of the room. The shadows binding Raven loosen up as several blades fly towards Crache, forcing her to jump back.</size>
But as soon as she lands, the bookshelf behind her suddenly shakes. Black streaks shoot out of the pages of the books, turning into a pitch-black raven that attacks Crache.

speaker: Crache
content: Get lost!
Shadows split into thin threads and tear the raven to shreds, then move Crache through the air to a truly safe place.

Raven has completely freed herself from Crache's clutch. In the tiny room, the black ink finally disentangles from the black shadows. The two sides lash out at each other's necks almost simultaneously, then halt at the same time.

speaker: Crache
content: When did you hide the ink in my shadow?

speaker: Raven
content: Haha, gonna accept that you lost to me fair and square? If not, then blame yourself for being both stubborn and uneducated. Can't believe someone like this has the nerve to skip class...

speaker: Raven
content: You're still so naive, little guardian. You can't outwit a grownup.

speaker: Crache
content: ...I dare you to try it again!

speaker: Raven
content: <size=44>No, thanks.</size>
Raven reaches out and effortlessly grabs the shadow trying to attack her neck.

speaker: Raven
content: We're really made for each other. We both manipulate dark substances, tread the darkness, and live in this broken land. You became my favorite student the moment I saw you.

speaker: Raven
content: You're the most bipolar child I've met. You can't see the light, nor can you fall into the darkness. You've been struggling alone all these years. You're a lot like my friends, so miserable and adorable at the same time.

speaker: Raven
content: When this war is over, take the children back to class. After my mission ends, I won't need to travel anymore. I'll rebuild Syndicate Academy and teach you well.

speaker: Raven
content: Believe it or not, I didn't create the school to trick you into fighting. I want you to live and grow up in peace. I have only one real purpose for opening that school...
Crache freezes, and in that moment, Raven suddenly yanks the shadow, almost tipping Crache over.

speaker: Raven
content: As Syndicate's great romantic poet, I must personally teach my works to my students, who will spread them to the world. That way, my poems will be immortalized for all eternity...

speaker: Crache
content: ...I gotta pull out your tongue, you lying bastard!
Knock... knock... Someone knocks on the door.

speaker: Crache
content: Ehh...
After realizing who it is, Crache flashes a look of fear. As she steps back into the shadows, she spits out one last vicious threat.

speaker: Message in the Shadows
content: I'll pull it out next time. You better watch out. The shadows have eyes on you.
She disappears.

speaker: Raven
content: Acting all tough in front of me but fleeing at the sight of him. What's there to be afraid of? Such a little cutie.
female_content: Acting all tough in front of me but fleeing at the sight of her. What's there to be afraid of? Such a little cutie.

content: She goes quiet after saying that. The knocking continues. Raven ponders for a while with her head lowered, then shakes her head and sighs. She changes her clothes, tidies up her things and puts out the fire.

speaker: Raven
content: All right, come in.

speaker: Raven
content: Someone came to have a heart-to-heart chat with me just now. Sorry for the wait. Where are those two kids of yours? One of them doesn't seem to be doing that well. Did you talk to her?

speaker: Raven
content: ...Mmm. Seems you've already made up your mind.

1:21 a.m., March 20, N.F. 113
Inner Bay Shelter lounge

speaker: Hecate
content: Though your emotions have nothing to do with me, they'll get in the way of our mission if you don't control them. You're erratic enough to begin with. It'll put Chief in danger.

speaker: Hecate
content: Go to sleep now.
She gazes straight ahead, completely ignoring that Hella is on the verge of exploding from anger.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Hmph! You make me so mad it's almost funny! After being worried sick about you, all I get is— "it's for the mission"?

speaker: Hella
content: Who are you kidding? It's not like you did that well on this mission, either!
Hecate doesn't respond, but her eyelashes quiver.

speaker: Hella
content: You think it's cool to keep a straight face? Did it make you stronger in battle? You were so slow and clumsy back in the mine. Even the Rustfire guys did way better. Why do you have to be such a downer lately?

speaker: Hecate
content: ...I was just not familiar with the new combat environment. I'll make up for it as soon as possible.

speaker: Hella
content: Cut the crap! You're so wound up that you snapped! You can't just tense up like this at the drop of a hat. You scare yourself to death before anything even happens to ${PlayerName}! No wonder you keep losing!

speaker: Hella
content: Your mind is a mess, yet you still want to act all tough. Who are you squaring off against? And you have the nerve to tell me it's none of my concern... fine, it's not!

speaker: Hella
content: Do whatever you want! I won't care about you anymore. Good night! Keep it up and pretend it's for the Chief's sake! Can't wait to see you get humongous dark circles under your eyes and completely fail at everything tomorrow again!
After Hella finishes her rant, she dives into the sheets and goes to sleep.
After a long, painful silence, Hecate speaks up.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Am I really that useless?

speaker: Hella
content: ...Zzzz.

speaker: Hecate
content: I already reflected on my mistakes... and making corrections.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Zzzz zzzz.

speaker: Hecate
content: Hella... I feel lost...
She clasps her hands together, uttering each word slowly, as if <color=#fb9259>confiding</color> in someone for the first time.

speaker: Hecate
content: I was born and trained in a lab to become a <color=#fb9259>controllable and useful</color> Sinner, someone who can successfully carry out any mission. My skills and knowledge have all been cultivated for this purpose.

speaker: Hecate
content: But I've never been good enough. Not skilled enough, not stable enough, not safe enough.

speaker: Hecate
content: The researchers said that I'm fatally flawed. I'm only useful up to age 14.
...Woosh! The covers get thrown aside as a black shadow rushes over and grabs Hecate by the collar.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Who said that? What lab? What age 14? Does ${PlayerName} know about this? Ugh, there's no way that dummy knows. Why didn't you tell anyone?

speaker: Hecate
content: ...I-I thought you were asleep?

speaker: Hella
content: I'm asking you, how much longer do you have?

speaker: Hecate
content: I'm already past the expiration date.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Huh?

speaker: Hecate
content: Hella, how old are you?

speaker: Hella
content: ...I-I don't remember. 15? 16, maybe?

speaker: Hecate
content: Do I look younger than you?

speaker: Hella
content: You are so annoying!!
Hella hops back onto the bed and wraps herself in the covers, poking her head out only after she cools down. She purses her lips, signaling for Hecate to continue.

speaker: Hecate
content: They said what'll cripple me isn't age, but mood swings and overthinking.

speaker: Hecate
content: Even with intense training, there's a part of Nightmare that I can't control, which will go manic easily. Adolescence is an especially dangerous time. The researchers thought I would no longer be able to control my mental activities after age 14.

speaker: Hecate
content: At that point, I'd either be killed by my out-of-control Nightmare, or disposed of as a dangerous failed product. That was what would have happened, but then they found a solution.

speaker: Hecate
content: The researchers removed my emotions through surgery.
Hella sits up and stares at her with wide eyes. This time, Hecate doesn't stop, and continues to mumble before Hella loses it.

speaker: Hecate
content: It was the right thing to do. Feelings and emotions are as dangerous and uncontrollable as the Mania inside us.

speaker: Hecate
content: Only by eliminating them can I safely exist. As the first successful case, I was transferred to the MBCC to complete missions and achieve my worth.

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh, that makes me so mad! Missions? Uncontrollable? You're not a tool! That's f*** ridiculous!

speaker: Hecate
content: But all of this has led me to meet Chief, so it has been meaningful.

speaker: Hecate
content: I'm very glad to have gotten this mission. My existence is worthwhile as long as I'm useful to him.
female_content: I'm very glad to have gotten this mission. My existence is worthwhile as long as I'm useful to her.

speaker: Hecate
content: But Hella, I failed.

speaker: Hecate
content: Back at Drifter Camp, my Nightmare was shattered by the Corpseborne. I should have tried everything to summon it back right away, because Chief needed it.

speaker: Hecate
content: Yet I failed to do that. I failed to hold onto Chief's hand, and failed to get Nightmare to protect him. I watched as Chief fell from such a great height... He almost died from that fall.
female_content: Yet I failed to do that. I failed to hold onto Chief's hand, and failed to get Nightmare to protect her. I watched as Chief fell from such a great height... She almost died from that fall.

speaker: Hecate
content: Someone once told me that my emotions weren't an unnecessary burden that would constrain me, but can instead become strength for Chief. Yet at that moment, I couldn't control my emotions.

speaker: Hecate
content: I lost my senses and couldn't move. I didn't know if the shackles were still there, nor did I check up on Chief right away. I failed to rush to his side. My mind went blank. I couldn't make a single decision.
female_content: I lost my senses and couldn't move. I didn't know if the shackles were still there, nor did I check up on Chief right away. I failed to rush to her side. My mind went blank. I couldn't make a single decision.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief was able to bounce back, but that's only because he's strong. But as for me... at that point, I had failed my mission.
female_content: Chief was able to bounce back, but that's only because she's strong. But as for me... at that point, I had failed my mission.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Hella, I'm really scared. What should I do...
She covers her face with quivering hands, falling into silence as her shoulders tremble. Hella looks at her quietly, then lets out a sigh.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Why are these dumbass labs everywhere... Hecate, come here. I want to tell you something.
Hella pats on the bed. Hecate goes over meekly and looks at her, waiting for her to talk.

speaker: Hella
content: Not being able to summon Nightmare is normal. During training, you fall into a long daze every time your Nightmare gets shattered. I'm a witness to that. It has nothing to do with your emotions.

speaker: Hella
content: Whether it's because the enemy is too strong, or because you're too young, or whatever other reason, we all fail from time to time. All we have to do is try again. It's the same for me when I try to learn how to read from you.

speaker: Hella
content: You feel bad right now because ${PlayerName} almost died.

speaker: Hella
content: It's the first time you've encountered something like this, so you're scared and discouraged but don't know what to do. You're like a headless chicken searching for non-existent reasons, and even started blaming yourself.

speaker: Hecate
content: It's because protecting Chief is my mission. I live for my mission.

speaker: Hella
content: No, the real reason is that it's ${PlayerName}. You're sad, angry and in pain because of ${PlayerName}, not because of some silly mission.

speaker: Hella
content: It's because ${PlayerName} is the first "person" that "Hecate" met outside that dark, terrible lab. And ${PlayerName} is the first thing that you met and chose for yourself in your own world.

speaker: Hecate
content: The first thing I chose for myself... in my own world?

speaker: Hecate
content: What do you mean by "my"?

speaker: Hella
content: I mean... something worth cherishing that you chose on your own. For example, there's no mission that orders you to protect me, but you still do because I'm your friend.

speaker: Hecate
content: There's no such thing.

speaker: Hella
content: You little ducking... Never mind... It's all that f***** lab's fault.

speaker: Hella
content: I don't expect you to get it right away. Even someone as clever as me can't learn to read all at once. But we have lots of time.

speaker: Hella
content: You'll encounter more things worth cherishing and embrace more of the world. With ${PlayerName} around, you won't get locked up by those bastards again. He'll protect you. You'll be free.
female_content: You'll encounter more things worth cherishing and embrace more of the world. With ${PlayerName} around, you won't get locked up by those bastards again. She'll protect you. You'll be free.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...I don't need to be free. Nor do I need to be protected. I just want the strength to protect Chief.

speaker: Hella
content: That's fine, too. As long as you make your own decision, you're free.

speaker: Hella
content: ${PlayerName} must want to see a Hecate like that, too.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...What does that mean?
Hella lifts her head up smugly.

speaker: Hella
content: Something very profound, indeed. Remember, we're Sinners. We have hearts of our own, and that's what gives us strength. No one can control our hearts.

speaker: Hella
content: Once you're able to leave that dark place behind and become the Hecate of your own choosing, you'll be stronger for sure.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Will I really be able... to become stronger...?

speaker: Hella
content: Of course. Trust me. But you have to take care of yourself, first. That dummy cares a lot about us.

speaker: Hella
content: Now that I'm not so worried anymore, I feel so sleepy! Come, the bed is nice and spacious. Let's sleep together.

speaker: Hella
content: Who knew we're both lab escapees! What a coincidence, hehe...
On the bed, Hecate moves a bit farther away from Hella.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...No, thanks.

speaker: Hecate
content: You're a bed hog.

speaker: Hecate
content: You were in the detention room across from me, so I already saw how you slept before Chief came. Every night, you'd flail about and hog the sheets.

speaker: Hella
content: I hate you!!
2 seconds later, fade out
CG1: Light shines in through the door, 1 second

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Good night.
CG2: transition cut, 2 seconds
You leave the pair's room. You go down the hall past the stairs to the shelter's command center and knock on the door.
All right, come in.
You go inside and see the dark poet.

speaker: Raven
content: Seems like you've already made up your mind.
You nod.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: First, we need to go into the mine again. We have to try harder to break through the contamination layer blocking the path and destroy the dead half of the Corpus. Then, we'll go exterminate the living half that has been exposed.

speaker: Raven
content: Mmm... this plan remains unchanged.

speaker: Choice
options: But I won't use any help from Rustfire.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm going to get the FAC to break through the contamination layer and remove the dead Corpus from the bottom.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The target is clear, and we don't need that many people. They'd agree to it.

speaker: Raven
content: ...As soon as the FAC enters Inner Bay, everything about us will be exposed. They will take over BR-002. You want to betray Rustfire.

speaker: Choice
options: This is to protect everyone's lives.

speaker: Raven
content: You want to dash everyone's hopes, reveal our secrets, and extinguish our one last dream...

speaker: Raven
content: Ha... History really does repeat itself.

speaker: Raven
content: You think I'd let an ugly plot twist stain my poem twice?
Her ink condenses, and something lands on your shoulder. One raven, two ravens... Jet-black feathers fall off their bodies. Raven stares at you coldly from behind.
You take a deep breath.

speaker: Choice
options: If you don't agree, there is still the second option.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I will leave this place to find the escaped half of the Corpus.

speaker: Raven
content: Take your time... By the time you find it, the Executive Committee would have razed the Drifter Camp to the ground.

speaker: Choice
options: No, I can buy more time for Rustfire.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I already have a lot of information about BR-002. I will use any means necessary to get the Executive Committee to stop the Black Ring. I'll make them drop everything else they're doing to focus on tracking down the living half of the Corpus.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Since the incidents in Eastside were able to contain the FAC, it shows that the City Council cares more about "those incidents" than all of West District. Let's just fool them, then.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We'll use the intelligence to tell them a story. We'll say that what happened in Eastside is closely linked to BR-002. Let's use... the abnormal fluctuations of the major black rings and our "old friend" Parma. Both are quite "mysterious" anyways.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=29>In short, we'll scare the councilors into thinking that they can't stop the troubles in Eastside without resolving the Corpus of BR-002 first. Since the FAC can't leave Eastside right now, we'll ask the Executive Committee to drop what they're doing and help us with West District.</size>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I get the chance, I'll also bring Rustfire into the mix. "The Drifter Camp has gained ample battle experience after dealing with the Corpus of BR-002." That way, you'll have more time and an extra layer of protection.
Since you walked through that door, this is the first time Raven has shown some enthusiasm.

speaker: Raven
content: ...Pretty creative. What are the odds of succeeding?

speaker: Choice
options: Comparing it to your suicide plan?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Both are quite slim. So why not try a safer approach?

speaker: Raven
content: ...Hahahahahaha!

speaker: Raven
content: Sorry, I just remembered someone accusing Rustfire of being stubborn and knowing only how to be cannon fodder. So it would seem like she has a point.

speaker: Raven
content: I'll join in, and also speed things up.

speaker: Raven
content: I don't want that monster wandering out there for too long. I have a pretty good idea.

speaker: Raven
content: If the apparitions at the bottom of the pit are contamination caused by the living Corpus devouring humans from outside, then the people it devoured might also appear as apparitions at the bottom, near the center.

speaker: Raven
content: While humans cannot penetrate the contamination, my ink can. This star journalist here can help you ask around where the living half of the Corpus is. What do you think?
She surprises you with her frankness.

speaker: Raven
content: Not only do I agree, I also want to help you sell this plan.

speaker: Raven
content: Haha, but I have to ask my friend first. He calls the shots.

speaker: Raven
content: Julien, did you hear what ${PlayerName} said? Do you accept?
She lifts up her hand. A jet-black raven lands on it, tilting its head.

speaker: Raven
content: Even though communications are cut off in Inner Bay, I can use my ink raven for long-distance communication. You two leaders can mobilize together.
You realize that Julien is on the other end of the raven. After a brief silence, you decide to speak anyway...

speaker: Choice
options: I'm glad you are still alive.

speaker: Julien
content: If I die, can you stay behind?

speaker: Julien
content: Ha... No? Forget it, then.

speaker: Choice
options: If this continues, Rustfire will only destroy themselves.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Contamination from BR-002 continues to increase, which shows that the other half of the Corpus is highly active. This has already exceeded your expectations.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've checked the Hypercube reserves in the shelter. Even if you all sacrifice your lives, it won't be enough to penetrate the layer. You should all know that, yet no one is stopping.

speaker: Julien
content: Because they believe in you. You're their hope.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Be rational. No one there can break through the barrier. If you keep clinging on to this so-called "hope" and making suicidal sacrifices, you'll end up ruining yourselves.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's not hope that's propelling Rustfire anymore. Now you're just doing insane things to run away from despair.

speaker: Julien
content: Hope is something precious. It holds a lot of power even when it's irrational.

speaker: Julien
content: Eight years ago, when BR-002 broke out, Rustfire didn't give up. They picked up the pieces, supported each other, and clutched onto hope while battling grief, gangsters and Mania.

speaker: Julien
content: We had a leader back then, too.

speaker: Julien
content: He was very strong and brave. Everyone trusted and depended on him. When he disappeared into BR-002, everyone believed he would come back. This faith was what made everyone persevere and keep going.

speaker: Julien
content: But he never came back. He betrayed Rustfire and defected to Nirvana.

speaker: Julien
content: After that, within a week, some fled, some joined gangs, while others simply gave up their lives. Many turned into Corruptors. Rustfire was left in shambles.

speaker: Julien
content: BR-002 didn't kill Inner Bay. He did.

speaker: Julien
content: Now, eight years later, many will also consider you the enemy if they see you with the Executive Committee. They will never be able to accept the Executive Committee, nor understand your choice.

speaker: Julien
content: For them, it would be losing their leader and hope all over again.

speaker: Choice
options: But I was never your leader.

speaker: Julien
content: Yeah...You're right.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Try it out, Julien. At least this is a realistic hope. Try... and see how it goes.
You want to say something else, but Raven gently covers your mouth. She waves, and the raven dissolves back into her bottle as ink.

speaker: Raven
content: Leave the rest to me.

speaker: Raven
content: Though he looks aged and hasn't forgotten what happened eight years ago, our architect has a pretty "young" mentality, especially after meeting you.

speaker: Choice
options: Did I remind him of something?

speaker: Raven
content: You make him remember a lot of things, but we have to look forward. No one will make things hard for you. I'll get someone to escort you out of Inner Bay, and let you know right away if we find any clues about the Corpseborne's other half.

speaker: Raven
content: But I have one condition. Leave your two little pals to me.

speaker: Raven
content: Let's see... how about I keep them as hostages! With these two cuties around, I can fool the others, and also deter you from betraying Rustfire. After all, you've never ventured far from them.
She grins and pats you on the shoulder. Her voice becomes gentle once more.

speaker: Raven
content: You probably already know that the battlefield you're heading to is far too cruel for them. They won't be able to handle it. You should've done this a long time ago.

speaker: Raven
content: Especially that girl. She cares about you too much. It'll kill her.

speaker: Raven
content: To make things fair, I'll let you keep something of mine as hostage, too. Here's my most beautiful and precious poetry book.
She really fetches her poetry book.

speaker: Raven
content: When things calm down, I'll find the chance to send them back to the Bureau. You can cast your shackles on me if you don't believe me. I have to go deep into the contaminated mine anyways. That way, I'll have your protection.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm surprised that you'd really help me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought you'd prefer the original plan. After all, it's more in line with your... dark aesthetic?

speaker: Raven
content: Oh, you must've misunderstood. I like those struggling in the darkness because they always hold onto a spark of light. That light is stronger than anything else in the world.

speaker: Raven
content: That spark of light is what makes the darkness meaningful.

speaker: Raven
content: That's why I also like your version of <color=#fb9259>hope</color>.
There's not much to pack. As you leave the room and close the door, the shadow beneath your feet quivers.
After a brief silence, a voice emerges from the shadows.

speaker: Voice in the Shadows
content: You won't be able to catch me, Minos Chief. Don't even think about it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll think about capturing you later. Right now, I have a favor to ask you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As the guardian of children, I want to ask you to protect those two.

speaker: Voice in the Shadows
content: ...Why don't you do it yourself?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm unable to do that myself right now. I'd only lead them to danger. So, please look after them for me.
Hecate opens her eyes groggily. It's hard to tell the time in the windowless shelter, but she feels like she had slept for a long time and had a long dream.
Hella is still kicking the covers with her feet. Hecate also notices a couple of extra blankets on her body that weren't there last night.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Chief?

speaker: Rustfire Member
content: We searched all over the shelter, but didn't find the Chief anywhere. What's going on?

speaker: Rustfire Member
content: He seemed off when he came back yesterday. Could it be possible that...
female_content: She seemed off when she came back yesterday. Could it be possible that...

speaker: Rustfire Member
content: But those two Sinners are still here. They're sound asleep... Things should be fine. Raven didn't say anything either, right?

speaker: Rustfire Member
content: Speaking of Raven, I heard she handed over several poetry books to the ruins patrol team... ${PlayerName} didn't want to sacrifice any team members last time. Did that lunatic go down into the mine alone this time...?
Raven sits at her desk, her head resting on one hand, her eyes shut and resting.
Her poetry book is falling deep into the mine. The pages scatter and float down, down, down... before finally landing in the pool, soaking up the contamination. The intense Mania makes her frown.

speaker: Raven
content: <color=#fb9259>O souls of the abyss, tell me your woes... Let me hear your unspoken cries, so that I may convey them...</color>
The ink gradually separates from the paper, merging into an ink-colored snake that swims into the depths of the contamination.
The murky whispers gradually seep into her consciousness. A plethora of eras, people, and emotions overwhelm her.

Raven's brows furrow deeper and deeper. Her eyes are shut as if she's having a nightmare. Her consciousness is being chewed away. Her quill pen dances wildly on the paper, scribbling down words no one can understand.

speaker: Raven
content: <color=#fb9259>Speak to me... and show me the way...</color>

speaker: Raven
content: ...Wow, I dozed off. Consciousness in the abyss is terrifying.
There seemed to be some familiar faces. Raven is inches away from grasping the truth, but she has to take a rest first. This has been too mentally draining for her.

speaker: Raven
content: Better go see those two kids first. Got a lot of explaining to do...
Forcing herself up, she wobbles to Hecate and Hella's room and knocks on the door.

speaker: Raven
content: Are you up, my dears?
No one responds. Raven realizes the door isn't locked.

speaker: Raven
content: ...No way. I'm in no condition to chase them down...
She pushes open the door. Several elite Rustfire combatants lay sprawled on the ground unconscious. The two Sinners had long disappeared.

speaker: Hella
content: Huff... Huff... Huff... Hecate! Wait! Wait up!

speaker: Hella
content: We should go back and clarify things. They all say the contamination in Inner Bay is abnormal. The shackles are not responding. We don't even know where ${PlayerName} is!

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief will come back for sure. If it weren't for us, he wouldn't have left.
female_content: Chief will come back for sure. If it weren't for us, she wouldn't have left.

speaker: Hella
content: What are you talking about? Those are just random guesses from the Rustfire folks. ${PlayerName} never said that.

speaker: Hecate
content: It's because I'm too weak. I became a burden, so he went about the mission alone. I'm so useless. I must find him and protect him, or else I...
female_content: It's because I'm too weak. I became a burden, so she went about the mission alone. I'm so useless. I must find her and protect her, or else I...

speaker: Hella
content: Watch out!!
Several remnant Nirvana mechs suddenly rush out!

speaker: Hella
content: How did we reach the bottom so quickly... I don't remember the water reaching here last time. Does this mean the other half of the monster has already...

speaker: Hella
content: Hecate, stop! ${PlayerName} isn't here! There are only monsters and contamination here! If you keep fighting, you'll...

speaker: Hecate
content: Out of my way!!

She rushes into the filth, which almost devours her. Suddenly, countless black shadows emerge from the ground. They shred the contaminants around Hecate, then firmly restrain the manic Nightmare and her master.
If you really want to find your Chief, you have to calm down first, you hear me?
A blue-haired girl emerges from the shadows.
Meanwhile, on the edge of a higher cliff, a few black ravens land quietly on a broken Nirvana mech to observe them.
After secretly leaving Inner Bay, you return to Syndicate, where the streets are just as you had remembered them.

speaker: Mutant Thug
content: Syndicate... Syndicate...

speaker: Mutant Thug
content: This is... our Syndicate!
A black raven flies out from the poetry book and pecks at the gangster's eyes, repelling him. A few Rustfire combatants also rush over to cover you, giving you time to react.
You effortlessly cast your shackles, repelling the manic enemies and saving several terrified refugees in the alley.
At the same time, the area touched by the shackles shows you another scene.
test
The horrific burns spread through the streets and scale the walls, merging with the gangsters' fire to light up Syndicate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...No wonder we had such a hard time fighting in Inner Bay.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This wasn't caused by fighting between Rustfire and the Executive Committee. The monster must have taken advantage of the chaos and accumulated a lot more power.
The bad thing is, the upcoming battle will be very troublesome. But the good thing is, you have some more bargaining chips.

Mixed with the roar of bullets and explosions, the human shrieks sound especially distorted. Many have already undergone visible mutations, and are hunting for any possible conscious target to attack. It's only a matter of time before they find you.
Before going into combat mode, you pick up a secret phone call.

speaker: Rust
content: Long time no see, Chief. Can you tell me what happened during your absence?

speaker: Choice
options: I can't do that at the moment, sorry.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I have something urgent to ask you. I need the FAC's help, and maybe even the 9th Agency's.

speaker: Rust
content: Go ahead, I'm all ears. Judging from the vibrant noises around you, we're probably going to lose contact with each other again soon.
You lead everyone to escape along a narrow path, and finally come to a relatively safe place.
The refugees behind you shudder and grab onto your clothes. They're all weak and wounded. An old woman tries to protect them with trembling arms.

speaker: Old Lady
content: ...Save us... Please save us...
Her trembling hands make you anxious. Finally, you calm down, turn around to take her hands, and tell her:

speaker: Choice
options: It's okay now. Rustfire will protect you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These combatants will lead you to safety. Syndicate will be a safer place when this is all over.

speaker: Rustfire Combatant
content: ...Then what about yourself?

speaker: Choice
options: I am going to do things in my way.

content: The long-awaited call rings.

speaker: Rust
content: Chief, we're seeing progress on our side. Your plan succeeded. But please also be prepared for the Executive Committee to be furious.
You take off the Rustfire cloak on you and put it on the old lady. You then fetch your MBCC jacket from your bag, and put your usual attire back on.
But at that moment, rustling sounds come from Raven's poetry book.

When you take out the poetry book, it opens by itself and flips to the last page with words— "Its stiff body is curled up in the soil, leaving you in complete loneliness." These are still the weird stanzas she usually writes.
But the next second, the letters begin to move. The ink swims like a snake, forming words that are clear and no longer dark.

speaker: Poetry Collection
content: Found it...

3:21 a.m., March 22, N.F. 113
Eastside - Nirvana Headquarters
A man in a suit sits at the end of a long table without saying a word. People on either side of the table are anxiously questioning each other.

speaker: ID-07
content: What's going on in West District? Why hasn't the company branch been set up yet? We need BR-004 to expand Hypercube production. We have to get West District stable and under control again.

speaker: ID-04
content: The gangs are easy to deal with. The Legion and Burns' forces are also in shambles. The Outland Affairs Bureau has its eyes on Quinn, and its President is now on the MBCC's watchlist. They wouldn't make any major moves right now.

speaker: Man In Suit
content: What obstacles do you still have?

speaker: Man In Suit
content: ...Is it those workers? You still haven't finished off the stragglers from eight years ago?

speaker: ID-03
content: It's a problem left over from history. If I had been around back then, I would have totally eradicated them.

speaker: ID-07
content: Then what has the Executive Committee been doing these days?! It's been half a year already. You still haven't been able to get rid of a bunch of rogue rebels with no money or proper weapons?

speaker: ID-03
content: O-originally, we were going to settle everything these few days. But just now, we were ordered to prioritize locating the whereabouts of a Mania monster...

speaker: ID-03
content: Moreover, there have been some issues with public opinion lately, so we're under a lot of pressure... If the Syndicans don't cooperate, who will do the work...

speaker: ID-04
content: That's your job to figure out. All 7 members of the Executive Committee have received ample funding from Nirvana... including you. We have it all on record...

speaker: ID-03
content: B-but, it's an order from the Speaker of the City Council. The 9th Agency submitted materials to him, so...

speaker: Man In Suit
content: ...What about the councilors?!
Everyone falls silent.

speaker: Man In Suit
content: The economic foundation of DisCity rests in Nirvana's hands. We control the Hypercubes. We should be able to get concessions from everyone, yet you're stonewalling me on all fronts.

speaker: Man In Suit
content: We're already overspending on dealing with hooligans trying to sabotage Nirvana, and now we're wasting money on an irrelevant monster?
All communications suddenly shut down, replaced by a blinking cursor. He knows immediately that he's about to get grilled by that troublesome existence again.

<color=#fb9259>X: </color>Hello.

<color=#fb9259>X: </color>Is the situation out of control again?

<color=#fb9259>Nirvana Director:</color> ...I didn't report it to the higher-ups. No need for you to come.

<color=#fb9259>X: </color>Good. I'll be leaving soon.

<color=#fb9259>X: </color>It's just that the underground shepherd has come to the surface. Right in West District. It must be happy to see such large-scale and long-lasting chaos there.
<color=#fb9259>X:</color> Is that something you forgot to report, or something you didn't discover?

<color=#fb9259>Nirvana Director:</color> Ah... about that... I don't know, I'm not, I have nothing to do with them. Tell the 9th Agency, I didn't...

<color=#fb9259>Nirvana Director:</color> I just want to protect Hypercubes, which are crucial to DisCity. I'm not on their side!
The Nirvana Director stammers nervously, trying hard to distance himself. The cursor flickers quietly for a while, then continues to send responses.

<color=#fb9259>X:</color> It's okay, I know you're not. You're just trying to pursue your own goals, and made a little mistake that anyone could've made along the way. It's fine.

<color=#fb9259>X:</color> My job is to make up for your mistake. Just like eight years ago.

<color=#fb9259>X:</color> All right. Sort out your demands, then help me out and give me some info.

<color=#fb9259>X:</color> After that, leave the rest to me.

speaker: Man In Suit
content: These are...
An ominous premonition runs through Julien's mind. His body shudders as deep feelings of hatred and fear rise to the surface.

speaker: Taran
content: Woke up from the pain again?

speaker: Julien
content: No... I'm fine.

speaker: Julien
content: How's the situation?

speaker: Taran
content: There's a lot less pressure on the Drifter Camp. Raven's propaganda worked. Many newcomers joined Rustfire. They also couldn't bear it anymore.

speaker: Taran
content: The Executive Committee also withdrew more than half of their armed forces. I guess ${PlayerName}'s plan really worked. We have some time to catch our breath.

speaker: Julien
content: What about ${PlayerName}?

speaker: Taran
content: Raven said he's leading the formal troops to find the Corpseborne. It's been confirmed to be hiding in a secret branch of the Executive Committee.
female_content: Raven said she's leading the formal troops to find the Corpseborne. It's been confirmed to be hiding in a secret branch of the Executive Committee.

speaker: Julien
content: Is that so...
Julien buries his head in his hands, tormented by both physical pain and anxiety.

speaker: Taran
content: Are you worried the Executive Committee will attack him?
female_content: Are you worried the Executive Committee will attack her?

speaker: Julien
content: ...I don't think they will. Raven also said they wouldn't be able to deal with the consequences.

speaker: Julien
content: But this is really reminding me of the past.

speaker: Taran
content: If you're really this worried, let me go take a look.

speaker: Taran
content: I've dealt with the Executive Committee many times, and I've also fought that monster before. Tracking, protection, rescue—you name it. I can do'em all.

speaker: Taran
content: Since you say he's hope, I'll make sure no one snatches him away.
female_content: Since you say she's hope, I'll make sure no one snatches her away.

content: Escorted by Executive Officers and a small number of FAC Elites, you arrive at your target location—the Executive Committee's secret branch.
You feel uneasy even though you don't see any visible signs of contamination. It must be here, but you can't figure out why it chose this place.

speaker: Armed Executive Officer
content: Chief, our messages went unanswered. Something might have happened in there.

speaker: Armed Executive Officer
content: What is this...?
The walls have crumbled, the ground has dissolved, and the whole place is blazing with icy flames. There's not a single living soul around. This is undoubtedly the work of that monster.
What shocks you even more is the interior design of the building. Iron bars, shackles, cells, and traces of struggle in the rooms...
This is a large-scale detention center, which immediately answers a question you've had all along:
There's only one reason why the Corpseborne chose this place. Whether it's Rustfire members captured by the Executive Committee, or residents of the Drifter Camp, they were all incarcerated here.
And they all became yummy snacks for the Corpus of BR-002.

speaker: Armed Executive Officer
content: The guards... all dead... The monster...

speaker: Armed Executive Officer
content: But where's the monster? Where...

speaker: Choice
options: Get out if you don't want to die!

content: It's time for a sinister game of <color=#fb9259>hide-and-seek</color> again. You summon your shackles, staying vigilant against anything that might come near you. The first thing you encounter is that familiar, nauseating voice.
...You... You again...
Distorted Corruptors crawl out of the cells one after another, rushing towards you. You want to find the source, but the stench of contamination surrounds you from all sides.
Violent tremors come from the pit, and the pool of contamination rises.
Somewhere close to the surface of the pool, the three Sinner girls are looking at each other.

speaker: Crache
content: The person you're looking for isn't here. He left early in the morning.
female_content: The person you're looking for isn't here. She left early in the morning.

content: Before Hella gets a chance to start cursing, she sees Hecate frozen on the spot, and rushes forward to comfort her.

speaker: Hella
content: Don't make stuff up! ${PlayerName} would never abandon us. He'll have an explanation for this for sure!
female_content: Don't make stuff up! ${PlayerName} would never abandon us. She'll have an explanation for this for sure!

speaker: Hella
content: Plus, who the f*** are you? Where did a little kid like you come from? You have a death wish coming to this kind of place?
Crache's face darkens, and the shadows under her feet pounce on Hella.

speaker: Hella
content: I'm asking you a question, why... Hey hey hey...
The shadow lifts up Hella upside-down by the ankles, and the two lock eyes with each other. Hella thrashes about like a fish out of water struggling for oxygen.

speaker: Hella
