content: Don't take offense. Gracelyn's just a bit of a worrywart. But hey, if Parfait trusts you with her secret, then we will too. Just don't let anything slip, okay?
Sibilla believes him. After all, if they meant to kill her, she wouldn't still be breathing.

speaker: Harry
content: Kick back and relax while you're in Syndicate. The Drifter Camp used to have lots of Outlanders around. Later we'll have Greta, our yooga master here, check out your injuries. Trust me, you'll be back on your feet in no time.

speaker: Harry
content: Oh, by the way, where are you from? Did you come for the Great Expo too? Is that how you met Parfait, through business?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Thank you, but I'm just a stowaway hiding here, afraid of getting caught. I'm grateful to Parfait for protecting me, and to all of you as well.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Don't worry about me. I'll just wait for her here.
Sibilla's command of Disian is better than Harry's expectations. He smiles awkwardly.

speaker: Harry
content: Ahaha... You were totally freaked out just now, huh? Don't worry—I got you. Let me fix you up first.

speaker: Harry
content: But our first aid supplies are pretty basic right now. The West District's still getting set up, so we're a little low on resources.
Harry finishes bandaging her wounds with quick, practiced motions, then releases her and steps back, giving her space.
Sibilla once again crouches silently in the corner, listening attentively.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: I ******* told her to get her ass back already and quit loitering around Eastside! What's the damn point of guarding that chump change? She's got it but won't spend it, won't even open her mouth—just sitting there scared out of her mind every day. For what?!

speaker: Harry
content: For that if something happens to you, at least she can bail you out as the big-shot stock market guru. But otherwise? Just for that stunt you pulled protesting at the mine, Nirvana would've locked you up until you died.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: I-I was there to expose their damn conspiracy! You think their fancy Great Expo and stock market tricks are legit? Their plot to grab the mine is right in my face! How the hell can Parfait even stand dealing with those snakes? Doesn't it make her sick?!

speaker: Harry
content: You really think so? I've always thought Parfait's playing the long game. I mean, let's be real—money runs DisCity now, no matter how you slice it. Gotta know your enemy if you wanna come out on top.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Hold up... those guys chasing us earlier... were they after Parfait or that woman? And wait, isn't Nirvana cutting some shady deal with the Fraser people to steal our mine?!

speaker: Gracelyn
content: No way, did we actually find an ally? Did Sibilla dig up some big secret or what? Parfait's bending over backward to keep her safe, so we better—

speaker: Harry
content: Yeah, yeah, Gracelyn, by all means—talk a little louder. It's not like those guys outside will hear us and bust in to murder us all or anything.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: !! You little brat...

The red-haired woman is left speechless. Despite their bickering, the air stays light—seemingly just another day in the DisCity slums. From the corner, Sibilla watches, the distance between her and the scene widening with every breath.
Until the door opens, and a black-haired woman walks in.
...Huh, who is this...?

speaker: Harry
content: <size=36>Shh... I'll explain.</size>
The two move aside and whisper something to each other, then quickly return. The woman's gaze has visibly softened.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: So you're Parfait's friend. You look like you've had a rough time... But don't worry, you're safe here. This place will keep you protected.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: Let me make you something to eat. You can rest properly once you've had some food.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Thank you.
Sibilla's gaze follows the black-haired woman. The pendant hanging from her wrist... is undoubtedly made of Aurum Secretum.
A sudden tug at Sibilla's clothes jerks her back to reality, tearing her from her daze. She glances down—a boy stares up at her, his face smeared with vibrant paint.

speaker: Allen
content: Who are you staring at, ma'am?

speaker: Ashley
content: Are you an Outlander? Did Parfait bring you back here?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Huh? Yeah... I am.
The two children exchange a smile.

speaker: Ashley
content: Could you help us with something? It's...
Rising onto her toes, she leans close and whispers something into Sibilla's ear...
[Scene Change]
A few minutes later.
Dirty water seeps from the ventilation ducts, plink-plonking into a metal bucket. Sibilla lifts the bulletproof blanket serving as a door curtain, and the aroma of hot food immediately greets her.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: Go ahead and try some. This budget curry is actually a specialty from the Drifter Camp. Just add a little water, and it has a surprisingly nice flavor.
The black-haired woman in a dark apron ladles a spoonful of curry over rice, then passes the plate to her fellow Outlander, a stranger she's never met.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Thank you. I'm Sibilla. May I ask what your name is?

speaker: Sable
content: You can call me "Sable."
Sibilla nods, taking a small taste of the curry as she searches for the right words to start a conversation. Then, an idea strikes her.

speaker: Sibilla
content: It's really good. It doesn't taste like something from DisCity. Where did you learn to make it?

speaker: Sable
content: I don't remember anymore. My body just naturally knows what to do.
She smiles.

speaker: Sable
content: This Drifter Camp curry was originally a family recipe from an Outland physician, but to say it's not from DisCity, I doubt you know DisCity food that well.
Sibilla's attempt at small talk lands like a stone. Awkwardly, she scratches her head.

speaker: Sable
content: Did the kids send you?

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Yeah.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Sibilla
content: Why it has to be me...?

speaker: Ashley
content: Because Parfait brought back both of you!

speaker: Ashley
content: When Sable was brought here, she also had wounds all over. We keep asking Parfait about her, but she won't tell us anything! We don't know where Sable's from, or how long she'll stay, or if she has any family or friends. She's being so sneaky about it!

speaker: Allen
content: But I just had a great idea! Since you were both brought back by Parfait all injured, maybe Sable is also an Outlander like you? Maybe you two will have more to talk about!

speaker: Ashley
content: I was just... thinking... what if she leaves DisCity and goes home someday? Not that she shouldn't go home! It's just... um... I'd miss her a lot.

speaker: Allen
content: We haven't talked to her about this yet! A-anyway... can you ask her first? Pleeease? You'll help, right?
Sibilla meets the children's gazes—hope and anxiety shimmering in their eyes—and finally nods. No matter where she is, she can never say no to children.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Alright, I'll help you.
[Exit Flashback]
After hearing her words, "Sable" breaks into a smile.

speaker: Sable
content: Heh, they're probably worried that if I leave, no one will cook for them anymore.

speaker: Sable
content: Syndicate is slowly rebuilding now, and with many parents working outside the home, those children have been left in my care. I'm happy to help—it's my way of thanking everyone for taking me in so kindly.

speaker: Sable
content: They really don't need to worry. I'm not going anywhere.

speaker: Sable
content: I can't even remember things from three months ago anymore.
Sibilla is stunned at those words.

speaker: Sable
content: Parfait says it's nothing serious, and she's helping me find a doctor to look into it. I'm very grateful to her. Being with the children... it puts me at ease. They always make me feel like I'm so close to remembering something—like that happiness about something important is just out of reach.

speaker: Sable
content: ...But every night, after having the same dream, everything slips away from me again.
Sable turns off the stove and casts her eyes downward.

speaker: Sable
content: In my dreams, I'm always walking in the rain. Through the downpour, I can almost see something, hear someone calling. I want to chase after it, to grasp it. It could be my homeland, my name, my love, my purpose, or just... something I simply cannot let go.

speaker: Sable
content: ...But in the dream, the heavy rain washes it all away—dissolves it until there's nothing left. It's like the burden I've carried for over a decade, the weight etched into my bones... it's just gone. Ripped from me without warning. And all I can do is stand there, watching it disappear through the curtain of rain.

speaker: Sable
content: By the time I wake up, the rain has stopped. Sunlight's coming through, but I can't remember anything anymore.
Sibilla's lips part, but no words come. Her eyes are fixated on the chain bracelet on "Sable's" wrist.
—Aurum Secretum. It's the excessive resonance of Aurum Secretum. She's one of Fraser's people, and worse—she's someone Fraser bled dry, left hollow. How can she even speak these words aloud?

speaker: Sable
content: ...DisCity may not be my homeland, but I don't have anywhere else to go back to...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Don't have anywhere else to go back to...

The woman's words thud in Sibilla's chest, stirring a dull, resonant echo. For the first time, the urge to speak swells in her throat, but before she can, a ragged sob cuts through the silence behind her.

speaker: Ashley
content: Sob... Sable, don't be sad. We'll stay with you. We'll help you remember and take you home...

speaker: Allen
content: Even if you do go back, don't forget about us. Come back to visit us when you have time. We'll miss you...
Sable panics, rushing forward to pull the two children into her arms. Their faces are streaked with tears while they've been eavesdropping.

speaker: Sable
content: Oh my, this is... I'm not going anywhere. I'm staying right here.

speaker: Sable
content: With all of you here, I already have a new home. Shhh, it's okay. Don't cry...
She is surely unaware of her own expression. Animated, warm, alive. This is not the face of one who has lost their homeland. Given time, her soul will find solace here.
As if to add fuel to the fire, the door curtain is suddenly thrown open.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Geez, what in the world? Why is everyone crying??

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Hey, Outland lady, why are your eyes all red too? What's up with that?

speaker: Gracelyn
content: ...PARFAIT, why the **** are you here?!!!
She drags Parfait through the window, and the room erupts into chaos.

speaker: Parfait
content: Hmgh... please, be gentle! Let's not ruin this touching moment with violence. That actually hurts—

speaker: Gracelyn
content: The hell are you doing?! Didn't I just tell you to go back to the other side?! Sneaking in and outta the slums at a time like this... What if someone catches you?!!!

speaker: Parfait
content: Ahem, elegant, be elegant! I've already checked outside. Everything's fine. No pursuers, no prying reporters, not a single suspicious soul in sight. Just let me relax a bit.

speaker: Parfait
content: Since everyone's feeling a bit gloomy, let's brighten the mood! Try this popular mood-lifting remedy from Eastside—the big streamer Thalia's go-to recommendation and my personal taste test approval: a premium blend cooler!
She pulls out a glass bottle with a uniquely shaped body. Just then, footsteps sound behind her as someone walks into the room.

speaker: Harry
content: Shh... keep it down! That gimmicky fancy drink is a no-go with Gracelyn. The fancier it is, the more she can't stand it. Nothing grinds her gears like rich people acting all high and mighty.

speaker: Parfait
content: Don't worry.

Parfait hurls sparkling juice and ice into a jug, cuts a lemon in half, and squeezes it with a deft twist of her wrist. A splash of ginger juice follows. She shakes it well, then pours the drink in one smooth motion, raising the glass high like a trophy.

speaker: Parfait
content: Ta-da! Presenting Parfait's budget special blend, crafted for under fifty DisCoins a glass, but delivering every bit of the joy. It's the magic of a gentle buzz, a moment that belongs only to you.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: HUH?! It's not the damn money I hate—it's your punch-worthy act! Flaunting, wasting, showing off like some high-and-mighty snob! I'm not going to touch it. Never—OWWW!

speaker: Parfait
content: Even if it's just ginger juice mixed with fruit sugar, one should approach it with unhurried enjoyment and a mindset that savors life.
Gracelyn opens her mouth to argue, but the children—their tears already forgotten—bounce past her, teeming with excitement.

speaker: Ashley & Allen
content: Yay!! Yummy drinks!!
[Everyone's stuffed and sprawled out.]

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Tch, all this just to jack those rich pricks' bougie-ass style. The hell's so special about some slinging ginger juice in some overpriced bottle?! Hic! This ain't even a damn drink—what, Eastsiders actually—hic!—guzzle this stuff? Ugh... my stomach's so gassy...

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Huff... Stop hanging out with those guys. Come back to Syndicate...

speaker: Harry
content: You say you don't want it, but you can't stop drinking. Let's be real, you love this stuff.

speaker: Harry
content: Sorry we can't treat you to something nicer, Sibilla. We're just making do with cheap stuff for now, but just wait. Next time you visit, this place is gonna blow your mind!
The little girl also crawls over.

speaker: Ashley
content: This fruit candy is super cheap... I got it from trading with the Homeless. Will you think it's yucky, Sibilla...

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Of course I won't. Thank you for your gift.
The girl flashes a bright grin, then pulls out another candy and presses it into Sibilla's palm.

speaker: Ashley
content: Here's another one for you! Thank you for talking so nice with Sable!

As hard candies are dropped into the ginger juice, a dozen hands around the tin table suddenly raise their glasses in unison. The thunderous cheers that follow send a resonant hum trembling through the rusty roof.
Sibilla imitates the others, pressing her fruit candy to the bottom of her glass. Sparkling bubbles swarm around it, sending the little candy dancing up and down in the fizz.
Until someone grabs her hand and pulls it upward.

speaker: Parfait
content: Come on, it's all about the ritual. Cheers—

speaker: Everyone
content: Cheers!

As laughter and banter swirl around her, Sibilla feels a hazy sense of déjà vu, as if such joy belonged to another life. The weight of a glass in her hand is familiar; the chorus of laughter is distant yet remembered.
Even that piece of fruit candy brings back a moment long past, a taste unforgettable in her lifetime.
She is grateful for her luck, grateful that kindness still exists in this world, that DisCity and Furor, despite everything, still hold something in common. She should be laughing with them...
But in the end, Sibilla only murmurs a hollow reply before lowering her head.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Ch-cheers...

Morning light finds Sibilla blinking awake. Parfait is already gone, the children sent home, and only Harry's scribbled note remains—he went out to work. Gracelyn lies sprawled out in a messy slumber.
Sunlight pours through the open window, carrying the sharp trill of birdsong. Still half-caught in the remnants of her own dreams, Sibilla reaches for the television, groggily turning it on.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Through our ongoing collaborative efforts, DisCity and Fraser have successfully overcome numerous longstanding barriers between us. We're now pleased to announce an expansion of our partnership across economic development, technological exchange, and security intelligence sharing.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Especially targeting the Outland extremists who have recently emerged to disrupt DisCity's peace.

speaker: Adelaide
content: They operate under clever disguises—the Great Expo personnel, merchant caravans, and even Outland refugees—all to infiltrate DisCity, using a calculated blend of truth and lies to cultivate sympathy and trust. Yet behind this facade, they've been conspiring with Underground extremists, secretly plotting destruction...
[Horo's Photo Displayed]

speaker: Adelaide
content: I'm pleased to report we've fostered mutual trust with the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. Critical intelligence on Underground infiltration has been shared, and Chief ${PlayerName} has provided invaluable combat experience. This partnership will continue to deepen moving forward.

speaker: Adelaide
content: As for those dangerous Outland elements hiding within DisCity...

speaker: Adelaide
content: We are determined to locate and address every one of them. In the meantime, we kindly request all citizens to come forward with any relevant information. For immediate reporting, please contact...

speaker: Sibilla
content: No... that's not true... He's lying!!
Sibilla abruptly stands up, disregarding any threat of pursuit or assassination, and bolts out of the dingy alley in a blind panic.
[The Great Expo Entrance]
In a secluded corner of the plaza, Thalia stretches her arms and rubs her stiff shoulders.

speaker: Thalia
content: Yawn... Day 9! Just hang in there, it's almost over!

speaker: Thalia
content: The viewer count... still a few more to go. Should I switch to Parfait's dinner party tomorrow, or stick with the closing ceremony?

speaker: Thalia
content: Looks like the Outland Expo just can't keep up with Nirvana's market boom for viewer attention... I'll need something more viral to get the sales going... Huh?
As she murmurs, Thalia's sharp gaze snaps to a sudden commotion in the plaza. Muscle memory takes over—her fingers flick the camera on before she even thinks.

speaker: Thalia
content: What's going on over there?
[Scene Change]
An Outlander stumbles into the center of the plaza, breathless and disheveled. The crowd recoils, their instinctive retreat carving an accidental stage around her.

Her chest heaves in raging emotions, her teeth gritted as she fights for control. Bloodshot eyes rake the onlookers—accusing, desperate. Finally, Sibilla speaks, trembling as she straightens up under the weight of countless stares. She forces the Disian words out with her best efforts, each syllable deliberate, yet some still twist defiantly on her tongue.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I am... Sibilla, an inspector of Furor. I've come to expose Fraser's lies... and denounce their crimes!
However, her words hang in the air, met first with a heavy silence, then scattered murmurs rippling through the crowd.

speaker: Passerby
content: Furor? What place is that? Never even heard of it.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Fraser has been lying from the start. The Aurum Secretum mining sites must be built in the most dangerous calamity zones, but instead of taking the risks themselves, they tricked my people into going in their place.

speaker: Sibilla
content: We built mining sites and research facilities, protecting their researchers, even though we had no Hypercubes to protect ourselves. We trusted them. But Fraser never warned us that the Aurum Secretum would have devastating effects. The Furorians' bodies slowly deteriorated, our numbers dwindling until, in the end, people died still believing in them.

speaker: Sibilla
content: But that's not all. Fraser has taken complete control over Hypercube trade, stockpiled resources, and extorted every village—all while lying to our faces and pinning the blame on DisCity. They've been fueling hatred in the Farland Alliance, turning people against DisCity. Because the more we despise them, the more we depend on Fraser, and the tighter their grip on us becomes.

speaker: Sibilla
content: There have also been forbidden experiments and brainwashed extremists. They take our children. They hunt down anyone who knows too much. I barely escaped... and I'm the only one who made it here. All I want is to tell you the truth, and...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Please, help us, stop those people! Please save Furor!

speaker: Passerby A
content: Don't touch me! You dirty hag... What gibberish are you speaking?
She's shoved to the ground, then a shoe slams into her side, deliberate and cruel.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Huh?
Sibilla stumbles unsteadily to her feet. She wonders if she didn't explain herself properly. Was something unclear? Was her accent too heavy? Her vision blurs as her head begins to buzz.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Was I unclear somehow...? Th-then I'll say it one more time...
This time, the audience offers their answer before she makes a sound.

speaker: Passerby B
content: An Outlander? Heh... What a filthy beggar.
The crowd stirs back to life. Most have already pieced together the situation, drawn their conclusions, and moved on. They quicken their steps as they pass Sibilla, veering wide to avoid her.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Ah... no... I'm not lying, please... just listen to me...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Please help us. I don't want money... Just help me spread the word, or even just telling more people would help...
Someone has noticed her at last. Several cameras now point in her direction.

speaker: Passerby B
content: Pfft, why'd you stop the act? At least be professional with your sob story. Go on, keep it up.

speaker: Passerby B
content: You want eyes on you? At least have a pretty face. Pathetic. We've seen dozens like you this week.
These hecklers attract attention better than she does. She's quickly becoming nothing but a public spectacle. How can she make them understand? How can she make them care?
...Would it draw more attention if those Fraser people came to kill her? Sibilla trembles as she pushes herself upright, then erupts into frantic shouts.

speaker: Sibilla
content: You Campbells!! Haven't you been trying to kill me all along? Come on then! I'm right here! Come and kill me!!

speaker: Sibilla
content: Let everyone see what you've done to Furor! What you've done to us!! Come on, show yourselves!!
She screams until her voice grows hoarse, but no one responds.

Sibilla realizes, with a sinking clarity, why no one has tried to kill her all this time. Fraser already knows the truth—she doesn't need to be silenced because no one would ever listen. Not DisCity, not Fraser, not a soul.

Just as despair threatens to swallow her whole, someone roughly grabs her by the shoulder. Has someone finally heard her? Her gaze snaps up to a uniformed figure. A public official? Has someone actually taken her seriously?!

Sibilla's fingers twist into the fabric of the stranger's uniform, a silent plea. The answer comes not in words, but in a crushing blow to her skull. Pain erupts, spinning the world into a blur. Through the dizzying haze, she barely catches the sheriff's face—his features twisted in pure disgust.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Quiet! This is the Great Expo! You've already been reported for causing a disturbance and spreading panic. Still looking for trouble? Move it!
Sibilla is yanked up by her collar and, still dazed from the blow, dragged across the plaza. The sheriff shoves her into the waiting transport and slams the door shut.
From a safe distance, Thalia watches in silence, her camera heavy in her grip. The Outlander's desperation coils around her, awakening a long-dormant compassion.

speaker: Thalia
content: Sigh...

Thalia sighs softly, subtly bending the crowd's focus toward Sibilla with her power. More and more people at the scene start to notice what's happening, yet the viewership of her stream stubbornly refuses to climb.

speaker: Thalia
content: If they're throttling the stream, there's nothing more I can do for you.

speaker: Thalia
content: Poor thing... but playing the victim card just doesn't work in DisCity.
She ends her stream and opens her terminal, thinking about who she could contact to help take the Outlander away, only to discover Sibilla is already gone.

By the time Sibilla regains her senses, the vehicle has already driven far from the plaza. She staggers upright and hurls herself toward the narrow barred window that cages her from the driver's compartment. Her voice tears through the iron grate.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Are you arresting me? That's great! Thank you for taking me in. Just get me to that Bureau, let me see that person. I'll do anything!

speaker: Sibilla
content: Can you understand what I'm saying? I—

speaker: Sheriff
content: Screw off! Who's got time for beggar trash like you?

speaker: Sheriff
content: They hold one Great Expo and thousands of filthy Outland beggars show up. The Outland Affairs Bureau should just drag the lot of you out to WhiteSands and let the worms feast!

speaker: Sheriff
content: Open your mouth again and I'll shoot you—Ugh!
His verbal abuse is cut short by a violent crash as a tremendous force slams directly into the driver's side, sending the entire vehicle flying through the air.

Inside the twisted carcass of the ruptured vehicle, the sheriff's head lolls to one side, lifeless. An ominous burning stench begins to flood the car as Sibilla struggles to claw her way across the floor, desperately reaching her hand toward the outside.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Cough...
In the crimson dusk, she spots two familiar silhouettes.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Arienna... Adriel...
Just as how they saved her back then, the two crouch down and reach toward Sibilla—then drive a knife through the back of her hand.

speaker: Arienna
content: ...So naive, Sibilla. Did you really think they'd help? DisCity doesn't care. They don't understand our suffering—they can't even imagine it.

speaker: Arienna
content: People living in a different world simply cannot see our pain.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...I know. I knew it all along...

speaker: Sibilla
content: When I was with them, I realized... we're from completely different worlds...
She loves that street they call a "slum." It has electricity, running water, and beds where sleep comes soundly behind a locked door.
No calamity alarms shatter the night. No families flee in panic, leaving lifetimes of labor behind.
When Harry felt ashamed of the "cheap candy" he offered, Sibilla didn't dare tell him... that such treats were most treasured back in her homeland.

In the Outlands, only the bravest and most diligent children can earn such rare, sweet rewards. The joy on the children's faces as they cradle candy in their palms is Sibilla's most cherished memory. Yet here, such things are apparently embarrassing to offer.

Parfait must hide her origins. DisCity sneers at "drifters" from the slums. People are embarrassed to offer cheap candy to guests. So... who would spare a second glance at someone as poor as her? Is it foolish to keep pursuing that Chief, hoping against hope?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Fraser... cares even less if we live or die.

speaker: Sibilla
content: So do you.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I've reached out to everyone I could find, and this isn't the first time I've been rejected...

speaker: Sibilla
content: If the people of DisCity won't help me, then I'll find someone who will, anywhere I have to go. It doesn't matter how many times I get turned away. I won't stop until someone finally listens... until someone actually cares enough to do something.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I won't give up. If Fraser wants to shut me up, they'll have to kill me first. I'm not stopping.

speaker: Arienna
content: ...I see.
Arienna stands up and brings her weapon to Sibilla's throat.

speaker: Arienna
content: Even if Fraser says you're worthless... even if part of me wishes you could live... you're too dangerous. You have to go.

speaker: Arienna
content: We really are the same, you and us. Neither of us has a choice.

speaker: Adriel
content: Die, traitor!
BOOM—Several steel bars pierce through the assassin's chest.

speaker: Arienna
content: Adriel!! Ugh—!

speaker: Sibilla
content: Arienna!!
[War Entrance]

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...It's you... the one from DisCity...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Does it have to be this way... To you, are Outlanders just... meant to die?

Several gunshots crack through the air, cutting her off mid-sentence. A man lunges from behind the ruins—one hand clutching a terminal playing Thalia's livestream, the other gripping a crude, makeshift gun. More people follow, stepping in front of Sibilla to form a shield.

speaker: Harry
content: Sibilla!!

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Who the **** are you?!! Killing people in broad daylight—you got no respect for the law?! Syndicate is no longer a place for ******* like you to run wild! Back the hell off! BACK OFF!

speaker: Gracelyn
content: I've called the cops!! I've already called the cops!!!
She snatches up a steel pipe and swings at the masked man with furious, unrelenting force, each blow producing metallic clangs through the air.

speaker: Harry
content: Who are you? Stay back! You'll regret messing with Syndicans!

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...If you're going to hide her, do it right.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Don't let her run away and get herself killed again.
He turns and walks away. After a long silence, Sibilla hears a whimper.

speaker: Arienna
content: Cough cough... Cough... Sob...
She rushes over to Arienna.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Hold on, just hold on! We're going to save you. I—
Before she can finish, Arienna suddenly grabs her by the collar.

speaker: Arienna
content: ...I get it... I really do... We're the same... So please, I beg you, don't ruin...

speaker: Arienna
content: Fraser is our only... ho... pe...
Her hand finally falls limp.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Please... no... wake up...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Sob... AAAAHHHHH!!!

speaker: Sable
content: What happened? This is...!!

Sable rushes to the scene, only to stumble upon a grisly tableau of blood and chaos. For a heartbeat, she freezes, stunned. But just as swiftly, she steels herself. With practiced hands, she takes out some fabric and starts tending to Sibilla's wounds.

speaker: Sable
content: I've stopped the bleeding for now, but we need to move her quick. She can't stay here—this is too much for her to take.

speaker: Sable
content: The safe house might be blown already. We need to go somewhere else.

speaker: Sable
content: Any news from Parfait?
Her companions shake their heads. They've been trying to reach Parfait through their network, but her terminal stays busy—jammed, perhaps, by interference.
Has she seen Thalia's stream? Does she know what has happened to Sibilla?

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Sibilla, pull yourself together... Let's head back first.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Right now, keeping you safe is the most important thing.
On the eve of Parfait's Dinner Party, the investment guru makes her entrance. The servants discreetly usher away extraneous personnel, leaving her alone in the cavernous banquet hall.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Earlier today, an Outland extremist disrupted the peace at the Great Expo. During their arrest and subsequent transport, their associates launched an attack on the escort vehicle, tragically claiming the life of a sheriff in the line of duty. We are deeply saddened by this profound loss, but we will not waver in our resolve.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Both Fraser and DisCity have implemented enhanced security protocols for the Expo. Every precaution has been taken to ensure tomorrow's closing ceremony proceeds without incident...
Before her rests an expensive glass of whiskey, a meticulously plated dinner menu, a neat stack of asset reports, and... several sticks of incense. Unlit, yet somehow, they begin to smolder.
Through the swirling smoke, Parfait can faintly hear the voices of her "friends."

- Was Fraser behind the Expo incident? If the 9th Agency gets involved, it could derail our plan. We can't risk losing those resources and assets from the Farland Alliance. - Oh, it's just a minor hiccup, nothing to worry about! My uncle already talked to the Outland Affairs Bureau, and Fraser's playing nice. They're basically handing us everything on the extremists—full life stories and all. - Is the opposition to the new mine handled? Without that big public fight, Parfait's advocacy alone might not be enough to sway DisCity's sharper minds. - We need more of our people in the Executive Committee. Get our actors moving too. They're not being paid to do nothing.

- Speaking of actors, let's talk about something more pleasant. None of this is really a big deal. I heard Parfait was at that dancer's performance too. She didn't get to buy her? - I had my eye on that dancer too. Too bad that Chief got to take her away—again. - Don't worry, we'll get another chance. Once I bring her back, we can set up a private show with that woman. Maybe even slip the Chief a free ticket.

- The Farland Alliance has been hit hard lately, calamity after calamity. They're desperate for Hypercubes, which means we can push our purchase prices way down. - You're absolutely right. Let's jump on this and make a killing. - Those pathetic little city-states are too scattered. Otherwise, we wouldn't even need Fraser's involvement.
The glass shivers—and inside, wreathed in rippling amber, a gaunt figure takes shape.

speaker: Parfait
content: Your health still worries me. I found some curious Outland remedies at the Expo. Care to try? ...No promises, of course.

speaker: Sillage
content: Heh, thanks. Chatting with you is always such a delight.

speaker: Sillage
content: You didn't attend the meeting today. Did something happen? Many people were lining up to speak with you.

speaker: Sillage
content: Back to your home in the slums again?

speaker: Parfait
content: Yeah. Everything about "Parfait Medici" can be gloriously displayed in public, but those memories of just "Parfait" have to stay locked away in that little house, never to be found out. And I have to visit from time to time to make sure they're still safe.

speaker: Sillage
content: Heh, why not just throw it all away? You've been so careful about hiding your identity, yet you keep your biggest risk around—can't bring yourself to let go of that old place.

speaker: Sillage
content: To have your "elegant life," you always have to give something up, you know.

speaker: Parfait
content: Well, I am the stock market guru, after all. A touch of greed is only natural. But don't worry, I haven't slacked off. In fact, after a few rounds of promotion, Nirvana stock has hit another all-time high. I'm sure people in the organization are more than pleased with their returns.
Sillage gives a soft laugh.

speaker: Sillage
content: By the way, someone's lit the incense asking for our help. A certain representative from Fraser. He said...

speaker: Sillage
content: A rat has escaped into DisCity, an inconvenience that could disrupt his plans. He's hoping to use the Sillage Society's hand to track it down.

speaker: Sillage
content: Relax, I never promised we'd help him. Last time when you went all around WhiteSands and still brought that spy butler back to hide, I didn't say anything, did I? I've never been fond of "Campbell" anyway. As for cooperation... let's just do the bare minimum and call it a day.

speaker: Sillage
content: Honestly, the only thing worth looking forward to lately is your dinner party tomorrow. So many of our friends will be there, after all.
The woman's voice drifts softly from the wine glass.

speaker: Sillage
content: You really are something else, Parfait. You have this way of winning people over without even trying. I like that about you, and that's exactly why I gave you the power, to let you more freely command "credit."

speaker: Sillage
content: But you know how it is—"trust" is fragile. Once lost, it's very difficult to gain back.

speaker: Sillage
content: Tomorrow's dinner party... You won't let me down. I trust you.

speaker: Parfait
content: Of course. At the dinner party, everyone will have their fill of delights.
The incense burns down to its final ember. Ethereal smoke, once lingering in the air, thins to nothing. And in the wine glass before her, Parfait's own face reappears.
At her dinner party, everything has a price tag—resources, technology, suffering, and war.
How much is this face, this identity worth now?
If its value were to plummet, how useful could it still be?
She sets down the wine glass, falling silent.

speaker: Parfait
content: Is it the member who takes on missions you trust...

speaker: Parfait
content: Or the stock market guru of DisCity...?
Having reached a conclusion, she picks up the wine glass and drains it in a single gulp.
Though at 300,000 DisCoins a glass, it truly pales in comparison to those homemade drinks shared with friends from a few nights ago—warm with laughter and barely 100 DisCoins apiece.
In the distance, a luxury car brazenly drives against traffic in broad daylight, executing one final stylish drift before coming to a stop at the hotel entrance.
[Luxury Hotel]
This enigmatic woman flouts DisCity's rules without hesitation, carving her own path in all things, yet surprisingly, she's chosen to meet at a very public place.

speaker: Catherine
content: I hear this is where they host the famous "Parfait's Dinner Party," so the food has to be good. Order whatever you want. My treat.

speaker: Catherine
content: But that companion of yours hiding at the table behind us can pay for himself, since he wouldn't even do us the honor of joining us.

Of course he won't join you—that's an agent of the 9th Agency here to secretly ensure your safety. The woman before you seems to know this all too well, and might have even noticed Schorl hidden in your coat pocket.
After all, she has deliberately instructed the server to take your coat away, claiming it was for some "dinner etiquette."

speaker: Catherine
content: Name's Catherine. I'm usually on the road for my business, so DisCity visits are rare for me. I'd like to actually stay and look around this time.

speaker: Catherine
content: How's that gift I gave you? I mean, that girl who dances with the blades.
For a moment, you pause and study her expression. Her eyes hold no ill intent, just an offhanded interest.

The listening device on you is still active. 9th hasn't sent over her identity details yet, but there's been no warning from his side either. You're clear to keep talking—this will also help the agents gather intel.
Since she was the original "buyer," you figure Catherine must be curious about Jasmine's situation. You describe her current condition briefly, without going into much detail.

speaker: Catherine
content: I see... a perfect "victim." She's the reason why you're upset? Hmm... looks like the young generation has barely seen war these days.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...Heh, you're surprisingly bad at hiding your emotions. She's the reason why you're upset?
You ramble on while she just watches you in silence. Finally, she gives a soft laugh, as if she sees right through you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why did you buy her, only to give her to me?

speaker: Catherine
content: I was only interested in her blades. Since you seemed to care about her as a person, I just went along with what worked for everyone.

speaker: Catherine
content: Are those blades at the FAC now? I'll go pick them up later.

speaker: Catherine
content: Let's talk more about that girl. She's the reason why you're upset? Looks like the young generation has barely seen war these days.

speaker: Catherine
content: You can talk to me about it. I've seen war myself.

speaker: Catherine
content: My family's been in arms for generations. We used to have connections with the former DisCity military and made our fortune through it—war has always been good business. When I caught wind of tension at the Great Expo, I came to see where the opportunities lie. Same as always.

speaker: Catherine
content: If tensions between DisCity and Fraser escalate, I could make another fortune and treat you to dinner a few times.

speaker: Catherine
content: Just giving an example—nothing special, just how things usually go.
She places cash on the table and rises to her feet.

speaker: Catherine
content: I can see you've lost your appetite. The food here is mediocre anyway. Let's go somewhere else.
You glance back at your agent companion, who signals for you to follow her.
She guides you out of the hotel and toward the sleek luxury sports car parked by the curb. All eyes turn to her, seemingly captivated by her commanding presence.
You slide into the car as planned and instinctively glance at the rearview mirror. The 9th Agency's agent should be tailing you to keep you safe.

Before you can react, the woman slams her foot on the accelerator, and the car lurches forward with a surge of speed. In the rearview mirror, 9th's disguised vehicle shrinks into the distance—utterly immobilized, powerless to give chase.

speaker: Option
options: What in the world are you up to?

speaker: Catherine
content: Just shaking off a few tails so we can have some privacy. It's not like I'm kidnapping you or anything—relax.

speaker: Catherine
content: We're on a main road with people all around. What's there to be afraid of? Just don't make a scene or I'll end up with a ticket.
She's been driving against traffic in broad daylight and making illegal stops. Since when does she care about DisCity's rules or traffic tickets?
You check your communication terminal—no messages from the agent. Meanwhile, Schorl lies silent in your pocket, completely unresponsive.

It seems she's not just an arms dealer, and her ties to DisCity go deeper than you expected. In fact, she might be a high-ranking official working undercover. You wonder if this is some new kind of evaluation test.

speaker: Catherine
content: The fight hasn't even started, and you're already choking for air. Lighten up, you can't run from what's coming anyway.

speaker: Catherine
content: As long as this city-state remains built on Hypercubes, war is unavoidable. Doesn't matter who fires the first shot or what flag they wave. This place will always be ground zero. You can hate war all you want, but that won't stop it. Time to wake up.

speaker: Catherine
content: Know your place, adapt to survive, then do whatever it takes to achieve your goals—whether they're for war or peace.

speaker: Catherine
content: This conversation can wait. For now, just focus on enjoying the moment while you can.

She glides through DisCity's streets with practiced ease, the car slicing through the night unhindered. Neon reflections streak across her glasses, while the windshield paints itself in the city's ever-shifting hues. For a moment, the world outside blurs into a dream, the vehicle adrift in a river of hues.

Catherine steers with one hand, the other stretched out the window—fingers splayed as if to catch the rushing wind and the streaking lights. A faint smile plays at the corner of her lips, etched by the flickering shadows. Only then do you realize the speedometer has surged past 300.
Without warning, a colossal shadow surges across your path. Tires shriek against the road as the car lurches violently, nearly causing you to lose your dinner.

speaker: Catherine
content: DisCity's peace has its charms...

She's been driving at breakneck speed, and though it feels like barely any time has passed, you suddenly find yourself at the MBCC. That violent drift just now was because you nearly crashed into the Bureau's exterior wall.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Yeah.
Your voice trembles uncontrollably as she opens the door, disengages all the security locks, and lets you out of the car.

speaker: Catherine
content: Time to get out, sir. Get some rest.
female_content: Time to get out, miss. Get some rest.

content: That's... it? No kidnapping, no coercion, no elaborate schemes—not even some kind of evaluation like you suspected.
After days of unrelenting tension, these fleeting hours of unexpected calm feel surreal, almost deceptive. You stare at her, utterly bewildered.

speaker: Option
options: ...So what do you really want from me?

speaker: Catherine
content: Didn't I already tell you?

speaker: Catherine
content: You looked like you needed air. So I drove. Good night.

You've barely taken two steps when your comm device buzzes with a flurry of notifications. The signal is back—your agent companion wasn't silent after all. The messages had been blocked by the person behind you.

speaker: Catherine
content: Hahaha!

You watch her drive away, biting back the dozen retorts burning on your tongue. At least the dinner was decent. And she did give you a ride home. Pulling your coat tighter against the chill, you turn and start walking back.
When you instinctively slide your hand into your pocket, your fingers touch something unexpected. You're certain it wasn't there when you left the Bureau today.

speaker: %u
content: This is... an invitation?
You quickly grasp the meaning behind this gesture, tuck away the envelop, and hurry back to the Bureau.

speaker: %u
content: Get me the 9th Agency on the line, and everyone at the City-State Security Bureau. Also schedule an internal meeting here at the Bureau. And...

speaker: %u
content: Is Elvira here? I need to speak with her.
At least she did make a fair point.

speaker: Catherine
content: Know your place, adapt to survive, then do whatever it takes to achieve your goals—whether they're for war or peace.
[Scene Change] Hospital
Max King walks down this hallway once again, but he never expected to find two people—who shouldn't be here—standing outside the room.

speaker: Max King
content: What are you doing here?! Tell me no one followed you. Are you out of your mind?

speaker: Hecate
content: Nightmare is keeping watch. If anyone comes, it will alert us.

speaker: Elvira
content: If you, the Speaker, can slip in here alone without drawing attention, then I won't be noticed either.

He should have laughed it off, deflected with a joke, sent them on their way—but he doesn't have the energy anymore. His tie strangles him, a noose disguised as silk. Max King tugs at it, even the motion draining what little strength he has left.
With a sigh, he ignores the two kids and walks on by himself.

speaker: Max King
content: That Chief sent you here, didn't he? Stop with all this sneaking around. It'll cause trouble if someone catches you. Tell him to make a proper appointment.
female_content: That Chief sent you here, didn't she? Stop with all this sneaking around. It'll cause trouble if someone catches you. Tell her to make a proper appointment.

speaker: Max King
content: But best to lay low for now. If you're trying to help the West District, don't draw attention. Too many eyes are watching.

speaker: Elvira
content: ${PlayerName}'s friend in the West District says you're the one who needs help. You're trying your best to deal with them carefully, but you don't know who you can trust.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Haha, you've got it all wrong. I'm just trying to keep my seat secure. My position is very fragile, so I have no choice but to fight with everything I've got.

speaker: Max King
content: Or... is the West District actually trying to win me over now? They want a puppet Speaker?

speaker: Max King
content: What's in it for you?

speaker: Elvira
content: ...I don't know. But ${PlayerName} said if we found you here, we could talk to you.

speaker: Elvira
content: He said you can be trusted when you're here.
female_content: She said you can be trusted when you're here.

speaker: Max King
content: What exactly is he trying to get at?
female_content: What exactly is she trying to get at?

speaker: Elvira
content: I know some names. What they want, the cards they're holding, and the leverage against them. I can show you the cracks in the high-ups—the ones you're not seeing.

speaker: Elvira
content: I remember every word Stewart told me. And now I'm giving you his true legacy. This is your weapon now.

speaker: Elvira
content: ${PlayerName} wants me to tell you this: Do whatever you think is right, Mr. Speaker Max King. He trusts you.
female_content: ${PlayerName} wants me to tell you this: Do whatever you think is right, Mr. Speaker Max King. She trusts you.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Trust... me?
[Scene Change]
After making all the arrangements, you send Schorl away and head alone to the Banyan special ward to visit Jasmine.
[Scene Change] A softly warm-tinted ring Bureau backdrop as Jasmine's special ward
When you enter, you find her not lying in bed. She's dragged the mattress to the floor by the simulated window, where she's curled up beneath the artificial sunlight, basking in its glow.
You approach her with soft footsteps, reaching out to comfort her with your shackles. She opens her eyes, tilts her head as she sees you, and offers a drowsy smile.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Hehe, what took you so long? I've been waiting for ages.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Work's been crazy lately. We're constantly refining the treatment plan, and it feels like we're so close to a breakthrough. I didn't want to take any breaks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How are you feeling?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Me? Oh, I feel wonderful. The voices in my head are gone, my scars don't hurt anymore... and now I even have good dreams. Is it because you've been watching over me at night?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The corruptive weapon that was making you uncomfortable has been taken away. It won't affect you anymore.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh, that's not it. I just know I'll get better as long as you're by my side. Sibilla was right—you're so strong and kind, always watching over us... and yet you never say a word about it.

speaker: Jasmine
content: But you always sneak away before I wake up, not giving me a chance to thank you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well, I need to turn in early. The Great Expo is not over yet, so I have to be there early to ensure everyone's safety.
She giggles, as if seeing through your clumsy lie but choosing not to call you out on it.

speaker: Jasmine
content: The Great Expo, huh... Well, that doesn't matter because you still came to see me today. It makes me so happy.

speaker: Jasmine
content: So, are you going to question me now? About Fraser? I don't know much, though. Everything was so confusing. They only fed me empty promises about putting me on stage to perform, but never mentioned what they were really up to.

speaker: Jasmine
content: And those Outland extremists they mentioned? I have no idea who they are either. I came near DisCity a long time ago, but even though I was right there, I just couldn't find my way in. I ended up tagging along with some desert bandits. They promised they'd take me in if I played bodyguard, but they never actually did...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh! Don't tell me you're all right about me being an idiot after all!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're not an idiot, Jasmine. You're just overly sensitive to Mania.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Think of how migrating birds lose their way in magnetic storms. The Mania field in WhiteSands is the same unpredictable, and it hits you hard.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But anyway, you've made it here.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hehe, I've been pretty lucky. The desert bandits kept me fed, and the Fraser people at least kept their promise of taking me to the Great Expo. And I met someone who was really kind. She told me you are better than anyone else in the world and would definitely make my wish come true.
She leans in closer and speaks in a hushed voice.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I still have one more wish... Chief, could you take me to the closing ceremony? It's tomorrow.

speaker: Jasmine
content: In my dreams, there's always this celebration that never finishes. I really want to see it through. The Great Expo would be perfect for that. Would you take me there? This is my only wish now. You'll help me, right? I'll repay you, I promise!

speaker: Jasmine
content: You can ask me anything. I'll do anything for you! Would you like to see me dance? My friend says I'm a great dancer, and the Fraser people say I can mesmerize anyone. I'll dance for you! Just... please take me to the closing ceremony!
Noticing your momentary hesitation, her smile wavers, replaced by a pitiful expression with watery eyes.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Is that not possible? Don't tell me you're going to lock me up and make me fight for you like those desert bandits...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I won't force you into anything, and I understand how you feel. Now, get ready for that celebration you want to finish.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Really? You promise?
She tries to throw her arms around you in excitement, but you gently hold her back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But in return, I need you to promise me one thing.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Yeah, go ahead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After the closing ceremony is over, I want you to stay with me. Let's go do something fun together.
She freezes for a moment, confused.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...What do you mean?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've always wanted to visit DisCity, right? Now that you've made it here, you can explore all around. There's so much you can do here—amazing food, fun spots, and beautiful sights. Trust me, it'll be nothing like the places you've been before.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Look how far you've come... Now you can finally try all those things you've been looking forward to. Just say the word, and I'll be right there with you.
She avoids meeting your gaze.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I... never thought about that.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I only know celebrations, nothing else. I never thought about other things, never really cared... I never thought about what would happen after the celebration.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well... how about we ask some friends for ideas? Once the closing ceremony is over, I won't have to work overtime anymore. I'll have plenty of time. Oh, right!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't you have a good friend? "Sibilla," right? We could go find her together. I'd really like to meet your friend.
She answers with silence, just as you expected.

speaker: Option
options: Let's go find your hometown together.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Don't bother with all that. I forgot about it long ago...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's alright. There has to be someone who remembers.
You pull out the information that you recently asked the 9th Agency to collect. Though the data is sparse, you notice a shift in Jasmine's expression.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I still remember that dream we shared. Your hometown was so alive back then—a bustling little village where everyone celebrated the harvest. They'd light bonfires, and the girls would make flower-woven targets. I remember parade floats rolling through the fields, carrying scarecrows, and fireworks too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your name, "Jasmine"... I'm sure it was given to you with many lovely blessings. If you can remember its meaning, that would make it easier to trace your origins.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And your dance... it's so beautiful, unlike anything I've ever seen. I'm sure if we ask around, we'll find someone who remembers it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even if your hometown is gone—even if the world has forgotten it—it still lives inside you, in every part of your life. And now, through you, it's become a part of me, too. Let's find it back together.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The war is over. Now we can look forward to the next celebration—bigger and brighter—no matter how long it takes... As long as we live, there will always be another chance.
She listens to you in silence, only whispering a response after a long while.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You're so kind to me...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Why are you being so kind to me?

speaker: Jasmine
content: You're clearly different from Sibilla, clearly from DisCity...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...But why are you nothing like all the others?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...In your eyes, what should the people of DisCity be like?

Like those who drove her away? The desert bandits who exploited her? The spectators who treated her as nothing more than a spectacle for their amusement? Or... the ruthless soldiers from her dreams who devastated everything?
Jasmine doesn't answer. Her eyelids droop—a fleeting shadow of melancholy, though for all the world she might just be a sun-warmed kitten succumbing to the drowsy contentment.
With a languid stretch, she squints her eyes and curls onto your lap, murmuring something soft and sleep-laden.
Lying across your lap, her brief melancholy fades as quickly as it came. She murmurs lazily in the golden light.

speaker: Jasmine
content: In DisCity, the only meat I ever ate was sandworms, and they tasted awful... I want to try the amazing food you mentioned.

speaker: Jasmine
content: And... if DisCity has celebrations or fireworks, I'd like to see them too. Rain, snow... summer, autumn, winter... And if there are more good people around you, I'd like to meet them too.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I like this kind of promise... You have my word, Chief. Take me to the celebration, and I'll come back to you after it's over. Just as promised.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Once the closing ceremony ends... I'll follow you anywhere.
A warm, contented smile brightens her face.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Thank you.
You walk out of the room.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, tomorrow is the closing ceremony. Jasmine...

speaker: Option
options: Take Jasmine to the closing ceremony
Don't take Jasmine to the closing ceremony

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Make sure to completely isolate her from the contamination source—those weapons. I'll do everything possible to control the risk. The shackles should stabilize her, and if she steps out of line, I can hold her down. Besides...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's a promise.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't rule out suspicions about her, and I must keep the risk to a minimum. Leave her here, and make sure to take good care of her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...After everything is over, we can take her to a real celebration.
You gaze at her, confined within the room. Yet, in return, she offers you an innocent, joyful smile.

speaker: Jasmine
content: See you then!
[Scene Change]
Several security personnel meticulously examine the tightly sealed hazardous item—a "performance prop" confiscated from the Outlander dancer detained by MBCC.
The higher-ups require inspections every three hours with several specific metrics to check, but they haven't explained the reasoning behind this requirement.

speaker: Guard
content: They've surely got it locked down tight. After all these years, how did a weapon from ████ end up with some Outlander? No wonder FAC is so worked up. Once they classify this information, the thing will probably never see the light of day.

speaker: Guard
content: What a waste for such a weapon to just gather dust...
He sets down the items and closes the door. Behind multiple layers of security, the crimson blades flash with a deadly gleam.

June 25, N.F. 115
The World Dome
The Great Expo Closing Ceremony

speaker: Host
content: After nine extraordinary years, humanity's most magnificent gathering now approaches its triumphant conclusion, ushering in a new era of order and peace.

speaker: Host
content: Looking back, we once marched through the shadows of adversity, forged in the fires of struggle, and measured the very borders of survival with our scars.

speaker: Host
content: But those days are behind us. Though disasters threaten, and though the storm of Mania rages on—so long as humanity stands united, marching forward together, the flame of civilization will be rekindled once more!

speaker: Host
content: And now, as we stand at the culmination of this historic gathering—marking both the close of one chapter and the dawn of a new era—we prepare to welcome the Commander-in-Chief, who will deliver a momentous address and review the assembled FAC troops. The stage is set, the moment is here. Let the FAC military equipment demonstration—our grand closing ceremony—begin!

Ceremonial cannons thunder in unison as the massive FAC equipment in the main hall activates, deploying anti-Mania barriers. Rows of soldiers march in flawless lockstep down the central avenue. The spectacle serves as a show of force, meant to inspire human resolve and project DisCity's indomitable might. Even military equipment from a decade past now stands ready for future sale.

The Outland delegations sit in their exclusive viewing section, their eyes fixed on humanity's greatest source of security—weapons they've never seen before, with blue Hypercubes flashing prominently on each device. An uncharacteristic silence hangs heavy among them.

speaker: Schorl
content: It's not over yet, Chief. Stay focused.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Copy that.
You need to stay vigilant. If there's going to be an "incident," now would be the final opportunity.
Your terminal vibrates. You know the moment has come.
A gruesome image flashes on screen: a murdered person lies amidst rampant contamination, while a chilling, twisted message is scrawled in blood across the ground—

<size=55><color=#dg1f1f>TRAITORS WHO SIDE WITH DISCITY</size></color> 
<size=80><color=#dg1f1f>WILL NOT BE SPARED!!</size></color>

speaker: 9th
content: Chief! Emergency! The Fraser Ambassador has been murdered inside the embassy with a message left. We're under attack!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Same here.
Sharp screams of terror erupt from the audience.
[Inside Parfait's Room]
In the Syndicate slums, several Outland assassins dart through narrow alleys, shoving aside people in their way until they precisely locate their target designation and kick the door open.
However, their assassination target—the publicly outspoken Furor inspector Sibilla—is nowhere to be found in this safe house.

speaker: Fraser Assassin
content: She's escaped?
[Scene Change] Parfait's Dinner Party
Meanwhile, inside the Medici Hotel, DisCity's wealthy elites exchange bewildered glances under the gilded gaze of The Golden City—a sprawling, fragmented masterpiece.

The contract with Fraser is signed, the investment secured, and the announcement—poised for strategic release—is ready to send a jolt through the market. Reporters, streamers, and influencers wait outside, eager for the breaking news. But at this pivotal moment, the event's host is missing.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Why isn't Parfait here yet... Did something go wrong...

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Hello? Did you find her? Is she alright? ...What?!!
[Scene Change] Hotel Lobby (any magnificent lobby would do)

speaker: Thalia
content: What, Parfait is missing?!
Viewers flood into the livestream in an instant, with question marks and exclamation points frantically filling all the comments scrolling across the screen.

A commotion erupts throughout the lobby as waiters rush about, nervously escorting indignant VIP guests discreetly out of the building. Meanwhile, the opportunistic streamers and reporters burst into a frenzy of excitement, with wild conspiracy theories instantly running rampant.
Meanwhile, in an inconspicuous corner of the lobby, a person quietly sets down his coffee cup.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Opportunity always favors the prepared, isn't that right, Adrian?
Max King gazes at the coffee on the table, its dark surface catching a faint glimmer of golden splendor around him. Maybe Parfait's Dinner Party isn't over after all—maybe it's only just begun.
[Scene Change] Back to the closing ceremony, war flame effect

speaker: Crowd
content: Attack—! There's an attack at the Great Expo! Oh god, they're killing people!!

speaker: Crowd
content: Spies! Outland spies!! Help, hel—Aaah!!!

From the local audience seats, numerous "DisCity residents" tear off their disguises and launch their assault. Meanwhile, the FAC units that were performing on the main avenue immediately shift into combat mode. Though they aren't trained killers, their experience protecting civilians proves useful nonetheless.

speaker: FAC Commander
content: Your foresight saved us, Chief. FAC combat units are already in position—just give the order. No enemy will reach our citizens. Not on our watch.

speaker: Schorl
content: Then my priority is to ensure your safety, Chief. The FAC officers are still en route to the scene, and they have granted you temporary field command authority. Please proceed.

speaker: Option
options: Move in as planned! Take them alive!

content: The situation is swiftly brought under control. The assassins are confirmed to be not Sinner, devoid of potent weaponry. With the Fraser delegation's aid in freeing several hostages, the attackers are now cornered, their escape routes cut off.

But a creeping unease settles in your chest, the familiar kind that whispers of danger before it arrives. Instinctively, you rush to Jasmine. She's still in the car, obediently waiting, waving and smiling at you. You sigh in relief, but just as you step closer to remind her—

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, behind you!
A fresh wave of chaos erupts as something rapidly approaches you, carving a brutal path through the crowd. The air shrieks with agony, the sound of rending flesh and terror closing in.
As the victims fall one after another, you finally get a clear view of the perpetrator's frenzied face—
[Transition] Corrupted Soldier Portrait

speaker: FAC Captain
content: That's not an Outlander assassin—it's someone from the Ring Institute! But... something's off about him!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's the deal with those blades...

speaker: Security
content: Eeehahahaha!!!

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Damn it, he's completely lost it... Stop him!

The man, possessed by the deadly blades, stands with eyes wide open, pupils swallowed. His body jerks unnaturally, as if the weapon in his hands is the one controlling him, cutting down every living soul in sight. Seeing the enemy charge at you, a swarm of FAC guards rush over.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait! Stay back!

speaker: Schorl
content: A correct decision. I can only protect you, Chief.

As it speaks, Schorl rushes forward, intercepting the first strike of the dual blades meant for you. But just as Schorl prepares to counter, the "man" pivots past him, surging onward as if you were never his true target at all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jasmine!

He slashes open the vehicle holding Jasmine with a single strike. A hand extends from within. The dancer braces against his shoulder, then in one fluid motion, flips over him gracefully. Finally free, she escapes the cage that has served as both her prison and her sanctuary.
Jasmine takes in the scene, her delight unmistakable.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I warned you not to touch those blades... They're dangerous, cruel, thirsty for blood... They are DisCity's weapon, your weapon...

speaker: Jasmine
content: You look so troubled, Chief. Won't you let me help you? I'm the only one who can, after all.
[Action sequence: Jasmine subdues the guard controlled by the blades.]

You hesitate to use your shackles while the two are locked in close combat, fearing even a split second of interference might cost Jasmine her life. Sensing your hesitation, her smile brightens. Her movements are fluid, dodging his savage strikes with feline grace, weaving around him like a serpent circling an enraged bear.

In just a few swift moves, she leaps onto the monster's shoulders, locking her legs around his throat from behind. With a sharp twist, she wrenches his arms in the opposite direction, effortlessly pinning her bear-like opponent in an unbreakable hold.
The blades lose their hold on their puppet, shuddering violently as they unleash a terrifying wave of contamination.

speaker: Security
content: You... It's you...

speaker: Security
content: I'll kill you!!

speaker: Jasmine
content: Shut up! Do as I say!

With brutal efficiency, she wrenches the poor researcher's arms from his body, cutting short his agonized scream. Jasmine lets out a laugh as she pries the blades from the severed hands—their stiff fingers still clinging desperately to the hilts. Tossing the lifeless limbs aside, she now reclaims her "weapon."
The frenzied twin blades roar, then howl—struggling, trembling—until at last, like a guttering flame, they fall silent in her hands.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Haha... That's better... You're nothing but a pair of blades. Who you kill and where you strike—it all happens on my command.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Now...
She takes a deep breath, as if savoring freedom, and opens her eyes to watch artillery fire bursting in the sky, her face alight with childlike wonder.

speaker: Jasmine
content: The fireworks... so pretty...

Yet the blades in her hands thrum with a savage, murderous energy. Now that the weapon is back in her grasp, you feel for the first time the maniacal power emanating from this seemingly fragile dancer.
She hears your call and turns her head, her smile bright against the smoky veil of gunpowder, lit by fractured rays of sun.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Thank you for bringing me to the closing ceremony. Finally, my wish will come true. The celebration I've waited for all these years... it's finally starting. Wait for me, Chief.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Once this is over, I'll come straight back to you. Just like we promised.
Her smile carries a barely perceptible hint of apology.

The situation is swiftly brought under control. The assassins are confirmed to be not Sinner, devoid of potent weaponry. With the Fraser delegation's aid in freeing several hostages, the attackers are now cornered, their escape routes cut off.

Yet something tells you it won't end this easily. A creeping unease settles in your chest, the familiar kind that whispers of danger before it arrives. Instinctively, you reach out to activate your shackles to sense a certain person in your mind.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, emergency—our rear is under attack.

The communication channel crackles to life. Piercing wails of agony first reach your ear. Then, the visual feed flickers on, revealing a hallway drenched in blood, a nightmarish scene of utter carnage.

speaker: Schorl
content: The targets are the Banyan special wards and a preservation station at the Ring Research Institute.

Your limbs go cold. That's where Jasmine is. And the MBCC squad—assigned to Banyan for care and security during this major operation—they're sprawled across the ground, lying motionless in pools of their own blood.
As the victims fall one after another, you finally get a clear view of the perpetrator's frenzied face—
[Transition] Corrupted Soldier Portrait

speaker: Guard
content: That's not an Outlander assassin—it's someone from the Ring Institute! But... something's off about him!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's the deal with those blades...
It's a researcher who has been driven to madness.

speaker: Security
content: Eeehahahaha!!!

speaker: Guard
content: Damn it, he's completely lost it... Stop him!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those blades...

The man, possessed by the deadly blades, stands with eyes wide open, pupils swallowed. His body jerks unnaturally, as if the weapon in his hands is the one controlling him, cutting down every living soul in sight. Those unaccustomed to battling Mania—much less their own colleagues—are paralyzed in shock. In an instant, the medical college becomes his slaughterhouse.

At last, he reaches his destination—and with a violent surge, shatters the thick glass barrier. A hand extends through the fractured pane. The dancer braces against his shoulder, then in one fluid motion, flips over him gracefully. Finally free, she escapes the cage that has served as both her prison and her sanctuary.
Jasmine takes in the scene, her delight unmistakable.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I warned you not to touch those blades... They're dangerous, cruel, thirsty for blood... They are DisCity's weapon, your weapon...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ${PlayerName} will be sad if this goes on... So let me finish it for him.
female_content: ${PlayerName} will be sad if this goes on... So let me finish it for her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Now...
[Scene Change] The Great Expo

speaker: Schorl
content: ...The rescue team just recovered this footage. It occurred simultaneously with the closing ceremony attack, approximately two hours ago.

speaker: Schorl
content: That's enough time for her to come here.

The shackles have already sensed her presence. Your gaze snaps to the edge of the panicking crowd—and there, amid the chaos of the battlefield, stands Jasmine. Artillery fire paints the sky in bursts of light, but she only watches, her face alight with childlike wonder.

speaker: Jasmine
content: The fireworks... so pretty...

Yet the blades in her hands thrum with a savage, murderous energy. Now that the weapon is back in her grasp, you feel for the first time the maniacal power emanating from this seemingly fragile dancer.
Even from a distance, she finds you instantly, her smile bright against the smoky veil of gunpowder, lit by fractured rays of sun.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Chief, I came to the closing ceremony after all. Don't be afraid, I'm not angry at you. You lied to me, left me behind... But I understand. You just wanted to keep me safe.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm sorry... but I was always going to come. My celebration... it's lasted for so many years. It has to end here.
Jasmine's appearance immediately puts everyone on high alert.

speaker: Schorl
content: What is her objective? Same as those Outland extremists from just now? There are too many viable targets here.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Don't you dare harm Chief!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No—I'm not her target, you are! FAC soldiers, fall back now! Paradeisos has me covered. Stay away from her!

It's too late. The pink figure glides through the crowd like a serpent. Before anyone can react, crimson blooms across the soldiers' white armor—one after another, they crumple. Blood rushes to your head.

The prohibition takes effect, sending spikes of light thrusting out from Jasmine's body. She stumbles, nearly losing her balance, but quickly dissipates the impact with a smooth roll as she hits the ground.
She looks up at you, not the slightest bit annoyed, wearing the same cheerful smile she always has for you.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Are you really serious? Use your power against me? I'm the only one who can control these blades, you know.

speaker: Jasmine
content: These blades only obey me. If you force those shackles on me, you're just surrendering my body to them. And then... these cursed blades will wield an S-Class Sinner's power. What do you think would happen then?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hahaha, let's not go there, okay? I'd hate to lose myself... I'd hate to let these wretched things hurt you.

Though reluctant to admit it, you know she isn't lying. Through the shackles, you feel it—something stirring inside Jasmine. Not just one presence, but countless voices, twisted together in a chorus of roars, howls, and sheer madness. You've heard these sounds before, the same ones that echo across that shattered battlefield deep within her mind, where such chaos reigned unchecked.
And you know exactly where these maddened voices come from.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Drop those blades now! Their Mania is already influencing you! Put them down!

speaker: Jasmine
content: Influencing me? No, I pull the strings here. They want me to slaughter everyone I see, just like how they killed my celebration... Ahaha, why would I ever listen to them?

speaker: Jasmine
content: I have no interest in killing—I just want your blade.
She hurls the blade from her left hand, slicing clean through the armor of a soldier charging from behind. His raised battle axe halts mid-swing, frozen in the air.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let go of that axe, or I'll finish you off too!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Drop your weapons! DROP THEM!!

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Don't fall back! Stop her! AAGH—!!

The soldier's hand gripping the battle axe—along with the entire arm—is sliced into multiple pieces by Jasmine. Those twin blades carve through his armor, slicing through flesh and bone as effortlessly as a knife through silk.

Schorl takes aim and fires a rapid burst from within the safety of your cover, but Jasmine moves too fast. With lightning reflexes, she twists aside, seizing an FAC soldier and hauling him into the line of fire. When Jasmine steps back into view, her face is splattered with crimson, her smile chilling enough to freeze blood.

speaker: Schorl
content: The combat capabilities of this generic model are limited. Chief, I can only guarantee your personal safety. Please maintain your distance.

speaker: Schorl
content: This woman possesses exceptional battlefield judgment and remarkable reflexes. Her intelligence is on par with—or perhaps even sharper than—that of an average person. It's highly likely that her behavior in the medical ward was an act. Don't waste any compassion on her.
Schorl's communications with you have always been close-range and barely audible, yet somehow Jasmine catches every word from that distance.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm smart? I'm normal? Hahahahaha, that makes me so happy!

speaker: Jasmine
content: But Chief... what I see, what I hear, what I smell—it's all different from you. Those precious things you care about? To me... they're just a waste.
[Scene Change] Suddenly overlay the current scene with a battlefield flashback filter in black and white with red accents
The shackles violently resonate as the scene before her fades to a pale wash—just like in her dreams.
But Jasmine freezes. She gazes at you across the vast distance, and all you can make out are the scars etched into her skin gradually glowing red.

speaker: Jasmine
content: The meat I eat always tastes like charred human flesh, and the water I drink forever reeks of blood. And I have to step so, so lightly... because one wrong move and a landmine might explode! But you know what? Landmines also make pretty fireworks!

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hard to imagine? Don't worry, you only need to visit a battlefield once to understand—life isn't really that precious.

speaker: Jasmine
content: People beg for life, shameless as stray dogs, only to die like crushed insects. Burned or chopped up, they're just sludge—no more noble than garbage beneath your feet. You see it once, and you'll never escape it. It clings to you... follows you everywhere.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...But it's fine. My mind went crazy—it doesn't hurt anymore. Artillery shells are fireworks, machine guns war drums, blood just another wine. Dead men don't care which side they fought for... so they'll all make peace, watch me dance, and applaud me. Isn't that what a celebration should be?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Your war ended a long time ago, and no one here was part of it. Do you really want to side with them and take revenge on all of DisCity?
