content: My name is... Tia...

speaker: Yokna
content: Good! Ms. Tia, here in the farlands, the Aurum Secretum is a heavenly blessing. Those who wield it are champions in our eyes.
She turns to face the crowd. Her voice rings out, a command that stills the air.

speaker: Yokna
content: Today, during the Tide of Ashes, Ms. Tia protected us with the Aurum Secretum. We of the farlands honor our debts. No matter how dire our circumstances, we will never neglect the one who saved us!

speaker: Yokna
content: Everyone! Bring out the finest drink we have! Light the bonfires! Tonight, we celebrate our friends who have come to us from afar!

speaker: Everyone
content: Yes!!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Huh... Whaaaat???
[Night Scene]

The ash clears with the coming of sunset. Beneath the dome of shimmering light, people move with the weariness of the wounded. However, their toasts are loud, their drinks splashing over battered hands as they laugh through the pain.
Half the settlement seems to have gathered, voices rising in animated retellings of the day's terror and the miracle Hypatia wrought.

speaker: Yokna
content: Ms. Tia, come here.
Yokna stands in the center of the carpet, her hand outstretched toward Hypatia in invitation.

The girl hesitates. She has seen farland celebrations before, from the edges as an observer. She knows the central seat is reserved for the guest of honor, surrounded by offered blessings with dance one by one.
But does she... truly deserve that spot?

speaker: Rust
content: Go on. What you did for them today deserves everyone's gratitude.
Guided gently from behind and welcomed from the front, Hypatia is ushered into the celebration beneath the shimmering golden dome.
Laughter and song rise around her. People move to a rhythmic dance, each taking her hands in turn, their words of gratitude warm and earnest.
Thanks to the Aurum Secretum, thanks to our savior, thanks to the fate that spares us one more day from the catastrophe's grasp.
May your heart be light, may your path be straight, may your destiny be fulfilled when you arrive...

Unlike the perpetual decorum of the nobility, this revelry feels raw and real, possessing a magic of its own. The drumbeats, the dancing, the shared blessings... each one weaving a stronger bond between them.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Destiny...
Pain, sudden and searing, lances through the brand on her neck. A cruel reminder, it scorches away any sense of worth.
Guilt, sharp and suffocating, rises in her throat. Through the heart-piercing pain, she clutches the communicator on her chest.
A gentle white light kindles within it, seeping warmth into her ribs, quieting the fire in her skin, easing the weight in her lungs.

speaker: Margaret
content: My power cannot remove it completely, but it can alleviate its flare-ups to some extent. To eliminate it entirely will require time... and your own willpower.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Thank you, Ms. Margaret.
Hypatia keeps a hand pressed to her chest as the burning fades. Around her, the celebration continues, with faces glowing like embers in the bonfire's light.

speaker: Yokna
content: What's wrong? Did someone offend you? Or are you feeling unwell?

speaker: Hypatia
content: No, it's just... I’m touched. I don't feel I've done anything remarkable, yet you all honor me so...

speaker: Yokna
content: Silly girl, surviving a catastrophe is the most remarkable. You saved lives; you've earned the best seat and the finest drink!
With a warm smile, she guides Hypatia to her seat.

speaker: Yokna
content: Rust, where'd you find this one? You brought her all the way out here just out of the goodness of your heart to help us?

speaker: Rust
content: We're friends, aren't we? If I were in a pinch, you'd lend a hand.

speaker: Rust
content: My friend here happens to be an exceptional Aurum Secretum researcher. Feel free to ask her anything you don't understand.
With a smooth swirl of his wine, Rust seizes the moment, introducing Hypatia to Yokna.

speaker: Rust
content: Yokna and I go way back. Helping her is like helping me. Consider this your way to repay me for that rough journey: lend them your expertise.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I would have done it regardless!

speaker: Hypatia
content: No matter what, I will ensure the Aurum Secretum barriers remain stable and protect everyone here.

speaker: Yokna
content: Thank you, truly. The Tide of Ashes has been worsening, costing us more lives each time. Without your help today, we would have lost many more.

speaker: Yokna
content: The farlands lack everything: technology, resources, skilled hands... And we're at a critical juncture. Who knows if spies have already slipped in... If you two could stay, it would be an immense help.

speaker: Rust
content: The place seems plenty lively as it is.

speaker: Yokna
content: It's that alliance meeting... Every power player has shown up, thrown this place into chaos. The bootlicking merchants are manageable; they just want profit. But I'm more worried about the warmongers, in and out all the time, scheming who-knows-what.

speaker: Yokna
content: Every time I see that lot, I want to tell 'em to stop stirring the damn pot. Just dealing with Mania is hard enough. We can't survive another ******* war.
Before the words have fully left her mouth, the thud of heavy footsteps crushes the festive air.

A dozen figures emerge from the narrow passage. Black blood gleams wet on their blades; cold light glints off their metal masks. Aurum Secretum Warriors, fresh from the kill, trailing the scent of death.

speaker: Lead Warrior
content: Since when did Crag's Nest become a dumping ground for every stray piece of scum? The alliance meeting is right around the corner, and you're not concerned about DisCity rats slipping in?

speaker: Lead Warrior
content: I've heard the rumors. DisCity sent some so-called Peace Ambassador to Fraser to flaunt their victory. Who knows what other vermin slithered in behind her?

speaker: Lead Warrior
content: Hmph. Not satisfied with stirring trouble in Fraser, now they want to infiltrate our meeting to pick at the bones? Think again! DisCity dogs... I'll gut every last one of them who dares show their face!

The lead warrior thrusts his arm upward, sweeping his cloak aside. From his inner arm to his waist coils a lattice of black and gold, a pattern that seethes beneath his skin like something alive. His expression is one of fierce, unsettling pride.

speaker: Lead Warrior
content: The war is not over. We must stay sharp! Our brothers and sisters in Furor sacrificed themselves as blades for the future of the farlands... We must carry the fight! Make DisCity pay for what they've done!
His presence is an immediate threat. Hypatia's hand slips inside her cloak, and behind her back, a blade of solid gold forms silently in her grip.

speaker: Rust
content: Now, let's all try to keep our manners, shall we? You're frightening my friend.
Rust steps subtly in front of Hypatia, shielding her from view while masking the shifting of her hands beneath her cloak.

speaker: Rust
content: The lady here is a whiz with gadgets. I know folks who need tech. She provides the brains, I provide the brawn, and I'm counting on her to help me turn a tidy profit.

speaker: Rust
content: If you've got any ideas about harming her, I'm afraid I'd have to take issue with that.

speaker: Yokna
content: Rael, Rust is an old contact of mine. He's trustworthy. And Ms. Tia here just repaired our Aurum Secretum barrier and saved all our lives. How could they possibly be DisCity spies?

speaker: Rael
content: Disians are cunning as foxes! Of course it's possible!
Rael's blade cuts through the air, its edge aimed at Rust's throat.

speaker: Rael
content: Look at this "friend" of ours. Desert navigator. Skilled fighter. Traveling repairman with a pretty girl in tow.

speaker: Rael
content: That sand ship outside is yours, isn't it? Last I saw it, the owner was a medic.

speaker: Rust
content: Sand ships, you know. They all look the same.

speaker: Rael
content: Yokna, what was he calling himself when you knew him?

speaker: Yokna
content: ...Uh, well... back then he was sort of... a relic hunter, I guess?
A heavy silence falls. Every eye locks on Rust, sharp with suspicion.

speaker: Rust
content: Sigh, a man's got to have a few side gigs to get by these days. You really have to cut off an honest guy's livelihood?
Rust's smile doesn't waver, but his hand has already found his weapon.
He tilts his head a fraction, his voice a low thread meant only for Hypatia.

speaker: Rust
content: When it breaks, run for the entrance. Take any sand ship you can find.

speaker: Hypatia
content: How could I leave you behind? If we go, we go together.

speaker: Rael
content: What kind of honest man has this many faces? Stop playing ******* games with me!
You all are too wound up, seeing enemies in every shadow. With our defenses fixed, we'll all be spilling less of our own blood, won't we?

Just as tension solidifies into violence, a middle-aged man pushes through the crowd. He plants himself between the two parties, all practiced smiles, and claps Rael on the shoulder, a gesture that looks like scolding but carries affection.

speaker: Rael
content: Jab, what are you playing at?

speaker: Jabara
content: I'd like to take advantage of this gathering to offer my sincere thanks. To everyone, and especially to our two heroic guests from afar! The Aurum Secretum Warriors cut down our foes, and the expert raised our shield. Without you all, none of us would have weathered this storm!

speaker: Jabara
content: Look, I've just secured a new shipment of arms from outside. With this hardware in your hands, you'll be unstoppable. You can root out every last spy and turncoat.

speaker: Jabara
content: So, as a personal favor to me... ease up a little, would you?
His perfectly calibrated praise does its work. As Rael's stance softens, Jabara seizes the opening, waving an attendant forward without a wasted moment.

speaker: Jabara
content: Quickly, show our esteemed guests the new stock. And give them the friends-and-family discount; put it on my tab.

speaker: Rael
content: Hmph.
He reads the room with precision, tailoring his words to their deepest interests. In moments, the tension that seemed ready to explode is contained.

speaker: Rust
content: Flattery and bribery in one tidy package. A real professional.
Jabara turns to Rust and Hypatia, his expression undimmed, as if the mockery had never been spoken.

speaker: Jabara
content: Pay him no mind, pay him no mind. The fighting's left him a bit... frayed. You two must be exhausted from your travels. Since you've come all this way, allow me to show you around. Our region may be impoverished, but the vistas are absolutely breathtaking.

Jabara's smile remains fixed, but his gaze keeps slipping toward Hypatia, who stays completely hidden behind Rust's figure. Beside him, Rael gives a low, cold snort and lets the challenge drop, though a flicker of unease toward Jabara betrays itself in his stillness.

speaker: Jabara
content: Don't worry, he won't make trouble. After all, ninety percent of the farlands' food supply passes through my hands. I am Jabara, just a simple merchant trying to get by. And you must be Ms. Hypatia Campbell? Your esteemed brother, Adelaide, has spoken of you. Meeting you today, I see his praise for your grace and bearing was entirely justified.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...! You know Adelaide?
Noting Hypatia's tension, the man's smile softens into something practiced and placating.

speaker: Jabara
content: Mr. Adelaide? Everyone knows him. We have occasional business dealings, nothing more.

speaker: Jabara
content: Please, set your mind at ease. A lady of your stature traveling with discretion must have her reasons. I won't speak of it, and I certainly won't mention anything to your honorable brother. It's simply that I've long held the Campbell name in the highest regard and couldn't pass up the chance to make your acquaintance.

speaker: Jabara
content: Mira

speaker: Rust
content: These noble families have rules for everything. If she were discovered and hauled back, it'd be weeks confined to some three-story manor, minimum.

speaker: Jabara
content: I understand completely. I wouldn't dream of disrupting Ms. Campbell's private excursion.

speaker: Jabara
content: I would only ask that, when your journey concludes, you must convey my humble regards to Mr. Adelaide.
The merchant then releases a heavy sigh, a deep frown creasing his brow as he shakes his head repeatedly.

speaker: Jabara
content: Times are hard, I tell you. The calamities grow worse. Several settlements have exhausted their Aurum Secretum and Hypercube reserves, forcing relocations. Then, during migration, they were caught in the Tide of Ashes... lost a devastating amount of supplies...

speaker: Jabara
content: Food is becoming scarce. To protect themselves, some settlements have even closed their gates to outsiders entirely.

speaker: Rust
content: What's the word from Fraser? Are they sending any aid?

speaker: Jabara
content: Ever since the Black Ring, communications have been a nightmare. No news, no broadcasts get through. It's been an age since I had any reliable word from Fraser. I wonder, Ms. Campbell, since you've come from that direction... might you have any insight into the situation there?
As he speaks, his eyes dart toward Hypatia once again.

speaker: Jabara
content: The Senate's post-war maneuvering, for instance... Take this "Unity Gala" invitation. Anyone with sense knows it's political theater. The highborns must already have their desired outcomes scripted. Why not tip us off in advance? Then we could... align our steps accordingly.

speaker: Jabara
content: Ah... I see, I understand completely. Your eyes tell me everything. I was hoping Ms. Hypatia might help me discuss a small matter with Mr. Adelaide... You see, I have a surplus of food stores, but the cost of transport is prohibitive. I was considering a modest price adjustment... perhaps an increase of twenty percent...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Transport it out? But the people here don't even—

speaker: Hypatia
content: Nngh!

speaker: Whispers
content: Disgusting... So disgusting... Die... Campbells... All of you deserve to die...!
A sudden, splitting pain lances through the back of her neck as whispers coil around her thoughts. It's the mental sorcery, triggered without warning.

Memories flood in: the glittering galas, the smiling toasts, the courteous handshakes. Behind the elegant laughter, certain faces were quietly marked as necessary "sacrifices," collateral damage for a greater game.
Hypatia lurches forward violently. The teacup in front of her no longer holds tea, but a swirl of bloody tears. She claps a hand over her mouth, choking back sound.

speaker: Jabara
content: Ms. Campbell...?

speaker: Rust
content: Ah, our journey was rather rough—sandstorms, contamination zones. The young lady is suffering from travel sickness, and I'm afraid this confined space is only aggravating it.

speaker: Jabara
content: Oh, how careless of me! Please, step outside for some fresh air at once!

speaker: Rust
content: We've been traveling a long while. Your family must be worried. This is a good opportunity to let her know you're safe.
Hypatia nods, offers a polite apology, and rises to leave.
[Scene Change]
In a quiet corner, she doubles over, retching up bile. After a few ragged coughs, she feebly draws out the little bird.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ms. Margaret, Mr. Rust and I have successfully arrived at the farland meeting site and have made contact with the leaders.
The little bird nuzzles against her palm, then a gentle female voice comes through.

speaker: Margaret
content: Hypatia... your voice... what's wrong?

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I've found that even among the farlanders themselves, opinions on the current crisis are deeply divided. Their leaders are in constant dispute, each pursuing their own agenda.
She quickly summarizes the situation at the settlement.

speaker: Hypatia
content: There is even someone who profits by undermining the collective. Should I expose him? Could this be some form of necessary balance I don't understand? Or... is it simply an unavoidable compromise?

speaker: Margaret
content: A person's everyday words reveal their true priorities. You are perceptive, Hypatia. With a little focus, you can discern the genuine desires behind their speech. Learn to listen for and understand these subtleties.

speaker: Margaret
content: The people of the farlands prioritize concrete gains... because without that focus, they could not have survived the calamities. This may be hard for you to accept, but stating your position, showing where your loyalties lie, establishing mutual benefit... these, too, are the foundations of building trust...

speaker: Margaret
content: But most of all, trust in your own capabilities. You need not descend to their level. An Aurum Secretum prodigy should operate by her own rules... your talents... can become their... hope...
Just before the voice fades completely, she asks the question that has been burning inside her.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Why... why can some people simply not see the suffering of others?

speaker: Margaret
content: ...Some simply lack the capacity for empathy. But more often... it is because they have not yet left the safety of the shore.
The signal frays, the bird's voice fading into static. Just as silence settles, she hears the measured tread of footsteps behind her.
Hello, Ms. Campbell. What a pleasant coincidence, meeting you here.
The newcomer offers a composed smile, his words smooth and measured. The emblem of the Luminaris Society glints from the embroidery of his tailored robe.
I am Daik. A fellow member of the Luminaris Society, like yourself, though my talents pale in comparison to yours. You likely wouldn't recall me.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ah, a colleague from the Society. It's a pleasure... but may I ask what brings you here?
Hypatia bows, a gesture of graceful composure meant to mask her pounding heart. Without a flicker in her expression, she severs the connection, letting silence fall between them.

speaker: Daik
content: For the same purpose as you, of course. To represent Fraser and the Society in uniting with our farland allies and aiding their afflicted people.
He smiles and gestures toward Yokna and Rael standing behind him, subtly indicating that he's already established contact with them.

speaker: Yokna
content: Should've guessed you were with the Society, seeing how you handled that Aurum Secretum device.

speaker: Yokna
content: Meanwhile, some people just had to go around barking about DisCity spies, stirring up dust for nothing.

speaker: Rael
content: Hah! Everyone knows your type. As long as someone can fix your broken junk, you'd wag your tail even for a genuine Disian.
Their argument swells, sharp and carrying, until the merchant's head appears in the doorway.

speaker: Jabara
content: Must you argue right outside my... Oh my!
At the sight of the elegant figures, the merchant's irritation melts into performative delight. In the same breath, Rust withdraws his presence, a subtle shadow behind the merchant's form.

speaker: Jabara
content: What an honor to have such distinguished guests at my humble threshold. Could you be looking for... Ms. <color=#fb9259>Hypatia</color>?
His gaze slides between Hypatia and the newcomers, a careful, tactical pause as he measures what to say, and what bond to claim.

speaker: Daik
content: That is one of our purposes, as Ms. Campbell is indeed a valued asset to the Society.

speaker: Daik
content: However, there are more pressing matters that require our collective attention. Might we adjourn to a more suitable location to discuss them in detail?

speaker: Jabara
content: Of course, of course! How rude of me to keep you standing in this dust and wind. Please, let us continue our discussion indoors, where we may speak at our leisure.
Jabara preens, visibly smug at having "discerned" Hypatia's identity. His smile is ostentatious, like a peacock spreading its feathers to claim dominance.
Hypatia and Rust make no move to leave. The Luminaris representative merely smiles, unsurprised, and gestures for them to enter the tent. The others follow.
Inside, the gathering is informal. They seat themselves with a relaxed air, and once settled, the Society representative begins to speak, his composure intact.

speaker: Daik
content: I bring important news.

speaker: Daik
content: I believe you have all received Fraser's invitation to the upcoming "Unity Gala" in the city, to collectively commemorate the conclusion of the Ash Campaign.

speaker: Daik
content: Naturally, that is the public rationale. The true impetus for the gathering originates from a more distant city-state...
He pauses, scanning the room as his tone grows grave.

speaker: Daik
content: Yes. The greatest DisCity has recently issued a formal peace overture. They demand Fraser convene representatives of the Farland Alliance to jointly define a, quote, "new peaceful relationship."

speaker: Daik
content: More regrettably, we have little choice but to comply.

speaker: Daik
content: DisCity deployed its catastrophe weapon and destroyed our painstakingly cultivated Black Ring. Their so-called Peace Ambassador presented a list of conditions. Should we refuse...

speaker: Daik
content: ...the consequence would be that warmonger Augustus massing her legions on our border.
—Impossible. These couldn't be Margaret's words.
Hypatia's brow tightens. Her gaze shifts toward Rust in the distance, who gives an almost imperceptible shake of his head—Keep listening.
A cold sneer escapes Rael.

speaker: Rael
content: Fine. Let's have this damn meeting. Get 'em all in one room. We'll just plant a charge under the table and blow the whole lot to the heavens.

speaker: Jabara
content: Oh, for pity's sake, simmer down! That's exactly what DisCity wants! Attacking envoys gives them the perfect war warrant. Do you have any idea what another conflict would do to us?!
The merchant looks imploringly at the Society's envoy.

speaker: Jabara
content: Representative, you must give us a path forward. This instability is strangling commerce. We need clarity.
Hypatia's fingers drift to the small bird in her pocket. She traces its shape, a silent gesture that feels, for a moment, like a tether to the distant woman in white.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Steady, Hypatia. Strategy. You must fulfill the task Margaret gave you.
The Society representative shakes his head with feigned seriousness.

speaker: Daik
content: Their methods are more refined than crude assassination. Their new Outland Affairs Officer, this "Peace Ambassador" Margaret Kervoz, is particularly adept at persuasion. All smiles and promises of technology-sharing.

speaker: Daik
content: She's barely offered more than vague assurances—"cleaning contamination," "joint calamity response," "exploring ruins for Hypercubes"—and yet she has swayed several of our allied factions. The Nirvana expedition she leads has already established an outpost near the Furor ruins...

At the name Furor, a ripple of unease passes through the farland leaders. For many here, Furor only became real after the Black Ring incident. It was a crisis they never knew when it was a plea, and one they still failed to answer when it became a calamity.

speaker: Yokna
content: Furor? Ain't that place... already a total loss? Contaminated ground.

speaker: Jabara
content: Indeed... The area is catastrophically unstable. To go near is to court death. Rumors speak of ghost-wails on the wind from miles off... and sightings.

speaker: Rael
content: Those DisCity vultures! I won't let them pick over those bones!

speaker: Daik
content: ...But we lack the leverage to stop them.

speaker: Yokna
content: So what's their angle? We've scouted Furor ruins. Nothing there but beasts and broken Aurum Secretum junk. Nothin' worth this trouble...

speaker: Daik
content: For this.
He draws out a slender glass vial, inside of which several miniature Hypercubes pulse with a soft, cerulean radiance.

speaker: Daik
content: With catastrophes rampant, Hypercubes are the only precious resource capable of countering Mania and shielding our people. Our breakthrough research at the Luminaris Society has confirmed a truth: they only precipitate from the remnants of a Black Ring.

speaker: Daik
content: And DisCity holds a monopoly. They use them as a leash, holding the entire world hostage, extracting every ounce of value we have. The wealth of their so-called premier city-state is built on that stranglehold.

speaker: Daik
content: Now consider. In their moment of "victory," they come to the edge of our Black Ring and propose "joint development"... What is their true objective?
Bang! Rael's fist crashes down onto the table.

speaker: Rael
content: Of course. Come to pick through our people's graves for treasure. That's the DisCity way!
The Luminaris representative gives a slow nod. The mood established, he now discards all pretense.

speaker: Daik
content: BR-005 and the Hypercubes it yielded are a miracle born from our people's sacrifice. They are the Alliance's first real chance in years to change its fate. DisCity failed to find Hypercubes at the main crash site. Now they look to its birthplace, Furor. They intend to steal our hope!

speaker: Daik
content: For our people and the larger strategic picture, we cannot openly break relations. But we cannot afford to fall behind in the exploration race, either. If Margaret Kervoz secures Hypercubes first, our claim to the BR-005 site becomes untenable.

speaker: Daik
content: Securing the Black Ring means securing Hypercubes first. This is precisely where the Society requires your assistance!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Hold on, our research on the Black Rings is still incomplete, and Farland's contamination protocols are not fully secure. A rash approach to Furor would be dangerously reckless!

speaker: Daik
content: Ms. Hypatia, I fear you have been absent from the Society's halls too long. You are unaware of recent... developments.

speaker: Daik
content: Our research on BR-005 has made a significant leap. New data has allowed us to triangulate several high-probability locations for Hypercube formation.

speaker: Rust
content: You bring the data. They bring the lives. That's the deal?
Not a flicker of emotion crosses the representative's face. This challenge was well within the Society's projections.

speaker: Daik
content: The risks are real. I will compel no one. The Society's message is delivered. The duty to protect your people... remains yours.
His gaze rests meaningfully on the silent representatives of the three factions.

speaker: Jabara
content: You understand my position. I'm a merchant. I must calculate the cost of everything. One misstep could mean ruin...

speaker: Yokna
content: I'll go.

speaker: Yokna
content: Give me the data. I'll take stock of my gear and can move out in a few days.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ms. Yokna, please reconsider! Or... take me with you. As an Aurum Secretum expert, I could offer your team some protection!

speaker: Yokna
content: Right. With your tech, maybe we could even neutralize Furor's contamination!

speaker: Yokna
content: Get our hands on Hypercubes, and we'll finally have a real bargaining chip against Mania, and against those DisCity bastards. Make 'em sit at a table that we set.
The Society representative only smiles faintly in Hypatia's direction, offering neither confirmation nor denial. Yet, for reasons she cannot name, a sharp pain lances through her nape.
Rael turns toward Yokna and whistles, sharp and dramatic.

speaker: Rael
content: Look at you, growin' a spine. Almost didn't recognize you.

speaker: Rael
content: Alright, I'm in for this madness. But if we find any of those shiny rocks, my crew gets the lion's share.

speaker: Rael
content: Gotta re-stock the arsenal. Last war left the cupboards bare.
Seeing the moment unfold, the merchant's hesitation shatters.

speaker: Jabara
content: Well, then... I shall contribute as well. For the future of the farlands, I, ahem, must certainly do my part.

speaker: Daik
content: It seems a consensus has been reached.

speaker: Daik
content: Then there is no time to delay. We depart for the Furor ruins at first light tomorrow. We cannot allow the Disians a head start.
The Society representative rises, cradling the luminous blue mineral, a stone of hope, its ethereal light pulsing softly in his grasp.
Hypatia's protest dies unspoken. The warrior is lost to his rage, the merchant to his ledger, the protector to her sacrifice.
In this economy of blood and profit, danger and death have become acceptable currency, and any advice would be weightless.
A cold sweat beads on her palms. Her fingers close around the little bird in her pocket, but its connection is severed. In her hand, it is only silent metal.
The moment the Society representative's eyes meet hers, the sorcery tears through her mind. Whispers become a roar, pain a splitting force inside her skull.
Her vision blanks into white static, and sound vanishes into a void.

speaker: Daik
content: You wish to join the expedition to Furor, too? I must strongly advise against it. Consider your current state, fainting at a simple meeting. A protracted journey into the wastes would be untenable. Should your health suffer any further, Mr. Adelaide Campbell's displeasure would be considerable. We could offer no satisfactory explanation.

speaker: Daik
content: There is a vacant residence within our temporary compound, which is secure and quiet. You and your companion will rest there to recuperate, Ms. Campbell. We have arranged ample personnel to attend to your needs. For your own safety, please remain until our departure for Fraser.

speaker: Daik
content: Leave the affairs of the alliance to us. The Luminaris Society—and indeed, Fraser itself—will shepherd our collective future. You do agree, do you not, Ms. Campbell? Hehe...
The so-called resting place is a cell carved into the rock. Three walls, no windows. The air inside sits thick and still, like the inside of a sealed tomb.
Guards wait at the door. Beyond them, three separate checkpoints, each manned by a small squad of four or five. The lockdown is absolute.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Rest? This is clearly—

speaker: Rust
content: A vacation. And a thoughtfully arranged one at that.
Rust finishes her sentence, his tone offhand, while his fingers trace a subtle signal against his leg. Hypatia reads it instantly and quiets.

The agent admires the room's layout aloud, already unspooling a roll of opaque tape. He sweeps the ceiling, the underside of the table, the backs of cabinets... In under five minutes, a dozen listening devices are silenced.
Only when he's satisfied does he set the tape aside, pick up an apple, and offer it to Hypatia.

speaker: Rust
content: The hospitality is generous. Fruit like this is a rare sight outside Fraser's noble quarters. You should eat, Miss Campbell. Regain your strength.

speaker: Rust
content: Your collapse earlier... it wasn't just exhaustion, was it? You were under some form of sorcery, an extreme mental coercion technique. The Senate's work? Before we left the city?

speaker: Rust
content: I didn't notice it earlier. I'm sorry—

speaker: Hypatia
content: No, I'm sorry! If I had resisted the sorcery, we wouldn't have had to leave the meeting. We missed vital intelligence, and I gave him the perfect excuse to sideline us. This is entirely my fault!

speaker: Rust
content: Well... that wasn't quite my point.
But his true intent is lost on her. Overwhelmed by pressing dread and sharp regret, she wears a path across the floor of their opulent prison.

speaker: Hypatia
content: The Society talked about taking the farlanders to find Hypercubes... They would never be that altruistic. It's a play for their loyalty.

speaker: Hypatia
content: They knew my identity, my connection to Margaret, and yet they didn't expose us during the meeting... That was no act of kindness.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Is this leverage? Who are they pressuring? What other schemes are in motion? What is their real purpose in taking people to Furor? And why isolate us like this?

speaker: Hypatia
content: I can't just wait here for whatever comes next... Ms. Margaret tasked me with reaching the leaders. Fraser is planning something more, and I have to uncover it. I have to stop them.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Mr. Rust, please, what should I do?
Her gaze finally lifts to Rust. A seasoned spy, a man of hidden resources... maybe he has a way?

speaker: Rust
content: What to do... How about we start by finding a way to treat the sorcery affecting you?

speaker: Rust
content: It's taking a toll. And as you said, Furor will likely be a battlefield. When that time comes, I don't want—

speaker: Hypatia
content: But we don't have that kind of time. We need to get to Furor as soon as possible. I can endure this. It's manageable.
Rust studies her expression: resolve sharpened by desperation, anxiety hardening her natural stubbornness. Changing her mind is no longer an option.

speaker: Rust
content: I see...

speaker: Rust
content: ...Very well. I'll think of something.

Rust's smile vanishes, replaced by a focused seriousness. He moves to the far side of the room, retrieves a prepared tea set, and methodically checks the leaves for tampering before beginning the brew. His movements are unhurried, deliberate—a man thinking through each step as the water heats.
When the tea is ready, he pours with quiet precision. Only then does he seem to reach a conclusion, extending a cup toward Hypatia.

speaker: Rust
content: Miss Campbell, are you fond of spy movies?

speaker: Hypatia
content: I've seen a few... but now isn't the time for that, is it? I mean—

speaker: Rust
content: Good. That means you have some experience already. Consider this a practical exercise; you'll play the lead.
Where Hypatia looks visibly bewildered, Rust's expression grows serious.

speaker: Rust
content: Hmm... Come to think of it, as a "distinguished agent" personally praised by Ms. Margaret, and a recipient of the 9th Agency Medal of Honor... I've never actually taken on an apprentice in all these years.

speaker: Rust
content: Interested in being the first, Miss Campbell?

speaker: Rust
content: Or may I call you Hypatia?
[Scene Change]
Dark. Stifling. Time congeals in the cavern's depths. For hours, the guard has listened in vain, ears straining for any useful sound. At last, a yawn cracks his composure.
Then, a cold numbness at the base of his skull, followed by a jolt of white-hot pain. His body seizes. Before he can turn, darkness swallows him, and he slumps to the stone floor.

Rust materializes from the shadows, drags the guard into deeper blackness, and looks up. Overhead, the cavern branches into a network of winding passages, intricate as veins threading through the mountain's flesh.
He angles his body, slips through a narrow split in the rock, and takes out a small Aurum Secretum figurine. A pause, then his fingers work the metal, bending it into an unnatural, deliberate shape.

speaker: Rust
content: Shhh—
Hypatia receives the figurine's signal. In Rust's hand, his own piece bends automatically into an "OK" gesture in reply, a sight he finds quietly amusing.

They meet in a narrow cave tunnel, moving single-file through the winding stone, guided by faint drafts of air. The path is treacherous in the dark, forcing Hypatia to stay close on Rust's heels, her steps cautious.
After circling the perimeter, however, they find the residence far more guarded than expected. The main entrance is sealed tight.

speaker: Hypatia
content: All the exits are blocked, and guards are posted. What do we do...

speaker: Rust
content: Then we find a key. Agent's Rule Number One: Every lock, every cage, every puzzle has one thing that opens it.
That kind of rule only exists in the movies!
Her aristocratic decorum keeps the rebuke silent. Instead, she quietly directs her words toward her newly acquired "master."

speaker: Hypatia
content: But how do we find it? Time is short.

The mechanisms blocking the doors aren't ordinary locks; they're integrated with Aurum Secretum sorcery. That means the corresponding keys won't be physical, but coded with a specific Aurum Secretum signature.

speaker: Rust
content: You handled them quite deftly when you captured me. You still have those little tools, yes? Toni Stark of Aurum Secretum?
Hypatia nearly chokes at his remark.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I see...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Any inhabited space needs ventilation. This Aurum Secretum spider can navigate narrow ducts and relay sound back. It should help us identify what we're dealing with.
The Aurum Secretum figurine in her hand shifts form, reshaping into a spider that vanishes into the ventilation duct. It scuttles through the narrow passages and returns to her palm moments later.
She looks up and signals to him in a hushed code.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Found it. The key is in the third room below, on one of the people inside.
Rust replies with a silent thumbs-up.

speaker: Rust
content: Have your little friend shadow them and find an opening to retrieve it.
Hypatia nods. The Aurum Secretum spider lowers itself from the vent on a silken thread, hovering just above the guards' heads. Everything is prepared; now, they wait.
Then, from inside the room, a conversation reaches Hypatia's ears, clear and unguarded.

speaker: A.S. Researcher A
content: Heh... These farlanders are so damn easy to bait. Mention Hypercubes, and their eyes go wide like greedy kids at a candy stall.

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: They're just backwater hicks, after all. Hey, you locked up, right?

speaker: A.S. Researcher A
content: Locked and loaded. Ugh, let's get out of this dump already. Slumming it out here is torture. Just looking at these locals makes my skin crawl. Oh, and get this: yesterday, some little beggar kid came running up...
Their words grow more brazen, more insulting. Hypatia's expression tightens, disapproval etched clearly across her face.
Arrogant, despicable, shameful. She bites down on the fury, forces her hands to still. She must endure this.
From beside her, Rust watches her reaction. A faint smile touches his lips as he taps the ground lightly, pulling her focus back to him.

speaker: Rust
content: Rule Number Two: Strike when the opportunity presents itself. Punishing the wicked never requires hesitation.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...But isn't this supposed to be a covert operation? What if we alert the other guards?

speaker: Rust
content: Heh...

speaker: Rust
content: Agents work under tremendous pressure with highly-strung nerves. Appropriate release is essential for maintaining mental and physical well-being. As for your concern about word getting out...

speaker: Rust
content: If it can't leave this building, then it's not really a leak, is it?
The legendary agent gestures with a hand. Tucked in his palm are several neatly severed communication cables.

speaker: Rust
content: Just clipped them on my way past; these are all the lines. Those poor guards can't reach anyone outside now.
Then what was the point of all that careful, nerve-wracking stealth? Are we really shooting a scene?
But before Hypatia can voice a word of protest, the agent—ever "meticulous"—is a drawn bowstring, his full intent aimed and ready to loose.

speaker: Rust
content: Get ready, here comes the action sequence climax—
Click! The lights in the room go out.

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: ****. Another power outage. What a shithole...

speaker: A.S. Researcher A
content: Wait, this is... an attack?! Look out—mmph!

In one fluid motion, Rust tears the air vent open and drops into the room. He lands squarely on one researcher's bald head, then spins, driving a hand strike into the neck of another. Seizing a flashlight from a nearby table, he angles its beam back up toward the opening.

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: Y-you... you... you're—?!!

speaker: Rust
content: Rule Number Three: Never waste a spotlight moment. Your turn, Agent Campbell.
Lit from below by the flashlight's "spotlight," Hypatia descends from the opening.

speaker: Hypatia
content: T-this "mission impossible"... I will complete it!

speaker: A.S. Researcher B & A
content: Nngh! Aah!! Ow-ow-ow—urgh!

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: Just take the key. Don't hit me, stop! I was wrong! I-I-I promise not to say anything. I'll donate to refugees tomorrow and support the farlands, I-I-I... OOOWW!!!
BWAK!
THUD!
CLANG!
Aurum Secretum gadgets shriek and scatter across the room. Researchers sob and crawl, pleading as they flee.
With Rust cutting through the close quarters and Hypatia unleashing Aurum Secretum from a distance, every guard sent their way is swiftly dismantled.
For the first time, Hypatia feels a raw, electric thrill. All her pent-up restraint shatters. She's free to unleash everything she's held back—no propriety, no decorum, just pure, satisfying payback.
Finally, she draws out a small, untested Aurum Secretum explosive of her own design. Since the invention, she has been waiting for the deployment opportunity.
Cradling it in her palms, she twists the ring, feels the mechanism hum to life, and—as the countdown bleeds its final second—hurls it.
BLAST—THEM—ALL—!!
[Exit Flashback]
The ship bucks violently, slamming Hypatia against her seat and tearing her from sleep.
Outside, night has swallowed the WhiteSands. At the controls, Rust pilots calmly, having just rammed a stray sand worm. He raises his sidearm and puts a round through it without breaking focus.
Right. They won. They gave the researchers a good beating, commandeered a Luminaris ship, and have been on the run ever since.

speaker: Hypatia
content: How long was I asleep? Have we reached Furor? Did we catch up?

speaker: Rust
content: Easy, the main show's over. Why not tidy up first?
He smiles and taps his own cheek. Hypatia freezes, then frantically wipes the corners of her mouth.
Had she overslept? Displayed some undignified habit in plain sight? Surely she hadn't <size=25>drooled</size> or lost her composure?!! Such things were unthinkable in the Campbell household!
The young noble lady's hands move in a flurry, only to pause as her fingers trace her own expression.

Her cheeks feel tight. The corners of her mouth are lifted. She's... smiling. That chaotic escape had followed her into sleep and returned with her to waking, bringing back a smile she had long forgotten.

speaker: Rust
content: Seems you had a good dream.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I did.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Thank you.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't mention it. We help each other out.

speaker: Rust
content: I got myself an apprentice and scratched that spy‑craft itch. I had fun too.

speaker: Rust
content: "An agent's duty is to uphold justice from the shadows!" Isn't that how it goes?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Pfft... Hahahaha!
Rust watches, quietly satisfied, as the rigidity of a Campbell child fractures, and gives way to Hypatia's unguarded, luminous laughing face.

speaker: Rust
content: ...That's more like it.
The night is ink-dark, stars gleaming like scattered silver. The sand ship cuts through the wind, carving two sharp trails in its wake.
[Scene Change]

Minutes later, the sand ship drifts to a halt in the shadow of a low dune. Ahead stands an abandoned safe house, a few scraggly trees clinging to its sides. The wind has stilled; a deep, watchful silence blankets the landscape. To the horizon, there is no trace of human life—a place that feels removed from all conflict and calculation.
Rust mutters something about needing rest and fuel after a long run, then heads off with their food stash to build a fire. All of it, he notes, was liberated from the Luminaris Society.

Soon, chicken sizzles on the makeshift grill, porridge simmers in an iron pot, and a careful spread of vegetables and fruit sits to the side. Even a sealed canister of drinking water appears. It's a mystery how the small, battered research sand ship ever held so much.

speaker: Rust
content: We've got time. Let's refuel first.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Mm.
Hypatia no longer urges them onward. He's right, of course, as he usually is.
She takes the ear of corn he offers and eats slowly, studying their surroundings. Above, a boundless starfield glitters; below the slope, a few weathered gray stones rest in the shadows.
For the first time in too long, she feels her shoulders loosen, her breath deepen.
And with that ease comes clarity. Her focus sharpens, her senses returning to their old, familiar keenness.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Furor doesn't have sand like this. The terrain is different, too.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Where are we?
She glances toward Rust, but the agent remains absorbed in tending the grill, his focus never leaving the flames.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Weren't we going to Furor?

speaker: Rust
content: What's waiting there will be brutal. Listen to your master: eat first, then move.

speaker: Hypatia
content: And after that? Where are you taking me?
The words catch in her throat, thick and bitter. Speaking feels like swallowing glass.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...It is Furor, isn't it? You will take me there, won't you, sir? I have to go. I—
The agent finally looks up from the fire. His gaze meets hers, and the silence between them is gentle, almost kind. But Hypatia already knows the answer he hasn't spoken, and it isn't gentle at all.

speaker: Rust
content: You're strong, Hypatia. But the battlefield ahead consumes everyone who steps onto it.

speaker: Rust
content: So, it's time I send you away from here.

The autumn wasteland night bites deep. Starlight is now a cold, punctured white, like countless tiny rents in the fabric of the dark, gazing down on the barren earth and the lost souls wandering beneath.
By the campfire, the fallen Campbell heiress huddles, hugging her knees. Even the flames cannot warm the grey pallor of her face. The food Rust prepared sits untouched and cold beside her.
She does not blink. Her eyes are fixed on the embers as they slowly die.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I won't go.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I won't go anywhere except Furor.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ms. Margaret entrusted me to reach the leaders of the farland settlements. She said Fraser is moving against everyone, that preserving peace means stopping their schemes... I must go.

speaker: Rust
content: While bearing that torturous sorcery?

speaker: Hypatia
content: You promised her you would help me!

speaker: Rust
content: What? You still want to save the person who betrayed us? Did the Tide of Ashes clog your brain with sand?

Her emotions clot in her throat before she can voice them. Rust's resolve is unyielding, and Hypatia, against her own will, trusts it. It's that very trust that now saturates her with a sorrow that feels ancient and absolute.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Do you judge me a burden? Because I can't withstand the Luminaris Society's sorcery? Because I...
...keep failing?

speaker: Rust
content: You know that isn't what I meant.
Rust's voice softens. He sets the still-warm cup of tea in her hands, taking her cold plate away. He then feeds more charcoal to the fire and watches, silent, as the embers fight to catch.
Only when the flames lift and steady does he seem to find his words.

speaker: Rust
content: I share Madam Margaret's high regard for you. The peace you have envisioned together is truly moving. I admire everything you've both done.

speaker: Rust
content: But she is, after all, <color=#fb9259>DisCity's</color> Peace Ambassador. However deep your friendship runs, Margaret holds an unshakable position. And trust me, that position does not align with yours.

speaker: Rust
content: You don't owe the Outland Affairs Officer your compliance. You've already gathered ample intelligence for her and scouted the dangers ahead. It's enough; she'll be satisfied.

speaker: Rust
content: Just look at how the Luminaris researchers have reacted. The Fraser authorities have already factored you into their schemes. The plots aimed at you are as thick as those targeting other leaders. If Margaret truly considered you a friend, she would agree to keep you off that field.
He says reassuringly, retrieving a thin blanket from the ship and draping it around her shoulders, but the gesture only deepens her shivering.

This ship goes no further. He will not take another step with her. Her journey ends here. Her breathing shallows; the spiritual brand flares, making her blood feel like fire in her veins. She forces herself still.

...Calm. She must stay calm. Any outburst now would only prove his point—that she's a child to be soothed with empty comforts. She refuses that. The road ahead is a war for adults, and if she wants to walk it, she must first earn her place.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...It isn't only for Ms. Margaret. This is my... own judgment. My choice.

Hypatia fights the tremor in her limbs as the sorcery twists through her nerves. Clutching the fraying ends of her control, she forms each word with painstaking care, willing her voice to sound steady and resolute.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I am an Aurum Secretum scholar and Fraser's frontline Mania specialist. All theoretical data from the Luminaris Society has passed through my hands. I know they lack DisCity's accumulated technological foundation.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Fraser cannot purge the remnants of BR-005. Even if a mine emerges from the ruins, it'll be nothing but a contaminated death trap, human bait laced with Hypercubes.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Countless refugees will be deceived into walking straight into it, their lives becoming consumables for Fraser to harvest "resources," just like Furor before. I know this pattern too well. The tasks they once assigned me followed the same design.

speaker: Hypatia
content: My city-state incites despair and hatred to control refugees; the Society I served uses truth to deceive believers; my research has been complicit in these crimes. Every comfort of my life has been built upon the suffering of others. And then... my brother...
She fights to stay steady, but at the mention of him, a tremor escapes her control.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Yes. The one who brought the suspicious individuals into Furor was Adelaide Campbell. He delivered the seed they called "inheritance" to the refugees. I believe you understand what that means, so you must also know what he has done.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...He is my brother. He led me out of the Campbell household, introduced me to experimental research, and opened doors for me. He was... once so close to me.

The past surges: tenderness and cruelty, sincerity and hypocrisy, colliding into dissonant shards that form memories beyond reason. Both the beautiful and the monstrous feel equally unreal, like pieces of the same fever dream.
The hand that once guided hers so gently was also steeped in blood. They had walked so closely that she must have walked in it, too, staining what she'd once believed was a path of light.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...He was that close to me. All of it happened where I could see. I understand what was done. Some things... I must do them myself.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ms. Margaret, Hella, Yokna, Rael, Jabara... and all the people of Furor. They're waiting. I have to go. This time, I must make it in time.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is my... inescapable responsibility.
She tries to speak, but her voice fails. A gust of wind tears her words away, burying them under the snap and rustle of the weathered tarpaulin along the hull.

Rust watches her closely. The young scholar's pupils tremble, her lips pale. It's hard to tell whether the sorcery is strangling her reason, or if her own obsessive fixation is feeding the torment planted inside her.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Responsibility...
He turns his gaze to the fire flickering against the dark.

speaker: Rust
content: The responsibility to prevent tragedy... Being accountable to others...
The flames gutter, but he doesn't feed them this time. He only watches, his expression cooling with the embers, until it matches the night's chill.

speaker: Rust
content: How far does that responsibility extend?

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Huh?
When his gaze finds her again, there is no trace of the earlier kindness left in it.

speaker: Rust
content: Will you challenge Fraser, toppling political alliances they've nurtured for decades? Or will you hunt the Undergrounders, rooting out sewer rats even the 9th Agency couldn't catch?

speaker: Rust
content: How far are you willing to go, and what price are you prepared to pay?

speaker: Rust
content: Is it responsibility driving you to this, or guilt? Do you truly wish to stop a conspiracy, or are you trying to atone for the past?

speaker: Rust
content: Or perhaps all that matters is that you suffer, treating this as your personal penance?
The protest rises, but she swallows it. Hypatia turns her head aside.
When she finally speaks again, the ideals have bled out of her voice. What remains is hollow—a dry, resolute echo.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...That doesn't matter, sir.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What I think is irrelevant. Whatever the farlands need, I will do. I will offer everything a scholar can provide.
Rust feels a sudden, ironic urge to laugh. The things she calls "irrelevant" are perfectly clear to him, and he knows exactly how much trouble it would be to move the immovable rock before him.
...It's all too familiar. He knows he should stop here, but the words slip out anyway.

speaker: Rust
content: Then start by reclaiming what makes you most valuable as a scholar.

speaker: Rust
content: Recover your composure and your wisdom. See yourself clearly. See the world clearly, then you will understand...

speaker: Rust
content: You truly did your best. That things did not turn out perfectly... is not your failing.
His tone holds no warmth, but neither is it harsh—only steady and inevitable, like ever-shifting quicksand.

speaker: Rust
content: You cannot fight the sins of an entire city‑state. Nor can you reclaim loved ones who have fallen to corruption or simply drifted away.

speaker: Rust
content: All distortion and suffering in the lands of famine stems from scarcity. Calamities have compressed humanity's living space. You cannot achieve a reversal unless you make the Perishing Star change its course...

speaker: Rust
content: But none of us can do that.
It's like a sigh that arrives too late, a eulogy echoing from a distance, spoken before an audience that isn't there.

speaker: Rust
content: The Black Ring born from the collective will... It's the terminal illness of our age. A fate chosen by so many. You can't undo that with a hero or two.

speaker: Rust
content: To carry the burden of others, you must first abandon the past and walk alone into the future. That is the true responsibility of a survivor, and it is no lighter than seeking death or atonement...

At first, Hypatia doesn't grasp his meaning. But she notices something else: Rust is looking at her, yet through her. His gaze is fixed on something she can't see. A jarring dissonance settles in her mind, and the contradictions begin to surface.

Why would a DisCity agent, who only came recently, know so much about the Luminaris Society? How can he, her supposed ally against the Black Ring, wield the Underground sorcery? Why, after just accepting Ms. Margaret's request, does he break protocol and urge her to leave? And why now? Who is he seeing when he looks at her?
The questions knot together, tightening, until instinct pulls one thread loose. She asks it softly.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Did something... happen to you in the past?
Her question draws him back. His gaze clears, returning from some distant place to rest on her, present and solid.
Then, at last, his familiar smile returns.

speaker: Rust
content: Hmm? Interested in my past? That'd take more than one night to tell, and fabricating stories is an agent's essential skill. Still care to hear it?

speaker: Rust
content: Actually, never mind. Time's precious, and we're nearly at the appointed hour.
He's said too much. Rust's eyes flick skyward, where a violet star drifts past the zenith—the signal from his contact.
That person will be here soon. Time to finish the preparations.

speaker: Rust
content: My friend will be here shortly to take you somewhere safe. Once you're clear of the interference, that little dove of yours should regain its strength. You'll be able to reach Margaret again.

speaker: Rust
content: You can report to her then. The Peace Ambassador will soon step onto her own battlefield. The intelligence you've gathered will be a considerable asset. This time, you will not disappoint her expectations.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't worry. My old colleague isn't as fragile as she might seem to you. With her methods, that gala in Fraser will certainly achieve "peace," regardless of what the organizers intended.

speaker: Rust
content: As for the Luminaris Society, the Underground, or the Black Ring... leave them to me. They're already my prey. You just need to pick whichever show you prefer. Infiltration, espionage, assassination, or explosions... take your pick.

speaker: Rust
content: Soon, the Fraser news channels will broadcast a brand-new spy blockbuster. Tune in and enjoy the show; thank you for your patronage in advance.
He turns to Hypatia, his expression softening.

speaker: Rust
content: Now then, Agent Campbell. If that excessive sense of responsibility is weighing you down to the point of suffocation, perhaps you should consider my advice.

speaker: Rust
content: Your brilliance should be directed toward a greater future, not crushed under the weight of guilt until you fall into a manipulator's trap and your talent withers prematurely.

speaker: Rust
content: Perseverance is admirable. But when the path ahead seems pitch black, there's no harm in waiting, showing patience before charging blindly ahead. Seek knowledge. Forge friendships. You may yet borrow light from unexpected places, illuminating paths you never knew existed.

Light... that illuminates paths? The phrase reaches her with perfect clarity, yet she can't recall what such light looks like. She tries to reconstruct it in her mind, gathering fragments of memory and shaping them into something that might resemble illumination.

And as the image takes shape, a sudden, profound longing rises in her chest. It feels like a thirst she never named, like a traveler sighting a mirage of water after crossing a desert—a yearning she cannot contain.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Where would it be?

speaker: Rust
content: I don't know. But it will appear. Because you are kind, principled, and just stubborn enough. Many will want to help you, and many more will need your help in return.

speaker: Rust
content: Keep moving forward, but always toward the light. Someday, the clouds before your eyes will disperse, and all the questions that trouble you now will find their answers.
A tremor runs through her. Memories surge, a flicker passing behind her clouded eyes, something like tears, or longing. In that moment, Rust knows his words have struck true.
Finally, a crack appears in the armor of her composure. Hypatia's lips part, desperate for more.
...But the words never come. They die unspoken, dissolving into a whisper of defeat.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Hah... There I go again... Always like this...

speaker: Rust
content: ...What is it?
When she lifts her head again, the stubborn rock is armored once more. Hypatia looks Rust squarely in the eye and delivers her answer, each word measured and precise.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I will take your advice and leave for safety with your friend. However, before that, I still wish to complete the one task that lies directly ahead of us.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...This isn't just about my personal obsession. It is also assistance you will greatly need for what comes next.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I suspect that after sending me away, you intend to go to the Furor ruins alone. Am I wrong? You called those people your prey; you won't stand idle while their conspiracy unfolds.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But the Luminaris Society's intelligence network is exceptionally complex. No matter how capable you are, you cannot decipher their data alone. I was once one of them, so I understand their systems, and I have conducted extensive research on Furor. That is precisely what you need now, isn't it?
Rust says nothing, perhaps surprised by the girl's sudden poise, perhaps genuinely considering her words.
Hypatia uses the silence. She stands and offers a deep, formal bow.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I apologize. I know I have been stubborn. I've caused you trouble throughout this journey, and now I make such a request. But before I can move forward with resolve... I must fulfill this duty.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I give you my word: during the operation, I will follow every command and will not complicate matters. Once I have provided the necessary support and ensured the safety of the farland leaders, I will leave Fraser exactly as you arrange.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...You may say suffering is inevitable in this land, but my intuition as a scholar tells me the moment for change has finally come. BR‑005 was a devastating blow, yet it is also the hope they have waited for so long. This is the most critical juncture.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I want to contribute, too. And there are things I can do now. If my skills are insufficient for field operations, then perhaps you could instruct me, Master? I should at least qualify as a somewhat talented student... shouldn't I? After all, I did manage to capture you three days ago.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I'm not entirely without worth. Am I?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Please. I am asking you.
Hypatia manages an uneven smile through swollen, red-rimmed eyes, and for a moment, a genuine brightness pierces the night.
How cruel that such light has fallen upon this dark, desolate wasteland.

Rust finally understands: he cannot move this stubborn rock alone. His gaze shifts toward the horizon. His contact hasn't arrived, but a different, fainter light glides in from the opposite direction, moving toward the plain.
It's someone else. He recognizes it instantly.

speaker: Rust
content: Hm... Not mine. Fraser pursuers, perhaps? Seems we were too engrossed in conversation and missed our window. We'll wait for the next one.
He rises, calmly smothers the campfire, and calculates the distance and timing. Enough time remains. Brushing his hands clean, he turns to Hypatia.

speaker: Rust
content: Well. Now we've got plenty of extra time. Anything else you wish to do? Tell me, I'll see it through with you to the end.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Thank you. I'm sorry to impose, but... thank you. I will give it everything I have!

speaker: Rust
content: Alright, alright. It's fine. I saw this coming.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I understand.
He covers their traces with sand, tosses the still-warm fire remnants onto the sand ship, then signals his contact and boards to reconfigure their route.
They'll take the long way, through high-risk territory to break any trail, before circling toward their true destination.
Sooner or later, she must return to the beginning: to see the ruins of Furor with her own eyes.
In Fraser City
The sky hangs low, a veil of gray gauze blurring Fraser's firmament. Yet the nobility's garden salon remains an island of fragrance and light, where laughter flows unchecked.
The hostess sits alone in a secluded corner, posture languid yet regal. With delicate fingers, she crumbles a honey cookie onto the table, smiling as small birds hop close to peck at the pieces.
A noble approaches quietly and takes the seat beside her.

speaker: Fraser Noble A
content: You seem somewhat preoccupied, Ms. Margaret. Not enjoying the salon?
Margaret's expression remains distant, still shadowed by unspoken worry.

speaker: Margaret
content: Forgive me. My mind was elsewhere. A cherished canary of mine flew from my window some days ago. With the state of the world beyond our walls—the contamination, the sandstorms... I fear for the poor creature...

speaker: Fraser Noble A
content: A pity. If it ventured beyond the city... I fear the odds are grim. The wastes are fraught with more than calamities. But please, do not despair. I have several fine canaries at my estate. You would be most welcome to visit and select a new companion.
Margaret shows no offense. She only smiles and lets out a long, soft sigh.

speaker: Margaret
content: You are too kind. But each creature has its own spirit, does it not? I was... particularly fond of that one...
After a long moment, Margaret rises to her feet.

speaker: Margaret
content: My apologies to everyone, but I must beg your indulgence and end this tea party early. A pressing matter requires my attention. Please, do continue to enjoy the afternoon.
With that, she gives a slight, graceful flourish of her fan and turns away, leaving the gathered Fraser nobles in speechless silence.
As she reaches the stairs, a figure steps smoothly into her path, blocking her descent.

speaker: Helga
content: Where are you heading to, ma'am?
Under Helga's icy gaze, Margaret's smile becomes a mask that gives nothing away.

speaker: Margaret
content: Envoys from the Luminaris Society made an appearance at the farland meeting. Negotiations proceeded favorably. A joint expedition to the Furor ruins is now being discussed.

speaker: Margaret
content: We both know what Fraser truly seeks in those ruins.

speaker: Margaret
content: So... you can rush back home, or you can stay here and continue to watch me. The choice is yours.
Deep in WhiteSands

Starlight washes over the WhiteSands, glazing a landscape thick with the mingled reek of rot and stagnant mire. An Aurum Secretum Warrior moves forward, flanked by a sleek Alchemic Beast that treks through the desert in silence.
A sudden vibration cuts the silence. The warrior retrieves a communicator and sees a message from the Luminaris Society.
The rat has fled, Saina. Track it. Terminate it.

speaker: Saina
content: Mission received.
She bends down, gently stroking the Alchemic Beast's head.

speaker: Saina
content: DisCity spy... I will kill you. I will spill your blood as an offering to my brothers and sisters!

Two Days Later
Outskirts of the Furor Ruins
Day surrenders to dusk. Angular structures stand as solitary sentinels on the sandy ground, their sharp edges softened by the orange-yellow wash of twilight.
This is their destination: the Furor Ruins. But to enter, they must first find a map that promises safe passage within.
According to Margaret's information, this desolate place should be the Furor expedition base, a joint DisCity-Nirvana venture for surveying the region.
Now, not a soul stirs. Only dust moves, settling silently on every forgotten surface.

speaker: Hypatia
content: It seems this site was abandoned days ago...

speaker: Rust
content: Supplies intact, gear in place, but no people... Not a good sign. Stay sharp.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Understood!

As they enter the camp, the equipment bears the clear insignias of both DisCity and Nirvana. Pushing deeper, the air changes: the dust thins, and the evidence of violent struggle grows. Machinery lies in shattered pieces, not just broken but pulverized with what looks like pure hatred.
Rounding the corner into the main hall, they find a body slumped behind a door. And there, scrawled across the far wall in a jagged, rusty brown, is a message:
<color=#dg1f1f>Discity Dogs, Get Out!</color>

speaker: Hypatia
content: These wounds... a mix of deep lacerations and blunt-force impact. Messy. Not the work of trained combatants. Could it have been... refugees?

speaker: Rust
content: Heh, refugees don't pass over bread during a raid just to chew on these instead—
Rust points to the cluttered table, where stale black bread sits forgotten. Beneath it, official reports lie scattered across the floor, their pages a chaotic mix of DisCity and Fraser languages.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Then who would do this...?
Rust casually picks up a report from the table, flipping through pages dense with technical jargon and complex equations. Finding it indecipherable, he tosses it to the expert.

speaker: Rust
content: No ordinary soul could parse this. Takes a particular kind of brilliant mind. Sound familiar?

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...The Luminaris Society?!
[Scene Change]

The building's power has long been dead. In the dim light, they can just discern the shapes of overturned tables and chairs, and the hulking forms of survey equipment, half-shattered.
On the tabletops, small, hardened remnants of abandoned meals share space with sheets of coarse kraft paper—the standard wrapping for farland dry provisions.
Hypatia's eyes catch on a half-buried corner of paper in the ash. She brushes it clean, revealing a fragment of data records, its text incomplete but unmistakable.

Log ID: DSC-BH-2307-05
Subject: Preliminary Investigation Report on Residual Traces in Furor (Birthplace of BR-005)

In accordance with the Committee's directive, our team has completed on-site surveying and initial analysis of residual traces in Furor. The summary findings are as follows:
Multi-point sampling and data analysis indicate that the area exhibits extremely high contamination concentration, yet Hypercube extraction levels remain exceptionally low. Comparison with existing Black Ring data confirms that BR-005 was an anomalously weak Black Ring, incapable of forming a viable mine. Consequently, this site holds no developmental value for Hypercube extraction.
It should be noted by relevant departments: The contamination originating from a Black Ring's birthplace does not dissipate upon the Black Ring's destruction. Significant purification efforts will still be necessary, leading to substantial development and long-term maintenance costs.

Additionally, this investigation has confirmed the dynamic nature of BR-005. Through trajectory backtracking and catastrophe trace analysis, it has been verified that BR-005 has been in a state of continuous migration since its inception. This movement has produced extensive contamination along its path, with contamination levels showing a steady increase, directly resulting in the formation of a high-risk "catastrophe corridor."

Conclusions and Suggestions:
Although energetically weak, the migration characteristics exhibited by BR-005 and the resultant contamination issues necessitate careful oversight and management.
By tracing its migration path, we have confirmed the potential for this Black Ring to undergo continuous strengthening, which would proportionally increase the likelihood of viable Hypercube extraction in the future.
Investigation Team Lead: Albert West

speaker: Hypatia
content: These are all investigative reports on the contamination in Furor... The readings are critically high; the situation inside is dire.
Hypatia sets the documents aside, her attention drawn to the room's center, where a massive device looms in the gloom.

speaker: Hypatia
content: A Hypercube signal detector. Left behind due to its bulk, most likely.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Though superficially damaged, the core structure remains intact. Critical components and stored data should still be recoverable.
Hypatia eyes the device briefly, then summons her Aurum Secretum. Without hesitation, she drives it deep into the structure atop the machine.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Nngh...
The sorcery whispers in her mind once more. Clutching her forehead, Hypatia fights for focus.
Disassemble, separate, secure... Her hands respond with flawless precision, stripping away a component housing in seconds.
At the same instant, a crimson sorcery pattern flares to life on the floor by the hidden door.

speaker: Rust
content: Well now... Seems someone really doesn't want these secrets getting out. You keep looking. See what else they have here.
Rust offers her a nod and strides outside.

speaker: Rust
content: I'll go have a word with those outside.
[Battle]
The Puppets surge toward Rust in an endless tide.
He meets them with flawless precision. Dodging, weaving, and launching counterstrikes in the same motion, he carves through the overwhelming numbers.
The walls are splattered with reddish-black fluid, yet the dismembered Puppets twitch and rise again. For every one that falls, another advances, their fearlessness as infinite as their numbers.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Their taste remains as charming as ever. Still utterly repulsive.

speaker: Rust
content: My part's done here. How's yours coming along?
When Rust returns to the hidden chamber, he stops short. The floor is a sea of chalked equations. In the center, Hypatia crouches with a grave expression, a piece of chalk still gripped in her hand.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No traces... none at all...
Hypatia points to her final calculations with absolute certainty.

speaker: Hypatia
content: The Hypercube radiation logs show absolutely no residual signatures!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Those signatures cannot be scrubbed. The only logical conclusion is... there is no Hypercube in Furor. Not now, not ever.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...The survey data is thorough. Meticulous. The probability of fabrication is negligible.

speaker: Hypatia
content: And the last observational entry was four days ago, meaning the attack coincided with the halt in reporting.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I see.

speaker: Rust
content: So the Luminaris Society had DisCity's data four days ago. They knew Furor held nothing but lethal contamination.

speaker: Rust
content: Yet at the farland meeting, they announced a Hypercube discovery... and arranged for the faction leaders to tour these contaminated ruins...

speaker: Rust
content: Heh, you actually got it right. Those Black Ring ruins were never a discovery site; they were a hunting ground, with the Hypercubes as the bait...
An ominous thought blooms in Hypatia's mind, and a cold dread climbs her spine in its wake. Even afflicted with the Senate's torturous sorcery, she has never felt a disquiet this profound.

speaker: Hypatia
content: The ones who accepted the invitation... they were faction leaders desperate to find Hypercube deposits, hoping to withdraw their people from the war.

Within their factions, they faced the greatest pressure to survive and were the most desperate to find Hypercubes. Thus, they treated the invitation with the highest priority, willing to explore personally.

speaker: Hypatia
content: And Furor was part of the farland territory... If they die here, no one would suspect Fraser. Leave a few pieces of DisCity equipment at the scene, and the blame falls squarely on DisCity and Nirvana.
She lifts her head. The confusion in her eyes is gone, replaced by pure urgency.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What they want... is the lives of those farland leaders. Yokna and the others—they're walking into a tomb!
The farland clans are already divided. Losing several key leaders would plunge them back into total disarray—easy prey for Fraser to carve apart.
They have to stop them! If they don't intercept them before they go deeper into Furor, the consequences will be catastrophic!
The modified sand ship tears along the edge of the ruins, fast as lightning.
As the ruined outline looms, distant figures sharpen into view: the Luminaris Society envoys, leading the farland delegation step by cautious step into the decaying maw of the site.
Hypatia tenses to move, but Rust's hand shoots out to stop her.
His hand points subtly to the side. There, people dressed like refugees appear to be resting, but their eyes are active, scanning their surroundings with vigilant care.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Those refugees... they're impostors?
Rust nods.

speaker: Rust
content: Your former colleagues have come prepared as well. A direct confrontation would be inconvenient. Best to avoid it.
He turns toward Hypatia as he says it, and a faint, involuntary smile appears.

speaker: Rust
content: Looks like you already have an idea.
Hypatia has already unfolded a survey map and begun marking it with swift, precise notations.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Routes... pathways... confirmed contamination zones... If I were the Luminaris Society... here... would be the ideal point for an ambush.

speaker: Hypatia
content: So... we reach the site ahead of them. Disable the traps... then block the routes leading deeper in.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Would a plan like that work?

speaker: Rust
content: Well done, Miss Campbell. Remarkable progress. Truly a genius in the making... I'd say you're ready for your final examination.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...This is hardly the time for jokes.

speaker: Rust
content: I'm not joking. In fact, I've already had your test designed.
With a smile, he folds up the map and hands it to Hypatia.

speaker: Rust
content: A rescue competition. Master versus apprentice. We take separate routes, locate the delegation leaders, and extract them, by persuasion or by force, your choice. The objective: get them out alive.

speaker: Rust
content: Victory conditions... we tally which route extracts more leaders? If you win—or if I lose—either way, Agent Campbell graduates with full honors.

speaker: Rust
content: Oh, and one major stipulation: the agent must return unharmed. Excessive risk resulting in injury means automatic disqualification.

speaker: Rust
content: So, can you handle this on your own, Hypatia?

speaker: Hypatia
content: But why—
He raises a hand, gently but firmly halting her question before it can be spoken.

speaker: Rust
content: We all have our stubborn streak, don't we? Consider this a personal favor, and I know you're more than capable of seeing it through.

Hypatia opens her mouth to speak, then closes it again. Both instinct and logic scream that something is wrong, yet she swallows her objections. The look in Rust's eyes... it holds a determination she has never seen before.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Then you must be careful as well, sir.

speaker: Rust
content: Well said. Do your best out there, top student.
Deep Within the Furor Ruins

Even with the Black Ring destroyed, the contamination here remains lethally potent. The air swims with dark gray particles; the ground, a sludge-covered ruin, is split by countless fissures like infected wounds in the earth.

The area is a fortress of hidden threats. Past the specialized devices at the heart of each trap, Hypatia senses more than a dozen Underground Puppets. These creatures are lurking in the shadows, their locations given away by the faint Aurum Secretum resonance in their cores.

Immersed in a Mania field where hallucination and pain entwine, Hypatia clings to her focus, hoping that she can disarm every trap without being noticed.
Or... she could strike first!
A golden streak pierces the gloom. An Underground Puppet freezes in place. She closes the distance in a heartbeat and cleanly severs its neck.

speaker: Hypatia
content: That's the third one...
Footsteps echo from behind. Hypatia melts into the shadows.
A net of Aurum Secretum erupts from the ground, wrapping an enemy in a swift, crushing embrace.

speaker: Hypatia
content: The fourth...
