And so it continues: the fifth, the sixth, the seventh... until finally, silence. Only the gurgle of contaminated fluid and Hypatia's ragged breathing remain.
Suddenly, a shadow lunges. Her body moves on instinct—crouch, sidestep, strike. Blinding gold light flares. The last enemy pitches backward into the murk.

speaker: Hypatia
content: You... were the last.

speaker: Hypatia
content: A shame, but when it comes to Aurum Secretum... you were simply outclassed.

With the Puppets eliminated, Hypatia turns her focus to the next target: specialized devices modified from abandoned DisCity survey equipment. They must serve some purpose beyond merely framing people.

Deftly, she removes the outer casing. Inside, an Aurum Secretum structure confirms her suspicion. These devices are using resonance to deliberately guide the ruin's contamination, funneling it deep into the heart of the trap.

speaker: Hypatia
content: To think they'd take my creation... and twist it into something this vile.
The girl's fist tightens. She once took pride in creating Aurum Secretum. But now, faced with her own technology turned into a weapon... should she feel remorse?
Hypatia shakes her head, forcing the thought away. This isn't the time for doubt. She centers her focus, ready to destroy the devices.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Disconnecting the primary circuit... done.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is...!!
The instant the device is disabled, black sludge surges together, forming one Puppet after another from the ground itself. Their focus snaps to the only target in sight—her.

speaker: Yokna
content: We've lost contact with the Lumanaris rep. Wandering deeper now is suicide.

speaker: Jabara
content: Look over there, an opening in the Mania! We can make a run for it.

speaker: Rael
content: Let go of me, Jab! I said let go!

speaker: Jabara
content: Forget your pride for now! Staying alive comes first. We'll sort the rest once we're out. You have my word.
[Scene Change]
From a distance, Hypatia watches the leaders slip through the opening she tore in the Mania. A slow breath of relief escapes her.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Not just Aurum Secretum assassins... but Underground Puppets, too. Has the collaboration between the Underground and Fraser grown this intimate?
But something is definitely off here. The contamination in Furor is far thinner than it should be at a Black Ring's epicenter; otherwise, tearing that opening would not have been nearly as easy.
She pulls out the map, finds the intersection where she and Rust parted, and resolves to regroup with him.
But after checking every branching path and shadowed corner, the truth is undeniable: all viable routes are sealed by contaminated cave-ins.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is...?!

Meanwhile, Saina stops short within the Mania field. The deeper she tracks, the more foreign objects she finds beneath her feet. It's clear now that someone has been laying groundwork here, preparing deliberately...
Deep Within the Ruins

At the other end of the ruins' uncharted depths, a cramped space—less than twenty square meters—has been freshly cleared. Aurum Secretum devices pulse along a roughly circular perimeter, pushing the thick contamination back to expose the ground beneath.

There, a web of cracks spreads, all converging inward toward a narrow, perfectly drilled abyss, just wide enough for a person. Banished beyond the barrier, unseen entities press against the Aurum Secretum field, rustling with a palpable anxiety at their separation.

Inside the circle, Daik of the Luminaris Society kneels at the pit's edge, carefully retrieving fragments. He strives for devout focus, but something in the agitated white noise beyond the perimeter snags his attention.

speaker: Daik
content: Who's there?

A point of red light pierces the darkness. A figure in black steps across the perimeter. The air crackles as Aurum Secretum and sorcery bite into his skin, peeling it back from his face, but he doesn't slow. By the time he fully enters the circle, the damage has already sealed itself over. Rust rolls his shoulders, offering Daik a casual, unnerving smile.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: I'm glad I've found the right man.

speaker: Rust
content: Hello, Representative. Weren't you meant to be leading the leaders on a grand tour? Did you get separated from the group?

speaker: Daik
content: Your lodgings lost communication last night. That's when I thought today might afford a chance for a... private meeting. I'm pleased I haven't been waiting for the wrong person, either.

Daik gathers the abyss fragment, its sinister glow pulsing in his grasp, and places it into an intricate Aurum Secretum vessel. After sealing it, he cradles the container in his palms and recites several phrases with devotional reverence. He then transfers it to a precisely crafted sorcery box, securing it within three successive layers before finally, cautiously, closing the lid.
Only then does he turn, lifting his gaze to assess the lone, uninvited guest standing before him.

speaker: Daik
content: So you're the spy who's been giving the Society such a headache. To see you in the flesh at last... Conventional wisdom had you targeting some high-profile dignitary. What prompted the sudden departure from Fraser to come here?

speaker: Daik
content: And that dead weight from the Campbell line? How did you shake her off? You killed her?

speaker: Rust
content: Miss Campbell is the only person in the Luminaris Society who truly merits the title of scholar. A mind of that caliber shouldn't be brought here to have her eyes sullied.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Especially by filth like this.

He raises his hand and fires three rapid shots. Enhanced by the ruin's contamination, the flesh-made bullets strike the three Aurum Secretum devices suspended overhead, shattering them alongside the one-eyed Underground rune sealed within.

The ground shudders. The Mania field twists violently, collapsing Daik's painstakingly simulated matrix. The surface rift snaps shut, and with it, the inheritance remnants he had fought to reclaim vanish.

speaker: Daik
content: A pity. That sorcery was painstakingly replicated. Data calibrated through countless iterations. We had only just begun to replicate some characteristics of a Black Ring. A remarkable feat... you shouldn't have destroyed it so carelessly...

speaker: Rust
content: Truly remarkable work doesn't need to hide in the shadows. You know as well as I do that yours cannot bear the light of day.

speaker: Daik
content: Heh. Aren't you just the same?
Daik narrows his eyes, studying the specimen before him with meticulous attention.

The agent's coat is made of an unusual material—both protective and restrictive, like a binding seal—pulled taut against his form, emphasizing his corpselike pallor. The injuries from crossing the barrier have vanished, yet on his neck, several uncanny dark markings linger faintly.
Around him, contamination slowly gathers. The marks on his neck begin to writhe like something alive, and from their depths, a faint red glow seeps through.
Daik can't help but smile at the sight.

speaker: Daik
content: The Sophos of the Underground once spoke of this art: using a Black Ring's power to reshape life. The blessed ones chase the Ring and flee from it, yet their very existence remains tethered to it.

speaker: Daik
content: How long has it been since you left your "mother"? Even breathing must be a labor for you now, mustn't it?
Rust doesn't answer. Instead, he closes his eyes, draws a shallow breath as if savoring the air, and then smiles to the watching researcher.

speaker: Rust
content: It is a burden, I won't deny it. But it's more than enough to handle the likes of you.
The crimson glow snakes down his neck and across his skin, igniting all the way to his fingertips.

Rust's eyes blaze red as energy surges from the fissures in his neck, flooding his entire being. He raises his gun and fires. Daik ducks with a sharp cry, shielding the collection box he just secured.

Simultaneously, the box itself shudders violently. An Aurum Secretum field erupts from it, bending the dense Mania field around it to warp the bullet's path. The shot veers into the darkness—a dull impact, then distorted shrieks. Guided by the Aurum Secretum, dozens of corrupted tentacles pierce the barrier, lashing toward Rust.
He doesn't flinch. Tossing his gun aside to tangle several limbs, he charges straight into the assault.

The tentacles slice through his coat, cut into flesh and vessels, then immediately convulse and crackle as if electrocuted. From Rust's wounds flows an alien fluid, neither blood nor ichor, melting the corruption like magma. The rampaging entities shriek and recoil from this human-shaped abomination.

Unimpeded, Rust closes on Daik, crushes the Aurum Secretum box underfoot, and seizes him by the throat, lifting him clear off the ground. Daik chokes violently, yet his voice travels directly into Rust's mind through the bones of the hand gripping him.
—The mad scholar is thrilled beyond measure at this close encounter with an experimental subject.

speaker: Daik
content: ...This vessel, just as they described. Even a form lesser than the Sages possesses such formidable power... What extraordinary heights have the Sophos' arts reached?

speaker: Daik
content: How did it feel... to receive a Black Ring's baptism? How resilient is the life it reconstructs? You've died once... no, at least three times, haven't you? What was it like? What changes did it forge?

speaker: Daik
content: ...If I were to unmake you completely now, could I observe the entire process of rebirth? How would your new form manifest? Would there be variations?
Rust finds the researcher's obsessive thirst for knowledge almost amusing.

speaker: Rust
content: Adelaide lacks the patience to explain these things to outsiders. Are there other Undergrounders lecturing in Fraser? Where? What have they been teaching?

speaker: Rust
content: ...Are you trying to create another Black Ring?

speaker: Daik
content: Aren't you anticipating it? Everything you are... is clearly a Black Ring's gift. You should be its most grateful apostle...

speaker: Daik
content: Argh!!
Rust slams him violently against his precious Aurum Secretum box, cutting his rant short. Daik looks up, and sees only cold hatred and contempt staring back.

speaker: Rust
content: Not everything. Take this, for example: your most coveted "Underground sorcery." I learned it on my own.
Blind rage surges as Rust grabs him, hand rising for another blow when suddenly—
Whoosh!!

With the Aurum Secretum box at its center, a sorcery of eight layers rises from the ground, forming a circle roughly six feet wide. The sudden resonance makes Rust freeze for a split second. In that instant, a wave of thick, black contamination surges from the side, tears Daik and the fractured box from his grasp, and rolls to a stop at the edge of the circle.

The sludge writhes as it deposits both man and box. After several fluid shifts, it reshapes itself into a hunched figure cloaked in black—an elderly form, robed and still. Beneath the grateful, reverent gaze of the Luminaris representative, the figure slowly rises.
They stare at one another in silence, each seeing something in the other's face that is at once deeply familiar and utterly alien.
The quiet holds until a slow drip of melting contamination falls from the ceiling. Only then does Rust bow his head and laugh.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Heh. I thought I'd have to tear Fraser apart brick by brick to find your kind. Never expected you to just... deliver yourselves to me.

speaker: Rust
content: Do you really despise me that much?
He speaks at last, in a tongue Daik cannot fathom, but to Rust, every syllable is clear.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: ...We gave you chances. More than one. To return to us.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Yet all we received... was betrayal. Time and again...

speaker: Undergrounder
content: So. Enough...
Sorcery draws the contamination into his palm as the Undergrounder prepares to strike. His voice, when he speaks, is heavy with sorrow.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: No one remains to speak for you. Those who still held any care for you are dead. You have failed every soul who ever placed faith in you.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: They will curse you for eternity. Never forgive. I have been tasked to kill you as many times as it takes. And when I am gone, others will come to scour you from existence...

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Traitor. Deserter. The one who abandoned the Black Ring and survived by walking over the corpses of his own... Remember my words. Remember who ends you... Remember...

speaker: Undergrounder
content: You are beyond redemption.
Rust listens quietly until the end, then lowers his head.

speaker: Rust
content: I see... What a pity.
Then he raises his head again, that familiar smile returning to his face.

speaker: Rust
content: After I died last time, it seems I forgot all of you again.
The words ignite the Undergrounder's rage. He launches into an incantation, and the recently recovered box against his chest begins to shudder violently.

Inside, fragments of the inheritance vessel still pulse with latent power. That resentful energy now awakens, magnifying the single-eyed sorcery until it multiplies across the chamber. From beyond, countless malevolent presences start to converge. The time for games is over. Rust tenses, every muscle coiling for the fight.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: You exist because of the Black Ring. The Black Ring gave you bone and blood, time and time again...

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Give it back, betrayer! No matter how many times you die, you must return it! You cannot escape...!
...Escape? The notion is so absurd that it nearly draws a genuine laugh from Rust.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I don't escape. I've been waiting all along.

speaker: Rust
content: The Black Ring gave me nothing but a curse. You'd better take every last shred of it back!

He raises his hand and drives his fingers into his own chest, sinking deep into the fissures etched across his body. Bone and blood dissolve and spill over, transforming into chaotic Mania under his will—a torrent he hurls forth, shattering the oncoming sorcery. All the while, a bone-deep fury consumes him.
Does he hate the person before him? No, that grudge is far gone from his memory. What does linger is the sound of their pious words, the memory of what was sacrificed in the name of "faith."
...In the end, regardless of which side they're on, when it comes to stubbornness, they're all the same.
His blood, bone, and flesh are ignited now. Every cell in Rust's body has become a weapon. Just as he prepares to unleash everything—
Whoosh!

speaker: Rust
content: —What?!

A hair-thin beam of golden light pierces the contamination, striking the Aurum Secretum box in the Undergrounder's arms with exacting precision. A high-frequency vibration shudders through the air, and the half-open lid slams shut as if crushed under immense pressure, sealing all chaotic energy inside. It cannot be reopened.
The Aurum Secretum box has been decrypted and locked; he can no longer complete the extraction. The Undergrounder lifts his head toward the source of the attack, but Rust is already moving.
He withdraws every ounce of power he'd been channeling for the confrontation and rushes toward the sudden intervener, placing himself as a shield between her and the fray.
Behind him stands Hypatia, of course. When she sees Rust approach, she flinches visibly. Her master is so stunned, the reprimand he had ready dies on his lips.

speaker: Rust
content: Sigh...

speaker: Rust
content: Didn't we agree to split up? You—

speaker: Hypatia
content: I've neutralized all the traps! The leaders are safe!
Her answer comes in a rapid burst. But the effect is spoiled when a grain-sized Aurum Secretum bee slips from Rust's pocket and silently flies back to its rightful owner.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm sorry. I was concerned it would be too dangerous for you to act alone...
She finally lowers her head, her voice soft with confession.

speaker: Rust
content: ...No apology needed. You performed exceptionally. You've already surpassed your master.

speaker: Hypatia
content: You're teasing me again...
But Rust isn't joking. The earlier rage has cooled, allowing his mind to clear and reassess.
The enemy's most dangerous weapon has already been neutralized—by his own exceptional apprentice, no less. She turned his strength against him. A lone Undergrounder no longer poses a real threat.
Across the space, the Undergrounder is staring directly at them.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: ...Aurum Secretum control... extraordinarily precise...
His gaze falls on Hypatia, and he chuckles with sudden recognition.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: So it's you... the "limb" the Famine Sage could not bear to sever...

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Truly... a remarkable talent...

Hypatia cannot comprehend his praise. The language is too warped, too guttural, like a nauseating, moan-like distortion. Beneath the cloak, his shadowed face feels impossible to look upon directly, stirring a deep, instinctive dread.
Can the figure before them even be called human? At his feet, the black sludge left by the Black Ring gathers and kneels, worshipping him—worshipping whatever he holds.
And when she sealed the Aurum Secretum box, Hypatia felt it: an evil once buried beneath Furor, still pulsing with the aura of the inheritance. It made her tremble even more.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Are we going to fight... that?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Wait! Your body—
Despite the dim light, Hypatia clearly sees the fissures etched across Rust's body. Their red glow seems even more ominous in the dark.
Rust shifts back half a step, shielding her from the Undergrounder's sight. As he does, he tugs discreetly at his collar, pulling it up to hide the marks.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't look. They're just unsightly blemishes. I'm fine; this is just me... restraining my true strength.

speaker: Rust
content: You saved all the leaders. Our mission is accomplished. We've won. Now, victory means leaving safely. You've passed your final exam; congratulations on graduating. Let's go.

speaker: Rust
content: They know their limits. They don't have what it takes to stop me.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Really...?
Hypatia remains uneasy. Unexpectedly, it is one of their opponents who speaks first, agreeing with Rust's assessment.

Daik clears his throat, his excitement still palpable from witnessing the battle's advanced techniques. However, with Hypatia's intervention and the Aurum Secretum box now sealed, a clear victory for his side is no longer feasible.

speaker: Daik
content: You're correct. Having seen your capabilities firsthand, I recognize we lack the means to detain you both. However... we cannot allow you to dismantle the Society's designs entirely.

speaker: Daik
content: The Unity Gala will proceed as planned, exactly as Fraser intends... We have allies you haven't accounted for.

The device concealed on his body transmits its signals silently. Daik is certain that their plan is still salvageable. Everything is proceeding on schedule, the critical moment drawing near; his only regret is that he won't be there to witness it.
He releases a quiet sigh and turns his gaze to the Undergrounder beside him.

speaker: Daik
content: ...For wisdom. For the city-state.
The ally receives the signal. Meanwhile, someone who knows him well senses that something is wrong.

speaker: Rust
content: You... Damn it!
Rust's hand flies to his holster, but it's empty. His weapons were already torn apart and consumed by the tentacles. It's too late to intervene.

speaker: Rust
content: Nngh—!
Something deep within him stirs. From the depths of the fissures, a force clamps down, locking his movements. He looks up. The Undergrounder is casting.

It's a vicious sorcery. The Undergrounder's left hand withers and rots; half his cloak crumples inward as flesh and fabric collapse. The fanatic is sacrificing half his body just to hold Rust, unevenly, for a moment. And meanwhile—

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ah!

Without warning, the Undergrounder raises his right hand and drives a beam of crimson light straight into Daik. The red Mania sorcery pierces through Daik's satisfied smile, blasting away part of his head in a spray of flesh. It happens too fast. Hypatia doesn't even have time to scream.
How... Weren't they allies? She can't process it, yet in that same heartbeat, she suddenly understands what Rust meant by "brutal battlefield."

Across the space, the fanatic's plan is complete. With only half a body remaining, the Undergrounder trembles violently, clutching the Aurum Secretum box as his ravaged form shakes with low, breathless laughter.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Remember... traitor who cast off his own name...

speaker: Undergrounder
content: No matter how many times... all the Black Ring gave you... will be reclaimed... cursing you unto death...
He vanishes into the pool of his own purulent blood, merging with the surrounding filth.

Only Daik's grotesquely disfigured corpse remains. Rust hasn't yet broken free from the curse, but he's already noticed something crucial: the enemy used the same flesh sorcery he knows. Then, footsteps approach from nearby.

speaker: Rust
content: Hypatia... get out of here. Now... You can't stay...

speaker: Rust
content: This is... their true purpose. You have to go...

speaker: Hypatia
content: I don't understand... No, I won't leave you...

speaker: Rust
content: Go...
BOOM!!

Following the narrow path Hypatia used to enter, a violent explosion suddenly blasts open the exit. For a moment, the thick reek of blood and decay is swept aside, and with it come those who will uncover the "truth."
The newcomers' eyes widen in horror at the scene: two blood-drenched figures and, not far off, a corpse.

At their head is an Aurum Secretum Warrior, her face twisted with fury. She too seems to have just broken free from a Mania field, and in her grip is a Puppet fragment stamped with a DisCity mark. She slams it down before them all.

speaker: Saina
content: ...I knew it... I KNEW IT!!!

speaker: Saina
content: TRAITORS! MURDERERS! I'LL KILL EVERY LAST ONE OF YOU!
Saina's blade flashes as she lunges, steel aimed straight for Hypatia's throat—a killing blow reserved for mortal foes.
CLANG!

Hypatia's Aurum Secretum petals erupt, shielding Rust and shoving the Alchemic Beast back. In the same motion, she sweeps a current of Aurum Secretum toward Saina, forcing her off course and breaking the lethal trajectory.
Battle after battle has sharpened the girl's instincts; she's now more capable in combat than she knows.
The interception infuriates Saina even more. Steel clashes against Aurum Secretum again and again, the metallic echoes ringing through the ruins, but she cannot break Hypatia's guard.

speaker: Saina
content: What are you all doing? Just standing there gawking?!

speaker: Yokna
content: Hold on!
Yokna moves cautiously, trying to hold back the Aurum Secretum Warriors as they ready for battle.

speaker: Yokna
content: Let's hear the facts first! I don't believe this girl could've done this.

speaker: Yokna
content: She's with the Luminaris Society too, and she's helped us before. Why would she kill her own colleague?

speaker: Saina
content: Why—?
Saina draws out her words, menacingly stepping toward Yokna.

speaker: Saina
content: To keep you from finding the Hypercubes, obviously. Leave you running in circles forever, beggars in your own WhiteSands!

speaker: Saina
content: Do you even know who she is?

speaker: Saina
content: Hypatia Campbell. Former administrator of this very place, Furor.
Saina lifts her curved blade, leveling it at Hypatia's face like an executioner delivering judgment.

speaker: Saina
content: And now, back in the same place, you've killed our guide. Planning to leave us all trapped here to die.

speaker: Saina
content: Do you really hate farlanders that much?

speaker: Saina
content: The people of Furor trusted you so much... You have no conscience left, do you?
At the word "Furor," the dormant sorcery in Hypatia's mind flares awake once more, stabbing a sudden, sharp pain through her chest.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... that's not true.
Hypatia steadies her breathing, willing her voice into something resembling calm.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I've analyzed the survey data for this region. There is no Hypercube here. The information the Society gave you from the start was fabricated.

speaker: Hypatia
content: In fact, the Society used the Hypercubes as bait to lure you here... with the intention of using the Mania to kill you all.
Hypatia's explanation hangs in the air, plunging the space into an uneasy silence. The faces of the farland leaders are a mosaic of doubt, denial, and weary suspicion.

After wandering for so long through the dangers of Furor, they have not been without their own uncertainties. But accepting her words means accepting the loss of their last, desperate hope. It's a pain none of them is ready to bear.

speaker: Yokna
content: We can't sort this out here. Let's continue this back at camp.

speaker: Jabara
content: But whoever's lying, they still want us dead! I say we retreat now, or we'll all be wiped out by the Mania—
[Screen Shakes]

speaker: Jabara
content: Argh!
Saina's Alchemic Beast pounces on the merchant, pinning him under its foot.

speaker: Saina
content: Shut up, you spineless worm!

speaker: Saina
content: She betrayed Fraser long ago! She conspired with Disians, sold our war plans, left my brothers and sisters... Not one of them came back!
Saina's gaze cuts across the disheveled merchant and the skeptical Yokna, sharp with contempt.

speaker: Saina
content: Whatever you worthless lot think... between her and the Aurum Secretum Warriors, this is blood debt!
Hatred is the easiest thing to provoke. It thrives beyond self-interest or morality. As one, the Aurum Secretum Warriors draw their weapons, all aimed at the two before them.
The air grows taut and still, drawn tight as a bowstring.
What should she do? Hypatia glances sidelong at Rust. The crimson glow at the DisCity spy's throat flickers wildly, pulsing like a fading heartbeat.
But thankfully, he's still conscious. For now.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Don't fight them head-on... Listen to me. I'll surrender, create a diversion. When you see the chance... run. Understood? You can make it.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Absolutely not. In our current state, if you're captured, they'll kill you without hesitation.

speaker: Hypatia
content: My status still holds some value to them. But you... they'll show no mercy to someone from DisCity.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I was the one who insisted you bring me here. I cannot... and will not let you die for it!

speaker: Rust
content: Hah... Don't worry. I can't die. I've still got people who...
Hypatia doesn't yet grasp the deeper meaning of his words, and at that moment, someone else arrives.

speaker: Saina
content: Can't die? Let's test that right here. I'll chop you into pieces and see what's left!
With that, Saina lunges again.
The Aurum Secretum weapon arcs toward Saina's flank, but Rael's curved blade intercepts it mid-air, buying a fraction of a second.
It's all the opening Saina needs. She closes the distance to Hypatia in a flash.
Though the Aurum Secretum whips back in defense, the concussive force still hurls Hypatia backward. She crashes into the wall with a sickening thud.
Rot-weakened stone gives way. The wall collapses inward with a roar of dust and debris.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Nngh!
A metallic sweetness floods her mouth. Her body won't respond.
Saina advances, step by deliberate step, blade poised for the final strike. Then, she halts abruptly.
Hypatia lifts her head. Between her and the warrior, she sees it: the tiny Aurum Secretum bird Margaret had given her, fluttering desperately in the line of fire.
It's far too small, too fragile, to stop an enraged Aurum Secretum Warrior. Yet there it is.

speaker: Saina
content: Die!

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... Don't!
The blade cuts through the air with brutal force, and the Aurum Secretum bird, without making a single sound, is cleaved in two mid-flight.
Then, a dazzling white light erupts from its broken form, engulfing the entire area.
Under the cover of the flash, reinforcements arrive at last.
A figure in pure white descends before the girl, white feathers drifting around her like a gentle blizzard, as if to soothe and purify the world itself.
The DisCity ambassador takes Saina's wrist in a soft grasp, and a strange warmth flows into her body, washing through every nerve.
The sensation tingles, then soothes. As if all her anger has been drawn out, Saina's entire being settles into abrupt tranquility.
Her weapon hits the ground with a clang. The conflict halts.
The newcomer gently waves her fan, offering a radiant, tranquil smile.

speaker: Margaret
content: Please, let us all compose ourselves. This is hardly the manner for a proper conversation.
Then, shrapnel, arrows, and stray projectiles—all are caught in a gentle embrace of feathers and lowered delicately to the ground.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ms. Margaret!

speaker: Margaret
content: You have done exceptionally well. Now, please leave the rest to me.

speaker: Margaret
content: I am Margaret Kervoz, Peace Ambassador of DisCity. The honor is all mine.
The phrases "DisCity" and "Peace Ambassador" serve as triggers, unleashing an instant wave of reaction.

Whispers, tension, and agitation ripple through the crowd as they fix their eyes on the composed woman before them. What trick did she pull? How was Saina—a demon of death only moments ago—turned docile as a kitten?

speaker: Margaret
content: Rust, take Hypatia and go. I will handle matters here.
After a swift assessment of both sides' combat strength, the man leans in to deliver a low, urgent whisper.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Hang in there, DisCity's Peace Dove.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Wait, Margaret is still—mmph!

speaker: Rust
content: I'm sorry.
He takes a final look at Margaret, surrounded by the crowd, then grabs Hypatia and slips away.

speaker: Margaret
content: Good. Now that the more... spirited participants have departed, shall we have a proper conversation?
White feathers still drift in the air, like a living barrier, keeping anyone from reaching Hypatia and Rust.

speaker: Margaret
content: You followed a promise here, filled with hope, seeking the Hypercubes... only to discover a cruel deception. Your efforts were in vain. I share in your outrage and your pain.

speaker: Margaret
content: I am well aware my presence is unwelcome. I once tried to avoid direct contact, to send intermediaries. But when I saw how you treated a girl who had genuinely aided you in the past, I could no longer remain silent. Knowing the danger, I came anyway.

speaker: Rael
content: She's a Disian... Kill her!

speaker: Margaret
content: Mmph...
Margaret gracefully evades the attack, her smile never faltering.

speaker: Margaret
content: I wish to speak with you all openly and honestly. We are not enemies. DisCity sincerely desires to help you overcome this plight.

speaker: Margaret
content: Look. I have come without weapons, without guards, without soldiers. Even my special power is merely a "little trick" to calm hostilities and encourage peaceful dialogue.

speaker: Margaret
content: What is it you still fear?

speaker: Margaret
content: I bring nothing but peaceful intent. My presence here is my proof of sincerity to you.
Though her smile is perfect, it fails to soften the hard gazes fixed upon her.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: Her power has a limit! Attack her directly!
A sudden storm of weapons—bullets, spears, arrows—descends upon the figure in white.
Twilight approaches, the last scent of blood carried away on the wind.
The old woman's steps across the sandy earth are both firm and light. After days of long travel, she finally lifts her dust goggles, revealing a pair of stern, penetrating eyes.
From the fortified hill ahead, figures rise one after another from behind sandbags and mounted guns, waving to her with unguarded joy.

speaker: Camp Guard A
content: It's Helga! Helga's back! Lift the lockdown!

speaker: Camp Guard B
content: Should've given us a heads-up, Helga! We'd have rolled out the welcome wagon!

speaker: Helga
content: Heh, save the fuss. Just let 'em know I'm here.
[Scene Change]

Inside the Farland Alliance council tent, the leaders have just concluded a hollow discussion. The real question—whether to bind their future more closely to Fraser—has, since yesterday's incident, been settled in a consensus.

This is the scene Helga walks into. From the seat of honor, Jabara scrambles to his feet, ready to surrender the chair to the rightful authority—the former revolutionary soldier and current Farland Alliance diplomat newly returned from Fraser.

speaker: Helga
content: Stay put. You look comfortable there, and I'm good standing. Wouldn't get a clear view of all your faces from way back there anyway.
Her gaze sweeps over the companions she hasn't seen for so long.

There is Yokna, who has governed the rift valley for years, reliable in minor matters, yet maddeningly indecisive when the stakes are high. Jabara, guildmaster of the merchants, has spent a lifetime chasing coin; he lacks vision, but can acquire anything, anytime. And Rael, all impulse and rough edges, but a superb warrior and an even better trainer...

The farlands would not function without them. Knowing their flaws all too well, Helga had instructed them before leaving to convene a proper council on the matter of Fraser and DisCity. Now, as her eyes land on the blackboard at the far end of the tent—the word FRASER stark upon it—a faint conclusion settles in her mind.

speaker: Helga
content: Let's hear it. What's the situation?

speaker: Jabara
content: Ahem. We trust you've been well? With the unrest along the route, and no word for so long, perhaps bringing some of our own escort would have been wise in hindsight...

speaker: Rael
content: Hmph. And who's to say "our own" ain't got DisCity spies mixed in? With her skills, she is safer moving alone. Not all of us need a whole damn guard detail just to cross a road.

speaker: Yokna
content: Enough. If our intel on DisCity wasn't shit and Fraser wasn't breathing down our necks, Helga wouldn't have had to risk her neck for us in the first place.
Yokna shoots a glare at the two men—all talk, no substance. She spits out her toothpick and launches into the story of everything that's happened since Helga left.

speaker: Yokna
content: Never would've guessed... that kid's Hypatia Campbell. No wonder she knows Aurum Secretum tech like the back of her hand. I liked her—still do—but... the proof's right there.

Helga's brow tightens. She remembers the girl as they met in Fraser days ago, but Margaret never mentioned authorizing a journey this deep into the farland territory. And the man with her... almost certainly a DisCity spy. Then there's also the Luminaris Society to consider...
Her eyes flick toward Saina, hunched in the corner, silently honing her blade without a glance upward.

The Luminaris Society's influence spreads through the farlands on the reputation of its Aurum Secretum Warriors. They already have the people's trust. Add a Disian to the mix, and this situation can only sour.

speaker: Helga
content: Seems the schemers got restless while I was away.

speaker: Helga
content: They all think they're hunters. All convinced there's treasure buried out here in these WhiteSands...

speaker: Helga
content: First they feed off our dead comrades' despair, then they prey on the living's hope. Fine. Can't blame us if we bag the prize before they do.

speaker: Helga
content: Step into these swallowing sands, and be ready for 'em to be your grave.
She steps to the blackboard and begins methodically laying out the intelligence gathered since her infiltration of Fraser City.

speaker: Helga
content: DisCity hasn't won. But we haven't lost, either. What matters now is this: neither DisCity nor Fraser has a damn clue where the Hypercube veins are since the Black Ring vanished.

speaker: Helga
content: That Black Ring, the one our farland kin poured everything into, is just gone. It's not that they won't tell us. They don't know where it is, either.

speaker: Helga
content: This "Unity Gala" is nothing but a consolation prize. A peace offering to shut us up.
The tent, after days of heated argument, falls abruptly silent. The leaders' eyes meet in flickers, then dart away.
Hands clasped loosely before her, Helga meets each gaze in turn, steady and deliberate, reading the unspoken conflict on every face.

speaker: Yokna
content: At least Fraser's still trying to get on our good side. They get it. We're all tied together. Sink or swim as one. They wouldn't just ditch the farlands when things get rough. Why else send that Society rep here to show off their Hypercubes?

Though her voice carries a hint of hesitation, Yokna continues to argue for the value of the Luminaris Society's Hypercube technology. Her people need that mine, and her determination to secure them is absolute.

speaker: Jabara
content: Can we trust any of it? What if... Fraser's just looking for a polite way to back out of their promises?!
Jabara's mind works with the volatile speed of a market ticker, churning out ideas that defy all conventional logic.

speaker: Rael
content: **** 'em all!

speaker: Rael
content: How many times have those DisCity mutts ground us into the dirt?! The only reason the farlands are still on a leash is 'cause we got no real way to fight the Mania. If it weren't for the Aurum Secretum tech, we'd all be corpses already.

speaker: Rael
content: That Black Ring that can mine Hypercubes was paid for in Furorian blood. And then it just happens to get lured right to the DisCity border? Whose damn scheme is this, huh?
Rael... Guess there's no point in even trying.

speaker: Helga
content: Farland Alliance... From the very first day, I've never once seen you all stand as one.

speaker: Helga
content: But this time... you've really outdone yourselves.
Helga swallows her rebuttal. With a silent, inward sigh, she turns to leave, only for Yokna's voice to cut through the tent's tension.
Yokna draws herself up, extracts a briefing document from her coat, and lays out their next plan.

speaker: Yokna
content: We've captured that DisCity Outland Affairs Officer who showed up after. Calls herself Margaret Kervoz. She's already secured in our rock prison.

speaker: Yokna
content: Care to question her?

speaker: Helga
content: ...The DisCity Outland Affairs Officer?
[Scene Transition: Exterior]
Rock Prison

A fortress of stone and despair. Prison cells are gouged into the sheer cliff face, each sealed by a heavy, steel-reinforced door. The only opening is a small ventilation window, its frame so savagely eroded by relentless wind and sand it has nearly melted away.
Beyond that barrier is nothing but a sheer, hundred-meter drop. The sole access is a rickety hanging cage. To leave otherwise would require wings.
Inside one cell, the prisoner appears almost serene. With slender fingers, she delicately peels open a withered grain to feed a small bird resting in her palm.
The groan of the prison door breaks the quiet. She turns her head and smiles.

speaker: Margaret
content: I'd almost thought you'd forgotten me. I'm pleased you've decided to visit at last.

speaker: Margaret
content: Last time, emotions were running rather high. I'm not sure how much you truly heard. Perhaps I should reintroduce myself properly.
The harsh surroundings cannot diminish her innate grace. She greets each visitor with a measured smile and the impeccable bearing of a hostess receiving guests in a salon.

speaker: Margaret
content: You must be Ms. Yokna, of the rift valley encampment. We met briefly before. Your people were... somewhat less cordial than you.

speaker: Yokna
content: That depends on the company, miss.

speaker: Margaret
content: And you are Mr. Rael. I've heard stories of your beautiful wings.

speaker: Margaret
content: Ah, Mr. Jabara. You may not recall, but we have met twice before: at the N.F. 106 Great Expo, and again at the embassy reception in Fraser.
Jabara's expression tightens. He swivels toward Helga, urgency sharp in his movement.

speaker: Jabara
content: As you know, I've traveled extensively for the Alliance over the years. It's... not surprising certain attentive parties might have noted my movements...

speaker: Margaret
content: I am aware that each of you leads a city-state or community in the farlands. You represent countless ordinary people who call it home.

speaker: With that, the short teenager bounces urgently toward Vautour Bleu in her lounge chair, grinning as he gives a playful salute.
content: As the Peace Ambassador, I have long wished to speak with you all directly about the future of the farlands. Yet my messages have been met with silence...

speaker: Margaret
content: Now, it seems, we finally have the chance.

speaker: Rael
content: **** your peace! The farlands never asked for peace from DisCity, not when it's built on our people's blood. We only want blood for blood!

speaker: Jabara
content: They say this one's silver-tongued in Fraser, yet leaves no trail. Now she has let two DisCity killers slip right through our grasp. We can't afford to be gentle.

speaker: Margaret
content: Please... let me explain.

speaker: Margaret
content: Consider, if this were truly a trap laid by hostile forces from DisCity, assassins would have been lurking around the ruins. The moment you emerged, they would have overwhelmed you.

speaker: Margaret
content: But that is not what happened. I came to you alone, unprotected, to clear their names and to speak with you directly.

speaker: Margaret
content: The real culprit has used your prejudice to frame two innocent people. Their goal is to sow deeper hatred between the farlands and DisCity.
Her voice holds a gentle warmth, and her manner radiates genuine sincerity.

speaker: Margaret
content: I know I am not welcome here. You may even see me as an enemy. The hatred between DisCity and the farlands has festered for so long it feels unbreakable. And now, we have just endured another war.

speaker: Margaret
content: But I had to come. For the sake of the peace I believe in.
All eyes watch the woman with wary scrutiny. Though their captive, she stands unbowed. Her posture is straight, her bearing unbroken and resolute.

speaker: Margaret
content: In my memory, the farlands and DisCity were not always at odds. When I was a child, my father often traveled here for diplomatic exchanges.

speaker: Margaret
content: It is true that during its expansion, the DisCorps government committed many atrocities against the farland people. That ended with the government's collapse after the establishment of EDGE in N.F. 103. Afterward, the farlands and DisCity entered a period of reconciliation.

speaker: Margaret
content: The turning point was N.F. 104. That year, DisCity suspended Hypercube exports to the farlands, declaring them an emergency strategic resource and imposing a full embargo.

speaker: Margaret
content: That embargo rapidly soured relations between us. By then, I was already in Fraser, hearing only one narrative—

speaker: Margaret
content: It claimed DisCity was hoarding vast Hypercube stockpiles while leaving people of the farlands to die in catastrophes, all while secretly selling them back at exorbitant prices to drain the farlands of their wealth.

speaker: Margaret
content: But the truth was quite different.

speaker: Margaret
content: In N.F. 104, a massive, unexpected explosion occurred in our Hypercube mining operation, deep in the West District mine...

speaker: Margaret
content: What you now call the Furor Black Ring is actually the fifth Black Ring. What exploded back then was the second.

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes... We understand the farlands' suffering because DisCity endured a similar calamity long before.

speaker: Margaret
content: That Black Ring destroyed vast infrastructure, and countless workers were lost to the Mania. Hypercube mining ground to a halt; far from exporting, DisCity itself faced a severe resource crisis.

speaker: Margaret
content: While we fought desperately to contain the Black Ring and restore production, the farlands not only offered no aid but launched waves of public condemnation and protests against us.

speaker: Margaret
content: Tell me... who was pulling the strings behind the scenes? And who stood to gain?

speaker: Yokna
content: Get to the point. What are you trying to say?

speaker: Margaret
content: Fraser acts as the middleman in trade between the farlands and DisCity. After the Hypercube shortage post-N.F. 104, Fraser stockpiled most of the Hypercubes that DisCity did export, then spread the lie that DisCity had imposed a monopoly and embargo, all to stir hatred.

speaker: Margaret
content: We tried to make amends. At the N.F. 106 Great Expo, we hoped for a peaceful gathering to unite all sides. Instead, Fraser detonated BR-003, sabotaging the Expo I had worked to organize and directly sparking the year-long Outland War.

speaker: Margaret
content: Do you truly believe BR-003 was a Ring Weapon deliberately created by DisCity? When such a thing emerges, who suffers most? Do you think we welcomed it?

speaker: Margaret
content: Fraser fears contact between us because they know the buried truth will surface. When it does, the people of the farlands will clearly see who they should truly stand with.

speaker: Margaret
content: I did not mean to assign blame, only to set the record straight. To you, they claim DisCity restricts trade; to DisCity, they express grave concern over the Farland Alliance's hostility. All while Fraser keeps its own hands clean.

speaker: Rael
content: I won't listen to your twisted words! No one but Fraser ever lifted a finger to help us. The Aurum Secretum Institute, the Anti-Mania devices—which of those wasn't built with Fraser's support?

speaker: Margaret
content: In fact, we have maintained normal trade relations. Mr. Jabara, you are aware that recent Hypercube shipments to the farlands came through deals with Nirvana, all at fair prices. I should add—I personally facilitated those agreements as well.

speaker: Jabara
content: W-what... how did you...?
Under the weight of their murderous glares, Jabara mops his brow, his hand coming away slick with cold sweat. Finally, with a visible internal shift, he steels himself to confess everything.

speaker: Jabara
content: Yes, alright! After the Great Expo, I secured the exclusive transport routes between our territories. When Fraser halted the Hypercube trade because of the war, I arranged several shipments through Nirvana. If not for the sandstorms and the Apostles after the Black Ring, those Hypercubes would already be in every town!

speaker: Jabara
content: Why are you shouting? Haven't you used Hypercubes too? I did this for everyone's good, and this is the thanks I get?!
Jabara's DisCity smuggling was the last thing Rael expected. Incensed, he turns his fury away from the traitor and fixes it on Margaret.

speaker: Rael
content: Spare us your divide-and-conquer tricks! Everyone knows Jabara's a weathervane who bends with the wind, and Yokna wasted her time at that worthless Expo because her nerve failed. Disian, our blood once soaked this sand from your blades. You should've known then, some of us don't forget...

speaker: Margaret
content: You take pride in wielding Aurum Secretum, don't you, Mr. Rael? Even Ms. Campbell never imagined her brilliant creation would birth such a twisted form of hope in these sands.

speaker: Margaret
content: But she didn't develop Aurum Secretum for war, or to turn on other humans. It was meant to fight the Black Rings, to survive catastrophes. When did the Aurum Secretum Warriors' purpose shift to vengeance? Who twisted your aim with hate, and now leads you chasing the Black Ring to your graves?
Margaret times her pause perfectly, watching the flush of anger darken Rael's face.

speaker: Margaret
content: Heh... I believe I've clarified the past grievances. I trust you'll judge wisely.

speaker: Margaret
content: Now, let me present what I've actually come to offer you.

speaker: Margaret
content: Recently, BR-002, the second Black Ring lurking beneath the West District mine, was eradicated. The threat is gone, and new mining operations have been revived.

speaker: Margaret
content: The West District is rebuilding its facilities. Once production resumes, the new Hypercube output won't just make up for the deficit since N.F. 104; it will surpass previous levels.

speaker: Margaret
content: We will soon be free from the scarcity that has plagued us, and this prosperity, I sincerely wish to share with all of you in the farlands.
The room explodes into a clamor of shock.

speaker: Jabara
content: Y-you mean... D-DisCity's new mine... the Hypercubes... you'd share with us?

speaker: Margaret
content: Of course. Provided we maintain a peaceful partnership.

speaker: Yokna
content: But as Rael said, the last time Disians showed up in WhiteSands, it brought only blood. If you truly want to negotiate, DisCity should show good faith first, just as Fraser has.
After a moment of visible struggle, Yokna grits her teeth and forces the words out.

speaker: Yokna
content: Fraser has already named their price. If DisCity wants to win us over, you'll have to offer more!

speaker: Jabara
content: Ah! Right! If that Society representative wasn't killed... we could've had our own Furor mine. Having our own would be far better than trading with DisCity!

speaker: Yokna
content: Exactly. Extracting Hypercube veins is difficult, but Fraser has promised the Luminaris Society will help us establish our own mining operation.

speaker: Yokna
content: We trust the Luminaris Society far more than your shadowy Nirvana!

speaker: Margaret
content: Heh... The Luminaris Society?

speaker: Margaret
content: Haven't you realized it yet? Who do you think staged that incident in the Furor ruins?
The warmth vanishes from her voice, leaving only a cold edge.

speaker: Margaret
content: Let me tell you something: DisCity sent our most skilled prospectors to camp near the Furor ruins for half a month. They surveyed for over ten days and found no trace of Hypercube deposits.

speaker: Margaret
content: The Luminaris Society's claim that they can find Hypercubes in Furor—what a daydream!
With a subtle gesture, Margaret calls a dove to her hand.
The small creature tilts its head, its soft cooing delivering Hypatia's logical assessment.

speaker: Hypatia
content: The Hypercube radiation logs show absolutely no residual signatures!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Those signatures cannot be scrubbed. The only logical conclusion is... <color=#fb9259>there is no Hypercube in Furor. Not now, not ever</color>.
A deathly silence hangs for a breath, then chaos erupts in the cramped stone cell.

speaker: Jabara
content: What?! You're saying there are no Hypercubes in those ruins? Impossible!! I've bet everything on this!
—No Hypercubes in Furor... The Luminaris Society lied to us?
—No, no. The real liar must be this woman right in front of us!!
—It's this damned Disian!!
Amid the chaos, a figure lunges toward Margaret. A sharp kick sends them stumbling back with a heavy thud. Into the cleared space steps Helga, her face stern.

speaker: Helga
content: Enough. Stop making fools of yourselves. Get out, all of you. I need to talk to this Disian alone.
Resuming her seat, Margaret unfolds her ornate, delicate fan. With practiced grace, she lifts it to conceal half her face, leaving only her enigmatic smile visible behind its frame.

speaker: Margaret
content: Thank you, Helga. I knew our friendship meant something.

speaker: Margaret
content: Now, it's just the two of us, like when you came to Fraser to kill me. Did you know you're quite bad at that job? Guerrilla warfare and assassination are entirely different. The first only needs conviction. The second requires letting go of all sense of conscience.

speaker: Margaret
content: Take Rael, a pure assassin. He isn't swayed by what he hears or sees. But you, my friend... you believe what your eyes show you.

speaker: Helga
content: Save your breath, Margaret. Your tricks don't work on me.

speaker: Helga
content: You're good at your job. You spun a web in Fraser for over a decade. So why are you in our hands today?
Helga's words are a scalpel, cold and deliberate, laying bare a raw nerve in Margaret.

speaker: Helga
content: You're short on people. Your so-called friends don't always listen. Now you're doing the dirty work yourself, even stooping to use Campbell's daughter.

speaker: Margaret
content: Now you're being unfair. I genuinely admire my young friend.

speaker: Margaret
content: She's kind and strong, but so often lost... the kind that makes you want to lend a hand. I've always believed she'll find her own way.

speaker: Margaret
content: Fraser is the one truly using you. They stirred your people to cultivate the Black Ring, then turned them into Aurum Secretum Warriors to die on the front lines. Don't you want payback for a blood debt like that?
Helga's eyes narrow. Behind her gray irises, a storm of memory churns—smoking gun barrels, wounds that never truly healed. Her body almost trembles, a tremor born of old pain.
Dead embers flare to life.

speaker: Helga
content: Revenge doesn't move me. If I were that easy to sway, I wouldn't have stepped into this cage myself; I'd have just let them kill you.

speaker: Helga
content: You're an Outland Affairs Officer and a spy. DisCity must've invested a lot in training you. So I'm sure you know why the farlanders hate you all so much...

speaker: Margaret
content: Grievances need settling. People want peace. That's exactly why I... chose this path. In the end, nobody wants war except the butchers who profit from it. Today's DisCity fights only for peace.
Helga lets out a short, incredulous laugh.

speaker: Helga
content: Fighting for peace? Don't make me laugh. After BR-005 fell, DisCity could've pushed for total victory, but you stopped. You ask me if DisCity didn't want to win? It's not that you didn't want to. You couldn't.

speaker: Helga
content: The DisCorps hang over your heads like a sword. They've earned their honors but can't go home. You've got a new mine in the West District, but after months of bickering, production hasn't even started. You're pressured from all sides, with massive wartime investments in Hypercubes and manpower waiting to be paid back.

speaker: Helga
content: How could you afford to break Fraser completely? What you really want is to dig up the power networks behind it, use them as leverage, and bleed them slow through blackmail. Your real goal is "mutual profit"!

speaker: Helga
content: So the serpent in the shadows turns into a dove released for peace, singing pretty while flashing its colors to fool the world.
Margaret's elegant smile stiffens, her teeth catching briefly on her lower lip.

speaker: Helga
content: Is there really room to drive a wedge between the farlands and Fraser? Or are we just bait in your game—cast out, fish hooked, line reeled in, then the catch slaughtered?

speaker: Helga
content: But now you're the stranded fish here in WhiteSands. Nobody believes you. Nobody helps you. I know about your "influence." It's temporary. Once they sober up, everything you've said will be just wishful thinking.

speaker: Margaret
content: And you? How much better are you than me? Your followers are fools helping to count the profits of their own slaughterers. What can you do besides scream for blood and more violence?

speaker: Margaret
content: You know better than them. Your trip uncovered plenty of Fraser's schemes. But who can you actually tell? I bet since you got back, you've been listening to endless squabbling, stuck and unable to move.
Margaret is right, Helga realizes. She isn't suited to the assassin's subtle craft. Her first impulse, provoked by mere words, was to reach for her gun.
Kill her? Then lead a brutal purge of every threat to the farlands? The logic of a soldier was clear.
But she is not that revolutionary commander anymore, the one who knew only how to aim and fire.
Without hesitation, Helga rises to her feet.

speaker: Helga
content: You have until dawn. Choose: be escorted to Fraser as a prisoner, or crawl back to DisCity. Whatever friendship we had is done.
Helga storms out, the door crashing shut in her wake. Outside, the clang of a bell cuts through the air, calling the pulley operator to duty.

speaker: Margaret
content: You can refuse my offer. But you know the truth: alone, you can't change any of it. The farlands will keep being used, lied to, and led down a path of ruin.
The rattle of shackles echoes as the iron cage ascends. Margaret finally rises to her feet. Her words come then, clear and unshakable.

speaker: Margaret
content: Stop limiting yourself. Look up. See the wider world. If history has shown that relying on Fraser is no longer rational, why not try a new path?

speaker: Margaret
content: After I'm gone, the farlands' fate will continue. Ten years, twenty, a century from now, in a future you won't live to see. Stuck here in WhiteSands, bled dry generation after generation... Is that really their only destiny?!
Finally, the iron cage grinds upward and out of sight. Silence reclaims the prison. Margaret lowers herself back onto the cell's only chair, the one with a broken leg.
It wobbles treacherously, but she finds her center effortlessly, a subtle smile curving her mouth.

speaker: Margaret
content: Helga, I'm afraid you're the one truly trapped in this desert.

speaker: Margaret
content: As for me...
Her gaze drifts to the prison window. The birds perched along its ledge stir as if sensing a silent command, their wings a sudden flutter before they scatter across the distant, open sky.
[Scene Change - Farland Market]

Across the sprawling encampment, only a few figures are packing their belongings. Most vendors barely look up, their attention already returned to their work. A well-dressed visitor approaches one of the stalls.

speaker: Vendor
content: The big blow's changed course, so we're pullin' up stakes. Ain't much left on the shelf. If you see somethin' you need, best grab it now before it's all boxed up.

speaker: Vendor
content: There you go! In a bit of a rush, are we?

speaker: Vendor
content: Ah, sweets for the young lady! Takes me right back to my own girl. Here, take the lot. A little sugar helps any journey sit lighter, and it looks like you've got a serious one ahead. You and your brother mind yourselves out there in the grit, y'hear?

speaker: Vendor
content: Whoa now, hold on! That's far more than we could ever use. You're too generous. Please, take some back. We don't hold with that sort of thing around here. Driving prices up just makes it harder on folks elsewhere tryin' to get by.

speaker: Vendor
content: I've already taken more than enough. Oh, well... bless your heart, miss, you're too kind. Well... if you're sure, I won't say no! Can't believe my luck, makin' a proper sale like this on my way out the door. My girl'll be tickled pink. Thank you, truly.
Still chattering, the vendor finally accepts the money pouch from Hypatia, his face lighting up with unrestrained delight.

speaker: Hypatia
content: We should be the ones thanking you. Truly, we are grateful for the supplies.

speaker: Hypatia
content: If it's not too much trouble, could you help bring these to the car? My brother is rather occupied at the moment. I'm afraid he can't step away.
The vendor, helping to load the goods, lets out a cheerful chuckle when he spots Rust in the vehicle.

speaker: Vendor
content: So you're the brother, eh? Keep your wits about you in the deep desert. Something's stirred up the beasts lately, more'n usual. You look after your little sister, now.

speaker: Rust
content: Haha, of course! What sort of brother would I be if I didn't? The kind better left as worm-food in the WhiteSands, I suppose.

This "brother" has a face pale as chalk, yet he wears a brilliant, incongruous smile. His words are even more bizarrely out of place. The vendor can only stare, bewildered, before mustering an uncomfortable smile in return. Hypatia smoothly steps in, ending the conversation.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Goodbye, and thank you, for everything. I wish you and your daughter all the best.
The moment the vehicle door shuts, Hypatia's smile vanishes, washed away by a tide of worry.
[Scene Change]
Wind screams, whipping sand into a biting haze as the open-top vehicle tears across the desert.
Hypatia grips the wheel, knuckles white, her foot jammed against the accelerator in a rigid lock.
Where can they go? Where should she go?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Supplies are secured. But... what's our next step?

speaker: Hypatia
content: The communicator remains silent. With no word from Margaret, the farland mission is at a standstill.

speaker: Hypatia
content: And Mr. Rust's condition... he can't move yet. Perhaps we should seek out the "contact" he spoke of. At the very least, we can get him to safety...
Just as she sinks deeper into thought, the vehicle jolts violently. Hypatia snaps back to reality. An ash monster is already on the roof, peering down at them.
—Bwak.

The creature is knocked clean off by a single blow from their newly purchased desert specialty: an extra-long, extra-dry, super-hardened bread. The culprit of this ridiculous maneuver is none other than the legendary agent Rust, who now slumps in the passenger seat with eyes squeezed shut, his forehead slick with sweat, like a feverish patient caught in a delirious dream.

speaker: Rust
content: Focus. We are technically running for our lives.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Mr. Rust, you've... recovered already?

speaker: Rust
content: Hard to rest when the driver is philosophizing and misses the local wildlife moving in.
Rust props himself up halfway, movements strained. He reaches to peel the Aurum Secretum sutures from his skin, then offers them back to her.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Mr. Rust... what truly caused these wounds?

speaker: Hypatia
content: I recognize traces of an Underground origin. Similar, yet not quite the same. They leave lasting damage, don't they?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Given the severity, perhaps it would be best to reach out to that "contact" you mentioned. If they are still nearby, they could escort you to a place where you can receive proper care.

speaker: Rust
content: And then what? Send you off on a solo rescue mission for Margaret?
Her face turns pale as she bites her lip.

speaker: Rust
content: Look, it's fairly obvious these aren't your garden-variety lacerations. This is a potent, volatile... secret power. When you're a fully-fledged legendary spy someday, you can file a formal inquiry.

speaker: Rust
content: Right now, I need to rest and concentrate on accelerating my recovery. If you're truly in need of a conversational partner...

speaker: Rust
content: Look. That bird is back.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...It's back?
Through the shroud of ashen dust, a wing of white feathers emerges from the distant haze, descending like a promise of divine guidance.

speaker: Rust
content: DisCity's Peace Ambassador has come to you.
[Bird Special Portrait] [Interactive Click]

This construct is different. It is formed almost entirely of concentrated special power, using Aurum Secretum only as a binding agent. This requires the host to pour a vast reserve of their own energy into it, forging what is essentially a personal "clone."

speaker: Margaret
content: ...Hypatia... is everything going smoothly...

speaker: Margaret
content: Can you hear me... or... have you not yet reached a secure location...
Finally, the tears she has held back for days break free, streaming hot down her cheeks.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I-I can hear you! Ms. Margaret? Are you alright? Are you safe?
A familiar, gentle voice flows from the little bird's beak. It flutters its wings, lifting in an unsteady arc, then hovers before the vehicle's windshield.

speaker: Margaret
content: I am well. The people of the farlands are extending every courtesy... Thanks to the intelligence you provided, our dialogue is proving most pleasant...

speaker: Hypatia
content: I... I'm just so relieved to know you're safe.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm sorry... I failed the mission you entrusted to me... and I put you in great danger.

speaker: Margaret
content: You mustn't worry. You have already performed admirably. I'm transmitting coordinates to a location where I have arranged for support and a safe house.

speaker: Margaret
content: You may rest and recuperate there. Once you have delivered the intelligence that you found inside Furor regarding the Underground to my specialists, we will proceed with the next phase of the mission.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Understood, Ms. Margaret. I'll set out at once... and I'll get there as quickly as possible. Please stay safe!

speaker: Margaret
content: Do not be afraid. Whenever you have need of me, I shall be with you...

speaker: Margaret
content: And I trust a certain legendary agent will, of course, honor his commitment and guide you with his utmost diligence. Isn't that so, Mr. Rust?
With that, the bird attempts to land on Rust's head. He smoothly intercepts it by donning his hat, a silent smile his only reply.
[Scene Change - Farland Market]

speaker: Helga
content: ...Name's Helga, with the Farland Alliance. You can trust me. We're tracking two DisCity spies who pose a severe threat to the Alliance, and I need your eyes. Just tell me straight: have any outsiders come through here?

speaker: Vendor
content: DisCity... spies? No wonder... No, ma'am, I sure haven't. Never laid eyes on a Disian in my life! DisCity's a world away. What'd they be doin' all the way out here?
Saina leans close to whisper something in Helga's ear. Then she saunters toward the vendors, her voice rising clear and deliberate as she speaks.

speaker: Saina
content: The two DisCity spies we're looking for are a man and a woman. They're killers. So I suggest every one of you think very carefully about whether you've seen them. Or...

speaker: Saina
content: ...would you like me to help jog your memory?
[Scene Change]
With the coordinates recalibrated, the off-road vehicle tears across the Whitesands, throwing up a plume of pale dust.

speaker: Rust
content: That perked you right up, didn't it? She certainly has a way with young girls.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Because... at least now I know what to do...

Margaret is safe, the plan can proceed, their objective unchanged. It's an enormous relief for Hypatia, who had feared she'd ruined everything. To make amends, she floors the accelerator, pushing the vehicle forward in a determined surge.

Outside, the Whitesands blur past in a pale monotony, but the scholar's eye catches irregularities along their route. Each time they pass large rock formations, clusters of shadow linger in the darkened recesses.
They gather in strange silhouettes, small groups lurking near the sandy paths. Their intent, and their target, is unmistakably clear.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...What... are those?

speaker: Rust
content: ...Pursuers. Stay sharp.
Rust tightens his grip on the gun he never holstered. Before his warning can fully leave his lips, the figures vanish, only to reappear instantly, clinging to the sides of their off-road vehicle.

A dull thud of metal, an explosive bang of tires. The vehicle lurches violently, nearly throwing Rust clear. He summons every ounce of strength to wrench the wheel, aiming their ruined momentum straight for a fragile section of rock wall.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I'll handle them. You do what you must.

The pursuers attack with ferocious intensity. Rust unleashes coils of red and black sorcery, snaring one attacker's legs while dodging another's blade. A wave of pain sears through his recovering body, making his movements falter.
Hypatia pulls herself from the vehicle and sees Rust surrounded, trading blows with multiple Aurum Secretum Warriors. The wounds on his half-healed body are reopening—he won't last much longer.

They can't afford a drawn-out fight! With that assessment clear, Hypatia's hands fly over the vehicle's twisted frame, fingers tracing the embedded Aurum Secretum. Resonance blooms under her touch, waking the metal at every node.
Just as she loses herself in the work, a cold glint flashes from the vehicle's shadow. A blade swings toward her, murderous and swift.
Hypatia arches backward in a desperate dodge, strands of severed hair drifting to the ground. Her eyes widen. She knows that face.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I remember you. You're... that Aurum Secretum Warrior from before!

speaker: Saina
content: Perfect. You recognize the woman who's going to kill you.
Fine sweat beads on Hypatia's brow. Though her mastery of Aurum Secretum far exceeds Saina's, it still takes every shred of her strength to bend the material just enough to pin her opponent down.
The two of them hold there, locked, each breathing hard, neither yielding an inch.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I don't wish to harm you... Please, don't make me do this.

speaker: Hypatia
content: We are not the killers. At the Furor ruins, there was a third force present, apart from us and the Luminaris representative. The Luminaris Society has long been collaborating with the Underground. That scholar never suspected them... which is why he was caught defenseless in the sudden attack.

speaker: Hypatia
content: There are no Hypercubes in the ruins. It was a trap set by the Underground—using false intelligence to lure the leaders, aiming to capture every neutral faction of the Farland Alliance at once! When we uncovered their plot, they immediately shifted blame, framing us as murderers while still achieving their goal: escalating the conflict.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Margaret has already warned you about the truth. Why can't you let this go?!

speaker: Saina
content: Heh... Truth? How many honest words have ever come from a Disian's mouth? You're all liars! All this damn contamination was brought by you!! This tear zone stands as proof of your crimes!

speaker: Saina
content: You want the farlands threatened and oppressed forever. You can't stand to see us live decent lives. That's why you're after those Hypercubes. Starting with that bird-woman, none of you deserve anything but misery. Don't even think about leaving the WhiteSands alive.
At those words, the last thread of Hypatia's restraint finally snaps.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What did you do to Margaret?!
Saina's eyes dart between the Aurum Secretum spider and Hypatia.

speaker: Saina
content: Her? She's finished. Hehehe... You hear me? That bird-woman has been taken. It's over for her!

speaker: Saina
content: Now that I'm in your clutches, I accept my fate. Drop the false pity! Go on! Kill me!!

speaker: Saina
content: Even in death, I'll be the spark that ignites the rage of every farlander... then... I'll drag you down to hell with me!
Blinded by rage, Saina explodes with sudden, shocking strength, driving her head violently into the Gilded Machina that binds her.
The impact hammers through Hypatia, staggering her backward, her weapon nearly flying from her grip.
Blood gushes from the wound on Saina's brow, running over the Aurum Secretum tracings. The metal drinks it in, and a thick, sanguine aura erupts from her body, heavy and suffocating.
She closes in, each step a dark, bloodied stamp in the white sand. The utter madness in her eyes is a chilling, visceral threat.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... why...
Nearly stunned by this raw, self-annihilating hatred, Hypatia recoils, her back hitting a ruined wall.
She can't...
She can't confront her like this.

In that moment, the dove streaks into view, intercepting Saina head-on. It moves with preternatural agility. Even when struck, it merely dissipates partially before cohering again, a phantom of energy and will.

Meanwhile, more Aurum Secretum Warriors have locked onto their position. Seeing Rust's injuries and his struggle against the numbers, they split their forces with chilling efficiency—one group pressing Rust, the other advancing on Hypatia.
This can't continue. Rust needs treatment. Now.
Hypatia takes a breath, forcing calm as her eyes sweep their surroundings.
Their car is a half-crushed wreck. No other vehicle in sight. They can run, but they need cover, a hidden place, and fast.

speaker: Hypatia
content: We can go in there.

An intense calamity tear comes into view. The area is a churning mass of perpetual storms and thick, vile contamination. The sky burns with a sickly purple-red hue, split now and then by jagged veins of lightning.

speaker: Hypatia
content: It's a catastrophe tear zone... a Mania zone that formed after the catastrophes shifted course following BR-005. Anomalies erupt there with unnatural frequency, and the terrain can reshape itself within a day. Once inside, we'd be difficult to track.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Both Mr. Rust and I are Sinners. Our innate resistance to Mania is higher than that of ordinary people... even Aurum Secretum Warriors.

speaker: Hypatia
content: If we hide in there, we might just lose them for good.
The growl of the engine returning to life cuts through the chaos like a command.

Rust evades a blade, weaves quick sorceries around his closest pursuers, and pulls back. As he passes the white dove, he lends his momentum to its strike, a unified blow that throws Saina off her feet.
The off-roader races alongside him. At the last second, Rust drops smoothly into the passenger seat.
His eyes follow Hypatia's gaze ahead, and he understands their destination instantly.

speaker: Rust
content: So that's your plan? A bit dangerous. Thrilling, though. It's one way to go, I suppose.

speaker: Rust
content: Go when you're ready. I'll handle the monsters. Remember, your only job is to protect your heart.

Before Hypatia can process his meaning, her foot stamps the accelerator. The car groans like a dying creature, lurching clear of the closing encirclement as it speeds toward the terrifying tear in the earth.
Saina, seeing her prey escape, charges after them in a blind rage.
Then, the vehicle plunges into the tear.

speaker: Saina
content: You're not getting away!!
Saina's enraged cries vanish behind them as the battered off-roader plunges headlong into the storm-ravaged catastrophe zone.
Weightlessness hits instantly. The violent tempest seizes the vehicle, tossing it like a child's toy.
The metal frame shrieks as panels peel away like paper. There is no control here, only the fight to remain aware as the world tears itself apart around them.
The vehicle does not land. At last, it comes apart in midair, shredded by the furious Mania.
The two are thrown clear like broken dolls, tumbling into the chaotic, lightless depths of the tear.

speaker: Saina
content: Damn it, after them!
Helpless to do anything but watch them disappear, Saina curses under her breath and immediately moves to give chase.
A swift, nimble figure steps in to block her path.

speaker: Saina
content: What are you doing?!

speaker: Helga
content: Fall back. That's an order!

The aura of command emanating from the farland matriarch steals the breath from Saina's lungs. Helga is indeed leading this operation, but hatred has already burned away reason. Saina lifts her chin, meeting the elder's gaze in open defiance.

speaker: Saina
content: Why? If even DisCity rats dare go in there, why can't we?

speaker: Helga
content: No one survives a Tide of Ashes that strong unprepared. Are you trying to get everyone killed?

speaker: Saina
content: Then I'll go alone! The cowards can stay! You talk about protecting us. Where were you when our people were humiliated, sacrificed? Now you won't even chase down two rats abandoned by Fraser and cut off from DisCity!
<size=52>SLAP!</size>
The sudden blow leaves Saina's mind blank. When sensation returns, her right cheek burns as if struck by a cannon.
Ignoring Saina's outburst, Helga pulls two sets of protective gear from her vehicle and tosses them at her feet.

speaker: Helga
content: If you're fool enough to go in there, don't you dare claim to be one of my people even if you come back alive!
Meanwhile, inside the tear zone...
Hypatia's head swims as consciousness returns. The world had spun her like a rag in a barrel. Now, as her vision steadies, she sees only endless gray mist stretching in every direction.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Ms. Margaret? ...Mr. Rust?

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Ms. Margaret? ...Mr. Rust?
The endless gray mist swallows the surrounding air and space. Yet when she speaks, her voice cuts through with shocking clarity, echoing through the fog.

speaker: Rust
content: Shhh—
A hushed voice comes from beside her, followed by a steadying hand on her shoulder. Hypatia turns to see Rust's form flickering in the gray mist, appearing and vanishing like a ghost.
Perched on his shoulder is the dove, radiating a soft, white light. Though faint, its glow mysteriously pushes back the dense fog, creating a small, clear pocket around them.

speaker: Rust
content: We're both here. But we're certainly not alone in this place.
He gestures toward several Apostle phantoms drifting aimlessly in the distance. They appear to have lost BR-005's call, leaving them disoriented and confined to wandering along fading energy traces.

speaker: Rust
content: This tear zone isn't like the Black Ring; it has physical boundaries. We just need to find the right bearing and cut straight across. And take care not to disturb our local "friends."

speaker: Rust
content: Let's move. Margaret has a little power left. She'll help shield you, too.

speaker: Dove
content: Coo coo.

The dove nuzzles its head against Hypatia's cheek. Though silent, the gentle pulse of Margaret's power flows through it, soothing the searing headache that has tormented Hypatia since they entered the catastrophe tear.
The three of them—if one counts the dove whose true body is far away—begin to pick their way cautiously through the zone.
[Fade to Black, Same Location]

As a pathway of the Black Ring, the tear zone perpetually maintains dangerously high M-value. An endless succession of contaminants and disaster phenomena bleeds into one another, twisting the terrain.
Carefully skirting Apostle remnants while dodging calamities, the three travelers look haggard already, and they've only been here a short while.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Pant... pant...

The longer they stay, the more Hypatia feels consciousness drowning in thick, resistant fluid. Her thoughts slow, her steps waver. Even with Margaret's constant aid, the mental strain remains overwhelming.
Shadows flicker at the edge of sight. Irritating whispers and hallucinations brush against her mind.
Rust and the dove have noticed her state. They stop deliberately, waiting. Hypatia grits her teeth, pushing herself forward. She refuses to be the one who holds them back.
After struggling up a high rock for a better view with them, her legs finally give out beneath her.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm sorry... the density of Mania here... it's far stronger than I expected.

speaker: Rust
