content: Without this intensity, we couldn't keep our pursuers at bay...

speaker: Rust
content: Don't worry, you're holding up. This tear zone is just an obstacle. We'll get through it. I'll handle the monsters. With Mr. Rust here, there's nothing to fear.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Is that what you were thinking when you made such a reckless choice?

speaker: Rust?
content: "Oh, this person is strong, so I can trust him. I'm with the right person, so I can let go." Hehehe... That's why you'll never be enough, Hypatia...
The voice is eerily cold, its tone entirely unfamiliar. As Hypatia watches in disbelief, the figure of Rust begins to distort before her eyes—

speaker: Hypatia
content: Who are you?!
[Scene Transition: Inside the Catastrophe Tear]
The monsters are gone. Emptiness reclaims the space.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ugh... nngh...
Hypatia clutches her head in pain, trying to pinpoint when the hallucination began. More urgently, if that Rust was an illusion, where is the real one? And where is Margaret?
She staggers, steadies herself, and scans the area. The gray fog has vanished. In its place, dim silhouettes gather, more shadowy figures taking shape before her.
Are they... illusions, or ghosts?
The phantoms emit faint, fragmented whispers, audible only when she draws near.

speaker: Wandering Phantom
content: You really think the elders were right? That we might find Hypercubes here, where the Black Ring passed through?

speaker: Anguished Phantom
content: No... there's nothing... No Hypercubes here. I was wrong. I never should've brought everyone here... Nothing inside but monsters... nothing at all...

speaker: Suffering Phantom
content: It doesn't matter if I die here... but you must... the folks back at camp... they're still waiting...

speaker: Lingering Phantom
content: Search again... keep looking... Perhaps in the next Black Ring... we'll find what we seek...
Hypatia faintly remembers hearing that after the war, many farlanders ventured deep into Mania fields and catastrophe tears across the Whitesands, searching for the lost BR-005 veins.
Others might have dismissed it as a reckless gold rush. But for the farlands, it was a desperate bid for their homeland's very future.
But they lacked the knowledge. They lacked protection. Most invested everything into little more than a dream.

Now their phantoms pass straight through her, a bone-chilling cold that seeps from her soles to her skull. She spins around, but they flow onward, unmindful of her presence, murmuring their regrets to one another as they fade into the gloom.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is...?

Perhaps it is her scholar's instinct, but she suddenly realizes these phantoms are all moving with purpose, drifting toward the same destination: the absolute darkness at the catastrophe tear's heart.
Where are they going? What lies in the deepest dark of the tear?
The questions burn in her mind, and she is just about to follow when—
[Flash images: Luminaris Society Director + Undergrounder + Laughter sound effect]
A pain sharper than any she has ever felt lances through her skull, dropping her to her knees.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What...
The pain is immense—excruciating, radiating from the marrow as if every bone is being charred by infernal fire.

The brand on her neck erupts, surging with frantic growth in this Mania zone. Like a poison vine gorged on nutrients, it spreads and burns, releasing all its long-suppressed power and agony back into her body.
The world flickers madly between black and white, the ghostly figures of the farlanders twisting into blurred distortions. Hypatia clutches her head, a silent scream locked in her throat.
Someone, please... help me...
Mr. Rust, Ms. Margaret, anyone... please... I beg you... help me...
Just as her consciousness teeters on the edge of collapse, a voice—gentle, yet unnervingly chilling—cuts cleanly through the fog of her agony.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Hypatia. So you've found your way here as well. I thought only one Campbell would ever stand in such a place.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What...
Through the haze of agony, a familiar figure materializes, someone who shouldn't be here. He crouches before her as he did in childhood, his hand reaching out.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Come with me, my dear sister. We have been bound by blood since birth. We have always been together... and so we shall remain. Isn't that true?

speaker: Adelaide
content: You know I have always needed you, just as you need me. Even if the world turns its back on us... by the Golden Rose, I will remain at your side. Is that not what you've always wished for?
...Brother?
The agony is overwhelming, and the buried, childish longing for family affection nearly swallows her whole.
Her hand moves on its own, reaching for Adelaide. But just before her fingertips brush his, a shock of cold reason tears through her mind.
Wait. What are you doing, Hypatia?
Have you really fallen this far? To actually consider seeking guidance from Adelaide?

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... you're not...

speaker: Hypatia
content: You're not my brother!!
At her near-frenzied shout, a streak of white light shoots from beside her and slams into the phantom.

It's Margaret's dove. The bird beats its wings with fierce fury, striking Adelaide's form like a raptor defending its nest, each impact sharp enough to pierce. Under the relentless assault, the phantom shudders, then dissolves into splintering light, fracturing like a shattered mirror.
Freed from the illusion, Hypatia drags in a ragged gasp. She clutches the dove to her chest and holds it there, unable to let go.
The agony from the brand still hasn't subsided; each breath is a slow, deliberate kind of torture.

speaker: Dove
content: Coo?
The dove, so ferocious a moment ago, now tilts its head and looks at her, nuzzling her cheek with tender comfort. A soft white light radiates from its small form, wrapping Hypatia in a calming glow.
The pain in her body suddenly recedes. Cradling the dove in her palms, Hypatia leans in, carefully returning the gentle nuzzle.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Thank you.
The dove takes flight again, moving with nimble grace. It hovers a short distance ahead, suspended as if waiting for Hypatia to follow.

speaker: Dove
content: Over here. This way leads out of the Tear Zone. We'll make for the rendezvous. I've already located Rust. Let's move ahead and regroup with him.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But I...
She bites back the words.
I want to explore deeper into the tear zone; I think I've detected unusual fluctuations. The sentence forms in her mind, clear and urgent, but she can't bring herself to say it out loud.
She is the one holding everyone back. Rust and Margaret have both stopped to wait for her. Without her, they might already be safe.
She led them into this peril. What right does she have to suggest they linger for further investigation?
What justification, other than a scholar's intuition—a guess, nothing more?
The dove, seemingly oblivious to her turmoil, grows impatient. It flutters up and down, darting ahead as if urging her to hurry.
Hypatia takes two hesitant steps forward, only to discover another dove has appeared behind her, in the opposite direction.
It's identical to the dove before her, emanating the same gentle, guiding radiance.
The realization hits like a physical chill: she is still trapped. The illusion hasn't broken.
Which way... should she go?
In the seconds she hesitates, two more doves materialize around her, then three, then countless others—reflected like fragments in a shattered mirror, each one dancing, beckoning.
Will you come with me?
The words seem to hum in the air, just beyond hearing.
Don't you want to follow?
And then, in perfect, unnerving unison, they wheel away, each taking a different path.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Wait—!
Wait! Don't go!

She dashes toward one of the light specks, but the sand beneath her gives way. It becomes soft, treacherous, as if the ground itself is against her. She stumbles, scrambles up, and runs again, hand straining toward that fleeing speck of white.
As if answering her plea, one of the doves wheels in a graceful arc and returns, hovering just before her.
Its form shifts, becoming the silhouette of a person.
The silhouette reaches out and takes her hand.
And just like in that dream, her palm meets a warmth that is utterly, undeniably real.

speaker: Margaret?
content: There, there, it's all right now. I won't let them harm you anymore.
Hypatia clutches her hand tightly. A gentle radiance flows from the point where their hands meet, a warmth so convincing she never wants to release it.
This is real. Undeniably, irreducibly real.
Margaret's voice reaches her then, soft and steady, comforting her in the same gentle way she always has.

speaker: Margaret?
content: You're simply exhausted. The destination is nearly in sight, which is why each step feels so heavy now. You have failed no one, Hypatia.
She places a comforting kiss on the girl's forehead.

speaker: Margaret?
content: The elderly scavenger looks toward the dilapidated amusement park, sighing.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What... should I do...
Her breath shudders as the brand on her neck burns deep into the marrow, sharpening the torment in her mind.
Yet she clutches Margaret's hand, stubborn, refusing to let go.

speaker: Margaret?
content: You will find those flowers. You will bring the promise of the Hypercubes to the farlands. This is not a place for you to linger. Rest a moment, and then continue on your way.
Margaret's gaze holds a gentle smile; even the wind around her seems to soften. A fine, sharp sting pricks Hypatia's dried-out eyes.
But just as she begins to elaborate on her discovery, she sees that Margaret's form is dissolving.
Even the warmth in her hand is fading.
The warmth vanishes. The illusion dissolves. All that remains is the Aurum Secretum, crushed to fragments in her own grip.
Her hands are empty, scarred with the searing marks of spent power. The dove is gone.
Understanding crashes over her, and with it, the feeling of falling, endlessly, into a hell of her own making.

speaker: Malicious Whispers
content: Just now... it was you... you strangled her... with your own hands... Just now... it was me... I strangled her... with my own hands...

speaker: Malicious Whispers
content: The more you seek guidance... the more you destroy...
The Underground mark erupts from the deepest layers of her mind. A torrent of whispers surges upward, drowning her consciousness in an instant.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What... what have I done...
A landscape of pure damnation overtakes her vision.

All matter has been violently fused. Countless fragments of different materials are tangled and melted like wax, each texture a silent testament to a separate, violent origin. Twisted limbs claw toward the sky in a desperate flee, while undulating walls pulse with the compressed layers of distorted, agonized faces.
Hypatia cannot look away. The frenzied energy has commandeered her sight. Even behind closed eyelids, the tableau remains, etched in burning detail.

speaker: Voice of the Dead
content: Hypatia... help us... We haven't fulfilled... that wish.

speaker: Voice of the Dead
content: You promised us a better life, so now, fulfill your promise, or else, join us here...

speaker: Voice of the Dead
content: Give yourself to us...

speaker: Voice of the Dead
content: Will you... kill me too?
As overwhelming noise crashes over her, the twisted dark mist has already crept silently to her feet.
Remorse and anguish stab through her, sharp as a spike. The pain is so visceral she buckles, folding at the waist, barely able to remain upright.

speaker: Hypatia
content: These are my...
Suddenly, something covers her eyes.
At once, the shouts and pleas fall silent. A weight lifts from her shoulders. Then, faintly, she hears a familiar voice.
Don't look.
That isn't real. Reject it, Hypatia. You can do this.

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: Reject it, Hypatia. You can do this.
It's a voice she knows. At first, she feels a surge of disbelieving joy. Then, as the recognition truly registers, it crumbles into overwhelming confusion.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Mr. Rust...? Is that really you?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Or... is this just another illusion...
[Flashback]

speaker: Hypatia
content: It's a catastrophe tear zone... If we hide in there, we might just lose them for good.
[Exit flashback]

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I failed again. I led everyone into danger... I harmed Margaret, and now I've hurt you as well...

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Or perhaps...

Everything before her hovers between illusion and reality. Wails of grief tangle with manic laughter; countless hands claw at her even as they try to pull her close. Some belong to those she has hurt and failed. Others are phantoms she has desperately begged for help.

speaker: Hypatia
content: It's because I've made no progress... because I still long to rely on someone... that's why these visions keep appearing...

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm sorry. I...

speaker: Rust?
content: Why mistake me for a ghost? I'm very much alive.

speaker: Rust?
content: Come on, now. Pull yourself together. A Mania-born hallucination wouldn't be this cheerful, would it? Listen to your master, open your eyes.
That light, cheerful voice cuts through the cacophony of madness like a clean blade. Slowly, Hypatia's unfocused gaze sharpens.
The legendary agent is indeed standing before her, wearing his characteristic, casual smile.

speaker: Rust
content: See? I told you so.
Rust is alive, seemingly unaffected by the contamination seeping from him. If anything, this hostile environment seems to energize him.

Whatever had been haunting Hypatia has been pushed back, now cowering at the edges of the darkness. These entities fear him. They don't dare draw closer, as if a single step would see them torn apart and assimilated into his form.
He has grown stronger. More formidable than she'd ever imagined. Problems she cannot solve, he always dispatches with ease. Should that make her glad?
Though her relief is short-lived. Another sharp, clarifying pain cuts through her. As reality fully reasserts itself, the true scale of her failures settles in, heavy and inescapable.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...The pigeon is destroyed. Something has happened to Ms. Margaret...
Hypatia raises her trembling hands, turning them over to reveal the scorch marks on her palms. They are the final, desperate testimony of Margaret's avatar, its last warning to her.
And in her own consuming fear, she had missed it completely.

speaker: Hypatia
content: She was in such danger, and I still insisted on keeping the connection open. I led them right to her... didn't I?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Hah... Here I go again. Always the same... I miscalculated the conditions of the tear zone, underestimated Fraser's ruthlessness, misjudged the sentiments of the farlanders... If I hadn't stubbornly pushed to go to Furor, you and Ms. Margaret would never have fallen into their trap!
She buries her face in her guilt-marked hands. The Society's sorcery is unnecessary now. Beneath the relentless tide of truth, the scholar's composure shatters like a dam, broken beyond repair.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Responsibility...? All I've inherited is the Campbells' arrogance. Nothing but pride... Who did I think I was? Without others' guidance, what have I ever truly accomplished?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Every stubborn choice I made... every single one was wrong. If I had just listened to you and left as told, none of this would have happened. How could I have been so blind until now...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Tell me what to do. Please! I swear I'll listen this time. I won't act recklessly again!

She clutches the hem of Rust's clothes with desperate force, like a drowning person clinging to the last solid thing in a raging sea. He is all she has left in her world, and she is terrified—terrified of misstepping again.
Rust watches her quietly. A long moment passes before he releases a slow sigh.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I should say something comforting now. But I can't, Hypatia...

speaker: Rust
content: This is as far as I can take you.

A red fissure tears open from Rust's collar, twisting upward before blooming outward like a grotesque flower. Beneath it churns a deep, malevolent chaos. And within that void, a single golden eye snaps open, its surface inscribed with shifting runes.
The hideous orb twitches, convulsing as it focuses, and it locks directly onto Hypatia's gaze. Instantly, she remembers.
This was the secret shared between Adelaide and his suspicious "friends"—a symbol that filled her with equal parts revulsion and primal terror.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is... the Underground sorcery?!

speaker: Hypatia
content: When did it take hold? How was this done? Who was it... No, why didn't any of us sense it?
[Flashback]
(Flashback to the Day 2 ending scene where the Undergrounder assassinated the Luminaris representative)
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...! It was that moment...

speaker: Hypatia
content: But it shouldn't hold power like this... With this degree of corruption, your body will—
The fissures expand, splitting Rust's skin like a series of smiles that don't belong to him, each grinning mouth a gateway to a far larger, more terrible entity.
The prolonged battle has woken it. The residual contamination in the area answers the call, shrieking as it flows into the host's increasingly fractured body.
—The Black Ring, long thought perished, has awoken within Rust. With absolute will, it turns against its vessel, violently pulling him back toward the abyss.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... <size=52>NO!!</size>

speaker: Hypatia
content: What should I do? Tell me what I must do! Please... I beg you!
Rust looks down. He tries to move, but his body isn't answering.
He lifts his head, finds Hypatia, and manages an apologetic smile.

speaker: Rust
content: Mmm... there's something important. Do me a favor: survive through this tear zone and find that "contact" I mentioned. Ask him to pass on a message. Tell that person back in the city: I...
He pauses for a moment.

speaker: Rust
content: Heh... never mind. If I actually left some final words, he'd probably beat me senseless.
female_content: Heh... never mind. If I actually left some final words, she'd never forgive me.

content: His smile is now edged with quiet irony. Noting Hypatia's desperate, shaking refusal, he falls silent. With visible effort, he raises his hand and lays it softly on her shoulder, the touch meant to calm the storm of her fear.

speaker: Rust
content: ...You don't need to do anything. At this point, it's irreversible. All of this is of my own making.

speaker: Rust
content: This body has a... peculiar resonance with the Black Ring. It reacts unpredictably in environments with strong Black Ring effects. I knew the risk, yet I still chose to come to Fraser, gambling like a desperate man... because I, too, had something I absolutely had to do.

speaker: Rust
content: Accepting Margaret's request, agreeing to accompany you to Furor, venturing into this tear zone... these were all my choices as well. I made them because I was intrigued by the possibilities you spoke of, and because... in you, I see who I once was.

speaker: Rust
content: I understand the weight you carry. It's far too heavy for a child your age.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Huh...?
As he falls silent, Margaret's words from the start of the mission come back to him. Whatever her motives, he has to admit she reads people better than he ever could.

speaker: Rust
content: Heh, calling you "a child" was condescending. You are an exceptional scholar. Perhaps even the kind of talent this land has been waiting for. I want to help you go further.

speaker: Rust
content: Walk away from this charade. Set down the burdens that were never yours to carry. Find someone who can truly guide you. People like that do exist; I've even met one myself.

speaker: Rust
content: He would protect you, cherish you, shield you from suffering you should never have to endure, heal your wounds, and guide you down the path you're truly meant to walk. I genuinely hope you find someone like that.
female_content: She would protect you, cherish you, shield you from suffering you should never have to endure, heal your wounds, and guide you down the path you're truly meant to walk. I genuinely hope you find someone like that.

speaker: Rust
content: ...But I can already sense it. You probably won't choose that "correct" path.

speaker: Rust
content: We've both trudged through our "mistakes" for too long. We're too stubborn. Incapable of letting go.

speaker: Hypatia
content: We're... the same?

speaker: Rust
content: Heh... indeed. If you're determined to continue down this road, stubbornly resolved to see it through to the end... then allow me, as one who has walked it, to offer a few pieces of advice.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Argh!!

The hands resting on Hypatia's shoulders suddenly shove her away. In the same moment, every wound across Rust's body ruptures at once. Contamination spills outward, swelling into a chaotic rift that yawns open around him. Half of his form is swallowed into the void; the other half twists violently, pulled into impossible shapes.
Rust doesn't fight it. From within the devouring chaos, his eyes find hers, and he smiles.

speaker: Rust
content: First, objectively analyze the situation before you. As a scholar, you should excel at this. Recognize which outcomes are inevitable and which actions are futile. You cannot save me.

speaker: Rust
content: Understand reality. Accept loss. This is... <color=#fb9259>Lesson One</color>.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No! You'll be—

Hypatia lunges forward to grab him, but the space between them warps and stretches. Each desperate reach only widens the gap, leaving her grasping at air as Rust is slowly pulled into the rift. He doesn't reach back.
He only watches her, this stubborn, bewildered aftercomer, soon to walk the path he leaves behind.

speaker: Rust
content: Now, the Mania here may create illusions—taking my form, Margaret's, or others'—to condemn you, attack you, hold you responsible for all that has happened... Do not panic. You will face far more of this in the future.

speaker: Rust
content: Once you leave this place, the path will not grow easier. Ahead, more people will blame you, make you their scapegoat. Those who hate you will slander your name. Even those you love may refuse to understand you.

speaker: Rust
content: If you have no time to defend yourself, cannot clear your name, and are unable to simply let go... if you remain stubborn and refuse to yield, then grit your teeth and endure it all. Until your stubbornness becomes second nature.
The Aurum Secretum she releases is swallowed by the rift as if called home. She stands helpless. Even the ravenous contamination denies her, forced back by the relentless push of Rust's own will.

speaker: Rust
content: You will grow accustomed to receiving no praise, to disappointing others' expectations. One day, you will realize that forgiveness and redemption are beyond reach. You will continue to lose things along the way, with only weakness and failure as your companions. And you can only endure.

speaker: Rust
content: But after enduring long enough, you will see... that pain is just pain. You can bear it. We have already fallen into the abyss, but once you grow accustomed to it, even the abyss cannot stop you from moving forward.

speaker: Rust
content: When that time comes, if you still haven't changed your mind, then pick yourself up and continue with what you "must" do. Only then will your "stubbornness" truly have meaning.

speaker: Rust
content: —That's it for Lesson Two.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But I'm all alone... I don't even know which way to go! I need someone to tell me what's right!

speaker: Rust
content: This isn't scientific research, Hypatia. No one will guide you, and "correct" exists only in delusion. This path likely has no endpoint, and you must walk it alone.

speaker: Rust
content: Living is its own kind of hell. Welcome to consciousness, <color=#fb9259>Survivor</color>.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ah...
Rust watches her near-panicked face and feels something long forgotten: a pang of regret.
Should he have been less flexible? Should he have been firmer and sent her away, to that one who could truly "guide" her—something he could never do?
If he had tempered his recklessness, listened to his advice to be more cautious... could he have avoided this? He's been scolded. He's even promised him to be more careful with his own life.
female_content: If he had tempered his recklessness, listened to her advice to be more cautious... could he have avoided this? He's been scolded before. He's even promised her to be more careful with his own life.

content: But... what good would it have done? He could never have convinced her anyway. This "apprentice" of his is, after all, too much like him.
Chaos rises over him in waves, pulling him under. His voice grows thin, filled with both regret and final guidance.
(Rust gradually disappears)

speaker: Rust
content: That is all the "wisdom" I can scrape from the bottom of the barrel, as one who has walked this path. I hope it helps a little when you stubbornly persist on your journey. As for the rest...

speaker: Rust
content: The rest is just useless blessings.
But she doesn't want blessings.

speaker: Rust
content: I wish... that since fate is fickle, it cannot always be cruel. May it grant you a few opportunities, and perhaps a little protection.

speaker: Rust
content: I wish you could meet a few more friends to walk with you for a while, to support you. Best of all, bonds strong enough to pull you back from the edge...

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... Don't go...
Correct her one more time. Scold her if he has to. Just... someone, please, tell her how to move forward. Show her the way again.

speaker: Rust
content: If you remain this stubborn, forever marching forward, then I wish you...
Hypatia finally breaks through the barrier and lunges forward, but her hands only close on empty air.
The rift has sealed, taking everything she wanted to hold onto. The bewildered scholar passes through the last fading imprint of him, stumbles, and finally collapses to her knees in the mud.

speaker: Rust
content: I wish you would reach your journey's end, as you desire...
His last words dissolve like ghosts, leaving only echoes to linger in the tear zone.
[Filter dims 2s]
She is all alone now.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What... what should I do...
[Black Screen]
No monsters, no direction. Only darkness lies ahead... An immense emptiness envelops Hypatia like a shroud, but she must move forward—alone, and regardless of what awaits.
[Apply multiple filter layers to this scene at the beginning]
The darkness slowly recedes, revealing Hypatia standing alone among ruins once more.
No one is left beside her. Even if she were to ask, "What should I do?" there is no one left to answer.
You must find the answer yourself, Hypatia. In this contaminated place, there is only one mystery that calls to the scholar in her, only one question that demands to be solved:
Why do the remnant wills drifting through this tear zone... still move forward?

speaker: Jabara
content: What?! You're saying there are no Hypercubes in those ruins? Impossible!! I've bet everything on this!

speaker: Daik
content: DisCity failed to find Hypercubes at the main crash site. Now they look to its birthplace, Furor. They intend to steal our hope!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Yes... that must be why Ms. Margaret brought people here...

speaker: Hypatia
content: According to the observation reports... the data is thorough, internally consistent. There's no room for fabrication... The reaction concentration in the Furor ruins truly isn't enough to form Hypercubes. DisCity, too...
The concentration is extremely low. This is a remarkably weak Black Ring, insufficient to form a mining deposit.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... it isn't weak...

speaker: Furorian Boy
content: Lady Hypatia... why did you not tell us the truth? Why did you leave us behind?
The images that have haunted countless nights return, flickering before her eyes once more. She stares, wide-eyed, and lets the nightmare unfold frame by frame.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I witnessed it myself... so many people, such intense emotion... they completely overwhelmed every Aurum Secretum barrier across Furor...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Average M-value 170... no, at least 480. Density... you'd need hundreds of Apostles to cause that level of destruction...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Mania that concentrated... wouldn't just vanish...
She pushes her weakened body up and slowly straightens her spine.

Without the insight to unravel plots or the courage to face powerful foes, a person who is both incapable and fearful... if she still dares to call herself a scholar, then this is her final, fragile claim to that title.

[Confidential Report of DisCity Scholars]

...The contamination originating from a Black Ring's birthplace does not dissipate upon the Black Ring's destruction. Significant purification efforts will still be necessary.

[Confidential Report of DisCity Scholars]

It has been verified that BR-005 has been in a state of continuous migration since its inception, from Furor to DisCity. This movement has produced extensive contamination along its path.

speaker: Hypatia
content: If both its origin point and its impact site show only this level of contamination, then...

speaker: Hypatia
content: A far greater amount of Black Ring residue must have been transported somewhere else... along its path of migration...

Countless words of accusation roar toward her again, sharp and piercing. This time, Hypatia neither flinches nor weeps. She lets them strike her, and she pushes forward through the numbed detachment...
And in doing so, she finally hears what lies beyond them.

speaker: Saina
content: All this ******* contamination was brought by you!! This <color=#fb9259>tear zone</color> stands as proof of your crimes!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Its concentration would have to be high enough to disrupt catastrophes, attract Apostles, and further condense the contamination...

speaker: Rust
content: This body has a... peculiar resonance with the Black Ring. It reacts unpredictably in environments with strong <color=#fb9259>Black Ring effects</color>.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Its properties would need to be uniform, capable under specific conditions of simulating effects nearly identical to the Black Ring itself...

speaker: Hypatia
content: The theory must be correct. At its core, there has to be...

Ahead lies an endless darkness. No light, no shadow, no path beneath her feet. Each step she takes feels unsteady, uncertain. This darkness is a distillation of every day and night she's spent lost in confusion and fear. Every instinct in her body screams for retreat, for escape, in a desperate, primal plea. And then—
Before she reaches the deepest dark, her silent plea is answered. A final vision unfolds before her eyes:
A shimmering golden light. The guidance her soul has always sought.

speaker: Adelaide
content: No matter what happens, I will always be by your side, guiding your way.

speaker: Hypatia
content: You couldn't guide my way... no one else can...

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'll find it myself...
Hypatia drags her body forward. Her steps no longer obey her will, carrying her slowly through what is both the first illusion and the last.
Reality is bitterly cold, and she has returned to it. Ahead, shadowy phantoms drift—faceless, silent, their gaze fixed on her.
She no longer resists. No longer fears. She simply walks, mechanically, toward the heart of the dark.
And as she passes through the cold spirits, she begins to hear their whispers.

speaker: Boy
content: Ta-da! Let me present to you the finest settlement in all of WhiteSands, City of Rifts, Furor! Welcome home, Lady Hypatia!
A cold that pierces the bone, a contamination that clings like tar—they climb her body together, slowly devouring the last fragments of her spirit.

speaker: Old Man
content: Lady Hypatia, you're back!

speaker: Old Woman
content: Ah, Ms. Campbell of Fraser! I knew you would come back to see us.

speaker: Middle-Aged Man
content: Thanks to the Aurum Secretum devices, all the homes damaged by catastrophes have been repaired. Everyone's moved back in, safe and sound.

speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
content: And thanks to you, the marketplace is open again. Every household has brought their crafts, their specialties. Look, isn't it livelier than before? We even have goods from other towns now!

speaker: Middle-Aged Man
content: Soon, it will not be just Furor. Once Aurum Secretum technology spreads across the farlands, everyone will have a safe place to live. Markets will stay open, day after day!

speaker: Boy
content: Wow, then I want to go see other places too! Help them build homes that are strong and beautiful! Then wherever Lady Hypatia goes, she'll see smiling faces... and taste delicious food everywhere!
Even in the deepest dark and coldest silence, people welcome her with cheers and smiling faces. And she remembers every one of them.
It feels like the old times again, as though she's back in Furor. But...
They are already dead.
The thought alone strains her composure. She should be on the ground. She should be running away.
Yet her earlier promise still stands. She didn't come here to flee.
She must keep moving.

The spirits press close, drawing strange gifts from within their flickering forms. They pass them through countless spectral hands until the offerings reach her. Their voices weave a gentle, insistent enchantment, urging her to stay... to feel how much they care.
Welcome home.
Welcome home, Hypatia.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm sorry.
She reaches out and accepts every gift, holding them close to her chest.
The inky contamination begins to corrode her hands and arms, seeping slowly toward her heart.
From this day forward, as a child of Fraser, will you dedicate yourself wholly to this city and lead its people toward prosperity?
Yes, I swear.
No matter the hardship, whatever the cost, will you never abandon your duty or betray your oath?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Yes... I swear.
Contamination seeps into her arms and chest, the brand at her nape burning. Images flash across her mind.
But she no longer cares. She no longer fears any of it.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I know... They're all just illusions. All of this... it's only contamination...

speaker: Hypatia
content: But what others may dismiss as meaningless, I cannot simply turn away from.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I... cannot let them go. And I will not...
If stubbornness is the chosen path, then be stubborn to the end, and carry all the hatred, curses, grief, and regret that come with it.
Remain sober to the pain that goes bone-deep; in hell, numbness is the true damnation.
Embracing the agony she cannot leave behind, Hypatia turns from the path out of the catastrophe tear. Instead, she ventures deeper into the heart of the wound.
From high above, two ant-like figures inch their way across the endless sea of white sand.
They move along the edge of the tear zone, tracing its border like a long, deliberate ribbon, stumbling again and again—yet always rising, always pressing forward.

speaker: Helga
content: ...Is your body really enhanced by Aurum Secretum?

speaker: Saina
content: I'm no match for you, obviously... I know. I'll go look for her.
Saina steals a nervous glance at Helga, then quickly volunteers everything she's learned.

speaker: Saina
content: The detector's signal matches the direction the DisCity spy fled. There's no doubt.

speaker: Helga
content: DisCity spy? What DisCity spy? You watch your tongue. You've seen it yourself the whole way. That girl is dedicated to Furor. She is no spy.

speaker: Saina
content: ...Yes.

The two of them scour the edge of the catastrophe tear, searching each location thoroughly, but find only vague traces. Even at their closest approach, they can't tell if the distant figure is an Apostle's illusion or a living person.
Time spent here lowers the odds of survival with every minute. Desperate, Helga cups her hands to her mouth and shouts into the depths of the tear.

speaker: Helga
content: Hypatia—!
Hypatia—!
For a moment, the distant figure hesitates as if hearing something. She turns, gaze drifting dazedly over her shoulder.
But she sees nothing. Perhaps she only imagined the sound. The girl turns away, swallowed completely by the dark.

September 25, N.F. 115
8:00 AM
Fraser Gold Palace
4 hours until the Unity Gala begins

speaker: Host
content: Ladies and gentlemen—and all our viewers at home—welcome to the opening ceremony of the Unity Gala! This morning, from the magnificent Fraser Gold Palace, we launch ten extraordinary days of celebration and diplomacy!

speaker: Host
content: Before us stands the Fraser Gold Palace, the longest-standing and most opulent structure since the Nighfall. It is more than an architectural marvel; it is a lasting emblem of artistry, wealth, and influence.

speaker: Host
content: Through our cameras, you can see the distinguished representatives of DisCity and Fraser already seated, while delegations from the farlands proceed with dignified grace into Fraser City, each bearing tokens of goodwill and fellowship.

speaker: Host
content: In the days ahead, leaders from across the lands will gather here to address the challenges left in the wake of the Ash Campaign. And, alongside the festivities, the highly anticipated negotiations for a new peace framework will commence.

speaker: Host
content: My friends, this is more than a celebration; it is the dawn of a new era! Here, beneath this golden dome, power, wealth, and vision will forge a renewed consensus for our future!
Meanwhile.
While Gold Palace Square brims with celebration, inside the festival venue, the host and staff work with quiet focus, conducting their final methodical checks.

speaker: Host
content: Very well. Once again, honored delegates, kindly keep to the agenda. It will proceed in three parts: document review, sequential signing, and final Senate ratification. The essential rule—

speaker: Host
content: —is that you must first signal the nearest staff member with the designated "request to speak" gesture before addressing the assembly. No exceptions.

After explaining the procedures, he smiles and gestures for the present delegates to take a short break. As he strolls casually toward the shadows of the stage wings, his smile vanishes. His voice drops to a lethal whisper, the words firing out like bullets.

speaker: Host
content: <size=28>Does management have actual numbers?! How many farland delegations are confirmed? When will those hicks be here? We're live across the network in four hours. If this hall looks half-empty on camera, what am I supposed to say? That our "peaceful" celebration gala couldn't even have the seats filled?</size>
A staff member wearing a "Stage Manager" badge hurries after him and leans in, whispering a clipped report.
Opposition delayed... DisCity delegation broadcast rescheduled... PR contingency plan approved. With each point, the host's tense expression gradually eases.

speaker: Host
content: Get our cheerleaders, the student volunteers, in here now. Full formal attire. Any empty section, seat them immediately. I want it to look like every seat is contested!
Instructions complete, his perfectly calibrated smile snaps back into place. He claps his hands once, sharp and clear, to summon the staff's attention.

speaker: Host
content: Ahem. Alright, everyone! Let's move into our final full rehearsal. For the seamless, polished presentation our audience deserves, I need your complete focus and cooperation! Thank you!

9:00 AM
Fraser Senate Council Chamber
3 hours until the Unity Gala begins
Multiple screens display a curated tour of Fraser City for the assembled senators.

The view glides from the celebratory crowds on Gold Palace Square to the soaring peak of the Sky Tower, before settling on a luxury hotel entrance. There, the farland delegation boards decorated parade floats, their foreign attire conspicuous against Fraser's backdrop, for a city tour preceding the formal meeting.

speaker: Valorian
content: It appears all is proceeding smoothly. Even our distant cousins from the farlands have found their designated places.

speaker: Elliot Baker
content: I do not celebrate at halftime, Valorian. Some... even in their absence, can leave surprises that unsettle the board. Nothing is settled until the final piece is placed.

speaker: Elliot Baker
content: Can you feel it? How many eyes are upon us at this very moment?

His gaze travels to the far end of the table, settling on Marcus Drake. With deliberate calm, the iron-willed Fraser nobleman advances a chess piece. It lands in the center of the display, triggering the unfurling of a strategic map that illuminates Fraser, the farlands, and DisCity in stark relief.

Our position has grown precarious in recent days. The unexpected reversal in the Ash Campaign was a swift blow. Now, mourning for the casualties mysteriously appears at refuge facilities across the minor states, while rumors regarding the truth of BR-005 spread like a contagion.

Fraser City itself is restless. The deterrent of BR-003 has emboldened the peace faction in the Senate, while several war-favoring nobles have seen suspicious financial movements. And not so coincidentally, all this began after that woman reappeared.

Even now, anxiety is written across the faces of the farland delegates attending the gala, in stark contrast to their usual demeanor. When the call to war loses its resonance, fear will fragment the Alliance... and threaten the very foundations of Fraser's economy.
<color=#fb9259>But it will not come to that. The Unity Gala begins shortly. All pieces are positioned. The trap is ready to spring.</color>
Marcus picks up three chess pieces and places them on the board.

The Black Ring's intensification of natural disasters has further destabilized the Alliance politically, driving the farlands to desperation for Hypercubes. The Luminaris Society scholars set a trap in Furor, baiting their leaders with false promises of the Hypercube technology.

After the Luminaris envoys delivered the technology, they were killed by two assistants of DisCity Ambassador Margaret, an act we orchestrated to forge a blood feud. The farland leaders were so enraged that they escorted her back to Fraser as a murder suspect.
As for those two assistants... He picks up two chess pieces and removes them from the board.

Hypatia Campbell and the DisCity spy codenamed "Rust" are already dead, unable to escape the Black Ring contamination in the tear zone. Once we retrieve their bodies, we can pin the entire blame for the BR-005 incident on them.

The final stage is simple: we will plant agitators at the venue to provoke the farlanders. Their hatred, once ignited, will drive them to break through Fraser's guards and kill the DisCity ambassador. This will spark a new war, while Fraser remains comfortably on the sidelines, reaping the benefits.
I hear she's a Sinner? Heh, perfect timing to test the secret weapon from the Underground <color=#fb9259>Sophos</color>.

speaker: Marcus
content: ...Hmph.
She is clever and cunning, a serpent that has always slipped through our grasp. We've never caught her in the act before. This time, we will...
Marcus lifts the Sophos piece and slams it down, capturing the square occupied by her piece.

speaker: Marcus
content: <color=#7683a2><i>All is in alignment. This will be her end.</color><i>
The other senators give silent nods of approval. The Unity Gala is about to begin. Everything will proceed as planned.
Marcus puts away the chessboard. The peace dove is his prisoner now. He could end her here, or...
If they want to take this a step further, turning the knife back on DisCity...
The Campbells aren't the only ones who know how to play this game...

10:00 AM
Fraser Hotel
2 hours until the Unity Gala begins
As the gala's opening draws near, the hotel housing the farland delegation grows quiet. Rael, who detests float parades, has lingered inside until the last possible moment.
Just as he turns to summon his companions, he brushes shoulders with an attendant dressed in Fraser attire.
With a suspicious look and hurried steps, the Aurum Secretum attendant rushes off, oblivious to the note that has fallen from his uniform.

Rael's instincts, ever vigilant, flare. In the attendant's blind haste, he sees an opening. With a fluid motion, he stoops, snatches the paper, and conceals it in his pocket. Only once he reaches a secluded corridor does he dare to unfold it. A line of deliberately distorted, encrypted text stares back, yet its meaning is unmistakable:
Mr. Jabara, your trade manifest has been delivered. Please come to Room X-2 alone for the handover. And be careful. Do not let Fraser or the Alliance discover this.

Room X-2 is a spartan staff quarters, dominated by a blazing fireplace. A stocky figure crouches before it, muttering as he deliberates over which pages from a stack of documents to feed into the hungry flames.

speaker: Jabara
content: Sigh, I've decided to burn them... Feels like such a waste, though. Could've used these to squeeze a better deal later...

speaker: Jabara
content: But that person was right. They'll search everyone at the gate. Can't leave them here in the hotel, either...

speaker: Jabara
content: I'm no traitor. Business is business. A man's gotta be flexible...
As he feeds the documents to the flames, the door crashes open behind him.

speaker: Rael
content: ******* you! What in the hell are you doing?!
Rael storms into the room, snatches the documents from Jabara's hands, and holds them to the firelight.

Hypercube smuggling routes with Nirvana. Stock manipulations rigging food prices. Unjust profit distributions... Page after page, the details coalesce into a single truth: only the middleman wins, raking in obscene wealth without a shred of risk.
His breath hitches, then turns to ragged panting. With a surge of fury, he hurls the papers aside, seizes Jabara by the collar, and hauls him violently to his feet.

speaker: Rael
content: You slimy bastard! You ******* played us!

speaker: Rael
content: We had a deal! Farland resources stay with our people! So what's this "cooperation" with Nirvana? When the **** did you start dealing with DisCity again?!

speaker: Jabara
content: Wait, wait! Let me explain! These are old, I swear! Nothing since that day! My dealings with DisCity ended then, I promise!
Jabara shoves the remaining documents behind his back, his movements frantic.

speaker: Rael
content: I don't believe you. I ******* don't. Hand them over.

speaker: Jabara
content: H-hey, don't!! Tho-Those are my livelihood!
After a brief struggle, Rael wrenches the remaining documents free. One glance is enough, and blind fury takes over. His hand snaps to his waist.

speaker: Rael
content: I'm gonna put a bullet in your head!!!
THUD!!
A dull thud sounds behind Rael's head. His body sways, then he crumples to the floor. Only Jabara remains, slumped against the fireplace with a face frozen in terror.
From the shadows, an Aurum Secretum Warrior steps forward and collects the scattered documents.

speaker: Jabara
content: You're—?!
Saina's knuckles whiten, the paper crumpling in her grasp as each documented corruption fuels her fury. The details are explicit, damning, and infuriating.
Yet with a final, shuddering breath, she squeezes her eyes shut, wrestles her rage into submission, and forces herself to speak.

speaker: Saina
content: What else is there? This isn't everything, is it?

speaker: Saina
content: Hand it all over. Now.

11:00 AM
DisCity Delegation Waiting Room
1 hour until the Unity Gala begins

Inside the room, every piece of anti-Mania equipment hums at maximum output. Aurum Secretum guards line the walls, their vigilant eyes fixed on the woman in the white hat seated at the room's center. Unfazed, she reclines in a custom chair, fanning herself with an air of utter leisure.

speaker: Marcus
content: How are you feeling, Ms. Margaret?

speaker: Margaret
content: Sigh, after a full day in a farland prison transport, then brought straight here and held until now... how do you imagine I feel?
She tucks a stray strand of blonde hair behind her ear, the simple gesture underscored by a weary note in her otherwise composed voice.

speaker: Margaret
content: I am, of course, fully prepared to be your gala's sacrificial lamb.
The air in the room seems to solidify. A slow, knowing smile spreads across Marcus's lips.

speaker: Marcus
content: Indeed, you are of great significance to today's proceedings.

speaker: Marcus
content: In your decade here in Fraser, you've woven connections, cultivated friendships, and infiltrated every circle. Even our Senate is threaded with your influence. Within our carefully constructed narrative, you—DisCity's so-called "peace dove"—have thrived. Your performance during the Ash Campaign was particularly... remarkable.

speaker: Marcus
content: You were the first to find the youngest Campbell daughter. The first to see her value. You extracted Aurum Secretum technical intelligence, breached our information blockade, and delivered it to DisCity—undoing years of strategic planning.

speaker: Marcus
content: Heh, I could overlook past surprises. But even now, under constant watch, you've somehow reached the farland leadership and shaken their loyalty. Was securing the victory pact not enough? Must you destroy the very foundation of our alliance?

speaker: Marcus
content: If you hadn't trusted that Campbell girl so completely, if you hadn't drawn her into your operations, the roles might be reversed today... What a waste. She held only marginal research value, yet you gave her all your faith and risked everything to protect her...

speaker: Margaret
content: Hypatia Campbell is a generational talent. To dismiss her as having "marginal research value" is absurd.

speaker: Margaret
content: I protected her because I cared for her. It was my choice. And you? Now that you have me, what revenge do you intend?

speaker: Marcus
content: It's regrettable. You possess noble lineage, rare talent, and a genuine desire for peace. To see someone like you driven to such a corner... it pains us.

speaker: Marcus
content: I know how you've been sidelined in DisCity, kept from the inner circle, denied policy support, betrayed repeatedly by Nirvana... Unpleasant, isn't it? And with the war-favoring DisCorps rising, your footing will grow even more precarious.

speaker: Marcus
content: This is your last opportunity, Margaret. Join Fraser. The Senate values you. You'll have greater freedom to pursue your ideals. Besides... we both know your ties to DisCity are not so deep.

speaker: Marcus
content: After all these years, you've integrated into Fraser's culture. I believe you've come to love this land and its rich heritage. Peace transcends allegiance. But only by removing DisCity's threat can you truly embrace your ideals.

speaker: Margaret
content: Rich heritage... Fraser does have a rich heritage. But I wonder, how much of it was built upon the plundered blood and sweat of the farlands and your colonial satellite towns?

speaker: Margaret
content: I love peace—true peace. Where people lay down arms, join hands, and move forward together. Not the counterfeit peace of the privileged, built upon trampled flesh and bones.

speaker: Margaret
content: In that regard, Fraser cannot offer what I seek. I must respectfully decline.
Margaret taps her cheek with the tip of her fan, offering a definitive refusal.
Marcus never truly expected to persuade her. In fact, her refusal is essential. Without it, the grand spectacle he has planned would have no conflict.
He lets his facade of warmth dissolve, revealing the cold ambition beneath.

speaker: Marcus
content: ...Heh... Hahahaha! Do you truly believe you can turn the tables? As you have with your silver tongue so many times before? What is your plan?

speaker: Marcus
content: Expose BR-003? Reveal the so-called "Fraser lies"? Or return home and force Nirvana to concede more benefits, to bribe those gullible souls outside?
He methodically outlines every strategy Margaret might attempt, having already sealed off each path long before she could take a single step.

speaker: Marcus
content: Wake up. It's futile. You know how long we have cultivated this. To the farlanders, Fraser is not just an ally against common enemies; we are the hand that relieves their suffering, the only god who answers their desperate prayers!

speaker: Marcus
content: You—an outsider, a Disian—think you can shake a century-old alliance? Like an ant trying to topple a mountain!
Just then, the host's countdown echoes from behind the heavy curtain. Marcus turns, lifting a corner of the velvet drape with one finger.
His view from backstage takes in the circular hall, now packed with farland representatives. Among them, his carefully placed "agitators" wait.
But he may not even need them. A raw, palpable hatred already burns in the eyes of the crowd, countless gazes fixed on the empty platform where the DisCity representative will stand.
Marcus smiles. This is exactly the audience he wanted.

speaker: Marcus
content: Well... the hypocritical peace dove of DisCity, struck down by vengeful farlanders. Oppressors slain by freedom fighters. The resistance reignited. Conflict burning eternal... Not a bad "contribution" from you to this gala.

12:00 PM
Top of Fraser Gold Palace
The Unity Gala officially begins
Above Gold Palace Square, birds take flight as parade floats and fireworks erupt in unison. A torrent of ribbons and petals falls like rain, washing the sky in flowing gold and purple.

At the peak of the Gold Palace, heavy curtains part to the swell of ceremonial music. The Fraser senators appear as the event's hosts, and standing alongside them is the Peace Ambassador from DisCity: Margaret Kervoz.
She stands apart, isolated like a defendant in a dock.
At her appearance, a low murmur of unrest begins to ripple through the farland representatives.

An Aurum Secretum Warrior shoulders through the crowd, her eyes burning with a hatred so palpable it seems to scorch the air. Her left leg, mangled by Aurum Secretum, drags with a heavy, unnatural gait as she advances. An Aurum Secretum blade is gripped in her white-knuckled hand, sparking against the floor with every step.
Marcus raises a hand, halting the guards who move to intercept. He watches Saina's approach with cold fascination, the ghost of a smile touching his lips.

Saina takes her place at the front of the crowd. Her gaze sweeps past Margaret, fixing instead on the Fraser senators at the center of the platform. Slowly, deliberately, she raises her Aurum Secretum blade, leveling its tip at their elegantly dressed ranks.

speaker: Saina
content: It was always you... behind all the suffering in the farlands... it was—ALWAYS—YOU!

speaker: Saina
content: <color=#fb9259><size=52>GO TO HELL, YOU FRASER BASTARDS!</color></size>
The raw fury in her cry sends a chill through the Fraser nobles. They had expected a warrior consumed by blind rage to execute Margaret before the crowd—not to turn the blade on Fraser itself!!

speaker: Marcus
content: What?! How dare you—!
Events erupt. Saina launches forward like a loosed arrow. The guards, originally ordered to permit the attack, now scramble to intercept. But it's too late.
She drives her heel into a guard's chest, catapulting him backward onto the signing table. Ceremonial vessels shatter; documents scatter. The hall plunges into instant chaos.

speaker: Crowd
content: Aaarrrgh! HELP!!

The orderly conference hall fractures into a battlefield. Saina drives forward against the tide of bodies—slow, relentless, propelled by a desperate will as she claws her way toward the platform where the senators stay.
Amid the turmoil, Margaret remains serenely seated. She unfolds her fan with a practiced grace, letting it shield the subtle curve of her lips.
Her eyes meet Marcus's across the chaos, holding his look of shock and fury. And then, very deliberately, she smiles.

speaker: Margaret
content: I need not lift a finger now. Everything that needed to be done... was already arranged.

speaker: Margaret
content: Shall we watch the spectacle unfold together?
The moment her words fade, Saina's blade splits the wooden podium in two. Splinters explode into the air, and with them, Marcus's carefully constructed script is destroyed.
[Monologue Filter Begins]

speaker: Margaret
content: From a very young age, I traveled with my father across the farlands, far beyond the borders of DisCity.

speaker: Margaret
content: I saw all kinds of people, cultures, and rhythms of life, unlike anything at home. Like stars of every color scattered across the earth, each shining with its own light.

speaker: Margaret
content: Some fought simply to survive. Some worked to preserve what they had. Some longed for change, while others prayed only for peace.

speaker: Margaret
content: Even amid catastrophes and recurring sorrow, they have never stopped speaking—in a thousand tongues, from a thousand soils—each carrying their own weight, each holding their own fragile, stubborn dream.
[Scene Change]
Saina steps onto the wreckage of the podium and seizes the fallen loudspeaker. Her voice, hoarse but firm, cuts through the chaos to fill every hall of Fraser Gold Palace.

speaker: Saina
content: I know it all! You conspired with Jabara and his kind to bleed the farlands dry. Fraser sells Hypercubes to us at several times DisCity's price. Of course we can't afford them!

speaker: Saina
content: You hoard supplies, gouge prices, and make DisCity and the farlands pay in blood!

speaker: Saina
content: It's not just Hypercubes. Fraser's ledgers show steel, grain, and even... people! You're all ******* monsters!

The ledger lands with a soft thud at an elderly representative's feet. After a moment of hesitation, he picks it up. A few quick page turns drain the color from his face. Alarmed glances shoot across the delegation seats, and a ripple of suppressed murmurs begins to build.

speaker: Saina
content: This ledger only goes back five years. You bastards must have older ones... Talk! When did it start?!

speaker: Jabara
content: Argh! W-we were just trying to survive! Isn't everyone the same...?

speaker: Saina
content: Cut all that crap!

The murmurs swell into an angry roar in an instant. Saina seizes Jabara by the collar and hurls his obese frame aside like a trash bag. A flash of her blade slashes open his coat, spilling hidden luxury silk and gem-studded rings—their obscene opulence glinting under the light.

speaker: Saina
content: Look at the starving, freezing people of the farlands. Look them in the eye! Do you dare say you're the same as them?!
[Intercut Monologue Filter]

speaker: Margaret
content: Differences inevitably lead to discord. In a world of widespread catastrophes and scarce resources, everyone must fight fiercely for what they desire. Friction and conflict... they're unavoidable.

speaker: Margaret
content: Yet I have always been good at coordination. I prefer elegant, gentle methods—finding common ground among divergent wants, weaving mutual happiness from seemingly opposing needs.

speaker: Margaret
content: Wherever I go, I plant seeds of peace. I... love peace of that kind. Graceful. Deliberate.

speaker: Margaret
content: But alas, the moment the gardener turns her back, those carefully tended shoots are trampled by careless feet, uprooted entirely by short-sighted hands...
[Scene Change]
The hall ignites. Farland delegates surge to their feet, their eyes burning with the fire of betrayal as a wave of collective fury crashes through the assembly.

speaker: Marcus
content: You are... Saina? Heh, such insolence. Have you forgotten who gave you Aurum Secretum? Who granted you power and dignity? And who made you suffer in the first place?

speaker: Marcus
content: We gave you the chance for vengeance against DisCity, and now you turn on us like their loyal hound?
He snarls, thrusting a finger toward Margaret in a desperate bid to redirect Saina's fury. But Saina doesn't so much as glance aside. Her fists clench until her nails bite deep into her own palms.

speaker: Saina
content: I... still hate DisCity. Even now. But...

speaker: Saina
content: That doesn't make you the righteous ones!
Saina clenches her teeth and takes a threatening step forward.

speaker: Saina
content: You've been lying to us... using our pain, our rage. You and the Society are no different.

speaker: Saina
content: My brothers and sisters who died for the Ash Campaign... They believed your lies until their last breath! And you still expect us to bleed for you?!

speaker: Saina
content: Listen! It's not DisCity I hate. I hate every monster who preys on the farlands. And that includes you!!

speaker: Saina
content: It's time to answer for what you've done. Get down here, and bring those Society snakes with you!
"Get down here!"
A voice in the crowd takes up the cry, and the farland delegation ignites. They surge forward, a wave of furious shouts, and the situation fractures in seconds.

The venue guards finally snap into action, weapons drawn against the civilians protesting in fury. It's the wrong move. Enraged, the farlanders seize anything at hand—chairs, candelabras, daggers drawn from hidden sheaths—and the hall erupts into open combat.
Meanwhile, from her place in the "defendant's seat," Margaret watches the chaos unfold below—a farce of history, replaying exactly as she has seen it before.
[Flashback Filter]

speaker: Margaret
content: They fan hatred and stoke the flames of war... Those in power never feel the sting when others bleed. They care nothing for justice or vengeance, only how conflict can be turned into more wealth, more power.

speaker: Margaret
content: Hmph. Even in their greed, these shortsighted fools never learn more elegant, harmonious methods. They always return to the crudest means, spending the lives of others like cheap currency. Myopic. Insatiable. And in the end, even their own gains turn to dust.
[Cutaway]

speaker: Saffar
content: DisCity hoarded their Hypercubes while calamity destroyed our home. Fraser talks about humanism, but all they've done is turn us into lab rats for Aurum Secretum, giving us nothing but ruin.

speaker: Arienna
content: ...So naive, Sibilla. Did you really think they'd help? DisCity doesn't care. They don't understand our suffering—they can't even imagine it.

speaker: Selyna
content: You get to live in luxury by sucking us dry, and you have the nerve to talk to me about what's right?!
[Return to Monologue]

speaker: Margaret
content: They never learn respect. They never learn reflection. History simply repeats... over and over again, unchanged.
[Black Screen Transition to N.F. 106]

N.F. 106
DisCity Embassy in Fraser

speaker: Margaret
content: That's impossible! I designed this Great Expo myself. I've spoken with every Alliance leader. I know their concerns! Dravyn has stepped down, and the farlands need time to heal. We drafted a five-year framework for mutual benefit. Breaking it now serves no one's interests! And besides—

speaker: Margaret
content: This is a Black Ring we're talking about! Who would benefit from worsening catastrophes? The farlands haven't even mastered large-scale Mania defense! I was here on the ground. There was no celebration, only panic! The people here didn't even understand what's happening!

speaker: Margaret
content: The Observatory tragedy was a setup. Someone is deliberately sabotaging this! Don't let anger blind you. Send Blackett. She can uncover the truth. Don't rush into war. Don't—
A Black Ring appeared at the Navigator Observatory. The Great Expo was terminated. The Outland War reignited, lasting one year, with affected regions...

speaker: Margaret
content: ...Even my most principled friend had to suffer for your folly...

speaker: Margaret
content: It's always the same. Always... No matter how strong the foundation I lay, once it's in your hands, you tear it down.
[End of Flashback] [Return to Present]

speaker: Crowd
content: Aaaahhh—! Heeelp!!
CLANG!

A sharp metallic clang rings out as Saina's blade intercepts a guard's strike meant for a civilian. But there are too many targets, too few of her. Dozens of meters away, another scream pierces the air.

speaker: Saina
content: You dare attack civilians...

speaker: Saina
content: I'll kill you!!
The Aurum Secretum howls through her veins as blood spills from her wounds. Every cut feels like a fresh brand of fire, but she can't reach them all. She is still not fast enough.
All the combat skills she has honed to kill Disians now fail her. They cannot outrun the slaughter carried out by her own people, cannot protect the civilians who had always stood behind her.
Just then—
BWAK!
A sniper shot cracks from behind. The attacking Aurum Secretum guard's head erupts, spraying contaminated matter across the ground. The body jerks once, twice, then slumps into the mud.

speaker: Saina
content: That's—?!
Saina spins toward the source of the shot. High above, framed against a pillar, Helga's silhouette remains steady in her sniper's perch. She raises a hand in a clear, distant signal of support.
Then, with calm precision, she shifts her aim, the rifle's scope settling on the woman seated center stage.

speaker: Helga
content: Is this what you wanted, Margaret Kervoz? What have you done? What in the hells are you playing at?!
The woman sits, perfectly composed. Her eyes lift, meeting Helga's gaze unflinchingly through the scope. Amidst the surrounding chaos, only her smile remains enigmatic and undisturbed.

speaker: Margaret
content: Are you curious what I'm thinking, Ms. Helga?

speaker: Margaret
content: What I'm thinking of, naturally, is nothing but peace.
[Flashback]

speaker: Margaret
content: Jabara is a pure pragmatist, sworn to profit, not to any flag. All it took was a few whispers through Fraser's business circles, rumors that DisCity was gaining ground while Fraser retreated... and he eagerly came to me, looking for an exit.

speaker: Margaret
content: Rael, by contrast, sees only in absolutes—hot-blooded, impulsive. He dismisses anything from DisCity as a lie, and has sworn to expose every conspiracy... Heh, how adorable. With just a little guidance, I can shape that righteous suspicion into something useful. His words carry far more weight with the masses than mine ever could.

speaker: Margaret
content: As for the bewildered Yokna and her people... they'll believe anything. Deep down, everyone craves a clear answer, someone to point the way, to tell them which path is true.

speaker: Margaret
content: And all of this was made possible by my lovely little canary, set free...

speaker: Margaret
content: She never needed to win their favor or extract promises. Hypatia simply has to be herself, and everyone who speaks with her lays their hearts bare. That is something I could never do.
[Flashback]

speaker: Rael
content: Disians are cunning as foxes! Of course it's possible!

speaker: Yokna
content: The farlands lack everything: technology, resources, skilled hands...

speaker: Jabara
content: I would only ask that, when your journey concludes, you must convey my humble regards to Mr. Adelaide.

speaker: Surveillance Dove
content: ...Coo.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Margaret
content: Only someone as sincere, as utterly devoted as you, could hold such power. Thank you for opening their hearts to me... for letting me see what everyone truly desires.
And Helga, who sees Fraser's plot clearly but remains powerless to stop it; even Saina and her fellow Aurum Secretum Warriors...
Through the bird communicator accompanying Hypatia, she has watched from Fraser as if she were there, understanding every move in the farlands as it unfolds.
[Flashback Filter]

speaker: Hypatia
content: Tell me... what should I do...

speaker: Hypatia
content: I know you're there. Please, don't keep hiding from me, Ms. Margaret, Mr. Rust... I'd be content just walking behind you. Please... Even if all I can see is your back, even if I'm only following your shadow...
[End of Flashback]
As the chaos continues, teetering on the edge of escalation, Margaret sits perfectly still. She is waiting, for that moment.
Now, let Fraser's mask fall completely.
Let the people of the Farland Alliance see the hypocrisy of their so-called shield. Let them realize these high-and-mighty nobles have never walked the same road.
Only when illusions shatter can reality be seen. Only when they face the harsh truth and lay down their hatred, will they see the true path, and the hand that's been waiting to guide them.
I will extend that hand... The moment is almost here...

speaker: Marcus
content: Madness... This is absolute madness! Guards! The Society! Where are those Underground Sophos?! Do something!

speaker: Marcus
content: Apprehend these riotous lunatics!
Amid the screams, shadowy Underground Puppets emerge from below—weapons originally meant for Margaret now turning on the farland crowd. They advance, and the massacre begins.
...The perfect moment hasn't come, but she can no longer watch.

speaker: Margaret
content: This has gone far enough... You still haven't learned when to stop.
Margaret rises and walks toward the crowd. The guards meant to watch her are now lost in the chaos; no one remains to stop her.

speaker: Margaret
content: When the weak cannot decide their own fate, and chaos only breeds more tragedy... someone must step forward to build bridges. To find a way through the deadlock.

speaker: Margaret
content: To find that solution, I am willing to use any means... and bear every consequence.
Whether exploiting human weakness or wielding Mania's power... a dove of peace does not obsess over keeping its feathers white. It only cares that peace will prevail at journey's end.

speaker: Margaret
content: Listen to what everyone truly desires, then do everything in my power to fulfill it. When conflicts arise, I find ways to harmonize opposing needs.

speaker: Margaret
content: A world where every wish and want can be reasonably met—isn't that the very meaning of "peace"?

speaker: Margaret
content: And that is precisely why I find your actions so intolerable. You use the crudest, most repulsive methods, not only destroying the peace I have built, but crushing the last hope of those who came to you for aid.

speaker: Margaret
content: Heh, you noblemen of Fraser... you hold yourselves above, yet wallow in incomprehensible stupidity.
[Big CG - Animated]

speaker: Margaret
content: If you do not understand what peace is...

speaker: Margaret
content: Then I will be the one to teach you.

speaker: Margaret
content: It is necessary compromise, anchored by conviction. It is occasional passion, tempered by reason. It is honesty preserved, cooperation honored, conscience upheld. It is extending a hand despite opposition, choosing dialogue even when the path is difficult.

speaker: Margaret
content: I'm sorry. Is the concept too difficult to grasp?

speaker: Margaret
content: Do not worry. Simply heed my guidance, and I will lead you toward true harmony and unity.
S-Class Mania erupts from her, instantly silencing the chaotic hall. Above, countless white doves materialize, scattering across Fraser City like a promise—each one a vessel of her will.

speaker: Margaret
content: Bid farewell to your Underground friends. A peaceful world has no place for their interference.

Only moments before, the farland representatives and Fraser guards had been locked in brutal combat. Now, they lie scattered across the floor, weapons slipping from slack fingers to clatter against the ground. Conscious but paralyzed, they stare up in pure terror at the one figure still standing among them.

speaker: Margaret
content: Oh dear... I let my true nature slip and lost my temper. That's hardly becoming.
At that moment, Marcus lets out a low, hoarse laugh. He leans heavily against the splintered podium, face bloodless, and raises his head in one final, cold act of defiance.

speaker: Marcus
content: Heh... You think you've won? How arrogant... This is the farlands. No one will believe you. No one trusts a Disian...

speaker: Margaret
content: Sigh, you're right, of course. My smile strategy won't be nearly as effective now. Once a peace envoy shows her fangs, trust becomes difficult to regain.
Margaret's gaze moves across the fallen—their expressions a mix of anguish and hate—before stopping on Saina. Even on one knee, braced by her sword, Saina's eyes meet hers, defiant and unbroken.

speaker: Margaret
content: And yet, all I ever wanted was to help everyone find peaceful solutions.

speaker: Saina
content: What could a Disian like you possibly understand...

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes... a Disian speaking of the farlands' suffering is indeed laughable. But if you refuse even the person willing to listen and help... what change can you truly expect?

speaker: Margaret
content: Tell me, will endless fighting, quarreling, killing... will any of that end your pain? Bring the happiness you seek?
Saina doesn't answer, instead turning her head away with bitter resentment.

speaker: Margaret
content: My words mean nothing to you, I understand. So...
She lifts her head. Her gaze sweeps over the shattered battlefield, past faces etched with hatred, greed, or confusion, then down the long corridor toward the palace entrance.

speaker: Margaret
content: ...My little bird should be returning any moment now.
With an elegant gesture, she beckons a snow-white dove in through the window. It alights on her fingers, nuzzles her temple, then bursts into flight, a streak of light arcing across the sky.
All eyes are irresistibly drawn to the white silhouette. It glides over the chaotic palace, down the long corridor, and lands, silent and certain, upon the shoulder of a young girl in the distance.

speaker: Saina
content: That's—?!
A frail silhouette emerges at the corridor's end.
She looks as if she has clawed her way out of the deepest catastrophe zone. Viscous black contamination clings to her, invading every surface of her skin and clothes.
She clutches jagged contamination crystals to her chest. They have pierced straight through her flesh—hands, arms, shoulders—yet she will not let go, staggering forward step by labored step.
Her movement is so slow that it feels intentional, almost ceremonial.
Not a soul moves. A silence colder than the grave descends, every witness paralyzed by the sight of her and the sinister glow she carries.
Who is she?
What is she carrying?
A weapon of mass destruction... or a treasure beyond value?

speaker: Saina
content: The Campbell girl...? How is this possible?!
Saina recognizes the girl. She and Helga had scoured the edges of the catastrophe tear zone for Hypatia, finally concluding she was lost. Yet here she stands, covered in contamination...
Saina struggles upright and steps forward, only to be driven back by the palpable force of contamination emanating from Hypatia.

speaker: Saina
content: What are you....?!
Hypatia does not respond. Her eyes are hollow, unseeing. She has no strength left to fight the contamination, no voice left to warn or explain.
Still, she walks. One laborious step at a time.
As she passes by, Saina sees it: nestled within the corrupted mass in the young girl's hands, beautiful crystalline blue fragments pulse with a faint, ethereal light.

speaker: Marcus
content: ...She's holding... Hypercubes?!

A wave of shocked whispers sweeps through the Fraser nobility. Marcus stares at Margaret, stunned, but she merely fans herself, her smile unchanged, as if all of this is proceeding exactly as she intended.

speaker: Margaret
content: Under the torture of catastrophes, what the farland people want most is simply to "survive." And now, Hypatia has brought them that hope.

speaker: Margaret
content: How unfortunate, Senator Marcus, that it was Hypatia Campbell—whom you dismissed—who achieved this miracle...

speaker: Marcus
content: ...So this was your game all along. Everything from the very beginning, all of it for this!!
The BR-005 vein, missing since the Ash Campaign... if it had been found by this DisCity woman...!
Watching the farlanders display expressions of fanatical devotion, almost all Fraser leaders share the same thought—
The DisCity woman's schemes must end here!

speaker: Marcus
content: Guards! Stop Hypatia Campbell! Do not let her advance! Seize what she carries! Kill her if you must!
Marcus lurches to his feet and smashes the call button with furious desperation, bellowing his command.

speaker: Marcus
content: Do not let her give it to Kervoz! We can't let the Disian have it! Kill her!!
[Scene Change: Luminaris Society]

Inside the Luminaris Society laboratory, Marcus's frantic voice crackles through the communicator. A woman in a white lab coat slowly looks up, her eyes on the live feed of the chaos, and speaks to the microphone with perfect calm.
Then, time to deploy the weapon of the "Sophos."
[Sky Tower Venue]

speaker: Monstrous Bird
content: HISSSS—

Inside the Sky Tower venue, a low, resonant hum suddenly rises from deep beneath, vibrating through the floor. Before anyone can react, an immense cyan bird appears behind the structure, wings spread wide enough to blot out the sun. A vast, suffocating shadow falls over the gathered crowd.

Its feathers gleam with an artificial, gem-like luster, and its form—though elegant in shape—radiates a profound wrongness. Slowly, its eyeless face rotates at the tower's apex, then locks onto its target with unnerving, mechanical precision.

speaker: Monstrous Bird
content: HISSSS—
Another piercing shriek tears through the air as the giant bird plummets, targeting Hypatia at the crowd's center!
Sensing the danger, the Aurum Secretum within her body surges into action, creating a resonating defensive barrier around her.
But her resistance proves far too weak. The artificial bird barely slows before driving onward.
BWAK!
The giant bird lets out a piercing shriek as the powerful impact from a sniper round staggers its massive form.
BWAK!
A second shot tears through its wing, spraying not blood but a shower of glimmering, Aurum Secretum-like crystals.
BWAK!

The third shot strikes the giant bird's face with precise force. Though it doesn't fully penetrate, the impact fractures the surface like glass. With a shriek of agony, the creature staggers back, its wings now useless and grounded.
Heads snap toward the gunfire. Helga is braced on the crumbling platform, fighting Margaret's psychic pressure just to keep her rifle steady.
The wind tears at her silver hair as she stands amid the gunsmoke, her sharp gaze sweeping across every farlander below.

speaker: Helga
content: People of the farlands! Are you really so helpless that you need a little girl to risk her life for you?

speaker: Helga
content: Go fight it!
Fraser's trying to steal the Hypercubes! "Fraser wants her dead!" "Protect her! Protect her!!"

speaker: Farland Refugee
content: If Fraser doesn't want her, then the farlands will!
