Shouts rise from the crowd. Even under Margaret's psychic hold, the people of the farlands surge forward, ignoring contamination to shield Hypatia with their bodies.
She's brought Hypercube. It's Hypercube!!

Battered and bloody, the Aurum Secretum Warrior plants herself before Hypatia. Aurum Secretum markings now cover her skin like living scripture, her burning gaze fixed on the approaching guards. She is now a wrathful deity ready to break upon them.

speaker: Saina
content: You bastards!

speaker: Saina
content: If you want to hurt her... you go through me first!

Some hurl stones with desperate strength, others raise broken Aurum prosthetics as shields, and the boldest charge the giant bird to disrupt its path. Their attacks scarcely mark its hardened feathers, yet not a single person flinches.
Margaret watches, a faint smile touching her lips. With a soft snap, she closes her fan and releases the psychic hold over the crowd.

speaker: Margaret
content: ...That's more like it.

speaker: Margaret
content: If one must fight, let it be for a cause like this.
OwO
Pushing her ability to the limit, the chaos around her—wind, shouts, the creature's hum—falls away. Her world contracts to the target and the crosshairs. Just like a mission, years ago.
Will this shot lead her down the right path? Is Hypatia truly what's best for the farlands?
So you're choosing again? If Fraser is right this time, this will be another mistake.
Think, Helga. If you hadn't pulled the trigger back then...
BANG!!
Amid the insidious, corrupting whispers, Helga pulls the trigger without hesitation, her mind perfectly clear.
The rifle kicks sharply. The bullet cuts through the air and strikes the creature's core with lethal precision.

speaker: Monstrous Bird
content: SCREEEEE—!
The creature shrieks in agony as its emerald glow flickers and dies. Its body convulses in midair, flight failing, then it plummets like a severed kite toward the Sky Tower's glass dome!
Boom!

A deafening crash tears through the dome, blowing out a gaping hole. Shards of glass and twisted metal rain down like shrapnel. The creature thrashes once through its mangled wings and issues a final, rasping cry. Then, it flees through the breach into the distance, leaving only ruin and a hall gripped by silent shock.
Every gaze lifts toward the gaping hole in the dome. Faces are frozen in disbelief, unable to process what they've just witnessed.
The heavy silence stretches for several long seconds.

speaker: Farlander A
content: D-did we... win? We defeated that monster? We defeated... Fraser?
The words fall like a stone into still water, sending instant ripples of excitement through the crowd.

speaker: Farlander A
content: We did it!!! Long live the Alliance!! Long live freedom!!
Cheers erupt like a broken dam, flooding the hall with joy.
HYPATIA!! HYPATIA!!!
The people of the farlands encircle her, their jubilation a living wave as they carefully guide her forward, avoiding the contamination that clings to her.
In this moment, the girl who brought the Hypercube has become the living symbol of hope for a people long in darkness.

speaker: Yokna
content: Hypatia... She's a true blessing for the farlands... Calling her our savior wouldn't even be an overstatement...

speaker: Yokna
content: We really can have our own Hypercubes. Now we can live...
Her voice fills with relief as she watches Hypatia walk toward DisCity's Peace Ambassador, toward the path the farlanders will take into the future.
[Black Screen]
The girl has never left the dark.
All sense of direction dissolves. Time loses its shape. Only the contamination remains real, accumulating, spreading, its pain a scalpel cutting through the haze.
Where am I now? Still in the ruins of the catastrophe tear... or have I made it back to Fraser?
She hazily recalls following someone back, but her sight holds only flickering shadows and phantom shapes.

speaker: Fraser Senator
content: Hypatia Campbell. For you to appear now, in this state... is most regrettable.

speaker: Fraser Noble
content: Disgraceful wretch... You betrayed the Society, defected to DisCity, and now you betray your city-state and your blood once more...

speaker: Fraser Senator
content: You conspired with DisCity, leaked our Aurum Secretum technology, and caused the Ash Campaign to collapse at its most crucial hour. Then you fled to WhiteSands rather than face judgment.

speaker: Fraser Noble
content: What would your family think? How would your honorable brother regard you? Where is your sense of responsibility?!

speaker: Fraser Senator
content: You have betrayed your lineage and your city-state. You are no longer worthy of the name Campbell!

speaker: Fraser Noble
content: Cease this! Do you intend to shatter a century of your family's honor with your own hands?!!
The surrounding phantoms roar, charging, and pass straight through her.
Familiar accusations. Her mind and body had long grown numb to them.
She does not let them slow her steps.

speaker: Boy
content: I see the blue shiny rock in her hands! Is that the treasure Mom told me about?

speaker: Boy
content: Does that mean we won't have to keep moving all the time?

speaker: Farlander
content: That's a Hypercube. Yes, we won't have to wander anymore... And, don't be so rude...

speaker: Farlander
content: She is a lady of noble birth. A brilliant scholar... She is our savior...
They all reach out their hands toward Hypatia.
Hypatia! Hypatia!
They chant her name.

speaker: Farlander
content: ...Are you alright? Your wounds...
They try to help her.
Or perhaps, they are simply watching her.
Under their hopeful gazes, Hypatia finally sees the treasure in her hands.
On the "worthless" tokens from the Furorians, faint blue crystal fragments have begun to form.
...A gift from an unshakeable past.
If I can bring these out, the farlands will be saved... Everything will get better...
Then... can someone like her, wandering in hell, finally be redeemed?

speaker: Yokna
content: What choice do we have? Fraser and DisCity both look down on us, but we have to pick one... Which side do we go with?!

speaker: Rael
content: I don't give a damn about Hypercubes! Aurum Secretum Warriors and DisCity are sworn enemies. Those DisCity mutts... I'll kill every last one of 'em!

speaker: Jabara
content: Who cares if it's Nirvana or Fraser? Money's money, and business is business!

speaker: Helga
content: You think a Hypercube mine fixes everything? Do you even know what the farlands really lack? What we actually want?
[Enter Flashback Filter] (Hypatia is still in the hallucination world; consider overlaying WhiteSands background on top of the hallucination effect)
The WhiteSands motorcycle roared across the pale dunes. Helga had the wounded girl secured behind her as she raced toward Fraser.
That peace dove's intelligence is solid. If we move now, we can still make it to the opening ceremony. Whatever you're planning, I'll be there to see it.
The wind screamed past them. As they rode, Helga answered the question the girl had asked when she was pulled from the ruins.

speaker: Helga
content: If you want to know what the farlands are really like...

speaker: Helga
content: The people here have never had a future.

speaker: Helga
content: We're used to living under someone else's shadow, following someone else's lead. When the metropoles stood, we obeyed them. After the great city-states fell, we answered to Fraser. We even tried DisCity once, but they never looked our way twice.

speaker: Helga
content: I've often wondered myself... where is the future for people like us?

speaker: Helga
content: Someone suggested an alliance, and against all odds, we built one. I knew nothing about politics or diplomacy, but I thought I could learn. And before I knew it, I became their leader.

speaker: Helga
content: Once I was a leader, I saw the hard truth: we thought we had choices, but we never did. We don't have DisCity's Hypercubes or Fraser's wealth. When catastrophe hits, all we can do is... wait to die... or pray the mighty feel generous enough to help.

speaker: Helga
content: If any major city-state so much as glances our way, we act like it's the highest honor. We'd walk through fire for them. Jump into hell without a second thought.

speaker: Helga
content: In this world, "being worth exploiting" became our best bargaining chip. "Switching sides" turned into a fine art.

speaker: Helga
content: You're not like us...
[Back to Illusion]

You are a Fraser noble, the distinguished Lady Campbell. You are a brilliant researcher at the Luminaris Society. You have a safe, comfortable life. You never should have been dragged into life-or-death matters like ours.
Child, if you've been helping us out of guilt, that's already enough.
—You don't need to stay here.
—You don't belong here.
—You are not like us.
...No. That's not true... Ms. Helga... <color=#fb9259>There is no difference between us</color>.
In that moment, a sliver of light pierces the endless dark. Hypatia finally sees the way forward.
Past the countless illusions that have clouded her sight, she can just discern a narrow, rugged path ahead.

speaker: Farlander
content: What choice do we have? Who can give us an answer?

speaker: Furorian
content: Thank you... these are all we can give... we hope... they'll reach the hands of our loved ones.

speaker: Fraser Noble
content: How dare you side with those wretches from the farlands, Campbell! Are you going to betray your own city-state, your own social class?!
Many obstacles remain ahead, and many blessings, but the Hypercube in her hands gives her the strength to push forward at any cost, and the resolve to complete her mission.
And so, she begins to run through the illusion.
The pain in her neck sharpens, as if urging her onward.
Go. Hurry. Run!
With every step, determination swells, and courage forges her path.
And so, she moves through the crowds in reality and the illusions in her heart.
[Scene Transition - Sky Tower]
At the end of the path, someone stands with a smile, arms opened wide to welcome her.

speaker: Margaret
content: Welcome back, Hypatia.

speaker: Margaret
content: You've achieved a miracle. I always knew... you could.
...It's a warm, comforting embrace, and for a moment her pain seems to dissolve. The weight she's carried feels, at last, like something she can release.

It has always been this way. In her darkest hours, it was Margaret who maneuvered, negotiated, and pulled her from the brink. It was Margaret who took her hand and said, "Trust me. Follow me," offering a path when she had none.
That embrace is always warm, a calm in the storm, a source of strength when everything else feels painfully uncertain.
So now, it is time to do what must be done.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Ms. Margaret...
The girl holds her mentor tightly. Her slender arms wrap gently as she leans close, her voice a soft whisper against Margaret's ear.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This was your plan all along, wasn't it?

speaker: Hypatia
content: From the moment you first approached me... you had it all planned.

speaker: Hypatia
content: You intended to use me to push the Farland Alliance away from Fraser and into DisCity's hands. Am I right?
The cheers of the farlanders swell around them, but in the small, private space between their bodies, the noise falls away, leaving a stillness that flows like water.
The girl retrieves the broken Aurum Secretum bird from within her garments, swiftly disassembling it to expose the hidden surveillance module.
After a moment of silence, DisCity's Peace Ambassador tightens her grip on her fan and speaks, her voice soft and deliberate.

speaker: Margaret
content: Isn't this outcome for the best?

speaker: Margaret
content: Look at their lost faces. Consider what they need... what they truly want.
Her gaze shifts to the crowd around them, their cheers ringing like the fervent hymns of worshippers witnessing a divine miracle.

speaker: Margaret
content: Hypatia, I have my stance, yes. But I promise they will never bring harm to you.

speaker: Margaret
content: You... do trust me, don't you?
Hypatia releases her hand and takes a small step back. She gazes at Margaret, at the person who has guided her and remade her.

She is such a gentle, radiant, and approachable soul. She can be temperamental, but more often she speaks with a passion for peace that ignites hope in others. It isn't a power or a performance. Hypatia knows this is Margaret's true heart.
Now, the sadness and confusion in her eyes are equally true. So are her attempts to persuade, to guide. She used Hypatia, yes, but she also cared for her, truly looked after her.
That is who Ms. Margaret is. No matter the time, the circumstance... whatever means she must employ... she will never abandon her purpose.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Thank you... for reaching across the divide between our city-states, for your steadfast and sincere pursuit of peace, for showing us a new way when all paths seemed closed.

speaker: Hypatia
content: To someone as weak and stubborn as I am... you kept offering your hand, guiding me earnestly, again and again.

speaker: Hypatia
content: When I was at my most lost, you were the one who guided me out of the fog. For that... I will always be grateful.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But the road ahead is one I must walk myself. Please... let me choose my own path now.
The Hypercube in her arms emits a soft glow, lighting her eyes with a newfound determination—a resolve no one has ever seen in her before.

speaker: Margaret
content: So... where will you go?
She asks softly, as if already knowing there's no turning back.
Having rejected guidance, where does your path lead now?
Hypatia doesn't answer. Instead, she steps past the Peace Ambassador of DisCity and onto the nearby podium.
A calm settles over her as her fingers close around the microphone. In that moment, every recent hardship flashes before her eyes.
(microphone screeches) ——————

speaker: Hypatia
content: People of the farlands... I am Hypatia.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This... is the Hypercube I retrieved from deep within the catastrophe tear. I am sorry that on my own, I could only bring back this small amount.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Along the way, I have heard your hopes. I have seen the future you dream of: a true mine at BR-005, a chance for strength, clarity, and even freedom...

speaker: Hypatia
content: I know the answer you are waiting to hear from me.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I am sorry... but I cannot give you that certainty.
The crowd slowly quiets. They watch Hypatia, their expressions shifting from celebration to uncertainty, staring at the girl they had just hailed as the farlands' savior.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I come from the Campbell family, a Fraser noble sheltered from hardship. I was sent to conduct Aurum Secretum research in Furor, yet I failed to protect the Furorians who aided me. I failed to prevent the cruel schemes. I failed to save the lives lost at BR-005.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I have always been weak, too often blinded when clarity mattered most, unable to make the right choice until it was too late—forced to watch tragedy unfold before me.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Even in Aurum Secretum research, the one thing I excel at... I have no control over how it is used. It may become scars on the bodies of Aurum Secretum Warriors, or weapons turned against others.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Even now, after risking everything to enter the heart of the tear... I only returned with this tiny fragment. I cannot promise to find more. I cannot promise to free the Alliance from outside influence. I cannot promise to sustain the farlands through every storm ahead.
Hypatia's voice wavers with nerves, but she clenches her fists and draws a steadying breath, reclaiming her control.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Of all my failures, what I regret most is my fear of standing alone, my need to depend on others, and how easily I let myself be swayed...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Because the road ahead seemed too frightening, too bleak, I doubted my own strength. I feared choosing for myself, I desperately sought guidance, and I clung to those who appeared surer of the way... only to be led astray.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Fraser or DisCity, who is truly sincere? Whose path is right? I do not know. I cannot answer that... and perhaps neither can they.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is where reality differs from scientific research. Every truth in this world is clouded by agendas and interests. There is no pure, reliable answer.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Often, we are not so fortunate. We must walk alone, groping through the dark.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Yet... I still choose to go on. Because there are people I want to protect. Things I will not abandon...

speaker: Hypatia
content: My homeland, my convictions, the love I hold, the trust placed in me, hope... Though I am not yet strong enough, I still wish to use what little knowledge I have to guard them.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Even without a guiding light, I will still measure the path ahead with my own steps.
A ripple of unease moves through the hall, and confused murmurs begin to rise from the crowd.
Are you leaving us, Ms. Campbell?
On our own, without the backing of any big city-state... we won't make it... Even if we get Hypercubes, someone'll just take them, and we'll be left divided again.
Isn't DisCity's Peace Ambassador pretty kind to us? Why can't DisCity help us?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Please keep watching me, Ms. Margaret. Thank you for lighting the way for someone like me, for guiding me to where I stand now...

speaker: Hypatia
content: I will not let you down on the road ahead.
The girl draws a deep breath, unclasps the Campbell family crest from her chest, and hurls it from the top of the Gold Palace.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I am not the daughter of Campbell, nor am I the savior of the farlands.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I am just Hypatia, an Aurum Secretum researcher.
I'm just like everyone here. An ordinary, vulnerable human being.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I cannot lead anyone... Even my utmost effort can only yield something as small as... these formless Hypercube fragments.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But I will keep moving forward. From now on, I will seek out more hope, bear every hardship, and protect our homeland in my own way.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I will survive on this land.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Perhaps we are not without resources after all. Because... for those of us who have endured on these lands of famine for so long, stubbornness is our most enduring strength.

speaker: Hypatia
content: And this homeland we cling to so stubbornly... is no dead-end crevice. Look up, you'll see how vast it truly is.
She pauses briefly.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Even after saying all this, standing alone still feels uncertain. Would you... walk this road forward with me?
At first, the crowd falls into utter silence. Then, a new sound rises, not cheers or pleas, but scattered voices slowly merging into a chorus... of steady, determined commitment.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Then let us begin our journey.

speaker: Hypatia
content: From this day on, my Aurum Secretum research belongs to the people of the farlands. Together, we will survive on these lands of famine.

speaker: Hypatia
content: On the path ahead, we will not be alone. The Hypercubes scattered across our homeland are blessings from our loved ones who departed first. They will watch over us as we go forward.
Amid the cheers, Margaret quietly lowers her fan.
The Farland Alliance has found its new leader. As an Outland Affairs Officer, the priority now is to befriend, not make another enemy.

speaker: Margaret
content: Walk forward, Hypatia...
This is your first step, taken entirely on your own.
As the artificial monstrosity ravages the tower, injuring all in its path, chaos erupts across Fraser City—this time, deep within the Luminaris Society itself.

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: What in the world is happening?! Why is something like that buried under our headquarters?! Adelaide never said a word about this.

speaker: A.S. Researcher A
content: It's no good. We can't override the anti-Aurum Secretum device. It's woven with the sorcery of the "Sophos." Someone must be controlling it... Could it be the "Sophos"? But why? Weren't they supposed to be with us?

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: Whoever's behind it, we're the ones who'll pay the price! Unauthorized deployment of an artificial weapon, disrupting the Unity Gala, slaughtering the senators... any one of those is enough to finish us!

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: We need to find the Director, now! We can't just stand around waiting for this to blow up in our faces.
In the shadows at the lab's depths, a woman in white stands motionless before a containment unit, her gaze fixed on the dark mist swirling inside.
Malevolent energy churns within, where a substance resembling a miniature Black Ring slowly gestates in the gloom.
The communicator in her pocket has been ringing urgently for several minutes. She finally touches the button and answers with unhurried calm.

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: Compose yourselves. I am fully aware of the situation. Everything is proceeding under the Sophos' guidance.

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: The Aurum Secretum Warriors positioned throughout the gala have already begun their operation. They will secure us the time and the leverage we need.

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: The warriors... might stop that artificial creature, yes... but that won't clear the Luminaris Society's name! We'll be held accountable!

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: The Luminaris Society... When did it become little more than a toy Adelaide Campbell handed to his sister? An empty title. Nothing more.

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: But the wisdom we pursue requires no such facade to conceal it.

speaker: A.S. Researcher B
content: Director Kantarella, what... what are you saying?!

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: ...Do you recall the man I had you hunt down? He was an enemy of the Sophos. A traitor to reason itself.

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: You eliminated him—truly eliminated him—with your technology and your tactics. Again and again, you cast him back into the oblivion of the Black Ring... Well done. The Sophos have taken note of your service. Now stay where you are and await their arrival.

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: Do not worry. You have been granted passage on the ark the Sophos have built. When the end comes, you will journey to the sanctuary of pure finality. That... is the true reward for those who follow wisdom.
She keeps her voice melodious until the last lie is told, then casually crushes the communicator and discards it into the nearby brush.
No longer needing to placate the witless masses or guide the perpetually lost, she can finally turn away, back to the quiet she has always craved.

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: The ark has very few seats. Those worthy of crossing the sea were always meant to be rare. For the ordinary, their greatest happiness is to die clinging to their beliefs, free of doubt and fear.
She lifts her gaze. Ahead, at the end of the hallway, stands the figure she reveres.
At this moment, the light of wisdom illuminates the hall of Luminaris. The Director's heart swells as her most sincere smile spreads, and she quickens her pace.

She had long been enlightened, long understood. In this apocalyptic world, people are sacrificial lambs; fame, power, desire—mere mist. She mocks the masses stumbling in blindness, trapped in a night without dawn. But she knows—
Only truth is eternal. Only clarity is precious. Only the Sophos who have pierced the darkness are worthy of being followed.
Now they have come for her, chosen her as they once chose Adelaide Campbell. The Director's steps quicken, her heart racing with anticipation.
...Until she sees the Sophos, normally so dignified and composed, shudder violently.

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: What?

The Underground Sophos holds most sacred in her heart tries to speak, but no sound emerges. Suddenly, the figure pitches forward, crumbling into a formless pool of black water that splatters across the floor.
And in that place now stands another figure, one who had suppressed their presence like the dead. He remained so completely undetected that even she failed to sense anything wrong.
No... it was that she had refused to believe they shared the same origin.
The figure shifts, stepping from the shadows. Beneath the bandages, a face emerges, one she utterly despises. The face she never wanted to see.
Good day, Madam Director. I was hoping to borrow a few materials from your Society. Would that be convenient?
Or perhaps you'd prefer... "Underground lapdog"? Does that suit you better?

speaker: Lana Kantarella
content: ...! How can it be YOU?!
Screams of anguish echo through the Society, yet only one person emerges from within. With deliberate calm, he answers the communication terminal that has been buzzing incessantly.

speaker: Rust
content: —Ah, hello? We actually have a signal. The peace dove certainly didn't waste any time setting up the comms network. Impressive work, really.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't worry, I'm not quite dead yet. After all, during that "interrogation," you told me to cherish this life of mine. So I fought tooth and nail, slipped death's grasp more than once, just to make it back to this side of existence...

speaker: Rust
content: After all that trouble, would it be too much to ask for praise?
Furious shouting erupts from the receiver, and Rust hastily pulls the terminal away, stifling a laugh.
—Still as blunt as ever. He'd known his stunt would set him off.
female_content: —Still as blunt as ever. He'd known his stunt would set her off.

content: ...But he deserves his thanks, too. Clawing back from that Mania abyss wouldn't have been possible without that relentless will. See, Hypatia? We're not the only two stubborn souls in the world. With a faint smile, Rust lifts the terminal back to his ear.
female_content: ...But she deserves his thanks, too. Clawing back from that Mania abyss wouldn't have been possible without that relentless will. See, Hypatia? We're not the only two stubborn souls in the world. With a faint smile, Rust lifts the terminal back to his ear.

speaker: Rust
content: Oh my, such temper... I might not dare come back to report until you've cooled off... Just kidding.

speaker: Rust
content: I've just come across something unexpected here at the Society, so my plans need to change. I'll be making a detour, and I'm not sure how long it'll take. I trust you'll understand.

speaker: Rust
content: Besides you, we have another <color=#fb9259>friend</color> who needs this information rather urgently...

He examines the documents from the Luminaris Society's classified archives: "Retrieval from Furor Black Ring Ruins." Alongside data on the outbreak core, the black box remains, and Hypercube crystallization, the Society had collected physical remnants—debris not wholly consumed by the Black Ring.

Among them, Rust recognizes familiar objects: a silver-iron pendant, a small axe, a fang blade. They are leadership emblems of a West District legendary gang, passed down for two generations. He'd heard about them more than once from a certain friend.

The residual traces suggest the last owner of the leader's pendant wasn't turned into a Corruptor; that young Legion leader simply vanished into the Black Ring. For Rust, this is the best news possible, and the start of a new mission.

speaker: Rust
content: Now, before we say goodbye, it's time for the grand finale. Can you tune in to the Fraser evening news right now? Are they showing the Luminaris Society in chaos yet?

speaker: Rust
content: Excellent. Consider this the latest spy thriller, now showing. My talented apprentice didn't pick a script before leaving, so I'm directing this one as I please.

speaker: Rust
content: Stealth, assassination, intelligence retrieval... all the essential ingredients are here. What else would you like me to spice it up with?
There is a long silence on the other end of the line, then a reply.

speaker: Option
options: I thought every spy thriller had explosion scenes?

speaker: Rust
content: As you wish, sir.
female_content: As you wish, ma'am.

content: He lifts his hand, glances at the live broadcast camera, and casually snaps his fingers. Then...
[Black Screen with Flashing White Light]
[Explosion CG]

A thunderous explosion booms behind him, the scorching blast lifting the edges of his coat. Without turning, Rust knows exactly how spectacular the display must look. He flashes a casual smile toward the camera, giving a small, confident salute.

speaker: Rust
content: What better way to deliver a fireworks show just for you?

Nearby, all of Fraser City has descended into chaos. Advanced cross-state broadcast technology faithfully transmits every moment of the Unity Gala to every connected screen, bringing this wave of determination to the entire world.
Twilight is shredded by flames. Wave after wave of shouts from the farlanders rises, powerful enough to shake the foundations of this ancient city of nobility.

speaker: Rust
content: No need for the rendezvous anymore. Our friends from the farlands are managing quite well on their own. Let's celebrate their victory.
[Scene Transition - Some Garden]

Evening, September 25, N.F. 115
Fraser City in Chaos

speaker: Fraser Soldier A
content: Over here!
Under the cover of night, a squad of heavily armed Fraser soldiers infiltrates a luxurious noble estate.
A white Aurum Secretum bird guides their advance until a sharp crack echoes from the garden, and the creature plummets, shot down mid-flight.

speaker: Fraser Soldier B
content: All units, enemy is dug in with heavy weapons, showing strong resistance. Advance in multi-directional formation.

speaker: Fraser Soldier A
content: Marcus Drake! By authority of the Senate, you are under arrest on suspicion of war crimes. Lay down your weapons and surrender immediately.
A gunshot answers him.

speaker: Fraser Soldier B
content: Prepare for forced entry. Breachers, stand by.
After a deafening explosion, the soldiers storm the study at the end of the corridor.

The room is choked with dust and smoke. At what was once a lavish aristocratic desk, Marcus sits, glaring at the figure stepping inside—Raphael Herbert, once the most radical voice of the war faction, now standing against his former ally.

speaker: Raphael
content: Surprised to see me, my friend?

speaker: Marcus
content: Hah... HAHAHA! All this time we've been infiltrating DisCity... and I never thought the real traitor would be right here among us. That you would be the one conspiring with our enemies.

speaker: Marcus
content: Have you finished moving all your assets? Once the tide turns, will you put on another face and come crawling back to us?

speaker: Raphael
content: Don't mistake me for a man of such petty motives, Marcus. No one wants war. I act for the sake of humanity's peace.

speaker: Marcus
content: Peace? You? What a joke! Why don't you use the coin you earned betraying this city to buy yourself a coffin?!
The moment Marcus reaches into his jacket, Raphael pulls the trigger.

speaker: Fraser Soldier A
content: Perimeter of the building fully secured, sir.

speaker: Raphael
content: Good. Withdraw.

After clearing the evidence, staging the scene, and placing the body, Raphael settles into Marcus's chair like a victorious king. He leans back, his gaze fixed on the grand map of Fraser spread across the wall.

speaker: Raphael
content: Now then... it's time to redraw Fraser's political map. Let's plan this carefully.

speaker: Raphael
content: All of this is for peace.

On the evening of September 25, N.F. 115, Fraser Senate war hawk Marcus Drake was found dead in his mansion, an apparent suicide.
A recovered note suggested he took his own life out of guilt over the Unity Gala's failure.
Five days later, his fellow senator Raphael Herbert was discovered in his garden pool, shot multiple times, which is suspected to be a covert assassination.

These deaths have ignited months of extreme turmoil within Fraser's ruling elite.
[Scene Change: DisCity Hospital Ward]
In a DisCity maximum-security cell reserved for the most dangerous criminals, a television plays on loop, broadcasting distant news from the Outlands.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...From this day on, my Aurum Secretum research belongs to the people of the farlands. Together, we will survive on these lands of famine.

The ward's lone viewer watches in silence for hours. The speech ends, the broadcast loops, and daylight fades to evening. Only then does the Underground's Famine Sage—no, Adelaide, eldest son of the Campbell family—finally lower his gaze.
...Then, he smiles with profound satisfaction.

speaker: Adelaide
content: My dear sister, you have walked farther than I ever could.
[Scene Transition - WhiteSands] [Hold for 2 seconds] [Scene Transition - Vehicle Interior]
Meanwhile, on the main thoroughfare across the wasteland outside Fraser City.
Margaret leans against the window with one hand, lazily fanning herself with the other, while deliberately ignoring the small black triangle hovering in front of her.

speaker: Schorl
content: Thank you for your service, Ambassador. I will be escorting you back to the city-state for the remainder of your journey.

speaker: Margaret
content: Heh. I have achieved unprecedented diplomatic success, prevented a war, reestablished ties with the Farland Alliance... and this is when they see fit to urgently recall their accomplished ambassador...?

speaker: Margaret
content: It would seem EDGE is less than pleased with the outcome. Did I truly ruffle their feathers that much?

speaker: Schorl
content: Yes. They find it difficult to believe someone of your caliber failed to persuade the farlands to relinquish the BR-005 development rights. Worse, you allowed them to discover the Hypercube first, thereby genuinely undermining DisCity's monopoly.

speaker: Schorl
content: As a result, even without Fraser's interference, we have lost control over pricing while the Farland Alliance has gained significant leverage. Nirvana is deeply displeased and is demanding an explanation.

speaker: Margaret
content: I suppose that's fair. Still, I despise having to justify myself to them, especially those fools at Nirvana who contribute little beyond dragging everyone down.

speaker: Schorl
content: You will not need to explain anything to them.

speaker: Margaret
content: Oh?

speaker: Schorl
content: Upon your return, the MBCC will immediately assume control of the investigation under the pretext of tracking Sinner activity. They will compile and submit the report themselves.

speaker: Schorl
content: Nirvana trusts them implicitly and would not bypass the Bureau to hold you accountable. As for the disciplinary recommendations submitted by the Chief... the rest of EDGE will raise no further objections.

speaker: Schorl
content: This form of "disciplinary action" will suffice.
Margaret turns her head, fixing the black triangle in her gaze. Through it, she sees the figure lurking behind.
...Of course. When he secretly gave her the real mission, that man had already calculated this very outcome.
Was this final move out of appreciation for her sacrifices, or would he not have bothered if she hadn't performed flawlessly while achieving all objectives?
No matter. The old fox's plan served the peace dove's interests, so she could overlook the details. She returns her attention to the passing wasteland.
...Let hope stay in the soil that awakened it, and let seeds root where they belong. It's not so bad, after all. One step closer to the "world peace" she seeks.
—Yet her fan flutters faster, stirring a cool breeze against her flushed cheeks as she fumes with impeccable diplomatic poise.

speaker: Margaret
content: Very well. I can't wait to meet this famous Chief myself.

speaker: Margaret
content: I am most curious to learn what was said to my little Hypa that left such a profound impression. She nearly derailed everything.

speaker: Schorl
content: Oh? I was under the impression that events unfolded largely according to your design.

speaker: Margaret
content: Hmph, not at all. In my original plan, my little canary was meant to return with me.

speaker: Margaret
content: It is so rare to find a child with such promise. I had no intention of letting a talent like that slip away.
She leans against the window, gazing out at the vast wasteland beyond.

speaker: Margaret
content: But now... what can be done? She has found her own path forward—spread her wings and flown toward wider horizons.
[Scene Change - Campbell Estate]

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...That should be everything.

speaker: Helga
content: ...Looking at all this, once you walk out that door this time, you ain't planning on coming back, are you?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Don't worry. I'll come back once the Luminaris Society is restored. There is still much dialogue to be established between Fraser and the farlands.

speaker: Yokna
content: Hey—Hypatia! Helga! Come take a look at my new sand ship!

speaker: Yokna
content: Before I head out this time, I gotta pick someone up. Hypatia, you probably know her. Calls herself Sibilla, a Furorian. The Nirvana merchant caravan was supposed to bring her to Fraser, but when they caught wind of that whole Unity Gala mess, they just dumped her halfway and bolted.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Sibilla...? She's safe? That's... wonderful.

speaker: Helga
content: Looks like the trouble in Fraser's gonna keep simmering for a good long while.

speaker: Helga
content: Hmph. Fine by me. Let them fight it out. Gives us folks in the farlands a chance to finally catch our damn breath. We've got so much more on our plates as it is...
Hypatia casts one last look at the place where she grew up, then turns and steps into the morning light.
She does not look back, striding forward with determined steps.
[Enter ED]

In the Distant Future
On a Peaceful Day

DisCity
Minos Bureau of Crisis Control

speaker: Schorl
content: Yes. The Farland Alliance remains, to this day, a loose and developing organization. However, they have made considerable progress in developing the BR-005 mineral belt, and their Aurum Secretum research is gradually surpassing Fraser's own.

speaker: Schorl
content: Having politically disentangled themselves from Fraser's influence, and with Ambassador Margaret having previously laid a solid diplomatic foundation... Paradeisos has determined they are worthwhile partners for cooperation, specifically in jointly combating catastrophes and balancing Hypercube production capacity.

speaker: Schorl
content: The technical delegation dispatched by the Alliance has now arrived in DisCity, wishing to exchange knowledge with the Ring Research Institute and Nirvana. One of their representatives is a Sinner who has specifically requested a meeting with the Chief of the MBCC.
The Farland Alliance delegation has made camp outside the city. Climbing the sand dune, you spot a blonde girl standing at the head of the envoy group.

She wears a common WhiteSands cloak, her appearance weathered by travel. The wind and grit of the farlands have left their mark on her skin, yet they cannot hide her innate poise. Blonde hair, mismatched eyes, and by the look of her, she seems only a little older than Hella...
Have you two met somewhere before?
As the thought forms, the young scholar is already walking toward you, her smile as bright as the sun overhead.
[Slow Transition to CG]
With a smile, she extends one hand toward you.

speaker: Hypatia
content: At last we meet, Chief.

speaker: Hypatia
content: It's a pleasure. I am Hypatia, an Aurum Secretum researcher with the Farland Alliance.
A hundred years into the Nightfall, humanity endures in the choking shadow of Mania, clawing its way back toward civilization, step by painstaking step.

So too this great city-state, drowned in ruin time after time, yet still it stands. Steeped in despair past counting, yet destruction never arrived. In time, the people have come to believe that DisCity is blessed, that DisCity is a land of hope, and that DisCity will never fall.
But only because fools remain blind to the designs of fate.

BR-001 Ruins Isolation Belt, The Rust
BR-002 Mine, West District
BR-004 Ruins Isolation Belt, Old Keylan Square
BR-005 Ruins Testing Site, WhiteSands

speaker: FAC
content: We've got M-value anomalies across BR-001, 002, 004, and 005, all happening at once. Every site's reporting signs of Underground activity.

speaker: 9th
content: Footage analysis confirms it's all autonomous combat puppets. No humans on-site, or rather, no intelligent entities. They're just running on preset sorcery.

speaker: FAC
content: We can handle them. The puppets lack a clear offensive objective. It's likely just a recon sweep, maybe a diversion, or some kind of scheduled response drill that's part of a longer game.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Got it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Contain the contamination and minimize casualties. Focus on the civilians. Keep them isolated, and keep them safe.

speaker: Hecate
content: The West District mine got the warning early. They've evacuated all personnel, and they even came forward with proposals for intelligence and security cooperation. Samuel and Matilda have submitted patrol and tracking plans for the Underground scouts.

speaker: Hecate
content: Everyone's heard how much you've thrown yourself into this. They're worried you're pushing too hard. They all want to help, to do their part, Chief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know. Thank them for me.
Years of deep collaboration with every department have honed your instincts. A disruption like this can hardly stir a ripple now. You're more than ready for this.
Now, you just need to—
A phantom image cuts through your vision, gone in a blink. Dizziness washes over you, and your hand finds your temple before thought catches up.
...Not again...

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Chief, are you alright?
The sound of Hecate's familiar voice jolts you back to your senses.
You draw yourself upright, your voice regaining its composure, knowing that your next words will ring clear across every battlefield, heard by all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All four sites, stand ready for engagement. And make sure the Ring Research Institute is notified. Tell them not to lower their guard. We all know what's happening on the surface is just a diversion.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Our enemy's real target is <color=#fb9259>BR-003</color>.

May 13, N.F. 116
03:30 PM

EDGE Emergency Meeting

speaker: Schorl
content: The latest action reports have been synced. All Underground assaults on the ruin observation stations were successfully repelled. Losses are roughly 20% below projections. As we're starting to map the enemy's operational patterns, intelligence and surveillance teams can now coordinate for effective predictive countermeasures.

speaker: Schorl
content: The MBCC Chief played a pivotal role in this outcome, particularly in tactical command and threat assessment. EDGE has opened a special channel once again to invite ${PlayerName} to join us. This is both an expression of gratitude and a request for him to deliver the action debriefing in his capacity as core field commander.
female_content: The MBCC Chief played a pivotal role in this outcome, particularly in tactical command and threat assessment. EDGE has opened a special channel once again to invite ${PlayerName} to join us. This is both an expression of gratitude and a request for her to deliver the action debriefing in her capacity as core field commander.

speaker: Schorl
content: Whenever you're ready, Chief ${PlayerName}.

The moment the neural link engages, a sharp sting pierces your temple. A wash of pale blue light sweeps across your retinas as lines of text stream, shift, and reassemble within the dataflow. Though your body hasn't left the office, your consciousness has entered a dim, empty hall.
Here, face and voice no longer matter. <color=#fb9259>SHP-13</color> is your only marker in this digital conference of minds.
[System: SHP-13 has entered the session.]

SHP-13: There isn't much to add beyond what's in the report. I assume everyone's read it. As for the root cause of all this... I need to take us back to <color=#fb9259>last August</color>.
SHP-13: During the Ash Campaign, EDGE publicly deployed the BR-003-based Black Ring weapon for the first time, using it to strike the farlands with a catastrophe-level deterrent. It put an end to the enemy's reckless use of BR-005 to draw in Apostles of Ashes against the city-state.

SHP-13: The tactic was a success. But it came at a steep price: BR-003 was exposed. This, of course, didn't slip past the Underground, and they've been on the hunt ever since.

SHP-13: Since last September, we've tracked 19 rounds of anomalous activity across the Black Ring ruins. Started with single-site strikes, then the scope kept expanding. Now every observation station's getting harassed.
SHP-13: We've been able to fend them off, but let's be clear, attacks at this level aren't their real objective. And beyond the surface ruins, the enemy's been ramping up intelligence operations as well.
You pause for a moment.
SHP-13: The Underground wants BR-003. Should they succeed... I believe everyone at this meeting knows what that entails better than I do.
After a stretch of silence, a line of text not your own lights up before your eyes.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> What do you propose?

SHP-13: I'll keep doing my job. But staying on the defensive like this only gives them more chances to test us. And right now, we don't have the capability to hunt them down, and we won't for the foreseeable future either.
SHP-13: So I've got just one suggestion. Or rather, one request.
SHP-13: You can deploy me and all my combat units. Attach me to whichever department you see fit. All I want is to eliminate that Black Ring and neutralize the threat, as fast as possible.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color><size=50> Objection.</size>
A response fires back with near-zero delay, as if on pure reflex. You knew there'd be interference.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> Once a Black Ring is suppressed and eliminated, its Mania signature changes completely. The residual contamination left in the ruins becomes virtually useless for trace study, and we've already exhausted what little value was there. As for BR-000, its Mania is far too violent. It lacks viable research conditions.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> That leaves only <color=#FFBC6F>BR-003</color>.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> Its properties are one of a kind. It's the only Secondary Black Ring humanity can reliably keep under stable control. The research value is incalculable. We've already sunk massive investment into a full control and monitoring infrastructure. The experimental environment it offers, the material samples, the data stream... all of it is indispensable for studying Black Rings, Mania, the DisSea, and even the global catastrophe patterns. It's—

SHP-13: The threat it poses is just as incalculable. You're telling me that because we can study a Black Ring, we should overlook the fact that it's still a top-tier Mania catastrophe waiting to happen?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> You—

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> Let us keep this rational, everyone. 07 is simply upholding their responsibility, presenting the scientific perspective, nothing more. This is standard EDGE discourse. No need to be so tense.
Another designation intervenes at just the right moment, extinguishing the spark of argument before it catches, and smoothly takes the floor.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> To summarize: Representative 07 votes against SHP-13's proposal. Correct?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> ...Yes. I object.

SHP-13: ......
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> Then let's return to the original order. 04, your position?

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-04:</color> ...We take SHP-13's concerns seriously. From the moment this was first raised, we've conducted thorough internal assessments of every detail.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-04:</color> BR-003 is positioned above the city-state. For such an aerial Black Ring, suppression at that altitude presents extreme difficulty and prohibitive cost.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-04:</color> Should anything go wrong during the operation, a Mania overflow at that height means contamination raining down onto the city-state below. Containment would be next to impossible, and for cleanup, we'd be looking at astronomical figures.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> <color=#FFBC6F><size=42>Yes. We've run those projections.</color></size>
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> This isn't a combat mission. It's an extraordinarily complex, multi-layered operation.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-04:</color> And based on current data, 003 is small in size. Whether it could even be converted into a stable, extractable mine after suppression is highly uncertain. High cost, low return. Its input-to-output ratio simply doesn't compare to the West District's second mine.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-04:</color> Post-war finances are strained. Development on the second mine has been stalled repeatedly. Meanwhile, the farlands are aggressively exploring BR-005. That's already putting real competitive pressure on DisCity.

options: Is this an assessment based on Nirvana's interests?

content: EDGE-04: ...I'd ask that we approach this discussion rationally. EDGE-04 oversees strategic resource planning for the city-state's core operations. And DisCity has always stood on the frontlines against catastrophes. Keeping it stable and well-resourced is a necessity for our civilization to endure. EDGE-04: At this stage, resources and focus must be directed toward projects with a demonstrable return trajectory. That is the objective, rational course.

Objective. Rational. What a tidy way to frame it. Nirvana's greed for the West District's mine has been showing its teeth for a while now. Or maybe everyone present is perfectly aware, and the mask was never really on.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> Thank you for your contribution, 04. If I may, I'll speak now.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> I trust your judgment, Chief. You are among our most essential frontline assets. Dependable, perceptive, and never one to mince words. The Underground poses a genuine threat. I won't dispute that.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> But the city-state faces more than one threat.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> The war has only just ended. The international landscape is anything but stable. Fraser's alliance with the Underground has already proven, quite vividly, the reach the farlands can have.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> And until the 9th Agency's foreign intelligence network is fully rebuilt, we have no way of knowing how many other city-states have been tempted down that same path, quietly aiding the enemy of humanity behind closed doors.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> Peace is a delicate thing. We all know the farlands have stayed their hand for one reason alone: the deterrent of BR-003.

options: ...But DisCity has its own military now.

content:
SHP-13: Nirvana Port, the Shattered Blade... General Augustus is back. The city-state has more than enough conventional strength to defend itself.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> But trust and alignment between us still need time to mature.

EDGE-05: The general has turned down a great many of our overtures. We had hoped the trust the two of you share might put her more at ease, that this meeting might see full attendance, given it was you who initiated this proposal. EDGE-05: A pity. [System: EDGE-08 Absent]

SHP-13: She's just out tracking down her troops. Before she left, she made it clear that the Shattered Blade stands behind whatever I decide.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> Yes, she did say that, didn't she. Then let the record show one vote in favor from External Affairs Representative 08.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> You see? The general remains as free-spirited as ever. Doesn't even bother to conceal a position this significant. She'll need time to grow into these responsibilities.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> And until that time comes, we have no choice but to keep our cards close and protect ourselves. Wouldn't you agree?
With a Black Ring?

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> I must apologize, SHP-13. At this juncture, my vote is one of opposition. But please don't read that as a withdrawal of support.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> BR-003's fate will rest in your hands, in due course. And while we await the opportune moment, your efforts will not go unacknowledged. All necessary support to counter the Underground—intelligence, funding, resources—will be made available to you. Manpower, too, of course. I trust we're in agreement on that?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-05:</color> Representative <color=#fb9259>06</color>?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-06:</color> I have no objections. Whatever this meeting decides, I will see it through.
One yes, three no, one abstention... There it is again.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> Well then. Representatives 04 through 08 have cast their votes. That leaves us.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> SHP-13, your proposal is now under formal deliberation. This is no routine undertaking. Should a weapon-grade Black Ring be modified, suppressed, or eliminated, the ramifications extend well beyond fiscal, security, and infrastructure concerns. They demand a comprehensive reassessment of the city-state's entire strategic posture. We must first hear from our specialists.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> Representative 07, please present your analysis from a professional standpoint.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> Understood.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> In consideration of everyone's time, I'll begin with a simplified summary, followed by supporting data in detail. My assessment will cover the following areas: BR-003's characteristics and current status, contamination risk evaluation, existing facility conditions, projected costs, and several related factors.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> First—

SHP-13: I know how these so-called scientific assessments work. You start with the conclusion you want, then build your evidence around it. We've all seen this before.

SHP-13: And I know BR-003 is tied directly to the core projects of your <color=#dg1f1f>research representative</color>, 07. They've been the most vocal advocate for preserving it from the start. An evaluation weighed down by that kind of vested interest isn't going to convince me. They're just here to recite the objections you've already settled on.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> <size=60>Everything I say here has always been in service of my position and my responsibilities!</size>
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> Heh... Alright, alright. Let's all take a deep breath and keep things rational, shall we?

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> As a guest we invited, SHP-13 might be unfamiliar with how we conduct things. But for EDGE members, rationality is the only standard by which we speak and decide.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> And we must model that standard for our collaborator as well, mustn't we?

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> ......Yes.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> Representative 07's report will be compiled for you afterward, in a more accessible format. I do hope it earns your trust.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> But before all that, I'd like to hear your perspective. What is your intention for BR-003? Whose forces do you envision deploying? And the approach? Will it be a small elite strike team going in?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> I recall you've often said you'd rather not drag ordinary personnel into the hazards of a Black Ring. So then...

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> Are you planning to resolve this yourself... to devour it with your shackles?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-02:</color> Wouldn't that be... too risky?
The questions are softly delivered, but they trigger a spike of wariness in you.

SHP-13: Of course I'll need support. FAC assets externally, maybe even the Ring Research Institute. Internally, assistance from the Sinners. I'll use my shackles to keep their contamination stabilized as best I can. And naturally, I'll submit the full operational plan for EDGE review. SHP-13: If what you're worried about is me losing control once I'm inside the Black Ring, well, you're free to invoke those Rules you planted in me.

SHP-13: Isn't that the very reason EDGE is willing to trust me in the first place?
SHP-13: Your only purpose in using me is to <color=#fb9259>fight Mania</color>, isn't it? So what's there to hesitate about?

SHP-13: In this city-state, every soldier fighting on the front lines, every person living under the shadow of the DisSea... they bear these risks every single day.
SHP-13: Because a Black Ring hangs right above their heads, and the Underground has been waiting for their chance. Mania is the greatest threat civilization faces. And if there were a chance to eliminate it, countless people would act without hesitation, whatever the cost.
SHP-13: And yet...

SHP-13: The highest decision-makers, out of all people, are the ones dragging their feet?
SHP-13: A <color=#fb9259>testing site</color>, a <color=#fb9259>mine</color>, a <color=#fb9259>war weapon</color>... are these really worth more to you than Mania and the disasters it causes?
[EDGE Briefing Hall, Transition 2s]
The entire meeting goes silent for two seconds. No text, only stillness. Then another channel, one that has never spoken, flickers to life.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-01:</color> You seem rather worked up, Chief. Are things truly that pressing?

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-01:</color> EDGE is not your enemy. That said, we all have our limitations. That's precisely why we divide seats and responsibilities to complement one another. It's also why we invited you here.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-01:</color> I imagine you're often privy to... certain information. The kind most people cannot access, or perhaps cannot comprehend, even.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-01:</color> Have you uncovered something that has you this uneasy?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-01:</color> If there's any intelligence, you can share it freely. We are prepared to assist in analysis and help you find answers.

SHP-13: ............
Don't say it.
[Small CG: Nightmare]
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-01:</color> Chief?
Control your mind. Don't say a word.

SHP-13: ...Anything I can share is already in my reports. Recent operations have put me on alert, yes, but it's nothing concrete. It's more of a... battlefield instinct. That's all it is.
SHP-13: My gut tells me...
It is true, after all. You don't have any solid intel to offer them.
...You've only had a strange dream.
Your mind hasn't quite grasped what those fragments signify yet, but something deep inside already warns you—
It's dangerous. Don't tell anyone.
[Reuse Nightmare]

speaker: Strange Voice
content: I thought I'd go my whole life without ever laying eyes on you again... and yet here you are. Guess I owe that thing called fate a word of thanks.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Still... now that you've shown up, should I take it you're here to stand in my way? Or did you come to snatch something for yourself?

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Hehehe...
[Eyes Snap Open]
Your eyes snap open. You lift your head and find yourself staring into the open sky.

Beyond the window stretches an endless blue sky dotted with white clouds. It is at the very same height as in the dream, though BR-003 is nowhere in sight. Without realizing it... you let out a breath you didn't know you were holding.
...Another dream.

The frustrating "work" and unsettling premonitions weave together into nightmares that bleed you dry, stealing every moment of rest. Sleeping has become more exhausting than staying awake. You should find a way to vent, to release it all, but—

Softly, the sound of trickling water reaches your ears. A familiar, subtle fragrance drifts with it, stroking your nerves, until, little by little, you feel the afternoon sunlight warming your skin again.
A page turns, the whisper of it brushing past the fine hair at your temple, gently calling your eyes toward it.
[Enter CG: Celine First Meeting]
The woman murmurs the words on the page, her voice hushed and rhythmic, like poetry spoken to no one in particular.
"Time stops for no soul, as the river will not linger. And when you wake, the fleeting light of bygone days drifts away like a dream..."
Her voice, gentle as the poetry it carries, fades into silence. She shuts the book softly and looks your way.
Ah, you're finally awake. You look positively worn down. Was the EDGE meeting truly so trying?
If you'd care to share, I'm more than happy to listen. Recording and analysis have always been my specialty, as you well know.
Her smile, steady and familiar, always settles something inside you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course. I need your help.

DisCity Central Library
Head Librarian Celine Fabius

An S-Class Sinner originating from Paradeisos. Her case file was officially transferred to the MBCC and processed just two weeks ago.
Ability: Memory Maniafication.
[Flashback - EDGE Hall]

speaker: Schorl
content: The scope of information you're interested in spans quite a range of categories, Chief, and the access permissions involved are... let's call it a labyrinth. My current module set isn't really built to navigate that gracefully. Fortunately, there's a dedicated institution designed to field requests like yours.

speaker: Schorl
content: EDGE has granted you a special information security clearance, so you'll now have high-level access to the <color=#fb9259>DisCity Central Library</color>. Beyond borrowing books or films you might enjoy, you'll be able to pull extensive backups of EDGE data.

speaker: Schorl
content: You'll also find exceptional professionals there who can provide the help you need. I'm confident they'll earn your trust.
[Flashback End - Central Library]

speaker: Linda
content: Let's see here... you're requesting Nirvana Group Comprehensive Import and Export Records, Investigation into the N.F. 114 Council Massacre, Ring Research Institute Technology Breach Compilation...

speaker: Linda
content: These files are all classified at very high levels. Accessing them will leave a record, and the relevant entities—Nirvana, the Public Security Bureau, the Ring Research Institute—will be notified immediately. Are you sure that's alright?

<size=42>Linda</size>
Ph.D. Candidate in History, College of Humanities, DisCity United University
Central Library Resident Researcher

speaker: Linda
content: I'm just worried if they find out you're looking into sensitive material like this, it might bring trouble your way...
A hint of concern crosses her face as her eyes move to Celine, her professor and advisor, who's next to you.

speaker: Option
options: Will it cause trouble for you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have nothing to hide. Let them know. I don't care.
Jump

speaker: Linda
content: Oh, no, not at all! All information management here follows proper procedure. Plus, we're just research scholars, historians. We've got no resources, no influence. Nobody's going to bother with people like us.

speaker: Linda
content: It's just that your position is far more sensitive. If anything were to...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's even less reason to worry if it's just about me. It'll be okay, really.
end

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides, your professor herself has said it: historians must keep a neutral, objective stance. Don't trouble yourself too much on my account.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now then, has that stance of yours tilted a little in my favor, Linda?
Linda instinctively claps a hand over her mouth, then gives her head a small tap.

speaker: Linda
content: Ah, sorry. Someone with zero political instincts like me shouldn't be presuming to second-guess your actions.

speaker: Linda
content: But Professor did say you're different from the rest, that you're a friend to us. So, think of that just now as a friend being concerned. It doesn't compromise our academic position. Right, Professor?
As usual, she looks to Celine for guidance, and her advisor answers with a gentle smile.

speaker: Celine
content: Your professor would also like to remind you: the fourth draft of your thesis is due in three days. I trust you've gotten through all the feedback, right?

speaker: Linda
content: Shoot—!! So sorry, I won't disturb you two any longer. I'm going now. Bye!
The young scholar scurries away hurriedly, flustered. She stumbles just a little as she crosses the threshold, until her figure melts into the brightness beyond.

speaker: Option
options: You've got a remarkable student there, Professor.

speaker: Celine
content: Indeed. Of all the students I've had the privilege of teaching, she's the finest, and the most persistent. I'm counting on her to carry on my work someday.

speaker: Option
options: I imagine the teacher deserves some credit for that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Linda's told me more than once how much she looks up to you. Best decisions of her life, she says. Both joining the history department and finding you as her advisor.
The words draw a smile from her.

speaker: Celine
content: Come now, Chief. Every time you show up with that flattering tongue of yours, I know you've come fishing for information. But... your voice sounds especially forced today. And you look utterly worn out.

speaker: Celine
content: Did something go wrong with EDGE?
Her smile settles into something gentler, her eyes warm with earnest concern.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I really can't hide a single thing from you, can I, Professor?
[Flashback - EDGE Hall]

speaker: Schorl
content: Celine Fabius is a scholar of considerable renown in academic circles. She also serves, by EDGE's commission, as our city-state's specially appointed <color=#fb9259>chronicler</color>, in charge of collecting, recording, enriching, and preserving our history from every conceivable angle.

speaker: Schorl
content: Her family holds deep roots in Paradeisos, which has left her with no shortage of connections. Yet despite her abundant resources, she maintains the integrity and restraint expected of a chronicler and witness. Quite admirable, if you ask me.

speaker: Schorl
content: The professor's grasp of DisCity's history—as well as the social, economic, and political currents beneath it—runs deep. Her standing is unimpeachable. I do hope she'll provide the assistance you require.
[Flashback End - Central Library]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That EDGE meeting... Everything you warned me about all came true. They have absolutely no intention of letting go of BR-003.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: 04's almost certainly from Nirvana. Talks a fine game, but all that's running through their head is Hypercubes and profit margins. Honestly, them taking a jab at me while they're at it is whatever. Big corporations have always had it out for me. But what's everyone else's excuse?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've got 05, who talks in circles, slippery as an eel. No idea who's backing them, but they've clearly got weight to throw around. Everything they calculate comes wrapped in all this lofty "city-state interest" language.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then there's 06, who's basically dead weight and just goes along with whatever. And 08 didn't even show. All she left was one vote in my favor. How is that supposed to count as "support"? If she'd actually been there, she could've at least helped me chew them out!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: 01, 02, and 03 claim they won't participate directly. But at an EDGE vote of this level, that's simply not possible—they'd already made up their minds long before. They never would've delegated the decision otherwise.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Still, out of all eight of them, the loudest and by far the most annoying is <color=#fb9259>EDGE-07</color>.
Celine listens to you with a tender look in her eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Theoretical experiments. Professional assessments. They have the nerve to brush off a threat as blatant as a Black Ring, and all they ever have to say for themselves is "research"—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see it now. This whole "scientific rationality" routine is just a front. 07's real job is to cover for the rest of them, dressing up every greedy, self-serving agenda in respectable clothes.

speaker: Celine
content: ...So. You came storming in here to borrow sensitive materials because you needed an outlet for all that anger. You wanted word to get out, to let them know you're furious, that you intend to investigate, to retaliate... You wanted to rattle them a little, I suppose?
She cocks her head, a teasing smile hovering at the corners of her mouth. Now that she's summarized your rant so neatly, it makes your recent actions feel a bit immature all of a sudden.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Ahem. That was part of it, yes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not naive enough to think borrowing "sensitive data" like this will actually get me anywhere. Those people wouldn't stash genuinely damaging intelligence somewhere an outsider like me can just reach and grab. And even if I did find something, who knows how much of it is actually planted by them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That said, I do believe coming here will get me what I'm actually after.
You turn your gaze directly to her.

speaker: Option
options: —Through you, that is. Head Librarian Celine.

content: You look at Celine Fabius.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've heard rumors about your memory, that you've mastered nearly every record in the Central Library, plus classified intelligence passed down through generations of chroniclers. So please, tell me everything you know.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How did BR-003 become a catastrophe weapon? Why wasn't the same process applied to the other Black Rings? What exactly makes its nature so "unique"? Does DisCity have the technology to lift it into the sky and to hide it at will? Keep it hidden from the Underground's eyes?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That and, how many factions are tangled up behind it? Beyond the rational excuses on the surface, beyond the motives I can already see, are there deeper connections? Do they all feed into the positions those EDGE representatives take? Are those factions controlling EDGE itself?

speaker: Option
options: Please, Professor. Tell me the truth.

content: Celine holds your gaze, listening quietly, giving you her utmost attention. When your questions finally taper off, she lets her eyes fall, gathering her thoughts.

speaker: Celine
content: My, those are bold questions. A few of those statements, should they ever leave this room, would stir up quite the storm in Eastside.
The professor's tone, sincere and tender, never fails to hearten you. More importantly, though, is her expression right now, which you've seen before. Your words have intrigued her.
An opening like this absolutely cannot be wasted.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not going to sit around and wait. If the representatives' leanings decide whether my proposal passes, and they love hiding behind "scientific rationality," then that's where I'll hit them first.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Tell me everything there is to know about <color=#fb9259>EDGE-07</color>. I know they're deeply tied to the Ring Research Institute, and it's the only institution directly bound to BR-003 as well. You and the Institute both fall under United University, and you hold a senior position in the College of Humanities. You have to know what's really going on.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want their real motives for clinging so desperately to the Black Ring. The interests at play, the entanglements, and so on. At the next EDGE meeting, I'll tear down the <color=#fb9259>banner of science</color> they're hiding behind and force them to make the truly <color=#fb9259>rational</color> choice.
Celine hears out your impassioned words with a gentle smile, letting your enthusiasm crest and ebb. When you've finally wound down, she leans forward just a little.

speaker: Celine
content: You flatter me, Chief. In terms of influence, research funding, student numbers, institutional standing... the College of Humanities can hardly hold a candle to the College of Science, let alone to its crown jewel, the Ring Research Institute. The Institute's status has nearly eclipsed United University itself. I have no standing to intervene.

speaker: Celine
content: And in any case, for security reasons, the identities of EDGE's highest representatives are kept strictly confidential. How could a simple scholar like myself possibly hope to catch a glimpse of such things?

speaker: Celine
content: If it is information you want, I must ask you to go through the Central Library's proper channels. Most of the time, our role is simply to listen and record. As observers, we are bound to remain fair and impartial. I can't very well undermine institutional protocol by always giving you backdoor access, now can I?
Her gaze finds yours, and her tone drops into something gentler. She offers a tender smile that feels equal parts apology and regret. You know exactly what she's trying to say.
—Great. All that performance for nothing. Looks like it's time for some verbal back-and-forth.
[Flashback]

speaker: Schorl
content: Earning her support will be no simple task. Celine Fabius is not one to choose sides lightly, after all. That objectivity and spotless integrity are the bedrock of her reputation.

speaker: Schorl
content: There's also... some commentary on record. A scattering of assessments, if you will. She's said to have a rather distinctive perspective: truth, in her view, is a precious resource. Not something to be handed out freely. The word people use is... "shrewd." Extremely shrewd. If you want information from her, you'll need to go prepared with something of your own.

speaker: Schorl
content: For your reference, of course.
[Exit Flashback]
Held by her tender gaze, you correct your posture, settle obediently into your seat, and step into the negotiation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand your position. Perhaps I should put it another way—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Tell me about the dynamics within United University. Just name a few key people, the sort of things you'd hear in passing. I can chase down the leads myself, do my own digging.
Celine takes a moment to consider before giving a slow shake of her head.

speaker: Celine
content: The College of Humanities commands little respect, I'm afraid, and I've been buried in my own research. I wouldn't be much help.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then... could you at least get me inside the university? I'd just stick close to you. That way, I can skip most of the security checks and slip in without raising any eyebrows.
A soft sigh escapes her as her eyes fall.

speaker: Celine
content: I'm simply a fragile lady who so rarely leaves home. Travel would hardly suit my condition.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But... all I'm asking for is the truth! As a historian, isn't it your duty to bring truth to the people? To pass it on to those who come after?

speaker: Celine
content: The deeper one wades into history, the more one understands: truth is a blade with two edges. It cuts your enemies, certainly, but it threatens you just as readily.

speaker: Celine
content: At this particular moment, I would strongly caution against wading too deep.
She is truly flawless and unyielding. You've just witnessed the full artistry of a Paradeisian who navigates people like a second language.
But you've known her long enough. You didn't walk into this unprepared.

speaker: Option
options: Of course, I'd never expect to get something for nothing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You mentioned your interest in the West District's development to me before. The people there hold a deep distrust of Paradeisos.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I happen to have a few friends on the inside. If I were to make introductions...
Something suddenly flickers within her eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They might just be willing to set aside their prejudices and share some interesting stories with you.

speaker: Celine
content: ...Do elaborate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The truth behind the High Tower Black Ring. Rustfire's buried history. The things that never make it into the official record... Firsthand accounts. The real story. Wouldn't you want—

speaker: Celine
content: Deal.

Her hand flashes down onto yours, swift as a shadow and entirely at odds with the lazy Paradeisos elegance she wears so well. Then, as if she fears you'll slip away, her next words come rushing out in a quickfire briefing.

speaker: Celine
content: EDGE identities are an absolute red line. BR-003, too, is classified at the highest levels. Under no circumstances can I disclose either to you through unofficial channels. If you truly wish to investigate, you must earn the proper clearances yourself.

speaker: Celine
content: That said, the Ring Research Institute's organizational structure and key personnel are all publicly accessible. Your current clearance already grants you access. What I can offer is a way to study them all thoroughly without leaving a trace. Without anyone ever knowing you looked.

speaker: Celine
content: As for the forces lurking behind them, the ones with agendas that will never see the light of day, and what exactly those agendas entail...

speaker: Celine
content: Two days from now, the College of Science will host a private <color=#fb9259>project symposium</color>, open only to its most valued benefactors. They'll be unveiling certain unpublicized research and discussing avenues for further investment.

speaker: Celine
content: I can furnish you with intelligence on the venue. If you can find a way to infiltrate under a suitable cover, I believe it would advance your investigation considerably.

speaker: Celine
content: That is what I can offer at present. Would this be of use to you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Very much so. Please, tell me more about—

speaker: Celine
content: Wonderful. Then, everything you mentioned just now. I want all of it. The people, the clippings, old logs, on-site surveys, the victims' families, and their personal effects. I trust you'll see to it that everything is arranged.

speaker: Celine
content: Consider what I've just given you the "deposit." Once you've made the arrangements and I've completed my interviews, I'll provide you with further intelligence. So... no backing out now.
The speed of her turnaround is nothing short of remarkable. You—

speaker: Option
options: ...I feel like I just walked right into that.
So much for being a neutral, uninvolved chronicler?

speaker: Celine
content: Hehe, whatever gave you that idea? I was simply moved by your earnestness, Chief. This is a fair exchange, nothing more.
Her hand slips free of yours. Just like that, the poised and serene professor returns, although the sleeve lifted to her mouth can't quite disguise the delight still dancing in her gaze.

speaker: Celine
