speaker: Donald
content: Ahem! Well, hey there, handsome! You look awfully familiar. Spitting image of an old buddy of mine, actually. How about we grab some skewers? They do amazing barbecue in the satellite town!
female_content: Ahem! Well, hey there, gorgeous! You look awfully familiar. Spitting image of an old friend of mine, actually. How about we grab some skewers? They do amazing barbecue in the satellite town!

speaker: Celine
content: It was truly an unforgettable experience. I met the hero of legend and made the acquaintance of a teacher from the Syndicate Academy, who turns out to be a journalist and poet as well. She shared so many fascinating stories with me. The kind you'd never find in any newspaper.

speaker: Celine
content: And then there are Romanesque's two leaders. Heh... This is the first time I've collected "echoes of the dead" as historical source material. I still don't know how to analyze something like that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You might want to take some of what you heard with a grain of salt. Especially Raven's, uh... "literary creations."

speaker: Celine
content: Of course. Organizing the materials, extracting the information, discerning each narrator's subjective lens, and finally distilling a truth one can stand behind... that's the fundamental competency of any chronicler worth their title.

speaker: Celine
content: But for me, the greatest reward was crossing that divide between East and West. Walking down streets I'd only ever seen in photographs. Meeting the people who actually live there. At first, they were wary of a "Paradeisos scholar" like me, and curious, too. But by the end of each conversation... every one of them shook my hand.

speaker: Celine
content: Words, in the end, can only hold fragments. The real history has settled into every brick and stone of West District, into the people whose lives are woven into that place. When they opened their hearts to me... that's when I truly saw the marks time had left behind. And the light still shining through them, too...
Her gaze drifts somewhere far away. It's a long while before she draws it back and lets it settle on you again.

speaker: Celine
content: I can imagine how much you treasure them. And I can guess, at least a little, how difficult it must be for you in circles like these... The calculations, the maneuvering, the impossibility of reading anyone's true intentions. You're not at ease here, are you?

speaker: Celine
content: I can't make your choices for you. The advice and intelligence I offer are just one more voice in the noise. One perspective among many. I'm glad you trust me, but in the fog of an age like ours, you're the one who must ultimately tell truth from falsehood.

speaker: Celine
content: It's not so hard, really. Sometimes you just need to set aside the reports and summaries other people have compiled. Step out of the study. Go see and hear for yourself, up close. The way you took me to the West District.

speaker: Celine
content: As long as you know what you truly want, and you're clear on which lines you will never cross, I believe you can keep moving forward. You'll be able to walk whatever road that leads you down.
As she speaks, your gaze falls upon the book she's handed you. It remains there, fixed, for a long while.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're right. I think I do know what I want.

speaker: Celine
content: Then that's enough. Look into your own heart. And make your choice.

You remotely access Terminal 0490 once more and sync the materials Celine has provided. She's given you a basic overview of the internal dynamics at the Ring Research Institute, a detailed record of Isomer's promotions, as well as a list of projects she's been tied to since assuming the directorship.

An appended note reads: *Materials incomplete. For reference only.* Still, it is more than enough to keep you occupied for a good while. To be frank, you'd much rather see a few lines of Celine's own commentary on the woman. Sadly, the history professor clearly had no intention of leaning one way or the other on this matter, so you'll just have to draw your own conclusions.
That said, within the synced data, there is a section that catches your eye.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nirvana and the Workers: Decades of Cooperation and Conflict. The Formation and Current State of Drifter Camp and Rustfire. ...Heh. You tucked individual biographies in here too? What is this, Lives of the "Saviors"?

They're her notes from the fieldwork she's just conducted, so much of it is still unorganized. Yet, you find yourself flipping through them anyway, chapter by chapter, page by page. When you finally come back to yourself and stop, it's nearly daybreak already.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Isomer
content: You may not have ambition. But everyone has something they refuse to compromise on. Something they'll protect at any cost.

speaker: Isomer
content: You don't want BR-003 falling into the Underground's hands. So... what's the harm in working with me?
Outside the window, the first light of dawn is breaking. BR-003 remains out of sight, yet the weight of that colossal presence high above pressed down on you all the same.

They built such a facility primarily as a deterrent. But perhaps, too, there are those who hope to use it to shield the people below. Whatever the case, until you witness it for yourself, you will never see anything but its phantom.
And so, you finally make your choice.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your application has been approved. You'll be boarding BR-003 shortly. That said, given the sensitivity of the matter, I will be accompanying you. Is that acceptable, Chief?

speaker: Option
options: I've accepted plenty of things already.

speaker: Schorl
content: You're growing more mature by the day. It's rather heartening to see.

speaker: Isomer
content: Hello, Chief of MBCC. It seems you've reached a decision.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cooperation aside, I'll support your safety inspection and provide a responsible assessment. Beyond that, I can't promise anything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I imagine that's good enough for you, Director.

speaker: Isomer
content: Quite enough. Thank you for your cooperation, Chief. Then, in return...

speaker: Isomer
content: Your security clearance has been granted. Welcome to the BR-003 Observation Hub.

May 20, N.F. 116, 11:00 AM
2,800 Meters above DisCity
Ring Research Institute BR-003 Observation Hub
In the VIP seat of the high-altitude shuttle, you watch as the buildings below shrink as a ghostly pattern in the sky slowly grows before your eyes.
Whoom!

The shuttle jolts hard. Blinding color floods the cabin, and in an instant, the blue sky and clouds vanish, replaced by a dark crimson void. It's as if you and the aircraft have tumbled straight into the Black Ring.

But a second look tells you the Black Ring's glowing bands still lie motionless on the horizon. It's the wreckage outside—broken machinery, suspended and rushing past at savage speed—that tells you you're almost there.
[Presentation Room]

speaker: Schorl
content: As you can see, BR-003 is currently the only Black Ring that humans can reliably control. It offers us an exceptionally valuable environment for experiments.

speaker: Schorl
content: The work conducted here includes: dimensional eigenvalue calculation, real-time Mania fluctuation monitoring and early warning, ring structure maintenance and reinforcement, dimensional concealment technology, and so forth.

speaker: Schorl
content: At present, the primary focus remains the investigation of fluctuation data within Mania dimensions. Sarah oversees technical verification, Barrie specializes in signal modeling, while Enya coordinates data analysis.

speaker: Schorl
content: As for the most fundamental layer—the theoretical work on Mania dimensions, that is, would fall within Dr. Lemma's domain.
Schorl walks you through the Observation Hub's operations. You listen, then turn toward the scientists at the right moment.

options: Is weaponizing Black Ring part of your research as well?

speaker: Sarah
content: The previous team completed the basic framework back in N.F. 108. Our involvement is mainly in technical testing and follow-on application development. The primary project is research into Mania dimensional superposition.

speaker: Sarah
content: As for the specifics of the Ring Weapons, for security reasons, all related content has been transferred to higher-level EDGE authorities for centralized oversight. The Ring Research Institute and the Observation Hub are limited to supporting roles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It wasn't exposed until last year's war. How did you keep it hidden before that? Was it your dimensional concealment technology?
They make no attempt to deny it.

options: And what exactly is the underlying principle behind this technology?

content: Your eyes drift toward Lemma. Her head remains lowered throughout, and you cannot tell if she is purposefully feigning obliviousness or simply lost in thought.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let me guess. This is also something I'm not allowed to know?

speaker: Isomer
content: We're partners, Chief. There's nothing to hide between us. It's simply that the theory is rather complex. Lemma is thinking over how to best present it.

speaker: Isomer
content: It might be a bit much to ask of a proud genius. Allow me.
She approaches you with a warm greeting and places herself right at your side, leaving Lemma with no space at all.

speaker: Isomer
content: As we understand it, Mania originates from the invasion of our material dimension by an unknown psychic dimension. The laws governing each side are fundamentally incompatible. Force them together, and the rules collapse, creating twisted, unpredictable chaos. That is what we call a catastrophe.

speaker: Isomer
content: But <color=#fb9259>dimensions</color> aren't limited to two extremes. Hidden within that seemingly chaotic fusion zone between the material and psychic dimensions, there exist multiple <color=#fb9259>sub-dimensions</color>. They don't follow a simple linear sequence. Instead, each is relatively independent, relatively stable, distinct yet layered, entangled in fluctuating multi-state configurations. And it's that very entanglement that creates the semblance of chaos.

speaker: Isomer
content: Think of it like separate slabs of stone that have been stacked atop one another, forming a stratified composite. A Black Ring is the dimensional fusion boundary we can currently observe. It can also be understood as the most prominent of these sub-dimensions. Or rather, a superposition state of multiple sub-dimensions, all overlapping.

speaker: Isomer
content: Building on this theory, we monitor Mania fluctuation data along the Black Ring's perimeter and have fitted six possible mathematical structures. One model's foundation was laid by Summer. Lemma's team carried it further and has since obtained several eigenvalues.

speaker: Summer
content: Oh, you guys actually solved it? Not bad, not bad at all.
Isomer offers her a gentle smile, then takes your arm and guides you to the other side. She summons a floating digital screen and places it before you.

speaker: Isomer
content: Under finite boundary conditions, we can simulate Mania fusion through equations, measure and estimate the relevant parameters, and solve for several eigenvalues. Mathematically, each eigenvalue corresponds to a discrete sub-dimension within the current Mania field.

speaker: Isomer
content: As long as the boundary conditions hold, the eigenspace can remain relatively independent and stable. We transfer BR-003 into the safest one among them, and just like that, it'll vanish from <color=#fb9259>this side of reality</color>.

speaker: Isomer
content: Our current dimensional computation work and the fissure technology derived from it both rely heavily on BR-003's Mania field. Its unique dimensional signature provides the stable boundary conditions that keep our experimental environment and calculations consistent.

speaker: Isomer
content: Once we've fully mastered this technology, we'll be able to apply it across far broader scenarios. I have no doubt it will prove valuable in supporting your field operations as well.
Lemma rolls her eyes.

speaker: Isomer
content: Well then, Lemma, why don't you give Chief a proper tour? You are the project lead, after all.

speaker: Lemma
content: This way.
You have to admit that compared to simulated experiments, the Ring Research Institute's cutting-edge applications perform far better in the field than you'd expected.
And the demonstration of teleportation between multiple fissures is beyond anything you could have imagined. Honestly, you could almost call it magic.

speaker: Lemma
content: This covers our latest progress. Through Mania dimensional entanglement, transitions between superposition states can produce effects like energy conversion, matter transfer, and so on. They're all theoretically sound, all carrying enormous practical value.

speaker: Lemma
content: Of course, implementing any of this relies heavily on BR-003's unique properties. Its Mania field possesses an inherently complex dimensional superposition. That's what lets us identify relatively stable time windows that provide the environment our experiments require.

speaker: Lemma
content: Scaling these technologies beyond this facility and into broader applications will demand significantly more verification. Other teams have been assigned to pursue that. I'll be providing support as needed.
The displeasure on her face is unmistakable, and yet she sees her report through with quiet diligence. By all accounts, she's a project lead worthy of the title.

speaker: Isomer
content: All of these achievements were spearheaded by our Chief Scientist. Summer's departure dealt a devastating blow to the Institute. The project stalled for two full years before Lemma took up the burden, reconstructing the complex models from the notes her predecessor left behind, then carrying them through to computation and full verification.

speaker: Isomer
content: She was only fourteen at the time—a genius scientist, the pride of the Institute, and its undisputed heart.
Lemma rolls her eyes again.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Spare me the performance. You've never once asked about our progress.

You don't let these little interruptions distract you. Instead, you focus on absorbing the technical briefing. There's something else you need to confirm regarding the technology used to conceal BR-003.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So if the enemy were to solve for your eigenvalues first, wouldn't that expose BR-003 to them instead?

speaker: Lemma
content: We have interference and concealment countermeasures, as well as comprehensive protocols in place. We alter the eigenvalues in time to prevent decryption. Combined with our dimensional defenses, these measures bring the risk down to an acceptable level.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But you've been taking hits on a regular basis. Think about it, how many attacks have there been since last August?

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Our progress has fallen behind, yes. The war disrupted too much. The Black Ring was forcibly exposed, used as a deterrent, and that left lasting damage. We still haven't solved for enough stable switching dimensions to fully guarantee security.

speaker: Lemma
content: That said, the theory itself is sound. We're working to close the gap. Once we raise the accuracy rate by another 2.3%, it'll meet the threshold for reliability.
You draw a deep breath, barely keeping your irritation in check. These scientists are definitely brilliant, yet it is just as undeniable that they can be remarkably naive and obstinate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those "comprehensive safety protocols" you mentioned are nowhere near ready, are they? Isn't that why you're so on edge? You're well aware that this project is extremely critical, with all these resources and manpower at stake. At the same time, you know full well the enemy is making their move. The problem is, you aren't prepared.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...There's still time. It's not over yet. I'll do everything I can to make it work.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Does this stubbornness come from the fact that EDGE can't bear to give up such a powerful catastrophe weapon? Does DisCity need it that badly to keep the world in check?
Silence falls over the room. Outside the window, dark crimson shadows slowly drift by.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Even after all these years, no matter how EDGE has evolved since its founding, scientists have always been its core. What we pursue is truth. Our weapons are will and rationality. Our only enemies are catastrophe and the unknown. It's that simple.

speaker: Lemma
content: Don't lump me in with people who have twisted agendas.
Isomer brings her hands together in a single, ringing clap, and the crisp sound severs the thread of your dispute.

speaker: Isomer
content: This is a lecture hall. Keep it professional. Save your philosophy and politics for somewhere else.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...I'm done here. He's clearly not in the mood for testing today anyway. We'll save it for next time.
female_content: ...I'm done here. She's clearly not in the mood for testing today anyway. We'll save it for next time.

speaker: Lemma
content: I need to get back to my calculations. That'll be all from me.

speaker: Isomer
content: I never said discussions aren't allowed.
Lemma barely takes a few steps before being called back. She turns around, visibly biting back the urge to argue any further.

speaker: Isomer
content: Time is running short. If you can't set aside your differences and work together, how are you supposed to collaborate later when every conversation turns into an argument? Your testing schedule still needs to move faster.

speaker: Isomer
content: Take this somewhere else. How about you find a room where you won't disturb anyone?

speaker: Isomer
content: For instance... the <color=#fb9259>common lounge</color>? Even if things get heated in there, no one will hear a thing from outside.

Lemma flinches as though something has stabbed her at the words "common lounge." Her whole body goes rigid in an instant. She wrenches her head toward Isomer, the motion stiff and unnatural, and after a long pause, she finally forces a few words through gritted teeth.

speaker: Lemma
content: No... Not that place! That place won't do.
Without any warning, Lemma's entire demeanor shifts. A strange, taut edge of unease creeps into her voice, the change so startling that it catches you off guard momentarily.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What is the... common lounge?

speaker: Isomer
content: Just a small sitting room in the residential quarters. They like to gather there, to chat and discuss things. It also serves quite well for arguments. There's no need to keep up appearances in there.

speaker: Lemma
content: I said no!
All at once, the blood drains from Lemma's face, and her gaze flickers away, refusing to settle.

speaker: Isomer
content: Really? I thought you loved that room, much more so than you do the lecture hall? After all, you all do spend most of your time in there, no? You've made plenty of breakthroughs in that space as well.
With those words, she turns her gaze to you.

speaker: Isomer
content: Schorl can escort Chief over. I have work to attend to, so you'll have to resolve this yourselves. I'll leave Lemma in your care, Chief. With you there, I have nothing to worry about.

speaker: Isomer
content: Persuading someone and reaching an understanding doesn't always require arguing, now does it?
The ghost of a smile touches Isomer's lips.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...You're doing this on purpose!
Furious, Lemma spins around and pulls out her terminal to make a call. Her other hand clenches so tightly that her nails nearly dig into her palm.
Though the other end doesn't seem to be answering.

speaker: Lemma
content: Tch... of all times...

speaker: Warning
content: Your call cannot be connected. Please leave a voice message.

speaker: Lemma
content: Enya! Listen to me, they're on their way. Don't open the door. Don't let anyone in! Whatever you're doing, stop! Pack everything away! I'm coming right now!

speaker: Lemma
content: Don't let them find out, you hear me?! Not under any circumstances!
Unfortunately, a certain ticking time bomb, who had been completely silent on the sidelines, has chosen this exact moment to go off.

speaker: Summer
content: Ooh, yes! I've totally grasped the fundamentals of dimensional fissures now! This is so cool! For the first test run, how about we open one straight into the common lounge?
Lemma can't even get a word out before Summer snatches your wrist.

speaker: Summer
content: Let's roll, Chief! Here we gooo!

speaker: Lemma
content: Summer!! You—
With a sweep of her hand, Summer carves a gash in the air itself. A fissure tears open before her. Still holding fast to your wrist, she strides straight through.

speaker: Summer
content: Wohooo!
Summer's exhilarated cheer echoes through the rift, leaving Lemma's near-desperate cry of protest far behind.
Inside the fissure's passage, layers of light and shadow sweep past as security cameras and gates flash by like a feverish carousel.
Iris scanners, armed patrols, electromagnetic fences, blast-proof isolation doors... One would think this "lounge" is actually a secret fortress, with how it's sealed tighter than a vault.
It even outstrips the Bureau's highest-level security protocols. You can't help but wonder what exactly lies behind all these layers of lockdown.

speaker: Lemma
content: Whatever you're doing, stop! Pack everything away!

speaker: Lemma
content: Don't let them find out, you hear me?! Not under any circumstances!
Undisclosed Ring Research Institute experiments? Dangerous samples? Forbidden research findings? Or something that even she doesn't dare let outsiders know about...
These grim thoughts race through your mind as you bypass the final barrier, slamming open the massive blast-proof door ahead—
[Idol Music Blasts] chu-lu-chu, pa-pa-pa!

In an instant, a pink melody drowns the corridor. Saccharine synth tones, skipping drumbeats, and lyrics that babble like some primordial language—unintelligible, yet maddeningly catchy—assault your eardrums from every direction.

speaker: Sarah
content: ♪~ Louder! Use your core! What, did none of you eat today?!

speaker: Barrie
content: Clap, clap, clap—hey!

speaker: Enya
content: Da, da, da—huh?

Inside the lounge, Sarah enthusiastically waves a glowing light stick, bobbing to the rhythm. Barrie is slouched on the sofa, clapping along to the beat. Meanwhile, Enya stands by the blackboard, rigorously practicing some idol's signature choreography in front of a mirror.
Enya's hand freezes mid-air as she spots you and Summer in the doorway. The music pounds on, but everyone else goes completely rigid, as if someone hit the pause button for reality itself.
You stand at the entrance of the common lounge, eyes drifting across walls blanketed in a riot of colorful idol posters, unsure what to do or make of the situation.
So much for a classified project... Honestly, kids these days...
You open your mouth, caught between a "Sorry to interrupt" and a "Please, go on." Ultimately, words fail you, and all you can do is awkwardly stare at the paralyzed trio.

speaker: Enya
content: Ah.

speaker: Barrie
content: Enya, you dropped your chips. You still want those?

Enya shakes her head with stiff, mechanical motion. In the thick, near-suffocating silence, one soul remains blissfully detached from the gravity of the moment, launching herself into the room with a buoyant bound.
Summer picks up the fallen bag of chips from the floor, digs some out, and starts munching away with loud, unabashed crunches.

speaker: Summer
content: Sup guys! It's been a hot minute!
At last, the sheer mortification in the room dawns on her.

speaker: Summer
content: Oh, come on. You're all still so shy about this stuff? It's been years! If you really like something, just own it. Be loud about it, like me! There's no need to be embarrassed!
She glances at the posters on the wall.

speaker: Summer
content: Huh... wait. I remember when I bailed five years ago, you guys were into someone totally different. Back then it was all "so-and-so's the best" and "I can't wait for this and that," wasn't it?

speaker: Summer
content: Did your taste change, or did your old fave get cancelled?
You sweep your gaze across the room. Someone's face has definitely shifted.
Summer is still mid-sentence when Enya, visibly agitated and clutching two light sticks, cuts her off.

speaker: Enya
content: Hey! It's called a "graduation." A normal graduation. Unlike a certain senior who's been on the school roster forever and still doesn't have a degree.

speaker: Summer
content: Ohhh, is that so? I'm so happy, Enya. You still call me senior.
She breaks into a wicked grin. Enya's expression slowly melts into a deep, spreading blush, almost like those words were a switch.

speaker: Enya
content: You... Don't think you can still pull rank on me just because you're my senior—

speaker: Barrie
content: Enya, stay calm! Summer's been held back for years. You've already graduated. Technically, you're the senior now. Don't stoop to her level.

speaker: Enya
content: ...Y-you're right! We're operating on entirely different planes now, Summer! What would a shallow, flavor-of-the-month fan like you know about our true, undying loyalty to Phanuel?

speaker: Summer
content: See, that's where you're wrong. If we're talking pure charisma, real people literally got nothing on anime characters. Just look at these G*nd*ms!

speaker: Summer
content: Is it not gorgeous? Is it not glorious? Every year, new models of these perfect beings are born into the world, arriving right before my eyes. When ultimate beauty incarnate enters my field of vision, how could I not fall in love? Perhaps if I were blind.

speaker: Summer
content: So it's not that I'm fickle. It's just that the world is overflowing with beauty. There's far too much of it. I physically can't love it all fast enough!

speaker: Sarah
content: ...Please. I'm begging you. Stop using player logic to justify your idiotic mecha obsession. It's so gross.

speaker: Barrie
content: I mean... there's nothing wrong with liking more things, though? We're all just pouring our love into something that makes us feel good. In that sense, we're kind of the same.

speaker: Enya
content: Absolutely not! The person I stan is a real, living, breathing wonderful human being. I live in reality! I'm nothing like Summer with her plastic model delusions!

speaker: Sarah
content: Yeah. Compared to robots in plastic belts punching and kicking each other, idols who work hard, shine bright, and bring smiles to the world are way more inspiring.

speaker: Summer
content: What are you even saying?! G*nd*ms don't just move. They transform!

speaker: Enya
content: And that's supposed to impress me? Amoebas can transform too! I don't see you stanning them!

speaker: Summer
content: Who says I don't? Among my most treasured thirteen G*nd*ms, the one ranked seventh is the Amoebo Transformer! Don't tell me you've never—

speaker: Enya
content: AAAHHHH—!!
Enya lets out a mortified wail. Sarah, on the other hand, rolls her eyes.

speaker: Sarah
content: You've got some nerve bringing that up. Look at the mess you left behind five years ago.

She turns, flings open the storage cabinet beside her, and hauls out a cart with a clattering rattle. It's piled high, filled to the brim with model kits, parts cases, and neatly numbered storage boxes.

speaker: Sarah
content: The whole five years you've been gone, we've been the ones doing dust prevention, moisture control, and Barrie-proofing. BY HAND! MANUAL LABOR! Do you have any idea what a nightmare your precious thirteen G*nd*ms have been? Do you know how much of our actual research time they've eaten up?

speaker: Sarah
content: All because of that tearful little plea you made before you ran off. Enya threw herself into it completely. She used to look up to you, her "genius senior," so much. And what did you do? You didn't even warn her about the need to do pest control. Just look at her. You've traumatized the poor girl!
Summer gazes down upon the cart's abundant hoard. A heartbeat's contemplation is all it takes before she lunges at it like a starving cheetah springing on its prey.

speaker: Summer
content: Ohhh! My beloved RX-93, RX-78-2, MSZ-006, VXV-016, RX-0... You're still in perfect condition! I missed you so much! Sniff... I'm so sorry I left you for five whole years... You must have been so lonely...

speaker: Sarah
content: ...See? This is what being a weeb does to a person. Turns your brain to mush. Phanuel is way better. She's the cutest in the world.

speaker: Sarah
content: Come on. Let's get away from Summer. We'll practice in another room. We still haven't nailed the fan chant. ♪~

speaker: Summer
content: ...Enya... Sarah... Barrie...
Barrie responds with a cheerful greeting, completely clueless. The other two girls, however, shudder visibly.

speaker: Enya & Sarah
content: Wh-what do you want? Stay back, I'm warning you—

speaker: Summer
content: Thank you—!! I owe you my life!!!
Summer pounces on the girls and bowls them over in an instant. A chorus of shrieks erupts. Watching the children tangled together in chaos, your mind drifts back to earlier...

speaker: Sarah
content: Don't get so full of yourself. I remember perfectly well how you slunk away in disgrace five years ago.
So... this is what that was all about? The hobbies of young geniuses truly are unfathomable.
Before you can even crack a smile, a soft, pained gasp sounds from behind you.

speaker: Lemma
content: Ah!

It's Lemma. She's finally caught up, having pushed herself to the limit in pursuit. Her bangs are disheveled, her shoulders rise and fall with each breath, and she needs to clutch the doorframe just to keep herself upright. To add insult to injury, the moment she looks up, her eyes meet yours.
Gradually, a flush spreads across her face, blooming deeper and deeper into vivid scarlet.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...N-no... it's not what it looks like. What you see here is just... just...

speaker: Lemma
content: Aaaagh—don't you dare laugh!! We're mature scientists! We're by no means childish!!
The moment your laugh breaks free, the "mature and reliable" genius scientist lets out a miserable cry and flees, practically wailing as she runs.
[Special Scene]

It takes some time, but with Summer's intelligence (or rather, bald-faced betrayal), you locate her at last in a lonely, deserted corner at the hallway's end. Lemma's facing the wall, her shoulders drawn tight as bowstrings, not daring to glance back.
After a long pause, a tiny, muffled whimper escapes her.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...It's a perfectly normal way to relax... Even the most brilliant scientists need breaks. We have to engage with society. It's... not childish at all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Absolutely. Maintaining a healthy work-life balance boosts productivity.

speaker: Lemma
content: Exactly... As long as it doesn't interfere with work. Everyone takes their responsibilities seriously. And besides, I'm keeping an eye on things.

speaker: Lemma
content: I'm not into idols. I don't need entertainment. I never leave my post. I am the final safeguard, mature and reliable.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I believe you. You're all exceptional scientists.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Then stop laughing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A professional like me would never... pfft.
She whips her head around to glare at you, her face burning in a deep, furious red.

And that's all it takes to trigger her. The blonde girl winds up and pummels you with a flurry of fists. Unfortunately, her punches, soft as cotton, deal no damage to you. Looks like the little scientist hasn't exercised much.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, no, I wasn't laughing at you guys for being fans. I just think you kids are adorable.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Watching you try so hard to play the grown-up and cover for your friends... it's priceless. Pfft... "What we pursue is truth." Hahahahaha...

speaker: Lemma
content: AAHHH—!
Five minutes in, her fury finally burns itself out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't know my way around this place too well, so I couldn't find any snacks. Want to go grab some together?
She glares at you, still catching her breath.

speaker: Lemma
content: What's this about? Just so you know, I know exactly how you operate. Don't think for a second you can butter me up just like that.
She has a point. When she acted as EDGE-07, the two of you did nothing but argue endlessly. You've never once had a single civil conversation.
With such a jarring shift in attitude, you can't blame Lemma for quickly jumping to such a conclusion.

speaker: Lemma
content: Or is it because you think I'm just some helpless kid now? So you're gonna act all big and patronizing?!

speaker: Lemma
content: Don't you dare look down on me! Those three are the ones geeking out over idols. I would never be that childish! What I pursue is on a completely different plane. It's truth. TRUTH!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Okay, okay, I got it.
...And that's not childish?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't push yourself so hard, scientist. I'm here to help. If you need something, just say so.
The words shut her up instantly. She pulls back her fists, curls into a small, defensive ball, and stays that way for a long while before finally mumbling something under her breath.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...You've already been plenty of help. Thank you.

Faint bursts of laughter still drift over from the lounge area, making this corner on the other end of the hallway feel all the quieter by contrast. That sharp, bristling edge she'd had, the one ready to push back against the whole world, finally begins to soften, bit by bit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Could you give me your honest take on those data anomalies? I'd love to know what the investigator working closest with BR-003 really thinks.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...I can't say for sure. There are too many possible causes. It could be interference from leaking Mania due to proximity to the Black Ring. The last forced deterrence badly damaged our equipment, and some of those flaws still haven't been fixed. Or it could simply be a miscalculation.
She pauses, then presses on, her voice much quieter now.

speaker: Lemma
content: Between the dimensional superposition and the Black Ring's influence, the data we collect here is overwhelmingly dense. On the other hand, the timing and frequency of these anomalies don't match the Black Ring's natural fluctuation cycles. And the equipment failures don't show any of the usual signatures either.

speaker: Lemma
content: There are far too many phenomena I can't reliably explain, and verifying any hypothesis feels practically impossible. Even if I could, setting up countermeasures is...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You suspect a deliberate external intrusion, don't you?
She looks up, stunned. Looks like she never expected you to actually guess it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've investigated every other Black Ring site. The Underground's activity is widespread, scattered, but I don't believe they're interested in picking through dead ruins, no. It's classic misdirection, their specialty. The real target has always been BR-003, the only Ring still active.
She says nothing. A few seconds slip by in silence, and that faint softness that had just begun to surface slowly sinks back beneath her guarded expression.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...You asked earlier why I insist on keeping BR-003 intact, knowing full well the Underground will inevitably come for it. You wanted to know why I kept stonewalling your plan to deal with it preemptively, despite the immense risks. The answer's simple.

speaker: Lemma
content: Playing it completely safe won't get us anywhere. The Underground can operate with such freedom because their grasp of Mania dimensions is far beyond ours. EDGE has hunted them for decades and still hasn't found their hidden entry points. The gap between us is... practically generational.

speaker: Lemma
content: Every single attack catches us completely off guard, and every pursuit comes up empty. They detonate Black Rings, and then simply vanish without a trace... They act with total impunity, and it's because we're failing. It's because we're behind a pack of lunatics, technologically.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...So that's why you're holding onto BR-003 this desperately. You see it as our best chance.

speaker: Lemma
content: Yes. It was a stroke of pure luck, and we have to seize the opportunity. I must surpass them. I have to get to the root of the problem and rip it out. But...
She looks up, and for the very first time, genuine unease flickers in her eyes.

speaker: Lemma
content: If these anomalies really are deliberate attacks orchestrated by them, then... they're too precise. It's all too effortless for them. Their timing is always flawless, keeping pace with our progress at every turn. And they "just happen" to bypass every single obstacle I've been stuck on.

speaker: Lemma
content: It's as if someone is standing far above me, calmly watching as I drag myself through the mud. They are weaponizing my own methods just to mock me. To humiliate me.

speaker: Lemma
content: Every time they create an anomaly... It's like they're saying, "You're so slow. I can barely stand to watch anymore."
But just as you're about to press further, a shrill alarm rips through the air, tearing the silence apart in an instant.

Red warning lights flare to life one after another. A cold, mechanical drone echoes between the metal walls. Lemma's expression shifts in a heartbeat; she spins around and lunges toward the instruments beside her.

speaker: Warning
content: Abnormal dimensional fissure expansion in Surveillance Zone 3!
Data flickers and spikes wildly across the screen. Lemma's eyes sweep over the cascading torrent of readouts, and her pupils contract in a sudden jolt of alarm.

speaker: Lemma
content: Wait... This Mania spectrum... it's...

A Mania dimension tears open, completely out of the blue, its signature unidentifiable, its behavior beyond all control. Fissures far exceeding testing parameters in both size and number bypass the monitoring and alert nodes, spawning one after another in rapid succession. And what emerges through them are...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Underground Puppets!

speaker: Option
options: Give me the coordinates. I'll handle them!

content: Red warning lights pulse relentlessly. Where light and shadow warp and blur, space itself grows ever more unstable. The initial fissures were barely the size of a person, but the new ones tearing open are more than massive enough for colossal Underground Puppets to force their way through.

The rifts rip through the station walls, hurling fragments of metal and stone into the void. Meanwhile, Mania concentration continues to spike. Your power, too, surges in the contaminated atmosphere, allowing you to hold back the enemy's advance for a moment.

But this is hardly good news. Once the Observation Hub, engineered to the highest Mania defense standards, is breached, there'll be no way to close the existing fissures. Worse yet, the endless tide of Underground Puppets will inevitably overwhelm what remains of the security line.
Over the long-range comms, voices from observation stations across the network rise and clash in mounting chaos.

speaker: Researcher
content: Zone Three, pressure's spiking, requesting backup! Shields are about to give. The Mania field's gone completely unstable!

speaker: Researcher
content: Enya's team is moving into position, but... where's Lemma? Lemma, do you copy?
The distant boom of explosions and crashing metal echoes in the background. Then, a girl's voice cuts sharply through the noise.

speaker: Summer
content: Get moving, Lemma! Quit slacking!

speaker: Lemma
content: Slacking?! Me?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ??? When did you even get here?!

speaker: Lemma
content: I'll be fine! Just worry about yourself!

speaker: Lemma
content: Those damned Undergrounders... They're not even bothering with the act this time. Launching a direct invasion is one thing, but they're also using my dimensional fissures against me...

speaker: Lemma
content: This is a direct challenge! They're throwing down the gauntlet at me. Of course I'm picking it up!

Fissures flicker and swell in every corner of the Observation Hub, merging ceaselessly into vast, gaping breaches. Through these tears, the warped, overlapping chaos of Mania dimensions looms behind the surging horde. The enemy has taken your technology and turned it against you, wielding it with far greater mastery.

speaker: Warning
content: Warning: Mania shield efficiency declining to 62%... 58%... 52%...

speaker: Lemma
content: ...The shields are degrading too fast. This depletion rate is abnormal! Activate backup defenses, now!

Lemma's fingers frantically fly across her terminal, rapidly mobilizing every single piece of experimental equipment within the Observation Hub. She's managing to hold the defensive line while simultaneously wrestling the unknown adversary for control of the fissures.
Just then, several unfamiliar error reports flash onto the screen. She freezes for a split second, then grits her teeth and throws herself back into the fight.

speaker: Warning
content: Caution: Shield depletion approaching 70%. Estimated complete failure in 30 seconds. Countdown initiated... 30, 29...
The light barrier cast by the shielding units slowly dims, its glow growing fainter by the second. Meanwhile, error reports continue to pile up on her terminal screen at an alarming rate.

speaker: Lemma
content: Tch... Like hell I'm losing this!

As Lemma desperately fights to hold her ground, the light before you suddenly dims. An exceptionally massive puppet flickers between the fissures, blinking in and out of existence as it closes the distance to the glowing barrier almost instantaneously.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lemma, get back!

You seize the initiative. A torrent of overflowing Potestas power surges, brutally pinning the puppet in place. Black fragments and a foul stench scatter through the air around you, followed by the familiar, piercing sting of Mania.

The puppet's twisted limbs remain paralyzed, barely a step away from Lemma's terminal. A few meters closer, and the entire operations console would be obliterated. Lemma knows this as well as you do, and her small frame tremors at the thought of it. Still, she refuses to back down.

There's no time left. The situation has spiraled completely out of control. You need to reach the one person who can actually take command, but the encrypted channel seems to be jammed by the dimensional chaos, and the contact you struck that deal with still gives no response.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Schorl of EDGE-07, protect your owner! She's in danger!

speaker: Lemma
content: ...? How do you know about...

You're too busy driving the puppet back toward the defensive line to answer her right now. But you can still feel the panic radiating off her, the sheer overwhelm. She doesn't belong on a battlefield like this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You need to go. I'll hold the line!

speaker: Lemma
content: ...No. I am not a child.
A faint quiver lingers beneath her instinctive retort. You sigh inwardly and speak to her in earnest.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This has nothing to do with being a child or not. You're a scientist. Your battlefield isn't here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're someone who's supposed to push into the darkest frontiers, for the sake of humanity. Not get dragged down fighting filth that should've been left far behind.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...I refuse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't allow you to get hurt!

You shove open the control room door, seize her hand, and try to force her into the seat to strap her down. However, with just a single lapse in your attention, she slips free from your grip, spins around, and hits a few keys. The console locks down. The safety restraints snap shut, and you can't pry them open again.
When you turn back, Lemma is rising unsteadily to her feet. Her body is still trembling, but the hesitation in her eyes is now gone.

speaker: Lemma
content: I'm the head of the Observation Hub. The equipment, the data, and everyone's safety—all of it falls on me. I'm not running away!

speaker: Lemma
content: Besides, it hasn't come to that yet.

speaker: Lemma
content: Come out, Keylan-II!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ???? Key what?? What did you just call this Schorl?!
Her black triangle zips out from her pocket. There, dangling incongruously from the lower tip of the sleek, high-tech bot is a... cute little figurine.

speaker: Lemma
content: Activate emergency safety protocols. Grant administrator access. Locate the nearest available secondary terminals.

speaker: Keylan-II (?)
content: (Processing. User appears to be in a hurry...) Command received. Initiating emergency search across all Observation Hub sectors for available secondary terminals.

speaker: Lemma
content: Found them! Three terminals nearby are still intact. Knew my design would work! The layered isolation kept the damage contained. Now I just need to link to any one of them, and we can reboot the anti-Mania barrier and take back control of the fissure generator.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't do this alone. At least wait for actual backup, not—

speaker: Lemma
content: By then it'll be too late. I've got Keylan-II backing me up. Just hold out for sixty seconds. Sixty seconds is all I need to restore the link.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sixty seconds?! That shield's barely going to hold for a few more seconds! You'll be completely exposed! Those puppets—

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Fine. I was a little shaken. Just a little. Don't you dare write me off because of that, SHP-13. Like you, EDGE-07 is also a core force in humanity's fight against Mania.

speaker: Lemma
content: We hold our position, buy time, and counterattack. The odds of success are no lower than 70%—that's my rational assessment. If a 70% chance can secure BR-003, provide us with firsthand intelligence on the enemy, and advance our chances of victory and progress, then that's sufficient. Besides...

speaker: Lemma
content: Those are just some Underground Puppets... I'm the genius of a new generation. Humanity's greatest scientist.

speaker: Lemma
content: No way in hell I'm losing!

speaker: Warning
content: 0. Shield fully deactivated.
As the shield shuts down completely, the protective barrier of light fades to nothing. In the distance, more giant puppets let out low, menacing growls.
Fifty seconds left. You have to hold this ground and wait for Lemma to deliver on her promise—
Every fissure seals shut. The purple rifts close one by one, and the puppets' shrieks slowly fade into the distance.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Did we make it?
Slowly, Lemma drags herself up, disheveled and coated in dust. Her hand is still clamped tight on the terminal button.

speaker: Lemma
content: I told you! I knew it would work! ${PlayerName}, look!
Before you can respond, a mass of twisted shadow begins to coalesce behind her out of nowhere.
The already lifeless puppet remains crumple inward, as if crushed by invisible hands, and where their abdomens were, a new fissure is slowly opening.
Unlike any of the dimensional fissures before it, this one appears darker, much more viscous; its edges seem to bleed, and it exudes a sickening Mania aura.
The secret channel, silent until now, suddenly reconnects, and an urgent shout cuts through.

speaker: Isomer
content: Get away from there!!

speaker: Lemma
content: Huh?
She turns, and the sight seizes her utterly still.

The creature forcing its way out of the fissure is impossibly massive, nearly filling the entire passage. Its body is a grotesque patchwork of countless puppet remains stitched together, every piece still writhing.

speaker: Lemma
content: Argh!!

You release the shackles. In the dense Mania-saturated air, your power flares to blinding intensity, yet it does nothing to stop this abomination. All you can do is throw yourself toward the scientist and shove her aside.
A searing pain rips through you. You never see the puppet move. Instead, that vile fissure seizes hold of you, dragging, tearing, until it devours you like some unseen, gaping maw.

speaker: Lemma
content: No! ${PlayerName}—
Her frantic voice fades further and further away. The void beyond the fissure has swallowed you whole.
[Black Screen + Purple Smoke]
Where am I?
Your consciousness is torn apart, then reassembles itself piece by piece. In the murk between states, it's the cold that finds you, one that mirrors the temperature of your own body.

You lie half-submerged in water, your soaked shirt clinging to skin, and the slightest shift stings like flesh peeling away, almost like... the water is boiling. And yet, a deep chill has settled inside you. Red light pulses and sways before your eyes, a vision caught somewhere between dream and delusion.
A strange, cloying fragrance wafts through the air, thick enough to choke on. From it, tendrils of violet smoke curl into a warped human shape and drift toward you, unhurried and near.

Several lances of blue light tear suddenly through it like a volley of bullets, blasting it apart into a mess of pulp that splatters into the water. And before you, veiled in haze, a black triangle takes shape.

speaker: Blurry Black Triangle
content: Chief... Chi...
You lack the strength to even answer. It simply hovers beside you, blue light still sweeping the darkness. Following the beam, you spot more indistinct shapes farther out. And then you see...

Crimson spikes spear up through the water, ripping aberrations limb from limb. Fragments of all sizes now drift on the surface. So you were fighting your own battle all along. How long has it been? Even your shackles have wearied, now capable only of gathering close, standing guard at your side.

speaker: Twisted Shadow
content: A heavy price... why is it him... wrong person... intercepted...
female_content: A heavy price... why is it her... wrong person... intercepted...

speaker: Twisted Shadow
content: Careful. Were our faces seen? Shh, keep it down... we might be recognized... Just kill... kill...
Every strike cuts through nothing but smoke. Here, in this uncanny space, wrapped in curling incense, you have no way to tell substance from shadow.

speaker: Twisted Shadow
content: Don't worry. He's barely holding on... won't make it, can't get out. A <color=#fb9259>defective</color> one, after all...
female_content: Don't worry. She's barely holding on... won't make it, can't get out. A <color=#fb9259>defective</color> one, after all...

speaker: Twisted Shadow
content: Just look... A defective thing worshipped by those Overground fools, fit only to mimic, never to touch true divinity...
Schorl, too, slowly falls silent. Along its polished surface, twisted crimson threads have taken root and spread. All blue light is unmade before it can coalesce, siphoned away.

In its final moment, it lowers itself, drawing close to you, still straining to convey something, but the red threads seal it shut. Finally, it is dragged beneath the surface into utter silence. Only chaotic, dark laughter coils around your ears.
Then, all at once, the world falls quiet. A voice rises from ahead. Frail, and yet startlingly clear.

speaker: Frail Voice
content: ...There now. Mr. E won't be back for a while... Please, allow me to keep our guest company.

speaker: Frail Voice
content: The fact that he's here at all... consider it a message from "god."
female_content: The fact that she's here at all... consider it a message from "god."

content: Her voice scatters the chaos. The cloying fragrance draws back, and your consciousness seeps back in.
[Barely Open Eyes] [Empty Scene]

This is not the Observation Hub. It's some other dimension, yet undeniably real. Beneath your feet, the submerged tiles burn. Lifting your gaze, you can just make out the pool's edge, where a set of steps climbs upward and vanishes into shadow.
You remember now. You pushed Lemma aside, tore into the puppet, and were swallowed by the fissure within its body. Looks like it's dragged you somewhere else. The Sillage Society, perhaps? Or...
Did Lemma's dimensional engineering pinpoint the Underground's entrance? The air here is loathsome, yet tinged with a familiarity you cannot name.
Something stirs across the water's surface, spreading as it dissolves the scattered debris piece by piece. It's... threads of blood, fine and seeking, like tendrils of dodder vine.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Who are you?

speaker: Frail Voice
content: I am Sillage, the <color=#fb9259>Sage of Death</color>.

speaker: Frail Voice
content: Which, at the moment, I suppose... makes me your enemy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Like Adelaide. You're an Undergrounder...
[Release Shackles] Furious Questioning

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It was all you... BR-003... every Black Ring... the catastrophes, Mania... when does it end?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you lunatics even want?! How many more have to die?!
She offers no answer to your frantic questions. You cannot see where she stands; you only feel the touch against one of your shackles, a contact that sends a tremor rippling through you.

speaker: Evelleon
content: ...Shackles... How nostalgic...
[Entrance] [Back View] [Intersperse two nightmare images (no one in center)]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't—

speaker: Evelleon
content: Shh... It wouldn't be ideal to let them hear you.

speaker: Evelleon
content: All I want is to take a look at you. That's all. Nothing else.

speaker: Evelleon
content: ...So, we meet at last.

speaker: Evelleon
content: How did you get in here? No one told me you would board the Ring. The sorcerers weren't after you either. You shouldn't have been pulled into this...

speaker: Evelleon
content: Did you force your way through the fissure with your shackles? Or did you somehow find new friends, even in a place like that?

speaker: Evelleon
content: I've heard you're always throwing yourself into the fire for them. Not exactly the best habit, I must say...
Her fingertips graze your wounds. The sting dissolves, your senses flood back, and to your bewilderment... her movements carry something strangely, impossibly gentle.

speaker: Evelleon
content: I never meant for you to get tangled up in this. Stand down. Don't get yourself hurt. It's not time yet... This is not something worth going to war over.

speaker: Evelleon
content: Or... we could make a deal. I have someone precious to me too. So, I need <color=#fb9259>BR-003</color>. Give it back to us.

speaker: Evelleon
content: In return, I'll have a word with Mr. E. Keep his dogs on a shorter leash. I'll do what I can to spare your friends. How does that sound?
Every word of this bargain sickens you. Clarity has returned, and with it, your shackles strike, plunging through her body in one clean thrust. She, however, does not react.

Dodder vines swiftly creep over her wound, spiraling around your shackles. An indescribable dizziness overtakes you. You try to pull back, only to find that the shackles have already fused into her, leaving behind only a hollow.

speaker: Evelleon
content: Even your tempers are alike... No matter. There's no rush.

speaker: Evelleon
content: Little broken Shepherd... Since you won't hear me out, do keep yourself safe when you go back. Don't die too soon.

speaker: Evelleon
content: ...I'd still like to see you two reunited. Dearest siblings, together at last...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You...

She lifts her eyes toward some point in the dark, and a smile crosses her face. Then, she pats your cheek gently before releasing you. You sink back into the water, suspended only by the finest dodder threads winding beneath the surface, still pumping something into your veins.

Already, she has turned her back, walking into the haze of purple smoke and strange fragrance. The wraithlike figures from afar erupt into exultant cries, chanting a name in frenzied worship, one utterly foreign to your ears.

speaker: Evelleon
content: The lamb has been offered. Come forth, praise its name. Sillage shall guide you through the narrow gate; death shall ferry you into eternal life.
Mania seethes, rising in unison with the chant. The warped crimson mark on the woman's waist kindles before your eyes, blooming like a flower unfurling its petals. It makes even the shackles tremble.
She intones the chant, raising her cupped hands high, the water pooling in them like blood. Her gaze lifts toward the sky, heavy with expectation. And then, from the very point she watches...

Beams of laser tear through the smoke, stabbing directly into the pool and scattering water into the air. The ritual convulses and breaks. The gathered shadows flee in chaos, and there, suspended above, a familiar fissure rips open. Then you hear—

speaker: Other Side
content: <size=45>Now!</size>
In that very same breath, your shackles quiver with recognition. A familiar voice reaches your ears.

speaker: Distant Voice
content: Lemma, we good on the numbers? 'Cause I'm firing!

speaker: Distant Voice
content: Hang tight, Chief! Backup's inbound. Here comes the big climax!
Ah... At last, the world before you sharpens into clarity. Your heartbeat finds its rhythm again, and you know with absolute certainty what must be done.
[Release the shackles]

The water around you is hurled aside. A sphere that spans two meters blooms around you, the black triangle at its heart. Inside, space splinters into countless fractured layers, and you feel your own body beginning to come apart with it.
But someone has already traced the shackles to you, locking on with unerring precision. Arms wrap around your waist from behind, pulling tight. You glance back, and it's exactly who you thought—

speaker: Summer
content: The hero has arrived!

speaker: Evelleon
content: Since you won't hear me out, do keep yourself safe when you go back. Don't die too soon.

speaker: Evelleon
content: I'd still like to see you two reunited. Dearest siblings, together at last...

When you open your eyes again, you are in a hospital room. The arrangement is unfamiliar; this is not the Bureau, you realize. Then your gaze finds the emblem on the wall—it's the Ring Research Institute.
At your bedside, Summer stands with her hands planted on her hips, talking animatedly into her phone.

speaker: Hella
content: The hell happened to Chief?! That big dummy got into that much trouble?!

speaker: Summer
content: Relaaax, we got Chief back, safe and sound! We've got two big shots on the case, y'know!

speaker: Summer
content: Especially a certain blonde grump. She did all the heavy lifting. If only she wasn't too shy to show up here.
Seems like she isn't aware you're awake. She's still chattering away into her terminal, giggling and boasting with unmistakable delight. It's Schorl who takes notice first.

speaker: Schorl
content: Hello, Chief. You're looking better than anticipated. Shall I let everyone know?
You shake your head and simply raise a hand toward it, fingers forming the number seven.

You think back to the moment you were taken. The enemy's original target, Lemma, was right beside you back then. Whatever else she may be, she is still a child. You can't help but wonder how she's faring now.

speaker: Schorl
content: If her well-being concerns you so, would you like to go check on her?
[Scene Change]

She's not in the dormitory, nor the lab. You've heard that Lemma pulls more overtime than anyone. She has practically turned her office into a private living space, one she never lets anyone enter. Alright, then. You'll slip over and find out for yourself.

Another long, curving corridor stretches ahead. The entire length is lined with cameras and monitors, which Summer disables with a simple wave of her hand, one after another. That said, what's truly surprising is that Lemma hasn't noticed a thing.

At the corridor's end, a plain, modest door hangs slightly ajar. Through the gap, you can just make out Lemma's voice. She's talking to someone on the phone. She hasn't even realized the door is open, or that someone has arrived. Her spirits have sunk so low that even her voice has gone soft, diminished.

speaker: Lemma
content: Mm... yeah... I do understand. I'm being rational about this. It just... doesn't sit well with me.

speaker: Gentle Voice
content: You contributed so much. Plus, you made an unexpected breakthrough with your dimensional calculations, no?
That voice... you know it from somewhere.

speaker: Lemma
content: But he still got hurt because of my call, at least in part... It was my first time out in the field, seeing it firsthand... Watching someone get injured... it's somehow worse than studying Corruptors...
female_content: But she still got hurt because of my call, at least in part... It was my first time out in the field, seeing it firsthand... Watching someone get injured... it's somehow worse than studying Corruptors...

speaker: Gentle Voice
content: Then go tell him how you feel. Say you were worried. Thank him. If you feel sorry, apologize. Though I'm quite certain he wouldn't mind it at all.
female_content: Then go and tell her how you feel. Say you were worried. Thank her. If you feel sorry, apologize. Though I'm quite certain she wouldn't mind it at all.

speaker: Gentle Voice
content: Think of Keylan and his expedition team. Not all of them were brilliant scientists, yet they still became true companions bound by the same vision. You've always wanted comrades like that, right?

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Yeah.

speaker: Gentle Voice
content: There you go. And look, seems they've already come looking for you.

speaker: Gentle Voice
content: Keep it up, Lemma. You'll do just fine.
And of course, the door gives a long, mournful creak right at this moment of all times. Lemma spins around, and the second she sees you standing there, her face floods with bright red.

speaker: Lemma
content: You—I—wh-who said you could just come in—?!

BAM! Summer catapults herself from behind you, flinging the door wide and tumbling into the room in a maneuver that tears a horrified shriek from Lemma. And at last, you are granted full view of the astonishing chamber belonging to none other than the Ring Research Institute's Chief Researcher, Head of the Observation Hub, genius scientist, and EDGE-07 seat holder among humanity's foremost leaders.

The first thing to seize your attention is an enormous Keylan poster mounted on the wall. Against it stands a glass display case: on its highest shelf, figures of the expedition team; on its bottom, rows of manuscripts, all carefully arranged. You struggle to contain your astonishment as your eyes sweep further across the room. Off to one side, a desk lies strewn with keychains, card sleeves, protective covers, glittering stickers, and expedition team cards—some still only half-finished.

speaker: Schorl
content: Lemma's idols, so to speak. A rather... extensive collection.

speaker: Summer
content: Told you she's one of us! Same old Lemma... What's the point of hiding it?

speaker: Summer
content: So, what'll it be, princess? In the market for the latest collector's edition expedition figures? I'm sure I could coax Faye over at the MBCC Supply Office into helping us develop them.

speaker: Barrie
content: It's totally fine, Lemma. We all look up to idols. It's how we grow, how we feel love. There's nothing to be embarrassed about.

speaker: Enya
content: Exactly! We're into real people, which is way more sophisticated than whatever anime fantasy Summer lives in. We're warriors of real love, comrades on the same front!

speaker: Sarah
content: Your idol's figure is a little faded. Honestly, it kind of looks like he's balding. Do you want me to touch it up?
The blonde girl's cheeks burn brighter and brighter, the tension coiling so tight a single pinprick might undo her, and that's when her gaze finds yours.

You meet her eyes, a dozen unspoken questions crowding your mind. Was she hurt? Was she frightened? How did she bring you back? Was there a breakthrough in the dimensional technology? Who was with her on the call?
But your gaze slips, just for an instant, to the space beside her—to the black triangle suspended there, a strange little doll swaying from its form—and the question that finally escapes you is:

speaker: Lemma
content: <size=50>DON'T SAY IT!!!</size>

speaker: Linda
content: Lemma practically lives at the library. Naturally, we got to know each other pretty well after a while.

speaker: Linda
content: She's especially into the history of science. At one point, she even dreamed of writing her own book titled DisCity's Golden Age of Science. Too bad research ended up eating all her time, so... she's been pinning her hopes on Professor Celine to carry the torch instead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see.
So that's who Lemma was speaking to earlier. A scientist and a humanities professor... an unexpected pairing indeed.
That reminds you. You turn your gaze to Linda.
The word "dissertation" makes her face seize up, as though she's on the verge of a cardiac episode.

speaker: Linda
content: Well... I've only just passed the internal review. I was a wreck during the defense. You know, the history department hasn't produced a single PhD in forever. All my classmates, seniors, juniors... they've all jumped ship. Some bailed right after undergrad and went straight into law, finance, that sort of thing.

speaker: Linda
content: I quite literally don't have a single peer I can turn to for advice. And whenever I ask my professor, all I get is, "It's great, don't worry. Well-written. Start thinking about publication." Is that not terrifying?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That sounds about right. I read through your dissertation, you know. Your account of the West District was thorough and completely objective. My friends and I were genuinely moved by it.

speaker: Linda
content: I... I'll keep doing my best.

Linda offers a shy smile. A sense of deep and profound ease settles over you. After long stretches of work, you always find yourself drawn to places like this, somewhere to shake off the weariness and restore the spirit.
Which reminds you that there's another lively soul here you're particularly keen to track down and amuse yourself with.
A few steps more, around the corner, and you locate one of the study rooms. You push the door open.
The blonde genius scientist very nearly leaps clean out of her skin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Didn't you say you were worried about me? You've been sneaking glances through the window this whole time, surely you didn't think I wouldn't notice? Come on, since I'm here, let's hang out.

speaker: Lemma
content: No... I've got your number now. You're a cunning old fox, just like her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Celine mentioned you're into the history of science. Especially the expedition. Lucky for you, I happen to be an expert. You can ask me anything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm out on missions every Illusory Moon cycle. I'd say I know quite a few things.
She shoots you a glare.

speaker: Lemma
content: No thanks. I've already read all your mission reports.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The esteemed EDGE-07, keeping tabs on a humble MBCC Chief's field operations? Is that part of the fangirl routine too?

speaker: Lemma
content: That was work! WORK! Rational data collection! You... you're impossible—!
There, there. You've squeezed enough entertainment out of this. Push any further and she'll actually bolt. You dial it back, settle into the seat beside her, voice softening.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Unusual idols. I'm a fan of theirs too, actually. What is it you like about them? The "talent" part?

speaker: Lemma
content: Of course! A brilliant mind is one in a million, humanity's rarest resource. Genuinely priceless. We can excel at anything we set our minds to, far beyond what ordinary people can manage. That deserves admiration. We have every right to take pride in that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pfft. You say that, but I've actually met expedition members. None of them were half as cocky as you.
She shoots you another death stare, though this time she keeps a lid on it.
Lemma then drops her gaze, fidgeting with the book in her hands. Only now do you get a clear look—there, on the cover, is a handwritten title that reads DisCity's Golden Age of Science.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...That's exactly why I think those scientists, the true geniuses, were the greatest people in the world.

speaker: Lemma
content: They were brilliant enough to go into politics, build business empires, or trade stocks to amass a fortune. Those with true intellect see wider, further, and deeper than anyone else. Countless paths naturally open up before them. No matter what they choose, they are bound to succeed.

speaker: Lemma
content: But instead, they picked the loneliest road. Fields humanity doesn't even understand yet. They chose the most dangerous, most grueling, most uncertain place, and challenged the unknown there. As well as... themselves.

speaker: Lemma
content: Science is the cruelest battlefield. You walk a narrow path along a lonely peak, raising your torch to light up the darkness, and time after time, all it shows you is your own failure and ignorance.

speaker: Lemma
content: Doubt, arrogance, cowardice, anxiety... Any one of them can kick you straight into the abyss. There, no one will stand beside you. Even if you keep going, you'll never know whether you're simply a fool—too stubborn to realize you've been walking the wrong path all along.

speaker: Lemma
content: Yet they kept walking. To this day, the theories they built serve as torches for those who follow. Their spirit, precious as gold, still guides us forward. The road they once walked alone has become a glorious legacy. Now it's been passed down into my hands. I love it. I've always loved it.

speaker: Lemma
content: I... want to become someone like them.
Her wish comes out as a whisper, like a stone dropped into a lake.
You can't quite name the feeling stirring within your chest. Yet before you realize it, the question has already left your lips.

speaker: Lemma
content: Scared of what?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of those ruthless Undergrounders. Of... the Black Rings, the catastrophe itself. You...
...You're just a kid. You could get killed at any moment, like what almost happened back there.
She lets out a soft, amused laugh, that proud, self-satisfied look of hers slipping back into place along with it.

speaker: Lemma
content: Who do you think we are? We're scientists! Ignorance is way scarier than death to us!

speaker: Lemma
content: Besides, I'm EDGE-07. Best of the new generation, a certified super genius. Even if my tech falls into the wrong hands, I'll outmatch them in theory, in calculations, in pure intellect.
She tilts her head back, hands planted on her hips. It's a mirror image of Summer's pose, lacking only a foot braced triumphantly upon the desk.

speaker: Lemma
content: And if science alone can't hold back the catastrophe, then I'll stand on the front line myself. I'll face what ordinary people are too scared to face in their stead. I'll conquer that fear. I'll tear the unknown wide open for all of humanity. I've even got a whole team with me!

speaker: Lemma
content: That's my mission as Lemma. It's what a true genius should... no, must do.
Another stone dropped into the water.
Lemma turns to face you, and something within her eyes completely changes.

speaker: Lemma
content: So stop being so spineless, and stop talking about shutting down BR-003 already. We have to <size=45>face it</size>. This is our best shot at cracking the Black Rings. You did pretty well last time, didn't you? Fight on, don't chicken out!

Water leaps into the air in glittering droplets, and the sun, passing through pane after pane, finds its way at last to her golden hair. You simply watch, your gaze lingering far longer than you intended.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I have to say, you really are a little like them.
You reach out and ruffle her hair.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pushing yourself this hard... You sure you're not going bald yet? Let me check.

speaker: Lemma
content: !@#$%^&!! Ugh, don't touch my hair!! You're so annoying!

speaker: Linda
content: Oh! Teacher—
At the sound of Linda's voice, Lemma bolts upright. Her eyes light up, and she's already poised to lunge toward the door.

speaker: Lemma
content: Professor Celine! Uh...
But it's someone else who walks through that door.

speaker: Raven
content: So I hear DisCity's finest student is in the house! Let me have a look. Set a good example for my wayward student here. You want your name in the history books too, do you? Splendid! Let this great poet compose an ode to a great scientist!

speaker: Lemma
content: Aaahhh—!!

speaker: Crache
content: Quit scaring the kid. And who are you calling wayward?
[Small CG: Everyone has gathered]

speaker: Hecate
content: Hella, you're carrying so many books... Are you actually going to read all of them?

speaker: Hella
content: What, I'm just looking at the pictures. I'll flip through them real fast! I wanna learn stuff too, okay? Crache feels the same, right?

speaker: Hella
content: Besides, don't we have a little young lady at home who can tutor me?

speaker: Elvira
content: But Hella, these are all doctoral dissertations... Black Ring research and things like that... I can't understand them either... Oh, there's a famous scientist right beside you. Maybe she could—

speaker: Lemma
content: Excuse me?! D-don't come any closer! Don't you dare infect me with your dumbness—

speaker: Summer
content: Lemma, that's totally unscientific! Intelligence doesn't spread through cell contact, you know? Guess you didn't even need to be infected——

speaker: Lemma
content: SUMMER!!!

speaker: Linda
content: Slow down, slow down! This is a library. Please be quiet—

The room swells with more and more people, until it seems it can hold no more. At last, you find a gap and slip away, leaving the warmth of the crowd behind. You climb the stairs alone and find Celine in another small room.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It might be faint, but the shackles can sense registered Sinners, Professor. I know where to find you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why hide away up here? Were we too much?

speaker: Celine
content: Not at all. After my trip to the West District, and after meeting with you, I've been full of new ideas for my research. And besides...

speaker: Celine
content: As you might be aware, Linda's been on my case. I really do need to catch up.
You observe her perfectly unruffled expression and think to yourself: Sure, but the 8 whole camera feeds on the screen next to you say otherwise. You've been watching the whole time.

speaker: Celine
content: On top of that, you've finally made genuine contact with EDGE-07. You should take the time to connect. Your relationship was rather strained before, after all—with all those misunderstandings between you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those stories about the scientists... you're the one who told them to her, aren't you? You made them sound so romantic. I bet you'd be able to write the most beautiful fairy tales.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can hardly imagine someone so pure-hearted coming out of a place like the Ring Research Institute otherwise.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's lucky to have a teacher like you.

speaker: Celine
content: You're flattering me again.

You stepped willingly into United University, entered the Ring Research Institute, and boarded the Observation Hub, all for BR-003. So many faces, so many things. You witnessed minds that should have remained incorruptible eroded one after another, as halls meant to inspire reverence crumbled piece by piece.
And yet, just moments ago, in that child, all the stifling weight you had carried was swept clean away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
