content: Do as you see fit. I'll back you up on this.
The voice of the Speaker of the City Council is unmistakable. Daniel immediately straightens in his seat, his eyes darting toward the door as it's abruptly pushed open.
9th Agency operatives and senior sheriffs gradually fill the room. Someone refills your cups. Someone else leans against the doorframe, leafing through a file. No one speaks or looks at him.

People involved with the Sillage Society seem to place an almost superstitious faith in their so-called "connections." Knowing certain people boosts their confidence, but the moment an opponent brings out a few powerful figures, that confidence evaporates instantly.
It's time. You rise and circle around behind him, placing a hand on his shoulder. You feel him tense for an instant.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know you're not just waiting for your lawyer. You're also counting on a few <color=#fb9259>special friends</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you waiting for this?
You hand over the "evidence." The poor man takes one look, and his eyes go wide.
[View Image] Death Incense

speaker: Option
options: This was found in your basement.

speaker: Daniel
content: This... How could you... Did you have a search warrant? What about my privacy... I... I don't know anything...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The security of BR-003 is the top priority. Mania threats must be eliminated. The MBCC has special authorization for all related operations. Search warrants and lawyers are irrelevant at this point.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As for those friends of yours... I don't know how influential they might be. Perhaps they're capable of protecting you. Or perhaps...
You lean down, moving close to his ear.

speaker: Option
options: They'll take this opportunity to cut you loose and save themselves?

content: Daniel shudders.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ha, it's just a guess. You certainly know your pals better than I do, Mr. Horston. You know how they treat their "friends."
Having said that, you straighten back up and give his shoulder a pat, smiling.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I believe you have no ill intent. You only want to inherit the family business, help it flourish, and earn your place in the family. You were simply deceived and exploited by certain dangerous individuals in the Sillage Society.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In a situation like this, the sooner you come clean and distance yourself from them, the better. A competent businessman like yourself should be able to do the math.
One last gentle pat, and his body sags under the impact.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's fine if you don't want to talk. I have other "guests" waiting for me anyway. Let me go check on them. Take your time.
The moment you turn to leave, Daniel Horston finally grabs your sleeve. His lips are drained of color, trembling so hard he can't form words. And that's how you know...
It worked.
[Black Screen] Style 14

Daniel Horston inherited his family's ties to the Sillage Society. His involvement has largely been limited to networking and pursuing business opportunities. He has benefited from the arrangement and, from time to time, carried out assignments on the Society's behalf—smuggling goods, gathering intelligence, silencing troublesome individuals, and the like. He has even botched some of these relatively minor tasks. As a result, he has never earned the chance to discuss further collaboration with Isomer, nor has he even met the Sillage Society's inner circle.

In his eyes, the organization is little more than an exclusive club with an air of mystery, a place to make money and build connections. Strange incidents happen from time to time, certainly, but this is the age of Mania. A few oddities here and there hardly seem worth dwelling on.

The Sillage Society's members are extremely cautious and rarely meet in person. (Daniel, it seems, has never even been invited to Euphoria.) Communication happens primarily through incense burning, a method that's both safe and discreet. It also fosters the illusion of being guided and blessed by some mysterious higher power.
And just as Elvira theorized: The incense is strictly bound to its designated user. It must be lit by that individual personally in order for it to "work."
In Daniel's house. To avoid alerting the Sillage Society's informants, you change into plain clothes and bring only Schorl inside with you. The black bipyramid rests quietly in your chest pocket.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: As you ordered, the other guards are maintaining a 50-meter distance. Your entry is therefore highly risky, Chief. Please be careful.

speaker: Option
options: I still have you, don't I?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even Mania has to obey some logic. This half-burned incense stick can't be stronger than you. Otherwise, the Sillage Society would've already obliterated DisCity. Why would they still be operating in the shadows?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just stay alert. From this point on, radio silence. Don't let them spot you.

speaker: Schorl
content: Understood. I appreciate your recognition.
...Didn't that sound a little smug?

Daniel, meanwhile, is far from relaxed. He leads you into a special room, closes the door, locks it, and pulls every curtain shut. Darkness swallows the space, as though he's completing some kind of ritual.

Finally, with trembling hands, he lights a candle. In the vast room, this single flame is the only source of light. Still shaking, he produces that broken half of an incense stick and brings it close to the candle's flame.
Before he lights it, he turns back to look at you. His eyes are desperate, almost pleading.

speaker: Daniel
content: ...You'll protect me, won't you?
He can't see the shackles you're gripping lightly, but he can see the steady resolve in your eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm watching. I won't let anything harm you.

Reassured, he turns back around. He takes a deep breath and lights the incense tremulously. A wisp of smoke rises, winding and spreading like a living thing. The candle's flame dims gradually until it goes out entirely.

Your eyes adjust to the darkness quickly. Then you see it clearly—around the smoke, a dark purple mist hovers, faint at first. Slowly, it grows thicker, expanding and creeping into every corner of the room.
[Sillage CG Flashback]
That's right. It's <color=#fb9259>her</color> scent, laced with ominous Mania, seeping into your mind.

The boundaries of space seem to writhe and dissolve, as if the darkness is reconnecting to her domain. In a daze, through the mist, you hear a drifting, somber voice and glimpse overlapping, shifting figures that seem so unsettling.

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: Through chaos wanders the lamb, blindfolded and bowed. Mired in dust and mud, it knows nothing of the stars above, for it never raises its gaze...

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: The exalted one stands upon the dais, staff in hand. Through silent nights of contemplation and beyond the veil of mist, he shall see with clarity, and he shall guide the way...

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: Bow before the abyss, chosen one, and confess unto chaos. Thereafter, <color=#fb9259>she</color> shall guide you; <color=#fb9259>she</color> shall favor you... Sillage shall lead you through the narrow gate, and death shall ferry you into eternal life...
As if it can smell the two of you, the smoke moves and coils around Daniel slowly, then winds its way to you. The scent grows stronger. The voices draw closer.

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: You lit the incense. You, too... were chosen, guided, and rewarded...

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: ...Why, then, do you betray <color=#fb9259>her</color>?

At the accusation, the fragrance coiling around you both constricts violently. A suffocating grip closes around your throat. In the corners, the drifting purple smoke gathers suddenly, writhing and condensing into familiar Puppets of the Underground. They lunge straight at you.

speaker: Daniel
content: Ahhh!!!

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: You glimpsed the truth. Why return to ignorance? You were granted power. Why accept cowardice?!

You yank him behind you. In the same instant, Schorl leaps out of your pocket. Together with the shackles you unleash, it blocks the first two waves of assault. Then, bullets shatter the windows from outside, and alarms blare.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: The combat unit will soon breach the area. Chief, prepare to engage the enemy.

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: Heh heh heh... Bound by your petty morals and blinded by ignorance... you think you can judge us? You dare challenge us? Then suffer the curse of death!

As expected, the Underground Puppets fall before you, just as they always do. Its frame crumbles apart, dissolving into pale smoke before fading into dust in the air. Only a faint trace of that drifting voice remains, circling like the final echoes of a curse.

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: Heh heh... Go on... Keep struggling... Open those unseeing eyes of yours and behold...

speaker: Drifting Voice
content: Death is the only truth visible even to fools...
Daniel cowers at your feet, pupils trembling, both hands clutching his head in a desperate grip.

speaker: Daniel
content: I knew it, I knew it... I've been cursed. I'm gonna die, hehehe, hahaha...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What curse? That's Mania, not witchcraft. Forget all that superstitious nonsense. Get over here.
You pull him away from the lingering contamination, then beckon Schorl over. You have it run a quick scan on Daniel.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: His M-value remains within a safe range. Mr. Horston is merely in shock. He has not been harmed. You did a great job protecting him, Chief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Good. We'll use this opportunity to officially declare him dead. Put out the word. The 9th Agency should be willing to place him under witness protection. He can lie low for a while.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And most importantly, run a full scan of the scene. Save all data of the traces.
It obediently turns back to get to work. You leave the scene to Schorl and send Daniel away. Then, you head to a quiet spot at the far end of the corridor and place a call.
[Scene Transition] Office

speaker: Max King
content: Did it work? Was I helpful?

speaker: Option
options: Of course, it's all thanks to you.

speaker: Max King
content: Haha, anyway, you did all the heavy lifting! I'm glad it worked! Once we've dealt with the real enemy, we'll throw a proper party in the council hall. When that day comes, just...

speaker: Max King
content: Do as you see fit. I'll back you up on this.
The two of you share a laugh. You'll remember how to terrorize idiots with this line in the future. Quote it out of context. Play dumb afterward. Leave no evidence behind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It certainly caused quite a stir. The Sillage Society even attempted to wipe us out. The lead behind this man is probably useless now. The enemy's very vigilant. They won't hesitate to sever any unwanted ties immediately.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For now, please keep an eye on the people around you. Make note of anyone who starts making moves. I'll look into their ties to the Ring Research Institute on my end.
King agrees without hesitation.

speaker: Max King
content: It's my honor to help you. Nonetheless...

Though the communication channel he's using is provided by Shattered Blade and specially encrypted to reduce the risk of interception, the Speaker still instinctively lowers his voice, carefully passing along the observations he's made within the council.

speaker: Max King
content: There have been plenty of accusations against Isomer recently, some even harsher than those directed at you. But when the claims were investigated, none of the accusers could provide solid evidence, and some even became evasive when questioned further.

speaker: Max King
content: The "suspicious projects" were investigated too, but she deflected every accusation, shifting the blame onto Former Director Professor Lambert, Nirvana, the Ring Research Institute, Paradeisos, the war, and even the accusers themselves.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I can imagine. The current Director doesn't seem to hide her ambition at all. She's probably made plenty of enemies. Yet she's held onto her position this whole time without anyone finding enough dirt to force her out. She must have other tricks up her sleeve.
You recall that moment...
[Flashback CG: Isomer's Scheme]

speaker: Isomer
content: You get your Black Ring, I get my seat. A perfect win-win. What do you say?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She prefers not to get her hands dirty herself. Instead, she identifies people's hidden desires and offers them a partnership, drawing them into her web in the process. Heh... If I'm being honest, I'd be embarrassed too if Lemma ever found out about the things I've been up to.

speaker: Max King
content: Now that's a real schemer. She's been playing this game for years, hasn't she? Despite all the enemies she's made and all the shady things she's done, she always manages to come out clean. She's clearly been ten steps ahead of everyone else the whole time, and she's meticulous about covering her tracks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Or she might be backed by someone powerful.
You rub your fingertips together, watching the residual purple smoke dust gradually fade, your thoughts drifting to its owner—your true enemy.
And the person on the other end of the line seems to read your mind.

speaker: Max King
content: Watch yourself, Chief. No matter how you look at it, she's way too ambitious. Someone like that is dangerous. Proceed cautiously.
You smile. Elvira said the same thing. You make a mental note of the sincere warnings from your two friends.

speaker: Option
options: "The rougher the sea, the higher the price of the fish."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And I've already secured the most important prize from this trip.
With that, you end the call with King and glance toward the other end of the corridor. Schorl has finished scanning and drifts leisurely back toward you.
Before it can finish its report, you are bombarded by notifications. You open them and find that they're from the technical experts up in the sky.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So eager, huh? Alright, here you go. Send the data, Schorl.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The contamination left clear residue at the scene, and it is directly related to the characteristics of Death's Mania and their core sorcery. Let's get this firsthand data to the technical experts. It should help refine their model and bring us closer to cracking the enemy's dimensional technology.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Understood. Transmission initiated. Progress: 13%, 18%, 23%...

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: I assumed you would return to the Observation Hub and deliver it to Lemma in person.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Analyzing my thought process again? Heh, well, you're right. I did want to do that. But right now, something more important requires my attention.
You look at the black bipyramid.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did the urgent meeting request I made two days ago get approved? ...You don't have anything else scheduled for him, right?
You pause to think, then add:

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I promise I won't lay a hand on him this time.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Of course. You've already proven yourself to be both rational and reliable. We trust you, and we depend on you. Everything we do is for the sake of the investigation into the Underground.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Progress: 100%. Data successfully transmitted to the Observation Hub. Your meeting request has also been approved. Shall we depart now?
[Scene Change]
You return once again to the 9th Agency's highest-security cell and see a familiar face.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Long time no see, Chief ${PlayerName}.
He watches you enter, a composed smile crossing his face.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Long time no see, Chief ${PlayerName}. You always look so grim when you visit me. Rough day at work again?

It's been months since you last saw him, and Adelaide is still wearing bandages. Whether that's because his weak body heals slowly, or because his sharp tongue has earned him another beating from someone else, you can't say.
Though you've heard both the 9th Agency and EDGE have been keeping him under the tightest security, holding him in an isolated cell for over half a year now.
Then again, maybe he's faking it. Or maybe that's just a Fraser thing. Maybe they enjoy being bound up like that over there.
In any case, you sit down across from him and cut straight to the point.
A perfectly measured look of surprise crosses Adelaide's face.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Then I'm very glad you made it back alive.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know you have deep ties with Sillage. Euphoria was an intelligence hub the two of you founded together. You had dealings at the Great Expo. And during the Ash Campaign, you helped funnel a significant portion of capital to Fraser.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's no point in dancing around this. Here's what I want to know: her detailed background, her abilities, her current location, and the sorcery she uses for shifting and hiding between dimensions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've been imprisoned here all this time, but the Underground has never sent any rescue. They've abandoned you. There's no need to remain loyal to them anymore.
He chuckles.

speaker: Adelaide
content: The Campbells are no longer useful to the Underground, just as Fraser is no longer useful to Sillage. I've served my purpose, Chief. If I were in their shoes, I wouldn't risk my neck trying to save a spent pawn either.
His usual spiel again. Despite his huge investment and precarious position, he still tries to sound indifferent, as if he hasn't staked his own life on this gamble.
You pause briefly, then continue.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I believe what you said, that you've achieved your goal. I imagine you're quite confident that the enterprise you've built is already on the right track.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You must have already placed it in the hands of the <color=#fb9259>right person</color>, haven't you? I may have a chance to invite her here. Your sister, Quinn's President, whose real name is <color=#fb9259>Eirene Campbell</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Or perhaps the one far away in Fraser...
Good. The look on his face right now pleases you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hella's quite fond of that young scholar, and DisCity is very interested in Aurum Secretum technology right now. Even with our strained relations with Fraser, I believe it's still possible to invite her to DisCity under the premise of academic exchange.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oh, I forgot to ask. Which sister would you prefer to see, Mr. Adelaide Campbell?
Adelaide looks at you. For the first time, those heterochromatic eyes lose their composure as he stares directly at you.
Before you can decipher the meaning behind that look, he averts his gaze and lets out a sigh.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You've picked up some terrible habits lately. You're becoming quite difficult to deal with.

options: I'll keep learning from you in the future.

content: The jab earns you a faint smile from him. Now, the Sage of the Underground straightens up and speaks solemnly, his gaze fixed on you.

speaker: Adelaide
content: We are the ones who forged a direct pact with the lord of the Underground. Four people. Four flowers. I received her power and sowed her seeds in her stead, so that more worthy souls might be chosen. Since we preach the "gospel of Mania," we might as well call ourselves the <color=#fb9259>Sages</color>.

speaker: Adelaide
content: <color=#fb9259>Pestilence</color>, the plague, dwells in the city's shadows. This Sage seeks out companions through information networks and cognitive influence. She prefers to stay in the shadows, yet she is diligent and reliable in her work... until you "defeated" her. After she "disappeared," DisCity's dark web dissolved along with her.

speaker: Adelaide
content: <color=#fb9259>Famine</color> embodies the despair of deprivation. Those with nothing left can only turn their gaze toward the very calamity destroying them, borrowing the power of Ash Crystals in exchange for the faintest glimmer of hope. Even among the Sages, this one is the weakest.

speaker: Adelaide
content: I'm not a Sinner. I can only control a few <color=#fb9259>borrowed</color> Apostles, nothing more.

speaker: Adelaide
content: To the Sage of <color=#fb9259>War</color>, Rancor is the ultimate weapon painstakingly forged by the Underground, yet it was taken by your people so early on. At this point, I'm afraid I know far less about it than that general behind you.

speaker: Adelaide
content: As for the sage of <color=#fb9259>Death</color>...
His eyes darken for a moment.

speaker: Adelaide
content: ..She embodies both death and life itself. Be careful, Chief.

speaker: Adelaide
content: That Sage isn't dangerous because of who she is. Far too many desire her. Her influence has seeped into the world for far too long. You want to take on the abyss, yet you know nothing about it.
...She's death, but also life itself?
[Flashback N9CG back turned] 0.5s

The question rises to your lips, but never leaves them. An inexplicable premonition settles over you, as though you're no longer in the safety of a prison cell under your control, but have been dragged into his domain instead.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You said the Undergrounders never tried to rescue me. That they've abandoned me... No. I'm the one who told my friends not to make any rash moves.

speaker: Adelaide
content: It took quite a bit of effort to convince them. I told them not to worry, that DisCity wouldn't kill me. EDGE understands that only by keeping me alive and in captivity can Famine's mark remain in "human" hands. But if I were to die...

He raises his left hand. His face gradually blurs, yet the twisted mark on the side of his palm grows ever clearer—sharp, ominous, shaped like a flower. And with it comes a strange yet familiar feeling.
You think of that woman. Is it her? Wait... It's not that simple.

You feel a resonance of the shackles deep within your soul. Adelaide's voice sounds distant, yet also seems to echo directly within you through some unknown medium. The mark on his hand looks strikingly familiar.

speaker: Adelaide
content: This power would immediately return to its true owner, then be granted to the next candidate. A new Sage of Famine would be born, becoming a threat to DisCity all over again. And unlike what happened with the Sage of War, you could no longer steal <color=#fb9259>her</color> power.
Adelaide looks at you for a long moment. Then, he smiles.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You see? Even after meeting your enemy, you still know nothing about her.
The flower dims and fades. He lowers his hand. In an instant, all senses return to normal. Before you sits the same bandaged prisoner, slumped weakly in the familiar, secure confines of the cell.

speaker: Adelaide
content: I shouldn't say any more. For one thing, my own understanding is limited. And for another, they did help make my wish come true. In any case, they're "friends" I should cherish and be grateful for. As for you...
He looks at you, still smiling, but there's an unsettling earnestness in the smile.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Your "enemy" isn't responsible for every evil in this world, ${PlayerName}. The spread of Mania isn't the result of some kind of conspiracy. It's the echo of our times, what the people want... It was always inevitable.

speaker: Adelaide
content: All these disasters and tragedies, all this ugliness and absurdity, they were bound to happen, with or without us. The Underground simply glimpsed the inevitable future early on, and resolved to embrace that fate. That's all... They're more determined than anyone else.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Perhaps one day, when your path finally becomes clear to you... you'll become one of them. You'll come to see that enmity was never the only possibility.
He's still smiling. The faint sincerity dissipates entirely, and Adelaide deftly sidesteps your question.

speaker: Adelaide
content: One last piece of advice: Don't focus only on external threats. You may be surprised to discover that the real danger facing BR-003 and those scientist friends of yours is actually lurking within your own walls.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Advice? Or misdirection? I'm not going to believe everything you say.
He doesn't seem bothered by your response.

speaker: Adelaide
content: My sister has come so far. She must have received help from many along the way. I can't thank all of them individually, so I'll take this opportunity to thank you in particular. Besides, sharing this information with you hardly changes anything in the grand scheme of things.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Time is running short, Chief. I hope you and your allies are prepared for what's coming.
Then the man falls silent, and you know the interrogation is over. The realization astonishes you. It's as if you began to understand him at some point. As if he no longer feels like an enemy.

...Was it the flower? From the moment he revealed it, a dangerous sense of familiarity began creeping through your nerves—like a warm greeting, or an ominous warning: Something is drawing closer and closer to you.
Don't let it come closer.
You stand up abruptly, grab your coat, and head for the door.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...If I need to, I'll be back.
[Black screen] Door closing sound, 1s
The meeting doesn't sway you from your original plan. Using BR-003 as bait to lure out the Underground proves successful, and the Observation Hub soon welcomes its "honored guests" once more.

speaker: Evelleon
content: If this is what he wants...
female_content: If this is what she wants...

content: The defense is a complete success.

You don't even need to be there in person. With the strategy you planned in advance and the operatives you deployed, the Observation Hub is able to target the invaded fissure ahead of time and crush the Puppets, eliminating the threats while collecting a fresh batch of real-time data.
You even have the luxury of catching your breath back at the Bureau, away from the battlefield. Despite how smoothly everything has gone lately, an inexplicable weariness has settled over you.

PixelBackup37:

Then there's Osborn from the Ring Research Institute. And Ron. Which one of them isn't guilty of gross negligence? They're practically begging to be prosecuted!

PixelBackup37:
