[Bureau]

Nightingale leads reinforcements to Eastside while other Sinners remain at the Bureau. The television is broadcasting news about countless disappearances and the abrupt paralysis of the Gray Mirror app.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief...
[Rooftop]

The shackles are straining to break through the contamination, but they can't harm Bianca at all. She didn't lie about one thing. She is indeed just an ordinary person. Her disaster-causing ability does not belong to a Sinner.
Amid the turbulent Mania, a normal person without any special power is just a twig that will snap in an instant. Bianca's sanity is gradually being shattered, overtaken by the power she so desires.
Yet she's smiling so brightly, opening her arms to joyfully embrace the Mania. It's as if what's rushing toward her isn't a maniacal monster, but the justice she's long awaited.

speaker: Bianca
content: Hahahah! How many people do you think Gray Mirror will backfire on? A hundred? A thousand? An entire district! So many have voted for you. Surely they won't disappoint me!

speaker: Bianca
content: It's all thanks to you that Gray Mirror has become the hottest topic in town! Look...
[Go insane CG]

speaker: Bianca
content: How massive it's gotten!

speaker: Chaotic Voices
content: Malice... Malice! Feed me more malice!

Contamination has ripped open a gaping rift between virtuality and reality, obscuring the sun and reigning supreme over all, as digitalized Corruptors descend one after another. Amid the chaos, the flow of people in the streets continues as usual, as if completely blind to the terrible disaster.

...No. It's not invisible to all ordinary people, but non-Gray Mirror users. You hear screams everywhere. People are shrieking and fleeing, bodies being gnawed by digitalized contamination and voices severely interfered, finally twisting and shattering under the astonished gazes of the crowd.

speaker: Bianca
content: It's the final episode of the anime! The last boss is coming...

speaker: Bianca
content: Great, here comes the ceremony where I'm to declare the victory of justice! I'm the master of Gray Mirror. I permit it!

The virtual contamination finally condenses into a huge grinning mask. Its hunger makes you tremble. This monster craves malice, and its first meal will be its summoner. It opens its maw and rushes toward Bianca...
You block the monster's first attack, raising your hand to unleash the shackles and repel the giant mask with all your strength. It doesn't buy you much time and anger has taken over you.

speaker: Chief
content: Done with your monologue? This isn't a power you can wield. Do you have a death wish?! Are you proclaiming your so-called justice with these monsters? What kind of justice is that?
The response is a long, deranged laugh. Bianca shakes uncontrollably as she cackles. Her body is gradually being segmented by digitalized grids, the last bit of rationality faded from her eyes.

speaker: Bianca
content: Yes, I have no right, and neither do they... Our hands are all dirty. How can we partake in such an important ceremony?

speaker: Bianca
content: Only you have the right to vote! Come on, Ashy, cast your vote of justice!
Suddenly, she grabs your collar and faces you. The malicious mask is no longer approaching, yet you glimpse the same madness on the girl's face.
...No, it's a trap. Mania has seized you. She leans closer eagerly, in delirium, her every word shakes your nerves.

speaker: Bianca
content: Everyone who's participated in the vote has committed cyber violence. Can we still call them good people? No, we both know how bad they are.

speaker: Bianca
content: So, just tap on here, and everyone who's voted for you before will disappear! Isn't it simple?
The same voice, warm with enthusiasm, has slowed down to gently tempt you into making a choice, but where your palm touches her skin, you feel an abnormal chill.
Distant screams remind you that the disaster is still ongoing, and you must break free from Bianca and subdue this master of Gray Mirror who calls you a partner.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you the Bianca I know, or a puppet controlled by another puppet? Do you really wish to be like the very Gray Mirror fanatics you despise in the guise of justice?

speaker: Chief
content: You hate them for erasing others based on their narrow standards, but what about you? Aren't you also judging the Gray Mirror users by your standards and lynching them in the name of justice? How are you different from those you despise?

speaker: Chief
content: As long as it eliminates your perceived evil, you don't care even if you turn into a monster yourself? What does that make you? Do you call this duplicitous, pathetic thing your justice?

The shackles slash through her body. A fierce reaction occurs between the red light and the contamination, making Bianca moan in pain. You struggle to get up and take a step back to keep your distance from her.

She doesn't follow you. Her unenhanced body has reached its limit. Bruises are spreading and burning every inch of her skin, climbing up her smiling face, yet her gradually weakening laughter tightens your heart more and more.

speaker: Bianca
content: ...Haha, you're right! I use the forbidden Mania in my self-indulgent investigations and executions. No matter how I glorify it, I must have hurt some innocent people. I'm a bad guy too, even worse than them!

speaker: Bianca
content: But I can't let those guys off, no matter what. I'm sick of seeing them escape punishment all the time. This world should be more black and white, and no one should be able to hide from their crimes. The bad guys must be accountable for their bad deeds.

speaker: Cabernet
content: This is the real reason I invited you here, my partner in justice!

She staggers to her feet. Contamination carries her body toward you and Mania stretches her right arm out to you. You instinctively raise your hand to release the shackles, but suddenly... your hand is gently grasped.
Bianca holds your hand tremulously, letting the red light pierce through her own palm. The distant Mania mask roars furiously, but the journalist ignores it.
You look up to meet her gentle, mischievous eyes filled with smile.
You...

speaker: Bianca
content: I'm so glad I met you, Ashy. Thank you for always steering clear of evil. Thank you for sweeping away all my confusion.

speaker: Bianca
content: Once I have destroyed those bad guys, could you finish me off, for I have turned into a villain too?

speaker: Bianca
content: Bad deeds should be punished. Someone in this world can still judge me. This is a world of justice. This is my dream...

The red light has dissolved some kind of invisible boundary. The distant clamor of the chaotic Purge has faded. The cocoon of Mania contamination around her gradually breaks down and fuses with your consciousness through the shackles. This time, it doesn't bring you pain, but... a deeper and more obscure emotion.
In a daze, you hear someone running endlessly and questioning indignantly. Anger, sadness, confusion, guilt, total incomprehension, and powerlessness. Everything washes over you before vanishing.

You regain consciousness and find Bianca gently resting her forehead on your shoulder, all the agony and grievance peeled off her mask. She smiles in such contentment and relief, still that cheerful, enthusiastic apple-cheeked girl who keeps running and never looks back.

speaker: Chief
content: I won't cast this vote. I won't judge Gray Mirror, and I won't judge you. I'm no different than you and them. None of us have the right to judge or sentence anyone.

speaker: Chief
content: I will stop you on my own terms. I've promised you to end Mania here. I won't let it hurt anyone else, nor will I let it hurt you.

speaker: Chief
content: But Bianca, I'm not doing all this for that broken dream of yours... I'm only following my own belief.

speaker: Bianca
content: Haha, of course, you're right. Keep going and never give up. Because... I'm just as stubborn.

The massive mask is impaled and split by the shackles, but new malice keeps pouring in, causing it to reassemble and expand again. If this continues, the connected Gray Mirror Space, its users, the Fifth Avenue, and even the entire Eastside will be overrun by this digitalized Mania. This will not end if the core of the monster is not crushed.
Where could the core be... You look at Bianca, who is leaning on your shoulder, weak and unconscious.

speaker: Bianca
content: Once I have destroyed those bad guys, could you finish me off, for I have turned into a villain too?

speaker: Bianca
content: Bad deeds should be punished. Someone in this world can still judge me. This is a world of justice. This is my dream...
[Exit flashback]

speaker: Chief
content: I know you've decided to give up everything for this power. But if Mania hasn't devoured you completely, if you're still holding onto that initial dream of yours, even just a little...

speaker: Chief
content: Help me find the core.
The mask takes shape again, and a hurricane of Mania mixed with ruthless malice envelops the two of you, yet you stand unyielding, spikes of red light reaching into this broken puppet...
[Shackles][Blank Screen]

speaker: Childish Cries
content: *Cries sadly.
You hear a child's piercing cries from the depths of your consciousness.
You follow the cries through the white void and finally find their source.
[Little Bianca]

speaker: Girl
content: No... Sob... It's not fair... You're wrong, Miss!
She keeps crying and seems to get even angrier at her own words. The way she punches and kicks the air reminds you of someone.

speaker: Chief
content: Hey, stop crying. Here, I've got a treat for you.

speaker: Girl
content: What treat?
The girl calms down as quickly as she acts up. Her tears immediately stop.

speaker: Chief
content: An apple candy. Do you like it?

speaker: Girl
content: Wow! How did you know I like apples? My nickname is Apple. My parents say my head is big and my face is round and red, like an apple. But apples are too big for me to hold, so Mom makes apple purée for me! Have you tried it? It's warm and tasty!
And once she starts talking, she never stops, just like that person you know.

speaker: Chief
content: Tell me why you were crying and I'll give you an apple candy, okay?

speaker: Girl
content: Sure! It's because a classmate was bullied just now!

speaker: Girl
content: The kids from the Star Class were bullying a girl in overalls. Everyone was pulling at her straps, so she fell over! She fell so hard!

speaker: Girl
content: Yes! But I'm from the Moon Class, and I don't know the kids from the Star Class, so I couldn't tell who was bullying her. I could only show the teacher. But they all said I was lying! Their teacher didn't believe me either, because I'm from the Moon Class! That made Apple so angry!

speaker: Chief
content: What about the bullied child? Didn't she speak up for you?

speaker: Girl
content: She asked me not to tell the teacher. She said she was scared. Even if the teacher helped her this time, they would bully her again next time. She said I'm from the Moon Class, so I don't have to worry about that, but not her...

speaker: Girl
content: And then, and then, you saw me... Apple cried a lot! Apple was so embarrassed!...

options: That's not embarrassing. I didn't hear anything.
That's not true. Apple is the bravest.

speaker: Chief
content: I saw the brave Apple standing up for the weak and feeling upset about an unfair judgment.

speaker: Girl
content: Really...? Then, will the brave Apple win? Will those bad kids be punished?

options: Of course. Your voice will be heard.

speaker: Girl
content: Really?

speaker: Bianca
content: What if it's not the kids from the Star Class, but even more unknown and unidentifiable culprits?
You watch the girl grow up, pick up a camera, and get her press pass.

speaker: Bianca
content: I thought growing up meant gaining power, but turns out not every fairy tale has a happy ending...

speaker: Bianca
content: It turns out the world isn't as black and white as I saw it when I was little...

speaker: Bianca
content: In the face of an endless journey, what should one do?

speaker: Bianca
content: Bianca, quick, think of something. There are many more of these kids in overalls...
Bianca lowers her head, as if looking at her younger self, lost and confused.
This is the center of the Mania monster's power. You've found the core. This is the earliest malice that fed the monster... Bianca's malice. But it's also the root of her initial dream.

speaker: Chief
content: ...But you know that curbing violence with violence won't get you what you want. Even Gray Mirror can't bring you your ideal world.

speaker: Bianca
content: Any advice then, Ashy? What will you do if you know it may all be futile even if you persist?
She looks up like a child waiting for a lesson from a teacher, eagerly awaiting your response. You can think of many examples of futile persistence... It seems all you can offer her is silence.

speaker: Bianca
content: Haha, hahaha... You don't know either...

speaker: Bianca
content: You don't know what to do either, but since you're more powerful than me, I must yield. Is that it?

speaker: Chief
content: No, it's just that whatever I say seems useless. You've already yielded, but not to me.

speaker: Chief
content: When you chose to take over the Gray Mirror server to execute your justice, you had already lost.

speaker: Chief
content: The brave little Apple who spoke up for the innocent lost to the temptation of power. The girl who thought the world should be black and white chose to be tainted with darkness herself.

speaker: Chief
content: You want evil to be justly punished. The journey to this goal is indeed long and tough, and the end might not be in sight for a long time. But the journalist named Bianca has already given up midway.

She stares at you blankly as the luminous spikes from the shackles firmly pierce through this embodiment of her obsession. Cracks appear on her body. Soon you hear the sharp noise of something breaking, and the vision before you shatters into fragments. You return to reality.
[Rooftop]

You've broken the core, and the colossal mask in the sky disintegrates into scattered green characters, rapidly vanishing. Bianca has woken up, her figure overlapping with that lonely, confused girl back in the consciousness.

speaker: Bianca
content: ...Hmph!

speaker: Bianca
content: I don't understand what you jibber jabbered about nor do I want to hear! I won't listen to you! That wasn't a fair fight!

options: Maybe next time I'll let you win.

speaker: Chief
content: When you become Eastside's top journalist. We can have another match.

speaker: Bianca
content: Sure, then when I become Eastside's top journalist, we'll drink apple juice together again! We'll drink till it gets dark!

speaker: Bianca
content: At the press award ceremony, you must sit closest to me and watch me receive my award!

speaker: Bianca
content: But... they won't give an award to a villain, will they?
She suddenly goes silent, smiling at you.

speaker: Bianca
content: I yield, Ashy. I won't play dirty.

speaker: Bianca
content: You're right, I was judging others by my own standards. I'm no different from those who voted. I made a mistake. I'll accept my punishment!
She stands with her arms akimbo, lifting her head proudly.

speaker: Chief
content: How will I punish you? I'm just a little "investigator".
She doesn't answer or expose your obvious lie, simply pulling out a can of apple juice from her pocket.

speaker: Bianca
content: Here, take this. I promised you the prize.
You fumble to catch it, and when you look up again, Bianca is already running off into the distance without looking back.

speaker: Chief
content: Wait, that's...!
[Blank Screen]
I know!
That's where the loveliest, bravest little Bianca is!

"Dear teacher of the Star Class, this is Bianca from the Moon Class. I want to say sorry to the kids in the Star Class, so my mommy is helping me write this letter. Because you didn't punish the bullies in the Star Class, I put some sand from the garden in their lunch milk as punishment."
"Now that we're even, you can punish me! But I won't give up. If I see kids from the Star Class bully others again, I will still tell on them!"
I must pick up the microphone and camera. I must let everyone see this!
I will keep going…
Keep going forward!
The end must lie ahead!

[Black Screen]
...Clack.
From the depths of your consciousness, you hear the clicking of high heels on stone tiles.
...Click... clack...
The sound draws closer to you.
At last, I've found you, my love.
Is the voice speaking to you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I am...
You try to explain who you are, but the words catch in your throat, refusing to come out. You attempt to recall anything about yourself, but your mind is completely blank.
You are my destined other half. The one I've longed to meet in every dream and waking thought.
Our story is about to begin. My lifelong wish will finally be fulfilled.

Are you... really? The ethereal whispers drift around your ears, unfamiliar breath drawing near then fading away. A cold sensation grazes your fingertips, and your mind wavers, struggling to discern if it's real.
We will become lovers for all eternity, together in life and in death. We shall never be apart...
Never apart...
More and more voices close in on you, surrounding you from all sides. The mental contamination grows increasingly intense, suffocating you until you can barely breathe—
Never apart... Never apart!!!
You open your eyes. A dull pain throbs in your forehead, and your mind feels foggy—as if you've been struck with a blunt object. The persistent, heavy ache makes it difficult to think clearly.
Thunk! Your forehead hits straight into a wooden board. Your already muddled head now feels even worse.

You feel the cold wooden boards with your fingertips. The space around you is so narrow you can barely move. The air is stale, carrying the smell of damp, rotting wood. Strangely, this cramped space feels oddly familiar to you, as if you somehow know how to get out—

Holding your breath, you push against the wooden boards with all your strength. There's a "click" as a latch somewhere gives way. The boards immediately loosen and swing outward. A sliver of light seeps in, and cold air rushes into your lungs. At last, you have enough space to sit up.
[Castle Great Hall]

In the suffocating silence and dimness, faint moonlight spills through fractured stained-glass windows. The beams weave through crumbling antique furniture, casting twisted shadows over a floor strewn with rubble and dust. You don't recognize this place.
Looking down at where you were just lying, you realize—this isn't some wooden box, but a <color=#fb9259>coffin</color>.
Your coffin sits at the center of this unfamiliar hall. In the dimness, you can barely make out a line of small text engraved on the casket.
To Graves's true love—bound by an eternal vow.

Where are you? Why are you here? Who is Graves, and what connection does she have to you? Your head feels foggy and heavy, as if weighed down by some invisible force. The world around you is blurry and unfamiliar. You strain to remember, but your memory yields nothing.

Yet there's something about you that suggests experience with unusual situations. Despite the memory loss and the confinement, you feel no panic. Your heartbeat and breathing remain even and steady. With surprising composure, you trace words in the dust with your finger, piecing together your thoughts and trying to make sense of it all.
Situation A: "Reborn as the Vampire Lord" Betrayed by villains and trapped here, I rise from my coffin reborn. This time I shall reclaim everything that is rightfully mine!

Situation B: "I Lost My Memories and Ended Up in a Strange Castle?!" A truck drove by, the world suddenly collapsed, and I was swept into a vortex of space and time by mysterious forces. Now I must fulfill my destiny as the hero who will save the world!
Situation C: ...
A flicker of another possibility stirs in your mind, but it remains hazy, refusing to take shape. You attempt to grasp these fragmented pieces, but they drift like fog, impossible to pin down.
You can only catch a few key fragments:
Ghost bride, wishes, wedding...

Judging by the moonlight's shift across the floor, you've been left stranded here for nearly an hour. You move slightly, trying not to look so much like a forgotten statue left to gather dust. Unfortunately, besides the occasional breeze that almost scatters your notes written in dust, nothing around you has changed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you can remember how to get out of a coffin, you can certainly find a way out of this castle.
You steel your resolve and turn your attention to the only source of information available—your place of rebirth.

Sometimes the most unlikely actions bring unexpected breakthroughs—perhaps you'll wake from a nap with your memory restored. Whatever the case, your "pre-death" self certainly was a person of action; you climb back into the coffin even before you've finished the thought.

This small rectangular box provides an unexpected sense of comfort and safety, as though you're being swaddled like a baby. But after fifteen minutes of lying there, sleep remains elusive, and your mind stays blank, offering no new insights.
The same familiar, homey feeling settles over you, yet you're surrounded by a suffocating silence. Your efforts remain fruitless.

The whispers from your dream, the inscription on the coffin, that haunting ghost story you can't forget... All these tangled thoughts scatter your attention, leaving you more wide awake the longer you lie there.
...Clack!

You've barely moved when that familiar yet unsettling sound reaches your ears, stopping you cold.
It's footsteps. Each step grinds against the dust, drawing nearer and nearer to where you are.

options: Lie down and pretend to sleep

content: Slowly and carefully, you lie back down, feigning sleep with your eyes half-closed, but the footsteps draw ever closer. Then, a cold breath brushes against your face—
You hold your breath, trying to pinpoint the sound's direction. When you turn around—
There's no one there. No footprints in the dust on the floor, not even a speck of disturbed dust floating in the air. You're certain you didn't imagine those sounds...
Awake so soon? Forgive my absence... my love.
The prickle of hostile intent triggers your combat instincts. Without hesitation, you lift both your hands, aiming them at the air—

Release what exactly? You have a nagging feeling that something red and sharp should emerge from your palms, but nothing happens. As you stand there, hands outstretched, the cold, unfamiliar presence creeps closer, crawling up your spine and lingering at the nape of your neck.
Are you trying to play hide and seek with me? Well, I've caught you.
[First Encounter Small CG][Entrance BGM]
I've won. As my reward... please forgive me for leaving your side.
The presence draws closer to you, yet maintains a delicate distance as if afraid you might break. A pair of bloodless hands gently encircle you, cradling you protectively in their embrace.

You must have been anxious when you opened your eyes and I wasn't there. I'm sorry—I was just taking some time to prepare myself. It's such an important day, and I wanted to look my absolute best for you.
Now that you're awake, let's begin our ceremony right away. I've been waiting for this day for so long... Finally, I have a wedding of my own.
She greedily breathes in your scent at the nape of your neck. Her ice-cold fingertips trail from your neck to your shoulders, down your arms... and farther along your body.
Finally, as her hands wander to more intimate parts of your body, you can't help but break your silence.

options: I don't think that's appropriate, miss.

content: [Portrait violently shakes]
You... you don't recognize me?!
I thought our fated connection would make you instantly recognize the tight bond between us!

You understand every word she speaks, but the sentence they form leaves you completely baffled. The woman in the white wedding gown cups your face in her hands, then sighs with a mix of indulgence and resignation.

That's all right. I can wait as long as it takes... until our hair turns silver, until the roses wither, and the moonlight fades. I'll wait until you can accept what's in front of you—accept that we're destined to be together.
After all, I'm Graves, <color=#fb9259>your beloved</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Beloved?
Is she the one who called you her true love in that coffin inscription? You frown, taking a cautious step back, but the self-proclaimed bride firmly grabs hold of you.

speaker: Graves
content: Of course, I wouldn't mind if you called me "darling" instead—after all, we'll be wedded soon enough. You could also call me dear, honey, sweetheart... whatever you prefer, really.

speaker: Graves
content: Or perhaps you'd prefer something more... thrilling? Something special? In that case, you could call me mommy, kitten, your good girl, or even your loyal little slave...
Graves doesn't seem to realize there was anything improper about what she said, gazing at you with an expression of pure innocence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I think I'll just call you by your name. Graves, you may find this hard to believe, but I don't remember anything, including you. Are we really in a relationship?

You feel a twinge of guilt, worried you might be some soap opera villain who abandoned their lover after a car accident or terminal illness. Luckily, Graves doesn't seem particularly disappointed by your cold demeanor.

speaker: Graves
content: Graves... I love the way my name sounds when you say it. What do you want to know? If you're asking about me... just know this: everything I have, everything I am, is yours.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Have I done anything to you?

speaker: Graves
content: Well, no—I mean, not yet. After all, we're destined lovers. I've fantasized countless times about our meeting, about giving myself completely to you. Now that you're awake, why don't we...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Perhaps, before we get to that, could you tell me what this place is? It looks like some movie set. Why am I here? How did I get here? Who are you, exactly? And what has happened between us?
Graves seems momentarily stunned by your rapid-fire questions, her surprise written all over her face.

speaker: Graves
content: Oh, that's what my dear wants to know! You could have said so earlier.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: (I haven't exactly had the chance...)

speaker: Graves
content: A proper lover should satisfy their partner's every curiosity. Why don't you rest a little, and let me tell you everything... in detail?

speaker: Graves
content: About... our story.
(Scene change)

A swarm of spiders drags out an ancient, dust-covered sofa from somewhere. You're painfully aware of what lies beneath the fabric—clusters of insect eggs cradled in the worn cotton—but Graves's enthusiastic urging leaves you with little choice but to sit.

Next, a pair of faded, cracked porcelain cups appears before you. Graves picks up the matching teapot with grace and starts pouring. Though not a drop of liquid flows from the spout, she ceremoniously hands you the empty cup as if completing a proper tea service.

speaker: Graves
content: Morveth Castle has been abandoned for so many years. I'm afraid I don't have any proper pastries to offer you. Please, do enjoy this tea.
Morveth Castle... why does that name ring a bell? And this peculiar "tea" before you... something about all of this feels oddly familiar.

speaker: Graves
content: What's wrong, dear? Why are your hands trembling? I'm afraid my brewing skills don't match Sister Elsie's. Does it not suit your taste?

You glance at the empty cup in your hands, containing nothing but cobwebs and dust, then look up at Graves's expectant gaze. Despite knowing better, you raise the cup to your lips and pretend to drink from it.

speaker: Graves
content: I'll brew tea for you every day from now on.
"That won't be necessary..." you think to yourself, but don't say it aloud.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'd like to know more about our love story. How did we meet? How did we fall in love? And why was I lying in a coffin?

speaker: Graves
content: It truly is a moving, everlasting love story.
You nod eagerly, realizing all the answers are right in front of you. You feel like you might start remembering something soon.

speaker: Graves
content: The story of our love began exactly one hour ago...
But... you've only been here for an hour. Still, Graves appears completely enraptured, so you just keep listening.

speaker: Graves
content: When the moon reached its zenith, I made a wish to the night sky, hoping I too would be granted a destined lover.
Perfect. You've now grasped the basic settings of her story.

speaker: Graves
content: Then I waited quietly beneath the moonlight...
Whoa, interesting story arc.

speaker: Graves
content: Then... you appeared in the coffin, and so we're lovers now. We're going to live happily ever after together, just like in a fairy tale.

speaker: Graves
content: I know, you haven't heard enough, have you? What a touching story! It feels almost unreal, like a hazy, beautiful dream. I truly hope we never ever have to wake up from it.
Her eyes well up with tears. Seeming to realize she's too caught up in her own thoughts, she quickly wipes the corner of her eyes and pours you another cup of "tea."

speaker: Graves
content: Hmm? What's wrong, darling? Why aren't you saying anything? Did I not explain myself clearly?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you saying... we've only just met?

speaker: Graves
content: That's right.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We just fell in love?

speaker: Graves
content: Yes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...This so-called love story is actually just beginning.
She smiles with satisfaction while you remain stiffly silent. Unable to fully process her disturbing concept of love, you steel yourself to continue your questioning.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, what kind of person was I before we met?

speaker: Graves
content: Whatever works for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What do you mean by "whatever works"?

speaker: Graves
content: No matter what form my love takes, I would gladly embrace you. Whether you're alive or dead, a creature or even an object—as long as you're the one destined to fulfill my dream, I'll take the vow without hesitation. So none of that really matters.

speaker: Graves
content: Even if you'd never awakened in that coffin, it wouldn't have mattered. I had it all planned. I would've spent my life caring for you—watching over that little coffin forever. Every day, I would apply makeup to keep you looking healthy and clean your body with warm water.

speaker: Graves
content: I would have watched over you every day, keeping all those spiders and insects away from your corpse...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cor...

You're certain you're alive and well right now, but hearing her say that word still sends chills down your spine. You can't imagine what fate would have awaited you if you hadn't managed to climb out of that coffin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Um, may I ask one last question?
Your voice is measured, your tone laced with your hidden intention to bolt the moment you get your answer.

options: What will be the ending of this story?

speaker: Graves
content: Ending? Could there be any better ending than a perfect wedding?
Marriage? Bride? Wedding? Morveth Castle—these words explode in your mind one after another, triggering fragments of memory:
[Flashback][Bureau][Silhouette]
A Ghost Bride... bound...intruder...marriage pact...
Shrouded her chosen in cobwebs... consume concoctions of insect bones...
Formidable curse... destined love...
[Exit flashback]

You don't recognize the voice, but you're certain it's telling the very story that's unfolding before you. That fleeting thought you couldn't quite hold onto while writing on the dusty floor is now taking shape.
Situation C: The Ghost Bride Who Wouldn't Take No for an Answer...

speaker: Graves
content: Darling, you're full of questions! You must be as excited as I am! Are you just as eager to see us standing together in a sea of flowers, surrounded by guests showering us with blessings?

She doesn't give you time to refuse—THUMP! THUMP! THUMP!
A sudden sound reverberates throughout the hall. Not drums, but footsteps—orderly, steady, countless feet striking the floor in unison with a cold, mechanical rhythm.
Your eyes shoot up, scanning the dome, and it hits you—the sound isn't far away at all. It's coming from directly above, from the floor above this marble surface where you stand.

A chill runs down your spine as you see... shadows. Countless shadows cast down from the sealed-off second floor, blocking the faint moonlight. Grotesque silhouettes—claws, armor, and inhuman limbs—layered upon one another, engulfing the entire staircase.

speaker: Graves
content: They're my friends. Are you ready? The wedding is about to begin.

First, your modern uniform clashes starkly with Graves's ornate, classical wedding dress, which makes her look like she's walked out of an oil painting. You two couldn't look more mismatched. This whole "destined lover" idea is almost certainly her one-sided fantasy.

Then, there's Graves herself—her obsession with marrying you is far from normal, and her behavior is wildly unpredictable. If you are truly experiencing the ghost story you just remembered, defying her would not be wise.

Finally, you're alone, unarmed, and have no memory of who you are. Worse yet, you're surrounded by numerous supernatural beings in this castle. It's clear that there's no way to fight back, and escape is impossible.
Though your memories are foggy, your mind remains sharp. Under the watchful eyes of these "friends," you quickly come to understand your predicament.

speaker: Graves
content: Have you decided? Just nod, and we'll begin the ceremony right away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What if I don't nod?

speaker: Graves
content: Then I'll wait until you agree. We have all the time in the world.
She leans against your coffin, her fingers trailing softly along its edge, her expression betraying an unsettling blend of obsession and longing.

If she doesn't care whether her marriage partner is alive or dead, she certainly won't be bothered by a little resistance. Graves has all the time in the world, but you can't afford to wait her out forever.
If the mere mention of the key elements in this ghost story was enough to awaken fragments of your memories, then immersing yourself in the story should trigger an even stronger response.
You look up and meet your bride's gaze.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: (If this is my only option to break this stalemate...)

speaker: Graves
content: Dear guests, thank you for coming.
Graves speaks in a soft, clear voice as she lifts the hem of her dress slightly and performs an elegant curtsy to the bizarre assortment of guests.

speaker: Graves
content: We have received your blessings and you have our most heartfelt gratitude.
You bow too, though not by choice. You glance down at your limbs tightly bound with spider silk... Graves even had the spiders tie it into decorative bows.

speaker: Graves
content: Now, let us welcome our honored officiant to deliver the address!
Delighted and excited, she first arranges a circle of strange bones on the dilapidated table, then produces a small human bust from seemingly nowhere.

The bust is severely damaged, with only half of its head remaining, though traces of its once-elegant features are still visible. Graves places it solemnly at the center of the bone circle, a look of devout reverence spreading across her face.
Clearly, this is the "honored officiant."
The hall falls into silence, with only the occasional rustle of moving spiders echoing through the empty space. Graves smiles at the bust, nodding now and then, as if listening intently.
The scene before you is so unnervingly bizarre it makes your skin crawl. You can't help but wonder if she's engaged in a conversation meant for her ears alone.
After what feels like an eternity, Graves finally turns around to you again.

speaker: Graves
content: Make your vow now, my love. The officiant is waiting.

speaker: Graves
content: It asks if you're willing to take Graves as your partner, for better, for worse, for richer, for poorer, in sickness and in health, in joy and in sadness, to support and cherish her... Do you accept?
The bride's burning gaze fixes on you, as focused and intense as a stage spotlight. Beneath the steps, countless eyes—and grotesque things that only vaguely resemble eyes—lock onto you all at once.

speaker: Graves
content: Say it now. Say you'll spend the rest of your life with me, until the end of time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I vow...
A Ghost Bride... bound...intruder...marriage pact...
You begin slowly, trying to make your voice sound calm and solemn. As the words leave your lips, familiar yet chilling memories resurface, flashing through your mind.

options: I vow to take Graves to be my partner.

content: Shrouded her chosen in cobwebs... consume concoctions of insect bones...

speaker: Letta
content: I will spend the rest of my life with you...
Transformed into armored statues, forever cursed to adorn the castle's halls....

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...through every trial, every joy, until the end of time.
Those who dare defy her... The bride... deep-seated resentment...

speaker: Graves
content: I accept your vow.

More and more details of the story begin to emerge. Graves, the protagonist of this tale, gazes at you with tender affection, tears glistening in her eyes. She gently cradles your hand and slowly presses it against her chest, the tender gesture carrying an indescribable sense of devotion.

speaker: Graves
content: I, as your wife, shall respect and cherish you. I will spend the rest of my life with you, until the end of time.

speaker: Graves
content: From this day forward, we shall never be apart.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Never apart.
In harmony with her voice, the spiders below begin to chant softly, as if performing an eerie ritual. Thick white mist gradually rises from the floor of the hall, blurring the surroundings.

speaker: Graves
content: Now, let's put on the token of our love.
Graves leans in closer, gently taking out a ring. At the same time, countless spiders surge from all directions like a relentless tide.
Spider silk wraps tightly around your limbs, hoisting your left hand like that of a lifeless marionette. Each strand seems to dig into your resolve, forcing you stiffly toward the ring.
Instead of a gem, an eyeball rests at the center of the ring. Its pitch-black pupil stares fixedly at you, compelling you to hold its gaze.
Formidable curse... destined love...
Never... to be pa—rted...

Around you, the monsters move in perfect unison, their footfalls heavy and synchronized, creating a rhythm that celebrates your union. Yet this "celebration" lacks any warmth, only intensifying the oppressive atmosphere hanging in the air.

speaker: Monsters
content: Congratulations! Congratulations!

The monsters growl in unison, their sounds intertwining with that piercing wail from your dream, making your eardrums throb with pain. Yet amid this intense agony, your palm begins to warm slightly, as if some unseen power within you is resisting instinctively.

speaker: Monsters
content: Never apart! Never apart!
[Shackles Effect]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is—
[Bureau]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hecate?

Bureau
Recreation Room
Two hours ago

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Long, long ago, in the far reach of the satellite towns, lay the mysterious Morveth Castle.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: It is, in whispered tales, believed to be haunted by a bride—a Ghost Bride who bound any intruder with a marriage pact.

speaker: Hecate
content: What is a marriage pact?

speaker: Labyrinth
content: An extremely perilous hominid relationship, as speculated. The Ghost Bride shrouded her chosen in cobwebs, compelling them to consume concoctions of insect bones. Those who dare defy her were all transformed into armored statues, forever cursed to adorn the castle's halls.

speaker: EMP
content: I thought this was supposed to be bedtime story sharing, not horror stories!

speaker: Hecate
content: This story came from a picture book that suddenly appeared in the Bureau, right? Where is it now?

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Already handed over to Master.
[End of Flashback]

You stare at the red thorns in your hand, tearing through the air with their twisted, bramble-like shape, glowing with a light that brings you comfort. A flood of information surges into your mind as forgotten memories and senses reawaken. You remember now. This is your—
You are not Graves's so-called "true love," nor are you some reborn hero from another world seeking revenge. You remember now—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So this ghost story actually originated from the Bureau itself? And what's this <color=#fb9259>picture book</color> they mentioned...?
The shackles haven't fully restored your memories. Instead, they've reawakened your ability to sense the Mania around you, intensifying your headache and worsening your dizziness.

speaker: Graves
content: What's wrong? Why would you hurt me? Why... would you ruin our wedding?

You force yourself to look up despite your discomfort. The bride stands helplessly amid the red light. The instinctive reactions from your shackles were too intense, leaving her with minor injuries. Still holding the ring, her hands now bear scratches from your shackles.
Though you still don't understand how you ended up here, you recognize that this bride is also a victim of her own misguided affections. You withdraw the shackles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm sorry, but I'm not the one you're supposed to marry...

speaker: Graves
content: You must be getting impatient, aren't you? Don't worry, once we put the ring on, it will all be over soon.
Graves ignores your explanation, forcing a smile as she extends the ring toward you once more.
Your honest reaction feels cruel in the face of the scene before you.
The exquisite decorations are shattered by your shackles, fragments scattered across the floor. The bride stands amid this chaos, slightly wounded yet smiling as she awaits your answer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have no idea how I ended up here by accident. I've wasted your time and somehow made those promises with you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm truly sorry for ruining your wedding. I sincerely hope you'll soon find the person who's truly meant for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I'm not the "true love" you've been looking for.
You made yourself perfectly clear. Yet Graves refuses to let go, gripping your wrist tightly.

speaker: Graves
content: Why? I worked so hard. I tried to make myself beautiful. I tried to become worthy of this lovely dress. I've found so many friends to attend our wedding... Everything I have, everything I am, belongs to you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That belongs to you.
Her grip on your wrist suddenly tightens. She looks up at you as though she's just heard something she cannot understand. Tears begin to fall, one by one, onto the burn scars left by shackles.

speaker: Graves
content: No... No... I wasn't wrong. I'm so close. After waiting so long for someone to stand by me, after all the struggle to finally make my dream wedding happen... I'm this close...

speaker: Graves?
content: He doesn't like us? Then what's his type? We can become whatever he wants!
female_content: She doesn't like us? Then what's her type? We can become whatever she wants!

content: Her breathing quickens as your shackles pick up an unsettling pulse. Strange shadows flicker across Graves's body, and unstable Mania begins to surge in the air.

speaker: Graves?
content: I'm not good enough. There must be something. Think! Is my hair a mess? Did I wear my veil wrong? Am I too thin? And that most important thing... he can't find out...
female_content: I'm not good enough. There must be something. Think! Is my hair a mess? Did I wear my veil wrong? Am I too thin? And that most important thing... she can't find out...

speaker: Graves?
content: If he finds out, he will hate me, abandon me!
female_content: If she finds out, she will hate me, abandon me!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Graves?
She suddenly jerks away from you, as if shocked by electricity, her body trembling as she wraps her arms tightly around herself.

speaker: Graves
content: All we want is just a wedding. If even that is too much to ask, it must be because we're too terrible!
[Red flash] [Lights out]

A violent wind suddenly erupts, sweeping through the entire hall as the bride before you vanishes into thin air. A moment later, all the lights go off simultaneously, plunging everything around you once more into impenetrable darkness.

Your instincts flare, the shackles tightening in your palm as you prepare for combat.
Yet as seconds tick by... silence envelops you. The danger you anticipated fails to materialize.
The violent wind gradually subsides and the swirling dust begins to settle. In the moonlight not far from you, you see the silhouette of a twisted, monstrous figure that wasn't there before.
She raises her deformed hand, frantically trying to hide her face. The figure in the darkness cowers and trembles uncontrollably.

speaker: Graves
content: Don't... don't come near me.
She's a Sinner. And worse... a Sinner on the verge of becoming a Corruptor.

speaker: Graves
content: I've turned into this hideous thing again... No wonder everyone hates me... Even my destined lover finds me repulsive...

speaker: Graves?
content: Careful, Graves! He's getting closer, he's going to see us like this, see how ugly we truly are! Then we'll never deserve happiness again!
female_content: Careful, Graves! She's getting closer, she's going to see us like this, see how ugly we truly are! Then we'll never deserve happiness again!

content: Moonlight pours through the high window, casting mottled patterns of light and shadow over the floor. For a moment, you think you see two figures, their shapes twisting and blending together in the dim glow. But when you try to focus, only a single monster remains, her body riddled with contamination.
Seeing you approach, she frantically raises her deformed hands, desperately trying to hide her face.

speaker: Graves
content: Stay back! Y-you've got the wrong person, I'm not Graves... I know nothing about this castle, true love, or any ring!
Her denial only makes her seem more suspicious.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then I'll go find the real Graves and ask her what all this is about.

speaker: Graves
content: No, you can't! Our wedding isn't over yet!

speaker: Graves
content: The ceremony isn't complete yet—you haven't even put on the ring... We haven't kissed, the guests haven't given their speeches. And there's still the cake, the champagne, the banquet, Mr. Crow's singing performance, and the spider couple's dance...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait... kiss?

speaker: Graves
content: No!

speaker: Graves
content: No!
You let out a soft laugh, finally feeling some of the tension release. Her perfect bride facade has vanished, revealing a glimpse of her childlike innocence.

This situation isn't so bad—it's even within your "comfort zone." The coffin reminds you of the Romanesque Hall, the decor echoes the style of Sloane Street, and the ghost story brings to mind the Buonanotte Factory. An unfamiliar, enclosed space thick with Mania, an unstable Sinner with inexplicable fixation...
It's practically tailor-made for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't worry, I won't come closer. Let's just talk, okay? Graves, you want to get married, to complete this ceremony, right?

speaker: Graves
content: Right... not just any wedding ceremony. I want the most perfect, most blissful one.

Graves remains huddled in the shadows, nervously tracing circles on the ground with her finger. Her joints are completely deformed, sharp black claws faintly visible. The moment she notices your gaze, she quickly withdraws her fingers, burying them in her palms.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why are you so obsessed with weddings?
Graves doesn't respond.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why are you so fixated on <color=#fb9259>me</color>?
The silence lingers. She yearns for a wedding yet refuses to confront the truth behind her obsession. Surely, there's more to your connection than just this hastily woven "love story."

But seeing how her body trembles uncontrollably, pushing her further could trigger another emotional breakdown and Mania outburst. Whether your goal is to gather more information, or to wait for MBCC's rescue at dawn when they notice something is off, escalating things now would only make it worse.
What's certain now is that this Sinner who claims to be your bride has shown no intention of harming you, even while on the brink of deterioration with an unstable mind. You soften your voice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I offer you something you can't refuse, would you tell me a few things? About how I ended up here, and why you chose me, of all people.
Graves shrinks back slightly, her posture alert and wary.

speaker: Graves
content: What offer?
[CG]

speaker: Graves
content: What did you say?

She lifts her head, emerging from the shadows. Under the moonlight, you finally see the full extent of the contamination covering her body. Her skin is mottled with discoloration, signs of decay corrupting this young body from the inside out.
But she seems to have forgotten all that now, her face showing both incredulous hope and tear tracks left behind from her earlier fear.

speaker: Graves
content: You truly mean it? Even without being bound by spider silk?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll cooperate and see the wedding ceremony through, just as you want.

speaker: Graves
content: You've seen what I look like—aren't you afraid of me? Aren't you afraid of being mocked for marrying a monster?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've seen far more terrifying monsters than you.

speaker: Graves
content: Then will you stand with me and accept the blessings from everyone in the castle? I even promised Dullahan he could give a speech on behalf of all the guests. Aren't you afraid of them?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't know who Dullahan is, but these guests are your friends, of course it's fine.

speaker: Graves
content: We'll pop the champagne and cut the cake together!
[End CG]

You respond to each of her requests with patience, your voice soft as you address her concerns. Moonlight spills through the latticed windows of the great hall, its silver glow casting a gentle light between you. At last, she has no more questions.

With deep focus, she cradles the ring she has yet to place on your finger, carefully polishing it using the last clean patches of her white veil. When she finally tucks it away, no longer trembling with fear, you let out a sigh of relief.

speaker: Graves
content: Wonderful! Now I won't have any regrets. I'll finally have the wedding I've always dreamed of!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, should we start from the beginning?

speaker: Graves
content: Huh? Right now?

speaker: Graves
content: No, no, no, no!
Before you can even react, a blue shape, swinging like a rattle drum, retreats back into the shadows.

speaker: Graves
content: N-not now! I'm not presentable! Wait until I transform back—and I still need to fix my makeup... Oh no, my dress is dirty too!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Actually, I don't really mind...

speaker: Graves
content: Well I do mind! What kind of bride would look like this?

speaker: Graves
content: Wait for me. I want you to see me at my most beautiful and perfect self. You should dress up too! It's such a rare occasion, after all.
Get dressed up? Before you can even process this thought or say anything, you feel a sudden grip on your back!

speaker: No. 15
content:
No. 15's skilled with needle and thread! Patch and mend, nothing to dread! Dullahan's got experience to spare! Together we'll help, a reliable pair!
The couple's debut must be perfect indeed, a makeover is what you need!

speaker: Dullahan
content: Struggle. Futile.
What's with this sudden sing-song chant? You spin around toward the source and recognize two figures you'd noticed earlier among the guests.

On the right stands a headless figure, its body completely encased in heavy armor. The one on the left is equally bizarre—a grinning face, crudely stitched together from mismatched parts. You know things are about to go terribly wrong.

options: I think I'll pass on the makeover.

content: You're dragged away without any chance to protest. Though forcibly separated from Graves, your thoughts remain locked on her. You keep thinking about her fixation, and... the dark shadow clinging to her.
[Black Screen Transition]
Only after the monsters have escorted you away with their musical performance does Graves, her body covered in contamination, dare to peek out from hiding.
She gazes at the scattered wedding decorations strewn across the floor, then gently lifts a delicate veil woven from spider silk to her nose, inhaling its scent.

speaker: Graves
content: So you didn't lie to me after all. You really did find me someone willing to be my love.

speaker: Graves
content: All of this feels too good to be true... This isn't just a dream, is it?
The grand hall lies empty and still, but Graves seems locked in conversation with something unseen, her words directed at the empty air.
[Corrupted Graves Appears]

speaker: Graves?
content: If this is a dream, I hope I never wake up from it...

speaker: EMP
content: Please stop!

speaker: Labyrinth
content: EMP, considerable timidity detected. According to preliminary investigations, this story is largely fabricated. The story shall continue: at midnight, ghosts congregate, playing wedding elegies, with eerie wails of the white ghosts echoing—
The bedtime ghost story session in the Bureau continues. EMP lunges forward to cover Labyrinth's mouth.

speaker: EMP
content: I'm begging you, please let me sleep in peace!

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Labyrinth A.I. Maid III is equipped with an audio system in her chest. Legend has it that the hoary Ghost Bride...

speaker: EMP
content: Aaaaaahhhhh!

speaker: Hecate
content: Would anyone actually be willing to marry the ghost bride?

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Negative. The bride, driven by a deep-seated resentment, hence cast a formidable curse, vowing to wait for a destined love—a love that lasts beyond the confines of death.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: An eternal... lover, never... to be pa—rted till death.
[Chief's Lounge]
The Bureau is eerily quiet in the dead of night. Every now and then, a patrolling guard walks past the door, their footsteps echoing before fading down the hallway.

In the Chief's lounge, unnoticed by anyone, a strange fragrance drifts from the picture book at the bedside. Its cloying sweetness, reminiscent of rotting flowers, creeps closer to the sleeping, vulnerable figure on the bed...
[Bureau]

speaker: Hecate
content: Is Chief still not awake?

Hecate stays by the Chief's bedside, refusing to leave. Hours have passed since the guards first detected the strong fragrance emanating from the Chief's lounge. Despite every effort, Chief shows no signs of waking up. Meanwhile, Nightingale continues her investigation into the suspicious picture book.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Master is experiencing fatigue and requires rest, as would a human.

speaker: EMP
content: That's right! Stop frowning, Hecate. He's probably just exhausted and catching up on sleep. I'm sure he'll wake up soon. Maybe he's feasting in his dreams right now.
female_content: That's right! Stop frowning, Hecate. She's probably just exhausted and catching up on sleep. I'm sure she'll wake up soon. Maybe she's feasting in her dreams right now.

content: [Castle Gallery]

speaker: No. 15
content: What do you think of this fish necktie?

speaker: No. 15
content: Then surely you'll like these little brooches made of rat flesh?
You're wrapped in putrid, decaying rags that barely resemble formal clothing. Fighting back the urge to vomit, you force a strained smile.

speaker: No. 15
content: What about these? An intestine belt and semiconductor wings! You'll surely be the most dazzling person in the hall, second only to Graves!

In a side hall on the second floor of Morveth Castle, the mechanical girl known as No. 15 bounces excitedly among the ruins, completely absorbed in this dress-up game. But as the newlywed-to-be, you don't share in her delight.

Though you still can't remember how you arrived here, you've gradually grown accustomed to the Mania permeating the castle. Slowly, you're reconnecting with the shackles, and your instincts and experience in handling Mania incidents are beginning to resurface.
Resolving the Sinner's obsession with weddings will break this Mania space—could it really be that simple? That flickering black shadow on Graves fills you with unease.

speaker: Graves?
content: I'm not good enough. There must be something. Think! Is my hair a mess? Did I wear my veil wrong? Am I too thin? And that most important thing... he can't find out...
female_content: I'm not good enough. There must be something. Think! Is my hair a mess? Did I wear my veil wrong? Am I too thin? And that most important thing... she can't find out...

speaker: Graves?
content: If he finds out, he will hate me, abandon me!
female_content: If she finds out, she will hate me, abandon me!

speaker: Graves?
content: Careful, Graves! He's getting closer, he's going to see us like this, see how ugly we truly are! Then we'll never deserve happiness again!
female_content: Careful, Graves! She's getting closer, she's going to see us like this, see how ugly we truly are! Then we'll never deserve happiness again!

content: [Exit flashback]

Graves seems to converse naturally with her, as if entirely accustomed to her presence. She even refers to herself and Graves collectively as "we"... You turn your attention to No. 15, who's busily focused on dressing you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No. 15, is it alright if I call you that? Graves chose you to help, so you must know her quite well?

speaker: No. 15
content: Of course. Graves has been in this castle since she was young. She witnessed each of us come into existence. It makes me a bit emotional to think that Graves has finally found a partner of her own... Hmm, you've got quite a slim waist.
No. 15 responds while continues working without pause.

speaker: No. 15
content: Come to think of it, we're actually quite alike. Just like you, I was created because someone came to the castle, wishing to meet their true love. I'm manifested by a wish, too. Lift your foot.

speaker: No. 15
content: But I'm less fortunate. My guy was so fickle. One moment he thought I wasn't as cool as some superhero, the next he complained I wasn't as obedient as a house elf, and well, you can see the result—
She makes a face with her misshapen body.

speaker: No. 15
content: Hehe... Anyway, it was all so long ago. I don't even remember what kind of person I used to be, but this is fine too. Thanks to him wanting fifteen different types of lovers, I ended up with the name No. 15!
No. 15's tone is upbeat, but you can still tell this isn't exactly a happy story.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Seeing how Graves longs for marriage, I assumed all the love stories that took place here were beautiful ones.

speaker: No. 15
content: ...It will be. I believe she'll find the most beautiful love. Because... she found you!
As she speaks, she holds a mirror up to your face.
[Grotesque Deformed NPC Silhouette]

speaker: No. 15
content: I get it, say no more. My brilliant styling has left you doubting if that's really you in the mirror.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your sense of beauty has been completely twisted by whoever made those wishes!

speaker: No. 15
content: Huh? Should I replace the intestine belt with lace instead?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not the point!

Ignoring your protests, No. 15 continues rummaging tirelessly through her collection of scraps. You look at her more closely now, realizing the wish-maker didn't imbue her with any expectation of love—only the careless marks of indecision.

Perhaps it's because she can't change what happened to her that she genuinely wishes for Graves's happiness. And perhaps her distorted sense of beauty isn't entirely her fault, given she's merely a wish vessel. You recall that the shadow once said something similar:

speaker: Graves
content: He doesn't like us? Then what's his type? We can become whatever he wants!
female_content: She doesn't like us? Then what's her type? We can become whatever she wants!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No. 15, does Graves have any other close friends? The kind she would share all her secrets with?

speaker: No. 15
content: If anyone could get Graves to open up... it would probably be you.

Oblivious to your intention, No. 15 contentedly straightens the edges of your coat. You glance at your utterly hideous reflection in the mirror, then look down at the monstrous outfit adorning your body.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Talking to herself? To another side of... her?
[Red flash] [Heartbeat]
Your shackles react again, sensing the aura of that shadow attached to Graves. "It" is still agitated, active, prowling nearby! You grab No. 15 by the arm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where is Graves now?

The mechanical girl, completely unaware of the urgency, watches as the anxious Chief abandons the formal attire she had so meticulously prepared, hastily throws on a gray trench coat, and strides in the direction she pointed. Only then does she realize she forgot to tell the Chief:
That direction leads to an endless maze.
[Corridor]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This must be the place.

Guided by your shackles, you arrive at a corridor that seems to stretch endlessly into the dark. The hallway is empty, its floorboards creaking slightly from years of neglect. The candle holders on the walls have long been extinguished, their rusted surfaces streaked with hardened wax that drips in eerie, twisted patterns.

Tightly shut doors line both sides of the corridor, each one like a gateway to another unknown world. The cold and darkness press in around you. You can sense that the shadow clinging to Graves is nearby.
[White flash] [Horror sound effect]

Suddenly, a faint yet eerie sound breaks the silence. It's quiet but piercing, like nails scraping against jagged stone, accompanied by rubbing and murmurs that seem to shift and fade. The noise feels far away yet somehow near, as if it's creeping up right behind you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Who are you?

There's no response. Your words vanish into the empty air like stones cast into a bottomless sea, quickly devoured by the silence. The only sound in this desolate corridor is the echo of your footsteps against the floor.
[White flash] [Sound effect] [Shadow jumps out] [Shadow slowly fades away]

A sudden rush of air brushes past your back, as if something darted by. It happened too quickly for you to catch on. You spin around, your eyes scanning the dimly lit corridor—but there's nothing there.

Only the stained glass windows stand silently on the walls, their once-vivid patterns now faded and peeling. Thorns have forced their way in from outside, violently piercing the glass and leaving a jagged hole. Through the gaps, an icy wind howls softly, rushing down the corridor with a faint yet grating whine—like someone snickering in the shadows.
You stare into the empty corridor, confirming there's nothing behind you, and breathe a sigh of relief. Just as you're about to keep walking—
Are you truly ready?
Was that a vow, or merely a lie...
The somber question echoes against the stone walls. A massive shadow stretches across the floor in the moonlight, but when your eyes trace back to its source, you find nothing there.

Do you accept her festering heart? Will you kiss the blue mold blooming from her spine? Do you promise to never wipe away the bloodstains on the wedding ring? Do you swear to love her shattered skull more than any intact soul?
The resonant voice echoes all around you, its probing questions closing in, yet the speaker refuses to reveal themselves.
Vows? Promises? Laughable. Childish ceremonies can't shield you from impending deaths, nor prevent the inevitable separation.
I once made the same vow: "I'll stay with you forever." But then the war came and took everything. In the end, all she got was a cold, silent tombstone.

The shadow vanishes abruptly. You look around, as the painted eyes from the ancient oil portraits on the walls stare at you. You can't identify who was questioning you, but whoever it is clearly harbors intense hostility toward you and your upcoming wedding.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't have such a profound understanding of marriage, nor your kind of experience. If possible, would you be willing to reveal yourself and share your wisdom? I'd very much like to hear your perspective.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You seem to care so much about this wedding, yet you hide in the shadows intimidating the couple with your negativity... Is this what you call "maturity" and "caution"?
Your tone may be gentle, but the shackles on your wrists haven't loosened one bit. The voice isn't provoked by your words—it only responds with a cold, mocking laugh.
A toast to your courage, a toast to your foolishness, a toast to your... arrogance in knowing nothing of separation.
This feels different from the obsession that grips Graves. The shackles don't react to the voice—this isn't the "shadow" you're searching for.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank you for your "blessing," but I have more important matters to attend to ensure our wedding proceeds smoothly.
An unintentional trap is a hundred times crueler than any calculated harm! You shouldn't give her false hope!
Now, say your vows—will you take her hand, knowing you'll weave her wedding dress from lies?
From the depths of the corridor, a dark figure emerges once more, its long sword scraping against the floor with an agonizing screech as it moves toward you. This is anything but friendly!
Acting on instinct, you open a small door in the hallway and squeeze inside.
[Black Screen]
Foolish young one, do you honestly think this is a celebration?
Or perhaps... your promises are nothing but empty lies that won't last even a moment? You'll leave her to face everything alone, abandoned once again!
The accusing voice doesn't fade away—instead, it grows sharper, each sentence seemingly tearing through the air and slipping through the door crack.

You press your body against the cold stone door, holding your breath. The room is pitch black, the sound of your heartbeat breaking the silence. It draws closer—footsteps echo faintly, like something prowling in the darkness, its presence cold and suffocating as it approaches.
You instinctively tighten your grip, power pulsing in your palm as you waver, hesitating whether to rush out and confront whatever's out there. Suddenly, you hear a soft sound—
The candles inside the room light up.
At the same time, the red spike pulses in your palm. You sense that the shadow you've been searching for is now just within reach.
[Study]
The candlelight illuminates the aged study. On the desk at the center of the room lies a note—the handwriting is crooked and messy, but the ink is unmistakably fresh.
<color=#7683a2><i>Don't be afraid. The one outside the door means no harm. You're safe here.</color><i>

Unlike the rest of the castle, this place lacks the suffocating chill and eeriness. Despite being covered in cobwebs and dust, the room somehow radiates a warmth, as if someone has poured their heart into the decor. A soft rustling sound breaks the silence again, and suddenly there's another note beneath the candlestick.
<color=#7683a2><i>Go out and keep right to exit the corridor. No. 15 is waiting for you.</color><i>

The candlestick casts a gentle, warm yellow glow across the cluttered desk and picture frames on the wall. The edges of the frames show signs of decay, and the canvases are covered with a thick layer of dust, making it impossible to discern what they depict.
After wiping away the thick layer of dust, you discover several ancient oil paintings depicting various scenes:

The first painting shows a corridor. Arched vaulted ceilings and carved pillars adorn the hallway, giving it a regal, palace-like grandeur. Sunlight streams through tall stained-glass windows, casting dappled patterns of light, while the stone-tiled floor reflects a subtle sheen. It looks somewhat similar to the corridor outside.

The next painting depicts a magnificent great hall. Enormous crystal chandeliers hang high above, while a long red carpet stretches from the entrance deep into the ceremonial space, adorned throughout with fresh flowers and colorful silk ribbons.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this... Morveth Castle from the past?
As if someone heard your question, another note appears on the table.
<color=#7683a2><i>Yes, this place was once a true sanctuary for weddings.</color><i>
Unlike the eerie environment around you, the places in the paintings are colorful, brimming with a sense of vitality and warmth.
The wooden desk where the note sits is cluttered with books, papers, and dried-up ink bottles. You push them aside and uncover a book with a black cover hidden underneath.
The moment your fingers brush against the brittle cover of the book, you hear a sharp, nervous gasp from a shadowy corner of the study.

February 14, N.F. 82, Newlyweds: John Smith & Mary Brown Procurement list: White tulle, rose petals, champagne, cake, candles... February 27, N.F. 82, Newlyweds: James Wilson & Emma Davis Procurement list: Red silk, lilies, red wine, chocolate, music box... March 2, N.F. 82, Newlyweds: Michael Johnson & Lily Martin Procurement list: Blue ribbons, tulips, champagne, fruit tarts, decorative lights...
Flipping through the pages, you can almost feel the castle's former vibrancy, a place once filled with life and joy. Yet, the golden days seem to have been short.

June 28, N.F. 83, Newlyweds: Alexander Green & Sophia Clark Procurement list: White tulle, rose petals, champagne... December 13, N.F. 84, Newlyweds: Henry Taylor & Emily Anderson Procurement list: Red silk, lilies, red wine...
With the DisSea Explosion as a turning point, weddings at the castle steadily declined afterward. Yet, among these records, one entry stands out starkly from the rest.
November 2, N.F. 89, Abandoned infant: unnamed Procurement list: milk powder, diapers, blankets...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: An abandoned infant?

Before you can examine it more closely, a dark shadow flashes before your eyes, snatching the book away. Another scrap of paper has appeared on the desk, the handwriting even more crooked than before:
Don't look!!! (///A///)

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why can't I look?
Your question is met with silence. But as you glance down, you immediately notice an unmistakable clue.
A familiar white veil peeks out from behind a bookshelf. Adorned with pearls and blue roses, it still bears traces of Mania contamination that hasn't fully faded.

options: Pretend you don't know it's her

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you write these notes? Thank you. I hope I'm not disturbing you.

speaker: Very well. You've managed this exceptionally well, after all. You can proceed as you wish.
content: Graves? Weren't you preparing for the wedding? Why are you here?

speaker: Graves
content: —! I... ahem! I'm not Graves, you've mistaken me for someone else. I'm just a nun who cleans around the castle... That's right, I heard someone was lost, so I came to help. If you follow the corridor to the right, you'll reach the ceremony hall.
Yet another classic case of Graves accidentally giving herself away. It seems her appearance hasn't fully recovered yet, and she doesn't want you to see what she looks like.

options: Right, I've got the wrong person again.
I see, please forgive me for intruding.

content: You choose not to expose her, instead sitting down on the floor with only a row of bookshelves between you. She clearly didn't expect you to get this close—in the flickering candlelight, her silhouette stiffens, curling up tightly as if bracing herself.

speaker: Graves
content: Why are you still here?
If you told her you were looking for Graves—and even planned to kick that suspicious shadow in the butt—she'd probably startle like a frightened bird and run off again.

speaker: Graves
content: There aren't any scary monsters in Morveth Castle. They all exist because of lovers' wishes, and they're all my friends.
Your flimsy excuse worked even better than expected—she seems to believe your made-up story. While exploiting her innocence makes you feel a bit guilty, this is definitely a good opportunity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank you for the directions, Sister. You seem quite familiar with Morveth Castle.

options: Then you must know Graves quite well, right?

content: She freezes for a moment, but quickly recovers and slips back into her "role."

speaker: Graves
content: Of course! I'm the nun of the castle after all. I know her better than anyone!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'd like to hear her story.

speaker: Graves
content: Why? It's not a good story.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I mean, she is my bride, I've got to learn more about her, right? Marriage takes two people, after all. I can only tell whether a story is good or not after hearing it, and...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see something in her. I sense that Graves is hiding something from me. I want to learn more about her, and this place.
The figure behind the bookshelf seems to freeze for an instant, but continues speaking nonetheless.

speaker: Graves
content: Graves wasn't pretty at all... When Sister Elsie found her, she was just a dark, wrinkled little thing. But Sister Elsie said all babies look like that when they're born.

speaker: Graves
content: But as she grew older, we noticed something was off. Red skin, sharp teeth... she would pounce and bite at the slightest disturbance. She... she wasn't human.

speaker: Graves
content: Monster... that's what we all called her.
Her voice grows quieter, and you catch the soft rustle of her burying her face in her arms.

speaker: Graves
content: Ever since she arrived, fewer and fewer couples came here to get married. We couldn't make a living anymore, so many of us left one after another. That monster was a bad omen—she brought misfortune to Morveth Castle.

options: She shouldn't be blamed for this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Couples stopped coming here to get married because of natural disasters and urban development. It wasn't her fault.

speaker: Graves
content: ...It was her fault. If she'd done as she was told and stayed hidden, she wouldn't have scared off so many couples. Morveth Castle wouldn't have been left with nothing but those awful ghost wedding stories.

speaker: Graves
content: She tried to hide her face, but ruining things was always what she did best... You know, ever since she was little, she loved hiding in the corners of the hall to secretly watch the wedding ceremonies. Sister Elsie caught her several times.

options: I've heard Graves mention her before.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's no longer here with us, is she?

speaker: Graves
content: Sister Elsie was very old, even older than the Morveth Castle itself. She said she would eventually have to leave... She said all human stories follow the same pattern—people meet, then part ways.

speaker: Graves
content: So she was alone again. She stuck to her usual routine: waking up, praying, making lunch, and then hiding where no one could see her, waiting for couples to arrive. It went on like that for a very, very long time, until everyone forgot Morveth Castle even existed.
Graves's voice becomes muffled and subdued. She clearly doesn't like telling this story.
You're separated by bookshelves, unable to see each other's expressions. Candlelight flickers between the wooden shelves, bathing you in a gentle warm glow while leaving Graves hidden in shadow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So Graves has always felt abandoned. What she wants isn't just a ceremony, is it?
You lean closer toward her side of the bookshelf, the aged wood creaking softly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What she really wants is...

options: A fate where she's never abandoned.

content: You can't see her face, but through the gaps between the books, you glimpse the veil-wearing girl clutching her arms tightly as she lifts her head.

Above your heads, the bookshelves display the past of this wedding sanctuary: books on wedding cultures from Outlands and photo albums of newlywed couples captured in moments of blessing. To her, they are like stars in the night sky, offering solace when her insecurities and doubts creep in.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But these only show you the most beautiful moments in relationships. I'm no expert on this subject myself—since I got questioned about it in the hallway. But... are "weddings" and what you truly want really the same thing?
Graves begins to tremble defensively, as though her most guarded secret has been laid bare. That familiar dark shadow once again weaves itself around her form.

speaker: Graves
content: It will happen, I know it will. As long as I stay beautiful and attentive, I'll eventually find someone who won't abandon me.

speaker: Graves
content: ...For better, for worse, for richer, for poorer, in sickness and in health, in joy and in sadness, to support and cherish me...
She speaks faster and faster, her voice shaking violently.

speaker: Graves?
content: I've waited for so long. Why haven't things worked out? It's because I don't deserve it, isn't it?

speaker: Graves?
content: No one wants to stay with me! Everyone always abandons me!

This is it—the source of the obsession feeding the Mania crisis at Morveth Castle: Graves's hidden side. Her suppressed emotions break free from their disguise, twisting and writhing as they take shape, threatening to swallow her whole.
This unusual Mania doesn't stem from an external force—it is born from the insecurity, loneliness, suffering, and confusion that have always resided within her.
Without hesitation, you rise to your feet and move behind the bookshelf, approaching her desperate figure as she digs her claws into her skin in despair. Gently, you take hold of her decaying hands.
(Flashback)

Fifteen Minutes Earlier
Castle Corridor

speaker: Dullahan
content: Do you accept her festering heart? Will you kiss the blue mold blooming from her spine? Do you promise never to wipe away the bloodstains on the wedding ring? Do you swear to love her shattered skull more than any intact soul?

speaker: Dullahan
content: Now, say your vows—will you take her hand, knowing you'll weave her wedding dress from lies?

speaker: Luminita
content: No, no, no! If you say it like that, you'll scare them away!

speaker: Dullahan
