Sallie regrets this decision. She's bombarded by Milly's stories for what feels like an eternity, until Milly's throat is parched and Sallie's mind begins to wander.

speaker: Milly
content: ...Anyway, he's going to come for me, and then we'll live happily ever after!
female_content: ...Anyway, she's going to come for me, and then we'll live happily ever after!

speaker: Sallie
content: ...If I understand correctly, you two have never actually met, have you?

speaker: Milly
content: Well, we've met... once?

speaker: Sallie
content: And you confessed your love after meeting just once?

speaker: Milly
content: Ah, well, I could never say it out loud! It's too embarrassing!

speaker: Sallie
content: Does he know you're waiting for him?
female_content: Does she know you're waiting for her?

speaker: Milly
content: Not yet, but soon! Once I get more famous, someone will definitely tell him!
female_content: Not yet, but soon! Once I get more famous, someone will definitely tell her!

speaker: Sallie
content: Do you really believe that he'll show up one day, fall in love with you, and take you away?
female_content: Do you really believe that she'll show up one day, fall in love with you, and take you away?

speaker: Milly
content: Of course I do!

Sallie covers her face. Is Milly hopelessly romantic or just painfully naive? Is she an Eastsider? Drop Milly anywhere in Eastside and she'd be scammed in a heartbeat! Though... that's not so different from her current situation anyway.

speaker: Milly
content: Talking about myself this whole time... Now your turn, Sallie! What's your sweetheart like?

speaker: Sallie
content: That's all in the past. I don't want to talk about it...
Memories of that abruptly ended relationship chill her voice.
But when she looks up into Milly's eager eyes, sees the lingering bruises on her skin, Sallie can't bring herself to refuse.
...She'll tell her something. Think of it as making a child happy.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...Alright, alright. His name is Theodore. He used to come in to the bar to watch me dance. Not in a place like this, of course... and not this kind of dancing.

speaker: Sallie
content: He's a rich boy from a good family, nothing like a poor dancer such as me. It was his rowdy friends who dragged him into the bar the first time.

speaker: Sallie
content: At first, he was so timid he could barely speak straight. He got so flustered trying to talk to me, he'd mess up my name. He came every day, but we never exchanged more than three sentences. He was a complete idiot.
She'd long ago decided to put the past behind her, but speaking of it brings the memories back, vivid before her eyes. Sallie's voice softens.

speaker: Sallie
content: But... one day, when I was being harassed by a drunk, he jumped in front of me. He was shaking all over, but he didn't back down an inch. I guess it was... brave of him.

speaker: Milly
content: How touching! If he knew what you were going through here, he'd come rushing to save you!

Does he know? Or does he not care? The last time they saw each other, Theodore had sworn he'd fight for their future, that he'd mustered the courage to go home and make his case. Then, like in every clichéd Eastside romance novel, he never returned.

Faced with a broken promise, Sallie had decisively cut him out of her life. She never trusted those arrogant rich people to begin with; going out with Theodore had just been... a moment of weakness, a lapse in judgment. She isn't some fool who'd fall head over heels for a pretty face.

...But thinking about it now, she really doesn't know what happened to him. Before he left, he'd given her all his money for safekeeping—everything he'd saved trying to make it on his own. It wasn't much, but it wasn't nothing. When the debt collectors came for her, Sallie didn't touch it. She doesn't know why.
Did she want the satisfaction of throwing the goddamned money back in that bastard's face? Or... was there a part of her that still fantasized he'd break free and come back for her?
But right now, there's someone more worried than she is.

speaker: Milly
content: Oh, he doesn't know? He must be worried sick! No wonder you want to escape so badly... We have to do something fast.

speaker: Sallie
content: Escape...?

speaker: Golden Mask
content: What kind of look is that?! What do you think you are?! How dare you look at me like that?!

speaker: Mr. E
content: So don't even think about leaving. No one leaves here without my permission. Unless they're dead.
Sallie begins to tremble, and Milly notices. She stops talking and gently takes Sallie's hand.

speaker: Milly
content: Sallie. Look at me. Take a deep breath. It'll pass. Everything will pass. I'm here. I told you I'd be on your side, that I'd help you escape—and I meant it.

speaker: Sallie
content: But what about you? What will happen to you after you help me? Won't Mr. E...
In her mind's eye, she sees Milly being dragged away by Mr. E again. That suffocating sense of helplessness still makes her blood run cold.
But the person in question doesn't seem to care in the slightest.

speaker: Milly
content: It's fine! Mr. E spoils me. He wouldn't really do anything to me. See? Not a single scar left.

speaker: Milly
content: Besides, this is an elopement! So romantic, so epic! I've studied many romance movies. It's time to put all that into practice.

speaker: Milly
content: Your sweetheart has some status, right? Then we just need to get the word out, let him know you're here. The guests on this ship have their own connections. Someone's bound to be able to reach him!

speaker: Milly
content: And... I have the perfect person to help us—<color=#fb9259>Cassian</color>! He knows more about what goes on aboard this ship than anyone. He's got this!
Milly beams with confidence, one hand balled into a fist to cheer Sallie on. Her hair shines like gold, and for a moment, Sallie is dazzled.

speaker: Sallie
content: We've only known each other for a few days... Why are you going so far to help me?

speaker: Milly
content: Because of love, of course.

speaker: Milly
content: We're companions with love in our hearts. If leaving this place will bring you happiness, then of course I'll help you.
So many questions remain, so many concerns... but in this dark, suffocating club, Milly's words are like honey and sunshine. Alright, I'll play along. Sallie thinks, finally nodding her head.
The clock in the corner chimes. Milly brushes her skirt and rises to her feet.

speaker: Milly
content: Hehe, it's about time. I need to get to work and provide cover for our plan. Don't forget it, okay?
The room feels empty the moment Milly leaves, filling Sallie with unease. She nervously stands up as well.

speaker: Milly
content: Oh right! I have a gift for you.
She hurries back to Sallie and reaches out a hand, gently brushing her finger across the corner of Sallie's lips.
In that instant, Sallie is enveloped by a familiar sweet fragrance, like the honey dripping on her that night, but different. She feels a strange power enter her body.
Milly withdraws her finger and presses a small golden lip balm into Sallie's hand, flashing a mischievous smile.

speaker: Milly
content: Relax. He'll definitely come.

speaker: Milly
content: Until then, if any bad guys try to hurt you again, use this lip balm to protect yourself, okay?
In the banquet hall near noon, no one was present except for Cassian, who was polishing wine glasses by the bar.

The nightly routine of absurd theatrics had yet to begin, and the crystal chandeliers hanging high above remained unlit. Only a few rays of sunlight filtered through gaps in the heavy curtains, casting dappled shadows on the spotless carpet. Last night's revelry had long since faded, leaving only a ruin of silence and desolation.
This is one of Cassian's rare moments of respite. He wouldn't call it enjoyable, but at least he can drop that smile, stiffer than any mask, and find brief solace in solitude.

His movements are unhurried. He lifts a wine glass by the stem, tracing slow circles around the rim with a cloth. Every few turns brings a dull pain to his fingers, an old injury, not sharp, but impossible to ignore.

Cassian doesn't wince, doesn't even alter his rhythm. He endures in silence, as he always does. Pain is something he's long grown used to. He keeps his head down, polishing the glass with quiet, almost mechanical precision. Until a shrill voice shatters his precious calm.

speaker: Sallie
content: Ask that bartender for help? Milly, are you serious?!

speaker: Milly
content: Shh! Keep it down!
Two sets of footsteps approach, stopping just outside the banquet hall doors. Cassian's hands pause for a fraction of a second.

speaker: Sallie
content: I mean, you do know he tricked me into going to Mr. E's office, right? That guy's so weird. The second he leaves the bar, he gets all gloomy and gives everyone the cold shoulder. I don't trust him.

Realizing she's getting worked up, Sallie lowers her voice, but Cassian can still hear every word through the thin wall. He shakes his head, sets the dried wine glass upside down on the rack, and picks up the next one.
Cassian isn't bothered by her blatant badmouthing. He's heard it all before, and he's long past the point of wanting to explain himself. But he doesn't want to get dragged into unnecessary trouble.
Especially not before he achieves his goal.

speaker: Milly
content: ...Well, do you have a better idea?
But it seems luck has never been on his side. After a tense silence, he hears Sallie stomp in frustration. Here comes the trouble.

speaker: Sallie
content: Ugh, fine. Let's give it a shot. Doesn't hurt to try.
The next second, the doors swing open. Two girls, who might as well have the word "trouble" printed all over their faces, walk right up to his bar.

speaker: Milly
content: Cassian! I knew you'd be here!
Milly greets him cheerfully. Cassian inwardly sighs. Without looking up, he says flatly:

speaker: Cassian
content: Sorry, the lounge is closed. Please come back later.

speaker: Sallie
content: We're not here for drinks!

speaker: Cassian
content: Then all the more reason to leave. I'm afraid I don't provide other services aside from drinks.

speaker: Sallie
content: What's with the attitude?! See? I told you, there's no use talking to him!
Sallie glares at Cassian, but Milly tugs on her sleeve and steps forward with a hopeful smile.

speaker: Milly
content: Look, Cassian. I have this brilliant plan to help Sallie find her true love, and we need your help! Can you get a message out for us?
Cassian finally looks up, meeting Milly's innocent eyes. His face remains as calm as ever, his indifference bordering on cruel.

speaker: Cassian
content: Give up. Whatever you're planning, don't try to be clever under Mr. E's nose. You'll be dead before you even know what happened.
His tone stays level, but his words hit like ice water. This isn't a threat, more like a cold, rational statement of fact. But Milly is unfazed. She blinks, her voice full of determination.

speaker: Milly
content: That's exactly why we need you. We can't do it alone! And we just can't stand by while Sallie loses her true love, that's too cruel... You have to help us!

speaker: Cassian
content: I can't help you with that.
He shakes his head gently, completely unmoved by the mention of true love. Milly giggles and takes another determined step forward.

speaker: Milly
content: But I know you can! I've asked around. You have ways of getting messages out. Besides, you used to be the heir of a powerful family in Eastside, until someone framed your family and brought it down... Aren't you here to find the person who did that to you? To get your revenge?

speaker: Sallie
content: ...W-what? Is that true?
Sallie's mouth falls open, stunned by this sudden revelation. Cassian sets down the glass and doesn't say anything. It might be a silent confirmation, or an invitation for Milly to continue.
Sallie's eyes dart to Cassian's hands, folded in front of him. Long, pale fingers like a pianist's, but wrapped in strange metal braces that barely support the frail, scarred joints.
Cassian notices her staring and discreetly pulls his hands back behind the counter. Milly takes a deep breath and presses on, her voice urgent.

speaker: Milly
content: But you haven't made a move yet, which means you're not ready. Or you're still looking for the right moment. You need help, too!

speaker: Cassian
content: How can you help me?
Milly spreads her hands, her face brightening with that same guileless smile, like an eternally optimistic fawn.

speaker: Milly
content: I'm a Sinner. My ability lets me influence and control people's minds. That might come in handy, right? Think about it. You give the word, and I can smooth the way for you. You can get information easily from anyone you want!
Only when Milly reveals her hand does Cassian finally show some interest. His expression shifts subtly as he begins to assess the two girls in earnest.

speaker: Milly
content: You help us send a message to find Sallie's true love, and we help you gather clues about your enemy. It's a fair trade. We help each other out.
Milly blinks her shiny eyes, clearly confident in her plan. Cassian is quiet for a moment. The questioning look in his eyes slowly settles into cool acceptance. He gives a slight nod.

speaker: Cassian
content: I can help you. But only if the information you bring me is worth my while.

speaker: Milly
content: Deal! That's fantastic, thank you so much!
Milly excitedly raps her fingers on the wooden bar top, like she's sealed a sacred pact. She pulls Sallie to her side and waves at Cassian.

speaker: Milly
content: Just sit back and wait! We're getting right on it. We won't let you down!
They turn to leave, but Cassian suddenly speaks up.

speaker: Cassian
content: ...Wait.

They turn back, looking at him with confusion. Recalling the conversation he overheard and Sallie's obvious distrust, Cassian slowly shifts his gaze to her. For a rare moment, he almost looks hesitant.

speaker: Cassian
content: I didn't send you to Mr. E's office to trick you. Just... think before you act. Don't pick a fight if you can help it. Or you'll end up dead.

Sallie freezes, her face flushing. The misunderstanding and anger she'd been holding on to suddenly have nowhere to go, leaving a flustered unease. She wants to say something, but Cassian has already looked away and gone back to polishing the glassware.
The glass is already spotless, yet he continues to wipe it, again and again, like the hands of a clock in their endless cycle.
Euphoria may be a luxury multi-deck cruise ship, but for dancers like Sallie, their world is limited to the stage, bar, backstage area, cafeteria, and employee lounge.
Only when they are chosen by a guest do they get a chance to enter the luxury suites or accompany the VIPs in other recreation areas.
Many dancers are more than willing to get close to the guests. It means a period of freedom, money, and indulgence.

For the guests seeking pleasure on the ship, there's no difference between day and night. The bar is always the most popular spot, a place for encounters, flirting, and discreet exchange of information.
Sallie takes out the lip balm Milly gave her and stares at it.

speaker: Sallie
content: Protect me... will it really work? This... honey lip balm?

speaker: Milly
content: When I put the honey on you just now... what did you see?
She hates to admit it, but Sallie had thought of Theodore.

speaker: Milly
content: Hm? Are you blushing? Hehe, don't be shy. Whether seasoned players or heartless fools, anyone who touches my <color=#fb9259>honey</color> will see the one they love. Well? Is your head full of Theodore now?
Milly draws closer, gently stroking Sallie's arm. Sallie flinches and takes a step back, the spot Milly touched suddenly feeling very uncomfortable.

speaker: Milly
content: At first, my honey only numbed people. Mr. E said my ability is mild mind control. I can control the thoughts of anyone who touches the honey.

speaker: Milly
content: But it's more than that. Your body, your mind... they will only respond to that one person.
Milly winks. Sallie realizes something and suddenly blushes.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...What do you mean?
Milly smiles sweetly and offers no further explanation.

speaker: Milly
content: It doesn't matter. Like I told you, the guests only come to talk with me about love. Because that's all they can do.

speaker: Milly
content: If you're really scared, use this to protect yourself.

speaker: Milly
content: Just find a way to apply it to a guest's skin, and it will flip their true love switch. And when that happens... they won't have room in their heads for any other nasty thoughts. People in love are always the sweetest and most honest.
...So it's basically a tool for extracting information.
Sallie hovers near the bar, trying to identify a guest who might give up information.

speaker: Flirtatious Guest
content: Well hello there, sweetheart. Haven't we met somewhere before?
A guest suddenly extends his hand, blocking Sallie's path. She takes his arm, using the gesture to dab the lip balm onto his wrist.

speaker: Sallie
content: Oh, my. Your hands are rather dry, sir.
The moment the lip balm touches his skin, the man freezes as if struck by lightning, and his eyes suddenly grow... tender.

speaker: Flirtatious Guest
content: ...You know, I'm not the type to fool around.
Sallie blinks with feigned innocence.

speaker: Sallie
content: What's wrong? Are you... thinking of someone? Is there a love you need to confess?
Her questions touch his heart. The man clutches his waist with one hand, the other trembling against his mask. Tears glisten in his eyes as if he's seeing a love long lost.

speaker: Flirtatious Guest
content: I've... been looking for someone.

speaker: Flirtatious Guest
content: You look so much like her. When I saw you, I can't help but move closer. But I shouldn't lie to myself... I've had twenty-seven lovers since, but none of them could ever replace her...
Sallie's eyes go wide. As the man's nose begins to run, she quickly grabs a tissue and hands it to him.

speaker: Flirtatious Guest
content: Oh... you're such a sweet girl. Just like she was...
Then, things get strange. The guest pulls her over to the bar and asks Cassian for two cocktails.

speaker: Flirtatious Guest
content: I gave her riches enough to fill a city, but all she wanted was for me to light a hundred bonfires for her... I bought her a mansion, but she told me she was still lonely...
He rambles on and on about his one true love while boasting about what a romantic and compassionate partner he was.
Sallie plasters on a smile, throwing in a ditzy comment here and there. Soon, the man passes out drunk, slumped over the bar.

speaker: Sallie
content: Whew... I wondered why they just wanted to chat with you... So this is what you meant by the true love switch...
From another corner of the bar, Milly turns her head as if she'd sensed someone watching her. She catches Sallie's exasperated, amused stare and flashes an innocent, playful smile.
Night falls, and the club becomes a honeyed trap. A veneer of glamour enshrouds the entire cruise ship, masking the scent of damp and decay.

It isn't a performance night for Sallie or Milly, but they've dressed up anyway, not in their flashy stage costumes, but in understated, tasteful clothes that let them blend into the circles of money and power, to uncover a story that isn't theirs to tell.

speaker: Milly
content: Come on, smile. Don't be so tense.
Milly smooths the ends of Sallie's hair and whispers in her ear.

speaker: Milly
content: With that look on your face, you won't get a word of truth out of those people.
Sallie nods and takes a deep breath. She tries to mimic Milly, smoothing away the tension in her brow and forcing a stiff smile that she pins to her face like a mask.

The dance floor swirls like a golden tide, swallowing the line between desire and indifference. Milly glides toward a middle-aged man drinking alone at the edge of the floor. He's wearing an impeccably tailored navy suit, the collar embroidered in gold thread with the crest of some old aristocratic merchant guild.
The moment their eyes meet, Milly's face lights up with an innocent, radiant smile. She lets her gaze fall to the glass in his hand, feigning the perfect amount of surprise.

speaker: Milly
content: Your drink has such an unusual color... blue like the deep sea, but with light shining through... I've never seen such a beautiful cocktail. What's it called?
Her approach is a bit abrupt, but the patrons here have always welcomed attention from the Jewel of Euphoria. The man smiles, casual and nonchalant.

speaker: Guest A
content: You'll have to ask that fellow. He's the one who made it. The color's just for show, but the taste... well, it's not bad. That guy's got some skill.
He jerks his chin toward the bar, his tone offhand, like he's praising a well-trained pet.
Milly follows his gaze.

Cassian stands behind the bar, his sharp profile outlined by the light refracting through a glass. His movements are steady and graceful. Lifting a glass, pouring a drink, giving a firm shake... every motion is a pleasure to watch.

He wears a charming, proper smile and says something that makes a wealthy lady giggle. He leans down to light her cigarette with attentive care, nothing like the silent, weary young man from the other day.

speaker: Milly
content: Who is he, anyway? With skills like that, he must be a pretty famous bartender, right?
Milly looks back at the man and asks with feigned curiosity. But the man scoffs like he's heard something absurd. He shakes his head, eyes glinting with undisguised ridicule.

speaker: Guest A
content: Him? Oh, he's famous alright. Just not for mixing drinks. In our circles, he's famous for being a joke.
Meanwhile, Sallie is striking up a conversation with a lady dripping in jewels. The woman takes a sip of her drink, her tone airy.

speaker: Guest B
content: Who in our circle doesn't know about his family? They squeezed their way into high society with some special permit. Enjoyed the spotlight for barely two years, and then... pop! The whole family was gone. I heard they were at a party one night, and by the next day, they were either in prison or dead. Like something out of a play. What a fall from grace.

speaker: Sallie
content: But why would...
Sallie is at a loss for words, until another woman pipes in, her face dripping with contempt and mockery.

speaker: Guest C
content: What else could it be? His family were pawns put on the board by Falke himself. They were dead from the start. You didn't really think they earned all that fame on their own, did you? What a joke.

speaker: Sallie
content: I... I see.

Sallie is still processing what she's just heard. To hide her shock and revulsion, she lowers her gaze and takes a sip of her drink. The lady, however, mistakes this for being awed by the ruthless efficiency of the power struggle, and her voice grows more smug.

speaker: Guest B
content: That's right. Mr. Falke pulls all the strings in Eastside. To put it nicely, that little upstart family was a necessary sacrifice for some scheme. To put it bluntly, they were scapegoats on the chopping block. When the axe would fall was entirely up to Falke.

speaker: Guest B
content: But the funny thing is, they really thought they'd made it into high society! Prancing around at parties, putting on their aristocratic airs. It was hilarious.

Sallie presses her lips together and says nothing. The harsh laughter rings in her ears. She looks down and pretends to smooth out her dress, trying to hide the fury in her eyes. She doesn't want to hear another word. But she remembers one name: Falke.
She quickly excuses herself and slips back into the crowd, but she can't help but glance back.

Cassian is still standing behind the bar, his back perfectly straight, like a bronze pillar that's been tarnished but never bent. The woman he was serving turns to leave, offhandedly tossing a few large bills onto the counter. They flutter off the edge onto the carpeted floor.
Cassian looks down at them silently, his face unreadable. After a moment, he bends down, gathers the bills one by one, folds them neatly, and puts them in the cash box.
When he looks up again, that perfect smile is back on his face, as if nothing has happened at all. He's already greeting the next customer.

speaker: Guest D
content: Who doesn't know they were nothing but a joke from the start? Don't tell me you've been fooled by his looks too. Are you really taking him for some fallen young lord?

speaker: Milly
content: He is a very convincing actor. But if you look closely, you can still tell the difference between him and a true member of the upper class, like yourself.
Milly quirks her lips, feigning agreement. The guest nods with satisfaction, like he's found a kindred spirit.

speaker: Guest D
content: Hahaha, right? They were the only ones who had no clue! They thought they were one of us, when really everyone was just waiting to watch them crash and burn.

Whenever Cassian's name comes up, their first reaction is always laughter. Theatrical, contemptuous laughter. They laugh without restraint, like discussing some trivial gossip, or savoring a farce that has run its course.

speaker: Guest E
content: He used to put on quite a show at parties. Pretty, played piano well enough, really stood out at first glance... But you know his type, right? Just there for decoration. Once you're done with the decorating, you toss them out and nobody misses them.
The gilded glasses glint harshly in the light. They chat and laugh merrily, treating someone's downfall as their after-dinner digestif.

speaker: Guest F
content: So, really, it's no surprise he ended up like this. Their kind always falls the hardest, the ones who are coddled their whole lives but never taught their place. Who would ever mistake them for nobility? Don't make me laugh.

speaker: Sallie
content: That's true. Nothing escapes your notice when it comes to character.

Sallie inclines her head, forcing down the revulsion as she raises her glass to the noble lords and ladies. Feeling quite pleased with Sallie's flattery, one of the women pats her hand with a titter, as if bestowing upon her some supreme honor.

speaker: Guest E
content: Oh, my. The way you talk, I'd almost think you were one of us.

That evening, Milly and Sallie made their way through groups of guests, catching more fragments of conversation. Some were vague, others deliberately hollow and evasive, but a few gleamed with chilling truth.

At first, they could still plaster on a smile and play along with a flippant laugh. But as the night wore on, the laughter became harder to fake. They could only force their smiles, letting those harsh words cut into their hearts.

On this ship, it makes no difference. Bartender or dancer, man or woman, Sinner or ordinary person... they're all the same. To those pleasure seekers, they are nothing more than faces that can be easily replaced, symbols to be summoned, demeaned, and commanded at will.
Stamp on one, and no one would even bother to see what they'd crushed under their heel.

It isn't until the night is almost over that they get a break. When a tipsy customer slings his arm around Milly's shoulders and starts to brag, she manages to pull the key piece of information from his loosened tongue with her ability:

Falke, who has just concluded district development meetings in Eastside, is boarding the ship in a few days. Mr. E has personally arranged a private banquet for him, along with a luxurious upper-level suite, complete with private access and round-the-clock security. It's one of the most impenetrable areas on the entire Euphoria.

speaker: Tipsy Guest
content: You know, he never dared to come here before. Terrified someone might get the dirt on him. But not anymore. Oh no. He's finally... cleaned out all those annoying little obstacles. No one can get in his way anymore. Tsk, tsk. Mr. Falke can finally let loose and have a real good time!
At dawn, as the last of the revelers disperse, the two return to the backstage lounge with what they've found. Cassian is already there, waiting.
After hearing their report, he merely nods slightly, the corner of his mouth lifting in an almost imperceptible curve.

speaker: Cassian
content: ...Thanks.

He still sits perfectly straight. The metallic gleam on his fingers flickers before disappearing into the shadow of his sleeves. Just like the man himself, a master of hiding secrets in the spaces between light and shadow.
After a moment of silence, Sallie finally asks hesitantly.

speaker: Sallie
content: Are you... really planning to go through with it? That man... he has so much power...

speaker: Cassian
content: I've been waiting for this moment.

speaker: Sallie
content: But you're going alone...

speaker: Cassian
content: I can handle it.
Cassian's tone is soft, but it isn't the calm of indifference. It's the calm of a man who is forcing madness and hatred deep into his bones, holding himself together with every ounce of his will.

speaker: Milly
content: Then at least take this... With it, you can use my ability. Just in case.
Milly pulls a golden lip balm from her pocket and carefully places it in front of Cassian. But he doesn't touch it, only shakes his head.

speaker: Cassian
content: Thank you, but I don't need it. I'm already prepared.

speaker: Sallie
content: Do you... not trust us?

speaker: Cassian
content: No. This is my business, and it has nothing to do with you. You don't need to be dragged into it.
Without giving them a chance to respond, Cassian continues.

speaker: Cassian
content: The message you want me to deliver. Is it ready?

Sallie nods and pulls a handwritten note from her pocket. It contains basic information about someone named <color=#fb9259>Theodore</color> and a brief message for help. She clutches the note as if it's her last hope.

speaker: Sallie
content: Please, find <color=#fb9259>Theodore</color> and get this message to him.

speaker: Cassian
content: I will.

Footsteps come from outside, and the three of them fall silent. Cassian takes the note and rises to leave, the wan yellow lamplight brushing the hem of his shirt. He disappears into the shadows at the end of the corridor. He doesn't look back.

Cassian cradles the bottle in his palm and gives it a gentle swirl. The amber liquid sloshes in soft, lazy circles. His gaze falls silently on the curved glass, his expression cool and detached, as if he's watching some vision that has nothing to do with him.

The elevator doors open with a ding. He walks slowly into the ship's private lounge. Rose-colored light spills from the crystal chandeliers, and the air is thick with a familiar, suffocating mix of alcohol, leather, and sickly-sweet perfume.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: Hello, pretty boy. What brings you here so early today?

A sultry voice purrs from the couch. A woman, draped in gossamer silk, reclines against the cushions like a warm, dangerous pool of water. She regards him with the unsettling, suggestive smirk she always wears, one eyebrow arched in amusement.

speaker: Cassian
content: ...I'm here to serve your wine.
The woman crooks her finger, and Cassian obediently approaches. He seats himself beside her, eyes downcast, like a well-tamed cat. She takes the bottle, examines the label, and her eyes light up.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: The reserve vintage from that exclusive winery? I've been trying to get my hands on this for ages. How did you manage to find one?

speaker: Cassian
content: An ambassador was feeling generous yesterday. I remembered you mentioning this a while back and thought you might enjoy it.
His voice is gentle, his eyes eager to please. The woman chuckles and pats the back of his hand, her voice smug.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: Always know how to please me, don't you? Alright. What is it you want this time?

speaker: Cassian
content: Same as before. I have a message I'd like you to pass along to that person.

He retrieves a folded slip of paper from his pocket and offers it to her respectfully. The woman casually takes it, still toying with the wine bottle. She unfolds the note and glances at it, then clicks her tongue.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: This note... is rather curious.
Her finger traces the lines on the page, the smile slowly fading from her lips. Cassian watches her eyes, forcing down his rising unease. His voice remains as gentle as ever.

speaker: Cassian
content: In what way, madam?

speaker: Noblewoman
content: These words... they're so polished. Deliberate. Almost poetic, but not quite... What little secrets are you hiding in there?
Her gaze is mocking, but her voice is suddenly laced with ice. For a moment, the air feels like a taut wire.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: You were never this careful when you asked me to contact those little friends of yours before. If you ask me, people only use codes in their letters for one reason: they don't want others to find out.

speaker: Cassian
content: ...I don't understand what you mean.
Cassian feels his limbs turn cold. His heart sinks, yet he still tries to keep up a look of composure.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: Cassian, I've always been quite fond of you. I've been willing to turn a blind eye to your little errands. But if you really take me for a fool... well, that's not so cute.
The smile returns to her face. She reaches out to caress his chin, her thumb slowly stroking the corner of his lips. The gesture is intimate, but it sends a chill down the spine.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: And from what I recall, there's only one rule on this ship: that the service staff, like you, is not allowed to leave... So tell me, Cassian. Who are you trying to help escape?

speaker: Cassian
content: ...You must be overthinking this.
His tone is gentle, almost pleading. He doesn't push her hand away. He simply sits there, eyes downcast, as if he's making one last attempt to persuade—or deceive her.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: Oh, Cassian...

She sighs, shaking her head as she slowly rises to her feet. Looming over him, she looks like a proud predator. A lock of her hair brushes against his cheek and chest as she looks down at him, her eyes filled not with anger, but with pure, undisguised contempt.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: Even a dog knows how to show its gratitude. But you? You thought you could lie to me? Use me? Who the hell do you think you are?
She takes a step closer, her voice now sharp as claws.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: Tell me. What do you think Mr. E would do with this little note? You know all too well how he deals with wretched slaves who break his rules, don't you?
The air freezes. Slowly, Cassian finally lifts his head. In his calm eyes, a chilling cold begins to surface. His voice is soft as a breeze, but it cuts straight to the bone.

speaker: Cassian
content: ...What a shame. I didn't want it to come to this.

speaker: Noblewoman
content: What did you say?
She frowns, her gaze following his hand as his fingertips brush against the rim of the bottle.

The next second, the liquid inside roils. The aroma of wine thickens into an overwhelming, acrid scent, forming invisible tendrils that bore into her nostrils, her ears, the depths of her consciousness. The woman's face goes slack, her eyes losing focus. Like a marionette with its strings snipped, she pitches forward into the couch.
The room falls silent. Cassian stands there, his chest heaving, palms slick with cold sweat. He only awakened his ability recently, and he's far from skilled. But thankfully, it worked this time.
He bends down and retrieves the woman's communicator. He punches in a number he knows by heart, sends that crucial message, then quickly deletes the record.
The number belongs to an information broker in Eastside. The man owes him a big favor and has been helping him collect information, relay messages, and gather supplies.

The broker has a broad intelligence network. Before Cassian boarded this ship, the man had given him the frequency for a public emergency channel in the WhiteSands. "Dunno if it'd work where you're going," he'd said, "but better safe than sorry."
This time, he's asking the man to find <color=#fb9259>Theodore</color> and tell him, "<u>Sallie is trapped on Euphoria. Please come and save her.</u>"

He can't contact the man himself, because on this cruise ship, every move of the service staff is monitored. Only guests, like the noblewoman, have the freedom to communicate with the outside world and the opportunity to get word out.
After destroying the note and cleaning up the scene, he doesn't hurry to leave. Instead, he calmly begins to search her.

The woman is a prestigious guest aboard the ship, a master player of power games and a regular patron at Mr. E's private parties. Sure enough, in her concealed inner pocket, Cassian finds a silver-gray access card engraved with identification codes for the upper-level suites.

He stares at it for a couple of seconds, his lips twitching, before slipping both card and communicator into his own pocket. Finally, he carefully props the woman up into a sitting position. He picks up the knocked-over glass, refills it with wine, and gently places it back on the coffee table.

Where light meets shadow, he straightens up. The wine is still swirling slowly in his palm, glints of amber light dancing between his fingers. The woman, her mind addled by the liquid and her memory compromised, sits frozen, her eyes vacant.

speaker: Cassian
content: The wine has frayed your nerves. You won't remember what just happened. But I can't fully control this power yet, and my aim isn't great. So if you find you've forgotten something else... well, my apologies.
He turns and leaves. The wine swirls silently, settling back into the bottle.
Outside, the corridor remains unchanged, the red carpet meeting the dark night. And here, amid the unending, raucous revelry, a hidden thread has quietly come loose.

The night is intoxicating. Dazzling lights shimmer amid ceaseless indulgence. Cassian stands behind the bar as always, dressed in his pristine white shirt, cuffs perfectly pressed, his face calm. He mixes drinks, smiles, and makes small talk with flawless grace.
But sometimes, he glances up at the clock on the wall.

As midnight approaches, he quietly lifts a silver tray bearing a bottle of unlabeled wine. He crosses the red carpet, slipping into a blind spot of the banquet. This is the time window that Milly and Sallie learned from the staff; the moment when the security shifts change, patrols are thin, and the watch is lax.

He avoids the main hall, circles around the back corridor, and stops before a metal door hidden behind a gilded, carved wall. He swipes the silver keycard. It beeps softly, and the door swings open to reveal a private elevator to the upper-level suites.
He steps inside and presses the button for the top floor.
The moment the doors open, two fully armed security guards block his path.

speaker: Security Guard A
content: Stop. You're not a resident of this floor. How did you get up here?

speaker: Cassian
content: Mr. Falke ordered a bottle of wine. His usual blend. I'm here to deliver it.
Cassian holds the tray steady, his voice gentle. But the other guard steps closer, brow furrowed, warily examining his name tag and the silver tray with growing suspicion.

speaker: Security Guard B
content: We weren't notified. Turn around and leave, now. Or we have the right to—

He doesn't finish his words. With the slightest tremor of Cassian's fingers, the wine in the bottle ripples imperceptibly. A few amber strands rise from the liquid, slipping through the gaps in the cork and into the guards' nostrils. For a second, their expressions go slack, a flicker of confusion clouding their eyes.

speaker: Security Guard A
content: Right... I remember now. There was something like that. Go ahead. Make it quick.
Cassian doesn't reply. He nods quietly and steps through the space they make for him.
From around a corridor comes a stifled sob. Cassian follows the sound and sees a figure slumped on the carpet in the dim light, someone who looks remarkably like his former self...

The young nobleman, who once dominated the high society, is still wearing a gold-embroidered jacket, but his face is stained with tears. He clutches his head, choking back sobs, mumbling a name over and over with despair and humiliation.

speaker: Young Noble
content: He... he won't see me... Said I'm not worth his time... My family... we have nothing left...
The guards posted nearby pay him no mind. They're used to this scene. He isn't the first to break down here, and he won't be the last.
Cassian doesn't stop either. He spares the familiar figure one silent glance, then looks away. There is no time for sympathy, no time to dwell on the past. He has more important things to do.
He presses on, his steps firm, leaving the broken echoes and desperate struggles behind.
His control over his ability is still rough, and dealing with the security guards has drained considerable energy. A burning heat spreads through the depths of his consciousness.
He feels exhausted, yet strangely awake. The exhilarating rush of impending revenge; the power, restlessness, and craving as his mind merges with Mania.
At last, Cassian reaches the end of the corridor.

The warm glow of the sconce falls across his face, illuminating quiet, detached eyes that hide a cold, razor-sharp edge. He seems to be looking into a mirror and seeing the man he has become. Before the wreckage of his old dreams, he has finally reached the turning point of fate.
Cassian takes a deep breath. He raises his hand and knocks on the heavy, gold-trimmed door.
The show has started. The dressing room is deserted, its lights off. The door creaks open, and a figure peeks inside cautiously before tiptoeing in.

speaker: Milly
content: I was only gone for three days... and they already packed all my stuff away.

She walks to her vanity, where only a few basic makeup tools remain. Her fingertip glides across the surface, tracing a line through a thin layer of dust. Crouching down, she rummages through the drawers until, at the very back, she finds the familiar doll in the gray trench coat, and a few letters she'd written.

speaker: Milly
content: Thank goodness you're still here... Otherwise I'd really have to give Mr. E a piece of my mind.

She sits the doll in a corner of the vanity, then sets down the letters on the tabletop, next to the photograph she always carries with her. She doesn't turn on the lights; leaning against the table, she lights a small candle. Its fragile flame casts a gentle glow on this fleeting moment of peace.

speaker: Milly
content: This place hardly ever gives us time to rest... No dancing, no guests to entertain. It's nice.

speaker: Milly
content: Remember when I told you I was going to help Sallie elope? I meant it. It wasn't just some crazy idea! I even took out the creep who was hurting her. Got a few cuts myself.

speaker: Milly
content: But it's okay! It doesn't hurt anymore. Mr. E had me patched up. After all, there's a long line of guests waiting to chat with me. Hehe, it's almost embarrassing to say it out loud.
She gently traces the outline of the person in the photo, leaning close as if worried they might not hear.

speaker: Milly
content: I know Mr. E keeps us locked up here because he's afraid of us. His eyes are everywhere...

speaker: Milly
content: But even the most airtight cage has cracks, right?

speaker: Milly
content: Once I know the name of Sallie's sweetheart, I can find a way to get word out. The guests, Cassian, the staff who love to gossip... they could all be our chance.

speaker: Milly
content: Speaking of Cassian... that guy seems easygoing, but he's got his guard up. Still, I know he's waiting for his chance. As long as we want the same thing... he'll help me. I'm sure of it.

speaker: Milly
content: What do you think, darling? It's a pretty solid plan, isn't it?

speaker: Milly
content: It feels... incredible. I'm actually helping someone. I can protect someone! It makes me so happy.

speaker: Milly
content: When we see each other... will you be proud of me?
Outside, the festive music is winding down. Milly knows her rare moment of peace is over. As footsteps approach, she reluctantly stows the photo and letters and closes the drawer.

speaker: Milly
content: Oops, someone's coming... I'll talk to you later. Maybe the next time we talk, I'll have good news. Wait for me, okay?

For some people, power is a sweet burden that makes them crave the superiority to match. Laws, morals, general equality... all become sources of discontent. Deep down, they hunger to stand above the masses. Trampling on other people has lost its novelty; what they truly desire is to crush rules and reason.

And so, Euphoria became the perfect choice. After all, anyone can buy the company of celebrities and socialites in DisCity, but few have the nerve to entertain themselves with Sinners; ordinary people lack the means, or the rights. Now this is the true privilege.

Once a few of these rotten old leeches were reeled in, it was natural that a clientele eager to gain their favor would follow. Through careful dealings and a constantly grown legend, Euphoria was shaped into the fabled haven among the elites.

That's what Cassian explained, though Sallie doesn't quite understand. Not being a Sinner makes her less popular, which also leaves her free to listen in from the corners. It doesn't take long for her to pick up on something.

speaker: Guest A
content: Heh, I heard that good-for-nothing son of theirs got dumped by some woman. He's been moping at home since.

speaker: Guest A
content: We all told him to get out, have some fun. Play around with girls, sure. But a club dancer? Dude's got no standards.

speaker: Guest B
content: If you ask me, with how shaky things are right now, he should forget about the chick and focus on shoring up his connections. His family doesn't have much to their name. Who knows, they'd be back to square one any day.

speaker: Guest A
content: They might want connections, but others might not want theirs. A lot goes into marriage alliances: money, power, social circles. Can't afford to ignore any of those.

speaker: Guest B
content: Haha, well, that's what this place is for! Blow off some steam, have a little fun, and still get some real business done.

Sallie barely dares to breathe, her heart pounding. She glances at Milly, who makes an excited heart sign with her hands. She sneaks a look at Cassian. The bartender gives no outward sign, but offers the slightest of nods. So... they really are talking about Theodore?
She wants to hear more, to learn about his situation. Why did they say he was dumped. What happened?
But love affairs are too common in Eastside to warrant discussion. The conversation has already moved on.

speaker: Guest A
content: Only he has the luxury of moping about a breakup. We have bigger problems to worry about! A lot of backdoor deals got investigated after the Great Expo. My old man's terrified they'll start coming for everyone who greased Fraser's wheels at the <color=#fb9259>Sillage Society</color>.

speaker: Guest A
content: Hey, you got any inside info on that?

speaker: Guest B
content: Me? I do stocks, how would I know about that stuff? Last time I heard about... Fraser infiltrating DisCity, it was from you guys here.

speaker: Guest C
content: Shh... keep it down! You don't talk about that in the open. Walls have ears. Someone might get the dirt on you.

speaker: Guest D
content: Ha, you must be new here. Still learning the ropes, huh? Let me put it this way: this is the only safe place to talk. Euphoria's lips are sealed, and none of us here would ever rat each other out. Nobody wants to hear Mr. E say to them...

speaker: Guest D
content: "You wouldn't want word getting out about your visits here, would you?" Hahahaha! See? We're all in the same boat!

speaker: Guest A
content: Exactly. And here's some good news. I heard from <color=#fb9259>Sillage</color> that the Bureau Chief is dead! You know, the one who wouldn't stop yelling about catching traitors? The clown's gone, for real!
The lounge erupts in laughter. Sallie doesn't quite understand what they were saying, but in that moment, she feels an inexplicable chill.

In a corner of the room, as the crowd cheers for one person's death, Milly, whose smile is usually as brilliant as the sun, suddenly turns ice-cold. Her face falls into shadow, her hand clenching her wine glass. A dinner knife lies not far from her reach.
The moment sends chills down Sallie's spine. But the celebrating crowd clearly has no idea of the impending danger.

speaker: Guest A
content: You know, that dog from the 9th Agency. Got beaten half to death at the Great Expo, gone missing now. They say there's a new Black Ring—BR-005.

speaker: Guest A
content: Sillage says the Chief was linked to the Black Ring and the Mania rotted him away. Great job, Fraser. A Black Ring that big? No way he's still kicking after that.
female_content: Sillage says the Chief was linked to the Black Ring and the Mania rotted her away. Great job, Fraser. A Black Ring that big? No way she's still kicking after that.

speaker: Guest B
content: Well, that's the best news I've heard all day! Serves him right for hounding us! Come, raise your glass, my friends! It's time to celebrate!
female_content: Well, that's the best news I've heard all day! Serves her right for hounding us! Come, raise your glass, my friends! It's time to celebrate!

content: Bang—
The sound that follows isn't the clear clink of a toast, but the explosive crack of shattering glass.
Rather than raising her glass in toast, Milly crushes it in her grip. The blood-red liquid runs through her fingers, dripping slowly to the floor.

speaker: Guest B
content: What the hell?! What's your problem?!
The festive atmosphere is shattered. All eyes turn toward the disturbance, the air suddenly tense.
Sallie turns at the sound and stares into a face pale as death. Milly's eyes are vacant but sharp. She's ready to tear apart everything in her sight.
Dropping the shattered glass, she snatches the dinner knife. Her shoulders tense, coiling to lunge into the crowd.
Without time to think, Sallie throws herself forward and wraps her arms tightly around Milly.

speaker: Sallie
content: It's nothing. She's just... so excited, she got a little carried away... broke her glass and cut her hand. I'll take her to get it cleaned up.

speaker: Sallie
content: Milly, you've had too much to drink... Come on, let's step outside for some air, okay?

speaker: Sallie
content: <size=30>I know you're hurting, but this isn't the time to break down... Please, not here. Don't let them see you like this.</size>
She turns to Milly, speaking in a hushed whisper while reaching out to grip Milly's wrists, shielding the knife in Milly's right hand with her body.

speaker: Sallie
content: Please, Milly. For my sake... okay?

They stand locked together for a moment. Finally, with a tremble through her shoulders, Milly's clenched fingers slowly loosen. The knife slips from her grasp and clatters to the floor with a sharp, cold clang.

speaker: Cassian
content: Just a minor accident. Please, don't let it spoil your evening.

speaker: Guest B
content: Tsk... Get her out of here! Totally ruined the mood.
Cassian steps out from behind the bar to calm the startled guests, positioning himself between Milly and the crowd.
Meanwhile, under the cover of the other dancers, Sallie helps Milly get away from the scene.
The ship's doctor bandages Milly's hand before sending Sallie back to work. Sallie wants to stay, but can't find an excuse.

Milly doesn't look like she wants to talk. For the first time, the woman always as bright as the sun has lost all traces of her smile. Her eyes are vacant, like a gaping abyss. She sits stiffly in the dressing room, quiet and still, in a space filled with a cold, dead silence.

There's no way she can work like this. The doctor seems ready to report her condition. Sallie paces anxiously, slipping away when she finds a chance. She runs into Cassian at the doorway. They gaze at Milly, who still sits frozen, lost in a black hole of time.

speaker: Sallie
content: What's... the matter with her?

speaker: Sallie
content: You and Milly go way back. You must know something. Why don't you fill me in? So I can comfort her...

speaker: Cassian
content: You're worried about her?
Sallie gives him a withering look. Cassian shows no hint of mockery; he only toys with his finger chain in silence.
After a few seconds, he finally relents.

speaker: Cassian
content: You know Milly has a lover, right?
Of course she knows. The man who holds a special place in Milly's heart... her hero, her love, her dream.
female_content: Of course she knows. The woman who holds a special place in Milly's heart... her hero, her love, her dream.

speaker: Sallie
content: Why are you bringing that up? Don't tell me...
Then it dawns on Sallie: he's the subject of the guests' gossip—the MBCC Chief.
female_content: Then it dawns on Sallie: she's the subject of the guests' gossip—the MBCC Chief.

speaker: Cassian
content: In a place like this, you have to find something to hold onto. If you don't, you'll go insane, or turn into some mindless beast they have to put down.

speaker: Cassian
content: It's not my place to tell Milly's story. We all came here for different reasons, but we meet the same end...
He pauses, his gaze drifting down the long hallway.

speaker: Cassian
content: You think she's an idiot, don't you?

speaker: Sallie
content: Well... at first I did, but now I...

speaker: Cassian
content: It's fine. She is an idiot. She was sold to the lowest rungs of the Syndicate.
Fear runs through Sallie as she remembers her own ordeal in Eastside. Milly, then... Cassian could see what she's thinking.

speaker: Cassian
content: In the Syndicate, she was another face in the muck. No one cared what she looked like. It wasn't until she got here that Mr. E spent the money and time to dress her up into what you see now.

speaker: Cassian
content: See that blond hair? To the gang, Milly was just a good luck charm. They bought her for good fortune, dragged her to every business deal, called her a Sinner who could bring wealth. And when they didn't get rich, they beat the hell out of her.

speaker: Cassian
content: She tried to run many times. Each time, they dragged her back and beat her worse. Eventually, she couldn't run anymore, just survived on her sad, B-class ability. Back then, all she could do was numb those who touched her, so they wouldn't hit her quite as hard.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...So that's why she loves that person so much. The hero of Syndicate. But that place has been liberated. How did she end up here...?

speaker: Cassian
content: Some people are just born unlucky. That's all there is to it.
They fall silent.

speaker: Cassian
content: Right before the West District was fully liberated, before she could finally be free... the gang sold her off to the desert bandits for one last score.

speaker: Cassian
content: Later, Mr. E found her when he was going around looking for weak Sinners. He bought her cheap, grew her talent... and turned her into the Jewel of Euphoria.

speaker: Cassian
content: The reason she's held on this long... is probably because in those dark Syndicate days, she really did see a hero.
Backstage, Sallie gently knocks on the door before stepping inside. She finds Milly, who's curled up in a ball, and crouches down beside her.

speaker: Sallie
content: Milly... were you crying?

speaker: Sallie
content: It's just hearsay. It might not even be true. Maybe it's just a rumor the Chief put out to throw them off.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...Do you really love him that much? You've never even met, or spent any time together.
female_content: ...Do you really love her that much? You've never even met, or spent any time together.

speaker: Milly
content: We did meet once...
Milly finally speaks, her voice slow and choked with tears.

speaker: Milly
content: He's good. He's great. He's the best person I've ever met.
female_content: She's good. She's great. She's the best person I've ever met.

speaker: Milly
content: Everything I'm doing here... is so I could be by his side. I want to be like him. I want to become a good person, like he is.
female_content: Everything I'm doing here... is so I could be by her side. I want to be like her. I want to become a good person, like she is.

speaker: Milly
content: If he's gone...
female_content: If she's gone...

content: Milly's voice trembles as she trails off. Sallie grasps her hand, trying to give her strength.

speaker: Sallie
content: You're already a good person, Milly.

speaker: Sallie
content: You've been helping me this whole time, haven't you? Where I used to work, back in Eastside, the girls always said to watch out for love. That it can make you lose yourself, make you think you can't live without someone.

speaker: Sallie
content: But that's not true. You can live without anyone. When one person leaves, another one will come along to love you. At least... in here, I really, really want you to be okay.

speaker: Sallie
content: You were going to help me escape, remember? When we get out of here together, so many more people will love you. You'll see a bigger world, sing on bigger stages!

speaker: Milly
content: A bigger world...?

speaker: Milly
content: What do you mean?

speaker: Sallie
content: Huh?

speaker: Milly
content: He's the best person in the world. I don't need anything else.
female_content: She's the best person in the world. I don't need anything else.

speaker: Sallie
content: What if he never comes? Are you just going to wait forever? What if he really is dea—
female_content: What if she never comes? Are you just going to wait forever? What if she really is dea—

content: Milly's grip tightens on the gray doll, and Sallie cuts herself off. After a long silence, Milly speaks quietly.

speaker: Milly
content: That won't happen...
[Footsteps]

speaker: Cassian
content: Don't bother. Mr. E is much better at brainwashing than you are. He's been filling her head with nonsense for years to keep her under his control.
Cassian is leaning against the doorway.

speaker: Cassian
content: She didn't have your luck. She never went to school, never saw the world outside. What you're talking about... are things reserved for the fortunate.

speaker: Cassian
content: Those born unfortunate can't even see the path to change their fate.
He walks closer and crouches down, so Milly can look directly into his eyes.

speaker: Cassian
content: Milly, I have good news. You'll want to hear this.

speaker: Cassian
content: I've found Theodore's address. Unfortunately, he's away on a trip. But he's expected to be back in two weeks.
He turns to look at Sallie.

speaker: Cassian
content: Wait a little longer. When he's back, I'll let him know you were sold to this place. I'll arrange a meeting.

speaker: Milly
content: ...Really?
A glimmer of light shines in Milly's eyes. Even in her grief, she still feels happy for her friend.

speaker: Milly
content: Did you hear that, Sallie? Your love is coming for you. He's going to save you from this place.

speaker: Cassian
content: It's true. Everything will be alright. And your love will be fine, too.

speaker: Cassian
content: Good people don't die that easily, right?

speaker: Milly
content: Ah... that's right... I can't stay down in the dumps forever. Sallie needs me. I have to pull myself together!
She pushes herself to her feet and pats her cheeks. Her pale face brightens with that brilliant smile again, just like when she takes the stage.

speaker: Milly
content: Come on, Sallie. We still have a lot to do.

speaker: Milly
content: Don't you worry about a thing. Trust Cassian. And trust me, okay? Mr. E won't do anything to me. The worst he can do is lock me up for a little while.

speaker: Sallie
content: But then you'll be all alone...

speaker: Milly
content: It's okay. Waiting isn't hard.
She cuts Sallie off, as if to bolster her own courage.

speaker: Milly
content: ...It's not so hard, when you have something to believe in.
The show waits for no one, certainly not for Sallie and Milly's plan.

Milly is in an awful state. Mr. E's doctors patched her up, but it was only a surface-level fix. Her skin looks flawless, but the damage to her bones and muscles remains. Her movements lack their usual grace. Her balance is off, her gaze distant. She can't even spot properly in her turns.
Right now, her mind is consumed with worry for ${PlayerName}. Though she tries to act like nothing's wrong, her body can't lie.

speaker: Snow
content: What's wrong with Milly today? Don't tell me she's throwing the show to give us a chance.

speaker: Magician
content: Aren't you always looking for more clients? Go on, steal her spot. Get a taste of what it's like to be the star. This is your big chance.
The performers waiting in the wings jostle and taunt. In the restless backstage, Sallie watches Milly's strained smile from behind the curtain and can't help but feel worried.
...If I don't do something, things are going to end badly.
[Begin Battle]
Sallie strides onto the stage. Instead of heading for the champagne tower, she claps her hands, signaling for the spotlight to find her. In an instant, she covers for Milly's mistake.

The lights dim; the audience gasps in surprise. The spotlight fixates on her, drawing all eyes like when she fell on that first night. But this time, Sallie doesn't panic. She walks to the center of the stage, breaking from the routine. A spin, a flick of her hair. She moves with sharp precision.

Her dance is fierce, sensual. Each step slashes through the air like claws. Whistles and applause begin to rise from the crowd. Meanwhile, Milly regains her composure and slips back into position. The show continues without a hitch.

speaker: Selene
content: Nice save.
As she passes Selene, even the resident ice queen offers a quiet compliment. Miracles do happen.

speaker: Magician
content: ...Hmph, show-off.
The Magician scoffs, but her action betrays her words as she quickly adjusts her moves to match Sallie's lead. It almost looks like... she's enjoying herself.
I changed the dance routine... I just hope Mr. E isn't watching...
Well, at least Milly's safe. I covered for her. That's all that matters, right?

The joy of helping her friend and the thrill of the long-missed applause fill her with happiness. She used to fantasize about moments like this back in Eastside: earning respect with her own skill. Back then, she'd bow to the audience. So out of habit, Sallie looks toward the crowd. In the next second, she freezes.

At the edge of a distant booth sits a man without a mask. He's surrounded by leering dandies, their arms slung around his shoulders. Everyone at that table is roaring with raucous laughter. Despite the dim lights and noisy crowd, Sallie recognizes that face instantly.

speaker: Sallie
content: Theodore?!
The moment their eyes meet, Sallie's movement falters. He recognizes her, too. Of course he does. How many times has he looked up at her on a stage like this?
Thump thump. Her heart hammers. She'd imagined Theodore might come, but not this soon.
Did he get word ahead of time? Did he come all this way for her? How did he convince his family?
Fireworks explode in Sallie's mind, filling her with joy.

speaker: Sallie
content: Idiot... you idiot... I...
But the touching reunion never comes. As Theodore snaps out of his shock, his first instinct is to whip his head away, avoiding her gaze, almost like he's about to flee.
It isn't the joy of seeing a lover again. It's the shock on Merlot's face when his mask was torn off. The panic of a dark, vile sin being dragged into the light. It's fear. Shame. Guilt.
It is not love.
Cold reality crashes over Sallie like ice.

speaker: Cassian
content: I've found Theodore's address. Unfortunately, he's away on a trip. But he's expected to be back in two weeks.

speaker: Cassian
content: Wait a little longer. When he's back, I'll let him know you were sold to this place. I'll arrange a meeting.

speaker: Sallie
content: That's right. He hasn't gotten the message yet. He couldn't have known I'm here. He didn't come to save me. Then... what is he doing here?

speaker: Sallie
content: He's a patron, of course! Just like everyone else here. Like that bastard in the mask! He's an honored guest on this ship. He's here to have his fun with me!

speaker: Sallie
content: Haha... I'm the fool... I'm the real fool!
The music doesn't stop. The show goes on.
Sallie's dance turns staccato. She grinds her hips, turns, teasing the guests below. Her eyes nail Theodore to his spot; that coward doesn't even have the courage to look up.

speaker: Sallie
content: See, Milly? Love is so foolish! How did I ever believe in such lies?
On stage, Sallie unleashes all the anxiety and fear she'd felt since being brought to this place. Her arms fly open, tearing threads in the air, like breaking free from unseen chains.
As the music draws to a close, a bitter smile appears on Sallie's lips. On the final note, she slams her fist into the stage, striking out the end to her love story.

speaker: Sallie
content: Milly was wrong. It was never true love... it was just some small-town dancer who didn't know her place!

The lights dim, and the room erupts in cheers. Sallie throws her head back, shoulders heaving as she gasps for breath over her racing heartbeat. Her eyes scan the audience... but the familiar figure is already gone.
The curtain slowly falls to thunderous applause. Sallie can't remember how she made it off the stage.
[Event]

Sallie stumbles back into the dressing room on unsteady feet. Milly and Cassian are already there, waiting to discuss the next steps of their plan. Sallie's spirits are crushed, a bitter anger simmering in her heart.

speaker: Cassian
content: You shouldn't have done that. Drawing attention from Mr. E and the guests does us no good.

speaker: Milly
content: Don't blame Sallie, it was my fault. She had to step in because I messed up.
Milly scratches her cheek sheepishly. Despite her low mood, she tries to perk herself up to defend Sallie.

speaker: Milly
content: And it's not all bad. At least Sallie won't be bullied anymore. Mr. E protects the ones who are popular.

speaker: Cassian
content: That's irrelevant. The problem is, once you're noticed, it becomes much harder to escape.

speaker: Cassian
content: In any case, you two can't afford any more complications. We need to get Sallie out of here as soon as possible. Let's move the plan up.

speaker: Cassian
content: There's been a mysterious fleet lurking nearby. I've hidden a small boat on the muster deck that can make short trips. Once we're out of here, we can try slipping into that group. Even if they're desert bandits...

speaker: Sallie
content: It won't work. I... I'm not going.
Sallie, who had been silent until now, speaks in a hoarse, exhausted voice. Her words shock the other two.

speaker: Sallie
content: Think about it. The guests, all masked and covered up... what Mr. E said when he threatened you... all the unspeakable things they discuss...

speaker: Sallie
content: I get it now... From the moment we were sold here, dancers like us were never meant to leave alive. That's why they can be so reckless... why they can speak so freely about those things.

speaker: Sallie
content: So don't waste your time. Staying here isn't so bad, is it? I've made a place for myself. I'll probably have a good life here. Haha, maybe Euphoria is about to have its second Jewel?

speaker: Milly
content: Don't say that!

speaker: Milly
content: Mr. E promised me before, that if my love came for me, he'd let me go. It's the same for you, Sallie! Once Theodore comes for you, Mr. E will let you leave.

speaker: Sallie
content: Theodore? Come for me? Hehehe...
She leans her head against the wall, her body shaking with a low laughter. It goes on and on, until her hair falls over her face, leaving only a grin that keeps stretching.
Finally, she stops, tired from her laughter.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...There's no need to wait. He's already here.

speaker: Milly
content: ...He's here?
Milly looks at Cassian, bewildered. Cassian is clearly taken aback, but when he sees Sallie's bowed head and hears the spite in her voice, his expression turns grave.

speaker: Sallie
content: Shocking, right? Hehe, he's here. I saw him, and he saw me. He wasn't wearing a mask. Probably a new guest who doesn't know the rules. Haha. I wish you could've seen the look on his face...

speaker: Sallie
content: So ugly... I've never seen such a wretched face. Why do you think he looked that way? Because his former lover had sunk to this place? Or...

speaker: Sallie
content: ...because he knows how shameful it is, coming to a place like this to get his kicks? I wonder if he's scrambling to find a mask right now. Haha...

speaker: Sallie
content: He's not here to save me. He's here to have fun. Just like every other guest here. Like that masked bastard. They're all the same, scumbags!

speaker: Sallie
content: Milly, you told me that if we found him, he would get me out of here. That we could be together. And I believed you.

speaker: Sallie
content: Well, we've found him. What do you think he'll do? Profess his love for me with a straight face? Or just kill me to shut me up? A lowly dancer like me... must be a real embarrassment to him here, right?

speaker: Milly
content: Sallie...
Milly reaches to take her hands. They're as cold as ice.

speaker: Milly
content: M-maybe there's some kind of misunderstanding? Should we find a chance to talk to him first?

speaker: Milly
content: You said he's here? I'll go find him right now! I'll set up a time for him to meet you.
Sallie laughs even harder. She stares at her new "friend."

speaker: Sallie
content: A shadow casts over Labyrinth the vacuum from behind. A fuzzy furball tiptoes over, with apparent interest in the cleaning robot.

speaker: Sallie
content: You heard it too, that day. For new rich families like his, the only way up is through connections and resources. Before they establish themselves, they won't let anything drag them down.

speaker: Sallie
content: And me? What can I possibly give him? I'm just a nobody stuck in the wings, drowning in debt, with no connections and a tattered reputation. The gap between us isn't something a love letter can bridge.

speaker: Sallie
content: Roarrrr!

speaker: Sallie
content: I was an idiot! Caught the fancy of a rich boy, lost my job, got loan sharks on my tail. He said he'd do everything to make me happy. Haha...

speaker: Sallie
content: And then? He vanished. Where was he when I ended up in this hellhole? Did he come here to save me?

speaker: Sallie
content: It's pathetic...

speaker: Sallie
content: It was so obvious, and I pretended not to see. I knew this world was rotten to the core, full of scheming and deceit, yet I still fell for his lies!

speaker: Sallie
content: Why did I ever think he would come for me? Why would I think he's any different from all those beasts in human skin?

speaker: Sallie
content: And the most pathetic one of all is me. Milly, I actually let your stupid nonsense about true love get to me... I actually thought I could escape this place!

speaker: Sallie
content: And now? Reality slapped me right in the face.

speaker: Sallie
content: To hell with true love! To hell with light!

speaker: Sallie
content: I thought I was rational. Realistic. But I still went along with your charade. Haha. What a joke.

speaker: Milly
content: Sallie!
As her tirade goes on, Sallie is on the verge of a breakdown. Milly rushes forward and throws her arms around her, holding her as she starts to sway.

speaker: Milly
content: You should still go see him. You're different from me. You and Theodore dated. You should know what kind of person he is better than anyone. You're so smart, you wouldn't be so easily fooled, right?

speaker: Milly
content: Go ask him. This is a rare chance to see him again. Even if it's just to see him for who he truly is.
Milly's attempts at comfort does nothing to ease the tension. Sallie slowly looks up and smiles mockingly.

speaker: Sallie
content: I really envy you... Milly, you're even dumber than I am.
Milly is taken aback. Cassian realizes what Sallie's about to say and steps forward, trying to put himself between the girls.

speaker: Cassian
content: Sallie.
Sallie ignores him. Shoving him aside, she keeps her eyes on Milly. She grabs Milly's wrists and pulls her close.

speaker: Sallie
content: You never went to school, did you? Never saw the outside world, right? Well, let me tell you.

speaker: Sallie
content: Did you know, Milly? Out there... in Eastside, in DisCity, love is the dumbest joke there is. All that talk about love and destiny... it's all lies. There's no such thing as love at first sight.

speaker: Sallie
content: That's not a fairy tale. It's a script designed to fool people, just like the act you put on onstage.

speaker: Sallie
content: What is love, really? It's a hormonal impulse, a hit of dopamine, a fantasy painted out of loneliness. Tell you the right story, feed you the right lines, and you could mistake a devil for an angel.

speaker: Sallie
content: And they love girls like you who are desperate to be loved. So easy to trick. So easy to tame. And once you're tamed, they can use you for a long, long time.

speaker: Sallie
content: You know how disgusting they are. Why else would you use that lip balm to protect yourself?
Milly tries to speak, but Sallie cuts her off harshly.
She can't stop. She won't stop. Her eyes are bloodshot, her grip tightening on Milly's wrists.

speaker: Sallie
content: Tell me, Milly, has Mr. E ever told you that to love someone is to sacrifice everything for them? That they're the best thing in your life, that you should satisfy their every need, that their happiness is your happiness?

speaker: Sallie
content: That's what your boss told me when he made me serve the guests. That's what the masked bastard meant when he put a collar on me and told me to be his dog!

speaker: Sallie
content: This so-called love is just another way of getting you to pretty yourself up and serve yourself on a platter for someone else's amusement!

speaker: Sallie
content: Even if your Chief shows up one day, do you really think he's here to take you away? Don't be so naive. Does anyone good ever come to this place?
female_content: Even if your Chief shows up one day, do you really think she's here to take you away? Don't be so naive. Does anyone good ever come to this place?

speaker: Sallie
content: He's here for the show, for a new thrill. He's no different from Theodore, or any other masked scumbag on this ship. They're all just assholes, getting off on feeling like gods!
female_content: She's here for the show, for a new thrill. She's no different from Theodore, or any other masked scumbag on this ship. They're all just assholes, getting off on feeling like gods!

speaker: Milly
content: He's not like that!
female_content: She's not like that!

speaker: Sallie
content: And how would you know? You don't even know if he's dead or alive!
female_content: And how would you know? You don't even know if she's dead or alive!

content: A deathly silence fills the room.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...It's pathetic. Pinning all your hopes on someone who probably doesn't even remember your name. You read a few newspaper stories and thought he's a hero. Idiot.
female_content: ...It's pathetic. Pinning all your hopes on someone who probably doesn't even remember your name. You read a few newspaper stories and thought she's a hero. Idiot.

speaker: Sallie
content: Those with money and power can make the press say black is white. In the papers, anyone can be a hero. You don't know him at all. All you want is a hero who can save you. As long as they say a few sweet words and beckon at you, you'd come running and wagging your tail, even if it were some petty bum.
female_content: Those with money and power can make the press say black is white. In the papers, anyone can be a hero. You don't know her at all. All you want is a hero who can save you. As long as they say a few sweet words and beckon at you, you'd come running and wagging your tail, even if it were some petty bum.

speaker: Sallie
content: What you love is nothing more than a fantasy. You love the fairy tale where you're saved, and the idea of yourself, waiting faithfully for your savior. The person you confide in, the person you adore... it's always been a delusion living in your head. And here you need to help me elope, just to prove your "true love conquers all" bullshit?

speaker: Sallie
content: Stop being an idiot! When that man finds out and comes to you with a gun in his hand, will true love keep you alive? Does this rotten world even allow for such miracles?!

speaker: Sallie
content: No, it doesn't... Only you are stupid enough to believe that there are still good people in this goddamn world. To think that people like us still have hope. Only you refuse to see reality.

speaker: Sallie
content: We've fallen this far, and you think you can just plug your ears, shut your eyes, and find happiness by believing in love? Well, good for you. Go on, keep it up!

speaker: Sallie
content: Only idiots can still smile here. Cling to your precious love and rot away on this ship, for the rest of your life!
Sallie's voice rings through the room. Milly hears every word. What is the expression on her face?
That face, usually bright with a radiant smile, has frozen like wax. Silent, Milly simply looks at Sallie, staring directly into her eyes.

speaker: Milly
content: Are those words... really for me?
Sallie doesn't answer. Maybe she has nothing left to say. Maybe in the next second, the Sinner before her will pull out that delicate dagger of hers and plunge it into Sallie's chest.
But Milly doesn't do that.

speaker: Milly
content: If letting go of unnecessary love will keep you safe from suffering... then I want you to find happiness. I want you to never be hurt again.

speaker: Milly
content: But that's not for me.

speaker: Milly
content: I don't care.
She looks away and stands up. A knock comes at the door.

speaker: Host
content: Milly, Mr. E wants to see you.
Milly walks past Cassian and straight out the door. She doesn't look back.

Sallie has said everything she needs to say. She leans against the wall, arms crossed. The fierce emotions drain away, leaving a vast, joyless emptiness. She can't even manage a laugh; only numb, quiet despair remains.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...Elopement is off. I won't see Theodore. I don't need your help. It's not worth it.

speaker: Sallie
content: Love isn't worth it at all...
Sallie's words hang in the air, a bitter punchline to a cruel farce, mocking herself and everything else.
The dressing room falls silent. Only Cassian and Sallie are left. The dim yellow light falls on the peeling paint, like hardened old wounds.

speaker: Cassian
content: You were taking your anger out on her. You know it.
Sallie doesn't respond. She stares at the floor, devoid of all emotion. After a long time, she speaks in a low voice.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...Don't worry about me anymore. Don't take the risk.

speaker: Sallie
content: If you help someone escape... you'll get yourself killed. That man won't hesitate to do that.

speaker: Sallie
