content: Thanks to your reputation and Furor's, we got some refugees out, but most are still stuck in the camps. They've been under Fraser's thumb for years. When the real conflict breaks out, who knows where their loyalty will land.
Horo looks over her shoulder, where the refugees who evacuated with them are setting up camp.

speaker: Horo
content: The Legion's stretched thin, and calling for backup from DisCity would take a while. Can you sabotage the detonation from inside?

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...It would be challenging. I attempted to reach out to my colleagues within the institute, but none have responded. I fear they may be confined, just as I was.

Horo remains quiet, watching the sun's dying light paint the dunes blood-red. Decision time approaches. Without shelter, her hardened Legion members might endure the night, but the refugees and wounded would freeze to death when temperatures plunge after dark.
Likely sensing Horo's hesitation, a weary sigh breaks through the communicator's static.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...And Hella? How is she doing now?
[Black Screen Transition]
At this moment, Hella stands atop a sand dune, her eyes fixed on the distant research institute complex.

The thin blanket wrapped around her does little to shield against the biting evening wind. Gusts threaten to tear it away, but Hella pays no mind. The cold is a relief, cooling her overheated thoughts.
Beneath her feet, barely visible sketches sprawl across the sand. Crooked lines link scattered words, helping her piece together clarity.

speaker: Hella
content: Thinking... sometimes matters more than a tough fist...
She murmurs the words ${PlayerName} had left her before she departed MBCC, then picks up a branch to resume drawing in the sand.
She may never match ${PlayerName}'s skill, but all that time spent with that dummy taught her something: how to analyze, how to strategize.
Hella tightens her grip on the branch and begins sketching again.

speaker: Hella
content: Just like ${PlayerName} said... the weak have their own ways of fighting...

speaker: Hella
content: There must still be something... something I can do...!
[Enter thinking screen, center text, with Hella's voiceover.]

The Aurum Secretum Institute has two underground levels. The first one's a maze, and the second one's their main experiment site. The "Cocoon" formed by the inheritance is still growing. When the time comes, that thing and Synex are gonna... trigger the Black Ring down there.
So to stop this whole disaster, we've gotta either wreck the Cocoon or drag Synex outta there.
First problem: the refugees and those Aurum Secretum devices... Tons of refugees, but at least they're easy to trick. Shouldn't be too hard...
The branch drops down as she scrawls "trick away" next to "refugees" in crooked letters.
Then there are the institute's own guards. Not a lot of them, but they're tough as nails and total jerks to fight.
...Maybe the Legion could help keep them busy? But do we even have enough people? Ugh, a straight-up attack's still way too risky, isn't it...
Okay, fine, let's say we somehow bust past the outer guards, then we've gotta deal with Synex's underground maze, which means another brutal fight...
...GAAAAH! Synex, you absolute idiot! Who builds a death trap like this?! You're literally making it impossible for me to save your dumb ass!

speaker: Thani
content: Hella? What are you drawing?

speaker: Hella
content: ...I'm trying to figure out how to get Synex out.

speaker: Thani
content: Then... let us help!

speaker: Hella
content: You?
Hella turns around and sees the refugees standing behind Thani.

speaker: Thani
content: Hella, even after everything you told us about the Aurum Secretum experiments... we still think of Synex as our <color=#fb9259>hero</color>.

speaker: Thani
content: It's not because she got to live the life we all wished for... but because even when things were so, so painful, she still found the strength to fight back.

speaker: Thani
content: We... we might not be strong, but we won't let anyone throw our lives away like they don't matter! Our lives belong to us, and we'll protect them ourselves!

speaker: Hella
content: You guys... Alright, let's figure this out together!
[Return to scene, background change, small avatar mode]

speaker: Hella
content: Synex and the inheritance are both at the very bottom of the institute, but we'd have to fight through too many security levels to get there. We don't have the numbers or the guns for that kind of suicide mission.

speaker: Thani
content: Hmm... With all these refugees crowding the ground level and guards at every turn... If only there was a way to get straight through to the bottom floor...

speaker: Refugee
content: There is one, Thani! Don't you remember? There's a path that goes straight inside.

speaker: Thani
content: Eh?

speaker: Hella
content: Ahhh...!

speaker: Hella
content: That Aurum Secretum pipeline!!
[Black Screen Transition]

speaker: Horo
content: Alright. I'll let her know.
As Horo tucks away her communicator, she glances up just in time to see Hella hurtling down the crest of a sand dune, diving straight for her.

speaker: Hella
content: Horo! I figured it out!

speaker: Hella
content: Synex was totally right! We gotta make some serious noise! Like, something so big it drags everyone in!

speaker: Horo
content: Wait, what are you talking about—
Horo opens her mouth to tell her to calm down, but the words die on her lips as she sees the fire reignited in Hella's eyes.

speaker: Hella
content: Come with me! You gotta hear this plan!
Hella pulls Horo along as they head up the sand dune.

speaker: Horo
content: These are...

The sand sprawled with vast, intricate drawings. Though the artist's strokes still hold a childlike roughness, each mark bears the weight of deliberate effort—every line distinct, every shape painstakingly formed.

speaker: Hella
content: Synex, the inheritance, all those refugees and test subjects underground... They've got way too much under their thumb. Even with the Legion's strength, there's no way just a few of us can take them head-on.

speaker: Hella
content: Just like back in Syndicate...

Hella shares stories from her time in Syndicate. The Drifter Camp, BR-002, the new mine... She's known it for years: the weak aren't powerless. Even ordinary hands can clutch blades. Even ordinary voices can roar.

speaker: Hella
content: Look, I know I'm not strong enough alone. One person can't win every fight. One person can't save everyone... But that's fine!

speaker: Hella
content: If one can't do it, we bring two! If two can't, then we drag in everybody! We'll throw all our strength together and turn this place upside down!

speaker: Hella
content: Everyone's got something to give. Every little bit counts! The more chaos we stir up, the more cracks we'll find to hit them where it hurts!

speaker: Hella
content: Like this... and then that! That'll handle the outer refugees and guards. Then all we need's a strike team to slip into the research institute mid-chaos... preferably someone who's already been in there...

speaker: Hella
content: So, what do you think? Don't tell me you're gonna back out now.
Horo sees it. The gleam of determination burning in Hella's eyes.

No one notices the exact moment it happens, but now they stand together—Legion members, refugees, allies old and new—all drawn to Hella and Horo's side. These are the people they've fought for, the ones who've fought beside them. Now, they are more than a crowd; they are their strength.
No matter how weak she seems, no matter how hard she's struck, Hella always rises—swift, stubborn, unbroken. This is the Hella Horo knows.
Somehow, that crafty troublemaker from Syndicate has become something extraordinary. A spark that ignites, a force that unites.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Heh.
She still calls herself weak, but isn't this the proof?

speaker: Hella
content: You'll come with me, right, Horo?
Horo grins, reaching out to push Hella's head down and ruffle her hair vigorously.

speaker: Horo
content: Of course. "Back out" isn't in the Legion's vocabulary.

speaker: Horo
content: Since you've already made up your mind, the Legion will be there with you—

speaker: Horo
content: So become the spearhead, Hella.
[Background - Refugee Camp, Overcast]

June 25, N.F. 115
3:41 PM

Vicinity of the Aurum Secretum Institute, Farlands

Inside the refugee camp, armed institute guards brandish their weapons as they herd people toward the central clearing. The only road leading to the research institute is a heavily fortified gauntlet of checkpoints, nearly impassable.
The crowd stirs with restless fear, murmuring among themselves but too terrified to resist.
Then, a scream shatters the silence.
—Ahhh! A monster! A monster's coming!
The cry lands like a detonation, sending shockwaves through the camp. Chaos erupts—shouts, scrambling bodies—and suddenly, a mass of robed refugees, faces hidden, surge toward the guards.

Fear's fragile dam breaks. Panic ignites, and the crowd stampedes toward the institute's entrance, a thrashing tide of bodies. Guards bellow orders, but their voices drown in the frenzy. Within seconds, they're swallowed by the human storm.

speaker: Institute Guard
content: Stop... stop right there! Hands up!
But in the swirling chaos, orders are lost to the wind. The crowd surges forward, unstoppable. The guards exchange grim glances, then the metallic click of rifles being cocked echoes through the air.

speaker: Institute Guard
content: What the hell do you think you're—ugh?!
A dull thwack cuts him off mid-sentence. His body stiffens, then crumples backward like a felled tree. The attacker tosses aside the wooden stick, exhaling sharply.

speaker: Thani
content: Hup! Sweet dreams, Mr. Guard.
Thani glances back, just in time to see the other team vanish into the institute's entrance, swallowed by the pandemonium.

Three Hours Ago

Outskirts of Fraser City, Farlands

speaker: Horo
content: You... drew all this?

speaker: Hella
content: Not by myself. Everyone helped!
Hella waves a tree branch, pointing to a circular pattern at the bottom of the sand map.

speaker: Hella
content: This is our target—the core laboratory located on the bottom level. The inheritance and Synex should both be there.

speaker: Hella
content: We can sneak through the drainage pipes. They'll take us straight from outside the city right into the maze on the first underground level. That way, we dodge the refugees and the guards on the surface.

speaker: Hella
content: The maze has always been Synex's turf. She stashed something deep inside, a "contingency plan" that can disrupt the ritual. We've gotta find it fast, and once we do, we go straight to the core area—

speaker: Hella
content: Break Synex's chains and smash the inheritance to pieces!
Horo doesn't answer right away. Instead, she takes the tree branch from Hella's grip before leaning over the map. With deliberate strokes, she circles several junctions connecting the areas.

speaker: Horo
content: The institute won't leave those checkpoints unguarded. You got a plan to handle them?

speaker: Thani
content: L-leave it to us! We deal with those people every day, so this bit of trouble is nothing new!

speaker: Hella
content: Yep! Thani and the others will keep the guards busy while we handle things inside the maze!

speaker: Hella
content: And once we hit the core, we'll have Synex backing us up! She'll be a strong ally for sure!

speaker: Horo
content: Synex's defense map shows heavy guard presence underground too. At this critical stage, security will be at its peak. Can we really enter the core area in one piece?

speaker: Hypatia
content: You're overestimating their combat capability.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Once evacuation begins, living personnel will be replaced by Aurum Secretum automatons. You just need to destroy the core receiver to disrupt their command signals and disable them entirely.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I've modified Hella's communicator with a special function. Once destroyed, it will emit a pulse disabling all Aurum Secretum receivers within twenty meters. Use it when necessary.

speaker: Hypatia
content: As for me...
With a skillful drift, Hypatia steers the sports car onto a different road.

speaker: Hypatia
content: BR-005 involves more than just the institute. The Campbell family and Fraser Senate stand behind it. If complications arise, they would undoubtedly summon reinforcements.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'll sever communications between Fraser and the research institute, cutting off their final recourse.

speaker: Horo
content: I have one last question.

speaker: Horo
content: What exactly is Synex's "contingency plan"? And how sure are we that it can actually stop the ritual?

speaker: Hella
content: Well... honestly I don't really get it either, but...

speaker: Hella
content: No plan ever goes perfectly anyway! Didn't Synex say she likes how I stir up trouble? Well, I'll give her a show she won't forget!
Back underground, half the maze's barriers have collapsed since their last visit. Hella and the Legion weave swiftly through the wreckage, making straight for the center.
Performance 1
Performance 2

speaker: Horo
content: What's... happening? The alchemic beasts are attacking the guards?

Aurum Secretum mechanical guards lie strewn across the ground, smashed aside by the rampaging monsters. The creatures claw open their armored husks, feasting on the glowing Aurum Secretum cores within.

speaker: Hella
content: So this is the "contingency plan" she left me? Gotta admit, it's pretty damn clever!
Before she can say more, a deafening roar echoes from the depths of the maze.
Roarrrr—

The ground heaves. From the abyssal dark, a monstrosity of impossible scale erupts. It swings a razor-sharp blade, splintering upon each strike, only to be reforged by Mania. The sheer force rips at the seams of reality.

speaker: Horo
content: Hella! Is this also a part of her "contingency plan"?!
Despite feeling the ground trembling beneath her feet, Hella breaks into an excited grin.

speaker: Hella
content: This big guy definitely wasn't around before! If Synex went through the trouble of unleashing it...

speaker: Hella
content: This thing must be it!
[Background - Core Testing Site]
Saffar frowns. It's too quiet. The silence prickles at his instincts—something is wrong. Beyond his grasp, events twist unseen, slipping like smoke through his fingers.
His skeptical gaze cuts to Synex. She's still shackled, yet when their eyes meet, her lips curl into a smile.

speaker: Synex
content: Suspecting me again? Or... are you finally doubting others? Those you've never dared question?
His silence only makes Synex's smile widen with delight, her voice tinged with mockery.

speaker: Synex
content: How curious. The Black Ring is about to explode. Everyone's fled like frightened rats... and yet, here you stand. Why, I wonder?

speaker: Synex
content: Is it pity? Distrust? Or that meaningless quest for redemption you're clinging to?

speaker: Synex
content: Or maybe... you know I'm right, but lack the spine to admit it?

speaker: Saffar
content: ...My duty is to ensure the plan proceeds without disruption and oversee your successful reception of the Corpus. My personal safety is irrelevant.

The monster's eyes narrow, a glint of cunning sharpening her gaze. Her lips part, revealing the sinuous flicker of a serpent's tongue. Saffar's brow furrows as the cold weight settles deeper in his chest.

speaker: Synex
content: Tsk tsk tsk. Still lying to yourself, I see.

speaker: Synex
content: Do you really think Fraser would just hand over their Hypercubes? Wake up, darling. They'll just use the mine as bait. You're all just expendable, glorified slaves on Fraser's leash.

speaker: Synex
content: That DisCity girl you pity? She's survived a Black Ring too. Funny, isn't it? That Hypercube mine set on fire by the miners... Guess who took it?
Synex lowers her head slightly, her tone softening.

speaker: Synex
content: Let me go, and I'll peel back the truth for you. The real Black Ring project. Then you can see just how... foolishly naive you've been.
A violent tremor splits the air. The walls shudder as distant roars and the clash of steel bleed through the stone. Saffar whirls around, only to find Synex smiling in contentment.

speaker: Saffar
content: Synex?! You did this?!

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, it's nothing special. Just a little prearranged surprise. We are colleagues, after all. Wouldn't it be rude not to share the fun with everyone?
Her shackles rattle as she lifts her wrists gently as if to mock him. The metallic chime twists into the chaos beyond, swallowing her voice.

speaker: Synex
content: Save your breath, Saffar. I'm done running now.

speaker: Synex
content: I'm going to stay, to destroy it all.

speaker: Saffar
content: You...!

BOOM—! An even louder tremor tears through the air, its shockwave rippling up from below. Synex's lips move, her words swallowed by the shuddering chaos, but Saffar hears them anyway. He goes rigid, lightning-struck, breath trapped in his throat.
The monitoring screen flickers to life, issuing a commanding order.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Saffar, the refugees outside are rioting. Our plan cannot tolerate any deviation. Suppress them by any means necessary.
Saffar ignores the order, only staring at Synex in disbelief.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Saffar!
Saffar's mouth opens, then snaps shut. His Adam's apple bobs once, twice, as if choking on unspoken words.
But in the end, he says nothing.

speaker: Saffar
content: ...Yes.

Only Synex remains in the testing site. Hermis's gaze lingers on the still-smiling woman, his eyes devoid of warmth. To him, she is nothing more than a specimen—perfectly preserved, flawlessly suspended—awaiting the precision of his scalpel.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: I had hoped to keep the Corpus vessel intact...

speaker: Director Hermis
content: But given the circumstances, we have to take special measures.
[Research Institute Corridor with Sunset Filter]
Leaving the dark, oppressive underground behind, Saffar finally feels the warmth of sunlight on his skin again.
The institute lies abandoned, its halls empty, its personnel long gone. An unnatural silence lingers, broken only by distant, muffled clamor from outside.
[Flashback: Background Change]
Amid the thundering sounds of battle, Saffar heard a whisper in his ear.

speaker: Synex
content: Darling, even pawns should think once in a while. All those years groveling for Campbell... You grew up, but never wise. But for old times' sake, I'll throw in a little bonus tip...

speaker: Synex
content: It's the endgame now. Go see the truth for yourself. I'll tell you exactly where to look.
(End of Flashback)
Taking a deep breath, Saffar pushes open the door to the director's office. Following Synex's instructions, he finally discovers a concealed drawer.
Minutes later, he staggers out, his mind reeling.
The daylight is fading. The dying sun stretches his shadow long across the floor, and there, at the far end of the corridor, a figure lurks in the darkness.

speaker: Saffar
content: Do you... have something to tell me?
The hooded figure remains silent, merely raising a hand to point downward.
The underground? Synex's maze? Intruders? Or...

speaker: Saffar
content: ...Hella?
[Underground Area]

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh, come on, come on, COME ON!! These things are way too tough! And they just keep coming!
After leaving the underground maze, the group makes a swift advance toward the core laboratory, only to be cut off at the entrance by another squad of heavily armed Aurum Secretum guards.
Hella whips her water pipe in a wide arc, striking one guard with a deafening clang—its head flies clean off. Yet the headless body only staggers, rights itself, and lunges at her again.
Horo steps in, her axe flashing down in a single brutal strike. This time, the body crumples, motionless at last.

speaker: Horo
content: They're not living things, after all. But good thing we can still put them down—
No sooner does she speak than two massive Aurum Secretum guards emerge at the far end of the corridor, their armored frames dwarfing the ones before.

speaker: Horo
content: Dammit! These guys aren't going down easy...! Hey, Hella, time to use <color=#fb9259>that thing</color>!

speaker: Hypatia
content: I've modified Hella's communicator with a special function. Once destroyed, it will emit a pulse disabling all Aurum Secretum receivers within twenty meters. Use it when necessary.

speaker: Hella
content: Yeah... right...
Hella strokes the communicator in her hand, visibly struggling with herself, unable to bring herself to crush it.

speaker: Horo
content: What? You really can't bear to let it go?

speaker: Horo
content: ...My bad. I owe you one. I'll get you a new one when we get back to Syndicate.

speaker: Hella
content: Sniffle...

speaker: Hella
content: I-it's just a communicator, not some priceless treasure... Let's do it!
Gritting her teeth, Hella tears the communicator from her neck and hurls it to the ground with all her strength!
With a sharp crack of its shell breaking, a shockwave of golden light erupts, surging outward. The guards caught in the blast seize up, collapsing in twitching heaps.

speaker: Hella
content: You bastards! I'm coming for your boss next and settling ALL scores!!
With that final curse, Hella whirls around and storms through the main door.
At the testing site, Synex stands shackled at the center of the space, the Mania on her seething with such ferocity that the very air around her seems to tremble.

speaker: Hella
content: Hey, Synex! Can you hear me?! Ugh—

speaker: Synex
content: ——
The next moment, Synex explodes forward with feral intensity. Hella barely twists aside to dodge her attack. And then she sees it:
Runic brands flicker to life across Synex's skin.
[Background - Core Research Institute]
The attack ceases abruptly. The Aurum Secretum shackles—linking Synex to the Cocoon—jerk taut, pinning her in place.

speaker: Hella
content: Huh?
At first, Hella only stares, bewildered. Then, a sound from above. Her gaze snaps upward just as an image flickers to life before her, projected from the observation room overhead.

speaker: Hella
content: Hmph, so the old guy lurking behind the scenes finally shows himself. You ready to surrender, or what?

speaker: Director Hermis
content: No. Sacrificing a valuable Corpus vessel to stop a mere intrusion would be inefficient. For the current situation, we have a more optimal solution.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Think of this as a "proposal."

speaker: Hella
content: A... proposal?

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Precisely. You've all thoroughly proven your worth. Fraser has no interest in the backgrounds of talented individuals, only in rewarding them properly. We can offer far better compensation than DisCity ever could.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Rather than fight a losing battle... why not join the side bound for victory? What do you say?
Hella and Horo exchange glances. Half a second later, Hella sighs, brushes the dust off herself, and straightens up.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Heh. And here I thought you were gonna say something important. Turns out it's the same old crap.

speaker: Hella
content: "You're so talented," "Join our side," "We'll appreciate you more"—blah, blah, blah—
She raises a single defiant finger high, pointing it toward the ceiling.

speaker: Hella
content: Don't ******* underestimate us! How many times d'you think I've heard this same tired bullshit? Your scam's weak as hell. Go practice for another 800 years before you even try to trick someone!
Horo remains silent, simply standing beside Hella, her position already crystal clear.

speaker: Synex
content: ————!!

The battle resumes. Synex's attacks grow frenzied, each strike more erratic than the last. As Hella barely evades them, she catches the glint of Aurum Secretum snaking across Synex's skin. And beneath its glow, Synex's flesh cracks, peels away, as if her very body is unraveling.
From her neck, a chain of Aurum Secretum extends like an umbilical cord, tethering her to the monstrous Cocoon at the area's heart.
The chain hums in sync with the Cocoon's pulse, amplifying Synex's power, but at a cost. With every surge, she became less human.

speaker: Hella
content: Synex! You bastard, snap out of it already! Argh!
Her words are useless. Another onslaught comes, relentless.

Clang— Horo's massive axe intercepts the blow, but even she staggers under the force. The Legion's defense is barely holding Synex back, yet there's no opening, no chance to counterattack. She's a storm of violence, unyielding, unstoppable.
And at this rate, Synex won't last. Her body will shatter before the battle even ends.

speaker: Hella
content: Damn it...
[Brief Scene Change: The director watches a video feed in a room]
The Legion's defensive perimeter continues to collapse. The man observes it all with a cold scoff—the outcome is inevitable. There's no point in watching any further.
Just as he turns to leave, an eerie disturbance prickles his senses.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: This is...

With a guttural snarl, Synex shatters through the Legion's last defenses. She raises her arm for the killing strike, only for the fighters at her flanks to surge forward in perfect unison, locking her down in a brutal, coordinated counterattack.

speaker: Horo
content: Hella! Now!!!
A metallic glint cuts through the monster's blurred vision. The dagger, temporarily sealed by Aurum Secretum, flares to life in Hella's grip as Mania erupts, devouring everything in its wake.

speaker: Synex
content: ————?!!!

speaker: Hella
content: Hey... Synex, you bastard. We've got way too much unfinished business for you to just run away like this...

speaker: Hella
content: Wake up, you hear me?! Get up and pay what you owe meeeee!!
BOOM—!!!!

The burst consumes nearly the entire testing site in a wave of searing energy. Thick smoke billows in every direction, obscuring the director's view of the chaos below. His frown deepens with frustration.
He steps forward, straining for a clearer look—
BANG!!! Razor-sharp claws slam against the observation room's energy barrier, sending a shower of sparks erupting through the haze. A figure emerges from the smoke.

speaker: Synex
content: Hahahaha! I've been dying to do this for ages!
The monster's restraints lie in ruins, severed by the blade. She is free.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Fool. The Institute gave you more than enough freedom. You just lacked the sense to appreciate it.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Do you really think you can survive outside? Cut off from your Aurum Secretum supply, you'll die.
Another brutal strike. The barrier shudders, its surface alive with violent arcs of electricity, buckling under the force.

speaker: Synex
content: You call freedom on a leash freedom? Don't make me laugh!

speaker: Synex
content: You're all so arrogant, only staring at what's in front of your faces, at your little chains and seals, convinced they could cage monsters...
Suddenly, Synex releases her grip. A slow, deliberate smile curls across her lips as she plunges from above. The glow of the Cocoon pulses below, waiting to embrace her fall.
The director's expression finally changes.

speaker: Synex
content: So you never understood. What I—what we've always needed was never that damn thing...

speaker: Refugee Child
content: Thani, Thani! Quick, look over there—

speaker: Thani
content: ...What is that?!
BOOM—!!!!
Countless bombs ignite, their thunderous blasts ripping through the institute's halls. The grand main facility erupts in gouts of flame, resembling, oddly enough, a celebration.

speaker: Refugee Child
content: Fireworks! They're setting off fireworks!
Every entrance and exit lies blown open. Freed from restraint, the alchemic beasts surge forth in a frenzied tide, scattering in all directions.

speaker: Institute Guard
content: How the hell are all the alchemic beasts loose?! Fall back! Someone stop them— AAGH!
The guard's words die in his throat as the swarm engulfs him.

speaker: Sandra
content: Cough, cough...
Amid the chaos, the woman sneaks her way toward the research institute's entrance. She doesn't know what drives her—stubborn hope, perhaps, or something deeper.
BOOM. The stone pillars above collapse in a deafening crash. Sandra is too close, too slow. She braces for impact, squeezing her eyes shut... But the pain never comes.
A tiny alchemic beast has thrown itself between her and the rubble, its fragile body straining to form a shield. It trembles, writhing, its voice a whisper of half-formed words.

speaker: Little Yuri
content: I'm... back...
No language can contain their longing. At last, the mother pulls her child into her arms.
[Black Screen]

speaker: Synex
content: Cages are for livestock, not monsters.

speaker: Synex
content: We don't want to die, but neither do we want to live like this, rotting in a cage, forever trapped...
[CG - Devour]

speaker: Synex
content: Ha... Haha... Hahahahaha!
Synex tears a deep gash into the Cocoon, her teeth sinking in and rending its shell to fragments.

Shards of the Apostle slip through her fingers as the thing inside is forced into a grotesque, premature birth, its first sound a hateful wail shattering the air. And as the newborn horror writhes, the other monster laughs, wild and delighted.

speaker: Synex
content: Life's too short to play by the rules. And since no one asked my opinion... why not tear them all to shreds?

speaker: Synex
content: Come on, let's make this chaos legendary!
[First, within the main testing site]

speaker: Synex
content: Mmm... Thanks for the treat.
Synex swallows the crystal torn from the monster's chest. Under the group's relentless assault, the cocoon-spawned creature staggers, then collapses, its body crumbling into dust.
With a slow, deliberate flick of her tongue, Synex licks her fingertips, savoring the remnants of her feast. Her gaze snaps upward, but the figure behind the barrier is long gone.

Meanwhile, the masked man sprints through the ruins, debris scattering in his wake. The experiment failed, but the plan isn't lost yet. If he can just reach Fraser in time, the data he carries might still turn the tide.
But...
A shadow shifts. A figure steps into his path, cutting off his escape.
[First, within the main testing site]
After delivering the final blow, Hella can't help but cheer triumphantly.

speaker: Hella
content: Yaaay—huh?!
The entire chamber shudders violently. The research facility, already weakened by the earlier explosions, groans under the strain, its underground section on the brink of total collapse.

speaker: Horo
content: Crap, this place's coming down!
Hella's gaze snaps upward. The shattered skylight from her last escape is still there, but this time, Synex isn't here to throw her through it. How are they supposed to get out now?
Before she can scramble for a solution, a grinning, sinister voice cuts through the chaos behind her.

speaker: Synex
content: Now that I think about it... Hella was the only one here last time. Our dear little Legion girl still hasn't felt the thrill of being thrown through the air, has she?

Then, a deafening roar echoes from the distance. Something massive barrels toward them, shaking the ground. Hella and Horo barely have time to turn before they're yanked off their feet, collars seized in an iron grip.

speaker: Hella
content: Huh—?! Wait, what the hell are you doing this time—?!

A tidal wave of alchemic beasts surges forward, their bodies merging, limbs weaving together in a grotesque yet seamless dance. They form a living pathway—part staircase, part writhing wave—bridging the crumbling floor to the opening above.

Their movements are terrifyingly precise, as if this escape has been rehearsed a thousand times before. Layer upon layer of shifting, interlocking bodies propel the three upward, just as the world beneath them gives way.

speaker: Synex
content: Get ready...

speaker: Synex
content: We're taking off!
[CG - Alchemic Beast Parade]

speaker: Hella
content: Ahhhhh—!
The high-altitude wind howls, slamming against their faces with enough force to make their eardrums roar. Hella grits her teeth and forces her eyes open.

Behind them, the explosions and collapsing structures fade into the distance as the escapees surge forward, a living tide weaving through ruins and flickering firelight. Their voices rise in long, wild calls, half communication, half exhilaration, echoing into the chaos.

speaker: Horo
content: I-I'm going to fall!
At Hella's side, Horo staggers, fighting to keep her footing in the relentless rush, while Synex...

speaker: Synex
content: Hahahahahahaha!
The gloomy sky tears open, revealing a burst of light that bathes Synex and the endless stream of creatures surging behind her.
At the crest of the wave, she rides, charging toward freedom.
[Scene Transition: Research Institute Exterior, Damaged]

speaker: Thani
content: They're back—!
The alchemic beasts disperse, depositing Hella and the Legion members onto the ground, only for them to be swept up again as the refugees celebrate their victory, tossing them high into the air.

speaker: Hella
content: Aaaah—! Wait, hold on—! Grab me tight—Don't let go—!
Synex doubles over laughing, clutching her stomach. But then, from the edge of the crowd, a figure catches her eye.

speaker: Synex
content: Ooh?
His white coat, once pristine, is now smudged with dirt and the unmistakable marks of gunpowder.

Their eyes lock for a long moment. Then, without a word, he flicks something toward her. Synex catches it midair: a shard of Aurum Secretum. With a barely perceptible nod, he turns and vanishes into the crowd.

speaker: Synex
content: You stubborn little thing.
Synex shakes off the moment and turns to leave, only to feel a tug on her tail. Spinning around, she finds Hella clutching to the tip of it.

speaker: Hella
content: Almost let you slip away again! We said we'd settle this for good! You've screwed me over way too many times. This isn't something you can brush off with just a few coins—eek!
Still clutching the tip of Synex's tail, Hella barely has time to register the tight grip around her waist before it coils around her, yanking her off her feet and into the air.

speaker: Synex
content: Hmm... what an interesting mess. And here I thought I was finally free—just wrapped up my last "job," ready to go play explorer...

speaker: Synex
content: Let's see... what should I do with you?

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, how about I just... take you away with me?

speaker: Hella
content: What?! HELP! Some creep's kidnapping a child here! Put me down, you jerk! HORO—Horo, help me!
A quick glance to the side confirms that Horo—the mighty Legion leader—is in no shape to help. She clutches her stomach, still pale and unsteady from their recent wild ride.

speaker: Synex
content: My, my, what a fiery little thing! And here you were so adorable just moments ago, crying my name.
In response to such nonsense, Hella retaliates by making a face at her.

speaker: Synex
content: Well, that's that. Scores settled, asses kicked—everyone got what they deserved. Time for the little ones to scamper home for dinner... and for me to hit the road.
With a quick flick of her tail, the woman drops Hella to the ground.

speaker: Synex
content: As for you and me...

speaker: Synex
content: We'll talk about it when you catch me someday!
Hella stumbles down the staircase formed by the alchemic beasts, limbs flailing. By the time she scrambles to her feet, Synex and her troop of creatures are already striding away.

speaker: Hella
content: Hey—! Y-you don't just run away, you bastard!!!
Hands on her hips, Hella fumes, but a reluctant smile betrays her. Shaking her fist at the departing figure, she declares her officially wanted.

speaker: Hella
content: What a lunatic... hmph...

speaker: Hella
content: You're SO dead next time! When I come back, I'm gonna kick your ass so hard you won't sit for a week!
Synex doesn't look back. With a loud, hearty laugh, she waves farewell, her silhouette soon swallowed by the surging tide of alchemic beasts and swirling dust.
[Background - WhiteSands at Sunset]
Somewhere in the farlands. The Legion has "borrowed" a sand ship from the research institute and is now speeding through the dunes.

Though the conspiracy has been thwarted, Fraser is no longer safe for the wanted group. With no other options, they board the stolen sandship and set course for DisCity, bracing for the long journey back home.

speaker: Hella
content: Whistle~

speaker: Horo
content: Someone's really excited to go home, huh?

speaker: Hella
content: Behold! The one and only superhero who crushed Fraser and wrecked the Aurum Secretum Institute—the strongest Sinner ever, Hella! That's me!

speaker: Hella
content: Once we're back at MBCC, even ${PlayerName}'s gonna have to show me some respect—not a single excuse this time! Because I took out one more Black Ring than he did!
female_content: Once we're back at MBCC, even ${PlayerName}'s gonna have to show me some respect—not a single excuse this time! Because I took out one more Black Ring than she did!

speaker: Hella
content: And I've got every last victory written down in my diary, black and white, no arguing! Ha! This time, ${PlayerName} won't have any excuse to stiff me on my allowance!
As Hella boasts with her usual swagger, Horo can't help but crack a smile.

speaker: Horo
content: And the rest? Did you achieve what you set out to do?

speaker: Hella
content: ...When I first left Syndicate, all I cared about was getting stronger. But if I'm being honest? I had no clue what that actually meant or how to do it.

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh, I was such a loudmouth back then, running my mouth about becoming some super badass. Pretty embarrassing, huh?

speaker: Hella
content: Now I'm still... not that strong. But there are so many people out there who've got it worse. Even if I'm not some powerhouse, I wanna help however I can.
She may still be as weak as before, but this journey has taught her things far more precious than mere strength: the art of deception, the courage to sacrifice, and... the weight of trust.

speaker: Hella
content: And that's good enough for me.

speaker: Hella
content: Anyway! Let's get home already! It's been so long. They're probably losing their minds missing me!

speaker: Hella
content: We've got loads of time ahead of us for more crazy adventures! Horo, you better not leave me behind next time—promise! No take-backs or you're a total loser!

speaker: Horo
content: Alright, it's a promise.
Hella leans out the window, savoring the evening breeze on their journey home.

speaker: Hella
content: Too bad the communicator's busted. Can't even tell Hypa the good news... And who knows where that blue-haired weirdo Saffar wandered off to...
Hella leans against the window, watching the sun bleed into the horizon. Then, she goes completely still. The silence stretches too long. Horo glances up, brow furrowing.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Hella?
[Cut to Multiple Reaction Shots with Changing Backgrounds. Korryn's Perspective]
On the outskirts of DisCity, a woman in a cowboy hat raises her glass in a toast, laughing with her companions as they tally their spoils.
But then, she freezes. Her gaze snaps up, sharp and sober, as if something in the depths of WhiteSands has called to her.
Meanwhile, the blonde girl speeds toward a distant point, her foot nearly pressing the accelerator through the floor. Yet no matter how fast she drives, the gap refuses to close.
The beast horde surges forward, an unstoppable tide, until the figure standing at its peak suddenly lifts her head. The Aurum Secretum within her burns, resonating with something far away.
[Return to Hella and Horo's Perspective]
The Furor beads hanging from Hella's body have silently shattered, unnoticed. But there's no time to gather the fragments. Her gaze locks on the horizon—
Dark clouds churn over the area where Furor was. At the heart of WhiteSands, atop a lone hill, the sun is nearly swallowed by a second black disk—an eclipse of unnatural darkness.

speaker: Horo
content: That's... Wait...

speaker: Horo
content: Don't tell me the real <color=#fb9259>inheritance</color> is...?!
[Fade out for several seconds, then Background - Refugee Camp]

speaker: Thani
content: ...? Saffar?

Thani returns to the refugee camp after the battle. The tents now stand empty. Every soul has fled but one. Saffar stands at the camp's edge, his fist clenched around some object. His eyes track the retreating tide of alchemic beasts as they vanish into the horizon.
After a moment, he turns his gaze back, his voice remarkably calm.

speaker: Saffar
content: It's nothing. I just wanted to come back for one last look.

speaker: Saffar
content: I still have some matters to attend to. I need to go now.
The young man turns his head, a faint smile crossing his face.

speaker: Saffar
content: Goodbye, Thani.

June 25, N.F. 115

5 Hours After the Attack On
The Aurum Secretum Institute

Communication between Fraser and the Aurum Secretum Institute has finally been restored, unleashing a sudden surge of activity across all channels. Most remain oblivious to the institute's shadow operations. They know only fear, the crushing certainty that their quiet lives are now in peril.
And deep within the data sea, a single point of light flickers to life.

- Someone jammed the institute's signal transmission during the attack. The "Cocoon" matrix is damaged, and the Corpus vessel is missing. - What about Hermis? What's the status on-site? Wasn't he overseeing the detonation? - Continue as planned! We've prepared enough vessels beforehand. We can't afford to stop now.

- No, the plan has already failed. - If we can't control the ground zero through the "Cocoon," then even if the Black Ring detonates, it won't be under our control. It's meaningless. - Let's proceed with the contingency plan.
- The true "Corpus" is in position. The seeds of the Black Ring were sown long ago. - The time for harvest has come.
[Black Screen]
Across the barren wasteland, a peculiar procession trudges toward an unknown destination.
Humans, beasts, and shapeless aberrations—the weak and the lost—gather in this endless march, following the sole flame that pierces the darkness.
A gale howls as the sin-stained sun sinks in the west. A creeping shadow swallows its light, leaving only a bleeding ring of crimson upon the horizon.
We are the lost, exiled to this place. We are the forsaken, left with nothing.
And we are the desperate... who twisted our lives just to survive.

In the director's drawer, Saffar uncovered a briefing document—Fraser's Hypercube reserves laid bare. Military. Defense. Commercial. Each category boasted astronomical figures, wealth beyond comprehension.
Yet as DisCity tightened its grip on Hypercube exports, as calamities ravaged the farlands, as resources dwindled and refugees wandered... Fraser could have provided aid. But it chose not to.
They bred hate in us, shattered our bones. When our homeland suffered, we raised empty hands in prayers, swore we'd give Him anything. But He said, "Your 'everything' is dust."
He turned to the next page. This time, it was a calamity status assessment report.
"██ is awakening, and Mania levels throughout the farlands are rising rapidly. The calamities are irreversible; resources will continue to deplete, until the farlands become nothing but a dead zone."

speaker: Saffar
content: Aligning with any power is pointless. We're not even worth being pawns. To escape the fate of being crushed... we have to take power for ourselves.
At last, deep within the magic box, he found the final glimmer of light.
Hermis is dead, the research institute destroyed. All channels of information leakage have been severed. The final possibility now rests in our hands.

speaker: Saffar
content: If we stand firm, united as one...

speaker: Saffar
content: Even we have the power to detonate the Black Ring and defy fate.
[WhiteSands, Solar Eclipse Filter]
The sun drowns in shadow, plunging WhiteSands into gloom.
A chilling silence grips the outskirts of Furor as Hella hurls herself from the sand ship. She dares not imagine what has happened—or what is about to happen.
Her heart hammers against her ribs, a frantic drumbeat urging her forward. She races into Furor.
[Underground Furor, Solar Eclipse Filter]

A black box hovers above the altar. Crimson engravings along its edges flare to life, pulsing in time with the rising chant that echoes through the chamber. Something stirs within—a foreign entity, long dormant, now awakening.

The shell of the inheritance fractures. Dark, viscous corruption bursts forth, spilling like a flood in all directions. The refugees—bent, emaciated, their forms warped by time and suffering—step forward without hesitation, wading into the spreading black tide.
Perhaps this, too, is part of someone's grand design, but it no longer matters. They raise their voices in ragged harmony, singing their gratitude for this mercy, this wretched thread of life.
[Furor, Solar Eclipse Filter]
Hella races ahead, forcing Horo to rush into Furor after her.
The Black Ring is pulsing to life. She can feel the air warping around her. Contamination erupts from beneath her feet, spewing forth corrupted souls.
The spirits of those buried beneath the white sands stir—awakened, ravenous. Corruptors, their hollow eyes fixed on the living, claw at Hella and Horo, desperate to drag them into the grave.
Shadowy tendrils coil around Horo's limbs, binding her. She twists, hewing through the specters with her axe. As they dissolve, ghostly pale-blue crystals materialize in their wake.
—Hypercubes.

speaker: Horo
content: Hella! Damn it... Get back here!!
Ignoring the danger, Hella charges deeper into the contamination's heart. Mania grows thicker by the minute, its whispers slithering into her mind.

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Our homeland... destroyed by calamity... leaving us drifting like rootless leaves... But this land... it's too barren... It can't sustain us all...

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Survival is too cruel... Death is our only choice...

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Stay away... Stop standing in our way...!
Horo lunges, yanking Hella back from an oncoming strike, only for a tendril to snare her instead.

speaker: Horo
content: —Ugh!

speaker: Hella
content: ...?! No! HORO—!
The corruption swallows Horo whole. Hella reaches for her—their fingers brush, then slip apart—and the darkness consumes them both.
[Black Screen]
In the darkness, Hella hears a chant.
Gentle yet stirring, like a mother's lullaby entwined with a warrior's battle hymn.
The chanting swells, deafening, piercing her eardrums. The world spins, and then—a violent shove from behind.
[Underground Furor, Crimson Filter]
When her eyes open again, she is underground in Furor.
The corruption clinging to her body hasn't faded. Black sludge, oozing from the inheritance, has already swallowed most of the altar, consuming the refugees gathered around it.
Yet the sludge avoids her. Partially corrupted figures press against Hella, their twisted hands shoving her away from the spreading corruption.

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Go back, Hella... Don't go any further... You still have somewhere to return to...
Before her, a blue-haired young man staggers forward, each step carrying him closer to his inevitable end. The corruption has already claimed most of his body.

speaker: Hella
content: —Saffar!!!
He halts, then turns his head—just slightly—gazing at the girl in the distance.

speaker: Saffar
content: ...Hella? Why are you here?

speaker: Saffar
content: You've already saved Synex. Weren't you supposed to go back to DisCity? This place isn't safe. You should leave.

speaker: Hella
content: You idiot, snap out of it! That damn black box is screwing with your head! Or did those Fraser bastards feed you more of their crap?

speaker: Hella
content: Don't let those jerks trick you!! The real Black Ring isn't some miracle thing—it's all lies! I know the truth... it can't even grant your stupid wish!

Hella lunges forward, desperation clawing at her chest, but something snags her, trips her, holds her back again and again. She can only watch, helpless, as the corruption slithers further, consuming Saffar inch by inch.
Yet his voice, when it comes, is eerily calm.

speaker: Saffar
content: You're right. Fraser, DisCity—even the Underground you told us about—none of them deserve our trust. They've all used us like pawns. I'm done letting them decide our fate.

speaker: Saffar
content: But... I trust you, Hella.

speaker: Hella
content: Huh...?

speaker: Saffar
content: DisCity hoarded their Hypercubes while calamity destroyed our home. Fraser talks about humanism, but all they've done is turn us into lab rats for Aurum Secretum, giving us nothing but ruin.

speaker: Saffar
content: But then, you showed up.
[Flashback: Saffar's Encounter with the Undergrounder]

That person told him to help the girl from DisCity—the girl whose homeland had once defied the impossible. Her people had detonated a Black Ring with sheer will, carving their own fate from the jaws of despair.
[Return to normal avg]

speaker: Saffar
content: You brought us stories of Syndicate—proof that even the weak can fight back, that we all have the power to defy fate. You showed us a new path... new possibilities.

speaker: Saffar
content: So thank you, Hella... For giving us hope.

speaker: Hella
content: No... wait, don't do this...

speaker: Saffar
content: Now go. You're the only one we refuse to see harmed.

speaker: Saffar
content: Goodbye, Hella.
The corruption has already crept up to his cheeks when the young man finally smiles. Just as Hella lunges for him, he raises a trembling hand—and pushes her away.
[CG - Sacrifice B]

Then, from the spreading darkness, an arm stretches upward, lifting the black box high. Countless arms follow, surging upward in unison as glistening crystals fracture from their bodies, falling like brittle rain.

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Thank you, Hella... for giving us strength, for giving us a choice...

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Thank you... Goodbye...

<color=#ca0c1b><size=44>Make a wish...
Power, wealth, anything you can imagine...

Pray to the Ring,
and it shall grant your desires...</color></size>

speaker: Voices of Souls
content: <i><color=#dg1f1f>I...</color>
[CG - Sacrifice A]

speaker: Voices of Souls
content: <i><color=#dg1f1f>...want a seed.</color>

speaker: Hella
content: No... come back...

Hella reaches out desperately, fingers clawing at the air but finding nothing. Her arms fracture and splinter under the relentless corruption, only to be mended by her regenerative power again and again.

speaker: Hella
content: Don't do this...

Her fingertips dissolve into nothingness, then reform, over and over. She keeps struggling to push forward, yet each effort is met with crushing resistance. She can only watch, helpless, as everything unravels before her.

Amid the chaos, the shackles buried deep within her shudder to life, surging forth in a feeble attempt to shield her. But even they are swiftly overtaken by the corruption. From the other side, a voice cries out to her, but Hella can barely hear it anymore.

speaker: Voices of Souls
content: <i><color=#dg1f1f>One day, it will grow, when the wars are over, when the storms have passed... when no one is left wandering the wastes... and we can finally go home...</color>

speaker: Voices of Souls
content: <i><color=#dg1f1f><size=44>To see how hope rekindles across this land of famine.</color>

speaker: Hella
content: NOOOOOOOO!!!!!
[Sharp cut to black screen]
[Fade out for several seconds, then transition to Black Ring small CG #1]
In the vast, endless desert, a crimson ring hovers above the jagged peak.
At first, tiny black specks appear in the distance, drifting closer. Drawn by some unseen pull, they surge toward the ring, vanishing into its glow without hesitation.
Then, more come—swarms of darkness, seeping from the horizon. They gather, coalescing into a churning tide, a storm of shadows rushing forth.
The crimson ring trembles as the black storm twists around it, merging and clashing, consuming and consumed—faster, hungrier—
And from the depths of the void, a voice whispers.

<color=#ca0c1b><size=44>So...

What is your wish?</color></size>
<color=#7683a2>I...</color>
[Series of flashback CGs showing various moments from Hella's journey, ultimately leading to the Chief]
<color=#7683a2>I... want...</color>
[ED]
You monitor the battlefield through a remote feed. Among the swirling Tide of Ashes, enemy silhouettes flicker in and out. The odds are turning against you.

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...It seems the Tide of Ashes is working in the enemy's favor, providing them with effective cover.

speaker: Siglinde
content: How would you like us to proceed, Chief ${PlayerName}?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Track their movements and pinpoint the enemy's Aurum Secretum device that controls the Mania field...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those Aurum Secretum guards are just monsters now. But even if they weren't, I'd still approve this operation.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Just as we'd expect from you, Chief. We're ready to follow your command to victory.
Peace is always fleeting.

In November N.F. 114, farland extremist and Sinner Jelena assassinated DisCity cabinet members in a brazen act of interference, disrupting the city's electoral process.

In June N.F. 115, the 13th Great Expo, held in DisCity, was struck by a devastating attack during its closing ceremony, resulting in significant casualties.

On June 25, EDGE detected the emergence of BR-005 in foreign territory.

Despite limited intelligence sharing, EDGE narrowed its surveillance to the energy field near Furor through an intercepted online video. However, while residual traces of the Black Ring's outbreak were discovered, the entity itself remains elusive.

As of now, BR-005's location is still unknown, but one thing is certain: the Black Ring remains active, its calamity waves rippling across the globe.

In early July N.F. 115, DisCity's task force stormed Euphoria, a secret club hidden in international waters. Recovered intelligence exposed the Farland Alliance's covert infiltration of DisCity and drafted war plans. Diplomatic relations have since deteriorated sharply. Both parties have issued mutual condemnations, recalled their ambassadors, and begun military mobilizations, bringing the two powers to the brink of war. The ceasefire agreement, established in N.F. 107, now stands effectively defunct.
Even as calamity looms and Mania spreads, humanity persists in its self-destructive divisions.

speaker: Diplomatic Statement
content: "The Great Expo incident is a profound tragedy born of the longstanding and deeply rooted historical tensions between DisCity and the farland cities. These tensions have, in the past, led to open conflict, and their continued escalation risks further destabilization."

speaker: Diplomatic Statement
content: "As a neutral city-state, Fraser urges both parties to exercise maximum restraint and prioritize de-escalation. The Farland Alliance must immediately halt its aggressive actions against DisCity, clearly articulate its grievances, and re-engage in good-faith negotiations."

speaker: Diplomatic Statement
content: "As the preeminent city-state worldwide, DisCity carries a responsibility to lead by example in upholding stability. However, recent reports confirming the involvement of former DisCorps personnel in the official operation against Euphoria raise serious concerns. Such actions dangerously inflame tensions and invite escalation!"

speaker: Diplomatic Statement
content: "DisCorps—the architects of the Outland wars' brutal expansion—are war criminals, devils devoid of conscience. The people of the farlands, who still bear the scars of their actions, rightly view them with unyielding condemnation. For the sake of peace, DisCity must take a stand: sever all ties, denounce their atrocities, and refuse to be complicit in their evil. To do otherwise, ████..."

speaker: Scarface
content: War criminals? Devils? Are they talking about us?
The fierce-looking man with a face covered in scars tilts his head up, his expression one of utter bewilderment.

speaker: Siglinde
content: From my experience, yes, they are.
The young liaison officer responds with practiced patience, bending down to retrieve the radio she lent Scarface, all while bracing for her teammate's inevitable explosion.

speaker: Scarface
content: GYAHAHAHAH! Fraser's still playing both sides like a buncha two-faced rats, huh? Who the hell they think they're fooling? Everyone knows they're the ones pulling farlands' strings! Can we smash 'em? Can we just kill every last one?
His boisterous laughter echoes through WhiteSands' depths and over the canyon, only for the roaring sandstorm to snatch it away in an instant.

July 25, N.F. 115 10:02
473 km Outside DisCity
Heart of WhiteSands

An immense Tide of Ashes churns around them, swallowing the landscape in a swirling shroud. Beneath its cover, a small troop moves like ghosts, their weapons primed and eyes locked on the valley pass below.

speaker: Doctor
content: Shh, keep it down. Keep yelling like that, and you'll be the first one we put down before the enemy gets here.

speaker: Scarface
content: Hah, you wanna fight with me? Hell yeah! C'mon, c'mon, let's go! I need to crack some skulls or I'll lose my goddamn mind!!

speaker: Siglinde
content: Huh, General Augustus just sent a message.

speaker: Scarface
content: <size=28>...Never mind.</size>

speaker: Siglinde
content: Just kidding. It's Command HQ calling.

speaker: Scarface
content: What? Damn you little—!!
The Liaison Officer delights in her companion's furious expression and, savoring the moment, decides to push her mischief further. She turns to another man.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Mr. Uris, the call is from the Chief of Minos, our acting commander. He says he wants to talk to that "iron head."
female_content: Mr. Uris, the call is from the Chief of Minos, our acting commander. She says she wants to talk to that "iron head."

content: The only soldier wearing a metal mask steps forward reluctantly. He accepts the communicator from Siglinde and answers the call.
[Scene Change] Command HQ
Iron Mask stiffens visibly as his image flickers onto the screen. The sight of you in his faction's commander uniform clearly unsettles him.

Good—let him squirm. Your relationship was never cordial to begin with. If he has complaints, he can take them up with his precious general. After all, she was the one who stuffed you into this gaudy uniform, all for the sake of "command presence."
After a weighted pause, Iron Mask snaps into a flawless salute, every angle of his body rigid with military precision. The gesture is textbook respect.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: We've picked up an abnormal ash storm signature in WhiteSands. Readings suggest at least three Apostles, plus signs of desert bandit transport activity. This Tide of Ashes seems highly suspicious.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Currently, the Apostles are advancing west, likely targeting the FAC-23A ash defense outpost 18 klicks away.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: We've got 18 recon personnel ready to deploy on-site, plus an ambush force of 50 with 32 anti-Mania mag cannons positioned on the flank. The estimated combat zone's outside our mag field support range, but Broken Blade Squad 8 is en route from 37 klicks northeast.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: General Augustus speaks highly of you, so please, feel free to share your thoughts. We'll consider your advice as the situation warrants.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Any signs the enemy's detected our ambush?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: No. The Apostles of Ashes show no unusual movements.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Good. A Tide of Ashes gives us every right to engage, and FAC won't face backlash for defensive action. Hold until Broken Blade Squad 8 is in position, then move fast. Secure all enemy supplies intact; we need whatever intel they're carrying.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And those things they sent—Apostles, Corruptors, whatever they are—if they're here to threaten us...

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Copy that.

speaker: Scarface
content: Win-win-******* win! Damn fine work, Commander! You're running this show no worse than the boss! Maybe we oughta make it permanent?

speaker: Scarface
content: I was just kidding! Quit staring at me through that broken slit of yours! You're making my skin crawl here!
The reliable lieutenant—codename, fittingly, "Lieutenant"—has already secured the necessary arrangements.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Detail three soldiers for cleanup. All other units move out immediately. Recon Team at 67B just lit up our boards. We've got a narrow window to secure the advantage.

speaker: Scarface
content: Alright, I'm going in! See ya all later—
After the battle, the sandstorm's fury has dulled to a whisper, just as predicted. Visibility sharpens by the minute, and the Tide of Ashes begins its sluggish turn away from the battlefield.

Now, the cleanup team moves in. They keep the feed live at your command, scanning the wreckage with methodical efficiency. Soon, they discover the shattered husk of the mysterious device you marked for destruction.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Completely obliterated, isn't it... No question it was vectoring the Tide straight toward the FAC outpost.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Chief, can you see this?
It's an Aurum Secretum device, the same kind the Outlanders use to resonate with some Apostles of Ashes, siphoning power from them. But this one is different.

Between its slotted grooves, something festers. A nauseating contamination, thick and dormant. Just watching the feed makes the shackles within you twitch, like a chain yanked taut by some distant call.

That might be Mania contamination unique to the Black Ring. Worse, the device wasn't just tuned to the Apostles. The evidence suggests a deeper resonance that matches the very Black Ring you've hunted for a long time.
BR-005, where Hella disappeared.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: ...We can handle that, but are you planning to conduct the examination personally, Chief?

speaker: Military Doctor
content: The contamination on this device seems abnormal, unlike anything we've seen. In your state, close exposure would risk severe physical strain. My team can handle the examination, and we'll provide a full diagnostic report. Otherwise...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No. Just bring it back. I have to—
[Contamination Flash]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ugh!!
Hecate catches you just before you collapse face-first into the sand table, but it's too late. The chaotic noise has already clawed its way into your mind.
Get back... Help me... Get out of here...!! Hurry over here... GET BACK... Come to me... HELP ME!
The world around you twists, reality fraying at the edges. You struggle like a drowning man, your resistance desperate yet futile as you fight to move forward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't be ridiculous... I can't stop... How can I stop here...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Bring it back... I must get it... get her back...
And then, with one final, shuddering step forward, you reach out—
[Fade to Black]
Only to walk into darkness.
In the suffocating darkness, you're trapped as if in a bottomless bog, every movement futile.
Yet... there's warmth. A fragile, lingering comfort.
Then, a shadow flickers before you, swaying like smoke caught in a breeze. It bounces around playfully, just beyond your reach.

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: So then I went "BANG—!" and they all went "UGH—!" like total losers! And then—pew pew pew pew—BAM!! Surprise attack! Wiped them out in one move! Even Horo freaked out!

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: Hahaha! You seriously missed out! I had some real adventures out here! No way my letters could've done it justice, and it's definitely not because I can't spell, okay?!

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: So many crazy places, so many interesting people... Bet you wouldn't even recognize me now! Not some little tagalong anymore. Me and my steel pipe? STRONG. Like, S-T-R-O-N-G, got it? Ha! Might even be tougher than you now!
Whose voice is this?
...So familiar that it brings tears to your eyes.

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: But... you know, I kept thinking... Why weren't you there? All my coolest, baddest moments... and you guys just... missed it. Every single time.

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: Would've been way more awesome if you'd been with me. You really should've come.

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: If only you'd come with me... I was all by myself... the whole time... It's so scary...

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: Help me... ${PlayerName}, help me...

speaker: Hella
content: Where are you...
She sobs quietly, completely unable to see you. The vision unravels, the dream tearing at the edges, filling you with panic.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hella!
[Release the shackles]
[Wake Up, White Out, Black Shackles Flash]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ugh!!
The nearly pitch-black shackles pierce through your palm. Waking from the dream is agony—your heart hammers against your ribs, and your breath catches in ragged gasps.
Your thoughts swim through a thick haze, and it takes a long moment before you grudgingly surface into full awareness, your surroundings slowly coming into focus—
[Scene Change] MBCC Infirmary
You're here again.

Ever since the BR-005 outbreak in late June, severe Black Ring contamination has been eating away at you. EDGE suspects Hella is trapped deep within the Black Ring at the farlands, and the Mania devouring her is now flowing directly into you through the shackles. All things considered, it's a miracle you're even conscious. You push yourself up, muscles trembling.
No one waits by your bedside. No battle reports light up your terminal. Is the front line holding? Or have they already written you off—a commander who keeps collapsing, now useless to the fight?
Groping for the receiver, you slowly dial a number.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, you're awake! How are you feeling? Do you need anything? I'll notify the doctor right away...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No need. Notify Command HQ instead... I'll be joining the strategy meeting.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Understood.
[Command Room]

July 26, N.F. 115 13:30
MBCC Chief's Office

To prevent your contamination from spreading, the strategy meeting has moved to a remote conference. Nightingale opens the call interface. On screen, an FAC soldier stands to acknowledge you, while the others seated around the round table appear to have been deep in discussion for some time.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Chief, it's good to have you with us. Please don't push yourself too hard.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: You'll find the battle report on your terminal. We'll skip the recap to save time as we still have a long list of items to cover.
You nod. In response, an FAC report materializes on your terminal, its stark summary outlining a crisis in motion:

Mania fields are fluctuating wildly across the globe, with the concentration and number of the Tide of Ashes increasing at an alarming rate.

Making this threat tangible, Apostles of Ashes, previously only seen in farlands, are now appearing near WhiteSands in unprecedented numbers.

Multiple defense outposts have fallen. Despite FAC committing vast resources to fortify the WhiteSands perimeter, nearly 90% of shipping routes are now impassable.

DisCity's external transport is crippled, trade has ground to a halt, and contact has been lost with two satellite towns.

On paper, manpower has recovered from the BR-002 campaign over the last two years.
New recruits are cycling through intensive training before being deployed to the DisSea and Ash Frontlines for vital combat experience.

However, what concerns FAC most is the source itself—

The missing farland Black Ring, BR-005. Its anomalous activity is the engine driving these global disturbances.
And now, it's sending destabilizing ripples into even more dangerous regions...
[Present battle report with images and text]
On the other end of the line, the meeting room is thick with tension, every word of the discussion strained and heavy.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: This is no ordinary sandstorm. There are strong resonance reactions detected inside BR-000, which can only be produced by a Secondary Black Ring—<color=#fb9259>BR-005</color>... In fact, the reactions are even stronger than during the outbreak of BR-005.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Which means that missing Black Ring has either grown exponentially, or... it's right on top of us.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: We're stretched thin. The FAC is committed at WhiteSands and DisSea, with assets tied down at Broken Frontline and Ash Fortifications. Our current Hypercube reserves are barely sustainable. We cannot hold without further support.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Paradeisos has already approved a budget increase for the FAC.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: This isn't about money! We've already lost five tide barriers in WhiteSands. What we need are dedicated anti-Mania assets. Until we neutralize the source, any repairs are just a temporary fix.
Anxiety, once sparked, spreads like wildfire. The acting representative from Nirvana also raises his voice in response.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Our Hypercube production is already maxed out. Need I remind you that Nirvana's balance sheets are still bleeding from the last deficit? How about you get West District to put pen to paper first?

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: But frankly, even if they signed today, it's too late. This is what happens when you indulge the Syndicans instead of making hard choices. You can't close the gate after the herd has already broken through.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...Damn it. So that's their play. They targeted the Chief because contaminating the shackles compromises every Sinner linked to them. Our most effective asset against Mania is down. Now we're forced to fight a war of attrition, burning through all the resources we have.
A moment of silence falls.

speaker: Outland Affairs Officer
content: We all know where the Farland Alliance stands. But Fraser... They talk a big game about peace and dialogue, but their trade with those extremist city-states hasn't slowed down for a second. Push them hard enough, and they'll likely directly funnel resources to our enemy.

speaker: Outland Affairs Officer
content: On top of that, we lost contact with our people stationed there a while ago. We still haven't heard a word... No one knows what happened to them.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...What about the <color=#fb9259>Third Observatorium</color>? Can they provide any support? The Mania outside the city falls under their monitoring jurisdiction. We need any data they have—even the smallest clue could be critical.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: The location of BR-005, its detailed properties, its connection to the Apostles... They have none of this information?
He turns to the inorganic triangle beside you, only to be met with a cold, unflinching gaze.

speaker: Schorl
content: ...The Third Observatorium has concluded its observations regarding BR-005. Its resources have been reassigned to other tasks.

speaker: Schorl
content: Should you have essential requirements, you may file a formal request with the Ring Research Institute. EDGE will evaluate the petition and allocate support as they deem appropriate.

speaker: Schorl
content: Please try your best to endure.

The soldier clenches his fists and drops into his seat. A stiff silence grips the conference room. Glasses are lifted; pages are turned. Then, the discussions resume, cycling through the usual litany: diplomatic hurdles, budget constraints, resource and personnel shortages, ineffective coordination...
As their dreary, convoluted arguments drone on, the chaotic noise of contamination echoes in your mind once more.
Look Look... What a scattered mess... Pathetic Pathetic...
...Opportunity Seize the opportunity... Hope There is hope now... Almost time...
Purge them all Change the world...

speaker: Hella
content: Help me...
[Snap Back to Reality] Sound Effect
A dull thud jerks you back. You find your fist on the table, your hand throbbing. On the other side of the screen, every face is turned to you, waiting.
As it happens, you do have something to say.

speaker: Option
options: ...The front needs helping hands, so let me go.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have experience dealing with the Tide of Ashes. And I was on the Euphoria operation, where we rooted out the farland spies.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The situation is critical, isn't it? So let me go.
Your words are iron-clad, ringing with resolve, but the FAC soldier doesn't dare to respond. It's another, more familiar voice that answers.

speaker: Langley
content: That was an unofficial operation. While your role was only advisory, you still overstepped. Have you forgotten how they hauled you back on a stretcher?

speaker: Langley
content: In your current state, no one in their right mind would put you on the frontlines.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then I'll gather intelligence from the rear.
As you say this, you switch to an encrypted channel, excluding several participants with low clearance. You lock eyes with the city-state's spymaster, your words deliberate and sharp.

speaker: Option
options: I need to see Adelaide Campbell.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where is he being held? The 9th Agency? Paradeisos?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is he still alive?

speaker: Langley
content: He's still alive. Why, you looking to kill him yourself? Like last time?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to know what he's confessed!

<size=80><color=#fb9259>BR-005 OUTBREAK
Time: June 25, N.F. 115
Location: UNKNOWN
Scale: UNKNOWN
Ground Zero: UNKNOWN</size></color>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Everyone knows he's the one pulling the strings behind the farland attacks. He controls the Apostles of Ashes, and he's an Undergrounder—an enemy of DisCity. BR-005 was his operation. He has the answers. So why is he not being interrogated?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You prevent me from seeing him, not letting me kill him... so what intelligence has that bought you? I thought the 9th Agency could make even stones talk!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need answers. Where is BR-005? What happened there? And what is the truth behind this outbreak?!
She offers a silent container for your outburst, her response deliberately detached.

speaker: Langley
content: All you actually care about is that little Sinner, isn't it?

speaker: Option
options: She's also important to the BR-005 investigation.

speaker: Langley
content: We've lost enough field operatives already. This isn't a grief counseling session. We're staring down the barrel of a potential war—one wrong move means irreversible consequences. So everyone needs to keep a cool head and remember what's actually at stake.

speaker: Langley
content: Get a grip. Unless you want to flood this command center with Mania or kill the adjutant standing closest to you first?
A tremor runs through Nightingale's hand as she supports you; the contamination bleeding from your body is a palpable poison to her touch.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...I'm fine, Chief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Ngh... Damn it...
Schorl floats over with an unhurried grace, its anti-Mania blue light scanning your body. Under its calming pulse, the corruption fades alongside your panicked emotions.
Noting the change, the spymaster allows her stern expression to soften. She rests her temple on one hand and speaks, her tone now measured and calm.

speaker: Langley
content: We're now on the 52nd round of interrogations with Adelaide. Standard methods won't break him—the man's a black hole. Given half a chance, he'll turn the tables on his interrogators... and that includes you.

speaker: Langley
content: So our top priority is to contain him, sever all external communications, while tracking the <color=#fb9259>enemy's intelligence network</color>.

speaker: Langley
content: The 9th Agency has deployed more operatives to the farlands, but with the vast distance and all the calamities between us, not one scrap of intel is reaching DisCity in time. Meanwhile, the enemy's network remains flawless. In wartime, that kind of disadvantage is fatal.

speaker: Langley
content: My suspicion? The Underground has taken over the <color=#fb9259>Mania dark web</color>. You noted that during the Black Ring incident, Adelaide seemed to be syncing precise time with an unknown party. That's our entry point. Monitor their signals, crack their encryption. And mark my words: this will be a marathon, not a sprint.

speaker: Langley
content: —You've had your answers. You can leave now.

speaker: Langley
content: This meeting was supposed to make conflicting departments bury the hatchet and focus on the real threat. But as it stands, you're in no position to contribute. Go back and rest up for now.
You find no words for a rebuttal. Clenching your fist in frustration, you rise and let Nightingale support you as you leave.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You said this meeting was supposed to make conflicting departments bury the hatchet and focus on the real threat...

speaker: Option
options: Then why is <color=#fb9259>that unit</color> not at this table?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The ghost unit stationed at Nirvana Port, the one whose name alone makes Outlanders hesitate... Why aren't we using them? Aren't they exactly the kind of force DisCity needs right now?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But you seem to fear them.

speaker: Langley
content: ...A hungry wolf may hunt a tiger for you, but wolves bite, Chief. Be careful...
Communication is completely down. A desperate need to be on the frontlines burns within you, but once again, you are left behind.
[Scene Change] Infirmary
After thirty minutes, your condition stabilizes and Nightingale takes her leave. She has been burdened with your duties since your collapse, and the weight of command now pulls her away.
Now, you're alone in the infirmary with only Schorl for company, its scanner still relentlessly sweeping over you.

speaker: Schorl
content: The contamination levels are becoming increasingly volatile...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Any changes with BR-005? Could it be close already? Or did Hella—cough cough!

speaker: Schorl
content: Please remain calm, Chief. It is impossible for a B-Class Sinner to become a Corpseborne. If your shackles were directly tied to the Black Ring's core, like what happened with BR-002, you would have difficulty regaining consciousness, just as you did in N.F. 113.

speaker: Schorl
content: That said, the present circumstances remain manageable. The fact that your shackles are still intact strongly suggests that the girl is alive and has not fully become a Corruptor. Your consciousnesses are still linked. I hope that knowledge offers you some reassurance.

speaker: Option
options: ...Going to the front would make me more reassured.

speaker: Schorl
