[Scene Change] MBCC
The battle report terminal in your hand is screen-shattered, yet casualty updates continue to flicker across the fractured display.

Outside your office, the hallway echoes with a rising tide of commotion. More and more registered Sinners are being affected by worsening contamination from the shackles, rushed to the MBCC for emergency aid. The Bureau has never been this chaotic.
And you—the source of the contaminated shackles—are not immune either. The approaching BR-005 weighs on you, an immense pressure that churns the contamination within, making it surge relentlessly.

speaker: Schorl
content: The Apostles are deliberately avoiding DisSea, which contradicts their nature. The evidence suggests the enemy is using BR-005 to deliberately restrain them.

speaker: Schorl
content: It seems that both the farlands and Fraser still fear BR-000. They don't dare let the Apostles enter and risk triggering an uncontrollable change.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, you mustn't shoulder this burden alone. Your body can't withstand much more of this stress.
Your knuckles bleach white around the terminal as the battle reports flash relentlessly. Each update sends the casualty count climbing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ..."The situation still remains within projected parameters." "Current events are proceeding within expected outcomes. It will be resolved." That's what you said.

speaker: Schorl
content: Yes, current events are still proceeding within expected outcomes. You don't need to worry.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Has the FAC finally stabilized their defensive line? Do they have the strength to push the Apostles out of the city?

speaker: Schorl
content: Regrettably, no. The FAC's main forces are still committed to DisSea, struggling against the Tide of Ashes. Based on current data, the confrontation line is continuing to advance deeper into the urban sectors.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are there any forces we can use to hit those city-states directly? Or do we have any means to strike them from the inside?

speaker: Schorl
content: Unfortunately, our intelligence networks and trade routes remain compromised. The enemy was exceptionally well-prepared for this conflict. They have decisively seized the initiative.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then... is there a way to punch through their lines? Something to directly break BR-005, their tactical core?

speaker: Schorl
content: Targeting BR-005 would be the most efficient solution, I agree. We have confirmed its location, but it is now surrounded by a growing concentration of Apostles of Ashes.

speaker: Schorl
content: This Black Ring exerts a powerful attraction and control over the Apostles. Broken Blade Squad 3's previous approach was, in fact, designed by the enemy. They are not likely to give us another such opportunity.
The mechanical triangle parries each "solution" you can think of with a calm, methodical precision, utterly devoid of anxiety.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I just remembered... you had another method before...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Two years ago, with BR-002. The person behind you proposed a plan. I would enter the Black Ring, find the Corpseborne, and act as a beacon. That way, you could fire the high-energy "Rules" and turn both the enemy and me into ash.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now I can't enter the Black Ring, but there's someone inside, marked by the shackles, and she's probably close to the core...
[Hella's Portrait]

options: Are you considering using that on her?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You want to use me to locate Hella, and then gamble that a locked-on strike through her will break BR-005's core? Is that it?

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, please, try to remain calm. Your contamination levels are spiking. And I'd advise against swatting at me. Excessive motion compromises my treatment's efficacy.
It hovers, performs several scans, administers an injection, and then returns to the previous topic.

speaker: Schorl
content: The scenario you describe is, technically, a viable option. It is the most economical and controllable path we have.

speaker: Schorl
content: However, we all know that your current willpower and ethical stance prevent you from supporting the plan's execution. And we cannot afford to lose you at the moment. When weighing the costs, the necessary sacrifice becomes clear.

speaker: Schorl
content: So, please rest assured. We have a backup plan, and it is progressing smoothly.
A sigh of relief escapes you, quickly followed by a stronger wave of confusion.

speaker: Option
options: ...So what exactly is this backup plan?

content: Schorl's only answer is a prolonged scan, continuing long after your Mania levels have subsided.
After what feels like an age, the mechanical triangle finally speaks again.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, some patterns never change, even in this era.

speaker: Schorl
content: Faced with catastrophes and Mania, humanity will still choose to fight amongst itself rather than unite for a solution. The fighting, the hatred... it continues.

speaker: Schorl
content: We know war is a constant. So, any power that can bring victory will be weaponized. We calculated the possibility of "catastrophe warfare" long ago. We've also gathered ample data to verify the enemy's technological capabilities...

speaker: Schorl
content: With help from the Underground, the farlands acquired a Black Ring with exceptional attraction to the Apostles of Ashes. It migrates like an Apostle itself and gathers the Apostles to advance on DisCity, creating the most violent Tide of Ashes—one far beyond our current defenses.

speaker: Schorl
content: This is the full extent of their capability. It is impressive, but it is also their limit.

speaker: Schorl
content: Understanding the Apostles is the pinnacle of Outland technology. But in the entire field of Mania research, they cannot compete with DisCity.
The black triangle doesn't answer. It attempts reassurance again, but its offer rings hollow in a voice mechanical as always, yet colder than ever before.

speaker: Schorl
content: There is no need for concern. Everything is proceeding as calculated. We've reached this stage thanks to your efforts; the plan's smooth execution is, in large part, your achievement.

speaker: Schorl
content: We appreciate your hard work, Chief. Now, please. Get some rest. Leave the rest to us.

speaker: Schorl
content: The war will soon end.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What are you really—
A chorus of startled cries echoes in the air, immediately chased by hurried footsteps. People begin to swarm, a chaotic current pulling them outside.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What's happening...?
Suddenly, a city-wide broadcast overrides all DisCity frequencies, its signal pulsing from every screen and speaker at once.

speaker: EDGE-03
content: Citizens of DisCity, members of the Farland Alliance, and people of all other territories... This is EDGE, addressing all of humanity.

speaker: EDGE-03
content: The Exploration, Defence and Governance Entente was founded for one purpose: to combat Mania and secure the future of our civilization. Since then, we have strictly maintained our neutrality, refraining from interfering with humanity's choices in matters beyond the protocol's scope.

speaker: EDGE-03
content: It has never been our intention to restrict the freedom of city-states to pursue their own paths. But when we're faced with decisions that threaten the survival of our entire species, EDGE must act. We cannot stand by and allow humanity to walk the path of self-destruction.

speaker: EDGE-03
content: If we had any other choice, we wouldn't take such drastic measures. But this war... it must end now.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Hey!
A Senate order, routed through the Mania dark web, drops like a bomb, shocking everyone.

—Our city-state is under anomalous attack. All offensive operations cease immediately. Prioritize defensive measures.

—Communication channels are severely compromised. All units hold position until repairs are complete.

—Repeat: This is a highest-level alert. All offensive operations cease immediately.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: ...Those DisCity bastards...!!
[Scene Change] On the Way Back to the City
On the return path to the city, for the first time, Broken Blade Squad 3 halts in its tracks. The apparition before them is so staggering that even these hardened soldiers hold their breath.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: General...
Augustus looks up at the sky.

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: We hear it... their blood still flowing, their cries a fanfare for our victory...

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: Their only fate is to be shattered... to become mere dust beneath our blades.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Bastards...
[Scene Change]
You exit the Bureau and step into an open area.
The Tide of Ashes—driven by the farlands and plaguing DisCity for nearly a week—has finally subsided. As the sandstorm weakens and the dust settles, the sky becomes clearly visible again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What... is that...

speaker: Schorl
content: ...It's a <color=#fb9259>weapon</color>. We use it to maintain peace, a necessary measure in the face of calamity.

speaker: Schorl
content: Nine years ago, a similar scenario once played out. It seems that human nature is truly constant.
Overhead, the optical camouflage fades, revealing several black triangles floating silently. They pulse with a soft blue light, their energy connecting to form a massive barrier.
At the center of this barrier, a massive shadow is imprisoned—a distorted sight all too familiar to you.
[BR-003] Transition 2s

speaker: EDGE-03
content: We abhor war, yet we will not yield to it. In the struggle against injustice, civilization shall be reforged, and technology shall advance once more.

speaker: EDGE-03
content: If humanity refuses reason, then EDGE will correct your course.

Since 06:00 on August 11th, the Tide of Ashes launched by the farlands has halted its advance, and the assassins infiltrating DisCity have ceased their attacks. With EDGE's deterrence taking effect, the city has gained a crucial respite to reorganize its defenses and attend to its citizens.
During this lull, a farland Sinner and Aurum Secretum Warrior named Selyna is transported by a Nirvana Port troop directly into the custody of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control.
[Scene Change] MBCC Corridor
Outside the prisoner's cell, Elvira stands watch alongside the stern guards. When you rush over, she jumps with surprise, perhaps scared by "Hella" behind you or from dread of your current demeanor.

speaker: Elvira
content: Chief? Are you alright? Where's Hecate?

speaker: Elvira
content: Sh-she's inside. The sedative hasn't fully worn off yet. She just woke up.
You enter the detention room alone and lock the door behind you.
[Scene Change]

In the interrogation room, the Outland prisoner is locked in a restraint chair, her limbs bound by anti-Mania chains. A wall of specially designed, blast-proof one-way glass divides the space between you, supposedly to guard you against her resentful aggression, though you suspect its true purpose is to protect her from you.
She senses your entry, a subtle shift in the air, and lifts her head. Though blindfolded, she seems to stare directly through the obscuring glass, seeking your gaze.

speaker: Selyna
content: Heh... So DisCity's commander is nothing but a cowering mutt, too scared to even leave the kennel.

speaker: Selyna
content: I forgot.

speaker: Selyna
content: I threw it away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You can't just throw it away. I've seen Outland spies like you before. Aurum Secretum is a part of you, bonded to your Mania. Activate your power and summon it, now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You deceived the Apostles of Ashes with it, didn't you? Is it connected to BR-005? It can stop the Tide of Ashes and expose the Black Ring, can't it? Answer me!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This has to end. The Black Ring, the Tide of Ashes... your greatest victims are innocent people. Civilians. They are never part of this fight. They have no stake in the war. The elderly, children, countless people who can't even defend themselves. This is pointless. Their deaths are meaningless.

speaker: Selyna
content: Heheheh... that's rich. You get caught in an ash storm and suddenly it's my fault? This is the Nightfall Era. Catastrophes happen. People die. Cities fall. It's just the way the world works now. Or are you DisCity big-shots still too spoiled to get that?
Ignoring the warning, you shove the security door open and burst into the cell, grabbing the prisoner by the collar.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whoever's pulling your strings, contact them! Your handler, Fraser, anyone—use your Mania dark web to reach them! Tell them to stop this now!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Apostles, the Black Ring... Mania should never be turned into a weapon. That's a line you don't cross. Humanity can't control the fallout. If this continues, if catastrophes start spiraling out of control across the globe, none of you will be left to pick up the pieces. You'll burn with the rest of us.
A calculating smirk plays upon Selyna's lips. She disregards your questions entirely, her gaze sliding past you to fix upon the shadowy figure suspended in the air behind your back.

speaker: Selyna
content: Hah... I get it now. It's you. You're the shackles.

speaker: Selyna
content: Then why come to me? Why not go bother <color=#fb9259>Adelaide</color>? Hell, even I heard about you nearly beating him to death. What's the matter? Get your wrist slapped by the higher-ups? They lock you out of his cell? Is that why you're down here wasting your time with a nobody like me?

speaker: Selyna
content: ...Or did you finally finish the job? Ooh, aren't you a piece of work? Hahaha—
[Flashback]
(Show clean background without text, then injured character portrait with repeated punching sound effects)

speaker: Adelaide
content: Heheh... Heheheh... That's right. Let it all out, Chief... Pour out your hatred, your grief, your frustration... The more you do, the closer you come to understanding the Outlanders...

speaker: Adelaide
content: At last, we're the same... We finally understand each other, don't we? Heheheheh...
[End of Flashback]

That man's laughter echoes in your mind—a taunt deliberately crafted to shatter your control. The mere memory of it sends a surge of fury through you, stirring the Mania within until it threatens to spill over.
Selyna watches, a smirk playing on her lips, visibly satisfied with her provocation.

speaker: Selyna
content: Don't act so surprised. What citizen of DisCity doesn't have my people's blood on their hands? This entire city is built on our bones. You don't need a reason to kill us—you never have.

speaker: Selyna
content: And "civilian"? That's a convenient word. In a city this size, how can you possibly know who's not involved? Maybe they're not fighting today, but what about tomorrow? Every war criminal was somebody's innocent child once upon a time... hahaha—weren't they?

You glare at her, meeting a gaze of burning, pitch-black fury. The same corrosive fire instantly kindles in your own chest. It devours your reason, sears your throat, and twists around your hands like burning vines, screaming at you to lunge forward and choke the life from her—
You clench every muscle, wrestling the impulse back into its cage as your voice comes out strained.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Was this Fraser's idea? Or was it the Underground? Open your eyes. They're using you. They pump you full of hate just so you'll charge into the fire for them. Your rage isn't a weapon—it's their weapon.

speaker: Selyna
content: You're the ones who planted this hate!
She unleashes a furious roar, poised to tear your throat out.

speaker: Selyna
content: For years, DisCity expanded! You burned our villages! You slaughtered countless people! You think we'd just forget that blood debt?

speaker: Selyna
content: Why don't you go ask your own gun-toting bastards what excuse they used when they pulled the trigger?! Did they feel righteous? Has a single one of them ever been punished?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's just like when... Nngh!

speaker: Jasmine
content: I have no interest in killing people, but... you're not really human, are you? You're nothing but DisCity's blade!

Before you can form a response, a surge of contamination lances through you, piercing your mind with a painful memory. Mistaking your pained hesitation for doubt, the prisoner barks a laugh. She leans in, pressing her advantage, and unleashes a torrent of bitterness stored since the day of her capture.

speaker: Selyna
content: You get to live in luxury by sucking us dry, and you have the nerve to talk to me about what's right?!

speaker: Selyna
content: So what if we use the Black Ring? You deserve it! You deserve to burn! For years, the Black Rings that hit your city churned up Mania catastrophes that ravaged our lands! You brought this on yourselves!

speaker: Selyna
content: And don't you dare act innocent! You've used them too! Look at that damn <color=#fb9259>sky</color> and tell me I'm lying!
[Empty Scene] Show BR-003 background for 2 seconds, play BGM

speaker: Schorl
content: As you can see, all Black Rings are connected to the source of Mania. Their fluctuations cause field changes on a global scale, which in turn trigger random catastrophes.

speaker: Schorl
content: This is technology that only DisCity, having endured more Black Rings than anyone, could have developed. We've been working around the clock, and we've just finished adjusting BR-003. It's now primed to unleash a catastrophe strike at a moment's notice.

speaker: Schorl
content: While our technology does not yet permit precise targeting of these strikes, it is a known fact that only DisCity is built to survive frequent catastrophes. This understanding alone will force them to stand down. In essence, it is <color=#fb9259>deterrence</color>.

speaker: Schorl
content: Make no mistake, this is an extreme measure. Using Black Rings and catastrophes as weapons crosses a line—it undermines the very foundation of civilization. As a beacon of progress, we would never initiate this ourselves.

speaker: Schorl
content: But after the Farland Alliance's reckless actions these past few days—after watching them use BR-005 and the Apostles of Ashes to attack civilians indiscriminately—their guilt is undeniable. Their crimes have given us all the moral capital we need to proceed.

speaker: Selyna
content: ...I see your game now. That troop of yours, the Black Ring tracking... it was just a smokescreen. All to hide what you were really building... your own Black Ring weapon to launch catastrophe strikes! You were just the bait!

speaker: Schorl
content: And we owe much of this success to your efforts, Chief. By drawing the enemy's focus onto the battlefield, you created the perfect diversion for our plan to proceed smoothly.

speaker: Schorl
content: Now, let's end this war together. Make them surrender and hand over BR-005. That is how we secure the chance to bring your friend back.
Countless voices echo in your skull, intensifying your headache into agony. You stagger back, pressing your palms to your temples, but the clamor only grows louder.

You reach for "Hella," seeking an anchor, but her form shivers and warps—Mania has poisoned your perception. She recedes into a haze, while the laughter of your <color=#fb9259>enemy</color> rings out, clear and terrifyingly close.
—Enemy. Her presence is an immense weight, and now every word she speaks is a needle driven into your mind, threatening to shatter your will completely.

speaker: Selyna
content: Let me brighten your day even more. It was the Black Ring that guided us here, Furor's will that summoned the Apostles to destroy you all. We followed this revelation, so we know the truth—

speaker: Selyna
content: That thing following you around? It's not the brat you know. It's a phantom. A piece of the Black Ring itself, breathing with <color=#fb9259>Furor's will</color>. It didn't come to you because it missed you.

speaker: Selyna
content: Haha... you've been cursed by the Black Ring. And you DisCity dogs get what you deserve! As for that Sinner brat...

speaker: Selyna
content: The Black Ring spared her life because she's awakened! She sees the truth now; she knows who fights for real justice! She's with us! She only sought you out to kill you! Because you're her ticket to redemption for the sin of being born here!

speaker: Selyna
content: Hahaha!... Look at you! You're already a corpse! That's the curse she placed on you! The contamination will consume your life, rot you until you die! Do you hear me?! She came here to kill you!!!

speaker: Option
options: You really get off on killing your own kind, don't you?!

content: [Release Shackles] No interaction needed, just special effects, screen flash, and vibration.
[Scene Change] Corridor Outside the Door

The sudden blare of the Mania alarm jolts Elvira. Ominous pulses bleed from the isolation cell—a chamber designed to be utterly soundproof. Her face drains of all color. In a surge of panic, she hammers her fists against the heavy door.

speaker: Elvira
content: Chief? What's happening? Are you okay?

speaker: Elvira
content: Hecate!! Where are you?!
[Scene Change] Back to Isolation Cell

On the other side, you have the prisoner pinned, your hands locked around her throat, driving her down into the interrogation chair. The Mania-infused shackles pierce her flesh, siphoning her power in a relentless flow.

That flow is now your weapon. The power that was once a burden is now a part of you. For the first time, you are in perfect, terrible resonance with it. The prisoner's face, twisted in hatred, triggers a cascade of hallucinations—a flickering montage of other faces.
[Jelena, Jasmine, Aurum Secretum Warrior, Adelaide]

Your body moves on its own, fighting on pure instinct. You no longer know what's in control—the Black Ring, a Rancor, or some unknown part of yourself. Your grip tightens relentlessly, and the woman's choking voice begins to fracture.

speaker: Selyna
content: ...See? Hah... See? I told you... I knew it...

speaker: Selyna
content: Go on... Do it... Just like you butchered my people. You're... all the same... cough cough... heh... all the same...
Her voice gradually falters.

speaker: Selyna
content: Look upon this... See it all...

speaker: Selyna
content: Black Ring... let your gaze... fall upon them...
The contaminated shackles compel your hands to squeeze harder, until a figure lunges forward and grabs your arm, as if trying to stop you.
[Portrait]

"Hella" clings to you, her whole body trembling, as if she is trying to hold you back, but is just as afraid to touch you. In your daze, that contact becomes an anchor, and the world begins to snap back into focus.

speaker: Hella
content: ...She said you... are different...

speaker: Hella
content: ...Said... you're strong... you will save everyone...

speaker: Hella
content: ...No... you are the same...
That face suddenly lifts and draws near, two pitch-black eye sockets so close they feel like they're about to swallow you whole. And you see it. She's smiling.

speaker: Hella
content: You're just like them—!!!

Amid the shrill cry, "Hella" suddenly shatters. The little arms wrapped around you burst into hellfire, sprouting countless tentacles studded with weeping blood-eyes and grotesque, grinning mouths. Countless departed souls roar, threatening to tear you apart and devour you.
And in the chaos, you glimpse—
[Montage: July Black Ring incident small CG, flashing white gradient portraits of Saffar and various refugee NPCs to show Chief is experiencing Hella's past]

The shackles break free, the same color as her. They plunge into her body, then merge seamlessly. The attack is useless. She squeezes you tighter, and your mind floods with the roar of anger and hatred.
—And beneath it all, a faint, desperate sobbing, so quiet it might be a hallucination.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: Go to hell!!
Your voice is a ragged whisper, a futile attempt to call out to "her." You reach out, desperate to touch "her," but your efforts are meaningless. You cannot stop "her."

The tentacles constrict your throat, silencing your final gasp. A corrosive fluid drips from "her" face onto yours, searing your skin and seeping into your shattering consciousness, a venom distilled from pure hatred. Your mind floods with the voices of despair:

speaker: Departed Souls
content: Curse you... Curse you all!
[Sword Flash]

Several silver flashes slice through the air, and the pressure holding you down vanishes. Before your eyes, "Hella" is cut clean into pieces. Her form fractures, lifting and scattering like shreds of torn cloth. In that final moment, "she" looks straight at you, arm outstretched—and without thinking, you reach back.
But all your fingers catch is a fading shimmer, slipping through your grasp along with her last faint whimper. "Hella" shatters in your hands, gone.
[Black Screen] 2s
The door swings open. Someone steps inside, catching you just as your strength gives out. Silhouetted against the light, a familiar voice reaches you.

speaker: Augustus
content: It's just a contamination phantom. Isn't your interrogation room equipped with an anti-Mania device? Turn it on immediately.

speaker: Augustus
content: And...
She looks at the Outlands prisoner lying on the floor. The woman has already passed out.

speaker: Augustus
content: This is not how you use prisoners. Take her away.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...! Understood.

Elvira is the first to move. She rushes to the prisoner's side, helps the woman to her feet, and supports her onto a stretcher with other staff members before following them out. In the doorway, she pauses and throws a final glance your way.
Then, only you and Augustus remain. She sheathes her sword and offers you her hand. You remain seated, too dazed to respond.
Wordlessly, she drags the interrogation chair across the floor and sinks into it beside you. Looking into your eyes, she begins to speak, her voice low and measured.

speaker: Augustus
content: I just got back from WhiteSands. Went to the location you marked, picked up Squad 3, and saw the famous BR-005 for myself.

speaker: Augustus
content: The Ring and its Apostle swarm are already on the move. Faster than expected, but they left a clear trail. I've already sent a team to hunt them down. We'll know more soon.

speaker: Augustus
content: Now, go get checked out. You can't save her until those injuries are treated and you're back on your feet.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...No. I'm going now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know where the Black Ring is. Right in the heart of the Apostle swarm, a place that's practically impenetrable. Hella's in there. She's not the Corpseborne, but she's fusing with the Ring.

speaker: Selyna
content: That thing following you around? It's not the brat you know. It's a phantom. A piece of the Black Ring itself, breathing with <color=#fb9259>Furor's will</color>. It didn't come to you because it missed you.

No, that is Hella. Through that entanglement, you finally truly connected with her. All the longing and joy are hers. The hatred and suffering are also hers. Everything you understand and don't understand about her... it's all her. She is every fragment of that chaotically shattered consciousness.

Thrown into the heart of war. Forced to witness hatred and despair that festered for generations. Made to confront ugly, impossible questions that even the most powerful could not solve. That is why she broke—into so many pieces.
—Because you, too, had no answers to give, she left in despair.
—But you truly had none. Who has ever found a true answer to war?
You struggle to lift your head and look at the general standing before you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said you wanted to cooperate. You wanted something in return... Fine. I'll do it. I know what you're after.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No one in DisCity trusts you. You're using me to get a foothold in this war, to expand your influence... to seize power. You want this conflict to escalate because it makes them desperate. It makes them need you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But BR-003 is here. EDGE will take over, and your plan falls apart again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So use me. Let's take on the Black Ring together. You pick the target; I'll follow. Use me however you need.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I just want her back. I'm out of time. I can't wait any longer.

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: Did you hear him did you hear that? He said it, he means it. Resolute in conviction, willing to die. That raw passion and courage, murderous rage and determination..
female_content: Did you hear her did you hear that? She said it, she means it. Resolute in conviction, willing to die. That raw passion and courage, murderous rage and determination..

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: Let him join us, let him fight, fight for you. He will be one of us. We want him, we want him, WE WANT HIM!
female_content: Let her join us, let her fight, fight for you. She will be one of us. We want her, we want her, WE WANT HER!

content: Augustus listens silently to every voice, every will thirsting for battle, and then—
Clank!
Her scabbard strikes the floor with sudden force, a sharp command for silence that shears your words short.
Silence floods the cell. Augustus stands with both hands resting on her sword, looming over you from the shadows, her voice heavy with undeniable authority.

speaker: Augustus
content: I picked you for a reason. I saw your potential.

speaker: Augustus
content: You despise war, but for someone you care about, you dragged your half-dead body onto the field and fought with your life. That kind of resolve... it's rare. I knew that raw material would forge an exceptional soldier—my kind of soldier.

speaker: Augustus
content: So I indulged you. I helped you. I was shaping you to fight by my side.

speaker: Augustus
content: But now, I've changed my mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If your goal is to crush the Outlands, you need me. My power is the only weapon that can counter their Black Ring. So why turn it down now? I thought you were different from them... those cowards too scared to use you.
She listens to your words with complete indifference.

speaker: Augustus
content: Loyalty isn't something I lack. And I have no shortage of "weapons" at my command.

speaker: Augustus
content: What I want is a warrior with an unbreakable will. Someone who can stare into the abyss and still find a reason to fight.

speaker: Augustus
content: You may be capable <color=#fb9259>now</color>, but answer me this:
[CG]

speaker: Augustus
content: Suppose I grant your wish. I give you my resources and my power, take you to the front lines, and let you give everything you have to save this person you care for. And you do. You push beyond your limits. You leave nothing on the field—

speaker: Augustus
content: But you still fail. <color=#fb9259>And that child dies.</color> What would you do then?
[A flash of Hella being tortured appears for 0.5s]

A prolonged silence fills the room, broken only by the sound of your increasingly labored breathing. She showed you that image only a moment ago, and yet you are already desperately trying to forget it.

speaker: Augustus
content: Can't find your answer? Or do you simply refuse to think that far? Death is a constant on the battlefield. Loss is routine. Not only could you fail to save her, but your desperate charge could get countless others killed. You could sacrifice everything and gain absolutely nothing. That outcome is far more common than you think.

speaker: Augustus
content: So I want you to imagine that moment. Really see it. And then tell me: when that happens, will you surrender to your hatred and become a vengeful demon drenched in blood? Or will you let it break you, leaving us to pick up the pieces of a broken weapon?

speaker: Augustus
content: Think. And then answer me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't let it... I won't let that happen! I will save her...
She studies your reaction, her gaze unwavering. The hand gripping your chin relaxes its hold as a slow, deliberate smile curves Augustus's lips.

speaker: Augustus
content: So, in the end, all you can do is run away...

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief!
[Return to portrait]
Hecate bursts in and catches you just as you collapse, probably sent by Elvira. Augustus takes the distraction as her cue to let go, rising to her feet and stepping back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't you dare judge me! I am taking this seriously. I will—
You try to stop her, moving on instinct as you summon your shackles to block her path. But the contamination that seeps out with them drains what little strength you have left.
Augustus looks down at your struggle, her expression unreadable—whether it's contempt and pity, you cannot tell.

speaker: Augustus
content: I don't need mindless killers. Raw power alone is worthless to me. I want soldiers who will hold the line, who will keep fighting until their very last breath—warriors who never break, no matter how hellish it gets.

speaker: Augustus
content: But that's not you. The reason you fight is far too frail.

speaker: Augustus
content: Stay back. This war is no place for you.
The door swings close.
[Scene Change]
Without another word, she strides out of the interrogation room. Her deputy is waiting outside, and they depart together under the gazes of nervous onlookers.
Not until they reach a nearly empty stretch of hallway does the deputy finally speak.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...Are you sure about this?

speaker: Augustus
content: About what? Think I said too much?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: No, I mean...

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: You clearly hold him in high regard. And he's essential for the coming battle, isn't he?
female_content: You clearly hold her in high regard. And she's essential for the coming battle, isn't she?

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: Why did you stop... General? We live for slaughter, we die for victory, yet now we lie silent in pools of blood...

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: We do not understand... The enemies still live, the Rancors still thirst for blood. He's one of us. Why not recruit him?
female_content: We do not understand... The enemies still live, the Rancors still thirst for blood. She's one of us. Why not recruit her?

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Yeah. With him, our job would be much easier. We'd probably get to rescue the person he's after, too.
female_content: ...Yeah. With her, our job would be much easier. We'd probably get to rescue the person she's after, too.

speaker: Augustus
content: But the sharper the blade, the easier it shatters. The moment his resolve breaks... the war will consume him.
female_content: But the sharper the blade, the easier it shatters. The moment her resolve breaks... the war will consume her.

speaker: Augustus
content: I won't watch another good blade shatter. Not again. Not after what happened to all of you...

speaker: Augustus
content: He doesn't belong in a war. This old debt... it's ours to settle.
female_content: She doesn't belong in a war. This old debt... it's ours to settle.

content: As she says this, she lifts her head.
At the end of the corridor, a pitch-black triangle slowly emerges from the shadows and hovers before Augustus.

speaker: Schorl
content: The EDGE meeting has just concluded. The consensus is to keep BR-005 operational. Let the Outlanders continue to believe they still have a chance. It keeps their attention right where we want it.

speaker: Schorl
content: That Black Ring is still in its infancy. With ${PlayerName} and that Sinner... our contingencies are more than sufficient. It's not a threat.

speaker: Schorl
content: Which is precisely why EDGE wants you to use this situation. Deploy covertly, push into the farlands, and eliminate the opposition directly.

speaker: Schorl
content: In return, you have my word, General Augustus: win this battle, and your exiled forces will be fully "exonerated." And, if you want it, the position of Commander-in-Chief is yours.

speaker: Schorl
content: After Dravyn's death, you led your forces away from DisCity because the title of "Commander" went to someone else, didn't it? That was twelve years ago. Come back now. This time, the position is undisputedly yours.

speaker: Schorl
content: The methods are yours to choose. Succeed in this mission, and I guarantee everything you and your forces lost will be restored.
Unlike the one that accompanies ${PlayerName}, this triangle has a small number engraved in a hidden spot.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...A bait perfectly crafted for me. You've certainly done your research.

speaker: Augustus
content: You promise me power. But in whose name do you make that promise? EDGE-05? The Cavendish family? Or <color=#fb9259>the Sillage Society</color> behind you?
A burst of electrical static sweeps through the air, resembling a quiet chuckle.

speaker: Schorl
content: In the name of <color=#fb9259>Bernadette</color>, and everything it stands for.
[Scene Change] WhiteSands Enemy Camp

speaker: Farland Advisor B
content: ...We've received a message from the Mania dark web. The Senate is on edge. They're demanding to speak with you.

speaker: Farland Advisor B
content: Lieutenant Colonel... do you...

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: ...Hang up. They're not afraid of the catastrophe, they're just afraid it'll land on their doorstep. I don't have time to waste on cowards.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: If DisCity has deployed that weapon and we flinch now, that will be true defeat.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Send our order through the Mania web: all Aurum Secretum Warriors who have infiltrated DisCity are to cease attacks and go to ground. I'll quickly reformulate our approach.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: The war isn't over. In fact, we've never been closer to victory. Press on! We can't let Adelaide's sacrifice be for nothing.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: We're past the point of no return. The world must change.
[Guerrilla Tent]

speaker: Helena
content: Brock, is your brain even connected to your mouth?! Or did that sandstorm just swallow all your promises the second you stepped outside?! This is the 182nd time! THE 182ND TIME you've broken your word!!!

speaker: Brock
content: Eeeek!!

speaker: Helena
content: "The modified Hypercube barriers are for protection, not for offense!" How was that not clear?! I said avoid the enemies, not go hunting them down while wearing the barriers in broad daylight!

speaker: Helena
content: I only snuck those notes to my boss and smuggled the supplies because you swore you'd play it safe! And this is how you repay me??!!

speaker: Brock
content: I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I promise I won't get you in trouble, okay?

speaker: Helena
content: This isn't about getting me in trouble! EDGE is a scientific organization that belongs to all of humanity! We oppose war!! I want peace. Actual PEACE! Do you even know how to spell that word? Does "keeping your promise" mean anything to you at all?!

speaker: Helena
content: It's because you always pull this crap that I—

speaker: Brock
content: I'm wrong, I'm a jerk, I'm the worst! I'll kneel on nails next time—ah, crud, someone's here, gotta bounce, talk later!
[Clack—]

speaker: Brock
content: Sigh... I finally get to call her, and all she does is yell at me?
A little head popped into view. It was Catherine.

speaker: Catherine
content: Your wife?

speaker: Dravyn
content: You've dealt some real damage to our commander. The Andohar family would be proud of you.

speaker: Catherine
content: Oh... She dumped you?

speaker: Brock
content: She's a comrade. Period! We watch each other's backs, not go on dinner dates. What kind of mushy stuff are you kids reading anyway?

speaker: Catherine
content: Hmm... She's from Nirvana Port, then? Why would the guerrillas have ties to DisCity's industrial port? What has she been shipping to you?

speaker: Brock
content: ...Where did you hear that?
A small combat knife pressed against Catherine's throat, and the joyful atmosphere immediately shattered.

speaker: Dravyn
content: That's a bold approach to intelligence gathering. You know, spies are executed here.

speaker: Catherine
content: For real?

speaker: Catherine
content: Then, can you use a gun instead? Bullets are faster. Blocking them would be more exciting.
As requested, DisCity Major Dravyn drew his gun and chambered a round.

speaker: Brock
content: Whoa, whoa, hold up! She's just a kid, no need for all that. And you, kiddo, quit snooping around—and messing with our ammo. We're on a budget here!

speaker: Brock
content: You took a wrong turn and ended up in our backyard, it happens! We'll get you sorted and back home, alright?

speaker: Catherine
content: If you're worried about a "diplomatic incident," keeping me here seems like the safer choice, doesn't it? Things might get boring if I leave.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Why should we keep you here?

speaker: Catherine
content: Because you need to keep secrets.

speaker: Catherine
content: You see, I know a few. The DisCity army was ordered by the metropoles to eliminate Captain Brock for his little rebellion. And yet, here you are—their military rising star—in his camp instead of leading the charge against him.

speaker: Catherine
content: And it's not just you. Nirvana Port, even EDGE... they're all colluding with you. The metropoles would love an excuse to finally discipline those unruly scientists.

speaker: Catherine
content: So, wouldn't it be simpler if you just kept me here? Unless the "just" guerrillas prefer to silence a little girl.
She knew she had the upper hand. A triumphant smile on her lips, she skipped cheerfully around the tent, the tense atmosphere only fueling her glee.

speaker: Catherine
content: Home is so dreadfully boring. My family sells weapons everywhere but never sees a real battlefield. It's all mansions, deals, and counting money.

speaker: Catherine
content: I'm sick of balls and banquets. Even hunting is just putting on airs. Soon enough, they'll just marry me off for some political alliance.

speaker: Catherine
content: So I snuck out. I'm going to have some fun before all that happens. And if I manage to pull off something big, my family will have to start listening to me.

speaker: Catherine
content: I want to see real commanders! The powerful weapons from my books that can turn the tide of battle! And a horse! I want to ride one on the battlefield, like a proper general in those portraits!

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...Your city-state is our enemy.

speaker: Catherine
content: Arms dealers have no homeland, and the Andohars have no enemies. If you have the need and the money, my parents would be happy to do business. Complete confidentiality guaranteed.

speaker: Catherine
content: Besides... are you sure you don't want to make use of me?
She looked at Dravyn, narrowing her eyes.

speaker: Catherine
content: I've seen how you pick your weapons, buddy. You're that type—the kind who doesn't care how it gets done, or what it costs... as long as it works.

speaker: Catherine
content: You're hiding from the DisCity army, making backdoor deals with guerrillas... You must want something pretty badly. Something you'd do anything for.

speaker: Catherine
content: If you're bold enough to kill me, why not be bold enough to use me instead? Most of your soldiers can't do what I can. Even the metropoles haven't fully figured out my superpowers.
With a soft chuckle, the 11-year-old girl leaned forward, a hand clasped to her chest as she marketed herself eagerly as if possessed by a demon.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...This, right here, is a top-secret next-gen weapon. One that might flip a war on its head someday. Don't you want it? Don't you need it?

speaker: Brock
content: Cut all that crap!
Before Dravyn could answer, someone else beat him to it. Brock grabbed the little girl by the back of her collar and hoisted her up into the air.

speaker: Catherine
content: Aaaah—I'm so scared—ha!
Her magnetic power flared, launching a pen that stabbed clean through Brock's hand. But he didn't even flinch.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...? Take this!
A military knife flew through the air. He caught it between his teeth, then grabbed it with his free hand and stabbed it into the ground.
Catherine froze, her eyes darting toward a handgun nearby.

speaker: Brock
content: Save your energy, it's not even loaded. Look, I know your playbook: three-meter range, can't reshape objects, and the acceleration you generate is mediocre at best. Honestly, it's barely better than that superboy's tricks on TV.

speaker: Brock
content: You're not stronger than me, kiddo. Don't underestimate the guerrillas. We're the reason your shiny home and all those metropoles are gonna come crashing down.
Catherine dangled in his grip, staring intently at Brock.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...With those? Your rusted-out guns and broken artillery? Please. You know that's not nearly enough.

speaker: Catherine
content: Fine, if I can't join you... I could be a hostage! Why not just get some weapons from my family? It's just business—very good business for you. And since they'd still want me back, I'm sure I could get you a discount.

speaker: Brock
content: You still don't get it.
With a sigh, he set the little girl down on a chair.

speaker: Brock
content: Look, kiddo, I might not be a dad, but my brother just got married. He and his wife are already picking out names for their three future kids. I get it. I know what parents are supposed to be.

speaker: Brock
content: Their whole job is to ensure their kid a happy life.

speaker: Catherine
content: The Andohars do want to make me happy. They make a lot of money to ensure it. And they are very serious about arranging my marriage.

speaker: Brock
content: I don't give a damn about their money or their deals. That's not happiness. They've failed at what parents should do. Completely.

speaker: Brock
content: You've never seen a real battlefield. You've never watched how fast a life can just... vanish. Out there, it doesn't matter that you're just a kid.

speaker: Brock
content: The violence... it consumes everyone. Even the ones with a good heart.
Deep in thought, she listened attentively and then tilted her head to one side.

speaker: Catherine
content: Then take me to see it?

speaker: Brock
content: No. I won't let you witness that. No child should.

speaker: Brock
content: You should learn about the weight of life through love, not through hate and death. If your family didn't teach you that... then they don't deserve to be parents.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...So... you're still sending me away?
At this, Brock's cool-guy act crumbled. He scratched his head with a conflicted expression.

speaker: Brock
content: I'm not that naive, kid. You've heard too much, and you've got all these dangerous ideas in your head. I can't risk the safety of my people.

speaker: Brock
content: I'm sending you someplace where they can actually teach you what matters.
He picked up the phone.

speaker: Brock
content: Hey, it's me. Yeah, I need a favor. Again. I've got a... a situation. A little girl needs a place to— No no no, it's not like that! Just listen for a sec!! Your place is safe, right? I need somewhere trustworthy.
After a frantic scramble of explanations, the guerrilla leader hung up the phone, drenched in sweat.

speaker: Brock
content: For now, I'll send you to Nirvana Port. Someone there will look after you, and you'll be safe and well-fed.
Dravyn stood speechless, and Catherine's face fell in disappointment.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...Fine. Last deal. You agree, and I promise I won't spill any of your little secrets.

speaker: Catherine
content: Do you have horses in DisCity? The real, four-legged kind. Can I ride a horse to Nirvana Port? Come on, say yes! It'd be so cool if I got to ride one!

speaker: Dravyn
content: Just send her away! Right now!
After all the commotion, they finally picked a day without sandstorms and sent Catherine off on a small vehicle bound for Nirvana Port.

speaker: Brock
content: Relax, kiddo. We smashed them good last time. Took their spirit and their gear. They won't be dumb enough to come back for seconds. Who wants to bite off more than they can chew?

speaker: Brock
content: So enjoy the quiet while it lasts! Take a real breath for once.

speaker: Catherine
content: "Quiet"?
She turned back.

speaker: Catherine
content: It was a major victory, I'll give you that. But if I were running your operation... I'd be more careful now, not less.

speaker: Catherine
content: Why would anyone go out of their way to crush an ant? They only would... if the ant showed it was strong enough to be a threat.

speaker: Helena
content: Cough cough... Is this thing on? Ugh... Huff... Okay... I'll try anyway...

speaker: Helena
content: Brock... it's me. We ran out of time. And vehicles. We cleared out the underground lab in Nirvana Port, and many people made it there. Hopefully, it'll protect them from the heat. Those guns you captured... they're important, right? I'm going to try and hide them before it's too late.

speaker: Helena
content: Just in case I don't make it back... there's something I need to say.

speaker: Helena
content: I hate war, and I've sworn never to take part in it. I'm a scientist. I wanted to help people through my research, not make weapons to kill. Not see my work turned into... blood. Every night, I see it. I can't escape it.

speaker: Helena
content: That's why I left you. I thought I could stay away from all this. But then I'd hear about our people suffering, see those smug faces from the metropoles... and I'd get so angry. So helpless. Part of me always wanted to run right back to you. To fight.

speaker: Helena
content: And now... many others will too. Hands used to work and farm will transport weapons for you. Those who heal lives will run into crossfire to save wounded fighters. We'll help, whatever the cost. However they retaliate.

speaker: Helena
content: We're not soldiers... but we can't just do nothing. It's in our blood, Brock. Yours and ours. This city... it's in us. We can't just watch it burn.

speaker: Helena
content: So promise me something. Just this one thing.

speaker: Helena
content: Keep their hands clean. The civilians, the volunteers—the people who still remember what peace feels like. However righteous the fight is... don't let killing become normal to them. Once you cross that line... you'll never come all the way back.

speaker: Helena
content: If you have to stay on this battlefield, then keep their hands clean. The people who believe in you—let them go home when this is over. Let them still remember how to live. You've already got blood on your hand. So you carry the weight. That's your duty as a soldier. Walk through the hell, so they don't have to.

speaker: Helena
content: As for me... I'll be waiting for you. On the other side.

speaker: Helena
content: ...But take your time, alright? Win this war. Live a long life. Grow old in a free DisCity... and then come tell me all about it.

The tape ended with a soft click. The clouds had parted, spilling moonlight across a sea of white sand. He lifted his head, dazed, and his eyes found the familiar silhouette of Nirvana Port in the distance—a view he had gazed upon countless times from this very spot.
Now, he stared only at the massive wreckage that buried his beloved. She had gone to hell ahead of him, just as she'd said she would.

speaker: Brock
content: ...We were so close...

speaker: Brock
content: If you hadn't knocked me out, I would've made it. At least we would've been together...

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...I couldn't let you throw your life away.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The military's in chaos. This is our opening. We move two days from now, gathering allies inside the city. But to unite them, we need a symbol. The guerrilla banner. And your name.

speaker: Dravyn
content: When we win, DisCity goes independent. The metropoles won't take it lying down. First, they'll cut supplies. Then they'll invade. It'll probably be more nuclear strikes coming.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Then the real fight begins. Fear everywhere. The city's gonna need hope, and you're the one who gives it to them. Isn't that what you do best?

speaker: Dravyn
content: So live. Do what only you can do.

speaker: Brock
content: Heh... You're right... You're damn right...

speaker: Brock
content: I can't die... Not now. She's waiting... waiting for me to bring her victory. I'll live—long enough to make every last one of them pay.

speaker: Brock
content: Catherine was right. Our gear's garbage. We need better. We must close the gap.

speaker: Brock
content: Let's move. The bunker at Nirvana Port is still stuffed with weapons we got last time. All the Andohar gear Helena bled to save. It's all there.

speaker: Brock
content: We're going in, taking it all back... and then we're gonna break their legs with their own damn guns!
Battle Report—from Dravyn
That's what Brock told me. And I believe he meant every word of it. He was going to use the enemy's own guns to kill them all.

June 17th to June 29th. Brock led search and rescue in the ruins of Nirvana Port. July 3rd. Brock escorted the survivors and supplies back to camp. July 10th. Brock met with every unit of the guerrillas. Handed out commendation medals he'd made himself. July 25th. Brock led the assault that destroyed the remaining missile silos left behind by the metropoles. August 27th. Brock united the DisCity army and staged the mutiny.
He still died, after giving his speech, after seeing the Independence Army formally established.
[Speech]

September 15, N.F. 66
DisCity

speaker: Brock
content: I never thought I'd come back like this.

speaker: Brock
content: Five years ago, when Speaker Damon was assassinated by the metropoles, I left the military. I joined the guerrillas to avenge my friend. After the massacre at Nirvana Port, I left WhiteSands and returned to the army. Both journeys were soaked in this city's blood and suffering.

speaker: Brock
content: All this time, DisCity has endured tragedy after tragedy. We've carried anger, fear, and grief. Some of us swore revenge. Others grew tired, wanting to compromise, to step back.

speaker: Brock
content: But we all know the truth: concessions won't earn us respect. Our suffering was never caused by "disobedience." It comes from one thing: a lack of "independence."

speaker: Brock
content: We have no sovereignty. No means to defend ourselves. That's what gives them power to trample over us—whenever they want.

speaker: Brock
content: And that's exactly why the Independence Army was born. That's why we keep growing stronger.

speaker: Brock
content: We're not just guerrillas and DisCity soldiers. We are councilors, teachers, workers, scientists. People from every walk of life, standing together on the same front.

speaker: Brock
content: Stay clear. Stay rational. Stay brave. We will overcome grief and fear. Even if it takes one year, ten, or twenty, our goal will never change.

speaker: Brock
content: DisCity will be independent. Sovereignty belongs unconditionally to the people. We must win this. And we will win.

speaker: Brock
content: A cause that inspires generations to face death without flinching? That cause... is bound to triumph.
In all his years of giving speeches, that last one was his best. But he had a terrible first draft. He threw it away. I fished it out of the trash.

"From now on, more people will step onto this battlefield. They will witness death. They will experience loss. They will kill... To achieve victory, their souls will never be clean again. That is the true sacrifice. And we must honor it. If we cannot avoid this bloody path, then we cannot only bring back hatred and death."

"We must fight to eliminate injustice. To forge something new, for survival, justice, peace, love. We must trade those battles and sacrifices for a better future. This is the promise we have to make them believe. And then we have to fulfill it. That is the only way to truly honor their sacrifice."
"That way... even with blood on their hands... they can walk through hell with a clear conscience."
Speech concluded, he rendered a bold salute, then marched with commanding strides down the long steps and back behind the stage.
The moment he was out of the audience's sight, he collapsed.

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...Brock!
And just like that... the leader of the guerrilla movement, the first commander of the Independence Army, was gone.

The cause was radiation poisoning. On a rescue op, his protective suit was damaged. But he didn't fall back. Pulled two of our people out of the hot zone. And while he was at it, he secured those rare pits we desperately needed.
He held on for three months after that. Fought like hell to live. Until now.

speaker: Brock
content: Gasp... Gasp... Well, I did my best, buddy... Just... couldn't finish the job... Don't go holding that against me, alright...

speaker: Brock
content: Is Death coming for me... I can see my wife...

speaker: Dravyn
content: Wait! Don't you dare... Catherine!! We need a medic over here, NOW!!

speaker: Dravyn
content: You are not dying here. I'll do whatever it takes, just stay with us! Do you hear me?!!

speaker: Brock
content: Ah... In that case... You're gonna have to... finish the job for me...

speaker: Brock
content: DisCity... It's... in your hands now...

The city gave Brock a simple funeral. A soldier's funeral. His final words lit a fire, just like he wanted. A new conviction in everyone who stands against the metropoles. On the ground, our fighters have a purpose. They're no longer lost.
But he still left me with the same question—
If conviction doesn't win the war, what's the value of the battle? What's the point of the sacrifice?
He gave them a flame, but he couldn't change the reality of this war. Even that Andohar brat knows it.

speaker: Catherine
content: Right before the explosion, Brock sent every last transport vehicle he had. Helena shoved me onto one and told me to get out of Nirvana Port.

speaker: Catherine
content: She stayed. Said those captured weapons meant a lot to Brock... that she had to go and salvage them.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...As if any of that junk could last a second against a nuke.
And yet, she didn't run away from the guerrillas. I saw her at the funeral. Dressed in black, standing with the rest of us.

speaker: Catherine
content: That nuke was bought from the Andohar family. I know it better than anyone. So trust me, it wasn't the only one. A strike like that will happen again.

speaker: Catherine
content: As the new commander of the DisCity Independence Army, can you accept that?

speaker: Catherine
content: ...I can't.
[Truth Declassified] Documentary

speaker: Newscast
content: In N.F. 115, DisCity has taken the decisive step of unveiling the long-concealed BR-003 to the public—a direct response to the aggressive Tide of Ashes launched by the farlands.

speaker: Newscast
content: As the optical camouflage dissolved, we witnessed the ultimate deterrent against humanity's most belligerent extremists, as well as the embodiment of DisCity's extraordinary efforts to suppress and relocate BR-003.

speaker: Newscast
content: Newly declassified documents now offer a glimpse into the prolonged city-state conflicts that have remained shrouded in secrecy.

speaker: Newscast
content: From previously released information, we know that in N.F. 106, DisCity hosted the 12th Great Expo. At that time, the observatory still stood on the surface, serving as a symbol of hope that this marvel beneath the stars might help mend the fractures between city-states.

speaker: Newscast
content: But that hope was shattered. During the exhibition, Mania extremists attempted to spread contamination, ultimately triggering BR-003 on site. The catastrophe claimed thousands of lives and shattered a fragile peace.

speaker: Newscast
content: At that time, humanity lacked the means to suppress the Black Rings. The mental corruption caused by hazardous information was irreversible. To protect the public, DisCity concealed the existence of BR-003, limited the release of information about the tragedy, and intensified its crackdown on Mania.

speaker: Newscast
content: For years, we were led to believe it was solely the work of Mania extremists. But now, with war once again at our doorstep, a more alarming possibility emerges: that the Outlands and the Underground Maniacs had already formed an alliance.

speaker: Newscast
content: They saw their opportunity in N.F. 103, the year FAC was crippled by the Eclipse Operation, and the last of the DisCorps forces had withdrawn. They believed it was the perfect moment to break DisCity apart and overthrow the established order.

speaker: Newscast
content: They failed then. And they will fail now. Because though DisCity's defenders may have been absent from public view, their loyalty never wavered. They've been vigilantly operating beyond our borders, guarding against external threats.

speaker: Newscast
content: Now, they have returned. And with them, we reclaim our strength, confront our history, and secure the future of our city-state...

speaker: Panicked Civilian
content: It hurts... It's burning hot... Help me...

speaker: Panicked Civilian
content: Why is this happening... hnngh... WAAAHH—
[Transition: Mimic TV Channel Change/TikTok Swipe] Sound effect, black screen

speaker: EDGE-03
content: If we had any other choice, we wouldn't take such drastic measures. But this war... it must end now.
[Transition: Syndicate Streets] Add TV static

speaker: Max King
content: Stay calm, everyone! The Speaker of the City Council is here! Your Max King has arrived with everything you need!
[Power Off] Sound effect: THUD— head smashing into screen

speaker: Max King
content: What the hell is this about?!
As he scrolls through a stream of videos, Speaker Max King comes face-to-face with his own image, and nearly hurls his terminal across the room in rage.

August 14, N.F. 115 15:00
West District Temporary Underground Defense Works
A fragile, three-day stalemate has held since EDGE's declaration on August 11th.

Though direct conflict has paused, the farlands' Tide of Ashes refuses to recede, blocking vital shipping routes. In response, DisCity has cranked its propaganda engine to full capacity, pushing the amended mobilization order into a second round of debate.
The message is clear: beneath the quiet, both sides are preparing, probing defenses, and gathering strength. Neither has any intention of stopping.

It all leaves Max King sick with frustration, a feeling he feeds by obsessively checking the very news that demoralizes him. Like now, he anonymously logs into a popular forum where the war has ignited a firestorm of speculation and fear.

<color=#fb9259>Outlanders</color><size=28> are all </size><color=#fb9259><size=52>butchers</color></size>. The more brutal we are, the better.
My cousin just enlisted <color=#fb9259><size=45>yesterday</color></size>. Says he's not afraid, <size=28>but I'm terrified for him...</size>
<color=#fb9259><size=52>Peace</color></size> talks are a joke. <color=#fb9259>Kill</color> all those Outland mutts!
The <color=#fb9259><size=45>FAC's</color><size=28> just a bunch of losers</size>. All this time and no real progress...

And then there's the deadweight <color=#fb9259><size=52>West District</color></size>!
The <color=#fb9259>new mobilization order</color> is REAL. They're literally grabbing people off the street into trucks rn. <size=28>If you don't wanna die, </size><color=#fb9259>STAY INSIDE</color>.
So easy for people to scream for war when <color=#fb9259><size=45>it's not their family on the front lines</color></size>.
<size=28>All these </size><color=#fb9259>armchair</color> generals <size=45>should be the first ones handed a rifle!</size>
<color=#fb9259><size=52>This is crazy! Actual madness!</color></size>

OMG the new <size=52>EDGE</size> <color=#fb9259>weapon</color> is terrifying. <size=28>That'll shut people up.</size>
But the <color=#fb9259><size=45>Tide of Ashes</color></size> is still there... so the <color=#fb9259>Outlanders</color> haven't really backed down, right?
How long until this <color=#fb9259>"ceasefire"</color><size=28> falls apart</size>? Bet they're back at it by <color=#fb9259>tomorrow</color>.
LOL it's the same story <color=#fb9259><size=52>every time</color></size>. <color=#fb9259>Ceasefire on paper</color>, fighting by morning.

I just wish we had <color=#fb9259><size=45>a real leader</color></size> who could actually <color=#fb9259><size=52>win</color></size> this thing...

<color=#fb9259><size=45>...How much longer will this go on? My stash is running low.</color></size>

Okay, so one of my relatives does supply runs to <color=#fb9259>Paradeisos</color> and gave me some <color=#fb9259>legit</color> tea:
That <color=#fb9259>big thing in the sky</color> is a distraction... The real power move is the <color=#fb9259>DisCorps! Those psychos</color> are coming back!

...Okay but lowkey they might be onto something. I saw some soldiers in weird, old-school <color=#fb9259>uniforms</color> the other day. Apparently not the FAC's.

I heard they're the reason WhiteSands became a <color=#fb9259>bloodbath</color> back in the day!
If <color=#fb9259>they</color> are really stepping in, the Outlands are so screwed.
See? This is what we need. The <color=#fb9259>old guards</color> know how to get stuff done.

But hello?? Remember they were all <color=#fb9259>insane</color>... Aren't we just trading one nightmare for another?

IDGAF, I'm all for <color=#fb9259><size=45>DisCorps</color></size>. We need an <color=#fb9259>iron fist</color> right now.
