This is a golden opportunity! Why aren't we grabbing it?! Are you people crazy?!
<color=#fb9259><size=28>I don't care who's in charge, just stop using us as cannon fodder...</color></size>

lol why is everyone so stressed? <color=#fb9259>It's fiiine</color>. Just be happy we can still post our nonsense online.
Who knows which one of us is gonna get <color=#fb9259><size=52>perma-logged off</color></size> next, heh.
<size=28>Will it be a catastrophe, a Black Ring, or DisCorps that gets us? </size><color=#fb9259>Same diff in the end</color>...
Reaching his limit, he fumbles for his phone to make the call he's always been cautious about, but someone arrives before he can—

speaker: Secretary
content: Is there something you need, Mr. Speaker? If you need to reach someone, I can handle that for you.

speaker: Max King
content: Do you really have to watch my every move?

speaker: Secretary
content: I'm afraid so, sir. These are extraordinary times. I need to stay on top of your schedule. Please don't hesitate to tell me what you need arranged.
Her meaning is perfectly clear to Max King. She is less an assistant and more a warden, her true purpose to monitor him and preempt any unsanctioned actions.
Apparently, his gut response to the last "directive" has been a mistake, eroding their trust and triggering this increased scrutiny from EDGE.

Is it his aggression in the council? A slip of the mask when he dealt with Nirvana during the Great Expo? Or is this always his destiny, to be the outsider who finally reached the inner circle only to find a locked door?
Looming over it all is the enigma of EDGE itself...
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Elvira
content: Public intel on EDGE is practically nonexistent. They have all this authority and all these secrets, but they also operate under a really strict, self-imposed code. Their ability to "guide" humanity is actually very limited.

speaker: Elvira
content: I heard that the scientists who founded E.D.G.E. set it up that way. And the original members were all scientists.

speaker: Elvira
content: But as years went by, the members changed. The group's makeup got more complex. Where they come from, in what areas and under what pretext they "guide" humanity, how members relate to each other... it's all a mystery now.
[Exit Flashback]
The invisible grip around his neck tightens again, stealing his words. Max King falls silent as he slowly puts away his terminal.

speaker: Max King
content: I need to get through to the MBCC.

speaker: Max King
content: Look at the West District. It's a powder keg. If this continues, we'll have a full-scale catastrophe on our hands. Chief ${PlayerName} has the capability and respect to get ahead of this. I need his support.
female_content: Look at the West District. It's a powder keg. If this continues, we'll have a full-scale catastrophe on our hands. Chief ${PlayerName} has the capability and respect to get ahead of this. I need her support.

speaker: Secretary
content: Sir, as I've said, Chief ${PlayerName}'s condition has taken a turn. Right now the Chief is being treated at the best sanatorium in Eastside and cannot leave at the moment.

speaker: Max King
content: Why there? Why not the MBCC? Or Banyan? Sending the Chief so far away makes no sense.

speaker: Secretary
content: We're living in extraordinary times. For someone of Chief ${PlayerName}'s stature, we must take every precaution. We can't be too careful with his security.
female_content: We're living in extraordinary times. For someone of Chief ${PlayerName}'s stature, we must take every precaution. We can't be too careful with her security.

speaker: Max King
content: ...If it's that serious, then I need to see him. ${PlayerName} is a crucial asset to this city. And he's a friend. I should be there for him when he's having a rough time.
female_content: ...If it's that serious, then I need to see her. ${PlayerName} is a crucial asset to this city. And she's a friend. I should be there for her when she's having a rough time.

speaker: Secretary
content: I'm afraid the doctors are insisting on absolute rest. No visitors. If you have a message, I can see that it's delivered.

speaker: Secretary
content: Besides, you're quite busy with your own affairs, aren't you? EDGE needs you in front of the cameras, keeping up morale.
A moment of silence falls.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Morale. What is any of this pageantry actually accomplishing?
Suppression, ridicule, surveillance—these threats leave him cold. They cannot touch him.
What truly torments Max King is his own powerlessness, a bitter truth underscored in moments like this one.
And so, no matter how deep his reluctance, the Speaker of the City Council allows himself to be "escorted" back to the cameras by the secretary's smiling, inescapable presence.
[Black Screen]
[Scene Change] Confinement Cell
Night falls. The interrogations have ended, and for a brief moment, Selyna's cell is left unguarded.
But she remains locked in the most severe form of anti-Mania restraint. Pain has made sleep nearly impossible, and at the sound of approaching footsteps, her eyes snap open.

speaker: Selyna
content: Who's there?!

speaker: Selyna
content: DisCity dogs... you come to kill me? Go ahead!!!

Standing before her is a frail, pale girl—utterly ordinary, with no discernible power or killing intent. She looks harmless; back in Selyna's homeland, someone like her would have been assigned to production duty, far from the front lines.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Selyna?
Her hand shakes, but she still reaches for the control panel and slightly lowers the suppression frequency.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...I'm not a guard here. I'm not here to kill you, but I can't set you free either. I just thought... you shouldn't have gone through all this pain.
Then Selyna notices the girl's elaborate clothing—the unmistakable style of a DisCity socialite, something she's seen in intelligence reports. Rage flares in the farland warrior's eyes.

speaker: Selyna
content: Don't think I'll fall for your tricks! Go to hell!!!
The silver-haired girl opens her mouth as if to speak, bites her lower lip, and eventually takes a step back.

speaker: Elvira
content: You don't have to be so hostile. I just... don't want to see an Outlander die like this.
Having mustered the courage to speak, she turns quickly and leaves, head lowered, leaving Selyna alone in confusion.
[Scene Change] El Exits the Corridor

Elvira slips away from the detention area, the special access card hidden in her palm as she steals back into the regular zone. Her heart still hammers against her ribs. So far, no one at MBCC has noticed her.
After all, the entire facility is in chaos right now.
[MBCC] Lounge

After EDGE declared a state of emergency, ${PlayerName} was taken away, officially for a health examination. But Elvira knows better. It is house arrest. Whether because he's in someone's way or simply deemed too unpredictable, the result is the same.
female_content: After EDGE declared a state of emergency, ${PlayerName} was taken away, officially for a health examination. But Elvira knows better. It is house arrest. Whether because she's in someone's way or simply deemed too unpredictable, the result is the same.

content: Without ${PlayerName}, MBCC has turned isolated and restricted, its internal flow of information choked off.

Elvira herself is also under surveillance. She needs more—intelligence that can bypass the Bureau's constraints, something beyond what Stewart's inheritance offered. She needs newer, wider sources. But she can't do it alone, not when trapped here.
What can she do...?

speaker: Max King
content: Stay calm, everyone! The Speaker of the City Council is here! Your Max King has arrived with everything you need!
The noise from the Recreation Area breaks through her thoughts. Elvira halts mid-step. The television is still on, and a familiar face flashes across the screen.
The absurd performance draws laughter from the crowd gathered around. Under all this tension, everyone needs a distraction.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...He's really bad at acting...
And yet... the spectacle gives her an idea.
[Scene Change] MBCC Corridor (or Witching Hour Underground Parking Garage)
In the MBCC's underground garage, a transport team from the West District delivers a new group of Sinners contaminated by the shackles to Nightingale.

speaker: West District Staff Member
content: That's the last of them. We gotta go. There are still a lot of people back in the West District who need medical attention.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Understood. Leave the Sinners to MBCC. We're counting on you over there in the West District.
With a crisp salute, the staff member turns and hurries back to his companion.

speaker: West District Staff Member
content: Let's hurry. We're short-handed as it is, we've gotta get back— Hm? Who are you?
An unfamiliar girl grabs his sleeve. She looks up at him, her expression timid.

speaker: Elvira
content: Please... let me come with you. I can help.

speaker: West District Staff Member
content: ...But your hands are shaking.
The West District has been ravaged by the Tide of Ashes—or rather, by the war it represents. Elvira reads the thought in his eyes: He can't let a child go there in a time like this.
The fear she feels is raw and real, far beyond the reach of her acting. For once, she lets it show.

speaker: Elvira
content: I'm sorry, I lied... My dad works at the Bureau, but my mom... she's stationed in the West District. I'm just... really worried about her.

speaker: Elvira
content: Can you take me to her?
[Syndicate Battlefield]
Twisted storms ravage the streets, unleashing waves of Mania contamination. The city lies in ruins as terrified civilians scatter in panic, desperately seeking shelter.
Yet for the FAC soldiers, these catastrophes are not the most terrifying enemy they face.
Against the rampaging Tide of Ashes, they stand their ground, defending every street as if it were their last.

speaker: Street Thug
content: Go to hell, you Outland mutts! This is all your fault!!
Fsssst— He ignites a Molotov cocktail, sending fresh waves of panic through the crowd.
An armored hand grabs him from behind, knocks him down, and snatches the bottle, extinguishing the flame.

speaker: Street Thug
content: Wh-what are you doing? I'm doing this for DisCity! They're obviously all—ugh!
The soldier lands a solid punch to the thug's face. Even the most good-natured among them has reached his limit.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Stop making things worse! What are you doing running around outside at a time like this? Get to a shelter now! The best thing you can do for DisCity is to keep your damn self alive, you idiot!

The subdued man is shoved toward the evacuation line, whimpering as he goes. But the damage is done. Panic has already taken root. Inside the shelter, people instinctively distance themselves from anyone who looks foreign.
Since the Great Expo, tensions between city-states have steadily escalated. Anti-Outland sentiment has trickled down, poisoning even ordinary citizens.
At this rate, the authorities will have no choice but to separate locals from outsiders inside the shelters, just to prevent further chaos.
But where would they find the personnel? In a place like Syndicate, with its constant churn of people—immigrants, descendants, drifters—hoping to avoid violence is a pipe dream.
—If real conflict breaks out, who should he protect?
The hand that struck through his armor burns like fire, even through the protection.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Siglinde
content: Sir, if I may. The FAC's core tenet is "protection." But in practice, does that not often mean you're reacting to a threat only after it has already manifested? Wouldn't it be too late?

speaker: Siglinde
content: I'm curious about your view on the principle that "the best defense is a good offense." Why hold to a purely defensive stance? Is it a matter of doctrine... or capability?
[Exit Flashback]

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Tch... She doesn't have a damn clue...
From a distance, someone in a small vehicle has witnessed the entire scene.
[Different Street]

speaker: West District Staff Member
content: I'm sorry, kid... With things as they are, we can't take you to the Executive Committee to find your mother anymore. There are too many dangerous incidents along the way, and we can't guarantee your safety.

speaker: West District Staff Member
content: There's a shelter entrance nearby. We can head there to take cover and help out while we're at it. Would that be okay with you?
Elvira nods.

speaker: Elvira
content: I'm coming with you.
She tries to appear braver, but as she follows them out of the vehicle, her legs tremble so violently she nearly stumbles.
The rumbling engines, the howling sandstorm, the screech of Manic Entities, the screams and roars of the crowd... She still hasn't adjusted to any of it. But what she just witnessed is worse.

Inside the underground shelter, a clamoring crowd presses into every available space. Some shove anxiously forward; others weep in silence. Many glare with naked hostility. It's impossible to tell who's from DisCity and who's an Outlander—everyone seems to be sizing up the unfamiliar faces in their own way.
In the thick air, heavy with gunpowder, mud, and sweat, Elvira catches a familiar scent.
[Flashback Intercut]

speaker: Street Thug
content: Go to hell, you Outland mutts! This is all your fault!!

speaker: Selyna
content: Don't think I'll fall for your tricks! Go to hell!!!

speaker: Jelena
content: See, Chief? Even those with blood-stained hands can have a heart. They can love. They just choose carefully who deserves their love... That's what DisCity has taught me.
[Exit Flashback]
Her head throbs as if splitting open, but she can't stop now. If she does, everything she's worked for will be wasted.
Where to next? Wait for the clerks to finish and follow them to the Executive Committee to find Matilda Cavendish? Or explore this area and gather more intelligence?
According to this morning's news, Max King is also making a public appearance in a nearby district. If she could meet him again... that might prove useful.
Elvira struggles to think as voices flood her ears—curses, pleas, desperate calls—all blending into a wall of sound.
Until a single name cuts through the noise, sharp and clear.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Wait, kids, don't go! We'll get medicine, but you have to keep yourselves safe right now!

speaker: Sibilla
content: Sable wouldn't want you to put yourselves in danger!
As the staff member finishes clearing the safety entrance, he turns to find Elvira standing in a trance, already moving toward the crowd of refugees.

speaker: West District Staff Member
content: Um, kid, we're already at... Wait! Where are you going?!!

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Sorry, I... I just remembered I have something to do...

Another sudden tremor shakes the ground. Half a wall shears away and crashes down, blocking the path between him and Elvira. In the chaos of falling debris, she seizes her chance and vanishes into the sea of people.
[Scene Change] Alley
Sibilla huddles in a triangular space formed by broken walls, barely sheltered from the onslaught of the Tide of Ashes.

Though she's no stranger to catastrophes, the devastation here—in this "prosperous," densely packed district—far exceeds anything she witnessed in her hometown. It's clear the Syndicans have no experience dealing with disasters of this scale.
She anxiously fiddles with an old mobile terminal in her hands. The Mania storm raging overhead chokes the air with interference, making communication nearly impossible.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Hello? Hello? Ashley? Allen? Can you hear me? Oh, thank heavens, this old thing still works...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Now you listen to me, and you listen good. Don't even think about going out for medicine. You wouldn't know what's out there, and we can't just give Sable anything. Her poor body's too weak as it is, and this is no common fever. Cold medicine won't touch it.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Once I find Gracelyn, I'll be back right away. I'll be counting on you looking after her, alright? Yeah, just wait for me. I'm on my way now—

speaker: Elvira
content: Wait—!

A silver-haired girl emerges from the mouth of the dark alley. She stands poised at the edge of the ruin, dressed in the unmistakable style of Eastside's upper levels—her clothes crafted from soft, lustrous fabric that glimmers with understated wealth.
Sibilla gasps. Her terminal clatters to the ground.
The girl doesn't seem to notice Sibilla's panic. A light sweat glistens on her skin from her hurried chase, and her eyes shine with urgency as she squeezes into the cramped corner.

speaker: Elvira
content: I... I overheard you mention someone named Sable. Is she unwell? Does she need cyborg repairs? Maintenance, or parts... I-I could help!

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Cy...borg? What?
With a deafening roar, the underground shelter collapses, sending dust billowing everywhere. Reacting on pure instinct, Sibilla seizes Elvira's arm and hurls them both sideways.
She barely manages to pull Elvira into the sewer tunnel.

speaker: Sibilla
content: We can get to an air-raid shelter from here, though it's a bit of a walk. We can set out once you've caught your breath.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Just a coincidence. Of course it is. The name isn't uncommon, but cyborgs are... Ugh, I'm so stupid...
The vibrant energy she displayed only moments before vanishes instantly, leaving in its wake an exceptionally frail figure—so thin she can barely hold up her own swaying body.

Elvira's head sinks low as her whole body seems to crumple inward, finally struck down by the immense weight of the fatigue and helplessness accumulated over the past days. She releases a long, weary sigh before she speaks, her voice reduced to a muted and hollow sound.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Ma'am, are you an Outlander?

speaker: Sibilla
content: I... I don't think so? My grandfather's generation settled here in Syndicate. You know how many of us there are here. So I suppose I'm a DisCity citizen now, haha.

She dares not say too much. Parfait had specifically warned her to keep a low profile before leaving, especially after Sibilla appeared on television with the investment guru, shouting those words... And conflicts have already erupted several times in the underground shelters.
...Sibilla lowers her head, realizing the lie she once told has now twisted into truth. Is this her punishment for lying as a whistle? Now she has no way to uncover what truly happened to Furor.
Elvira watches her for a long moment before speaking softly.

speaker: Elvira
content: But you must still hold deep feelings for your homeland.
She points to Sibilla's bracelet. Though broken and missing many beads, leaving it threadbare in places, it has been carefully restrung and clearly cherished.

speaker: Sibilla
content: It was a gift. From my friends back home.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Could you tell me about them?

Sibilla's hesitation hangs in the air. In response, the girl across from her lowers her head, as if talking about a faraway homeland evokes many memories. For a long moment, she is silent, lost in some distant world, before she begins to speak, her voice slow and heavy with the weight of nostalgia.

speaker: Elvira
content: <color=#fb9259>Jelena</color>... That's the name my mom gave me. I grew up here in DisCity, and it wasn't until I was older that I learned it was an Outland name.

speaker: Elvira
content: My mom was actually an Outlander. But by the time I learned the truth... she was already gone. I never got to know her. To know about her home, her people... or how she felt, living here.

speaker: Elvira
content: But I want to know. Whether it's about her, or about your friends... I want to know those stories from far away. Please.
Sibilla has always held her past—the far-away stories, her dread of Furor—apart from her new life in Syndicate. How could she burden them, when they've already given her so much?
But the girl's own raw history disarms her, touching a secret, guarded corner of the Outlander's heart.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...I see. Let's find somewhere safer to talk, Miss Jelena. We have time.

Originally tunnels from the Rustfire era, the underground shelter has been hastily converted, its conditions stark and primitive. Whenever tremors from the catastrophe above shake the foundations, a palpable wave of panic ripples through the caverns.

In this oppressive atmosphere, only the Speaker provides a glimmer of relief, playing the fool with such dedication that he becomes a beacon—the sole point of light in the overwhelming dark, drawing every eye and lifting every spirit he passes.

speaker: Max King
content: The Speaker of the City Council is here! Your Max King has arrived with everything you need! You are not alone facing this catastrophe! I'm right here by your side. I'll—hm?
Just as he tries to rally people's spirits, a small, ragged figure stumbles out of the gloom and clutches desperately at his hand.

speaker: Ragged Girl
content: H-help me... Mr. Speaker...

speaker: Max King
content: Are you alright? What happened—
Elvira?!
He recognizes her face and acts instantly, rubbing grime from his hands onto her features to disguise her, while speaking in a nervously urgent tone—

speaker: Max King
content: Oh, so you're a Sinner. Is your Mania flaring up? Then you must stay away from the crowd. Hurry, this way—

The mention of a Sinner losing control makes the pursuing cameras hesitate and pull back. It is all the chance Max King needs. He grabs Elvira's hand, and they dash around the corner, disappearing into the long corridor.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Max King
content: Why are you here? What happened? What's going on at the Bureau?
Elvira doesn't respond immediately. After a brief hesitation, she speaks in a hushed voice.

speaker: Elvira
content: Take me back to the Bureau first. I have something to do.

speaker: Elvira
content: I also have some intelligence. I'll find a way to pass it to you later.

speaker: Max King
content: I see. I'll figure something out. You just need to blend in with the group of abnormal Sinners. They'll take you there.

A mere few days apart, and yet the girl's eyes hold a different light. The once-timid illegitimate daughter, who once clung to the Bureau and her close friends for safety, now throws herself into the front line. She has clearly found a purpose—and with it, a newfound strength.
Watching her, Max King can't help but feel a tinge of envy. The crowd swarms around them, making any meaningful words impossible. It isn't until the moment of parting that a question occurs to him.

speaker: Max King
content: How did you know to find me here?

speaker: Elvira
content: You are on TV, aren't you? Lots of Syndicans have been watching. Some like you, some don't, but when they are all trapped in the shelter, everyone is wondering where Speaker King has gone.

speaker: Elvira
content: But you should be more careful. You're on TV so much. Anyone looking for you could easily find you. It's not safe. Watch your back, or you might get killed.
Max King freezes for a moment.

speaker: Max King
content: Many people have been watching... Anyone looking for me could easily find me...
His gaze sweeps over the crowd—faces marked by curiosity, excitement, disgust, and mockery. The reaction is unanimous: Max King commands attention wherever he goes.
And in this moment of stark recognition, a vague idea begins to take root.

speaker: Max King
content: —Your Max King is here!
[Scene Change] Detention Cell
After a day of grueling interrogation, Selyna remains locked in her cell. As the brief, guard-free window approaches, she hears footsteps and immediately recognizes them. It's that strange brat.

Selyna thought the little nuisance would have cleared out by now. Yet the girl shows up again. The footsteps stop at the control console. After a few seconds of tinkering, Selyna feels the restraining field around her weaken.

speaker: Selyna
content: @#¥@#¥@ (What's that brat up to... I'm not going to fall for her tricks...)
The thought flashes through her mind just as a faint melody drifts by on the air.
[Empty Scene] Elvira hums a melody. Can reuse Jelena's humming segment or just use the audio file.
...Does DisCity have tunes like this? She feels she's heard it somewhere before... somewhere in Fraser...
She cranes her neck to look, but finds only the visitor's retreating back, the melody fading away with her footsteps.
[Dimly Lit Hospital Ward]

The sharp scent of disinfectant surrounds you. Your body trembles with fever, wracked by chills as you drift in and out of a fractured consciousness. The strange odor of anti-Mania rays permeates the room, irritating your nerves.
Nightmares descend, and they ensnare you.

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: Get away... Get away...

speaker: Augustus
content: Stay back. This war is no place for you.
[White Flash] You finally manage to struggle upright and grab the person standing by your bed.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Chief?!
Your fingers close around Hecate's wrist. She startles at your touch, and the blanket she was adjusting slips from her grasp.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Sorry, I'm still a bit groggy...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why are you here? How would they let you come...

speaker: Hecate
content: I was worried about you, Chief. I asked Adjutant Nightingale for permission to visit. Are you alright?
Labored breaths, a racing heart, a cold sweat—the symptoms scream through you. Hecate's gaze is heavy with worry. In the past, you would have instinctively told her: you're fine.
But now...
You just cover her hand with your own and speak softly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not feeling well, actually. The Mania is still affecting me. But I think I'll be fine.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need your help.
The black triangle quietly drifts over from the corner of the room.

speaker: Schorl
content: I'll continue monitoring and suppressing Mania for you from outside your field of vision. That way, my presence won't unsettle you.
You lower your head briefly in thought, then look directly at it and say:

speaker: Option
options: That was my bad. I shouldn't have taken my frustration out on you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've grown too reliant on you when it comes to managing the shackles' contamination. Every time the Mania fluctuates, I end up directing my anxiety at you. That wasn't fair. I need to work on controlling my emotions better. If anything, I should be thanking you.
Schorl emits a series of strange sounds, unlike anything you've heard before. You can't tell if it's expressing confusion or merely recording your unexpected speech.

Nevertheless, it proceeds as requested. It activates its anti-Mania program to scan you, though the process seems to run a few more cycles than usual. Seizing the opportunity, you pose your questions.

speaker: Schorl
content: BR-003 is fully calibrated. We hold the advantage now, Chief. There's no need for you to take unnecessary risks fighting against the Black Ring anymore. BR-005 is also within controllable parameters.

speaker: Option
options: Are you planning to deploy BR-003?

speaker: Schorl
content: It remains a deterrent and a last resort. Causing mass casualties is never our intention, even if it's framed as serving the greater good. As long as alternatives exist, we will exhaust them first.

speaker: Option
options: So you're not launching a direct assault on BR-005?

speaker: Schorl
content: The enemy has anticipated that approach. They've stationed numerous Apostles of Ashes around BR-005 as a defensive measure. A frontal assault with our current forces would be costly.
The black triangle rotates slightly.

speaker: Schorl
content: We've formulated a more efficient strategy. If executed correctly, we can achieve victory with minimal sacrifice. To avoid causing you undue concern, I will refrain from detailing the specifics for now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To avoid causing me undue concern... It means this plan doesn't include rescuing Hella, does it? You might even be prepared to sacrifice her to keep "minimal losses." Is that it?

speaker: Schorl
content: We haven't reached that point yet.
With it, you feel its anti-Mania energy output slightly increasing. You make every effort to keep your composure.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's very thoughtful of you to carefully omit that part for my sake. I should thank you for that.
At your words, it emits that strange sound again. You decide to press on anyway.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Receiving such special treatment, should I take this as...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm still useful to Paradeisos? You need me emotionally stable and compliant because you still have uses for me. Is that it?

speaker: Schorl
content: ...You are important, of course. You may voice your requests freely. We always give them careful consideration, though we cannot promise they will be fulfilled.

speaker: Augustus
content: But that's not you. The reason you fight is far too frail.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...My goals haven't changed. But I can't keep making demands I know are impossible. Like she said, I still don't truly understand war. My convictions aren't strong enough.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't solve anything, can't even think clearly... because I've been drowning in confusion, anger, and pain. But that ends now. I can't keep avoiding questions just because I don't have answers.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: At least I should find an answer, in my own way.
You look at Schorl, finally speaking with genuine sincerity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Would you be willing to listen? To help me find that answer?

speaker: Schorl
content: The fact that you're approaching me honestly is progress in itself. Please state your request, Chief. I will convey it and await evaluation.

speaker: Option
options: Then... I want to meet someone.

content:
Scarface: Heya, little Chief! Been ages since we saw you last time. You still breathing out there? Ready to come bash some heads with us?
Scarface: Seriously, should we send a letter over or something?
Scarface: You know what we've been up to these days? Someone said they wanted a truce but just can't sit still. So we're gonna give them a very loud rebuttal! Gyahahahaha!
Military Doctor: Keep that noise to yourself. It's gross.
Military Doctor: I heard our acting commander is staying put. Stop your yapping and just kill the enemies.
You haven't checked your terminal messages for days, and quite a few have accumulated.
You close the terminal, no longer interested in the messages inside.
You tap out a brief response, but only silence answers. They must have moved to an area with poor signal reception again.
From the podium, the representative councilor from Paradeisos solemnly declares that, despite a days-long ceasefire, the Farland Alliance has ultimately chosen to resume hostilities.

speaker: Councilor A
content: The twenty-four-hour window has closed. It seems the Farland Alliance has chosen the path of greatest folly. They had a chance to end this. Instead, they have chosen to escalate.

speaker: Councilor A
content: In response, BR-003 has been activated for offensive operations. To mount a swift and decisive counteroffensive, we must consolidate the city's resources under a single, unified command. Therefore, we now bring to the floor for a vote: the DisCity Emergency Powers Act and the War Resolution Against the Farlands.

speaker: Councilor A
content: This resolution will authorize full military engagement and grant EDGE the clear, unambiguous authority to commandeer all city resources for the duration of this emergency. This is not merely procedural; it is the key to our victory.

speaker: Councilor B
content: But this draft... it deviates from the one originally proposed by Speaker Max King. Were these amendments approved by the Speaker himself?

speaker: Councilor A
content: Speaker King's position is always aligned with our own.
The other councilors whisper among themselves. The Speaker's absence is a profound shock at such a critical session.

Just as the chamber erupts in commotion, the doors burst open. Soldiers stream in, their strides long and determined. They shove the overwhelmed security guards aside without breaking formation, causing a collective gasp of shock and outrage.

speaker: Councilor B
content: What is the meaning of this?! The resolution hasn't even passed! DisCorps has no authority here. Get out!
Augustus glances at her with a contemptuous smile.

speaker: Augustus
content: I assumed the council leading this city would be smart enough to read the situation. Apparently, I overestimated you.

speaker: Augustus
content: The war is at our doorstep. It's time you learned who you can actually rely on to stay alive.

speaker: Councilor B
content: What—
With an air of unquestionable authority, Augustus strides to the front of the chamber and commandeers the central stage.

speaker: Augustus
content: I don't have time to waste on formalities. Let's cut to the chase.

speaker: Augustus
content: Under your "esteemed" leadership these past few years, DisCity has flourished, so thoroughly infiltrated by Mania extremists, completely exposed to Outland spies. The enemy knew every weakness before they even fired a shot.

speaker: Augustus
content: The FAC is pinned down in the DisSea. Our Hypercube reserves are almost gone. Even MBCC, our last bulwark against the Black Rings, has walked into an Outland trap and is now completely paralyzed.

speaker: Augustus
content: And now your so-called "ally" has unleashed a Tide of Ashes outside our walls. They've cut off every escape route. Let me be clear: they are not letting anyone out of this city alive.

speaker: Augustus
content: So, all those assets you've stashed in the Outlands and all those connections—what good are any of them if you can't physically escape?

speaker: Augustus
content: If we lose this war, your wealth becomes their spoils. And you won't be around to miss it.

speaker: Councilor A
content: ...Stop with the fear-mongering. We still have Paradeisos. And <color=#fb9259>BR-003</color>.

speaker: Councilor A
content: Compared to <color=#fb9259>BR-005</color>, our development of BR-003 is far more advanced. Our catastrophe weapon is superior. It can protect this city from any invasion.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hah, perfect timing! I've just received a new operational plan from EDGE. One that incorporates BR-003.

speaker: Augustus
content: Our goal isn't to break the enemy here. It's to bleed them dry while we spend as little as possible.

speaker: Augustus
content: While the FAC holds the line, I will take my forces to the Outlands. We will decapitate their war leadership and bring the entire region under control.

speaker: Augustus
content: EDGE has done the math. They trust in my capability to get it done. As for you?

speaker: Augustus
content: Your fortunes, your lives... to them, you're just a line item. Easily replaced with new councilors.
In the chamber, nearly half the councilors turn deathly pale.

speaker: Councilor
content: N-no one said the risk was this severe! Who can protect us? The FAC can't!

speaker: Councilor
content: Is there any way out of the city? Any way? Forget the assets. We need to get out!

speaker: Councilor
content: Can't we just destroy that Black Ring? MBCC... wait, what about the MBCC Chief? Isn't he the expert? Can your forces handle it?
female_content: Can't we just destroy that Black Ring? MBCC... wait, what about the MBCC Chief? Isn't she the expert? Can your forces handle it?

content: Their fear of war now greater than their fear of the rebel leader, they choose Augustus. The right choice.

speaker: Councilor
content: You said you wanted to reclaim everything you lost through war. So... if your forces can repel the enemy and protect DisCity, the council will agree to welcome you back.

speaker: Councilor
content: We'll give you everything. The FAC's authority, the rightful status of the DisCity military. EDGE has no right to interfere; they've failed us in this war. We will grant you absolutely everything.
Suddenly, a chorus of voices erupts. The councilors, their convictions shifting with the wind, rush to decide where to pledge their loyalties.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Is it really the case?

speaker: Augustus
content: So this chamber is now ready to "support" me? You're prepared to pardon our past on behalf of the city-state and restore DisCorps to its rightful place, just like that?

speaker: Augustus
content: And what of my opposition? I know many of you still hold a grudge.

speaker: Councilors
content: That's all in the past! Protect this city, and you'll have our full support as DisCity's general! Absolutely! We support you! The past is behind us! We stand with you now, General Augustus!
A single hand rises.

speaker: Clerk
content: I... object!
A sharp voice slices through the sycophantic chorus. The irony is palpable: it issues not from any councilor, but from the unassuming recording clerk stationed at the room's periphery.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Oh. I remember you.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: The military clique back then... they were all ambitious. Brutal. They'd always believed in rule through force. After they seized power, they brought nothing but suffering to the city-state. For twelve years.

speaker: Clerk
content: I know exactly what you've done.

speaker: Clerk
content: I may not be a councilor, but I understand the council's duty. It must resist both the temptation of self-interest and the threat of violence. Its sole purpose is to serve the city-state and its citizens. This is the institution meant to safeguard fairness and justice for all.

speaker: Clerk
content: No matter how you justify this—even if we ignore the past—it doesn't change the fact that you're trampling on our fundamental principles.

speaker: Clerk
content: Just look at what you're doing right now... storming in with soldiers, aiming guns, making threats. You exploit fear to corrupt them, all to seize more power for yourself.

speaker: Clerk
content: This isn't about "extraordinary measures for extraordinary times"... If you seize power like this, you'll only become more dependent on violence. The next time you face a challenge, you'll reach for your guns again, threatening and coercing until we're living the same nightmare all over again!

speaker: Clerk
content: Am I wrong, General Augustus?!
The answer he receives is solitary applause. Only Augustus claps for her challenger, leaving the councilors to watch with ashen faces.

speaker: Augustus
content: A fine speech. Do go on... Actually, let me ask—

speaker: Augustus
content: Who else agrees with him?
The moment her words hang in the air, a series of explosions thunder from outside, as if answering the general's challenge.

speaker: Augustus
content: It seems our enemy was counting on our schedule today. They've launched a precision strike on this building, hoping to decapitate our council before it can unite.

speaker: Augustus
content: Rest easy, councilors. My troops have already secured an evacuation route. Those who have cast their votes may follow my soldiers to safety.

speaker: Augustus
content: DisCorps will honor your support by ensuring you live to see tomorrow. Protecting this city remains our duty as soldiers.

speaker: Augustus
content: However, those who just voiced their opposition... you will stay.
A smile cuts across Augustus's face as chaos erupts throughout the chamber. She may blame the enemy's artillery, but the truth is written in the flash of each explosion—this is her masterpiece.

speaker: Augustus
content: I'd love to hear your thoughts in full. Come now, didn't you have more to say?

speaker: Clerk
content: ...You monster!

speaker: Augustus
content: How brave. It's good to see the new generation still has fire in its belly. I'll remember you.

speaker: Augustus
content: Besides this gentleman... anyone else?
Despite the council chamber's heavy soundproofing, the artillery outside announces itself as a deep, persistent tremor through the floor.
Augustus's gaze sweeps the room, silently tallying her trapped prey with amusement. One, two, three... eleven councilors. And one clerk. Just twelve people in total.

speaker: Augustus
content: Even fewer than I expected. Couldn't even convince your own colleagues to join your little protest.

speaker: Augustus
content: Last chance. Anyone want to change their mind?
Only a deathly silence answers her.

speaker: Clerk
content: ...I will not change my position. Surrendering now is pointless. As long as you plot to restore military rule, I will oppose you!
The others remain silent and unflinching. They stand firm, surrounded by guns, but in the end, not a single one steps forward to surrender.
A genuine smile finally graces Augustus's lips.

speaker: Augustus
content: Good. I was hoping you'd say that.

speaker: Augustus
content: Then let's stop the posturing. Time for the city-state's most stubborn councilors to see what DisCorps is really made of.
The lights abruptly die. In the darkness, a projection flares to life before the councilors, displaying a battered, broken army.
Their equipment is obsolete, their formations scattered. They look utterly vulnerable in the flickering light.

Augustus's gesture guides the projection upward, until it settles on a structure jutting from the wastes like a rusted tombstone: the ruins of Nirvana Port, its surface pockmarked by the unmistakable scars of a nuclear strike.
Long after the image fades, a stunned silence holds the chamber. Augustus intends to give them time to absorb the shock, but as the quiet stretches too long, she can't suppress a soft chuckle.

speaker: Augustus
content: Heh. Sorry to disappoint. But this is the reality. How powerful did you think an army of exiles could be after years in the wilderness?

speaker: Augustus
content: Our gear is obsolete. Our ranks can't be replenished. We've been wandering through sandstorms for years, struggling for basic supplies.

speaker: Augustus
content: These soldiers are covered in wounds, men who did the city-state's dirty work only to be cast aside. Mania corruption is eating them alive. Their morale is shattered; their minds are hanging by a thread.

speaker: Augustus
content: This... is the army I command. It can't defeat anything. It can only frighten you.

speaker: Augustus
content: BR-003 is no different. Just a bluff. EDGE can't actually deliver precision catastrophic strikes. The enemy saw right through it. That's why they've ignored our warning and expanded the battlefield.

speaker: Augustus
content: But you? You're still lost in a fantasy. You fear us. You publicly reject us. But secretly, you still believe we'll somehow defeat the enemy at your doorstep.

speaker: Augustus
content: Wake up! We can't save you. Only you can protect this city-state! So what are you waiting for?

speaker: Augustus
content: Economics, logistics, intelligence—they're all battlefields. War tests the strength of an entire city-state. But your infighting and paranoia have turned the front-line FAC into a hollow shell.

speaker: Augustus
content: And what are the diplomats doing?! Get out there! Build alliances. Navigate the negotiations. You are soldiers in this war, too.

speaker: Augustus
content: Stop the infighting. Stop the suspicion. Unite your allies. Pool your resources. Fight with everything you've got—your tactics, your wisdom, your very lives. Get up every time you fall. That is how you fight!

speaker: Augustus
content: So what if I try to seize power later? Then stand up to me like you are now. Show some backbone against intimidation. Unite and drive me back. It's that simple. That backbone is exactly why I chose you.

speaker: Augustus
content: Have you already forgotten the courage you just showed?
The recorder stares intently at the woman before him.
Is this some sort of manipulative rhetoric? He won't fall for it.
He will remember what these militants did when they seized power, even if everyone else forgets.
Exploiting the city-state's crisis for their own ends—that's what that person did. And she is no different. He can't afford to lower his guard. He must—
A raised hand in the silence cuts his thought short.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: I... on behalf of Nirvana, will provide supplies for the fight. It will take time, but I'll make it happen.

speaker: Clerk
content: You—

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: But I have conditions...
With a discreet swallow, the man races through his rehearsed points one last time. Then, steeling himself, he summons the courage to let the words tumble out in a single, rushed breath.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: These resources go under the FAC's unified management. They've been under long-term supervision. They've never betrayed our trust, and they have transparent protocols. They are the true backbone of this city's defense. That's who we support.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: If you truly have no intention of seizing power, if you really just want to protect this city-state... then prove it. Work with them.
The clerk stares at the Nirvana representative, dumbstruck.
Is he a spineless opportunist, or has he simply given up? Do they not realize how disastrous this will be?
Having finally managed to get through his carefully rehearsed speech, the Nirvana representative remains oblivious to the shocked stares around him.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: You've got to be kidding me. Quinn is donating stockpiled resources to the FAC? Is that actually true? And why would they come to you of all people?

speaker: Max King
content: My dear friend, is it not obvious? They've seen my livestreams! Everyone's reaching out! Plenty want to donate Hypercubes to support our brave soldiers in the FAC.

speaker: Max King
content: It's done wonders for their reputation in the West District, I tell you. Some are even saying Quinn ought to have a hand in building the new mine.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: You can't be serious. Quinn's president is Eirene Campbell, from Fraser's Campbell family! DisCity would never let her get anywhere near the West District mine. The 9th Agency is already looking into her.

speaker: Max King
content: Now, now... when we talk about ties to Fraser, isn't Nirvana in a similar boat? The impression you left during the Great Expo... not so easily forgotten, hm?

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Well... that... we could explain. We...

speaker: Max King
content: Let's not dwell on the past! Focus on the future. Your rivals are already putting on quite the show of allegiance.

speaker: Max King
content: It's not too late. Like you said, Nirvana's still a step above the Campbells. As long as you're willing to make a move, you won't lose to her.
With that, the Speaker handed over a check—a large sum, with an auspicious serial number that happens to be Parfait's favorite sequence of digits.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: ...I don't have the authority to deploy corporate assets. But there are... external contractors. I can send you their contacts.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Don't mention my name.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Naturally. Your heroism will be remembered.
[Exit Flashback]

speaker: Clerk
content: ...I'll keep in mind what you said. In the face of a crisis that threatens our very home, we have much to do. Cooperation with you is... necessary.

speaker: Clerk
content: ...But if during this time DisCorps causes trouble, if you try to overstep... I will stand against you immediately.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Excellent. You've finally learned to take the first step.

speaker: Augustus
content: So, for our next move—
Bam—
The heavily guarded door splinters open. Several silhouettes stand framed in the doorway, backlit by the harsh light.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Enough pretty speeches.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Show me your battle plans. Prove you can win.

speaker: Augustus
content: Of course.

speaker: Langley
content: Regaining trust always comes at a price. So tell me, are you ready to let the old foxes slip a collar on you?

speaker: Augustus
content: That depends what kind of collar you mean.
[Chief's portrait]
She watches you, a calculating smile on her lips.

speaker: Augustus
content: These shackles are tied to the Black Ring. Accepting them means accepting the contamination, doesn't it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm under the impression you need it to achieve your goals.
You walk toward her as you speak, just as you did yesterday when everything that mattered had been said.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Augustus
content: You've come.

speaker: Augustus
content: Our partnership ended a long time ago. Took you long enough to come say goodbye.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not here to say goodbye. I'm here to return to the battlefield.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You and your troops still need someone who can fight alongside you, don't you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If taking the entire city-state was something you could do alone, you wouldn't have come to me in the first place. You wouldn't have waited.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said you need someone who can fight with you. Does that person have to be a soldier?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is my first war; I was thrown into it. I tried to fight like a soldier because I wanted to protect the people I love.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I failed. That approach didn't work; it only caused more pain for them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even so, I still want to stay. To remain on the battlefield, but in my own way.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After all, war isn't just about hatred and killing. And victory isn't just about crushing the enemy. Don't you agree, General?
[Scene Change]
MK's feed is constantly updating. Once a major internet celebrity, he now commands everyone's attention with every comment he makes about the ongoing chaos.

In addition to Quinn and Nirvana's full support, the DisCity council has received a massive amount of mysterious funding from the Outlands, and through the same channel, they have bought a huge supply of Hypercubes.
This should have been impossible. Fraser never trusts outsiders on strategic operations. How could this possibly be?

Nevertheless, when MK shares the news, people find a new sense of hope. As public tension quickly eases, so does hostility, leading to a significant drop in the disputes, conflicts, and violent incidents that have been troubling the city-state.
[Scene Change] Detention Cell

speaker: Elvira
content: Those Outland elite operatives are too organized. They had to have inside help. If we can trace their comms, we might find the source.

speaker: Elvira
content: You said you could fix this, so hurry up. This war with them makes me sick.

speaker: Langley
content: Excellent work, Miss Stewart. You've got more talent than I gave you credit for. I'll pay you a visit when this wraps up.
[Scene Change] Flashback, Nirvana Port Command Center

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now to answer your question...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You asked me... what I'd do if I gave it everything I had... and still couldn't bring Hella back...
Answering this question proves so difficult, yet you refuse to give up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I really... lost her...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I'd get back up. And I'd destroy BR-005...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then... BR-003. BR-000. All of them. And every single bastard who creates them, every opportunist who tries to profit from them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hatred won't heal me. The pain and suffering... they're half from the Mania itself, and half from those vultures who feed on them. From now on, they're my enemies. I don't care about city-states or stances; none of it matters now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: From now on, wherever Mania rages, that's my battlefield. My enemy is all the suffering it brings. What happened to Hella, what I've been through... I won't let that happen to anyone else.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So no matter what it costs me, no matter how many times I fail... even if it takes the rest of my life. I'll keep fighting until I achieve total victory. Or until I die.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That... is my answer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't be your soldier, but it seems like we're headed to the same battlefield. If it's acceptance and trust you're looking for, you can find it in me—as your comrade.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Right now, I'm fighting to end this Black Ring war. Would you be willing to stand shoulder to shoulder with someone like that?
[Council]
You step up to Augustus. Taking her sword from Iron Mask's grasp, you offer it back to its rightful owner.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: DisCorps's name is already synonymous with pure, unchecked violence. It's a name people fear. If you're going to lead it, I trust you're ready for that weight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even the sharpest blade needs a scabbard. Otherwise, it can't be carried. It's the same with Sinners and the shackles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm ready, too. We'll shoulder every risk together, and claim victory as one.
A smile graces her lips.

speaker: Augustus
content: Heh, you truly are worthy of my attention. So what are we waiting for?

speaker: Augustus
content: Let's move. My blade's getting impatient.
[Scene Change]
At the ruins of Nirvana Port, the raging fires had died down, but through the howling night wind came the distant, muted thunder of guns from the front lines.
As enemy forces closed in, Dravyn attended to his duties. Amid the chaos, all those in panic instinctively turned to him, desperate to draw strength from their commander.

And that stubborn resilience of his did not waver. His face remained cold, betraying no emotion as he worked with methodical precision—issuing orders, coordinating logistics, processing intelligence...

speaker: Messenger
content: General! Catherine Andohar is gone. We can't find her anywhere. You don't think she's defected, sir? With everything she knows??

speaker: Messenger
content: And now, of all times...

speaker: Messenger
content: Damn it! After the trust we placed in her! After the resources we wasted protecting her! I knew it... Anyone from the metropoles can't be—
After pondering in silence for a moment, Dravyn set down his pen.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I know where she is.
At Brock's grave, Dravyn found the missing youngest daughter of the Andohar family.
Her gaze was fixed upon the headstone, yet seemed to look through it, reaching toward the distant front lines. In response, a rare gentleness softened Dravyn's hardened demeanor.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The Andohar family... Your father sent emissaries. Very generous terms. They say the head of the Andohar family will come himself next time. To bring you home.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Aren't you going to meet them?
She turned around and opened her mouth, speaking with impeccable "propriety."

speaker: Catherine
content: Are you trying to trick me, you old grouch? You'd never let me leave. I know too much. I'd be dead before I took one step past the gate.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Not here. You'll have Brock climbing out of his grave to scold you.
Catherine let out a soft giggle, her expression easing slightly.

speaker: Catherine
content: My father knows I don't want to go home right now. He's just using this as an excuse to meet you, Commander of the Independence Army.

speaker: Catherine
content: Let me guess... has the Andohar family already made you a weapons offer? They must think you're desperate. Perfect time to make a deal.
Dravyn merely shrugged, a silent confirmation. Before Brock's tombstone, the two fell into another shared, weighty silence.

speaker: Catherine
content: Brock said he didn't want me on the battlefield... But I'd already seen plenty of wars.

speaker: Catherine
content: I've been in a private airship of the metropoles, flying over settlements they were pacifying.

speaker: Catherine
content: I watched from the VIP cabin as bombs fell like hail. The people below held their makeshift weapons, refusing to surrender even in the face of death.

speaker: Catherine
content: Though the weapons on both sides came from my family. So we always knew how it would end.

speaker: Catherine
content: The budget difference, the tech gap, the training quality... The strong and the weak are objective, irreversible facts. The metropoles know it. That's why they don't care about the arms dealers' little games, but...

speaker: Catherine
content: But those people down there... they still cling to this hope. That the weapons they bought might hold some miracle. That it could suddenly turn the war, make all the stubborn dying mean something.

speaker: Catherine
content: Unfortunately, I've never once seen that miracle happen.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Are you saying our resistance is foolish?
She avoided answering directly, changing the subject instead.

speaker: Catherine
content: The Tide of Ashes will thin by mid-September. That's the metropoles' window. Their bombers will get through. Even with refueling and maintenance...

speaker: Catherine
content: By October at the latest, you'll face a second nuclear strike. This time, they'll be aiming at DisCity.

speaker: Catherine
content: Do you understand what that means?

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...I do.

speaker: Catherine
content: Your Independence Army can't stop it. Not as you are now.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I know.

speaker: Catherine
content: So what's your plan? Even if you placed an order with the Andohars today for nukes, it'd be too late. You can't threaten all five metropoles at once.

speaker: Catherine
content: Your troops are already losing faith, aren't they? Brock's gone, and your stubbornness alone isn't enough to hold them together.

speaker: Dravyn
content: You're right. We're fighting an uphill battle.
She looked at the gravestone again. This time, there was more than one surrounding them.

speaker: Catherine
content: If you surrender now, a lot of people would be relieved. They might even thank you for that. Even Helena and Brock wouldn't blame you, not after all this.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...Except me. The annoying Andohar brat.

speaker: Catherine
content: Don't you surrender, Dravyn. I've seen people with their backs against the wall—outnumbered, outgunned, still fighting while knowing all too well that they're weak.

speaker: Catherine
content: I want to see them win. I want to join the fight and help them win. Beating impossible odds—that's the kind of victory that matters the most.

speaker: Catherine
content: So fight harder. Think smarter. Weren't you supposed to be the stubborn one? If even you are thinking about giving up... then hand your command to me. I'll lead the fight myself!

speaker: Dravyn
content: Surrender isn't in my vocabulary. And yes, I'm not letting you go back, but not because I don't trust you. You wouldn't betray us.

speaker: Dravyn
content: You said you wanted to join the fight. That you were the ultimate weapon. I never forgot that.

speaker: Catherine
content: My superpowers? I've told you, my range is less than ten meters. Sending me against nukes would just get your soldiers killed.

speaker: Catherine
content: Desperation isn't a strategy, General. You're supposed to be the pragmatist here. Use your brain. Don't send me on a suicide mission.

speaker: Dravyn
content: So you'll fight... if I can give you a real shot at winning. Is that right?

speaker: Catherine
content: ...If your plan actually has a chance? Then fine. I suppose I could take orders from you.
Dravyn broke into a smile.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Haven't you figured me out already?
He took one final look at the gravestone, rose to his feet, and fastened his military cap.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I'm not like Brock. I have no lines I won't cross. No cost is too high if it leads to victory.

speaker: Dravyn
content: DisCity belongs to us. And now that I'm in command, I'm not giving it up.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The victory I want will come, one way or another.

speaker: Dravyn
content: So wait here. Those game-changing weapons you've been waiting for? I'll bring them to you very soon.

???: It's been a while. Are you still using the prototype I gave you?
Dravyn: Brock told me it works well. But it doesn't last long.
???: There are other organizations in this world conducting similar experiments, but that power they're dealing with is extremely dangerous.
???: They're carving out spaces beneath ancient and modern battlefields, using some kind of substance to create abnormal weapons.

Dravyn: You've helped us greatly in the past. Your abilities have been invaluable to both the Independence Army and all of DisCity.
EDGE Intern: My loyalty is to humanity. The world Keylan left behind shouldn't be defiled this way.
Dravyn: ...

Like a sinkhole, the pit swallowed broken blades and remains from the battlefield above, dragging them downward with the flowing sand. An indescribable, invisible distortion permeated the space, setting Dravyn's nerves on edge.
At the center of the runic array on the ground, twisted red crystal flowers bloomed. Among them lay a mass of filthy, humanoid flesh, curled and pulsing with a heavy, audible heartbeat.

speaker: Dravyn
content: This is...?
Dravyn's body tensed. He raised his gun and stepped forward, driven by a need to comprehend what he was seeing—and pulled by some hypnotic, inexplicable force.
It reminded him of Catherine's power, yet everything here felt undeniably more sinister...
The closer he moved, the stronger he felt an unsettling resonance with some unseen force. Could it be...?
Just then, a mass of black-red energy shot toward him, cutting his thought short. He dodged on instinct, whirled around, and fired.
Don't move!
From the shadows, a long-handled umbrella pointed at Dravyn, its tip writhing with black smoke, likely the source of the earlier attack.

Further back stood a figure clad in black, the umbrella's wielder. A bullet wound bled freely on his shoulder, yet he seemed utterly oblivious to the injury. Though a half-mask hid his eyes, his extreme tension was a palpable force in the air.

speaker: Parma
content: You're... an officer from the surface?

speaker: Parma
content: What are you doing here?! Who sent you? Who told you about this place??

speaker: Parma
content: Step back! Don't touch him! The ritual isn't finished. It cannot be interrupted!!

speaker: Dravyn
content: ... The ritual?
Refusing to retreat, Dravyn held his aim on Parma, his eyes flicking to the pulsing mass on the ground.
Then he remembered the warning from that scientist.
Those were weapons synthesized by catalyzing raw human emotion, a vortex that continuously extracted and refined suffering into a physical form.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Heh... So that's what it meant.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Parasites. Just like vultures picking over a battlefield... Whoever you are, that power you're stealing... it's harvested from my soldiers, isn't it?

speaker: Dravyn
content: This power... I should be the one deciding how it's used!

speaker: Parma
content: You fool... Come forth!
Beneath the peculiar umbrella, a foul black liquid spread continuously, dripping to the ground where puppet-like figures emerged one after another from the viscous pool.

A barrage of gunfire erupted underground like strings of firecrackers. Several team members, previously scattered throughout the space, converged toward the sound, swiftly forming a protective perimeter around Dravyn.

speaker: Vennon
content: Major! Did you find it?

speaker: Dravyn
content: Yes. It seems worth bringing back for research.
Their exchange only deepened the umbrella wielder's seething hatred.

speaker: Parma
content: ...You think those surface weapons of yours can defeat us? You're insulting us by even trying.

speaker: Dravyn
content: No. You should feel honored.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The soldiers you're facing are my elite commandos. Wasting them on gutter maggots like you is beneath their purpose.

speaker: Dravyn
content: So take pride in that, then die!
As the battle subsided, twisted shapes of crimson light rose from the humanoid mass, coalescing into the form of a flower.

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...That's it!
He moved forward to examine it, but a frail voice pulled at his attention.

speaker: Parma
content: ...So close... just a little more... Don't touch him... You mustn't...

speaker: Parma
content: You're not qualified... You can't take it... You'll die too... Listen, let's make a deal.

speaker: Parma
content: There's a war happening on the surface, isn't there? We can give you power, or help you kill your enemies. Anything you want. Just don't interrupt the ritual. I'll do anything...

speaker: Parma
content: The Sage must be born... We've come this far... Don't harm him...

speaker: Dravyn
content: Sage... What is that?

speaker: Dravyn
content: No. It doesn't matter...

speaker: Dravyn
content: If it serves my goal... if it leads to victory, I'll use any power. Whatever it takes.

speaker: Dravyn
content: If even my life can be spent in service of this cause... then that is the utmost glory!
He reached for the crystal flower, and pain tore through him. It was a silent explosion from his very core, a wave of invisible spikes shredding his nerves.

speaker: Vennon
content: Major!!

speaker: Parma
content: Stop! Ahhhhhhhh!!!
Dravyn instinctively clenched his fist, driving the sharp petals deeper into his palm. Blood, hot and slick, welled between his fingers as silent screams echoed in his skull.

<size=56><color=#dg1f1f>Surrender, just surrender</color>! <size=40>There's still a chance for us.　　<size=40>

　　　　　Stop <size=50>holding on stubbornly. This <size=36>isn't good for anyone. <size=50><color=#dg1f1f>Negotiate with them. There's a real chance it could work.</color></size>

Brock died <size=56><color=#dg1f1f>for nothing</color>! <size=40>The Independence Army can <size=50><color=#dg1f1f>never win!</color></size>

　　Why are you still hunting <size=50><color=#dg1f1f>spies</color></size>? <size=40>They are</size> <size=50><color=#dg1f1f>all around</color></size> you. <size=56><color=#dg1f1f>You can't win this!</color></size>

speaker: Brock
content: DisCity... It's... in your hands now...

speaker: Catherine
content: As the new commander of the DisCity Independence Army, can you accept that?
—If conviction doesn't win the war, what's the value of the battle? What's the point of the sacrifice?
Chaotic memories shattered through his mind, page by page, each one stained red and piercing his heart. The unbearable pain seized him, dragging him into the abyss.
Gritting his teeth, he clenched the petals with desperate strength, as if by sheer will he could wrest victory from the jaws of darkness.
<size=50>Yes, I will win! I will make it matter!</size>

Then, the red crystal flower began to dissolve, seeping into his skin. A sublime and profound power merged with his body and mind, flooding him with a long-forgotten peace as he sank into the waiting dark.
[Scene Change] Camp Infirmary (or a run-down hospital ward)
Upon waking, Dravyn found himself back at the camp. He was still alive. He carefully checked his own body, but the flower was gone. Then he saw it.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Vennon!

There lay Vennon on the adjacent bed, barely clinging to life. The malevolent blossom had taken root in the center of his throat. When Vennon tried to speak, only a hoarse, broken rasp escaped his lips.

speaker: Vennon
content: I was a spy planted by the DisCity military. My mission was to monitor you and Brock, find anything we could use against you.

speaker: Vennon
content: I intercepted your communications with EDGE, too. But after following you both... learning the truth... I defected. This is a spy's surrender. Will you accept it?

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...You fool. Then you should've known this would kill you!

speaker: Vennon
content: I know. I'm the fourth carrier. If I die, another will take my place... It is... an extraordinary power.
With the help of the EDGE intern, they expended tremendous effort to identify another suitable host and transfer the flower from the dying Dravyn.

speaker: Vennon
content: Following your orders... we secured it. A weapon that can turn the tide.
A violent, wracking cough seized Vennon, tearing from his chest and leaving him gasping for long, desperate moments before he could reclaim his breath.

speaker: Vennon
content: Martin, Tom, Joe... We all knew the risks. It's just one life. Dying on the battlefield or here... it's all the same. That's what it means to be a DisCity soldier.

speaker: Vennon
content: We're marching into the worst kind of war, the kind fought in human weakness, madness, and ignorance. One misstep... one moment of doubt... could be catastrophic.

speaker: Vennon
content: So we cut away weakness. Follow orders. No hesitation. No second guesses. We advance. Unwaveringly.

speaker: Vennon
content: Because we believe in you. We trust you'll lead us right.

speaker: Vennon
content: Back then, you told Brock he had to survive, no matter what. Now... I want you to remember those words.

speaker: Vennon
content: We're the DisCity Independence Army now. We need you. You are not allowed to die.
Vennon struggled to sit upright, attempting to move closer to Dravyn. The searing, needle-like pain in his chest momentarily sharpened his focus.

speaker: Vennon
content: Live. Wield the weapon we secured. Use it to bring victory. That's your duty, Commander.

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...Fool.

speaker: Dravyn
content: As my subordinate, you failed to follow a direct order. I won't tolerate insubordination. Your punishment: 100 weighted squats and 50 klicks in full gear.

speaker: Dravyn
content: After we win the battle and return to the city, you will complete every last one. Is that clear?!

speaker: Vennon
content: Yes, Major.
After Vennon's departure, Dravyn turned his attention to the documents, examining the letter from the EDGE intern.
There was one last thing to address, the most crucial matter...
[Transition] Small CG: Catherine at the gravesite

speaker: Catherine
content: You've kept a lady waiting far too long. I was starting to think you were dead.

speaker: Catherine
content: Well? Did you succeed?
[Fade to white] Return to present day
[Scene Change] Nirvana Port
Night has engulfed Nirvana Port. Scarface is splayed awkwardly across his bunk, mumbling into a crumpled pillow.

speaker: Scarface
content: BANG! Ha! Ain't I awesome? When you go out there... stand tall and proud!

speaker: Scarface
content: I'm a hero who defends... our city... a great hero who... protects Lily...

speaker: Scarface
content: Home... after I win this... I'll go home...

With a thunderous roar, the magnetic engines of Nirvana Port surge to life. The colossal fortress shudders, delivering Augustus's command across the port. Its course is set for the farlands, its purpose clear for war.
It is also a command from their long-missed homeland:
Reach the farlands. Eliminate all opposition.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: ...If that's your assessment, if it serves the city, then I'll see it done.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: We've done far worse. We hid behind glory, behind loyalty... and finally, behind obedience. Since we lacked the will to refuse back then, everything that comes now is a fate of our own making.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: I don't have the right to repent. My remorse changes nothing. Compensates no one. Not even death can absolve what I've done. Hellhounds would never dream of forgiveness.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: The Rancors know no emotions. We're your weapons, tools to turn the battle. Your only concern is victory.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: We will secure that victory for you. And then we'll reshape the world that made us. That is our final purpose. Nothing beyond that needs to concern you.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: We've long since fallen among the damned. And the damned have no right to speak of souls.
After the lieutenant's report, Augustus falls silent. The hushed whispers of Nirvana Port's Rancors echo by her ear, but she only listens, not uttering a word.
...Fraser's Hypercube stockpile exceeds that of all the farlands combined. Their true face has never changed. Power! All they seek is military power to dominate us all!

What they truly covet are DisCity's mines. Even if they seize control of DisCity again, the weak farlands will gain nothing. They incite hatred among the farlands to overthrow DisCity, and it would only return us to the past, when all city-states were enslaved by the metropoles.

Protecting DisCity from these sinister ambitions... this has been our purpose since the bygone era... We hunger for bloodshed, and only through it can this unjust world be saved. This has always been the way—
Now, prepare to embrace death and glory!

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Talk about swords dug from tombs. The weight of that is staggering.
Just then, footsteps approach, followed by a sharp knock at the door. The Rancors fall instantly silent.
Augustus looks up, her eyes shifting toward the sound.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...You've come...

speaker: Dravyn
content: We've completed our analysis of those things. Their function is very similar to your own ability. EDGE has accelerated development. The first batch of operational gear is ready, the operators are in training, and the new tactical framework is almost finalized.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The team is composed of volunteers. All of them are elite soldiers. High skill, higher morale. That won't be a problem.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Now, it's your turn.
Catherine reviews the plan.

speaker: Catherine
content: And this is how you plan to stop the second nuke?

speaker: Dravyn
content: We still have you, don't we?

speaker: Catherine
content: What, with my little spoon-bending party trick?

speaker: Dravyn
content: That "trick" is how we win.

speaker: Catherine
content: You expect me to fight a nuclear weapon?

speaker: Dravyn
content: Getting cold feet? I thought you'd outgrown the idea that a nuke is the ultimate power.

speaker: Catherine
content: Still trying to sweet-talk me? I know a gamble when I see one.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...But fine. I'll admit it, your conviction is real this time.

speaker: Catherine
content: You're not hiding anything else, are you? This plan... it's everything from the deduction?
Dravyn broke into a smile.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I omitted one detail: the probability of your death. In front of Brock, I can't lie. Anyone can lose their life on the battlefield.

speaker: Dravyn
content: But I still need you for this battle.
He extended his right hand, his expression remaining calm. Catherine tilted her head, as if contemplating something.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Fight for us, Catherine Augustus Andohar. You were born a warrior. Now become DisCity's sword.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Your enemy isn't the metropoles. It's the war—the fate you've learned to hate.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I will give you a weapon powerful enough to break it. And a glorious victory.

speaker: Dravyn
content: It will be a battlefield worthy of you.
Catherine nodded, reaching out her right hand to pat Dravyn.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...Of course you will. This is my debut, after all. Don't you dare screw it up.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...One... Two... Three...

speaker: Catherine
content: None of you are getting away!

EDGE-02: He claims he can handle the situation himself. Says he'll eliminate BR-005 without starting a bigger fight.
EDGE-05: The internal conditions of a Black Ring are highly complex, and our Hypercube reserves are not infinite. The resource investment and operational risk for protection would be significant.

EDGE-02: His counterpoint is that neutralizing BR-005 would cover the Hypercube cost and even yield a profit.
EDGE-07: Even if we ignore the probability of failure, our analysis confirms BR-005 is a low-yield variant. Its anomalous readings are solely due to its fusion with the Apostles. A successful operation would not provide a meaningful return on investment.

EDGE-03: It'd be risky for the Underground Shepherd to surface. She only emerged for BR-002 due to its strength; she has never displayed any interest in a weaker Ring like BR-001.
EDGE-03: BR-005 is demonstrably weaker than BR-001. Therefore, the possibility is negligible.

EDGE-02: Huh. That's a thought.
