[Farland Outpost in WhiteSands]
Selyna has finally finished her letter. Before departing, she's going to send it to the director general of the Luminaris Society, her most trusted mentor.

My Dear Mentor and Director General,

I have safely rejoined my unit and now stand ready to enter the battlefield. Thank you for your swift reply; it arrived at the most crucial moment, allowing me to cast aside my foolish doubts and reclaim my true resolve. I was nearly led astray by that brat's poisonous words.
You are, of course, absolutely right. How could I have forgotten? The Furorians made their sacrifice willingly and nobly. If she truly had a drop of Furorian blood, if she possessed even a shred of an Outlander's consciousness, she would be proud of her mother's choice!
To defile their sacrifice with such words... I should have realized sooner. The Outland blood in her veins has run dry. She is nothing but a DisCity native.

A brat raised on DisCity water is tainted to the core. I should have killed her when I had the chance. After all, you taught us that even children who speak Disian belong in hell!

Now, all hesitation is gone. The final battle lies ahead. The wealth they have squeezed from us lies ahead. The world's Hypercubes lie ahead. As you have always taught me, this prosperity is rightfully ours—it was always meant to be—and we will seize it with all our might.

Only the path we walk can mend this broken world. Only our cause is truly just.

We will fight to the very end. We will make DisCity understand: Justice will prevail.

With her final encrypted message sent through the Mania dark web, Selyna gazes across the endless expanse of WhiteSands, a battlefield now scarred with streaks of black and crimson. She takes a deep breath, a wave of pure exhilaration washing over her. Even the indolence of her fellow warrior nearby no longer bothers her in the slightest.

speaker: Selyna
content: Got anything else to say? Doesn't matter. I'm not lost anymore. My mind is set; only the final battle remains.

speaker: Synex
content: Oh? Really? I don't have much to add, honestly. Just... congrats, I guess? Good luck with that.

The wind sweeps across the white sands, lifting the Aurum Secretum chain in her hand. Fragments of Ash Crystal gleam with blinding intensity, fracturing her view of the distant city—a metropolis more prosperous and peaceful than Fraser—into a mosaic of shimmering shards.
As the chain sways, it hums with a resonant energy. Within that dazzling, power-laden light, she sees it: the city that rightfully belongs to her people.
There, she will erect a monument to her triumphs and raise a new future from the dust. At the end of this road paved in blood and sand, all farlanders will finally find a safe haven, free from fear.

Before departing, she recites the battle hymn one last time, a devout and solemn oath. The phantom of Nysa Sadikur is torn asunder and buried by the swirling sands, as if she had corrected that mistake.

speaker: Selyna
content: Yes... No more doubt... We are righteous. This war is just. Victory will be ours.

speaker: Selyna
content: Sands that buried my home, hear my words... Blizzards that stole my kin, gather at my fingertips...

speaker: Selyna
content: Confusion and fear are behind me. I stand here not for revenge, not for the past... but for hope. For the future...

speaker: Selyna
content: Catastrophes that shattered our land... forge the path forward for us...

speaker: Selyna
content: Today, we will use them to remake this world...
[Transition 2s]

In the distance, a blazing red cross ignites upon the colossal Apostle's chest. In response, the white sands below begin to flow like a spectral river, the howling wind spirals into a frenzy, and the very ground shudders.
As her chant swells, hordes of Apostles materialize from the void, their multitudes raising mutilated limbs to form a crushing tide of darkness.

speaker: Selyna
content: CHARGE—!!
[Scene Change] FAC Frontline
On the other side of the defensive fortifications, FAC soldiers are already in position.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Enemy incoming! All units on alert, prepare to engage!!

August 22, N.F. 115 22:00
Junction of DisSea and the Rust
FAC Broken Frontline
Siglinde's brow furrows.
Her eyes fix on the distant city. An unprecedented Tide of Ashes surges violently across the land, staining the air with the metallic tang of rust and the smell of scorched earth.

Yet more unnerving than the calamity ahead is the threat looming behind—from beyond the far end of the Broken Frontline. The Illusory Moon has not yet risen, but even through the anti-Mania barriers, she can hear the DisSea roaring.

The defensive line, built from the rubble of countless collapsed buildings, shudders endlessly as though battered by invisible beasts. In the shallows, reef rocks dissolve into a black, devouring sludge that consumes all it touches.
Hordes of Apostles push deeper along the Rust, using the river's polluted veil to dash forward. Outposts in their path fight desperately to hold, only to be overrun one by one.

Is this the enemy's final assault? Driving the Apostles from the front while stirring the depths of the DisSea from behind—a coordinated pincer attack on DisCity... The thought sends a cold sweat beading along Siglinde's temples.

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...Should we request reinforcements? I could contact General Augustus and persuade her to provide assistance.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: No need. They're on another mission.

speaker: Siglinde
content: But if the Apostles breach our defensive line, wouldn't the consequences be severe?

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Yes, but that's not going to happen.

Where does this old man get his unshakable confidence? Does he truly not care for the lives of his soldiers? With so many Apostles swarming the field, even ten lives per FAC soldier wouldn't be enough to hold the line. Unable to contain her curiosity any longer, Siglinde snatches up a telescope to survey the crumbling front.

The Apostles are gathering in ever-growing numbers, the majority already surging through the contaminated zone in a frenzied charge. Some powerful force is driving them—compelling them forward. Are there Aurum Secretum Warriors nearby?

Her gaze sweeps frantically across the battlefield, but she finds no trace of them. Those warriors' presence is always conspicuous, impossible to miss. She can't have overlooked them. And yet, the FAC's defenses at the end of the Rust are among their most fortified...

Wait... they were prepared for this? They knew the Apostles would cross the Rust. These fortifications... they're not just defenses. They were designed to funnel the hostiles right here, to keep them from spilling into the city?

speaker: Apostle
content: <size=52><color=#dg1f1f><i>—! —!!!!</color></size><i>
But the Apostles seem so erratic... so aggressively violent. She can't help but wonder what powerful force is compelling them to push this far.
A nearby FAC soldier takes the telescope from her hands and hands her an updated battle briefing.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Look, Aurum Secretum, Underground sorcery, all of it... it's just human ingenuity. But controlling Apostles? Truly controlling them? Never been done. If we could've, we'd have ended the catastrophes years ago.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: We've been fighting Apostles long enough to know their nature. They always have this desire to return to the DisSea. Even the thinnest crack in the walls around BR-000 is enough to trigger that instinct. They can't resist it.

speaker: Siglinde
content: A plan like this... it would require detailed technical parameters on the resonance between Aurum Secretum and Apostles. Where did you acquire this intel? And when? The Ring Research Institute hasn't pursued this line of research.
Though the soldier's expression is hidden behind a mask, Siglinde senses an unmistakable air of smugness.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: It came from one of our intelligence assets in the farlands. One minute is more than enough for her to get many things done.

She studies the battle briefing, her mind returning to the brief, precious window before the final battle when DisCity's intelligence network at the farlands had flickered back to life. In that narrow gap, they had managed to tear a critical pocket of intelligence.
As for how they managed to tear an opening into the Mania dark web—
[Flashback]

speaker: Langley
content: We've got a new lead. A captive brought back from WhiteSands, elite class at minimum, capable of manipulating Apostles with Aurum Secretum. During dispersed operations, these types will definitely communicate through the Mania dark web.

speaker: Langley
content: She's been cautious in custody—no outgoing signals. But compared to Adelaide Campbell? This one's practically gift-wrapped. Keep close surveillance.

speaker: Langley
content: It's our turn to play their game now. We'll piggyback on their own network. The moment she initiates contact, we trace and decrypt immediately. Even if we only have one minute, we must locate our missing agents in the farlands.

speaker: Langley
content: After that... they'll finally become useful.
The spymaster's gaze was cold and steady on the screen. On the monitor, the Outland prisoner fled in a blind panic, utterly unaware she was already tracked.
[Flashback]
Selyna raced through the dim alleyways, finally stumbling to a halt in a secluded corner. She gasped for breath—not from exhaustion, but from the emotional tempest raging within her.

The thought of returning to camp with her mind so clouded by doubt was unbearable. She had always been unwavering, a pillar of conviction on the battlefield, never permitting herself the slightest hesitation... but now...

Gritting her teeth, she unleashed her ability. Her fingertips traced Aurum Secretum patterns, emitting a specific frequency. The power of Mania answered, transforming into a torrent of raw information that flowed into her mind.

speaker: Selyna
content: Director... I'm out. I made it. But... I had to reach you. I can't just report to camp, not with this sickness in my thoughts. This war means everything to me. I can't move another step until I know the answer.

speaker: Selyna
content: You're the one I trust the most, and I believe in your integrity... So please, for the sake of everything we're doing, tell me the truth. I need to hear it from you.

As the fragmented transmission left her, the memory crashed over her anew, a fresh wave of turmoil. That girl from DisCity, the one who'd aimed a gun at her hours ago... what was her name? El-something-ra...
No, that's wrong. She wasn't from DisCity... The correct name, the real identity... was Nysa Sadikur. Of Furor.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Elvira
content: My mother... she was from Furor. She made a deal with Fraser... to come here to DisCity. To get close to the Speaker. She even had me... just to make it look real. She kept that secret her whole life. She never broke her cover.

speaker: Elvira
content: But I know now... even more than she did. I know what you did... Fraser... set off a Black Ring right on top of Furor, her homeland! You wiped out every last one of her people! She gave you everything for a promise, and it was all a lie!

speaker: Elvira
content: You said this war was righteous revenge! You said it was for justice, for all Outlanders! She believed you her whole life! So what is that? What is that Black Ring right in front of us? Tell me!

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Was she part of the plan, too? Was she just another thing to throw away when you were done with Furor?

speaker: Elvira
content: I thought... I thought her people were good. My people. I just wanted to help. I just wanted to understand you! But look what you did!

speaker: Elvira
content: I know you betrayed my mother! After what you did... how can you even say words like "justice"?
Early during her interrogation by the 9th Agency, Elvira had already voluntarily offered to cooperate.

She pledged her full assistance in dismantling the Outland intelligence network—a proposal with conditions the agents, recognizing her capabilities, readily accepted. And the final results proved highly satisfactory.
When she heard Sibilla's story about Furor, a complete plan was formed instantly, built on her observation of the fanatical Aurum Secretum Warrior.

speaker: Elvira
content: She's a lost cause... Her mind's been warped into nothing but vengeance. She won't listen to reason. So to get her to talk... I have to speak the only language she understands... Identity and hatred.

speaker: Elvira
content: So I pretended to be one of her people, to plant that seed of doubt. A self-righteous zealot like her can't stand that. She'll be desperate for validation, for someone to confirm her so-called justice. We just have to see who she'd run to—their military camp outside the city, or if we get lucky...

speaker: Elvira
content: If she starts doubting even her own comrades... maybe she'd try to contact someone in Fraser thousands of miles away...

Hiding in her small room at the Bureau to deliver her report, she clutched the little handgun she always carried. Leaning against the headboard, she spoke in a low, steady monotone amidst the dry clicks of the trigger.
It was a depth of calculation and cunning astonishing for a mere seventeen-year-old.

speaker: Langley
content: The former Speaker, a Fraser spy... What a twisted family to breed such a dangerous talent.

speaker: Langley
content: You played your hand well, Miss Stewart. Tell me, does this victory taste as sweet as you imagined?

A promising new talent, she noted with a smile to herself. As her hand swiped across the terminal, the encrypted message sent from Fraser decoded at last, revealing the long-absent symbol: the peace dove.
"The Senate's taken care of. Oh, and I pried some choice Aurum Secretum intel from a little Campbell scholar. Let's see if the FAC's gentlemen can actually put it to good use."
"Clock's ticking. The rats will pick up the scent soon, so I'm going dark. The rest is on you. I'm in no position to double back anyway. This is your turf, your play."
"And I think we both would rather not see they hit here with that disgusting thing in the sky."
[Broken Frontline]

Light indicators flicker across the sand table, tracing the paths of the remaining Apostle swarms as they flow from BR-005 toward the Rust, then onward to DisSea—only to be intercepted by the Broken Frontline. FAC's precise calculations ensure the defensive perimeter allows just enough controlled leakage to maintain a fragile balance.

Hypercube consumption continues to climb. The logistics department anxiously diverts resources from every available channel, including Nirvana. Once again, this "incomplete" force is being tested by fire, caught between impossible demands.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: See? Holding this line meant something. We buy that future, and someone else will take the chance and turn the tide.
The soldier says, his eyes fixed on the steadily rising monitoring feeds. The moment they reach the predetermined threshold, he rushes excitedly to the Commander-in-Chief to deliver the news.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Commander, civvies are clear. The gloves are off.
Siglinde glances toward the FAC's highest commanding officer. The old man remains absorbed in the sand table, yet he is unmistakably aware of her gaze.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Liaison Officer Siglinde, you don't actually trust FAC, do you? You're here primarily to gather intelligence.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: And you needn't worry. I understand. The schism in N.F. 103 created a rift that hasn't healed. In many ways, that makes your presence here more valuable. I also have messages I'd like to relay through you.
The old commander rises to his feet and makes his way toward the broadcasting station.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Unlike the old DisCorps, the FAC does not pursue war for its own sake or condone excessive force. We are not skilled at fighting human malice. We operate under constraints, stubbornly clinging to principles some see as weaknesses, unwilling to sacrifice others casually. And because of this, we cannot achieve the grand, sweeping victories others might.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: What you've witnessed in this war has left you disheartened. You doubt we can still fulfill our duty.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Do not make that mistake. Never forget where our real strength lies.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: We renounced killing because we made a conscious choice for life. We swore to bear its weight, to protect those in our care. That is not a limitation. That is the very source of our strength. And through it, we will become immeasurably strong.
The cacophony of the command center fades into a dull hum, drowned by the thunderous rumbles from the battlefield. Their rhythm is a key, unlocking memories long buried.
[Three DisCorps generations' portraits with black gradient]
Hearts waver and times change, yet some things must remain constant. He will be that constant.

Adrian Sterling—the Nirvana Port Commanding Officer of the Independence Army, the second Commander-in-Chief of the FAC—once more stands before the final line of defense, his voice cutting through the chaos with unwavering command.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Attention, all FAC stations. The Rust sector of the Broken Frontline will be opened for a precise window of 200 minutes. The enemy has weaponized the resonance between the DisSea and the Apostles. Now, we will turn their own weapon against them.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: We will give those monsters a taste of the true DisSea. Lure them in. Fight for control. Their Aurum Secretum and their pathetic Secondary Black Ring are no match for the power of the DisSea.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Our objective is to split their formation, isolate BR-005 completely, and carve a path for our allies. Prepare for simultaneous assaults from inside and outside the Broken Frontline. Holding the line against impossible odds is what we do!

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: They believe a Secondary Black Ring lets them command Apostles, disrupt the DisSea, and slaughter our people? Let those reckless warmongers bear witness.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Let them see the true face of the Mania we've been fighting all these years. Show them what a real catastrophe looks like!

speaker: FAC Soldiers
content: Yes, sir!!

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: As for you...
He turns to Siglinde.

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: Now go contact your general and tell her:

speaker: FAC Commander-in-Chief
content: "FAC will fulfill its mission without fail. Now, it's <color=#fb9259>your</color> turn."
Siglinde snaps to attention and delivers the DisCorps salute to the FAC Commander-in-Chief.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Yes, sir. Consider it done.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your request has been submitted to EDGE for resolution, and after discussion, they have agreed to grant you this opportunity to proceed.

speaker: Schorl
content: However, we will be implementing more rigorous safety protocols. We must ensure your protection, as you are invaluable to DisCity.
But with the Third Observatorium and your catastrophe weapon combined, isn't that enough?
That system was built to disrupt catastrophes. Protecting one person should be well within its capabilities.

speaker: Christina
content: Based on available data, killing a person is far simpler than protecting one. Warfare often serves as a prime example of that.

speaker: Schorl
content: Now, to the plan. Phase one: you will approach the Black Ring and identify an entry point.

speaker: Schorl
content: I will be unable to provide direct support during close-quarters engagement, but I will handle tactical analysis and coordinate FAC and DisCorps squadrons to clear a path for you. Their presence should dilute the direct impact of the Black Ring's Mania.

speaker: Schorl
content: Phase two: penetration. Once you cross the threshold, you will be alone. No support team, and certainly no Sinners, can follow you inside.

speaker: Schorl
content: However, once you are inside BR-005's Mania field, the Third Observatorium will be able to lock onto the unique signature of your shackles. This will allow us to track your position precisely, offer remote protection, and assist in threat neutralization.

speaker: Schorl
content: The Black Ring possesses depth characteristics similar to the DisSea. Hazard levels increase exponentially the closer you move toward the epicenter. If you breach the predetermined safety threshold and we assess your risk level as critical, please follow our extraction orders immediately.
I expected a "fight to the last" kind of objective.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your successful entry is the primary objective. The data we will gather from your incursion is itself a decisive victory.
Having delivered their decision, Schorl falls silent. Its optical sensors sweep over you from head to toe as it performs the last, precise calibrations on your anti-Mania armor.

speaker: Schorl
content: Good luck, Chief.
[Scene Change]
You step onto Nirvana Port's rooftop pad into the teeth of the storm. The wind lashes your face, and the Mania within you surges in response.

Through the raging veil of sand, you see it: BR-005 and the foremost Apostle move toward you from the storm's heart, a mountain of a figure whose head scrapes the bruised sky. Its form pulses with a twisted, chaotic red light, like a walking calamity. The shackles throb with a painful pull, whispering that your destination has come to you.
Your companion is already ahead. She turns back, waiting for you.

speaker: Hecate
content: I don't want you to suffer, Chief. I don't want you to get dragged into things I don't understand. This fight... it's not even yours. I care more about you being safe than who wins this war.

speaker: Hecate
content: But... I really want Hella back, too. She was my first friend. I can't sleep, knowing she's trapped in there.

speaker: Hecate
content: So I get it, Chief. I know this must hurt you even more than it hurts me.
Hecate pauses, her teeth catching gently on her lower lip—a gesture you've come to recognize as her struggle for composure.

Over the past few years, you have watched the landscape of her emotions broaden, revealing unexpected depths. But just as you school your own features into a mask of stoicism for the political stage, she is now learning the same difficult art of restraint.
...Or perhaps it is something more. She steps closer, tilting her face up to yours, her eyes holding something silent yet resolute.

speaker: Hecate
content: In this battle, you're the only one who can break the Black Ring. And you're the only other one who really wants to save her.

speaker: Hecate
content: So please... bring Hella back. I'll be right there with you. No matter what.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I will.
You take her hand.

speaker: Hecate
content: Mm.
The DisCorps aircraft roars toward your position. You board together and quickly don protective gear, your hands never parting throughout the process.
Between your interlaced palms, dark thorns of light flicker into existence—resonating, stinging, binding you both. This pain is a testament to the unbreakable bond between you and her.
Through the contamination corroding your bodies, at the far end of these extending shackles, deep within the Black Ring now turned into an Apostle, <color=#fb9259>Hella</color> is waiting.
—The three of you have never truly been apart. And soon, you will be reunited.

The aircraft closes in on the humanoid Black Ring. Upon reaching the safety threshold for ordinary humans, you mount Nightmare to press onward. The aircraft circles nearby, fending off any Corruptors that draw too close.

The air grows thin at this altitude. Wind-whipped sand scrapes against your skin, stinging your face. Under the resonance of the shackles, the proximity to the core of Mania weighs heavily on both you and Hecate.

The distance between you and the Black Ring shrinks rapidly. You see contamination twisting and hardening into a dark, impenetrable shell around the monster's form—save for the crimson light slashing diagonally across its chest like a fresh wound.

speaker: Hecate
content: BR-005 has a physical body now. We'll need to find a way inside.

speaker: Hecate
content: Wait, someone's over there—
You see a tiny figure stand atop the Apostle, shouting soundlessly from the edge of that massive glowing cross.
Before you can process her presence, a brilliant flash erupts from her body. She launches herself in a violent arc, hurtling directly toward Nightmare!

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, watch out!

The crystal on her hand flares, resonating with Aurum Secretum and morphing into monstrous claws. In one fluid, predatory motion, she seizes Nightmare mid-leap, using her tail as a grapple to swing onto its back. She's an Aurum Secretum Warrior!

The added weight is too much. Nightmare shudders violently before plummeting, crashing all of you onto the Black Ring's shoulder. The impact injures the great beast and sends Hecate sprawling down. You lunge, your hand closing around her arm just in time to anchor her.
Your head spins, but your fury burns through the daze. You look up to see the architect of this chaos calmly retracting her claws.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: Well, well, you must be the "big, gray-haired dummy" little Hella wouldn't shut up about.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: Me? Oh, I'm her friend too. The kind that's here to give her a proper send-off.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You—
Stay calm!
Fury still burns in your veins, but you force it down. Your focus snaps back, sharp and cold, pushing the dizziness aside.

speaker: Option
options: Get out of my way. I have no time to waste on you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is that red rift behind you the entrance to the Black Ring? Let me through, and we'll pretend we never met. Your life will be spared.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: Ooh, so cold. And here I thought we had something special. I heard you almost took Selyna out of the picture. And now you're giving me the cool treatment? I'm hurt.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: But you're making my job so difficult. Could you at least try to be a little more... I don't know, impulsive? Give me some anger, some drama! It'd make this whole acting much more convincing.

speaker: Option
options: No time to waste on her. Charge!

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: What I mean is—
With a gleeful grin, she grabs a floating blade and starts walking toward you.
She lets out a piercing whistle, hunches her back, and lunges. But someone else intercepts her path.

speaker: Hecate
content: Your opponent is me!
With a thunderous roar, Nightmare returns. It drives Synex back with a devastating blow, carving a deep, ragged gash across her torso.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: Well, well! Another one for our little party! Wonderful!
Hecate commands Nightmare to press the attack. A single look from her is all you need. As Nightmare strikes again, you break into a sprint, aiming for the glowing red crack ahead.
Now you see it clearly—a deep, jagged crevice in the monster's chest. The entrance.

But how do you reach it? The thought flashes through your mind as you run. Just as panic begins to set in, you see Synex turn her head. Her eyes lock onto yours, and a sinister smile plays on her lips.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: And while we're at it... Whoops! Clumsy me—
Her tail lashes out like a whip, catching your waist and hurling you skyward.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief!
You scream, instinctively releasing your shackles. Empowered by the Black Ring, the spikes bite deep into the Apostle's shell, anchoring you fast.
By sheer "luck," the trajectory was perfect. You're now hanging just within reach of the crimson fissure.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...What are you...?

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: Alright, alright, only one free pass today. You get to stay and play with me. Actually, you remind me of an old friend. Consider it... curing my homesickness.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: Hang in there, precious. You'll want to be on your feet to welcome them back.
[Scene Change] Tuco Time
Meanwhile, having secured another victory against an Aurum Secretum outpost, Augustus makes her return to the ruined Nirvana Port, her steadfast stronghold.

Below, she watches the DisCorps aircraft and FAC squads as they circle the Apostles and Black Ring—publicly cooperating but privately competing. The spectacle evokes a profound sense of emotion in her.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Look at that. It's been a long time since we've seen something like this. Uris, doesn't it get your blood pumping?
The iron-masked man offers no response to her playful question.
Because a much bigger "joke" has just appeared before his eyes.
Amidst the chaos, Nirvana Port Command receives an unexpected message.

A shipment of supplies has appeared mysteriously at the gates of Nirvana Port. It holds crate upon crate of Hypercubes and a massive stockpile of tactical Aurum Secretum. But the true mystery lies at the very bottom of the cargo: a single, hidden note, discovered by the bewildered guards.

To the high-and-mighty at the "Fortress,"

Happened to lighten the load of some Fraser boys.
Turns out that "Money LV." reputation is no joke. Even their trail supplies are fancier than our Sunday best.

We kept the cash, obviously.
The rest of this junk is just cluttering up our wagon, so it's all yours. Call it a donation.


A Generous Bounty Hunter & Associates
Several kilometers into the WhiteSands, Tuco's sand ship tears across the dunes. The woman clamps a hand on her cowboy hat against the whipping wind and casts a glance at the distant Black Ring.

P.S. Remind that MBCC Chief: payment's due after the dust settles.

I held up my end. Now you better damn well make sure <color=#fb9259>she</color> gets back safe.
Raising her binoculars, Augustus spots you in the distance—a lone figure struggling to keep your footing on the edge of the ominous red glow.

speaker: Augustus
content: All those troops, all those "allies," fighting to help that person win... Makes me want to cut through the chatter and just act.

speaker: Augustus
content: How about a change of strategy? If we stick to the script, they'll take all the credit.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: You're not thinking about...
The colossal Apostle Black Ring advances toward the ruins of Nirvana Port looming in its path. The Tide of Ashes churning in its wake crashes violently against the fragile steel structures.
<color=#dg1f1f>ROAAAR!!</color> As if sensing a threat, the giant humanoid figure strikes first.

It lunges forward, driving its fist into the ground before the ruined port. Sand cascades away like water down a drain, exposing the foundations and leaving the structure trembling on the verge of collapse.
Augustus stands firm at the base of Nirvana Port, facing the Black Ring head-on—unflinching, unmoving.

speaker: Augustus
content: Perfect position...

speaker: Augustus
content: Let's give them a show. Something to rally the troops. Signal all units: brace for impact. And try not to fall off.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...Understood.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Keep it down, will you? This thing's decades old. If we bring it down, the bill would be astronomical.

speaker: Augustus
content: Then I'll just bill the entire Andohar fortune for it.

An unearthly light glows in her eyes as the Rancors placed throughout Nirvana Port awaken at her command. They shudder, growing increasingly agitated as magnetic fields converge, shaking the entire metal bastion to its core.
[Scene Change]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Augustus?
You're still scanning for weaknesses in the contamination, searching for a way to breach the Black Ring's thick shell, when suddenly, the behemoth itself begins to tremble.
A single devastating blow punches through the Apostle Black Ring's armor of contamination. The shockwave surges upward, astonishingly, like a new Tide of Ashes erupting from within!
You grip the shackles with all your strength to avoid being thrown off, utterly stunned by the raw power on display.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Didn't you tell the council that Nirvana Port was a ghost town and the Eighth Division was completely out of gear?

speaker: Augustus
content: Of course it was a lie. Do you really think my forces would be that weak?

speaker: Augustus
content: It was just an act. Had to light a fire under those cowards on the council, force them to grow a spine. Makes the fight a lot more interesting, don't you think?

speaker: Augustus
content: There. The path is clear. The battlefield ahead is all yours.

speaker: Augustus
content: Now go. Make it a glorious victory!

speaker: Hecate
content: Go, Chief!

When released, the shackles thrust into the crimson glow at the Black Ring's chest as if pulled by an invisible force. The moment they pierce its heart, a world-ending shriek from the Apostle rips across the WhiteSands.
—You are less than a speck of dust before the cataclysm. A torrent of red light erupts from the breach, and you are utterly, instantly consumed.

A deathly silence envelops the camp, so absolute that dust hangs motionless in the air, thickening it into a suffocating shroud. After a long moment, an advisor finally clears a dry, constricted throat, the sound unnaturally loud in the stillness.

speaker: Farland Advisor
content: The supplies aren't coming. Raiders hit our lines... Fraser's final Aurum Secretum convoy was lost. After that... holding the Black Ring was impossible.

speaker: Farland Advisor
content: And Synex just sent word that DisCity's "Shepherd" keeps breaking through our lines. We couldn't stop him from charging into the Black Ring.
female_content: And Synex just sent word that DisCity's "Shepherd" keeps breaking through our lines. We couldn't stop her from charging into the Black Ring.

content: The young Fraser general silently studies the reports before him. The situation has become nearly hopeless.

Frontline Report: The Apostle swarm originally concentrated around BR-005 has been forcibly diverted to the Broken Frontline by the enemy. To think they would actually dare to open their DisSea defenses and use a near-suicidal tactic... Are they really so confident in their defensive capabilities?

Frontline Report: Regardless, the enemy only needed to create a single breach in the frontline to easily attract the Apostle swarm we had painstakingly gathered using Aurum Secretum.

Frontline Report: The so-called "Secondary Black Ring" is simply no match for the power of BR-000. In actual combat, all theoretical strategies have proven to be worthless jokes.

Frontline Report: Forward Command initially assessed that if we could hold out until the FAC was overrun by DisSea Corruptors and the external Apostle swarm, we might still have a chance to turn the tide.

Frontline Report: But the enemy's tenacity has exceeded all expectations. For nearly three hours, their defensive line hasn't yielded a single step.

Frontline Report: Moreover, we underestimated those old military forces from the Nirvana Port ruins. That woman took to the battlefield in her massive steel machine, capable of engaging BR-005 directly.
Frontline Report: The situation is spiraling out of control, Headquarters. Forward Command believes we have lost all ability to influence the outcome.
The young general closes the communication channel and sighs. To him, these crises might still be reversible with enough effort. But there is one thing he truly dreads—

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Any movement on the Undergrounder network? ...What's the word from the Senate?

speaker: Farland Advisor
content: They're urging a full withdrawal. Surrender is also acceptable, as long as we completely sever all ties with Fraser.
His voice is barely above a whisper, yet it rings in their ears like thunder.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: ...Even the Furor Black Ring we bled to take... handed over on a silver platter.

speaker: Farland Advisor
content: They say... there will be other opportunities.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: ...Heh. I know what they're really saying.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: We've been abandoned, right? The Senate wouldn't dare make this call alone. Someone got to them—either convinced them the war is already lost, or bought them off.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Was it the appeasers? Or have DisCity's spies crawled out of the shadows again? Hmph. I should've purged them all before we deployed.
A heavy silence falls over the tent. Around him, officers and advisors stare at the ground, their hope extinguished like cold ashes. Yet the young general's eyes never leave the sand table.
He stares intently, not saying a word, until at last his calm voice breaks the silence.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: ...Here's what happens next. I'll adjust our tactics, provide cover for the Aurum Secretum sorcerers, and launch another offensive. If you want to surrender, do it. Just stay out of my way.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: The Aurum Secretum has strengthened our Black Ring. The Undergrounders' tech still gives us options. If DisCity's "shackles" have already breached the Black Ring and become a threat... then I'll use that. I'll turn this into our final opportunity.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: If the Undergrounders were here, they'd say... this is the first fusion of shackles, Deus Corpus, and Mania's will. No one can predict what miracle might emerge.

He rushes back to the sand table. With the Apostles of Ashes diverted and his resources stretched thin, every second is critical. In the resonance pool, Aurum Secretum particles drift and swirl into ripples, disturbed by the battlefield's chaotic energy—forming a real-time visualization of the shifting Mania field.
His eyes remain fixed on the harsh red glow marking the shackles that are steadily advancing toward the heart of their precious Black Ring.
At last, it happens. That person breaks through all obstacles, piercing into the Black Ring like a blade, yet merging with it like a drop of water returning to the ocean.
Just as the weight of the moment settles, a piece of long-missed good news reaches him.

speaker: Selyna
content: Sir! The sorcerers have been delivered to the designated location! Your plan will proceed without fail! For victory, I swear to follow you even unto death!
Just in time!

His gambit activates at the perfect moment—any earlier, and the enemy might have detected it; any later, and all would have been lost. The timing is flawless. With this first critical step achieved, he is convinced: this is both a trial and a blessing, bestowed upon them by "God" Himself.
The young general clenches his fist and turns to address the soldiers still holding the line behind him.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: The Black Ring belongs to the farlands. It hungers for change more than any of us. As long as it stands, so do we. The Ring will show us its will.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: For our city-state! For glory! For our people, no sacrifice is too great! I swore an oath before this campaign: we will achieve victory. And we shall.

His words are met with the soldiers' fervent oaths, and the distant, ground-shaking roar of the Apostle Black Ring, locked in a stalemate with a colossal steel behemoth. Its cry is one of defiant rage, shaking the very earth beneath them.
It is a roar they have heard all their lives, echoing across all their ranks—a howl of fury, imprisoned by powerful, unforgiving new rules.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Come forth... DisCity's true weapon. This chance was bought with Adelaide's life. I will seize it with mine!
You burst into the Black Ring. It's like plunging headlong into a raging river; you are immediately drowning in concentrated Mania.
The current fights you, pushing back against your very presence. And through the roaring torrent—amid the countless voices of resentment, hatred, obsession, and joy—you hear a familiar one.

speaker: Hella
content: You're here.

speaker: Hella
content: Why are you here?

speaker: Option
options: I'm here for Hella. Give her back to me.

speaker: Hella
content: Am I not Hella?

speaker: Hella
content: Oh... so that's how it is... To you, we're nothing like her. We're just dead and gone.

speaker: Hella
content: Only she deserves to live.

speaker: Option
options: Don't try that guilt trip on me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Look at what you've done to her! To all those innocent people! You don't even think humans deserve to live, so why should I treat you like one? You're a monster, just like the ones you hate!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't you dare come to me wearing her face. You have nothing in common with the real Hella!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You never even considered yourself human, did you? How else could you kill so many without feeling a thing? You even hurt her, an innocent person who only wanted to help you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop the act! You never saw her as one of your own. You're different, right down to your core!
It listens, silent and still. Then, a smile splits its face.

speaker: Hella
content: Yes... We do feel it that way.

speaker: Hella
content: As someone from DisCity... as a Sinner... she has a place to return to. She is... not like us.

speaker: Hella
content: ...But Hella didn't see it that way.

speaker: Hella
content: She said we weren't so different. Equally weak. Equally powerless... just struggling to get by.

speaker: Hella
content: We all watch the strong defy their fate and charge ahead... while we're left secretly hoping...

speaker: Hella
content: "Turn around. See me. Look at me... save me..."

speaker: Hella
content: The weak are all the same.
Its voice softens, like a longing unearthed from forgotten years, tender and aching.

speaker: Hella
content: That's what she believed. It's why she brought us... all this way... to find you.

speaker: Hella
content: She thought you could save us...
It fixes its gaze upon you.

speaker: Hella
content: But you don't want to.
It closes in on you.

speaker: Hella
content: You've become just like the others. No different from the ones who terrified her...
Then, countless clones of it materialize, swarming around you.

speaker: Hella
content: So, you can no longer take her away...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mmph!

The shackles seep out, merging with it, with them, all while an eerie laughter rings in your ears. Meanwhile, the Mania within you decomposes your very being, melting you down to feed upon your essence.

A blue light flashes—the <color=#fb9259>insurance</color> Schorl promised. Though instantly engulfed by the maelstrom, it rips a tiny seam in reality. It's all the opening you need, and you seize it without a second thought.

You lunge for the phantom closest to her. You know, with every fiber of your being, that the "Hella" who came for you isn't just another of the Black Ring's deceptions. You trust that somewhere within that phantom, buried deep in the shadows, her true heart still exists.
You believe the real Hella is right here, and you can reach her. You just have to trust your instincts!
[Release the shackles]

speaker: Black Ring Phantom
content: AAAHHHHH!!!!!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: HELLA!!!
The shackles lunge forward, unerringly aimed at the only shadow that weeps. It shatters above you like glass, and with its destruction, a massive fissure tears open the blood-red sky.
Then, the sky transforms. A waterfall of crimson pours through the rupture—a mighty river roaring down with the singular intent to drag you into the abyss.
The Observatorium's blue light envelopes you, shielding you once more, but its flickering glow is clearly reaching its limit. Urgent warnings scream in your mind: Leave. Now.
[Screen Flash] Red Shackles Effect
It worked!

The other end of the shackles goes taut, snagged on something solid. Obeying your will, they violently yank you upward, against the falling torrent. Countless vengeful spirits shriek and rush at your face; malevolent winds slice at your body like steel blades. Yet you clutch the shackles, struggling forward, desperate for a glimpse of the path ahead.

Can you even see? Your vision is a smear of blood. Yet fragments from the crimson torrent splash onto your cheeks and hands. They vanish instantly, but each one sears your skin like white-hot embers, branding you with their memory.
[Flashback]

speaker: Horo
content: Hella! Damn it... Get back here!!
[Flashback]

speaker: Saffar
content: So thank you, Hella... For giving us hope.
[Flashback]

speaker: Korryn
content: Hella is the best girl in the world, the toughest little mouse. No one can say otherwise.
[Flashback]

speaker: Hypatia
content: Thank you. You not only saved my life, but the lives of everyone in Furor as well. I'm truly in your debt.
[Flashback]

speaker: Synex
content: No matter where they are, rats always find a way to survive. No masters, no chains—just pure, stubborn aliveness. They're free, and I like that about them.
[Flashback]
Another phantom emerges ahead, a solitary figure resisting the relentless current.

Unlike the others, she stands isolated within the torrent's heart, battered and devoured by its fury—struggling forward in vain, just like you. Is she crying? The image sharpens, and the sight of her lances through your heart. You scream her name, the sound tearing from your throat—
Your left hand reaches forward. Potestas erupts from your palm, and you unleash its full power, violently harnessing the Black Ring's own contamination to blast a path ahead.
It tears open another bloody wound.

speaker: Black Ring Phantom
content: So this is the shackles... This is ███...

speaker: Black Ring Phantom
content: What do you want? To devour us? To pass judgment? With all your power and your flawless nobility?

speaker: Black Ring Phantom
content: <size=52>Then bring it on!!</size> We don't regret a thing! And we're not afraid of your judgment!

speaker: Black Ring Phantom
content: The seeds we planted will break through the earth! This barren land where we fell will live again! We chose this hell! We sacrificed our future to get here, and this is where we make our stand! DisCity, Fraser, shackles, Corpus... no power, no fate, will ever make us kneel!

speaker: Black Ring Phantom
content: This is what Hella gave us! What <color=#7683a2>you</color> taught us!!

speaker: Hella
content: Don't do this...

speaker: Hella
content: NOOOOOOOO!!!!!

speaker: Black Ring Phantom
content: We don't care about your conflicts or your causes. We... only have one wish!

The shackles respond with violent agony, as if your very blood vessels have transformed into jagged spikes, ripping through your body to thrust forward. At last, you shatter the "wall" that stood in your way. The world gives way, and you are hurled into a void, utterly untethered, floating weightlessly through the chaos.
Until you crash hard onto solid ground.

In that moment of shocking clarity, you finally realize the truth. You were never ascending. You have been plummeting downward the entire time, surrounded by the swirling fragments of your own torn flesh and blood.

Miraculously, your consciousness holds. A strange, silk-like substance settles over you—gossamer threads light as a cicada's wings, yet their accumulated weight feels suffocating. They extend from your body, not restraining you, but pointing the way forward like a lifeline into the darkness.
With every ounce of strength you have left, you force yourself to stand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Look, I don't know you. I don't understand you, and I can never forgive you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I know Hella.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She fought with everything she had to get to you. She let herself be trapped in a Black Ring and endured all this without giving up... She must have had a goal. It can't be despair—Hella would never surrender to Mania... She had to have another wish... And I know the same is true for all of you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The "Hella" who came to me wasn't just her... it was all of you, too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If surrendering to Mania and becoming a Black Ring still wasn't enough... then what is it? What do you want from me by following her all the way here? Tell me...
No one answers. The spirits dissolve into the void, abandoning you to the profound depths of the Black Ring. A place of unsettling, unnatural silence.
Yet, a path remains. The gossamer threads stretch taut, pointing toward a solitary light in the immense distance. And within that light's core, a figure waits.
You move forward, step by arduous step. And then, faintly at first, you hear a familiar voice.
[Fade In Transition] 3s, Heartbeat Sound
[Illusion]

speaker: Hella
content: Hmm... was it a dream...?

speaker: Hella
content: You were in my dream again...

speaker: Hella
content: Hey, you big dummy...

speaker: Hella
content: While I was away, I had this... really long dream. Like, I was on this adventure, but on my way back... I fell into this river...

speaker: Hella
content: The current was so strong... I couldn't even stand straight... Everyone around me was getting swept away... and I couldn't grab onto any of them...

speaker: Hella
content: Then I realized, hehe... I was gone too...

speaker: Hella
content: I was so scared... I couldn't breathe...

speaker: Hella
content: All I could do was scream your name... hoping you'd hear me and come...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hella, wake up...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I'm here, Hella. Wake up...

speaker: Hella
content: But then I actually saw you... and I realized...

speaker: Hella
content: It was just a dream...

speaker: Hella
content: Haha... even in my dreams, I'm so weak. Can't do anything right...

speaker: Hella
content: I really tried to change. I gave it everything I had. I just... wanted to catch up...

speaker: Hella
content: Tell me... what I should do...

speaker: Hella
content: To be like you...
What I couldn't do... I know you can...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So... this is what she wanted...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Trapped in all that Mania... crossing all those catastrophes... fighting an endless corruption with nothing but a limited ability to heal herself. Even after merging with a Black Ring that big... she still fought her way back across thousands of miles...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...All just to come home to you. That was her only wish.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You can do this. Of course you can...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just keep going. One more step. Then another...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That kid never stopped waiting for you. She never lost faith...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So for her sake, you must...

You can advance no further. You are utterly enveloped, trapped within the layers of a suffocating cocoon. You cannot take another step. You cannot see what lies ahead. Your body is broken; your spirit, drained. She stands right before your eyes—so close you could almost touch her—yet an impossible chasm separates you.
At the very end... is there anything left to hear?

speaker: Augustus
content: I take you to the front lines, and let you give everything you have to save this person you care for. And you do. You push beyond your limits. You leave nothing on the field—but you still fail.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...What would you do then?
In the end... Just as she said...
You really have failed this time...

[Scene Change] Exterior Battlefield
(Hecate falls from the giant beast)

speaker: Hecate
content: Mmph...!
Razor-sharp spikes punch through Hecate's body, violently tearing through Nightmare. She stumbles, her footing lost, and begins to fall.

speaker: Synex
content: Whoops! That was a close one, darling. Tsk, tsk, so careless. You'd have taken quite a spill if I hadn't been here to catch you. Gave you a fright?

In a flash, Synex's tail whips out, hooking around Hecate's waist and yanking her close. Synex opens her mouth to tease, but the words die on her lips. The contamination seeping from the DisCity girl is a torrent—far too much to be explained by a mere fear of falling.
Hecate trembles uncontrollably in her grasp as the contamination visibly spreads across her body. Synex's senses flare; the scent has fundamentally changed.

speaker: Hecate
content: No... Hella, Chief...

speaker: Hecate
content: No...

speaker: Synex
content: ...Don't tell me...

speaker: Synex
content: Damn it— Argh!!
She turns to flee to safety, but the ground beneath her feet convulses. She is violently hurled into the air.

Below, the massive metal hammer—the ruined Nirvana Port once driven firmly into the earth—is now being forced upward. Under immense pressure, the Black Ring Apostle begins to rise, its form pulsing and swelling. Vile red markings spread across its surface like cracks, glowing with pent-up energy, charging for a single, catastrophic purpose.
With a final, tectonic heave, it unleashes its power—

speaker: Black Ring Apostle
content: ROAAAAR!!!

Selyna can barely contain her exhilaration. The strategy worked! The Aurum Secretum sorcerers have successfully locked the DisCity Shepherd in the Black Ring's depths, severing all external links. Both the Shepherd and his shackles are now imprisoned. Now, all that remains is for the Ring to consume him utterly.
female_content: Selyna can barely contain her exhilaration. The strategy worked! The Aurum Secretum sorcerers have successfully locked the DisCity Shepherd in the Black Ring's depths, severing all external links. Both the Shepherd and her shackles are now imprisoned. Now, all that remains is for the Ring to consume her utterly.

content: They will possess the most powerful Black Ring in history!! They've won. They've truly w—

A searing red light lances through her body. The Apostle Black Ring, having feasted on the shackles, swells with power exactly as she had envisioned. And with that power, it immediately turns and devours her and the nearby Aurum Secretum sorcerers, bringing their exhilaration to an abrupt and absolute end.

The last loyal Aurum Secretum warrior falls, slain by the very god they labored to create. And in her final moment, she dies laughing—a sound of pure, ecstatic contentment, fervently believing in a promised future.

content: That's the situation as it stands... Please assemble your Rancor forces, General Augustus.

speaker: Schorl
content: We'll be counting on you for the battle ahead.

content: The enemy has lured ${PlayerName} deep into BR-005 and imprisoned him. The ring is saturated with Aurum Secretum particles, which are being manipulated through the Underground sorcery.
