speaker: Schorl
content: It is now clear that planting the Aurum Secretum and containing Sinner Hella were premeditated actions. Their objective is to capture ${PlayerName} and absorb the shackles. If that fusion completes, the power of BR-005 will become uncontrollable.

speaker: Schorl
content: We must destroy the Black Ring before fusion is final. Your task is to suppress BR-005 and buy time for EDGE. We are mobilizing the Third Observatorium to channel BR-003's energy for a strike targeting the inside of BR-005.

speaker: Schorl
content: The shackles are still active, allowing us to track Sinner Hella at the Ring's center. A precision strike on her location will severely damage the Ring and interrupt the fusion process, giving ${PlayerName} a 67% probability of survival.

speaker: Schorl
content: Briefing complete. BR-003 will be ready in 2,291 seconds. Please begin the operation immediately.
They all know their next target is a resident of DisCity—an innocent, harmless young girl from their own streets.
Even the Rancors, perpetually roaring with anger, have fallen silent.

speaker: Rancors
content: ...It's one of our own this time... Not an enemy, but one of us... Again... Can it be me instead...

speaker: Rancors
content: But this is an order. If we don't... far more lives will be taken...

speaker: Rancors
content: Has it been decided... Is it final... Do we really have to do this... Then, there is no choice...

speaker: Rancors
content: For the city. For victory... This is a soldier's sacred duty... This is the price of war...

speaker: Rancors
content: It doesn't matter... We were damned for hell a long time ago...
The military doctor on Broken Blade Squad 3 watches, her eyes deadened with a fatigue beyond physical exhaustion. At last, a hollow, bitter laugh escapes her.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: I became a doctor to save lives... to keep my comrades alive. But my patients never lived long. In a war, the killers will always outnumber the saviors.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: The cruel joke is... when I finally got to wield a Rancor, learned to kill, I saved more lives than I ever did with my scalpel.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: I don't regret it, but don't call me a doctor. Not anymore.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: I have forever lost that right.
The woman who refuses to call herself a doctor gazes across her battlefield. She raises her head, as if to mourn this merciless order by offering the life of the monster before her.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: We've been damned for a long time. We're all bound for hell anyway, so let's go together.
Lieutenant's expression is grave, his eyes veiling a deep and helpless resignation. With a heavy sigh, he ultimately chooses obedience.
This duty was once sacred to him, but now it feels like a shackle, chaining him to this order and dragging them both into the abyss.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: ...This is an order, and a soldier must obey orders.
He feels beyond relieved that Siglinde isn't here to see it. Then, the iron-masked man beside him begins to speak.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: I saw no action in the DisCity Independence War. No foreign campaigns, either.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: All I got was this twisted power, passed down through generations of Rancors. And their memories that came with it.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: A warrior chooses their leader. They become their blade, their shield, until they stand victorious at the end.
The crimson flower blooms on his neck. In response, every Rancor in the Shattered Blade calls out, summoning their commander.

speaker: Rancors
content: Lead us, General... We fight for you... to victory...

speaker: Rancors
content: We are your faithful Reapers Rancors... Now, this loyalty is our only glory...
[Augustus War]

speaker: Rancors
content: ...My Reapers...
A memory surfaces, pulling her back fifty years.

speaker: Soldier
content: We won!!

speaker: Catherine
content: Dravyn!! Did you see that? We won!!

speaker: Catherine
content: It's over. Nuclear weapons are obsolete. As long as I'm here, no one will ever dare to launch one! Your troops are free to move!

speaker: Catherine
content: Oh! Where's Vennon's squad? They were brilliant! To think those forbidden weapons actually worked! We have to reward them! They deserve a parade!

She looked up to the sky where Vennon and the Reaper squad were taking off once more, circling high above everyone. Catherine could clearly see that iron-masked man saluting them all. His cockpit looked so beautiful, as if a blood-red flower were blooming within it.

speaker: Catherine
content: Vennon! Hurry up and come back! Ven—

The fighter jets departed as the seventeen aircraft of the first-generation Reaper squad formed up and flew toward the morning sun—toward victory, toward the city they had sworn to protect and had indeed defended with their lives. Their seventeen long, crimson exhaust trails truly resembled seventeen blades sliding smoothly back into their sheaths.
And just as Catherine thought they were about to disappear from view...
BOOM!!

speaker: Dravyn
content: Wielding the Reapers... it costs a piece of your mind. The more you use it, the more it consumes you. To maximize your power, the Reaper squad had to exhaust the weapons' full potential. They had prepared themselves for a point of no return.

speaker: Dravyn
content: But my soldier said he didn't want to be corrupted by the weapon in his hands. He said he wanted victory as a human.

speaker: Dravyn
content: And so they shall have it. Let us honor them as the heroes they are.

The blood-red blast dissolved into a plume of smoke and fire, vanishing in the sky. For a fleeting moment, the flame glittered in her eyes—a salute to their triumph, a burning requiem for the fallen heroes.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...Ah... I found it...

speaker: Catherine
content: This is what I really wanted...
As the mission time draws closer, the Rancors and soldiers grow increasingly restless.

speaker: Rancors
content: To battle! We are shattered blades, specters of the past!

speaker: Rancors
content: War is a sin. Killing is a sin. And we choose this sin! We have always chosen it! We are beyond forgiveness—

speaker: Rancors
content: So let our sinful slaughter carve a path for those to come. May they be spared our burden of guilt. May they have a right to choose... Hasn't it always been this way?!
Every Rancor howls and wails. Amid the crushing cacophony, Scarface finally breaks, his face contorting as he nearly bursts into tears.

speaker: Scarface
content: General, can we pick someone else? I'll dust anyone you point me at, I swear. Just not her...

speaker: Scarface
content: She's the one the Minos guy has been breaking his back to save, isn't she? What's her crime? Being a kid from our own city?
female_content: She's the one the Minos lady has been breaking her back to save, isn't she? What's her crime? Being a kid from our own city?

speaker: Scarface
content: We've been fighting this whole damn war and this is what's left? That can't be right. It ain't right!

speaker: Scarface
content: There's gotta be another way! I... I really can't do this—!
Before the chaotic mass of soldiers, Augustus takes a single step. The unrest vanishes, quelled by her mere presence.
Scarface's plea only deepens the shadow on her face. In one fluid motion, she is upright, driving her blade into the earth with definitive force.
A metallic crash echoes, and the world seems to bend. All the howling Rancors are instantly silenced, their clamor swallowed by her absolute authority.
In the face of her will, all chaos is utterly crushed. Though she wields no Rancor herself, every bearer of one is her living sword.
Now, she deliberately draws her blade from the floor and steps forward.

speaker: Augustus
content: Listen up, all Eighth Division Shattered Blade... no, all DisCorps units... Whatever orders you followed before, whatever loyalties you held... forget them. Cut it all off. Now.

speaker: Augustus
content: On this battlefield, I am your only commander. You will follow my orders, and mine alone.

speaker: Augustus
content: In return, I give you victory. Not a hollow one. You will not be asked to compromise your duty. You will not be ordered to make pointless sacrifices. You will have your justice, your honor, and your win. All of it.

speaker: Augustus
content: Now, your only mission is to suppress BR-005. You will not yield a single inch until I return.

speaker: Augustus
content: We must win this war, with not a single blemish on our victory!

By order of General Augustus before departure, <color=#dg1f1f>the original plan of engagement has been revised:</color>

All Broken Blade squads are to abort the direct assault on the Black Ring Apostle via Nirvana Port and evacuate immediately. Logistics personnel will remain to operationalize Nirvana Port as a containment measure, baiting and holding the Black Ring.

All main combat units equipped with Rancors will disperse into small, mobile teams. Their new primary objective is to sweep the battlefield and locate any overlooked Aurum Secretum devices.

Any discovered device is to be destroyed on sight. For subterranean Aurum Secretum installations, units are to confirm coordinates and call for targeted heavy artillery strikes from the rear.

General Augustus will infiltrate the Apostle Black Ring alone, with only one objective—

<size=50><color=#dg1f1f>Bring back everyone the Shattered Blade wants to save, alive!</color></size>
Within the Apostle Black Ring, the sea of Mania shivers with a subtle, alien disturbance. A foreign force has begun to seep into its depths.
Guided by an unseen hand, the Aurum Secretum's resonance center is transferred into the heart of the Black Ring. Invisible waves of energy coalesce, solidifying into threads of shimmering gold.
The threads multiply, weaving an intricate and relentless web that begins its slow, methodical sweep across the entire space.
A single golden filament grazes ${PlayerName}'s body, drawing a fine line of blood. He doesn't stir. He has retreated too far within to feel anything now.
female_content: A single golden filament grazes ${PlayerName}'s body, drawing a fine line of blood. She doesn't stir. She has retreated too far within to feel anything now.

content: The fine web trembles once, pausing as if making a final confirmation.

With verification granted, the golden web begins to draw closed. It tightens like a fist, the threads pulling closer, denser, deadlier. It will not stop until it has shrunk to the size of a person, and there, at its heart, it will excise its target from existence.
—But at that very moment, something blocks its path.

speaker: Hella
content: I had a dream... a long, long dream...

speaker: Hella
content: There was this river, a wide, deep, rushing river...

She tightens her hold on ${PlayerName}. Her own body becomes a shield, intercepting the lethal light of the web. She holds firm, but she knows if the opposing force amplifies its power even a fraction, her frail protection will shatter immediately.
Perhaps later, once her body has mended... then, she is certain she could stop it completely.
There is nothing more she can do now... She's just not as strong as ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Hella
content: How am I supposed to fight this? How strong do I have to be to walk against the current...

speaker: Hella
content: Tell me, ${PlayerName}... You're always pushing forward, always ahead of me...

speaker: Hella
content: ...You never lose... You always figure it out... Right?

speaker: Hella
content: ...Wake up.

speaker: Hella
content: This is a joke, right? Stop messing with me and wake up... Tell me you're fine... Look at me...

speaker: Hella
content: ...Was it me? Is this because I was just sitting here, pathetically waiting for you to save me?

speaker: Hella
content: Then forget saving me... Just save yourself! Wake up and get out of here... You hear me?

speaker: Hella
content: Damn Black Ring, let me talk to him...
female_content: Damn Black Ring, let me talk to her...

content: And so, Mania grants her wish.
Spike after spike, the pitch-black shackles pierce ${PlayerName}'s body, merging with the Black Ring and Hella's own form. Through this newly forged connection floods a profound and intense emotion.

Failed　　　　　 <size=38>I failed</size>　　　　<size=50> Why? Where did I go wrong?</size>　　　<size=52><color=#fb9259> I'm sorry</color></size> <size=50>I'm sorry</size>
　　　　　　　　 Think again <size=38>Try one more time</size> <color=#fb9259><size=52>Am I not enough? </color></size>Who else? Who can do it?

　　　　　　<size=38>She's waiting</size> Find another way 　　Can't let go, must not fail
<size=42> One more time</size>, one more time, <size=52> try again </size>　　　　　　<color=#fb9259> Just one more step</color></size>

<size=45>Be <color=#fb9259>stronger </color></size> 　　　　　 Try harder </size>
<color=#fb9259><size=52>Can't you do it?</color></size>
...Am I really this weak?
Tears shimmer in her eyes as light finally returns to the young girl's once-lifeless gaze.
In this moment, she understands everything. These are the emotions Hella knows most intimately, the very feelings that reside within her own heart. But...

speaker: Hella
content: Dummy... don't talk about yourself like that... I've been watching you all along...

speaker: Hella
content: ...You're obviously the strongest person ever...
A ripple disturbs the Mania space. Sensing the shift within the girl, the departed souls grow restless.
They coalesce from the chaos, swarming from all directions. They wail as they rush toward Hella, pulling at her, pleading with her, desperate to pry the two apart.

speaker: Hella
content: I know... I want to go with you all too...

speaker: Hella
content: But look at him...
female_content: But look at her...

speaker: Hella
content: I know I'm not strong... but even so, I still have things I don't want to lose...
She clutches ${PlayerName}'s hand, her grip tightening until warmth seeps back into her long-frozen limbs, until she can feel the steady rhythm of a precious heartbeat once more.
Just one more time. Don't let go. Even knowing she's out of her depth, she has to try.
Let the filth that corrupts you, corrupt me instead. Let the thorns that pierce you, pierce me in your stead. I will bear your suffering. I will carry your burden.
This stupid power of mine... it's useless for anything but patching myself up. But hey, at least it makes me a little stronger... At least I can hold on just a little longer...

speaker: Hella
content: I still can't do it... not on my own... But you're here now... I'll just borrow your strength...

The shackles piercing your body shudder and respond to her call. They rip free, only to plunge deep into Hella's own flesh. They writhe and burrow into her—a parasitic frenzy spreading, merging, and corrupting her very essence. They grow relentlessly, until—

speaker: Hella
content: Get out of my way...

speaker: Hella
content: I'm... taking him back!
female_content: I'm... taking her back!

content: Go now...
You're home...

Bent by tremendous magnetic forces, even the Black Ring twists in response. The invisible threads tear asunder while shards of weathered metal draw together and merge. The contamination within is suppressed, shaped, and bound to the metal, reborn into the perfect instrument of war its master desires.

Thus, the general who single-handedly charged into the heart of the Black Ring seizes her glory. With a skyward sweep of her blade, she effortlessly cleaves a rift within the Apostle's body before spurring her warhorse onward, leaping toward the next battle!

speaker: Augustus
content: Now, all units—stand ready!

speaker: Augustus
content: Crush them all!

speaker: DisCorps Troops
content: CHARGE!!

speaker: Augustus
content: Enough with the act. I know you're awake. On your feet. We have work to do.

speaker: Augustus
content: Any longer, and I'll be the one claiming the trophy for taking down that Black Ring.
The massive Apostle disintegrates—born from instability, now unmade by it.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: Come...

You struggle to your feet. Before you are the souls that once barred your path, yet now they release their hold without a fight. Has their wish changed? Or did you, in that fractured resistance, finally come to understand their pain, allowing them to achieve what they desired?

Their voices rise in a chorus, merging with the disintegrating Black Ring to birth a new, twisted form. These whispers—fleeting, ephemeral—were forgotten in death and ignored even as part of the Black Ring. Only in this final collapse do they at last leave a tangible mark upon the world.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: Our wish... is coming true...

The newborn creature calls to you, its voice a soft yet desperate plea, as if... those souls, too, are hoping. They hope that you might understand them, as Hella understands you; that you might share their pain, as Hella shares yours.

This is their final yearning: though their fate is sealed, if others can see their hatred and bear the weight of their pain, that shared burden may become an antidote to their suffering, much like... the shackles.
The war may not be over yet. But by destroying one of its engines, people have carved a moment of respite from hell. A moment for all to breathe.

With the collapse of BR-005, the FAC finally seals the Broken Frontline in time. Bereft of their guiding will, the surviving Apostles fall into disarray. The grueling battle rages for another three days before the lingering threat of the Tide of Ashes is finally purged.
Meanwhile, having razed the last Aurum Secretum stronghold, the DisCorps troops race back to the city to reinforce the final push.

Perhaps shocked by Augustus's pre-battle intimidation, the normally boisterous Rancors have fallen into an unnatural silence. Their quietude is disconcerting, leaving the soldiers feeling oddly hollow, as if a crucial part of their battle spirit has been lost.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Bring the wounded in! I'll handle the treatment!
Yet after all these years, for the first time, they are left in silence to hear the beating of their own hearts.
Synex prowls the allied camp, a cheerful whistle on her lips as she drinks in the beautiful disarray.

speaker: Synex
content: Well, that was a spectacular failure... Bravo, everyone! And that's my cue to exit stage. It's been a blast, really, but... so long, suckers!

speaker: Synex
content: Maybe I'll pay a visit to little Hella?

When the fire within has burned to ash, one must reflect on the past, and thus, find the strength to move forward. For ruins are not a forever shelter, and the next storm may already be on the horizon.

speaker: Max King
content: And at the final hour, who swoops in to save the day? Nirvana! Those Hypercubes were a masterstroke—flawless logistics! Now that's the mark of a true industry leader. Quinn's inventory? Doesn't even compare!

speaker: Max King
content: Consider the past forgotten! I'm going to sing your praises from the rooftops—a personal endorsement from me to the FAC and the West District! They'll see you as the heroes you are!

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: ...Your theatrics this time were disruptive. You've drawn a spotlight on yourself. Sooner or later, you'll be on their radar.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: No one will be there to take the next bullet for you.

speaker: Max King
content: Let them look. I've been on someone's radar anyway. If they're brave enough to take a second shot, I'll make sure the world watches it happen.
He looks up with a carefree grin.

speaker: Max King
content: Besides, I'm not alone anymore.

speaker: Max King
content: See? Even you're offering me advice. Things are looking up already.
[Transition] (Underground Shelter)

speaker: Gracelyn
content: We won? For real? Yaaaaaas! Get the good stuff, we gotta— ...Oh, hang on. Wait. No, no, I almost forgot.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: I'm just... I'm just glad it's over. We can breathe easy. And hey, I ain't celebrating them losing. I know you're from out there, Sibilla. I really hope your people are alright.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...I know. Thank you, Gracelyn.
Time and again, that girl's question echoes in her mind.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Sibilla, do you hate DisCity?
Hate? No, never. In her darkest hour, it was the people of DisCity who reached out to her. That truth resonates far louder than any propaganda.
If there is any hatred to be named, the true question for Sibilla is this: "Do you hate Fraser?"

Hate them for their deception, their incitement, their extortion and exploitation. For murder and inhumane sacrifice. The reasons are endless. In the depths of despair, hatred can reignite a cold heart; it is the most raw, the most primal of fires.
...If only such fire could truly end suffering. If only it could forge a better future.

But hate cannot even bring back the truth behind Furor. It cannot build the new path Sibilla must walk. There is no time to dwell in resentment—she must depart, and quickly. After all, she refuses to believe she has lost everything.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Ooh, but speaking of—what about that girl you met before? Uh... Jelena, right? The one from Eastside. She's gonna come around again? She's got a friend also called Sable, with roots out your way too, right? That's pretty wild! You should totally hang with her more.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I was actually thinking that myself. I'd like that.
[Sibilla's Flashback]

speaker: Sibilla
content: When all of this is over and things get better, would you like to visit again?

speaker: Sibilla
content: There are quite a few cyborgs living in Syndicate, and Outlanders too. I think you'd like it there.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Thank you. See you next time, then.
[Scene Change]
There is always a price to pay.

speaker: Passerby A
content: See, this is why we shouldn't judge all Outlanders. I heard we managed to fix the Hypercube shortage, and it was all thanks to Quinn. Apparently, President Eirene had already arranged the supplies and secured the WhiteSands routes right before she was detained. Did us a huge solid!

speaker: Passerby B
content: Oh, that's totally true! And get this—the word is she only came here in the first place because her no-good father, Campbell, was trying to have her killed. She's been done with Fraser for years. DisCity's her home now. We're the ones who actually took her in.

speaker: Adelaide
content: How merciless you are, sister. You placed your wagers on DisCity early—clever, to free yourself from this mire so swiftly. Then... would you be so kind as to retrieve your brother's remains from this foreign land and lay him to rest properly?

speaker: Adelaide
content: Ah, but I jest... You surely don't remember having such a brother.
His laughter dies abruptly, his gaze caught by a poster outside—a photograph of a Fraser commanding officer's aircraft, broken and burning.
Among the victorious crowds, a voice remarks, "He should've just surrendered. Fraser sold him out anyway... What a waste. So young, and he bought into every single lie."

speaker: Adelaide
content: ...And here I was... thinking we might celebrate your birthday in DisCity...

speaker: Adelaide
content: So this is the price...
There is always truth buried beneath.

EDGE-02: BR-005 has been neutralized. As agreed, SHP-13 did not absorb ██ to ensure survival. It's been successfully retrieved by the Ring Research Institute, but it's since lost all activity. For now, it makes an excellent research specimen.

EDGE-07: BR-003 has returned to concealment to recuperate. This proves the technology is still immature. We should halt forced requisitions immediately. If the enemy discovers its weaknesses, its value as a deterrent is gone.

EDGE-02: Then our involvement is concluded. Conventional warfare is outside our jurisdiction. It's time to hand specific operations back to the subordinate agencies.
EDGE-02: This operation has yielded many unexpected outcomes. We'll have our hands full with the ramifications.

EDGE-03: Before that, one point requires clarification.

EDGE-03: ...Reports indicate SHP-13 has expressed an intent to eliminate BR-003. For a subject of high emotional volatility, the statement still represents a genuine position.
EDGE-03: How should we address this declaration?

EDGE-01: He actually said that?
EDGE-01: Then it seems... both we and he need to work against the clock.
female_content:
EDGE-03: ...Reports indicate SHP-13 has expressed an intent to eliminate BR-003. For a subject of high emotional volatility, the statement still represents a genuine position.
EDGE-03: How should we address this declaration?

EDGE-01: She actually said that?
EDGE-01: Then it seems... both we and she need to work against the clock.

content: EDGE-01: Our monitors indicate the Underground Shepherd has begun to mobilize since BR-003's exposure.
There are always scars left by shadows, lasting a lifetime.
[Black Screen] Sound of a trigger being pulled

Elvira slumps in her room at the Bureau, her back against the headboard. The small handgun rests in her limp grip. She pulls the trigger. Click. Again. Click. The empty, mechanical sound hangs in the silent air. And then, slowly, a smile spreads across her face.

speaker: Elvira
content: Hah... She actually believed I was one of them. That we were the same... Heh... So pathetic. Who even made them this way? Fraser? The Underground?

speaker: Elvira
content: I will never forget... the ones who blinded them, used them, and sent them all to die... I will never forgive that.
In this age, suffering endures unvanquished; malice still spreads among mankind. Thus, war never truly ends—an eternal cycle, spinning on.

<size=50><color=#dg1f1f><i>Yet there will always be those who march into battle. One after another, they choose their path, defy their fate, and refuse defeat until their final breath.</size></color><i>
[Scene Change]

speaker: Augustus
content: So this is what the shackles are like when they're not contaminated... Hmm. They do feel clean. No more of that sticky, distorted sensation.

speaker: Augustus
content: You've been carrying this level of contamination while running around with me for over a month? I really did underestimate you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not one of your soldiers.

speaker: Augustus
content: Heh. Pity. I really did want you in my unit. But it's true that the battlefield's no place for you.

speaker: Augustus
content: Then... thank you, my ally.

speaker: Augustus
content: You made it back alive. Well done.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Storming a place like that... You really are DisCorps's commander. There's nothing you won't fight—no, nothing you can't win.

The necessary registration is complete. Though BR-005 has been eliminated, the shadow of war from the farlands still lingers. A new chapter of power struggles within the city is already unfolding, and above it all, BR-003 looms.
Your battlefields once overlapped with hers, but that season has passed. Perhaps now is the time to part ways.
—Though in the foreseeable future, like it or not, your paths are destined to cross frequently.
After a moment's thought, you forgo the formal DisCity military salute. Instead, you simply extend your hand.

speaker: Augustus
content: Go tell them yourself. We'll be waiting at Nirvana Port.
Your hands clasp, tighten briefly, then release.
The commander from bygone days departs with the silenced war drums, leaving you to the future.

speaker: Augustus
content: You don't get it. It was you who saved the Shattered Blade.

speaker: Augustus
content: Your survival is the greatest redemption those soldiers could have asked for.
Augustus returns to her troops, to her warriors who have been waiting.
For twelve years, they were specters, reunited with vacant eyes and blood-stained hands. But today, she finally sees it: a glimpse of the people they were always meant to be.

speaker: Augustus
content: You've done well. You didn't harm the innocent, never retreated in the face of powerful enemies, never blindly followed orders you didn't believe in, and protected everyone you swore to defend.

speaker: Augustus
content: You became the blade itself—edge aimed at fate, never yielding. Warriors like you are my most treasured weapons. Every moment you fought with your lives on the line shines with irreplaceable glory. This victory remains pure. Untarnished.

speaker: Augustus
content: Now, return to the world of the living. Then decide your own path.

speaker: Augustus
content: Property Owner

BR-005 has finally been taken down, yet no new mine has materialized at its point of origin or its final defeat.

This anomaly cannot be explained by the inherent weakness of the Black Ring itself, giving rise to a new theory: the Apostle Black Ring was immensely powerful at its birth but had drastically weakened by the time it reached DisCity's borders.

Vast amounts of its energy were mysteriously dispersed along its trajectory. This suggests the new BR-005 mine could be concentrated somewhere along this path, or that its power has fractured into numerous smaller deposits scattered far and wide. Around this suspicion, new conflicts are already brewing.

Sinner Hella, who escaped the Black Ring, has undergone comprehensive examination and treatment. With the full support of all relevant departments, the Black Ring's corrupting influence on her will eventually be entirely purged.

However, the profound fusion and corruption between Hella and the shackles have permanently altered her Mania characteristics, granting her an unusual aptitude for achieving deep resonance with others.

Her core ability remains self-healing and regeneration. Her exceptional combat prowess, however, appears to be fueled by a residual will of the Black Ring—a silent, watchful presence that now guards her.
[ED]

December 26, N.F. 72
New DisCity

speaker: Dravyn
content: Today, I stand before you as the second Commander of the DisCity Independence Army... and as your new Speaker of the City Council.

speaker: Dravyn
content: This position wasn't given to me by the metropoles. It wasn't bought for us by corporate interests. It was earned by the will of every DisCitizen who cast a vote. It is your trust I carry.

speaker: Dravyn
content: It means the metropoles' chains are broken. The predators are still at our gates, but we have taken back our dignity. We have taken back our freedom. And we will never give them up again.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The days of being exploited, subdued, and oppressed are over. As of today, this city-state is ours. From this day forward, the fate of DisCity will be decided by DisCitizens alone.

speaker: Dravyn
content: We stand here because countless heroes gave everything to get us to this starting line. We will honor their sacrifice, and we will carry their legacy forward.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Let the challenges come, from catastrophe or from man. We will meet them. We will build. We will protect. We will expand! Our city has risen. And it belongs to its people—its greatest strength.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I hereby declare: DisCity is independent!

December 27, N.F. 74
DisCity Cemetery
Memorial Day of the Satellite Town Strategy Victory

speaker: Augustus
content: "In order to preserve a core strategic military asset and prevent further damage from the escalating Mania contamination within the subject's body, DisCorps has decreed, with technical support from EDGE, that Sinner Catherine Augustus Andohar will be placed in cryostasis, effective—"

speaker: Augustus
content: HA? ...The hell is this?
She lashed out with a kick aimed at Dravyn, DisCorps's Commander and first elected Speaker. But with the practiced ease of years, he sidestepped the blow.

speaker: Dravyn
content: You're a vital asset that needs protecting. I have no intention of watching DisCity's youngest general turn into a monster, and being the one who has to put you down.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The war is almost over. Your skills are no longer required. Say your goodbyes properly, then go to sleep. You'd hate peacetime anyway.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hmph. If you lot had done your jobs and developed a Mania treatment sooner, I wouldn't be the one headed for the freezer.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The scientists at EDGE have done everything they can. 01 nearly worked himself to death developing this cryo-process to save you. A little gratitude wouldn't hurt. We'll wake you when it's time.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Or should I set an alarm? When would you like me to pencil you in?

speaker: Augustus
content: If I said "soon," that'd be like wishing for another war. Lieutenant would never let me live it down.

speaker: Augustus
content: Then wake me when you've all retired, lived your lives, and are about to kick the bucket. I'll give you a proper send-off. Make sure your funerals are spectacular.

speaker: Augustus
content: You're the great heroes of DisCity. You can't just fade away quietly.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Heh. Who knows? Maybe I'm hoping for a day when the world changes completely. A day with no more war, no need for your kind of power at all.

speaker: Dravyn
content: When that day comes, I'll wake you just to say it: "Soldiers like you are obsolete. Time to be a good girl and go get an education."

speaker: Augustus
content: Hah! What a dream. You'd better deliver on that, Mr. Speaker of the City Council.

She almost scoffed. Why did the old geezer look so reluctant to let her go? It wasn't as if he'd be alone—he had Victor and Adrian. EDGE still had 01 to cure his baldness. She was the one who would be lying alone for ages. She was the one who should be worried about loneliness.

Time was almost up. She took one last look at DisCity. This was never the city-state that had earned her loyalty, yet for years it had been her battlefield. The place where she had found her most treasured blades. She turned around—

And faced the warriors who had fought beside her across countless battlefields. In every resolute face, she saw the same defiant pride. They were the sharpest blades, forged by their own will, living on their own terms.

Catherine slowly drew her sword and placed it in their steady hands. Then, she took a medal that belonged to the Eighth Division of DisCorps, the general's insignia that Dravyn awarded her with a manner almost that of an adult placating a child.

speaker: Augustus
content: Take care of my troops. They're my pride.

speaker: Dravyn
content: You have my word.

speaker: Augustus
content: Well then, goodbye. I'll be waiting for the day I wake up.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I'll be waiting for that day too.

content:
"Lieutenant": The enemy is secretly transporting supplies to reinforce their front lines. Their so-called ceasefire is nothing but a facade.
"Lieutenant": Our sabotage efforts have had some effect, but without pinpointing their supply routes, we cannot truly cripple the enemy.
"Lieutenant": But please make no mistake. We will not waver. Every Broken Blade squad fights with one purpose: victory.
"Lieutenant": As for the battlefields beyond our reach, you may need to contact the FAC first. Some matters still require their involvement.
The man nicknamed "Lieutenant" lives up to his reputation. Even through the battle report, you can almost hear his low, calm voice—devoid of emotion, yet resolute.
[Black Screen] Or a corridor

speaker: Schorl
content: Are you certain about going alone? This individual is extremely dangerous. At the very least, allow me to accompany you.
If you're there, he'll never talk. I need to do this by myself.
Don't worry. You'll be right outside, right? If anything goes wrong, you can step in.
You push the door open and step into the quiet room. The door clicks shut behind you, and your eyes are drawn to the figure in the hospital bed.
[Scene Change] Hospital (Detention Cell)
It's the man you put there.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Hello, Chief. I'd nearly given up hope of seeing you again. What an unexpected pleasure.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Did you give your superiors your word not to harm me? But I heard you came this close to killing another prisoner just two days ago. Tell me, Chief, should I find comfort in such fragile promises?

speaker: Adelaide
content: Oh, do not misunderstand. I'm perfectly at peace with dying now. Beyond disappointing my family by not bringing them gifts, my existence has become quite irrelevant to the war.
You calmly take a seat beside the bed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well-informed as always, you bastard. Who did you persuade to feed you information this time?

speaker: Adelaide
content: Not quite "persuasion." Even in DisCity, there are kind souls who doubt the war, people with too many unanswered questions. Occasionally, they can't help but... "communicate" with me.
He bears fresh bruises since you last saw him, a stark testament to the "communication" others had with him.
Yet he seems utterly indifferent to them, his attention fixed on the placid stillness you now project.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You're no different, are you?

speaker: Adelaide
content: Your fury is so... unrestrained, Chief. It betrays how ill-prepared you were for this war. By all accounts, you should despise the very idea of war—yet here you stand, shackled to the frontlines. All for dear Hella.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've already seen her.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Oh?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought finally seeing her, knowing where she was, would make me more certain. More focused.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But the truth is, it's just left me more confused than ever. I can't figure this out alone. Which is why I had no choice but to come to you. The one who started all of this.
You look down at your hands. Your palms are now a rough landscape of skin, etched with the cruel corruption of the shackles.
My whole understanding was that the Black Ring held her captive. That the Outlanders who continued to imprison and control her, even after their fall, were monsters. Bastards, like you.
I was consumed by that rage, just focused on eliminating the enemy and bringing her home. It's why I pushed that prisoner so hard.
But then... that "Hella" stopped me. And she was forceful about it.
Afterward, they told me it wasn't really her. Just a phantom, a trick of the Black Ring meant to deceive me. But I know the truth...
Hella was really there. If she wanted to deceive me, she wouldn't have let go. If she wanted me dead, she had plenty of chances before that.
She just came to see me. Used the Black Ring's power to reach me... but for what? What did she want me to do?
I don't even dream of her anymore. So I need to know... those... things that were with her, the ones that sent her... what do they want?
They must all want something, to appear to me in her form. So tell me, Sage of the Underground. What did you do with BR-005?

You lock eyes, both searching for an unspoken truth in the other's gaze. Finally, Adelaide's repulsive smile falters and vanishes. For the first time, his expression is unmasked as he answers your question.

speaker: Adelaide
content: ...The Underground made a deal with me, only asking that I trigger BR-005 somewhere far from DisCity. I originally sought to achieve this with minimal sacrifice, but my plan failed. The Black Ring still ended up exploding.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Countless farland refugees took up the cause willingly, sacrificing themselves just for the chance of change. Even as the Black Ring consumed them, they clung to their defiant will.

speaker: Adelaide
content: These are the vengeful spirits now haunting the Black Ring, following Hella all the way to DisCity to settle their score with fate.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Perhaps you'd still like to extend DisCity's courtesy to them. Perhaps you imagine some elaborate tale of Fraser manipulating them. But even without wartime hatreds to fuel the fire... one truth remains unchanged.

speaker: Adelaide
content: The spread of Mania, the relentless march of calamities... the farlands have been pushed past the brink. Beyond DisCity's walls, they scrape by in the wastelands, clinging to life. And in their despair, hatred for DisCity is the only thing that keeps them going—the desperate hope that if they tear it all down, something might change.

speaker: Adelaide
content: And yet, even consumed by such profound hatred, none have ever wished harm upon Hella.
He lowers his eyes, revealing an uncharacteristically gentle expression.

speaker: Adelaide
content: They adore her. Even after learning her origins, they chose to protect her. She's incompatible with DisCity's sins. Everyone wants to keep her close.

speaker: Adelaide
content: That fragile girl shows concern for Outland strangers because of her own weakness... yet never lets that weakness stop her. She makes people set aside their hatred precisely because she keeps pulling everyone toward survival, toward hope beyond despair.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You've raised a child who shines like the sun. On behalf of many, I thank you for that.
...Don't talk like that.

speaker: Option
options: It makes me want to kill you more.

speaker: Adelaide
content: That's precisely what makes it a wasteland, where weakness itself is a sin, and those who cannot defy fate are doomed to be crushed beneath its weight.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Countless Hellas have been sacrificed, and there have been countless people like you who take up arms—to protect, to seek vengeance, to change this cruel fate.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Hella understood this. That is why she chose to stand with them. And you... you raised her to be so compassionate. Surely, then, you must also understand—

speaker: Adelaide
content: Behind BR-005 is no mere Apostle or calamity. It is the weight of conviction, a desperate plea for change.

speaker: Shadow's Voice
content: ...Get away... Get away...
A desperate plea for change...
Our spymaster warned me about you. Said you're a real expert at getting inside people's heads, making them doubt everything.
You must've run the same routine on others that you just tried on me. I bet those poor souls actually bought it, too.
But you did clear one thing up for me... so thanks for that, you bastard of Fraser and the Underground.
When Hella comes back, I'll settle all of it with you.
[Scene change] As you exit the hospital room, you find Schorl waiting for you.

speaker: Option
options: I held back. I didn't lay a finger on him.

content: So, does that help our trust level?

speaker: Schorl
content: Yes. Your restraint was commendable. Has this clarified your earlier concerns?
Not really, but... it's enough to know what I need to do next.
To start, you need to meet someone...
Just as the controversy surrounding the mobilization order reaches a fever pitch, Max King reactivates his long-dormant social media account.
Without any buildup, a single post bearing his unmistakable style instantly ignites the entire internet.

<color=#8dcdda>@MK_Max King:</color>
Alright, DisCity, let's talk. Straight talk.
I get it. The anxiety, the confusion, and even the anger. I feel it too. We're all just people, and nobody gets to sit out the storm.
Tomorrow, we vote on the Mobilization Order. Round two. This isn't just about the military; this is a historic choice for EVERY single DisCitizen.
But here's the truth, my friends. This is OUR turning point! This is the moment our city-state stands UNITED and leaps toward the future!

Let me be clear: DisCity's fate doesn't rest only with soldiers on the front line. It rests on YOUR will. On MY will. On EVERYONE'S!
War isn't some lone-hero adventure. It's a choice made by every citizen. It's US, together, unleashing strength we didn't even know we had.
Maybe you're just someone from Eastside. A shop owner in West District. A researcher buried in Nirvana's lab.
But since when are heroes only the ones holding guns on the battlefield? You can do MORE than you think!

Remember this: Every action. Every word of support. Every bit of effort—it ALL pushes this city forward.
Don't just watch from the sidelines. This era needs your voice. Your passion. Your responsibility. WE are DisCity. We don't WAIT for miracles—WE MAKE THEM.

I'm not stopping. I'm keeping this conversation going, and I'll keep moving forward. Tomorrow, you can find me on Third Avenue, Sixth District, and Fifth Avenue. If you've got concerns, opinions, big ideas? Come tell me. Don't hold back. As your Speaker, I promise you: I will LISTEN to every voice as we move forward. If <color=#fb9259>Max King</color> had any real power, would he be doing cringe parades in the streets every day? <size=52>lol</size>

<size=28>Does he even read the </size><color=#fb9259>mobilization order</color> he's talking about? I could do a better job than this guy.
<color=#fb9259><size=52>That stupid Max King</color></size> is at it again, posting like he's the chosen one, but we all know the real deals happen behind closed doors.
Give it up, man. Everyone knows you're just a figurehead. <color=#fb9259><size=45>Augustus</color></size> is the real deal.
Selyna wakes to the sound of familiar footsteps.

speaker: Selyna
content: ...@#%*. (Here she comes again.)
But she feels neither anger nor panic.
It's the silver-haired girl again, back for what must be the dozenth visit. After an absence of several days, Selyna notes the fresh wounds that litter her skin.

Not that Selyna cares, of course. A warrior's instinct is to observe. It's just that she'd been the same age when she enlisted. It's just that she sees a hauntingly familiar fire in the girl's eyes...

But this time, instead of timid kindness, Selyna is met by the cold gleam of a gun barrel. A bullet whips past, grazing her hair. She should mock the girl's pathetic aim, but an inexplicable rage ignites within her instead.

speaker: Selyna
content: You fooled me!

speaker: Elvira
content: It's you who lied!

speaker: Elvira
content: @#¥@¥! (It's you who lied!!)

speaker: Selyna
content: You're...?!
The girl calls out in nearly flawless Outland language, revealing a traditional Furor beaded bracelet dangling from her wrist.

speaker: Elvira
content: Do you recognize it? It was my mother's. She was an Outlander. She taught me her language in secret. I remember every word.

speaker: Elvira
content: %@@¥#¥@@%#...,¥%#&@#@%@#@# (Do you recognize it? It was my mother's. She was an Outlander. She taught me her language in secret. I remember every word.)

speaker: Elvira
content: My Disian name... is Elvira Stewart. But my mother gave me another name, Nysa Sadikur, to honor her family in Furor.
She raises her gun, head bowed, her entire body trembling as if suppressing a storm of rage. Finally, she lifts her gaze and, with every fiber of her being, cries out—

speaker: Elvira
content: I know about the Furor Black Ring! I know you betrayed my mother! After what you did... how can you even say words like "justice"?

speaker: Selyna
content: What did you say?
[Black Screen]
Elvira lied. Timid by nature, she nonetheless possesses a surprising talent for performance when the situation demands.
And now, she has decided the situation demands it.
[Alarm Blaring]

speaker: Alarm
content: Alert. Alert. Aurum Secretum reaction detected. Outland Sinner has escaped. Repeat, Outland Sinner has escaped—

speaker: Selyna
content: ...@#¥@#¥ (Damn it!! Damn it all!!!)
Selyna turns and flees. Elvira doesn't pursue; instead, she sinks to her knees, her breath coming in ragged gasps.

speaker: West District Staff Member
content: Miss Stewart! Are you all right?!

speaker: Elvira
content: I... I'm fine...
Immediately after, she activates a secret communication channel.

speaker: Elvira
content: Hello... it's me. The Outlander has left, and no one else noticed. Everything's under control.

speaker: Elvira
content: As we agreed, keep a close watch on her. Don't miss any opportunity.

More gunshots crack the air. Selyna twists aside just as one round strikes true, shattering her restraint. Behind her stands only the DisCity girl, her gun wavering wildly. She is no threat; Selyna could snap her neck and vanish before the echo of the shot fades.
But she doesn't look back.
Sound Effect: [Thunder] [Rain]
[Flash of Lightning] [Sea Surface]
A thunderclap jolts you back to consciousness.
You draw a ragged breath and are met with the burn of saltwater. It floods your ears, your mouth, your mind—until the storm's roar is all that remains.

You thrash, legs scrambling for a purchase that isn't there. Your entire world has shrunk to the sodden piece of driftwood you cling to. With every surge, the waves try to claim it, and you along with it.
Blegh...

But this is no ordinary seawater. It's a liquid contamination known as the <color=#fb9259>Black Tide</color>. In the depths, Mania creatures brush against your legs. You feel the sharp sting as they latch on, peeling back skin to siphon your life away.

The downpour fuels the contamination, whipping the waves into a frenzy beneath the lightning's glare. The cold has long since numbed your limbs; the hammering rain is just a dull percussion on deadened skin.

Darkness stretches to every horizon.
This is your third hour drifting alone in the abyss.

<size=45>July 12, N.F. 115 23:17

Operation BR-005 commences in...</size>
12 days 16 hours 30 minutes
[Thunder] [Lightning] [Small CG Back Silhouette]
High above in the dilapidated lantern room, the lighthouse keeper leans against the great lens, wiping monster fluid from her hands onto her coat before gripping the beacon's control lever.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: The 2,019th time...

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: The 2,019th time I've climbed up here alone.
With a grunt, she throws her full weight against the control lever, forcing the beacon to turn toward the distant seam between sea and sky.
The aged motor groans, its rumble merging with the wind and thunder, a cacophony lost in the distant darkness.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Take me away, you old things... Just end it all.
She grits her teeth, twists the handle, and the light erupts in the rhythmic pattern she programmed long ago, a flashing message sent into the void.
And like the 2,018 nights before, she stares expressionlessly toward the horizon that never responds. Until...
The beam cuts through the black chaos, casting a faint spot of light.
And in its path, a dark speck bucks against the waves.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: A mutated Tide Crawler? No... that's not it.
Carried closer by the tide, the speck grows into a distinct <color=#fb9259>figure</color>. A person. Clinging to driftwood, one arm waving a frantic signal against the storm.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: A living person?!
[Thunder] [Flash of Lightning] [Sea Surface]
A lighthouse!
Cough... Is anyone there?! Hel—

Hours of struggle have left your strength spent, your throat ragged from saltwater. Even the last air in your lungs is useless, your cries swallowed by the thunder of the waves. But you refuse to give up.

You are a plaything for the sea, hurled skyward only to be slammed down again, your insides churning with every impact. The contaminated water seeps deeper into your wounds, a corrosive fire, yet you kick on, driven by the sight of a distant light.
It doesn't look too far... The wind... I can go with the flow, ride the rising tide... cough, cough, cough!
You choke, nostrils flooding with putrid brine. By the time you gasp clear and look up—the light is gone.
HEEEY! Is anyone there...?
Darkness reclaims you. Your feeble call for help vanishes into the vast, indifferent ocean.
Even so, one thought burns through the despair: You still don't know Hella's situation. You can't die here. You absolutely cannot!
I remember the direction of the light. No landmarks, but I can use the wind and waves to orient myself. My bearings can't be too far off. I can...
Your waterlogged limbs, heavy and numb, respond with a clumsy, desperate paddle.

You've lost count of how much black water you've vomited, your world narrowed to the sight of that vanished light seared into your mind. Then, a new sound. The crash of waves against rock. Your strokes become frantic.
Finally, impact. Your knees strike stone, then your palms scrape hard ground as you haul your broken body onto the shore.
[Light Switch Sound Effect] [White Flash]

Solid earth. The relief is instantaneous, dissolving your last shred of tension, and exhaustion crashes over you like a final wave. Consciousness flickers; you dream of the sun burning your back. The crunch of footsteps on sand approaches, halting before you.
Rescue... finally?
You force your head up to face the blinding glare. This is no dream. The sun is a lighthouse, and what greets you is not salvation—
But murderous intent. A boot grinds down on your hand, stopping you cold.
[Small CG: Silhouette]

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Identify yourself. Name. Any tricks...

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You'll be dead.
[Inside the Lighthouse]
A loud thud echoes as you land hard on the floor, hands and feet tightly bound.
This place appears to be a space beneath the lighthouse. The air is thick and humid, heavy with the cloying stench of decay and salt.

Your captor stands guard at the room's only exit, a grim silhouette holding back the nightmare outside. The Tide Crawlers, driven inland by the storm, slam against the doors and windows. Their frenzied scrabbling and hungry, vicious laughter are a grotesque chorus beneath the roar of thunder and crashing waves.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Answer me. Who are you?

Her voice is a blade. You can't see her face in the gloom, but her malice is a physical force. The back of your hand, where her boot pressed you into the shore, throbs in time with your heartbeat, the pain sharpened by the rough rope chafing against the wound.
Given the current diplomatic climate, revealing yourself as <color=#fb9259>the MBCC Chief</color> might not be the best card to play.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Speak!
I can tell by your accent you're from DisCity. So am I. I was with a WhiteSands merchant caravan. Our group got caught in a sandstorm. I woke up in the sea outside.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: A caravan?
She takes a threatening step closer, clearly not convinced by your answer.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Prove it.
[Lightning and thunder]
The thunderstorm rages on, lightning briefly illuminating the room's interior.
I can. But you've got my hands tied. I can't reach it.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: I'll get it. Where?
In the left pocket of my coat.
She crouches before you and begins to search your pocket. You force your breathing to stay even, a fragile mask for the frantic drumming of your heart.
It doesn't take long. Her hand withdraws clutching a clump of letter paper, swollen and pulpy from its soak in the Black Tide.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: What is it?
A letter. From a friend. She went exploring in WhiteSands; I joined the caravan to look for her. If you look at the smudged part, she always drew a little mouse there—ugh!
Before you can finish your sentence, a heavy blow slams into your ribs. The air explodes from your lungs, and you curl involuntarily into a ball on the floor, gasping.
She stuffs the soggy wad of <color=#fb9259>evidence</color> down your collar, then mockingly pats your cheek.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You think I want a story?
You're the one who asked...
You swallow back the acid rising in your throat, struggling to recover.
I have more evidence. Right pocket.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Last chance.
She moves over you, crouching close on your other side. As if on cue, a flash of lightning bleaches the sky, illuminating the room.
Using the thunder's roar as cover, you coil your legs and kick out violently, aiming for her abdomen.

She has neither noticed your movement nor expected you to have any fight left. As she jerks back to dodge, her balance fails. The back of her head cracks sickeningly against the table corner you'd spotted.

She lets out a pained grunt. Ignoring the burn of the ropes, you wrench your wrists apart, feeling the bindings give way. You lunge forward, palm thrust out. Dizziness washes over you, but you grit your teeth against it. This power is your only leverage.
The spikes of dark light surge for her throat. But a knife is already at your neck, its cold point pressed to your artery.
The room falls quiet as darkness reclaims your vision.

You heard no draw, saw no glint of steel. She was simply faster... but how? Before you can even process this, the blade has already broken your skin, filling the air with the metallic scent of your own blood.
My <color=#fb9259>caravan</color> is still searching for me. They can confirm my identity.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Still lying... You're out of chances...
Believe what you want. But if you kill me, my companions will hunt you down.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You think that will scare me?

She shoves you back, pinning your shoulders against the wall. In the utter blackness, you feel her warm breath rapid against your ear. Under the pretense of holding the blade, she has pressed her body against yours, her arm a heavy weight across your chest.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Enough talk. I'm ending this now!
You don't sound well.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: SHUT UP!!!

A furious roar rips from her throat as she pins you in the corner, her full weight crushing you. She torques your arms into sickening, unnatural angles, and the pop of dislocating joints fills the air.

Yet, within the blinding pain, your thoughts become icily clear. You notice the violent tremor in her muscles, the scorching heat radiating from her body. This violent reaction is far beyond anything your limited strength could have provoked.
She's holding something back.
Then why save me? If you pulled me from the sea, why kill me now?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: I said... shut up...
You control the lighthouse, don't you? If it's safe inside, why were you out there? What were you doing?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: None of your ******* business!
You don't care if I live or die, do you? You only care about who I am... You're waiting for someone.

options: You were trying to see if I was them.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: NO!!! I'm not waiting for anyone! NOBODY IS COMING!

She stabs downward in fury, but the blade veers wildly into the wall beside you. She can no longer control her own body. Her gaze seems to fix on your neck, her breath scorching the air as the sweet, drawing ever closer.
The metallic scent of your blood fills the space between you.
I don't know who you're waiting for, but I know what you're afraid of.
It's the smell of blood, isn't it?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: I'LL KILL YOU!
You can't. Not in this state. And I can't fight back. So tell me what you're waiting for. Maybe I can help.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You're in no position to bargain!
Aren't I?

You tighten your grip on the knife, hot blood welling between your fingers, its metallic tang thick in the air. She tries to protest, but her strength is gone; she's drawn to your blood-soaked hand like an addict beyond resistance.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Let go... how... how dare you...
Let's try a different question. What's your name? Who are you?
With a final, desperate lurch, she wrenches the blade free and shoves you back into the corner. In the darkness, you hear only her ragged, greedy breaths, followed by the wet, swallowing sound.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You think you've won? Heh... Fine. Wait for your <color=#fb9259>companions</color>... it's no different than waiting to die!

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: I smelled your other wounds from the start. I know what those sea beasts do. There's barely a piece of you left that's not mangled!

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: None of us will see the morning!
With a resounding crash of iron, she is gone, disappearing in the downpour outside.

Silence descends, broken only by the relentless rain and the frantic rhythm of your own heartbeat. You count silently in the dark—one, two, all the way to five hundred—and only when you are certain she won't return do you finally exhale.

The tension drains from you, and with it, all your strength. Your limbs become dead weights as a deep, penetrating cold seeps up from the floor beneath you. By the weak moonlight, you examine your hands: the fingers are stained dark, the joints already locking in the chill.
Too bad for her. Interrogation is where I excel.
You can hardly believe you had the strength left to face her down. Your mind winnows down to a primal checklist: warmth, water, treatment, food... survival.
Shivering violently, you fumble your way around the circular room. Everything is damp, rotten. But by some miracle, your fingers close around a small, dry box. Matches.
An antiquated design, even for Syndicate.

The match flares, casting a dancing light on the cloud of your breath and reveals a small, iron stove. The fire you coax to life is too meager to heat the room or truly warm you, but its glow is a sanctuary.
You huddle before it, tearing strips from the hem of your coat to fashion crude bandages. Without medicine, stemming the bleeding is the only battle you can win tonight.
I should really wash this coat. Hecate and Nightingale will freak out if they see all these bloodstains.

You wonder when you'll leave this place and when you'll see them again... You force yourself to focus on warm memories to keep your emotions in check, knowing that in your situation, a backlash from the Black Ring would only cause more trouble.
Above, rain drips steadily through the cracked dome; the wind moans around the lighthouse walls. The coppery smell of blood is slowly being lost to the damp, musty odor of decay.
The smell that drove her away.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: None of us will see the morning.
Her sentence hangs in the air, cold and incontestable. This lighthouse, this sea, this lonely island—you still have no explanation for any of it.
You tuck the crumpled ball of "evidence" safely into your pocket, wrap the tattered coat around yourself, and stare into the flames.
I have to survive. I wasn't lying... This is a letter from Hella. I have to find her. I can't... I can't fall here. Not until I know she's safe.
A fragile sense of warmth finally blossoms in your chest, and with it comes an irresistible tide of fatigue, your eyelids growing heavier by the second.
Your body betrays you, slumping against the cold wall as you sink into a deep and dreamless sleep.
[Screen fades to black] [Sound of crackling stove continues briefly]
[Coast]

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...Bastard! I'll kill him! I'll kill him!
female_content: ...Bastard! I'll kill her! I'll kill her!

content: She hurls herself into the horde of monsters crawling ashore. Fangs tear into her shoulder, ripping a chunk from her coat.
Rain and seawater stream down her arm, mingling with the blood on her hands—the blood from the person inside the house. It's still warm, carrying a sweetness that has no place here.
Her alien blade—like a grotesque fusion of bone and metal—hisses through the rain, tearing through the monster tide with eerie whispers. It cuts faster and faster, an unstoppable frenzy.

She and the Tide Crawlers savage one another, contamination fluid drenching her completely. She does not retreat, her humanity lost to a feral madness. In the darkness, she is a monster among monsters.
Her voice is a raw, inhuman shriek, as if the sound of the blade itself speaks through her.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Damn it... I've had enough of this.
[Flashback]

March, N.F. 84
Border Observation Lighthouse OT-N07 Training Grounds

speaker: Fynn
content: Everyone, starting today, <color=#fb9259>little Ceto</color> is officially a lighthouse keeper! Let's give her a proper welcome!
The line of lighthouse keepers stared at their new member drowning in an oversized uniform, exchanging uncomfortable glances in silence. Herbert pulled Fynn aside.

speaker: Herbert
content: Whoa, hold on. We agreed we'd care for her until she was ten, then find her a safe home. What's... what's she doing back here?

speaker: Fynn
content: No one would take her. And frankly, she didn't want to go either. With tensions this high, who's going to adopt an orphan from an old battlefield? Her background is a question mark to them.

speaker: Herbert
content: But... but it's too dangerous here! The front line could shift any day. When it does, how are we supposed to protect a child?

speaker: Fynn
content: That's why she's not a child here; she's a keeper. I'll teach her to protect herself. To fight. To survive what's coming.

speaker: Fynn
content: Remember, she survived contamination as an infant. She has a natural gift for controlling <color=#fb9259>that thing</color>. She might just end up saving you one day.

speaker: Herbert
content: Oh, come on, I don't need a kid to... Ah, fine. She can stay. But I'm not letting her anywhere near—

speaker: Ceto
content: Why not?
A little head suddenly popped up between them.

speaker: Ceto
content: Teach me. I want to join. I want to be like you.

speaker: Fynn
content: Now that's the spirit! A lighthouse keeper never backs down. Come here, Ceto. Give me your hand.
The girl extended her hand with a solemn expression, watching as the captain placed a strangely-shaped dagger into her palm.

speaker: Fynn
content: You know the basics: logging signal fluctuations, monitoring the WhiteSands disaster zone, maintaining the water and ventilation systems, cleaning the base in time... But that's not what makes a true keeper.
Fynn gently raised the girl's wrist, pointing forward. At the edge of the vast white expanse of WhiteSands, a tiny Sun floated on the horizon.

speaker: Fynn
content: Look up. Look out at the horizon.

speaker: Fynn
content: You have to believe a better world is waiting out there. Stand facing it, fight for it, and never, ever let the lighthouse beacon go out.

speaker: Ceto
content: A better world... Can I really go?

speaker: Fynn
content: Absolutely. We'll all go back together. As heroes, returning to DisCity in glory!
[End of Flashback] [Beach, Daytime]
A mountain of monster carcasses rises from the shore, a testament to the night's grim work.
The lighthouse keeper stands at the heart of this sea of corpses, slowly lifting her head toward the distant horizon. Dawn has broken again.
The fragments on her dagger settle into silence. Surviving the Black Tide for the 2,019th time brings no sense of victory, only a profound exhaustion that has nothing to do with the fight.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...Status report: Lighthouse OT-N07. One keeper remaining. No abnormalities observed...
She recites, the words a hollow habit. As she walks toward shore, a detail pierces the fog of her fatigue.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...Report addendum. Lighthouse Seven, 2300 hours last night, a suspicious individual made landfall.
She kicks open the lighthouse's damaged iron door and searches the base cabin. It is empty. There's no trace of the suspicious individual in sight.
The only sign of the intruder is a thin trail of footprints on the stairs, marked with seawater and blood, leading up from the base.
[Flashback]

<size=45>July 12, N.F. 115 19:48

Operation BR-005 commences in...</size>
12 days 19 hours 59 minutes
Are we there yet? This Black Tide you mentioned?

speaker: Doctor
content: We're almost there. The Black Tide isn't far from Euphoria, but given your current state... are you sure about this? That "Black Tide" is actually a liquid contamination zone, a leftover from past campaigns. Going in will only make your condition worse. We could place you somewhere safer instead.
You're the ones who told me this contamination zone might hold buried Rancors... How sure are you about that?

speaker: Doctor
content: Your guess is as good as mine. Over two hundred observers were stationed there, but none survived after the contamination erupted. DisCity never heard from a single one of them again.

speaker: Doctor
content: If I must give an estimate... thirty percent?
You knew what Augustus had been searching for all these years—those scattered weapons she called "old friends." It was her sensing the Rancors' presence that brought the Broken Blade squad here.
Now, your hands clutched the porthole, trembling under the increasing weight of the Black Ring.
That's enough. Thirty percent is plenty.
Any advantage could tip the scales and increase my chances of bringing her back... I can't stop now. Not when we're this close.

speaker: Doctor
content: But that thirty percent I gave you? That's our chance of getting out of the Black Tide alive.
No sooner had those words been spoken than Scarface burst through the cabin door, completely out of breath.

speaker: Scarface
content: Man, this is nuts! We're... bleurgh... the Black Tide!

speaker: Scarface
content: Here we are!
[Deck]

A churning black sea stretched before you, its surface alive with the writhing of massive shadows and the flicker of monstrous silhouettes. The air reeked of decay and rusted metal. Each wave slammed against the hull, groaning the warship's steel frame.

speaker: Scarface
content: Talk about a warm welcome—bleurgh!

speaker: Doctor
content: Keep your breakfast down. It is strange, though. Those city-states' tech back then shouldn't have been capable of creating contamination on this scale.

The swells, black and several meters high, wrapped around the ship like living things, tilting the deck at a frightening angle. Surrounded by the roaring tide, you raised your voices just to be heard.
Is Augustus aware of the situation here?

speaker: Doctor
content: Well, she knows now. I just got her message—
All units, clear the contamination and advance at full speed! To the heart of the Black Tide!

speaker: Scarface
content: BLEURGH—!

Scarface vomited over the rail, then crushed a writhing creature that had crawled aboard and hurled it back into the sea. A trail of foul slime sprayed across the deck, releasing a putrid, fishy stench.
What are these things?

speaker: Doctor
content: Tide Crawlers. Hold on tight!

Another wave hurled the ship into the air. For a weightless moment, it hung at its apex before crashing back down. The impact threw everyone from their feet, and as the crew slammed onto the deck, massive waves engulfed the vessel, trying to drag you all into the consuming dark.

speaker: Scarface
content: Bleurgh— Filthy bugs stewing in black water! Back off, you freaks! Don't touch me!

speaker: Scarface
content: You heard the General! Straight into the Black Tide! Let's move—

speaker: Doctor
content: Get back here! Forget about moving out. We've got a bigger problem on our hands...

speaker: Doctor
content: We've lost the advisor.
[Underwater] [Bubbling sounds]

The black waves swallowed you whole, tearing you from the others despite your desperate struggles. Shadowy forms brushed against you in the depths, their gnawing teeth and clawing grips tearing at your skin and clothes.
A crushing weight filled your lungs, and a dizzying blackness encroached on your vision until consciousness slipped away. When you finally forced your eyes open...
You were clinging to a piece of driftwood, alone in the vast, empty ocean.
Ow!
You take a single step up the stairs, and your face instantly contorts into a pained grimace.
You had woken to a searing ache in every muscle this morning.
The small cabin at the base of the lighthouse remains dim, the hearth fire that sheltered you through the night having burned out hours ago, not long after you fell asleep.
The thunderstorm has passed. No monsters scratch at the door; only the rhythmic crash of ocean waves remains. Through the small porthole, a faint light filters down from an overcast sky.
Leaning heavily on the wall, you limp around the cramped space. No medical supplies. No water. No food. Your only option is the staircase, leading to who knows where.
Judging by the design of the equipment here, this place must have once belonged to DisCity...
A sharp twist of pain in your stomach makes the stairs blur and double. Your hand braced against the wall trembles uncontrollably.
Heh. Looks like I barely have the strength left to talk to myself...
But talking to yourself is your last resort, the only way to keep your mind sober. With each whispered word, you force one leg forward, then the other, continuing the climb.
The age of this place and the lighthouse observatory... they both match Broken Blade's intel. That woman from last night... she has to know something.

Could the Rancors be here? But that woman never returned after storming out last night. Does she not need to eat or sleep? Unless she was just a figment of your imagination... unless you actually died in the Black Tide.
No... Get a grip. Don't go down that road.
A fresh wave of pain yanks you back to reality. You haul your other leg up onto the next step. Above you stretches a seemingly endless spiral of stairs.
There may be no survival supplies up there, but you know something far more important awaits—
The beacon. Its light, cutting through the sea fog, would be the clearest distress signal you could send. Your best chance to contact your team. Your only shot at extraction.
I need to rendezvous with the team first...
[White Flash] [Flying Knife]
Your words are cut short by the whistle of metal slicing the air. A knife flies past your ear, embedding itself in the wall ahead, stopping your path mere inches from your face.

speaker: Shin
content: Get out!
You know that commanding voice. You don't need to look to know who it belongs to.
You're still alive too. Lucky, aren't we?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Are you deaf? I said get out.
I didn't come up here for the view. I need water, food, antibiotics. Point me to them, and I'm gone. I won't touch a thing.
She acts as if you aren't even there. Gritting your teeth, you force patience into your voice and speak again.
Look, I apologize for the interruption... but I'm dying.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: My congratulations.
The control room's up there, right? This is a rescue facility, not your private property. If you won't help, I'll activate the beacon myself.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: A nameless bastard has no right to touch the lighthouse.
Isn't a lighthouse meant to guide the lost? Right now, that's me.
You refuse to yield, taking another deliberate step forward—
Shing! A blade blurs through the air, severing a few loose strands of your hair before whistling back to its master's hand.
[Big CG: First Encounter]

You finally see her clearly, for the first time. Her frame is pure muscle, sculpted by brutal training, and her skin is rough from sea winds, a canvas for scars of every depth. But it's the look on her face that strikes deepest: a weary, unbridled ferocity.
Why are you so desperate to keep me away? What are you hiding?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You. Have. No. Right. Is that simple enough for you?
Then give me food and water.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: There isn't any. Just die.
You're all talk. Go ahead, do it.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: I won't dirty my hands.
A disbelieving laugh escapes you. Her stubbornness would be admirable if it weren't so fatal.
Fine... We'll do this the hard way.
Teeth gritted, you pull from your last dregs of energy. A faint, shimmering barrier of shackles barely materializes, deflecting her sudden lunge.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: I saw that last night. What is it? Outland sorcery? Are you with Fraser? Eastia?
You call it Outland. So you really are from DisCity. That means we're not enemies.
Your barrier shatters upon her strike before you can finish speaking. The impact sends you staggering back, your spine cracking against the damp stone wall.
Cough... What's the matter? My DisCity accent not up to your standards?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Why are you here?
I told you. I was separated from my companions, swept here by the Black Tide.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: I mean now!
I came upstairs looking for help. I need to get back to DisCity. To my people.
You barely sidestep a lethal strike. Her attacks come faster now, a relentless flurry that tears open old wounds as the Black Ring's pressure turns your limbs to lead.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: They can't come here. No one can get close!
I made it here, didn't I? How do you know it's impossible if you don't try?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: That was just your damn bad luck!
She closes the distance, grabbing your shoulders and slamming you back against the cold railing. When the blade rises for a final thrust—
You rip away the blood-soaked bandage, shoving the raw wound toward her face. The metallic scent explodes between you; she reels back as if scalded.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...You... cheap shot!
But it worked.
The sound of her ragged, trembling breath is your cue. You shove her back, creating a precious few feet of space.
Why are you so sensitive to blood?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: None of your ******* business!
That line again. I knew you'd say that.

She reaches for your bleeding hand, but you erupt into a frenzy of wild flailing. The coppery scent of blood fills the confined space with each frantic movement—and, incredibly, the absurd display actually holds her at bay.
The smell of blood may spread quickly, but your strength is fading faster. Your lungs begin to burn, each breath a ragged gasp.
...No medicine, huh. How did you treat those wounds on your body, then?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Those worthless sea beasts? Couldn't kill me if they tried. It's barely an itch. Everything scabs over in a week.
You don't treat the scars on your face either? Not worried about infection?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Heh... You think you're still in the city, pretty boy? No one here cares what your face looks like.
female_content: Heh... You think you're still in the city, pretty girl? No one here cares what your face looks like.

content: She grits her teeth and lunges. Instinct takes over; you jerk your bleeding arm high like a shield.
Without food and water, how have you survived?

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...I wish I knew.
It's only now you see it: the sunken abdomen, the sharp ribs protruding with each breath—the unmistakable anatomy of prolonged starvation.
But there's food on this island.
My blood for fluids. Flesh for protein. Fresh, and warm. But you didn't take it.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You're ******* nuts... Is it the hunger talking?
Though her bloodlust seems to have waned, she advances again. This time, evasion is impossible. Your vision tunnels into darkness, and suddenly, your foot slips—
Half your body dangles over the staircase's precipice.
But the fall never comes; a firm grip on your collar hauls you back from the edge.
See? The thought never even occurred to you. Like I said, we're not enemies.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...We're not friends, either.
She shoves you against the wall.
Yet you remain unnervingly composed, steadying yourself as if nothing happened and calmly beginning to rebandage your wound.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You're crazy.
