I'll take "crazy" as a compliment. If this place is as bad as you say, a little madness might be the only thing that keeps you sane.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...And naive.

She seems thoroughly weary of your amateurish struggle as well, her fighting stance dissolving. Her lean frame slumps heavily against the rusty railing as she tilts her head back to stare at the endlessly coiling stairs above.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Fine. I'll play along with your little DisCity story. I don't care what you are really up to. But remember one thing—

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Only the keepers are allowed near the beacon room. Try to go up there, and I'll throw you back into the sea myself.
Before ascending, she casts a final, wary glance over you from head to toe. Then she turns her back and walks away, as if fleeing a plague.
Wait.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: Tsk...
My name is ${PlayerName}. What's yours?
Though visibly irritated, she still stops in her tracks.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: ...Ceto.
[Beach, Daytime]
Ceto forbade you from entering the lantern room at the top of the lighthouse, but she never said anything about exploring elsewhere. And you have—you've scoured nearly every inch of the island.

She wasn't lying. The only medkit you found holds nothing but old bandages, worn so thin they've turned translucent. For water, you've resorted to the most primitive method: manual distillation and condensation. But the Black Tide's complex composition makes purification difficult. Obtaining even a single cup of clear liquid each day feels nothing short of miraculous.
Ceto, who slept curled on the lighthouse windowsill, took a moment to offer what she called advice.

speaker: Ceto
content: There are "ingredients" on the north shore. They're all yours.
You never really believed she could be that generous. Now, standing before her so-called ingredients, you stare in disbelief at a mound of corpses—Tide Crawlers—piled high along the shore.
...I'll just stay hungry for now.
You pick up a slimy, limp limb, grimacing as you prepare to fling it back. Then, your motion freezes mid-air. Something about the remains has caught your attention.

More precisely, it's the cutting patterns. These aren't clean blade wounds. They look as though they were made by an irregular, flowing substance that penetrated the flesh, then tore it apart from within. The edges are chaotic, shredded, littered with secondary scratches from embedded debris.
And you're certain that you've seen marks like these before.
[Flashback]

speaker: Doctor
content: The Rancors aren't really weapons; they're more like shapeshifting metal, condensed from the spiritual residue of battlefields. To control one, you need either immense willpower or the external power of Hypercubes.
What happens if someone can't control them?

speaker: Doctor
content: An unstable Rancor will turn on its wielder. It will consume them.
Just like what happened to Jasmine.
[Staircase]
Leaden gray light filters through the dust-caked lattice, slicing Ceto's silhouette into jagged fragments of light and shadow. Sleep is impossible.
She tries to ignore the stranger's scent still clinging to the air, but her bloodshot eyes remain fixed on the knife in her hand—on the constant, faint tremor she cannot steady.

speaker: Voice in Mind
content: Blood... kill him.
female_content: Blood... kill her.

content: [Inside the Lighthouse]
The rain begins again, a downpour of contaminated water from the Black Tide. Lightning flashes, thunder booms; you hunker down alone in the lighthouse, conserving your strength.
It seems that every night, the tide rises, and the monsters beneath it awaken to crawl ashore. The sealed cabin at the base of the lighthouse is the only safe place on this lonely island after dark.
You light the candles you scavenged today. Their weak glow does little to dispel the room's profound neglect.
Your body has seemingly adapted to the extreme cold and hunger; the pangs are no longer so acute. You can't tell if this is a good sign, or if it means you're simply one step closer to the end.
Leaning against the wall in a posture that conserves energy, you patiently rehearse prepared greetings in your mind:

Are there really no other food options besides the monsters? "I know I shouldn't be picky, but how are these creatures even prepared properly?" Or perhaps... "Do you have any medicine for food poisoning? Just in case."
But despite running through these lines dozens of times, no one returns.
Could her job really be fighting the contamination? The Black Tide out there is too vast for anyone to eliminate single-handedly.

Last night was the same: she stayed outside until dawn. After exploring the island today, you're no closer to understanding what a <color=#fb9259>lighthouse keeper</color> is meant to guard on this barren wasteland.
A rhythmic flash of light penetrates the rain-streaked window. You recognize the pattern.
Long, short, long, short...
[Flashback: Opening Small CG]

options: Is the lighthouse transmitting a signal?

content: If this place really once belonged to DisCity, they might be using the same coding system.
You strain to recall the lights from last night. The flashing rhythm matches tonight's signal exactly.
[End of Flashback] [Inside the Lighthouse]
Lighthouse Seven...
surrounded by contamination...
Is this a distress signal to DisCity? But as the light continues to flash, it begins to contradict your assumption.
[Lightning] [Coastline] [Ceto Dark Silhouette]
Personnel required: 25. Personnel present: 1.
By the lighthouse keeper's decision—
[Portrait: Injured Ceto]

speaker: Ceto
content: <color=#dg1f1f>I'll abandon the lighthouse and die fighting the monsters.</color>
[Ceto's Flashback] [Coastal Storm]

speaker: Ceto
content: Lighthouse Seven to HQ! All units, respond! The Black Tide has breached the first line! Requesting immediate backup! I repeat, emergency backup required!

The dry, scorching sands were abruptly drowned under a tide of viscous black liquid. The black water surged across the borders of WhiteSands with monstrous speed. Miles away, the piercing signal beams of Lighthouse One and Three were snuffed out one by one, like fragile stars devoured by an advancing void.
Ceto's hands trembled as she frantically hammered the unresponsive transmitter.

speaker: Rode, Lighthouse Seven Keeper
content: It's... no use. The signal's gone. It can't get through...
A relentless tide of horrors crawled from the foul ooze, converging on Lighthouse Seven. The isolated lighthouse keepers prepared for their last stand.

Rode heaved his massive alloy shield into place, but the sturdy metal was no protection. Sinister black patterns crawled across its surface, a living corruption that immediately began seeping into his arms.

speaker: Ceto
content: Rode!!!

speaker: Rode
content: Ceto, stay back! Go... find the Captain. Now!
Young Ceto started for him, but a piercing shriek from Jay cut her off. His legs were enveloped by crawling things from the black water, flesh vanishing to reveal gleaming bone.
Lia lunged to pull him to safety, but the contamination moved faster than she could. Her hands, acting against her will, snatched the curved blade from her waist and stabbed it toward Jay's heart.

speaker: Lia
content: I can't... I don't know what to do! Ceto, help me, I don't want to—
Her ragged scream was severed as a monster surged from the tide and wrenched her head from her body.
Through a haze of tears, young Ceto swung her dagger, a helpless witness as the insidious black slime swallowed the last traces of her comrades.

...It's coming... the slaughter we crave. ...Kill them all... the gunpowder is whispering my name... Yes... this is who I am, who we are... Tear them open! Grind them to dust! Listen! The song of ruin is played in the slaughter. Hack. Stab. Crush. Savor the taste of blood!

speaker: Ceto
content: Shut up! Captain... I have to find the Captain. She'll know what to do...
[Flash to Lighthouse Top]

speaker: Ceto
content: C-Captain?

Weakly slumped against the beacon light, Fynn used her longsword to prop herself up, her trembling hands fumbling over the SOS controls. She turned at the sound of Ceto's approach. Young Ceto saw it then: a swirl of crimson corruption in her right pupil, a venomous bloom overtaking the iris.

speaker: Fynn
content: Why are you... up here...

speaker: Ceto
content: The other lighthouses have gone silent. DisCity isn't responding to our SOS. Lia and the others... they're...

speaker: Fynn
content: Come here. Give me a hand.
She guided Ceto's hands onto the cold metal of the control lever. Then, she stepped behind her, pressing down her blade with all her remaining strength to keep it from impaling the child before her.

speaker: Fynn
content: Tell me! Where does this lighthouse point?!

speaker: Ceto
content: Toward your homeland. DisCity.

speaker: Fynn
content: Recite the Lighthouse Keeper's Code!

speaker: Ceto
content: Rule Number One: Signal and Surveillance! Monitor the border without fail. Ensure signal transmission. Report all enemy movement. We are the frontline guardians. We fear nothing, and are ready to sacrifice all for the city-state!

speaker: Ceto
content: Rule Number Two: Beacon Maintenance! The light is our most reliable signal. Keeping the lighthouses operational is our primary duty!

Her young voice rang out, firm and clear, its resonance carried by the lighthouse beam across the dark sea. Fynn gazed at the small, straight-backed silhouette before her. A faint smile touched her lips as she stepped backward...

speaker: Fynn
content: Good... That's right. You must believe... you must believe there's still clean land out there. Stand facing it, fight for it, and never, ever let the lighthouse beacon go out. Until rescue comes... You must survive!
The sound came from behind Ceto—the sickening, unmistakable thrust of a longsword piercing flesh. Yet when Fynn spoke, her voice carried a final, undeniable trace of joy.

speaker: Fynn
content: Lead the others and keep them alive. You are our hope now...

speaker: Fynn
content: Now, this is an order... do not look back.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Yes, Captain!
A heavy impact sounded from the lighthouse top, followed by the distant, splash as something—or someone—plunged into the churning black sea below.
You failed. They died on your watch... Weak. Pathetic... You just stood there! Die, embrace your fate...
[End of Flashback] [Beach at Night, Crashing Waves]

speaker: Ceto
content: AAAAAAAAHHHHHHH—

The downpour hammers her face, streaming in icy rivulets into her collar. Her muscles have turned to steel cables, frozen stiff by the chill. Every time she raises her arm, her blade cuts through the air with a sluggish whoosh.
Unworthy... you lack the will... How lucky. You're alive because they died... Why are you still alive...

speaker: Ceto
content: Why am I still alive...
She swings without aim, listening to the wet tear of monster flesh. An unsettling smile spreads across her face as she deliberately wades deeper into the churning Black Tide.
...Blood... blood is the true medal of a soldier... Drain them dry, kill them all...

speaker: Ceto
content: Kill them all...

Monsters pounce like ravenous wolves, their fangs ripping her open. She offers no resistance, letting them maul her freely. The rain sluices over her wounds, diluting the blood into a thick, dark fluid that runs in rivers down her body and into the sea.

speaker: Voice in Mind
content: Blood... blood...

Staggering through the horde, her blade flashes erratically, severing claws and splitting spines by instinct alone. Her consciousness drifts further on the sounds of water and thunder, until the world begins to fade to a featureless white—and then—
Something yanks her back with tremendous force.

speaker: Ceto
content: Bastard, get out of my way!
She kicks the "monster" away, but it surges back, grabbing her from behind.

speaker: Ceto
content: You dogs... still not full? Lia... Fynn... you didn't even leave their bones!

speaker: Ceto
content: Fine! I'll cut your bellies open... dig out my comrades... give them back to me!
Ceto twists free, drawing her blade, but the "monster" tackles her to the ground, pins her limbs, and wrestles the knife from her grip.

speaker: Ceto
content: Hahaha... scared now? Scared to die? Scared I'll drag you into the muck and suck your filthy blood dry?!

speaker: Ceto
content: Ptui!

With a violent heave, she shoves her opponent away, then lunges forward, reversing their positions. Now she is on top, pinning the "monster" beneath her as the merciless rain stitches their flesh and blood together.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm not afraid of you... I've got nothing left! Come on!

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm a monster now anyway!

Though a ferocious grin is carved into her face, something hot and salty mixes with the rain, falling onto your skin. The pressure of her hands intensifies, the knife trembling above your head, ready to split you open.

options: Look at me! See who I am!

content: Ceto!
She doesn't listen, driving her full weight down to grind you into the sharp gravel.
Ceto... open your eyes...
The vise of her legs tightens around your ribs; the ache in your chest sharpens into a scream. Your grip on her wrist trembles violently as the blade descends, inching closer to your face.

speaker: Voice in Mind
content: It's here! Fresh... kill... flesh... that shouldn't be here...

speaker: Ceto
content: Blood... you want blood? Fine. I'll give you blood... kill them all... this should've ended long ago!
Wake up!

speaker: Ceto
content: I am awake! I watched them die... right in front of me. There's no one left... no lighthouse keepers... NO ONE!
The rain is a shroud of ice, but where your bodies meet, her skin is a furnace of sticky, inexhaustible rage. Staring into her lifeless eyes, a strange thought flashes through your mind...
She looks like a reflection of yourself, had you lost Hella.
Your strength is failing. As the dagger begins its final, fatal plunge, your weak shackles suddenly pierce her body. The blade jerks to a halt, hovering a mere centimeter from your pupil.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...It's you...
It's me. DisCity sent me. I'm here to take you all home.

speaker: Ceto
content: Liar... you're lying to me again...
We found you too late. But it's not over. You're still here. You're the one who continues the hope.
She shakes her head, trying to pull away, but the effort is too much. She collapses back into you, her body going limp with exhaustion...

speaker: Ceto
content: Heh... DisCity...

In her daze, a voice seems to slice through the storm's roar and the monsters' howls. It's calling her name. She lifts her heavy head, her eyes finding the chaotic night sky, a void choked with dark clouds.

speaker: Fynn
content: Look up. Look out at the horizon.

speaker: Fynn
content: Stand facing it, fight for it, and never, ever let the lighthouse beacon go out.

speaker: Fynn
content: You have to believe a better world is waiting out there.
[Inside the Lighthouse] [Dizzy Heartbeats]

speaker: Voice in Mind
content: ...You survived again. Burden... Luck... A coward's pulse... You're all alone now...

speaker: Voice in Mind
content: He stopped you... defiled a soldier's destiny, dragging you back into the mire... You belong to death, and so does he... kill him... kill him...
female_content: She stopped you... defiled a soldier's destiny, dragging you back into the mire... You belong to death, and so does she... kill her... kill her...

speaker: Ceto
content: ...

speaker: Ceto
content: Shut up, damn blade...

Her eyelids are leaden, her vision a dark, rising tide. Only blurry shapes of light remain, swaying in the gloom. The lighthouse air is humid and cold, the walls themselves sweating the salty scent of the Black Tide. Through the haze, a shadow moves with busy intent.
A confused thought surfaces: wasn't she alone? Wasn't she the last one left?
Stay with me. Don't pass out on me again. I need to stop the bleeding.

speaker: Ceto
content: You...
She attempts to rise, but her body is a weak, sore ache. The fragile figure before her wavers and splits, a maddening blur that grates on her frayed nerves.
Don't move. One of those things got you good. Black Tide got in the wound. The Mania contamination's spreading.

speaker: Ceto
content: Also, the Bureau will pay for the subsequent restoration costs and admission fees.
Maybe not, but it still hurts like hell. The wound's on your back. Turn around and take your jacket off. I've got a little clean water to rinse it...

speaker: Ceto
content: Stop nagging!
With a sudden surge of strength, she fists a hand in your collar and yanks you close. Your labored breath washes hot against each other, and finally, recognition crashes into her eyes.

speaker: Ceto
content: I know!
She cuts you off, her grip locking onto your wrist with brutal force. You gasp at the sudden, sharp pain.

speaker: Ceto
content: The bandages... take them off.
What?

speaker: Ceto
content: From last night. The wound...

speaker: Voice in Mind
content: Pathetic... pitiful... Look at yourself... A monster. This is what you've become...

speaker: Ceto
content: Hurry!
Her knife flashes, a sharp sting as she slices your palm open, tearing through the old wound. Fresh blood soaks the crude bandage in an instant.

There's no time to react. Her hot, frantic breath is already on your skin. You feel the pull as your blood is drawn out, a strange, tingling suction. The sound of swallowing is deafening this close to your ear; the sweet, metallic scent thickens the air... Your thoughts dissolve into static.
And with it, fragmented, burning memories rip into your mind—not like a gentle flow, but like a net being violently torn open.
[Flashback] [White Screen Consciousness World]

speaker: Lia
content: Heeeey, DisCity! Can you hear me? I'm going to save so many people! I'm going to be a real hero!

speaker: Rode
content: I get to come home this year! Just... just everyone stay safe! Let everything go smoothly!

speaker: Miles
content: You hear that, all you jerks who looked down on me? When I get back, you'll be bowing your heads!

speaker: Herbert
content: I... I want my little girl to be proud of me! She's going to have a father she can look up to!

speaker: Fynn
content: You hear that? We're all coming back in glory!

speaker: Fynn
content: Our rallying cry is...

speaker: Herbert
content: Since when did we get a rallying cry?

speaker: Fynn
content: Oh, come on! We'll make one up! Don't be so rigid. Hmm... got it! Repeat after me!

speaker: Fynn
content: For hope, for dawn, for every soul—

speaker: Lia
content: Aren't those just lyrics from a song?

speaker: Rode
content: Impressive, I can't believe you recognize such an old song.

speaker: Fynn
content: Hey! Who are you calling old? Watch it, or I'll make you run laps!

speaker: Herbert
content: Okay, okay, easy now. You always overreact. I've heard the song too... Why don't we just sing it together?

speaker: Fynn
content: Wait, we're missing someone. Ceto! Come over here! We'll teach you how to sing it—
There once were all the prayers For our loved ones, keeping the light Here comes every victory For hope, for dawn, for every soul

speaker: Rode
content: Ceto, stay back! Go... find the Captain. Now!

speaker: Lia
content: I can't... I don't know what to do! Ceto, help me, I don't want to—

speaker: Fynn
content: Lead the others and keep them alive. You are our hope now...
Ceto jerks upright, her gaze darting aimlessly around the room before snapping into focus the moment it meets yours.

speaker: Ceto
content: Why are you here?
Who did you think I was?

speaker: Ceto
content: Don't ask questions you shouldn't. And stop making assumptions.
A former lighthouse keeper?

Her eyes fall on the wound in your palm, as she feels the strange warmth still tingling on her own lips. She offers no retort to your question, an unusual silence broken only by her awkward glance toward the table.
There, resting between you, is the dagger she always carries.

Relax, I didn't lay a hand on you. You made it clear you didn't want your wound treated, so I backed off. Didn't touch your knife, either. The shackles... they just react on their own when you... tried to harm me.
You, a person from DisCity, take it all in stride. Nothing about what happened seems to shock you; in fact, your gaze upon the blade holds a trace of familiarity.
This might sound strange, but I have a special connection with the <color=#fb9259>Rancors</color>. Like your knife. Sometimes... I can see things. Fragments of their history.
Unfortunately, without any proper gear out here, it's just vague impressions.

speaker: Ceto
content: Cut the mystical crap. If you've got something to say, say it. I'm not in the mood for games.

options: I saw pieces of your past.
I can hear the Rancor's voice.

content: The keepers were part of DisCity's Rancor division. But according to what I knew before coming here, they were completely wiped out in N.F. 84.
But your knife tells a different story. That a few survived. Held the lighthouses, waiting for a rescue from DisCity that never came. Taking heavy losses all the while.
You weren't just stranded and starving. You were fighting the Rancors' influence itself. From the moment you pick those weapons up, they never stop whispering in your mind...
They want blood. Slaughter... They want to hollow you out, turn you into a bloodthirsty puppet—

speaker: Rancors
content: Give me blood! Kill him! All of this is meaningless!
female_content: Give me blood! Kill her! All of this is meaningless!

speaker: Ceto
content: Enough!
The screams that have haunted her for a decade echo in her mind. In a flash, Ceto snatches the knife back from you.

speaker: Ceto
content: I don't care what you think you know. This is none of your business.
She rises and strides toward the door. You stop her just as her hand reaches for the handle.
So you can go throw yourself at the monsters again? Like yesterday? Is this a new death wish, or... have you just been bad at succeeding all this time?

speaker: Ceto
content: I don't know what you're talking about. I'm going to guard the lighthouse. It's my duty.
You kept me out of the lantern room today. You set the beacon to signal abandonment, didn't you? I don't know why you're giving up, but stopping you from self-destructing is my duty.
Straightening your coat, you turn to face her, your expression solemn, and extend your hand.
I am the Chief of DisCity MBCC, an advisor to the Rancor squad, tasked with retrieving the remaining Rancors from the WhiteSands border.
I'm here to bring the Rancors home.
For the first time, you witness a complex flood of emotions cross Ceto's face. She struggles to steady her breathing, visibly fighting the urge to bombard you with questions.
You offer her a long silence, refusing to press her.
You understand their resentment. How long had the keepers stood their post—ten years? Twenty? However time was measured here, their story was one of abandonment by DisCity.

Outside, rain patters relentlessly against the windows. Monsters growl and prowl the shoreline, waiting for the tide to recede. Inside the lighthouse, an unnatural silence hangs thick in the air. Then, suddenly...
A deafening explosion erupts from above.
[Beach Lighthouse]
The lone Sun amid the Black Tide, your only hope for rescue, Ceto's last remaining anchor—

Lighthouse OT-N07, which had never faltered since the Black Tide outbreak, is extinguished. On the night of July 13, N.F. 115, it has suffered critical damage under the attack of the Tide Crawlers and gone dark.
The solitary island is plunged into absolute blackness.

September, N.F. 74. DisCity completed its satellite town expansion, eliminating all opposition forces in the surrounding territories. The popularity and influence of Dravyn, the democratically elected Speaker of the City Council, reached its zenith.

As the glory of DisCity's independence burns bright, Speaker Dravyn leads our city-state to unprecedented heights! Now, we call upon our young warriors to secure vital resources and ensure stability and prosperity for all! Each mission is a sacred duty, a chance to demonstrate our strength and cement our city-state's future. Youth of DisCity, answer Speaker Dravyn's call! Take up the Reaper weapons, defend our honor with your passion, and ensure DisCity stands forever unconquered!

February, N.F. 78. To guard against counterattacks from metropole powers, DisCorps established a network of observation towers along the WhiteSands border. Equipped with the Reapers, these towers—dubbed "lighthouses" by other units—formed the Ash defense line. Their dual purpose was to monitor both the Tide of Ashes and Outland movements, while also serving as waypoints and supply stations for field squads.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:29. The DisSea Explosion occurs, triggering global catastrophic anomalies. Border stations detect a "black tide" forming at the Operation Skyfall nuclear impact site, where contamination has merged with Mania mutations into a physical entity.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:37. The Black Tide spreads at an alarming rate. Lighthouse OT-N02 organizes defensive perimeters and transmits distress signals to DisCity, requesting immediate reinforcements.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:40. Communications are disrupted by BR-000 interference. OT-N02's distress signals receive no response.

June 15, N.F. 84, 14:42. The Black Tide's spread rate and intensity vastly exceed all known parameters of the normal Tide of Ashes. Mania contamination expands rapidly. Lighthouse OT-N05 is lost with all hands.

June 15, N.F. 84, 16:15. Surviving lighthouses, cut off from command, abandon their posts and begin independent evacuation procedures.

June 15, N.F. 84, 17:05. The evacuation failed. Lighthouse keepers are surrounded by the Black Tide. Only 50 survivors remain. With her final breath, OT-N07 Captain Fynn transmits a rallying signal, directing survivors to regroup at OT-N07 and continue sending SOS signals to DisCity.

December, N.F. 84. The lighthouse keeper unit is reduced to 23 survivors. All supplies are nearly exhausted.

March, N.F. 85. Only 12 people remain. Herbert assumes command after Captain Fynn's death and reorganizes the team. The unit has endured by discovering a pattern in the Black Tide: it recedes during daylight hours and becomes active at night, when Tide Crawlers emerge to raid the shore.

The stone slab at the base of the lighthouse is covered in tiny inscriptions. Weathered by wind, rain, and salt, the earliest markings have faded almost to nothing. As your gaze travels downward, the handwriting grows increasingly erratic, the style shifting so dramatically it suggests a different chronicler altogether.

December, N.F. 86. Herbert is gone. 11 lighthouse keepers remain. Scavenging for supplies grows more desperate. Mania contamination remains an inescapable threat.

April, N.F. 88. Miles discovered how to create edible food from the monsters.

February, N.F. 89. 8 lighthouse keepers remain.

May, N.F. 89. 3 remain.

November, N.F. 89. All are gone.

In this place, the high-concentration Mania had warped the fabric of space-time, rendering dates useless as anchors for record-keeping. After a long gap, the crude inscriptions resumed, now following a new format.

Suicide attempt #13. Lost consciousness, then woke up. Failed.
...
#506, or thereabouts. Lost count. Tried again. Left my Rancor behind and jumped into the Black Tide. Failed.
...
#2019. Survived again. Found someone from DisCity who crawled out of the Black Tide.

#2020. That DisCity person is still alive. The lighthouse went dark.
Not a flicker of emotion crosses her face as she carves what she knows will be the last inscription.

A lighthouse keeper must maintain the lighthouse. Must signal DisCity. Must always fight. The duties are etched into her memory. She knows she should climb to the lantern room and attempt a repair, but a strange inertia holds her fast. All she feels is a vague, gnawing irritation.
The tower clock ticks on, its chimes counting the hours for no one.
With sudden resolve, she spreads her arms and lies back in the sand. Squinting at the sky, she tries to quell the storm raging within her.
The sun has been a stranger here for years, its warmth a distant memory. The sea breeze is the only thing that touches her now, carrying the taste of salt across her cheeks.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Maybe ending like this isn't so bad after all.

speaker: Ceto
content: At least I can finally get some peace and quiet.
<size=45>...Clink! Clank!</size> The jarring report of metal on metal shatters the silence.

speaker: Ceto
content: Finally. Some. Peace. And. Quiet...
Ceto grits her teeth, forces a breath, and turns over. But then—CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG!—the hammering escalates into a brutal percussion, a relentless pounding against the inside of her skull.

speaker: Ceto
content: Tsk...
She clamps her hands over her ears, but the noise, sharpened by pure malice, drills straight into her mind.
<size=55>CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG!</size>

speaker: Ceto
content: Stop it already!
At the other end of the beach, the "trouble" she'd scavenged from the shore is crouched over a pile of scrap. Hearing her, you look up.
Sorry for the noise. Just trying to get the lighthouse functional again.

Ceto's gaze sweeps over the heap of junk beside you: a tangle of broken pipes, bent valves, half of a signal device ripped from some forgotten machine. It looks as if an entire scrapyard has vomited its contents onto the sand.
Don't feel like you have to help. I can manage on my own.
Unless you'd prefer to lend a hand? We'd get off this island a lot faster if we worked together.

speaker: Ceto
content: Who said I want to work with you...
She answers with a cold grunt, then turns away, lying back down to present you with her back.
Since last night, your invitation to leave together has been met with nothing but silence.
[Flashback] [Inside the Lighthouse]
I am the Chief of DisCity MBCC, an advisor to the Rancor squad, tasked with retrieving the remaining Rancors from the WhiteSands border.
Ceto froze for a moment, then slapped away your hand that was extended in an offer of alliance.

speaker: Ceto
content: Hah. Here we go again. And what's your proof this time? That crumpled piece of paper in your pocket?

speaker: Ceto
content: Last time, what was it? A merchant caravan? Looking for a friend? Well, congratulations on the new identity.
DisCity never abandoned you. The Rancor squad has been searching all this time. We risked approaching the Black Tide specifically to find border soldiers like you.
While you were stuck here, surrounded, something might be happening in the city, too. There had to be a reason they couldn't answer your calls.
And I'm sorry I lied about who I was. I didn't know if I could trust you. I had my reasons.
Causes, reasons, excuses... Ceto only responded with a cold, scornful laugh.

speaker: Ceto
content: You done?

speaker: Ceto
content: If you're done, then open your eyes and look around!
Ceto dragged you to the porthole and forcibly turned your chin toward the storm and monsters raging outside.

speaker: Ceto
content: I let you poke around this island all day. Find anything to eat? Cook up a brilliant escape plan? You think you can survive that storm?

speaker: Ceto
content: You can't even save yourself, Mr. "Advisor"!
female_content: You can't even save yourself, Ms. "Advisor"!

content: There's still a chance. If we can just get the beacon working, send a signal...

speaker: Ceto
content: A signal?!
She slams her fist into the wall.

speaker: Ceto
content: What do you think I've been doing for the last eight thousand days? Ringing a funeral bell for everyone under these waves? Is that it?
She leaned in, her breath a cold whisper against your ear, her face a mask of ice.

speaker: Ceto
content: Keep your delusions to yourself. Don't you ******* drag me into them.
Without another word, she turned and retreated to the cabin's darkest corner, lying down and closing her eyes as if shutting a door.

Her outburst—the most words you'd ever heard her speak at once—left you speechless. You opened your mouth, but no sound came out. You had already seen the logs carved into the lighthouse wall, but at that time, the history of the old Rancors felt more impenetrable than ever.
I can't stand here and judge your past. What's done is done. But I can prove myself to you. No matter what it takes, I am getting off this rock and finishing what I need to do.

speaker: Ceto
content: It was a sacrifice. It was abandonment. A betrayal. The one thing it is not is the <color=#fb9259>past</color>.
...Help will come for us. I know it.
Your words hang in the air. A dead silence swallows the room, broken only by the eternal, hopeless sigh of the tide beyond the window.
If a miracle does happen... I'll ask you this question again: Will you leave this place with me?
[End of Flashback] [Beach, Daytime]
Irritating! That stupid question is as annoying as he is!
female_content: Irritating! That stupid question is as annoying as she is!

content: How can anyone be so naively certain of rescue? How can someone firmly believe they will reunite with their companions and work tirelessly toward that goal? Ceto cannot comprehend it. The very thought makes her feel as if sea urchins are crawling over her, their spines needling her skin. She shifts, but sleep remains impossible.
Even more grating is that persistent mumbling, buzzing like a mosquito that refuses to leave—
Checked the damage from last night after getting up. The monsters got the electrical circuits and the beacon housing, but the core light source is still intact. So we need power, and a new lens.
The radio's battery won't cut it for a bulb that big... Hydroelectric power? That's a massive project. We don't exactly have a hardware store lying around.
There must be some tools here for maintenance...

You deliberately draw out your words, testing for a reaction. As expected, Ceto isn't asleep. At the sound of your voice, she shifts slightly further away. Last night's tension clearly isn't dissipating.
No toolbox? Fine. I can make do with these cans. Where there's a will, right?
A wrench or a screwdriver... which first?
Ceto still shows no reaction, so you pick up an empty can with exaggerated deliberation.
Well, it's not like I have a choice. Unlike someone, I don't plan on turning into a salted fish on this island. So... time to start hammering!

options: I'm really going to start hammering now!

content: [White Flash] [Hammering Sound]
Something flies through the air and knocks the can from your hand with a sharp clang.
It happened so fast that it takes you a moment to process what it is: a key.

speaker: Ceto
content: South shore. Cellar.
You find a dim emergency light and fasten it to your waist before setting out alone along the island's abandoned southern path.
The moss on either side has been eaten away by salt and decay, leaving the stone slick and treacherous. You advance with painstaking caution, each step measured.
A cellar key? I've been searching this island for two days. Never found a cellar.

speaker: Ceto
content: Because you're an idiot.
Was that really necessary? It's childish.
What was the cellar for originally?

speaker: Ceto
content: A well. Connected to channels for the nine lighthouses. This was WhiteSands; we needed water.
Water? Then we could—

speaker: Ceto
content: No. It's useless now.

You squeeze through the split structure of the chamber, ducking under a section of collapsed steel beams. Inside, the darkness is absolute, deep as the ocean abyss. The only remnants of light are shattered wires tangled in the iron frames overhead. The air is noticeably colder here, raising goosebumps on your skin.

speaker: Ceto
content: When the Black Tide hit, that was the first place to go.

speaker: Ceto
content: If it weren't for those channels, the filth might not have spread so damn fast.

speaker: Ceto
content: They sealed it after the contamination filled most of it in. No one's allowed back.

speaker: Ceto
content: I won't stop you from going in. But don't blame me if you wake up the things sleeping down there.
"The things"?

speaker: Ceto
content: Tide Crawlers. The beasts that crawl ashore at night. They're quiet on the seafloor during the day... but start clanging metal next to their ears, and see what happens.
I'm not that stupid.

speaker: Ceto
content: Really? Couldn't tell.
You're really... Never mind.

Heeding Ceto's warning, you pick your way forward, avoiding loose debris and the soft, rotting wooden planks that sag under their own damp weight. The stagnant water in the cellar isn't deep, but its cold bites to the bone. As you reach the mouth of the passage, you instinctively pull your collar tight and hold your breath.
You said it was sealed. Can those things still get up through the cellar?

speaker: Ceto
content: People weren't supposed to go down, but there were always exceptions. Herbert did.
Who's Herbert?

speaker: Ceto
content: He took over as captain after Fynn died. Another keeper... Why am I even telling you this?

speaker: Ceto
content: Anyway, that toolbox you're looking for... is down there.
What about Herbert... what happened to him?

Following Ceto's instructions, you fit the key into the iron door leading below. As you descend the stairs, the air grows thick and oppressive. The cellar walls weep with humidity, blanketed in a sickly moss, and the stench of sulfur and blood hangs heavy—a foul perfume of decay and corroding metal.

At the passage's end, a rear exit has been hastily barricaded. The heavy door is reinforced from the inside with crisscrossed steel beams, but a small rift has been forced open at the bottom. A dark, indistinct shape partially blocks the opening.
The putrid stench intensifies, emanating directly from this dark mass. You instinctively cover your mouth and nose, your breath catching in your throat.
The shadow begins to resolve into a vaguely recognizable form. A cold dread washes over you as a horrifying suspicion solidifies.

speaker: Ceto
content: What happened... You already know the answer. Why ask?
[Red Flash with Horror Sound Effect] [Portrait: Dead Herbert]
It is a human corpse. Or, more precisely, half of one.
The right half soaks in the Black Tide, his remaining skin a grotesque map of complete mutation.
The left half remains inside the cellar, the hand locked in a death grip around a hydraulic cutter, frozen in the desperate act of trying to sever his own body in two.
A rusted toolbox lies fallen at his feet.
[Flashback] [Inside the Lighthouse]

speaker: Ceto
content: Where's Herbert? It's his shift.

speaker: Sienna
content: Ceto! It's "Captain" now. Don't be so disrespectful to the new captain of the lighthouse keepers.

speaker: Ceto
content: You're loud.

speaker: Sienna
content: Miles, look at her! What happened to make her like this?

speaker: Miles
content: Heh, has our little Ceto ever been any other way? That's just her character.

speaker: Sienna
content: Ughhh, I give up! No one can handle her but Fynn, anyway!
The name hung in the air, a ghost of someone already gone. In the stiff silence that followed, Miles scratched his head.

speaker: Miles
content: Oh, right. Herbert said we're running low on Hypercubes. Soon we won't be able to suppress those weapons. He went to look for more.

speaker: Ceto
content: Where would he even find more... Wait. He didn't go to—

speaker: Miles
content: The southern cellar. Said he had it under control.
[Flashback] [Cellar]

speaker: Herbert
content: What are you doing here?! It's too dangerous!

speaker: Ceto
content: You said you had it under control!
Young Ceto stood bewildered before Herbert, who was trapped in the doorway. Her mind had gone completely blank.

speaker: Herbert
content: I did... I almost made it. I just pried open a small gap. Look, right behind that door. Those blue, shining cubes... the things that would stop your nightmares. I just needed a little more time. But the Tide Crawlers... they found me first.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm not a child anymore! I know what those cubes are!

speaker: Herbert
content: Yes... You're not a child anymore. You're stronger than any of us. You can do many things that we can't. Our impressive little Ceto... could you do one last thing for me?
Herbert looked at the bewildered child and, summoning all his strength, extended his one movable hand to point at the dagger at her waist—the one Fynn had given her.

speaker: Herbert
content: Help me... find peace.

speaker: Ceto
content: What are you talking about?! I'll get you out... I'm getting you out of here!

Forcing herself to look away from his body, ravaged and festering from the monsters' feeding, Ceto's eyes fell upon the hydraulic cutter still hanging from his shoulder, fused with his corruption-riddled flesh. But she could barely see anyway; her tears had already blurred her vision.

speaker: Herbert
content: Don't cry. You can't afford to. There won't be any more Hypercubes to help you. From now on, you'll have to suppress the weapon's power all by yourself. Your emotions... they'll become a weakness your blade will exploit.

speaker: Ceto
content: Stop lecturing me! Push! We'll weld the door shut, and you'll be fine!

speaker: Herbert
content: I know... you never really accepted me as your captain. I'm not like you and Fynn. I can't command great power. I'm just an old logistics officer... who couldn't even complete his final task...
[End of Flashback] [Seaside]

The little girl from the past has grown up. Now, Ceto lies alone beneath the lighthouse, staring at the overcast sky as these memories surface. Not a single tear falls, yet she still lacks the courage to return to that place with the person from DisCity.
So, did you finally "help" him?

speaker: Ceto
content: He was the one who helped me.

speaker: Ceto
content: His blood quieted my blade like nothing else ever had.

speaker: Ceto
content: He told me... if it hadn't been for Fynn, he never would have agreed to let me grow up with the lighthouse keepers. He said...

speaker: Ceto
content: He said if I could really lead everyone out alive, he'd get to see his daughter again.

speaker: Herbert
content: I'd give anything to go home one last time... My girl would be your age by now...

speaker: Ceto
content: After that, we sealed the contamination with rows of steel bolts. We left Herbert inside. He was the last captain of the lighthouse keepers.
[Cellar]

You carefully pick up the toolbox, and for a moment, everything seems to be going smoothly. Then you glance up and see it: the straps that once secured the lighthouse keeper's uniform to Herbert's remains now hang loose in an undignified slump.

After a moment's hesitation, you set the toolbox down and crouch to restore some final dignity to the man. But as your fingers near the fabric, the hydraulic cutter lodged in his body clatters suddenly to the floor, its jaw gaping ominously toward the sealed-off Black Tide.
You were the finest of lighthouse keepers. Your child would be proud of you.
You offer a silent prayer to the poor soul, but as you turn to go, the hydraulic cutter lodged in his body clatters suddenly to the floor, its jaw gaping ominously toward the sealed-off Black Tide.
[Sound Effect with White Flash]
Following the direction, your heart stops. Behind Herbert's remains, thousands of crimson eyes have slid open, fixed on you with chilling hunger.
Whether coincidence or final warning, the cutter's message is clear—
<color=#dg1f1f><size=50>RUN!</color></size>
[Beach, Daytime]
You finally stagger back, toolbox in a death grip and lungs burning. Ceto hasn't moved from her spot. One glance at your heaving, disheveled form is all she needs to understand.

speaker: Ceto
content: I told you those things would wake up. A mortal body could never truly seal a breach.
I... I got what we needed, didn't I? Couldn't you... just once... say something nice? Huff...
Besides...

After only a few words, your lungs begin to congest, a coppery tang flooding your throat. The recent encounter was minor, which means your condition is far more advanced than you feared. You suck in a few ragged breaths, fighting to steady the rising panic.
It's that mortal body that's the real miracle. You might not believe it, but Herbert... he protected me back there.

speaker: Ceto
content: I believe it. That's exactly the kind of fool he was. Always putting everyone else first.
If you're upset, just curse at the Black Tide. Or in DisCity's direction. You don't have to be... so salty about it.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm not upset. Stop making assumptions.
By now, her prickly demeanor is familiar. You set the toolbox down without a word.
Alright, fine. Then tell me. Where do I need to go next?

speaker: Ceto
content: ...? Why should I tell you?
So we can fix the navigation beacon.

speaker: Ceto
content: How many times? I don't want to work with you—
You misunderstood. I'm not talking about working with you.

options: I mean working with the former lighthouse keepers.

content: This lighthouse isn't just yours. If there's even a sliver of a chance for rescue, I think they'd all want to see it shine again.

speaker: Ceto
content: You... what is wrong with you? Are you addicted to spouting this motivational crap?
A look of pure disbelief crosses her face as she pushes herself up from the sand, her eyes scanning you with new intensity.
What? Why are you looking at me like that?

speaker: Ceto
content: Just checking if you've taken something when I wasn't looking. How are you this amped up?
That's right, I just had a feast. Spiritual nourishment from the soldiers of the past.
Now I have even more reason to survive. To get out of here and find my friends. That thought works better than any stimulant.

And there is no more time to waste. Your body is a frayed cord, moments from snapping. Hunger, blood loss, the shackles' backlash—this relentless triad is pushing you toward a final collapse. You can no longer be sure you'll wake up tomorrow.
This, of course, is a truth you will never share with Ceto.
If you won't tell me, I'll guess. I was a pretty renowned micro-expression interrogator back in DisCity, you know.
So... North? West? East... You blinked. East it is.

speaker: Ceto
content: Can't be bothered with you...
There's a wrecked ship on the eastern shore, right? Might be something useful there.

speaker: Ceto
content: That ship's fifty meters out, half-submerged in the Black Tide. The cabins are probably nesting grounds for Tide Crawlers. Are you trying to get yourself killed... Hey!
She's barely halfway through her warning when you produce a hemp rope from your gear and swiftly secure it around your waist.

speaker: Ceto
content: What are you doing?
The eastern shore isn't far, right? I'm going to check it out.

speaker: Ceto
content: The hand-cranked generator's been underwater for years. It's definitely rusted through.
So there is a generator? Now I absolutely have to go. It might still work. Otherwise... why would you even mention it?

speaker: Ceto
content: ...What?
A perverse thrill shoots through you at leaving her speechless. She'd given you nothing but grief when you first arrived, but you've since decoded her "user manual"—and now you're testing its limits.
I'm going down to look. Don't worry.
Besides... what if I actually succeed?
Turning your face toward the endless Black Tide, you hide your unfocused, failing vision and call back to Ceto with a cheerfulness you don't feel:
Creating miracles is what humans do best.
[Deep Sea]

Step by step, you wade into the Black Tide, the hemp rope around your waist your only tether to safety. The ice-cold water climbs relentlessly—past your ankles, swallowing your waist, rising over your chest—until you are no longer walking but floating, adrift in the Black Tide.
You swim with painstaking caution, skimming the surface, desperate not to disturb what slumbers in the depths.
Your mind fixates on a single number: fifty meters. A grueling distance for someone starved and hunted, but for a rescue boat, it will be a brief dash to shore.
At what you hope is the right point, you draw a sharp breath, grip the rope firmly, and plunge into the darkness below.

speaker: Ceto
content: When we were first trapped, the lighthouse keepers gathered every vessel to break through the Black Tide. But the Mania field scrambled our navigation... monsters swarmed every hull. Not a single ship made it out.

speaker: Ceto
content: This rescue boat is all we have left. It was the smallest one. We couldn't risk losing it, too. Miles named it the Crippled Dawg. We'd take it out sometimes to collect floating debris, scavenging for anything useful.

The moment you see it, you understand the grim irony of its name: the Crippled Dawg. The rescue boat lies on its side, surrounded by dormant monsters, its hull split open like a fresh wound. Only half an engine remains, a testament to its final collapse.

A deathly silence envelops you. Thin rays of daylight pierce the murky water, illuminating a graveyard of twisted metal seats, a dashboard veined with shattered glass, and thick cables that hang like the suspended tentacles of some long-dead beast.
You hold your breath, extending a thick-gloved hand toward a corner of the cabin. There, half-buried in silt and debris, lies a metal box, its sharp edges just visible above the muck.
Cautiously brushing aside floating debris, your focus narrows to the crank handle on the box's side. This is it: the prize you risked everything for.

On the handle's grip, a massive charred handprint is seared deep into the metal. The impression is so vivid you can trace the outlines of every knuckle and palm bone, a permanent scream frozen in steel.

speaker: Ceto
content: I saw something was wrong from the top of the lighthouse, even before the Crippled Dawg ran aground...
[Flashback] [Lighthouse Top]

speaker: Ceto
content: Miles—!! Speed up! The tide's coming in! Hurry!

speaker: Ceto
content: I kept signaling him with the beacon. But that orange glow on the water... it just didn't move.
[Boat Cabin]

speaker: Miles
content: Damn it... of all the lousy timing...

The engine gave a final, sputtering cough, its death rattle a spray of electrical sparks before it fell completely silent. Even the backup batteries were mute, their indicators dark—victims of the corrosive Black Tide.

speaker: Miles
content: The kids back home are probably starving. I'm not letting these supplies end up as monster chow.

speaker: Miles
content: You think a little trouble like this can stop this old salt? I've weathered the Black Tide before!
[Lighthouse Top]

speaker: Ceto
content: It's moving!

speaker: Ceto
content: I immediately ran to shore to meet him. At the time, I didn't even stop to think how he'd gotten the stranded boat moving again.
Didn't you say there was a hand-crank generator on the boat?

speaker: Ceto
content: It's just a rescue boat. A normal person could have cranked until they collapsed and gotten nowhere. But Miles was different. He was a soldier. He had the power the battlefield gave us.
The Rancor.

speaker: Ceto
content: Yes. He gave himself to the blade.
[Boat Cabin]

Wedged between the generator and the cabin wall like a human lever, Miles braced his feet and gripped the twisted crank. His hands, calloused from a lifetime of spatulas, now faced a different kind of heat.

As he turned the crank relentlessly, Mania took hold, integrating his body with the boat's systems. It was a parasitic connection; the blade indiscriminately devoured his life force, converting it into a surge of power.

The cost was immediate and horrific: his skin blistered, smoked, and blackened. Agony threatened to unmoor his mind, but willpower held it at bay. He watched, detached, as his own blood and scalding fat dripped onto the generator with a sickening hiss.

speaker: Miles
content: Hah! Now I'm smelling like roasted meat! That's it—now turn! FASTER!

speaker: Miles
content: ...POWER—!!! TURN, YOU HUNK OF JUNK! BURN MY BLOOD TO STEAM—I'M GETTING—BACK—!!!
[End of Flashback] [Deep Sea]
With your last breath burning in your lungs, you dive to the cabin floor and clutch the heavy metal box. There, you come face to face with the island's chef and captain of the Crippled Dawg—Miles.
[Silhouette of a Bloated Body]

speaker: Ceto
content: When the boat stopped moving out there, I had to swim to it.

speaker: Ceto
content: I found him in the cabin. His body was still making the cranking motion, hands fused to the handle. But he was already gone.

speaker: Ceto
content: Water and monsters were pouring in. I couldn't take him with me. All I could take was what he'd gathered: one can of luncheon meat, two bloated cans of expired fish, and some waterlogged hardtack. Must have been relief supplies, dropped by other outposts early in the war and carried here by the tide.

speaker: Ceto
content: That's what he died for... and we ate it all in one night.

Miles's body is grotesquely bloated, skin straining against the uniform, hands forever frozen in a desperate grasp. Though ravaged by years in the sea, a ghost of a smile remains on his corroded face.

Your oxygen is critically low. You kick off the bottom, struggling toward the surface with the heavy box. After two frantic kicks, a primal sense screams that something is approaching from the murk behind you.

speaker: Ceto
content: Do you know what happens to soldiers like Miles when they surrender completely to the Rancors?
You glance back, only to find nothing but swirling darkness. Then...
A pitch-black, bloated figure erupts from the gloom. Before you can process it, a putrid, blood-tinged slime floods your nostrils.

speaker: Ceto
content: They lose their minds. Their bodies are consumed by that evil power.
The next moment, two hollow eye sockets lock onto yours. It's Miles, his form now a rotting, contaminated horror, pressing against you.

speaker: Ceto
content: They become just like the Tide Crawlers... Mania monsters.
Though weak, the shackles' momentary restraint on "Miles" is all you need. You shove away, clutching the generator, and swim upward. But the iron box is an anchor, dragging you down.
Your muscles scream, your kicks growing weak and uncoordinated. A pressure builds in your ears—the warning of oxygen depletion.
Light above! Almost there!
You tug the lifeline and surge upward, but after a few meters, your body betrays you, ceasing to move entirely...
A wave of blackness swallows your sight.
[Ringing Ears, Dizziness]
The warnings of prolonged hunger and blood loss—ignored for too long—choose this precise moment to crash over you.
Mmph!
Unable to call for help underwater, you pull the rope blindly, desperation overriding thought.
The sound of disturbed water closes in on you. Is it "Miles"? Other awakened monsters? You don't dare look. Any unnecessary movement now could cost you your life.
Your lungs are on fire. Consciousness flickers... Finally, the movement stops right beside you. Something coils around your waist.
You thrash to break free, but the grip only tightens, immobilizing you. It even starts wrestling for the iron box!
You drive an elbow back with your last strength, but it shows no sign of loosening its grip. As your fingers scramble to pry the thing off, they brush against the "monster"—and you freeze.

In that moment of shock, an air tube is thrust into your mouth. Air floods your lungs. The "thing" around your waist tightens, not as a restraint, but as a rescue, pulling you swiftly toward the surface.
The moment your head breaks through, you spit out the tube and gasp a question.
Ceto? Is that you?

speaker: Ceto
content: Who else would it be? A ghost?
I can't see a thing.

speaker: Ceto
content: It happens. We're still some distance from shore. Keep your voice down. Don't attract them.
The thing chasing me... I think it might be Miles.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...I know.

Silence falls between you as Ceto swims for shore at full speed, clutching you with one arm and the metal box with the other. But the Tide Crawlers are faster. You feel the water churn violently beneath you.
After a desperate distance, Ceto halts abruptly. Her hands work quickly, untying the lifeline from your waist and fastening it securely around her own.

speaker: Ceto
content: Listen. You're just oxygen-starved, and weak. Your sight will come back. When it does, pull me up. I need to keep these things contained in the water. Can't let them reach the shore.
What are you going to do?

speaker: Ceto
content: Enough questions. Take that damn box and get to shore. Now!

Before you can protest, she hurls you toward the shore like a sack of stones. You land hard on solid ground. Instantly, your blindness amplifies the chaos: a chorus of monstrous hisses, the sharp shing of a dagger being drawn.

The world narrows to sound and smell. The wet thwack of steel meeting rotten flesh. The rip of fabric. The overwhelming putrid stench of the creatures. And the low, resonant hum of Mania echoing through the shackles' connection.

speaker: Rancors
content: Are you cutting him open? Go on, look at it. Look at what spills out. ...Miles is long gone. He's mine now. Let him go. Let yourself go... Turning your blade on your own comrade? Is this how you protect everyone... you, the last hope of the lighthouse keepers? Trash, worthless... why are you the only one still alive... living like a pathetic coward...
[White Flash] [Coast]

speaker: Ceto
content: Now!
You haul on the rope just as Ceto disengages. Her blade sweeps through the Black Tide with terrifying force—
[Battle CG]
And the horde recoils. The twisted shadows, cowed by the power radiating from her steel, fall back to circle at a wary distance. She is moments from breaking the surface...
When a slender tendril, blacker than the deepest shadow, lashes out from a blind spot.
Watch out!
Monstrous claws rake across her back, sending a spray of blood into the water. She doesn't even blink.
In one fluid motion, she pivots. A frigid arc of steel flashes in a devastating backhand strike, cleaving her ambusher cleanly in two.

speaker: Ceto
content: Pathetic lump of meat. You're not fit to be compared to Miles.

speaker: Ceto
content: Pull me up!
[Beach, Sunset]

speaker: Ceto
content: Huff... Huff...
You finally shake off the last of the underwater horrors and drag your soaked, exhausted bodies onto the shore, collapsing onto the coarse sand.
A crackling campfire slowly steams the water from your coats, its warmth a welcome anchor to reality.
The sun bleeds slowly toward the horizon, calming the sea. The air hangs heavy with the scent of salt, the silence broken only by the crackle of the fire and the ragged sound of your own breathing.

speaker: Ceto
content: Sun's actually out. Shame it's almost gone.

speaker: Ceto
content: See those clouds? Moving fast. Not a good sign. Tonight's storm will be worse.
You've faced every storm alone so far. This time there are two of us. We'll be fine. We worked like a good team just now.

speaker: Ceto
content: That look... it's really the same.
She lies on her side beside you, a low curse escaping under her breath, one she didn't intend for you to hear.

speaker: Ceto
content: Herbert, in the cellar... Miles, heading back from the sea... They had the same look you did just now.

speaker: Ceto
content: Reckless. But so damn bright.
She closes her eyes, her attention turning to the gentle rhythm of the waves and the soft crackle of the fire.
You turn your head to look at your hard-won prize. The generator rests beside you, its metal casing glinting in the sunset's afterglow.

speaker: Ceto
content: Tide comes in after sunset. Fix the lighthouse now, or don't bother.
I know. But there's something more urgent first.
Ceto didn't expect you to bring back a medkit.

speaker: Ceto
content: Don't bother. It's a scratch. I wouldn't have noticed if you hadn't— Mmph!
[CG: Wound Treatment Close-up]
The sharp sting of your fingers probing the wound cuts her sentence short.
You don't stop, continuing to gently clean the gashes on her back with a precious reserve of fresh water.
Looks like the wounds from last night reopened. Does it hurt?

speaker: Ceto
content: No. I'm used to it.

options: I don't believe you. Should I press a little harder?
That doesn't sound like a healthy thing to get used to.

speaker: Ceto
content: Hey!

A brief, weary smile passes between you. The sea breeze carries the humid, metallic scent of blood and sweat. You see her muscles tense, a visible battle against her instinctive reaction to the smell.
In response, your own movements slow, your touch gentling. At this proximity, the sound of your breathing intertwines. This time, she doesn't pull away.
As you tend to her wounds, you finally see the map of old injuries covering her body—some faded to scars, others freshly scabbed, and a few still openly weeping.
Has anyone ever told you you have no sense of humor?

speaker: Ceto
content: Has anyone ever told you you have a death wish?
Actually, yeah. Plenty. But from someone who was sending out signals, saying she was gonna die fighting monsters? You don't get to lecture me about having a death wish.
[CG: Ceto's Profile During Treatment]

speaker: Ceto
content: Quit nagging already.

You fall silent, your world narrowing to the task of stemming the bleeding and securing the bandages. The only sounds bridging the quiet between you are the crackle of the fire and the relentless crash of waves. It is a small surprise, then, when she is the one who finally speaks.

speaker: Ceto
content: Miles... he was always the social one. Always dragging everyone together to try his latest "masterpiece." He was probably just lonely down there. Saw you and thought, "Finally, some company."
I know. When I first saw him underwater... he was still smiling.

speaker: Ceto
content: Same as when I found him back then. His mind was gone, but he was still smiling, mumbling something. Guess what he said.

options: I'm the greatest lighthouse keeper alive!
This pathetic Black Tide can't take me down!

speaker: Ceto
content: Heh... close enough. He said:

speaker: Ceto
content: Blood outlasts electricity.
[CG: Chief's Profile During Treatment]

The sky bleeds into a deep orange-red as the sun sinks beneath the horizon. In the distance, waves crash against the reef in a rhythmic pulse, as if the Crippled Dawg itself is murmuring its assent to the prophecy: Blood outlasts electricity.
If I were Miles, I definitely didn't bring that ship back because I "had a death wish." And I don't think Herbert was trying to end his life when he went for the Hypercubes, either.
They wanted to live more than anyone. They wanted everyone to live.
Blood continues to seep out, and you cover it with layer after layer of cloth.

Maybe you're right. We are alike. Even when I was surrounded by those things under the sea, I never stopped wanting to see the sun the next morning. No rescue, no supplies... didn't matter. I was going to find a way.
Far away, someone is still waiting for me. Someone who needs me.
[CG: Duo Wound Treatment]

You tell her about your first, contentious encounter with Syndicate's "little rat" after taking office, and how you watched her grow from a girl without a sense of self into someone who learned to feel, to care.
You describe the DisCity you know—a place slowly stirring back to life, yet with undercurrents still swirling beneath its fragile peace.
Ceto is as silent as ever, but you sense a rare, focused attention. This world beyond the Black Tide is a foreign concept to her, a place that only existed in the campfire stories of fallen comrades.

speaker: Ceto
content: DisCity...
Pensively, she repeats the name she's heard countless times in those brief respites from battle. It still sounds foreign on her tongue.
It seems she has no stories of her own to offer in return. Her eyes follow your hands as you tie the bandage into an ugly, clumsy bow. Finally, she speaks:

speaker: Ceto
content: The meat's ready. Eat.
[Sunset Background]
Over the fire, the monster's leg sizzles and pops, releasing a surprisingly savory aroma, a far cry from the foul stench you anticipated. After two days without food, it smells almost appetizing.

The first bite reveals a firm texture, followed by an unexpected yet delicious flavor—a mild, innate spiciness and a savory saltiness. For a moment, the taste is so rich and unusual that it almost makes you forget the origin of the meat.

speaker: Ceto
content: Miles spent forever figuring this out. Used me and Sienna as his lab rats until he got the contamination low enough. It's not completely safe; eat too much, you'll get sick. But it'll keep you alive.
She simply watches you eat, making no move to take any for herself. Despite her obvious hunger, she is restraining her instincts, just as she earlier resisted having her wounds treated.
Why aren't you eating? Did you poison it?

speaker: Ceto
content: Don't flatter yourself. If this island had anything as useful as poison, I wouldn't waste it on you.
She turns her face away, the usual disdain in her tone. But before she turns back, a piece of steaming meat is already there, blocking her path. You have anticipated her movement perfectly.
Well, if it's a lighthouse keeper's specialty, we shouldn't let it go to waste.
Her hand rises to push it away, then freezes mid-motion.

The dog tags on your wrist have caught the dying light, polished by you to a brilliant shine, their engravings sharp and clear as if newly minted. She recognizes them instantly, exactly as you intended.

speaker: Ceto
content: When did you—
I found them in the toolbox. I thought Miles might have had one on him too, so I looked a little longer underwater. Sorry for making you come get me.
You place the tags in her hand. She stares at the copper plates in her palm, gleaming like new yet etched with names from a forgotten era.
Around her, the savory aroma of roasted meat hangs in the air. She has mastered the recipe perfectly; it's a scent more familiar to her than any other.
[Ceto's Flashback]

speaker: Herbert
content: Sienna! That can was for Ceto! She's a growing girl. Who said you could open it?

speaker: Sienna
content: Hehe, don't be so stingy. Mackerel is the best with a drink. Brings out the flavor. Ceto's too young to appreciate it anyway.

speaker: Herbert
content: You opened the booze, too? That was our emergency disinfectant! I swear...

speaker: Miles
content: Relax! Eat up! The days of pinching pennies are over. I've mastered cooking monster legs. It's a hundred times better than this canned stuff!

speaker: Sienna
content: Well... maybe our little Ceto should be the taste-tester...

speaker: Miles
content: You turning your nose up at my cooking? I'll have you know Captain Fynn herself appointed me chef of Lighthouse Seven! You know what, I'll go back out tomorrow and find you some canned beef and potatoes then.

speaker: Herbert
content: You know, you're right. <color=#fb9259>Tomorrow</color> could bring anything. How about pouring me a bit of that?

speaker: Sienna
content: Sure thing... Hey, wait. Where's my can? Ceto—?! You little sneak, when did you... Get back here! No fair hogging it all!
[End of Flashback]
I saw the inscriptions on the lighthouse's base. The past of the lighthouse keepers... A story DisCity doesn't even know anymore.
But you still know. You remember why they came, the duty they upheld. You're their living legacy.
Ceto takes the meat. At first, her bites are tentative, but restraint quickly shatters. She eats faster, more ravenously, devouring it with a primal urgency.

The smoked aroma floods her senses. Her teeth tear through tough muscle fibers, her throat working relentlessly to swallow the rich, warm protein. Heat courses down her esophagus, flooding into her limbs. This is the flesh of a monster, nurtured by the Black Tide—a creature that fed on the blood and bones of countless lighthouse keepers.

Bite after bite, sensation ignites along her nerves. Her heartbeat drums in her ears, her breathing grows sharp and clear. Beneath the bandages, she feels her flesh knitting itself back together in a frenzy of itching, burning regeneration. And finally, she reclaims a warmth lost to time—
This is what it means to be <color=#fb9259>alive</color>.
[Beach, Night]

From the shore, you watch Ceto. At the base of the lighthouse, she paces off steps with a strange, ritual precision, finally marking a spot on the ground. Then, the long, solitary work of digging begins.
Need a hand?

speaker: Ceto
content: Almost done. Here, help me with this. Don't drop it.
You step forward to help her lift a tightly wrapped bundle from the earth. It is heavy and cumbersome, standing nearly half a person's height.
What is it?

speaker: Ceto
content: The last piece you need to repair the lighthouse.
She opens the waterproof tarp, then carefully, almost reverently, peels back the inner layers.

speaker: Ceto
content: A spare lens for the beacon light.
[Ceto's Flashback]
Four Hours After the Black Tide Contamination Outbreak

speaker: Ceto
content: Have I told you about Sienna? Of all the survivors... she's the one I hated most.

speaker: Ceto
content: She served under Fynn. After the contamination wiped out her unit, she was the only one left. So she gathered up all their gear... and came to find Fynn.

speaker: Ceto
content: Someone's there?!

speaker: Herbert
content: It's the radio operator from Lighthouse Two. What's she doing out here alone?
Ceto quickly adjusted her telescope, bringing the figure in the boat into focus. It was a young woman in a lighthouse keeper's uniform, waving her arms in the precise gestures of semaphore.

speaker: Ceto
content: What is she saying?

speaker: Herbert
content: She says... Lighthouse Two is gone. Contamination wiped it out. She's bringing critical supplies to regroup with us.
The girl in the lifeboat pointed to a lens wrapped in bloodstained cloth beside her, using semaphore to signal the message:
<size=50><color=#fb9259>"The Last Light"</color></size>
[Lighthouse Top]
The beacon repair is progressing better than expected. The new lens is installed, the circuitry is fixed and dry, and it's all successfully connected to the hand-cranked generator.

The problem is power. You lack Miles's raw strength. Each turn of the crank is like pouring a cup of water into a bottomless pit. You could crank for a lifetime and still not generate enough power for even a faint glow.

Fortunately, the tower has a backup battery array. With the main power system destroyed, it's your only hope. Protocol demands a full circuitry check and a pre-charge test, but time has run out for protocol.
Outside, the humid air grows thick as the water level rises rapidly. After a cursory check for obvious shorts, you start cranking. The power gauge barely twitches from zero.

After nearly half an hour, exhaustion seeps into your muscles. You should have let Ceto handle this brute-force work. But you gave her the more critical job: keeping watch. Just as the thought crosses your mind, Ceto climbs through the window from the tower's top—

speaker: Ceto
content: Wait. I saw a surface disturbance. Bearing northeast, 27 degrees.

You squint in the direction she indicates. The waves all look the same to you, a monotonous swell with no distinguishing features. Yet you have no reason to doubt her; this sharpened perception is how she found you in the vast, dark sea.
What do you see?
Ceto frowns thoughtfully, seemingly uncertain herself.

speaker: Ceto
content: A fleet. Large. Wave patterns are wrong. Probably interference from multiple ship hulls.

speaker: Ceto
content: Your friends... this DisCity team coming to rescue you... how many ships do they have?
Command-class. Three capital ships, ten escorts.
Your eyes meet. The same conclusion hangs unspoken between you: this could be the rescue team from DisCity coming for you.
After a moment's pause, you tighten the tool belt and grip the generator handle once more.
Whatever the signal means, this lighthouse is this desolate island's only possible link to the outside world.
The strength from the monster meat fuels you now. You plant your feet and crank the handle with everything you have.

After relentless effort, the charge meter finally creeps from 0% to 1%. You throw open the controller panel and manually override the signal, switching it from Ceto's preset frequency—"Abandon Lighthouse"—to a desperate, repeating "SOS."

The storm redoubles its fury. Wind screams around the lighthouse, and rain lashes the platform, making the footing treacherous. On the distant shore, several monsters breach the boundary. Drawn by the mechanical noise, they begin converging on the lighthouse.

speaker: Ceto
content: Two disturbances in one day. The Black Tide's retaliation will be severe. That fleet can't approach in the storm that's coming, even if they see a signal.
We still need to let them know we're here. Waiting to die isn't my style. The worse it gets, the tighter we hold onto any chance we get. Like I said before—
Someone is waiting for me.
You bow your head and keep working. Ceto stares at your back, her pessimistic retort dying unspoken.
The remaining glass panes rattle violently in their frames, threatening to shatter. Wind and rain whip sideways into the lighthouse, slicking the crank handle and making it difficult to grip.
Ceto was right—tonight's storm is worse than anything that came before.

The platform shudders violently beneath your feet. You grit your teeth, driving the handle down again and again. Your muscles scream in protest, your joints going numb, but the meter's crawl upward is agonizingly slow.
Just as you're about to be thrown off balance, a solid weight braces against your back, steadying you against the gale.
It's Ceto.

speaker: Ceto
content: The light's too weak. They'll never see it. We need full power. No distractions.

speaker: Ceto
content: The storm and the contamination... leave those to me.
You glance back and see that Ceto has fastened the dog tags you recovered for her to her belt.
There once were all the prayers For our loved ones, keeping the light Here comes every victory
Ceto draws her Rancor and takes a defensive position at your back.

Fragments of the weapon slither up her sword arm, adhering to her skin like a living, parasitic entity. She doesn't resist, allowing the razor-sharp shards to burrow into her flesh until they solidify just below her elbow.
Her irises ignite with a crimson glow, pupils contracting to predatory pinpoints—the unmistakable sign she is trading her sanity to the Rancor for power.
For hope, for dawn, for every soul!
[Lighthouse Top]

speaker: Rancors
content: Blood... so much blood... Go on. Pounce! Tear them apart with your teeth! Become a monster just like them!
Darkness has fallen completely, the storm screaming around the lighthouse. More monsters scramble to the top, their shrieks merging with the thunderous waves.
They smash through windows, claw through ventilation ducts, and ooze through every crack, yet not a single one breaches the perimeter Ceto holds around you.

speaker: Ceto
content: How much longer?
Behind you, Ceto asks, her voice grating with an unstable edge.

You check the battery level—2%. Theoretically, it's enough for a full-power signal, but the ancient equipment is a liability. If the power surges and fails, every effort you and Ceto have made will be for nothing.
Just a bit longer... Watch out!

Mid-sentence, a slimy tentacle lashes toward her chest. She twists aside, but the violent motion causes the Rancor fragments to rupture, slicing deep into her own palm. Blood streams down the blade's hilt.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm fine... Keep going!

With one hand pressed against her fresh wound, she rams the other into a monster's torso, her fingers closing around its core and crushing it to pulp. Gore splatters across her face. She staggers back, blinking hard as if to physically shake her mind back into focus.

speaker: Ceto
content: Hey, you... talk to me...
About what?

speaker: Ceto
content: Anything! Just... keep me here. Don't let the blade... take over!
Okay... Remember when I first got here? Two days ago.
The thunder nearly drowns out your voice.
You must've hated me. A burden showing up right when you... when you were about to end it.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Don't you know it.
Her movements are still brutal, but exhaustion is clearly taking its toll. Each swing of her blade is heavier, more labored than the one before.
And when you stopped me from climbing the lighthouse... You were afraid I'd see you were going to abandon the lighthouse. That I'd ruin your plan.

speaker: Ceto
content: Yes... You were... more annoying than I thought.
You thought guarding this place was pointless. You didn't believe DisCity was coming. You didn't even want to leave... So why help me?
You raise your voice to be heard over the roar of the storm.
Why give me the clues to fix the light? What are you fighting for now?!

speaker: Ceto
content: Khff...
The bandages you wrapped so carefully on the shore are now completely saturated with blood. The coppery scent of it catches in her throat, making it tighten.
Yet she fights on, one hand clamped desperately over the bleeding wound while the other cleaves a lunging monster in half to protect you.

speaker: Ceto
content: I don't know...

As black blood spatters the ground, she gulps for air, forcing words through her clenched teeth. Her vision swims, but with a final surge of will, she lifts her head to stare out at the vast, dark sea.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...I don't know what DisCity is really like... but...

speaker: Ceto
content: I want to get them home.

You've lost all sense of time—an hour? Two? The wind screams around the lighthouse top. Your palms are raw, blisters torn and bleeding, sweat stinging in the open wounds. Finally, the battery gauge climbs to 5%.

It has to be enough. Your hand rests on the switch. Memories flash—the Bureau, Hecate, Hella—but you force them down, swallowing hard. Your focus narrows to Ceto, a lone figure holding back the Tide Crawlers.
We are getting out of here!

speaker: Ceto
content: Okay.

The battery gauge plummets before your eyes. Inside the beacon, the tungsten filament glows deep red, then surges into a blazing orange-yellow. The space around you grows brighter, hotter with every second. Around Ceto, the world seems to fade. She thinks she hears people calling from behind her.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Fynn always said you had a gift for wielding that blade, that you could lead us out of here...

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Keep fighting! I was right, wasn't I? Blood outlasts electricity!

speaker: Vague Voice
content: This is the last light!

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Ceto—
[White Screen, Silence, Ear-Ringing]
The beacon's steady light cuts across the horizon where sea meets sky.
It pierces the long night, penetrates the thick sea fog, and carves a burning path across the ink-black waters, pointing straight toward the distant horizon where a fleet may lie.
The lighthouse's summit is awash in warm, cascading light. It spills downward, illuminating Ceto inch by inch:
Her arms numb and battered, the dried blood caked on her combat suit, fresh wounds glistening, even the dulled edge of the blade in her hand—all laid bare under the unwavering glow.
The world falls into a hushed silence, broken only by the sound of your heartbeats—
Thump.
Thump.
Your pulses sync with the rhythmic flash of the distress signal.
Between light and shadow, the beacon breathes.
