content: I can't pinpoint exactly when he was infected. The effects on the mind are a lot more subtle and gradual than physical symptoms.
Hilda raises a hand to interrupt you.

speaker: Hilda
content: Let's leave Horne for now. I'd prefer to discuss... the nature of this "anomalous power" itself.

speaker: Hilda
content: Since the calamity, this "anomalous power" has appeared worldwide in rare, sporadic phenomena. But while other city-states are still treating them as a disease to be cured, DisCity has already weaponized it for military operations.

speaker: Hilda
content: Have you heard of Catherine Augustus Andohar? Despite her family name, she sided with DisCity. At Nirvana Port, she assembled a unit of soldiers mutated by this power. Their battlefield performance was... notably effective.

speaker: Hilda
content: So, the questions remain: What is this "anomalous power"? What is its upper limit? And how do we counter it?

speaker: Hilda
content: As the "anomalous power expert," I'm sure you can provide some insight.
She wants to know about Mania, and is using this to verify your identity.

speaker: Option
options: That's classified. Why do you want to know?
My own understanding of this anomalous power is not extensive either.

content: You feign caution, but inwardly, you recognize a golden opportunity. <color=#fb9259>This is your chance to get closer, to earn her trust.</color>
With a well-timed sigh, you let your expression sober.

speaker: Chief
content: I can tell you. But what I'm about to share is unpublished research. Even if you hear it, it must not leave this room.
You feed Hilda the basics of Mania, carefully weaving in half-truths and plausible falsehoods.
Yet, she absorbs every word with unwavering focus.

speaker: Chief
content: This "anomalous power" is essentially a mental aberration caused by the calamity. I prefer to call it "Mania infection." The infected become immersed in extreme emotions, leading to physical enhancement and morphological changes.

speaker: Chief
content: Their weaknesses are just as clear: they're prone to losing control, and after enduring the corruption, their bodies eventually collapse.

speaker: Hilda
content: And yet, DisCity still chose to weaponize it. Does that mean they have methods to alleviate the effects or control the power completely?

speaker: Chief
content: Not as far as I know.
The discovery of the shackles lies far in the future. Until then, the infected have only their own willpower to resist the corruption.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...I see.
A glint of sorrow, swiftly chased by anger, flashes in her eyes before she schools her features into neutrality.

Her questions then deepen, becoming meticulously detailed: the telltale signs of Mania, the hallmarks of an awakening, the subtle precursors to loss of control... With her intense, curious gaze, she sheds the aura of an Outland spy and transforms into a devoted student, hungry for new knowledge.

speaker: Hilda
content: Experts must frequently enter heavily infected areas and encounter numerous contaminants. How do you protect yourself?

speaker: Chief
content: I can't. As a result, I've just become more... sensitive to contaminated objects.
[CG Fades]

speaker: Hilda
content: Which means...
Hilda stands up and walks to your side.

speaker: Hilda
content: The item you secretly took from Horne's pocket... it must bear the residue of the "anomalous power," correct?
The topic veers without warning, draining all warmth from the room. You feel your own expression lock into place.
You school your features in an instant, but it's already too late. Her eyes have caught that fleeting lapse, and she doesn't miss a thing.

speaker: Hilda
content: Hmm... That's a telling reaction. It seems my deduction was correct.
She steps closer, carefully studying your face.

speaker: Hilda
content: Your expressions are rather... unguarded. You haven't had the training for this, have you? You're quite easy to read.

speaker: Hilda
content: So, please. Don't lie to me.

speaker: Option
options: Take out the item obtained from Horne's pocket

speaker: Chief
content: I just intended to conduct my own investigation. There's no issue with that, is there?

speaker: Hilda
content: Relax. I'm not accusing you. I actually admire your professional initiative.
Giving your shoulder a reassuring pat, she picks up the recording pen. After a brief, examining glance, she presses the switch.

...You can't tell a soul. This stays between us. You know the clock tower in the West District? The one that flashes at night... ...Yeah, that one... Anyway, it's not just a clock tower. It's a meeting place for farland spies... The news recently... with the way the war is going, they're desperate... They've started a secret project called "Monolith," right there... to end it all in one stroke... What's wrong? Scared? It's alright, I'll take you back... Alright, alright, enough of that for now. Come here... let me see your little secret...
The remainder of the recording devolves into obscene flirtation, prompting Hilda to switch it off.

speaker: Hilda
content: This recording was clearly brought in from the outside. Since you had no prior contact with Horne, I assume it isn't from you.
With a grave expression, she picks up a file from the table, speaking as she flips through it.

speaker: Hilda
content: After Horne was stationed in DisCity three months ago, he began repeatedly failing in his duties. This included leaking classified information to dancers while intoxicated, and transmitting intelligence without using the proper code phrases.

speaker: Hilda
content: Among the intelligence he compromised were development plans for the Monolith. Due to his powerful connections, every report and complaint against him was quietly buried. He was never even detained for questioning.

speaker: Hilda
content: And precisely because of this, he became riddled with vulnerabilities, making him an easy target for blackmail.

speaker: Chief
content: So, after we arrived at the manor, someone approached him and gave him this Mania-contaminated recording pen, triggering his violent episode.

speaker: Hilda
content: Precisely. Given that, let's take a look at this.
She neatly arranges a series of photos on the table. The images are grainy and blurred, the telltale haze of an outdated camera.

speaker: Hilda
content: These are the individuals who made contact with Horne since his arrival. I need you to examine these photographs and identify who gave him the recording pen.
You study the three blurry photographs. They show Huck, Marlo, and Nolaine, respectively.

speaker: Chief
content: ...You expect me to identify the culprit just from this?

speaker: Hilda
content: That's correct. I believe these photographs are revealing enough.

[Exploration Starts: use Information Flow, or 3 options to examine the 3 photos]
When players examine the photos, Hilda will introduce each person. She'll provide information about Huck, Marlo, and Nolaine respectively.
Players can repeatedly examine the photos, and after viewing all of them, they can exit observation mode to make their selection.
In this photo, Horne and Huck sit across a table. Horne holds a glass of freshly poured red wine as Huck slides a long, narrow object toward him.
In this photo, Horne's wine glass lies shattered. He dabs furiously at the stains on his clothes with a handkerchief while in a heated argument with Marlo.
In this photo, Horne has clearly interrupted a conversation, now boasting loudly about his own exploits.
You lay the three photos before Hilda, urging her to look closely.
The first captures the moment Horne is handed a glass of red wine by a server, just as Huck steps into the frame to confront him. An argument is already brewing.
In the second photo, Horne's wine glass lies shattered. He dabs furiously at the stains on his clothes with a handkerchief while in a heated argument with Marlo.

The third photo shows Horne brazenly interrupting a conversation between Nolaine and another guest. He seems to be boasting, forcing Nolaine's attention onto him, while the two interrupted parties look on with clear annoyance.

speaker: Chief
content: We all assumed these photos showed Horne with three different people. But we missed it: there's a fourth person in all of them.
The server in the first one, the one offering the handkerchief in the second, and the man talking to Nolaine before they were interrupted.

speaker: Chief
content: That's the fourth person we keep overlooking. Edward.
Hilda applauds, a look of genuine approval on her face.

speaker: Hilda
content: Precisely. Edward is a master of presence. Unless you're actively looking for him, your eye simply slides right past.

speaker: Hilda
content: What led you to him?

options: I have a keen eye for detail.

speaker: Hilda
content: Is that so? I wouldn't have imagined our "anomalous power expert" would have an intelligence contact. What a surprise.
Hilda's Trust +1
(Paths converge)

speaker: Hilda
content: Your conclusion matches my own. I'll have someone extend an invitation to Edward. We'll "inquire" about this matter. Thoroughly.
She draws herself upright, and when she speaks again, her tone is softer.

speaker: Hilda
content: I owe you an apology, ${PlayerName}. I doubted your identity... or perhaps, I still haven't entirely confirmed who you are.

speaker: Hilda
content: But your knowledge of the anomalous power is undeniably professional. And beyond that, you possess a sharp deductive sense. To pick Edward out from so little... I am impressed.
Though her words are praise, her demeanor rests in a space between suspicion and trust. The look in her eyes is one of open curiosity and confusion.
You remain unshaken, meeting her gaze directly and responding with calm assurance.

speaker: Chief
content: I was just doing my job. It's nothing like your plan—using yourself and the "Monolith" as bait, gathering every dangerous suspect in one place. I'd never have the nerve for something that bold.
At your words of praise, Hilda's gaze instinctively darts away.

speaker: Hilda
content: Bold? DisCity runs inhumane experiments just for an edge, creating undead soldiers controlled by dangerous weapons... The mole sells our secrets and betrays the city-state, heedless of the consequences.

speaker: Hilda
content: Compared to them, my methods are the picture of reason.

speaker: Hilda
content: This isn't for me. It's for the people we've lost... and for the city-state's future. That is why I'm willing to be a piece on the board, to draw out the mole and sever this threat.
Her voice is cold and resolute, the words meant as much for herself as for you.
Just then, a sudden, urgent pounding at the door shatters the moment.

speaker: Marlo
content: Hilda, we've got a problem. Edward's gone. Vanished. We've turned the whole damn manor upside down; he's not here.

speaker: Hilda
content: What?
[Scene Change: Main Hall]
You hurry after Marlo into the main hall, where the others have already reconvened. He retrieves several items from a table and presents them to Hilda.

speaker: Marlo
content: We found this stuff in an empty room. Looks like he ditched anything that would've slowed him down.
You see a miniature recording device, cleverly disguised as a cigarette box, its model nearly identical to the one Horne was given.

Beside it lies an open personnel file, its contents fanned out across the table. With a jolt, you recognize them. These are the dossiers on everyone present, the very files you had asked Edward to compile upon your arrival at the manor. He actually followed through.

speaker: Marlo
content: No one on the perimeter saw a thing. The place is surrounded by forest and cliffs, and with this rain causing flash floods... he couldn't possibly get out. He's still here, somewhere.

speaker: Marlo
content: Let's get more people and sweep the grounds. We'll find him.
The others all nod, their faces set in determined lines. They're now convinced Edward is the mole, and that flushing him out is the only way this nerve-wracking gathering ends.
With that, you also join the search party.
The manor looms around you. Where do you begin?

speaker: Option
options: The third-floor study where the files were found
The terrace garden with an open view

content: The room is as the previous search left it, a storm of scattered papers and overturned pens. Among the chaos, you spot a stack of blank paper, presumably left behind by Edward.
There are no more clues here. You should look elsewhere.
A cold rain sheets across the terrace. You sweep the area thoroughly, only to find nothing but the grim weather.

speaker: Chief
content: ...I should go back.
The place is a wreck. You step in and freeze. You're not alone. You can sense another person breathing.

speaker: Edward
content: Haha... Of course it's you, ${PlayerName}. I had a feeling you'd be the one to find me.

speaker: Edward
content: Sigh... You know, a few other groups already swept through here. None of them even glanced my way. I was starting to get bored.
Peering into the darkness, you make out a figure slouched against the wall, idly toying with a small object in hand.

speaker: Edward
content: Let's not move, alright? I've got a gun. Not really my weapon of choice, so it's a bit unpredictable. I just... want to talk before I go.

speaker: Edward
content: Tell me, did you find the documents I left for you?
You nod toward the direction of the voice.

speaker: Edward
content: Good. I made sure Hilda's was the most comprehensive. I left it all for you.

speaker: Edward
content: ${PlayerName}, I don't know who you really are... but I would genuinely enjoy working with you.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you talking about? I don't understand.

speaker: Edward
content: Heh, it's okay. I get it. Don't worry, your secret's safe with me. In fact, I want to help you.

speaker: Edward
content: You know, with my disposition, I'm only fit to be a spy... but I've always hated skulking in the shadows. Doing something for you, though... that was different. It felt good.

speaker: Edward
content: You're the only one who actually saw me. You paid attention, you cared. Having a superior like you... it would mean a lot to me.

speaker: Edward
content: I was just unlucky... DisCity caught me in a bad spot. To stay alive, I had to feed them intel from the metropoles, including some about Monolith... And, well, I guess Hilda finally figured it out.

speaker: Edward
content: Ever wonder why someone like me was even invited to a meeting like this? I'm a decent spy, but I know nothing about cipher machines. She just wanted to smoke me out.

speaker: Edward
content: I suppose in her mind, it doesn't matter who the mole is. If she eliminates everyone, she gets the mole too, right?

options: If you tell me who the mole is, I can put in a word for you.

speaker: Edward
content: That? Nothing personal. The mole just told me to pick the weakest-looking target and test the waters.

speaker: Edward
content: That man was full of holes. Getting leverage on him was almost too easy.

speaker: Edward
content: ${PlayerName}, I think you're the one who's not seeing things clearly. You don't understand her at all... Let me give you some advice: don't pin your hopes on her. That woman's heart belongs entirely to the city-state. There's no room for anything else.

speaker: Edward
content: As for the "mole," you should stop trying to catch them. You won't be able to.

speaker: Edward
content: Well, friend... this is the path I chose. I ran out of options a long time ago. At least I got to have this last chat with you... <color=#fb9259>I've left something for you. Whether it's useful or not... that'll be up to you.</color>
He raises the gun and points it at his own head.

speaker: Edward
content: Well, we've talked long enough... It's probably time to... say goodbye.
A gunshot rings out, and Edward collapses. On his lifeless face, there is no pain or fear, only an inexplicable, profound look of satisfaction.
For a spy who never chose his life, this final, defiant act may have been one of the few decisions that were truly his own.
Minutes later, Hilda bursts into the cellar. Her eyes instantly find Edward's body, then you, standing over him.
Her lips press into a thin, hard line. Without a word, she strides to your side and, with a leather-clad thumb, gently wipes the blood from your cheek.

speaker: Hilda
content: Tell me what happened.
After you recount his final moments, silence hangs heavy in the air.
Hilda turns and kneels beside Edward's body, systematically collecting his possessions:
A bullet-shattered eavesdropping pen. Blood-soaked sticky notes, rendered useless.

Then, among the few remaining items, she finds a document, stained deep crimson. She immerses it in a special solvent, watching the blood dissolve away. As the page clears, she leans in, her gaze intense.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}, do you know what this is?
You're standing too far away to make out what it is.

speaker: Chief
content: These are Edward's things. How would I know?

speaker: Hilda
content: Is that so? But this is an investigation report. About you. He analyzed your behavior and noted several interesting discrepancies.

speaker: Hilda
content: It states that after arriving, you showed a strong interest in everyone present and requested personnel files from Edward. He couldn't understand why an "anomalous power expert" would need such information.

speaker: Hilda
content: As it happens, I share his concern.
She tilts her head slightly, waiting for your answer.
...That damned Edward! So this is what he left behind for you??
Frustration threatens to choke you, but you have no choice. You force the explanation out.

speaker: Chief
content: You warned me yourself that there were dangerous elements here. Is it so strange I'd want information to protect myself?

speaker: Hilda
content: If that were the case... why was the majority of this investigation report focused on me?

speaker: Chief
content: That was likely Edward's own bias. He did mention his... personal interest in you.
Edward's dead anyway. He's the perfect scapegoat.
Hilda's expression hardens as she continues her questioning.

speaker: Hilda
content: While showing interest in the people, you were also intensely curious about the "Monolith." Why?

speaker: Chief
content: We're all here because of the Monolith. It's tied to the city-state's next strategic moves. What's wrong with taking an interest?

speaker: Hilda
content: Yet for an anomalous power expert, you show remarkably little interest in the actual concentrations or anomalies around the estate. You don't even carry basic tools or weapons. That seems... careless, doesn't it?
On this point, you have no way to refute her.
Seeing you fall silent, Hilda releases a soft, weary sigh.

speaker: Hilda
content: Since you refuse to clarify, I'm left with no choice but to try a different approach.
From the drawer, she produces a glass syringe. The transparent liquid inside catches the light, glinting with an ominous promise.

speaker: Hilda
content: This is a truth serum. It lasts for about thirty minutes and will facilitate a more honest conversation. Be advised, it does carry certain side effects. Permanent memory loss, for instance. Or mental instability.
Is this a genuine threat, or is she just testing you?

options: Then you'll be wasting a dose. My answer won't change.
I'm an investigator sent by the metropoles to assess you.
Refuse and make a run for it

content: Edward had already seen through your act. The role of "anomalous power expert" was never a true fit.

Your real expertise is in reading people. You are a consummate observer, analyzing every word and gesture, profiling those around you with a unique blend of sharp perception and deep empathy, all backed by a compelling charisma.
You must concede, Edward's observational skills were remarkable. These were your subconscious tells, impossible to mask completely.

He chose to simply document these traits as "discrepancies" without drawing conclusions. This was a calculated move; whatever identity you claimed could work, as long as it explained these noted inconsistencies.
And so, the path is clear. You can finally return to your "true" identity: an official from the metropoles, sent to conduct a routine interrogation of Hilda.
[Interrogation Room]
Facing Hilda's syringe once again, you decisively raise your hands in a calculated show of surrender.

speaker: Chief
content: Fine. I surrender. I admit it. My true identity is an interrogation officer. My mission is to investigate potential traitors and, simultaneously, to conduct a review of you.

speaker: Chief
content: Indeed, I'm not an anomalous power expert. I simply conducted in-depth interrogations of several anomalous power wielders in the special division, which is how I acquired the knowledge.

speaker: Chief
content: Years as an interrogator left me with habits that are hard to shake. I tried to hide them, but you still saw through it. That was my miscalculation.

speaker: Hilda
content: How can you prove it?
You relay the official information from Schorl's files with calm authority.

speaker: Chief
content: I know that since your parents defected to DisCity, your position has been extremely sensitive. Even assigned here, you still face periodic interrogations from the metropoles to confirm your loyalty.

speaker: Chief
content: This is your 51st interrogation since arriving. Your previous interrogator was Makenna Hansen. It took place at an underground facility in the West District, 142 Danning Street. Her evaluation of you was—

speaker: Hilda
content: Enough...!
Hilda's voice slices through yours, cold and final. In its wake, the air itself seems to change. The unspoken balance of power between you subtly tilts.
Your eyes catch a fleeting storm in her gaze—a flash of doubt, a jolt of surprise, and woven through it all, a thread of pure nervousness.
It's strange. She should be a veteran of these verbal duels. So what is it about this moment, in this place, that frays her edges?

speaker: Chief
content: You refuse to believe it? Or are you afraid to believe it?
You refuse to let the silence hang. Instead, you meet her eyes with a stern, unyielding gaze, reflecting the pressure right back at her.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you resisting? Or... what are you hiding?
Finally, she draws a slow, deep breath, and turns to place the syringe on the table.
Then, her hands go to her coat, unfastening it. She sheds the garment, then methodically removes her firearms and personal items, placing them aside.
Her back is to you now. She leans forward, planting her palms firmly on the table's surface, her body forming a straight, unyielding line.
[Body Search CG]

speaker: Hilda
content: Proceed with the interrogation, then. Our time is limited. We can't afford to waste any more of it on this cat-and-mouse game.

speaker: Hilda
content: Once this is done, I expect we can set aside our suspicions and focus on the actual crisis.
Her words are a cold challenge, dripping with frustration for the entire process.

You return to the main hall to find small dinner tables already arranged. The meal itself is a testament to the times—a simple, ration-conscious spread of cold cuts and humble homestyle dishes. The only luxury is the wine: several bottles of a fine vintage, which Manphist is pouring into each guest's glass.

speaker: Manphist
content: Ah, look who's back. Our brave ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Manphist
content: I am Manphis Gesso. Formerly of the cryptography department... now retired. Though most who know me usually call me "Manphist." Please, allow me to propose a toast!

You accept the wine glass from Manphist. As the others begin their introductions, their gazes linger on you. It's clear that the earlier incident has made you the center of their calculating attention.

speaker: Helene
content: Helene Meiser. I'm an operative in Intelligence, a "Hatter." As for my job, well, I conduct... "in-depth exchanges" with any DisCity official gracious enough to share their time.

speaker: Casey
content: Ahem... I'm Casey Abel. Head of the Tomorrow Post, as well as its chief editor and writer. My team and I are responsible for "crafting" various exclusive news stories. We ensure the public receives the narrative precisely as we intend.

speaker: Casey
content: This is Mr. Johnson Madison. He also happens to be the handler who brought me on board.

speaker: Johnson
content: A pleasure, Mr. ${PlayerName}. I typically operate in the metropoles, so I don't find myself in DisCity often. I serve as the Personnel Director at the Economic Intelligence Center.
female_content: A pleasure, Ms. ${PlayerName}. I typically operate in the metropoles, so I don't find myself in DisCity often. I serve as the Personnel Director at the Economic Intelligence Center.

speaker: Huck
content: Huck Burrows. Radio communications expert. Currently undercover as a technician at the West District power plant.

speaker: Nolaine
content: Nolaine. I attend night school at Syndicate. My actual identity is an operative in the Cryptography Department. I report directly to Hilda.
Finally, the only one left is Marlo, who previously confronted you. He gives a cold snort.

speaker: Marlo
content: Marlo Bannings. Killing's what I do.
His foul mood is a palpable force in the room, casting an immediate awkwardness over the group. It's Manphist who finally cuts the tension with a well-timed cough.

speaker: Manphist
content: Pay him no mind. Marlo is an agent in our Operations Department. He specializes in handling... delicate matters. The sort best kept from the public eye.

speaker: Manphist
content: Now then, since everyone is acquainted, let us take our seats and raise our glasses, to this rare gathering!
(Transition, still the same scene)
Amid the gentle clinking of glasses and the murmur of dinner conversation, you slip effortlessly into the spies' discussions.

speaker: Johnson
content: Dreadful weather. You can't get a letter through, let alone a clean radio signal. Hilda certainly picked a charming spot for us.

speaker: Johnson
content: I dread to think what state the markets will be in by the time I get back.

speaker: Manphist
content: If I recall, the private equity fund you manage is doing quite well. Several acquisition partnerships with local DisCity companies, is it not? I'm sure it will all be fine.

speaker: Johnson
content: It's the times we live in... Everyone just wants to park their wealth somewhere safe to ride out the war...

speaker: Johnson
content: We've already secured the daily supply lines. Now we're negotiating for energy and finance... Natives here are shrewd, but it doesn't matter. DisCity is desperate for capital; they won't refuse a good deal.

speaker: Johnson
content: Ms. Casey has been an immense help. Just a few of her news pieces kept the antitrust regulators tied up in knots. Absolutely brilliant work.
A smile touches his lips as he raises his glass in a tribute to Casey. She answers with a grin of self-satisfied triumph.

speaker: Casey
content: Just a few small favors. Mr. Johnson is the one with the sharp eye, always picking "quality companies" with such... manageable histories. They're easy to tidy up.

speaker: Johnson
content: Economic development is an invisible empire. When everything in this city-state, from dawn to dusk—the bread people eat, the fuel they burn, the news they watch, the pensions they save—is tied to us... That is true "market penetration."

speaker: Johnson
content: Trust me, that day is not far off.
The glasses meet with a crisp chime, a sound as fragile and transient as the beautiful dreams they now toast.
He, of course, is blissfully unaware that his own downfall is already circling. You alone know the history that is about to unfold, and you keep your face a perfect, neutral mask.

speaker: Helene
content: ${PlayerName}, you've barely touched your food. Is it not to your liking? I could have the chef prepare a stew for you instead.

speaker: Chief
content: It's nothing. I was just spacing out for a moment.

You spear a piece of cold meat with your fork just as the conversation deftly pivots. It's clear they're avoiding revealing too much about themselves, skillfully steering the topic back to the safer ground of Monolith and Hilda.

speaker: Huck
content: So... why did Edward have to die? Hilda just executed him like that... How is she going to explain it to the superiors?

speaker: Manphist
content: Well, strictly speaking, Edward was planning to commit suicide. Hilda only intended to question him, so the blame can't be laid at her feet. Horne's death, however, is more complicated...

speaker: Casey
content: Horne mentioned earlier that Hilda's parents defected to DisCity. Is that true?
Helene raises a finger to her lips, her smile a deliberate and mysterious curve.

speaker: Helene
content: Oh, you must be new. The Hartleins' defection was a major scandal in Sevael. One is a city-state councilor, the other a media tycoon. Plenty were sent to apprehend them, but they slipped through the net regardless.

speaker: Helene
content: Rumor has it they were highly valued after arriving in DisCity. Lavish banquets, luxurious estates... probably not unlike where we are now.

speaker: Helene
content: A pity for Hilda, though. She was implicated and placed on "the list," which made it impossible for her to remain in the metropoles. She fled to the DisCity front line and had to claw her way up from the bottom to reach her current position.

speaker: Helene
content: Monolith is her passion project, and her pledge of loyalty to the metropoles. If it succeeds, she can return to the city-state, and her ascent will be assured.

speaker: Casey
content: So that's why she hates the mole so much... She's using our lives as stepping stones for her own promotion!

speaker: Nolaine
content: Hmph. Sounds like someone's conscience is acting up?

speaker: Casey
content: No, no, no... I just think it's all too reckless... After all, we're all on the same side... we're colleagues, right?
As if she has told the most wonderful joke, the room erupts in laughter. The sound is almost too loud, too unified, weaving an atmosphere of eerily forced cheer.
After dinner, shifts are assigned by a draw of lots, and everyone takes turns returning to their quarters to rest.

Your room is a makeshift archive, crammed with towers of old books and files that reach from the floor to the ceiling. A quick inspection reveals they are not classified, but rather mundane academic texts.
A sparse military cot is wedged into the corner, your only concession to comfort for the night.
You recall that Hilda's room is right next door... Before even thinking of rest, you begin a systematic sweep for any surveillance devices.
You begin with a cautious survey of the study. At first glance, everything seems deceptively ordinary.
But to be safe, you resolve to scour every corner.
Even if you fail to find any traces of surveillance, you'll learn more about the secrets this estate holds.
Through a narrow crack in the wardrobe, you can just dimly make out the interior of Hilda's room.
[Scene Change: Hilda's Room]

speaker: Johnson
content: Hilda, let's not be hasty. This is a mutually beneficial arrangement.

speaker: Johnson
content: I'm aware material wealth holds little appeal for you. This gold isn't for you. It's for the families of the deceased operatives under your command, a guarantee that they'll be provided for.

speaker: Johnson
content: But this last thing... the "special pardon." That is for you. All your work on the Monolith, your relentless hunt for the mole... it's all to clear your family's name, isn't it? To reclaim your place in the city-state? I can make that happen for you. With a single, easy step.

Hilda's eyes drift over the briefcase on the table, her gaze devoid of any interest, before finally coming to rest on Johnson.
She shows no shock, no greed, not even a flicker of anger. Her expression holds only a profound, ice-cold exhaustion.

speaker: Hilda
content: Mr. Johnson, I believe you've misunderstood a few things.

speaker: Hilda
content: First, my work is, and has always been, for the city-state and its peace. Not for accolades, and certainly not for the redemption of a name.

speaker: Hilda
content: Second, the lives and the blood we spill are a pledge to the city-state and our ideals. They are not a commodity for you to trade in. Your offerings are an insult to this office and to me.

speaker: Hilda
content: Take your things and leave. Or, I would be happy to escort you to an interrogation room. We can discuss the provenance of your so-called "gifts" in thorough detail.
Johnson's smile freezes solid. A beat later, he forces out a nonchalant chuckle.

speaker: Johnson
content: As you wish, Hilda. But I'll leave these here for you to... reconsider. Investigate all you like. I can assure you, everything here, including my sincerity, is perfectly legitimate.
With a graceful bow, Johnson takes his leave. Hilda stands unmoving, like a lone peak that could crumble in the storm at any moment.
Then she takes a deep breath.

speaker: Hilda
content: Such dedication, Officer ${PlayerName}. The daytime wasn't enough? Now you're conducting overnight surveillance from someone else's wardrobe?
It's clear the game is up; she has already noticed your presence. With no other choice, you push open the heavy wardrobe door and step out.
[Transition: Still in Hilda's Room]
Wordlessly, Hilda passes you a damp cloth and gestures at the dust covering you. She pours two cups of tea and settles into her chair, her gaze steady, as if waiting for an explanation.
But you decide not to play her game.

options: Why was Johnson trying to bribe you?
Why didn't you join everyone downstairs for dinner?

speaker: Hilda
content: The usual. Money and promises. Nothing of substance.

speaker: Hilda
content: Though his haste to leave was... notable. Almost like a man with a guilty conscience.

speaker: Hilda
content: I have my own matters to attend to. Besides, didn't the conversation flow more freely in my absence?

speaker: Hilda
content: I presume you managed to gather some interesting intelligence.
(Paths converge)
You avoid explaining yourself. She barely seems to care, her eyes flicking idly toward the secret passage you emerged from.

speaker: Hilda
content: That passage was built by the manor's original owner. The entire estate is riddled with them. Chambers and routes designed for concealment and escape.

speaker: Hilda
content: Most have fallen into disrepair over the years. Collapsed. Become dead ends. If you were to get into trouble in there, it's unlikely anyone would hear you.

speaker: Hilda
content: I'd advise against using them.
When she mentions the "original owner," you notice her voice slightly tightens around the words.
Suddenly, the dinner table gossip and the evidence you saw earlier snap together in your mind, forming a damning picture.

speaker: Chief
content: If I'm not mistaken, this was your parents' former residence?

Her parents' betrayal had shattered her credibility in the eyes of the metropoles. Yet, she deliberately chose their former residence as the stage for this critical mission. Seeing this contradiction as the key to her most guarded secret, you decide to press on this very point, your expression carefully neutral.
Hilda's hand freezes mid-pour, then she calmly sets the teapot down, her expression unfazed.

speaker: Hilda
content: Should I commend your powers of observation, or simply laugh that even you would listen to such gossip?

speaker: Chief
content: What can I say? When you're at a dinner table, you hear things, whether you want to or not.

speaker: Chief
content: But I'd rather hear the truth from you than rely on biased rumors.

speaker: Hilda
content: Is this a new round of interrogation?

options: I just want to understand you better.

content: Hilda's Trust -3
Hilda's Trust +1
She stares at you for a moment before lowering her gaze.

speaker: Hilda
content: Your guess is correct. The Hartleins came to DisCity after betraying the city-state ten years ago and secluded themselves here. In this very estate, they made contact with DisCity intelligence, provided them with intercepted codebooks, and even designed a new encryption system.

speaker: Hilda
content: They taught me to decipher complex codes. Instilled in me a loyalty to the city-state, to fight for a common ideal for humanity, only to betray it all and defect the moment I looked away.

speaker: Chief
content: You didn't know why they defected either?
Hilda seems wounded by that word, keeping her eyes downcast, avoiding your gaze.

speaker: Hilda
content: I didn't know. I was in school when the interrogation officers came for me. They asked if I had spoken to my parents, if I knew where they were. It was during that interrogation that I first learned of their defection.

speaker: Hilda
content: The Officers were convinced I was involved... I was placed in solitary confinement, interrogated every other day. This continued for a year.

speaker: Hilda
content: After my release, I tried everything to prove they weren't traitors. I searched my father's office, went again and again to my mother's workplace. I hoped they had just disappeared, or even died... That would have been better.
But she had never found the answer she hoped for.
[Flashback Filter]

The next several years were a bleak cycle divided between school, home, and the stark interrogation rooms. Her old life was dismantled, and her passion for cryptography became a ghost, glimpsed only in the lessons Manphist provided.
Through it all, she maintained a perfect academic record. Her brilliance and unwavering compliance eventually earned Manphist's recommendation, paving her way into the Intelligence Security Agency.

It was within the Bureau's archives that her long search ended. She finally uncovered the cold, clinical report: the Hartlein couple had been apprehended and executed in the remote outskirts of DisCity.
[End Flashback Filter]

speaker: Hilda
content: When I needed a safe house, I formally requested this location from the agency... It was the only legitimate chance I had to stay here.

speaker: Hilda
content: I wanted to understand them. And... to create ciphers that surpass theirs, right here in the place where my parents died. That is also my way of revenge.

speaker: Hilda
content: Childish, isn't it? Feel free to laugh, Officer.

options: I would never laugh at that.
I'm not like those interrogation officers.

speaker: Chief
content: Thank you for telling me this. Not to an interrogation officer, but to someone who's here to listen.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm sorry for bringing up painful memories. Please believe me; causing you pain was never my intention.
(Paths converge)
You pick up the teapot and slowly refill her cup.

speaker: Chief
content: Some interrogators forget there are people behind the facts. They only care to seek truth, no matter the cost, and leave wounds on their subjects... and sometimes even on the innocent.
Through the rising steam, you notice her fingertips trembling slightly.

speaker: Hilda
content: And are you not seeking truth from me right now, Officer?

speaker: Chief
content: No. I'm listening to the story of a brilliant cryptographer, not interrogating a suspect.

speaker: Chief
content: You weren't satisfied with the story you were given. So you used every tool at your disposal to find a deeper truth. That's the conviction that defines you as a code-breaker. No one has the right to mock you for it, not even yourself.

speaker: Chief
content: If you're willing to be open with me, I can help you in return.
You indicate the cipher strip with a subtle gesture. Her cooperation could unravel everything, simplifying this entire tangled web.
She finally meets your gaze, and in her gray-red eyes, you see a flicker of conflict.
The silence stretches, thick and heavy. Her lips part as if to speak, not once but several times, each time quelled by her own will. In the end, she offers no answer.
Instead, she simply lifts her teacup. Her hand is now unnervingly calm, the previous tremor entirely gone.
Your eyes open. You're back in Hilda's room, moments before the poison takes effect. The ghost of tea still lingers in the air, but now it carries a sinister weight.
Hilda, do you notice a strange smell?

speaker: Hilda
content: A strange smell?
You don't actually smell anything new, but a little misdirection is a small price to pay. As Hilda watches in confusion, you rise and begin a frantic search of the room.

The rewind function of the LINK device has granted you this "space-time jump" within Hilda's consciousness. You have a second chance, but time is short. You must identify her true poisoner before it's too late.

speaker: Johnson
content: Hilda, this is a rather... unconventional meeting place. Does it mean you've finally come around to my proposal?

speaker: Johnson
content: Well, well. Our "anomalous power expert" decided to join us. Don't tell me you're also here to get a cut, sir.
female_content: Well, well. Our "anomalous power expert" decided to join us. Don't tell me you're also here to get a cut, ma'am.

speaker: Johnson
content: Look, my position hasn't changed. The price is negotiable, so long as I get out of this dump quickly. I'm losing money by the second just standing here.

While Johnson talks, his nervous gaze flits repeatedly toward the door, scanning the room for anything he could use as a weapon. He'd suspected Hilda's hostility, but your presence as her backup is an unwelcome surprise.
A silent look between you and Hilda confirms the plan. The "good cop, bad cop" routine is a go. Your role is the calm, reasonable interrogator; hers is the intimidating force.
[Hilda's Room]
With Johnson's interrogation complete, the poisoning incident has reached a temporary resolution.
Once the room is cleared of the toxic source, Hilda offers you another fresh cup of black tea.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}, do you also find my... interrogation methods unsettling?
She noticed how you'd unconsciously averted your gaze earlier, and it clearly troubled her. Now, she seizes the opportunity to ask.

speaker: Chief
content: I understand the necessity of forceful measures. Different subjects require different approaches. Since gentler methods were ineffective on Johnson, you simply escalated to what was "effective" on him.

speaker: Chief
content: I just wonder if there might have been another way... if it was truly necessary to go that far.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...I see. I was indeed too aggressive. I will exercise more restraint next time.
Her blunt confession throws you completely off balance. Flustered, you grab your teacup and take a hasty, unthinking gulp, only to be jolted by a scalding mouthful of tea.

speaker: Chief
content: Hot, hot, hot...!

speaker: Hilda
content: Take your time. Freshly brewed tea needs a moment to cool.
A hand appears, dabbing a handkerchief at the spilled tea before you.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...I should thank you. If not for your sharp eye catching the poison in that briefcase, the consequences would have been unthinkable.

speaker: Chief
content: No need for formalities. We all serve the same city-state. We all want to see the Monolith completed, to help us win this war.
You continue playing the role of the loyal metropole interrogator, following her conversational lead.

speaker: Chief
content: It's a shame that after all the commotion today, not a single one of them turned out to be the mole we're after.

speaker: Hilda
content: An experienced mole naturally prefers to hide behind its pawns, letting them take the risks. That's what makes it so difficult to catch.

speaker: Hilda
content: But... there's no need to rush. The Monolith's development is progressing smoothly. We still have time to catch that mole by the tail.
Setting her teacup down with a soft clink, she produces the secret letter found in Johnson's room. She then unfolds it and holds it over the veil of steam rising from the tea.
Before your eyes, the heat coaxes a secret from the paper: lines of invisible ink resolve into rows upon rows of densely packed numbers.

speaker: Hilda
content: As expected, the one pulling his strings was the mole. It knew exactly how to manipulate Johnson, offering him precisely what he desired most...

speaker: Hilda
content: From Edward to Johnson, it's clear the "mole" isn't working alone. It was already recruiting allies from the moment it entered the manor.
She puts away the documents and looks at you with grave seriousness.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}... if the mole ever attempts to compromise you, let me know immediately.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe by then, I'll have already captured it myself and delivered it to you, all tied up.
Your remark earns a laugh from her, and it seems genuinely heartfelt.

speaker: Hilda
content: Then, let's wish ourselves success in all our endeavors.

She tucks a stray strand of silver hair behind her ear, the usual tension in her expression melting away. It's a rare and unguarded softness. Seeing an opening in her good mood, you venture a subtle question.

speaker: Chief
content: By the way, how did you crack that encrypted letter? Wasn't it just a bunch of numbers?

speaker: Hilda
content: This type of cipher typically uses a specific book as its key. I simply happened to have memorized the correct one.
Without a flicker of emotion, she rises and pulls a small green booklet from the shelf, passing it to you. The utter lack of hesitation makes it clear: this is not the key used on the strip.

speaker: Hilda
content: The Wilderness. Each number corresponds to a page and a word's sequence on that page.

speaker: Hilda
content: The first word is in the "Readers' Letters" section.
After several fruitless passes through the pages, you can't locate the section she described. Instead, your search only yields "Midnight Tales" and "Musings and Reflections."

Puzzled, you turn to the front of the book, your finger gliding down the table of contents. It finally stops on a single, inconspicuous entry. As you start to turn to the corresponding page, a finger presses down on the book, stopping you cold.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You've never read it before?
Her tone remains casual, but her gaze locks onto yours with the same unblinking intensity as the interrogation lamp that blazed down on Johnson.

speaker: Hilda
content: When it was popular in the metropoles, nearly every student had a copy.
It's a tactical error. Your instinctive flick through the pages the moment it touched your hands betrays you; the chance you'd be familiar with this decades-old popular poetry is zero.
Now, your mind scrambles, desperately reviewing the fragmented text you just glimpsed. Suddenly, one critical detail emerges from the chaos.

speaker: Chief
content: You're testing me?

speaker: Chief
content: I haven't read this particular edition. After so many years and reprints, the version I remember didn't have such a flashy binding.
With a calculated ease, Hilda releases her hold and withdraws her hand.

speaker: Hilda
content: If your memory is unclear, why not take this copy? Flip through it and give those verses a revisit. It may prove useful in the future.

With a nod of understanding, you carefully slide the book into your pocket. The shift in weight draws Hilda's attention; her eyes flicker over your attire, a calculated search for the cipher strip you took.
Too bad for her. You separated them the moment you had the chance. The strip is now safely hidden elsewhere; it will never find its way back into her possession.
Her expression betrays nothing. She simply looks away, rises, and crosses to the desk for paper and pen.

speaker: Hilda
content: Officer ${PlayerName}, I'm grateful for everything you've done. However, your credentials remain unverified through official channels. This necessitates a degree of caution, despite my personal desire for a closer collaboration.

speaker: Hilda
content: Therefore, I will be dispatching a formal inquiry to the city-state to confirm your identity. Should the verification be positive, you will receive a formal apology from me.

You nearly forgot—this estate is no sealed bubble, at least not for Hilda. She, as the owner, must have a line to the outside world. Your fabricated identity hangs by a thread, ready to snap at any moment.
After all, "you" are a ghost in the official records. The metropoles' officials could never have credentialed someone who doesn't exist.

The only saving grace is the Mania-charged air that clings to the estate, stifling electronic signals and slowing communication. To send a clear message, a guard would have to physically run it to a point beyond the grounds. It's a fragile delay, but it buys you precious time.
Your teacup is nearly empty. You drain the last bitter sip, the dregs catching in your throat like an omen.

speaker: Chief
content: I understand completely. If this resolves your concerns, it's for the best.

speaker: Hilda
content: Very well.
Hilda returns to the desk, draws a fresh sheet of letter paper, and begins to write, without even consulting her cipher book.
A gust of wind sweeps the corridor, causing the lamp flame to shudder. The only sound is the faint scratching of her pen, a rhythm that pulses in time with your own uneasy heartbeat.
Outside, the night deepens. The day's gentle drizzle swells into a torrent, lashing against the windows as if to wash the world clean.
[Main Hall]
In the main hall, Marlo fidgets with his lighter, the flame illuminating his gloomy face. He smokes restlessly, one after another, the glowing embers tracing his descent into deeper agitation.
[Room 2]
Filled with a quiet contentment after writing to her lover, Helene turns in for an early night.
[Underground Tunnel]
Under the cover of dim light, Manphist feels his way through the wine cellar. After carefully choosing two vintage bottles, he stealthily retreats to the sanctuary of his room.
[Corridor]
In the hallway, he runs into Huck. The man's face is clouded with a deep gloom. They acknowledge each other with only the barest of nods before continuing on their separate ways without a word.
[Room]
Nolaine spreads the day's gathered intelligence across the table, her eyes scanning the scattered pieces as she searches for a hidden thread connecting them.
[Corridor]
Johnson was summoned away abruptly and has never returned... leaving Casey to pace the corridor, each step wearing the floorboards thinner with her anxiety.
And so, the first night finally comes to an end.
[Day One Summary - Black Screen Text]

■ Eliminated Outland spies: Horne Heiko, Edward Simmons, Johnson Madison

■ Completed identity reconstruction; secured Hilda's initial trust<color=#7683a2> (questionable)</color>

■ Acquired dossiers on all remaining personnel

Keys Obtained: <color=#fb9259><size=52><u>1</color></size></u>


Consciousness Restoration: <color=#fb9259><size=52><u>20%</color></size></u>

Unresolved Matters:
□ The location of the Monolith blueprint remains unknown

□ The identity of the mole remains unconfirmed

□ Hilda's identity verification telegram remains unintercepted

□ Hilda's personal cipher strip remains undeciphered
Heavy clouds still hang oppressively low, forcing the manor's lights to burn despite the early hour.

You've spent a sleepless night hunched over Hilda's cipher strip, the cryptic symbols swimming before your tired eyes. All you have to show for it is the elimination of a few common encryption methods.

Yet it's a drop in an ocean of possibilities. A trial-and-error approach could take a year and yield nothing. You wonder how professional cryptographers ever crack these things. The task feels hopeless.
With the arrival of daylight, you reluctantly freshen up and step out into the corridor.
[Corridor]

As you walk through the corridor, you notice a guard in a blue raincoat at the manor's entrance. He appears to be a messenger, exchanging something with the guard outside the gates through the curtain of rain.
No one but Hilda could send or receive mail from this sealed manor. This must be the identity verification letter she mentioned yesterday, the one destined for her superiors.
You need to find a way to intercept it.

options: Go to the gate to intercept the letter from the guard

content: For now, you have no justification to intercept the letter. Your only option is to wait and watch.
[Main Hall]
A group has already gathered in the hall. Helene is quietly arranging breakfast on the large table. Your eyes are drawn to Hilda, seated alone and sipping a cup of pitch-black coffee.
Three empty chairs punctuate the table. The other guests shift uneasily, and you catch them stealing furtive glances at you and Hilda.
The silence is suffocating. In this tense stillness, you find yourself, quite unexpectedly, missing Edward's presence.

speaker: Hilda
content: The book... have you finished it?
Hilda's voice cuts through the silence as she gestures toward the copy of The Wilderness you'd brought with you.

options: I find your notes more interesting than the original text.

content: Hilda's Trust +1

speaker: Hilda
content: Just the scribblings of a younger me. If you found them worthwhile, then they served their purpose.

speaker: Marlo
content: Reading a book at a time like this? And The Wilderness, of all things? ...You two sure have leisure time to spare.

speaker: Marlo
content: "Fate, you blind thrower of dice, casting us onto fields shrouded in war... Aspiration, you sacred yet callous flame, flickering in this bloodied storm..."

speaker: Manphist
content: How nostalgic. That was a particular favorite of mine in my youth. It's quite remarkable that you still remember those lines, Captain Marlo.

speaker: Helene
content: Do forgive me for interrupting this little trip down memory lane. Is this some special Outland childhood reminiscence I'm not privy to?

speaker: Helene
content: What a pity. I'm from DisCity. Didn't have my nose in many books as a girl, let alone poetry.

speaker: Helene
content: Then again, if I hadn't... gotten myself tangled up with a man of such "lofty aspirations," I suppose I wouldn't be sitting here now...
She fixes Marlo with a pointed, challenging stare. He looks away, unable to hold it.
An awkward silence blankets the room, thick and uncomfortable, but it's shattered moments later by a guard's sharp announcement.

speaker: Guard
content: Reporting, ma'am! A new dispatch from Intelligence Headquarters. Shall I bring it in?
A cold knot tightens in your chest, and Hilda's gaze flicks to you for a fleeting moment.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Yes. Bring it in.
The guard crosses the hall, the sealed envelope pinched between his fingers like a verdict. With deliberate steps, he delivers it directly into Hilda's waiting hand.
Every eye in the room locks onto the letter. You are utterly powerless to stop it.
—It's too late.
Just as your mind starts to scramble, calculating when to rewind with your next LINK attempt, a sharp, concussive blast rips through the manor's foundations.
BOOM—!!
The lights whip violently, strobing the scene in frantic flashes before surrendering completely, plunging the world into choking darkness.

speaker: Marlo
content: Enemy attack! Get down! Find cover!
Gunfire erupts the moment he barks the order.
The walls and windows are pockmarked with the sickening thud of impacts, punctuated by the crystalline shatter of glass. A wave of screams is swiftly choked down as training overrides panic.
This is it! The perfect chance, and your only one!
You scramble through the chaos, feigning a stumble of terror as you crash into Hilda and reach for the envelope in her hand. A grunt is punched from her lungs.

speaker: Hilda
content: Who's there?!
Screams and gunfire are a deafening storm. You're so close! Your fingers brush the rough paper of the envelope. You seize it and yank with all your strength!

But as the letter tears from her grasp, it never reaches your hand. A bullet screams through the darkness, punching clean through the paper. For a heart-stopping moment, it flutters—a gray, withered leaf—tracing a silent arc before vanishing completely into the chaos.
Finding it now, in this impenetrable darkness, seems impossible. You decide to...

options: Avoid the crowd and investigate the true explosion site
Chase after the envelope at all costs

content: The explosion tore through the second floor. Given what's kept up there, there's only one thing the target could be: the Monolith prototype in Hilda's room.
[Scene Change: Corridor]
By the time you reach the upstairs corridor, the gunfire is sputtering out. The perimeter attack has been quelled, the guards' shots growing isolated, then ceasing altogether.
In the ensuing quiet, your eyes strain against the darkness. A single, vague silhouette is collapsed on the floor ahead.
The lights flicker, then flood the corridor with a harsh, steady glow, allowing you to make out the face.

speaker: Chief
content: Johnson?!
[Scene Change: could be Main Hall]

The scene is one of utter devastation. The electrical equipment at the corridor's end is shredded. A nest of wiring has been blown apart, its core still smoldering, tendrils of black smoke coiling toward the ceiling. The walls are scarred with soot.

And there, directly beneath the shattered electrical box, is Johnson. He lies on his back, an ordinary military knife driven deep into his chest. A pool of fresh, shockingly red blood is still spreading beneath him, gleaming under the emergency lights.

His eyes are frozen wide in a final mask of terror. His right hand is twisted into a desperate, clawing gesture, while his left hand is clenched in a death grip around... a single, severed piece of copper wire.
A choked scream escapes Casey at the sight of the body. She stumbles backward, nearly fainting, before Manphist lunges forward to catch her.

speaker: Casey
content: No... Johnson... No... Who did this? Tell me who did this!
Emotion overwhelms her. She lurches to her feet and stumbles toward Johnson's body, the stunned hesitation of the others granting her a tragic passage.

speaker: Casey
content: This knife... it's Marlo's. I saw it on him yesterday, during his argument with Horne!
Her gaze instantly locks on Marlo. His face darkens as his hand goes instinctively to the empty sheath at his waist.

speaker: Marlo
content: Tch. With all the shooting and chaos earlier, some rat probably swiped it in the dark.

speaker: Casey
content: You're a professional! You expect me to believe someone could lift your knife without you knowing? And how convenient that you just happened to be on the second floor when the lights came back on!
Casey steps forward, her gaze intense and bloodshot from a sleepless night, pinning Marlo in place.

speaker: Casey
content: You didn't leave it on purpose. You dropped it because ${PlayerName} cut off your escape! You knew you'd be trapped if you didn't run, so you fled. And now you're lying about it being stolen!

speaker: Marlo
content: Hey, Hilda. You just gonna stand there and let her run her mouth?
Ignoring their argument, Hilda strides to the blast site, her eyes scanning the charred plastic fragments and fine metal powder littering the ground.

speaker: Hilda
content: Nolaine, analyze the composition of this powder.

speaker: Nolaine
content: Let me see... Looks like a crude ammonium nitrate mixture. Homemade. Low yield, but enough to damage the junction and cause the outage. The residue contains copper shavings and fragmented engineering plastic.

speaker: Hilda
content: So, Johnson was sabotaging the electrical box before he was attacked. He succeeded, and then someone stopped him. Permanently.

speaker: Hilda
content: But why kill him? And why leave the body at the scene of the crime?
Her gaze sweeps across Marlo's empty knife sheath.

speaker: Hilda
content: One possibility is an intervention. A would-be hero discovered the sabotage and killed him to stop it. But it seems we have no such clever "detective" among us.

speaker: Hilda
content: That leaves the second scenario. The killer was an accomplice. The murder was to silence him.

speaker: Casey
content: That's not true...! Johnson would never do this! He was loyal to the metropoles! One of you must have forced him into it, then killed him to cover your tracks!

speaker: Marlo
content: ...I didn't kill him. When I got here, he was already on the ground.

speaker: Casey
content: Then why were you looking for him? When the shooting started, who would think to check the electrical box?!

speaker: Marlo
content: Now that you mention it... Huck was the one who asked me where Johnson was... Hey, was this your doing?!

speaker: Huck
content: Th-that's a vicious lie! You're the one caught with an empty sheath, and now you're trying to pin this on me?!

speaker: Casey
content: Huck, why did you send Marlo after him? Did you know what he was doing? Or did you put him up to it?

speaker: Casey
content: Johnson didn't know a thing about electrical systems! Someone gave him the tools, told him what to do... Let's see if the copper wire in his hand matches the spool in your toolkit. That should clear things up, shouldn't it?
Huck goes perfectly still. A tremor runs through him, and his gaze snaps involuntarily to the toolkit at his hip.
In the breathless silence that follows, Manphist carefully clears his throat, the sound cutting through the tension.

speaker: Manphist
content: Perhaps a suggestion. While we cannot ascertain the true culprit at this moment, might I propose that Marlo and Huck surrender their weapons first?

speaker: Hilda
content: A reasonable proposal. Please hand over your weapons.
Marlo's glare is sharp enough to shatter steel. A muscle twitches in his jaw as, with deliberate slowness, he opens his jacket and unbuckles his gun belt.
Huck's face bleeds of all color, leaving it a mask of stark fear.

speaker: Casey
content: What are you waiting for, Huck?

speaker: Huck
content: I told you, I didn't kill him! I'm not a murderer!
In a flash of motion, Huck wrenches a screwdriver from his belt and hurls himself at Casey, the closest target, shouting frantically.

speaker: Huck
content: Fine! Yes, I went to see Johnson! I invested everything in his private fund! I just wanted my money back! I gave him the tools to escape, that's all!
The sudden aggression is all the provocation Marlo needs; his weapon is already raised, his aim steady on Huck.

speaker: Marlo
content: Drop it, Huck! Now!

speaker: Casey
content: Huck, you fool! Killing me won't save you!

speaker: Huck
content: I confess! I sold information! I leaked the Cryptography Department's location! But don't you dare act high and mighty! None of you are clean!

speaker: Huck
content: You! How many bodies did you climb over to get where you are in the gang? How many families? And you—

speaker: Huck
content: You twist the truth, you ruin lives with your headlines! And you!

speaker: Huck
content: You fabricated the grounds to have your own comrades eliminated! Don't any of you see their faces when you close your eyes?!
His hand jerks violently. The screwdriver flashes, gashing deep into Casey's neck. A torrent of blood immediately streams down her skin.

speaker: Huck
content: We're all dead if we stay... Just let me go... Let me go! Hilda!
Hilda's gaze coolly assesses Huck and the hostage, Casey. She takes a deliberate step back, seemingly clearing a path.
But in that same movement, her hand makes a subtle, deliberate gesture meant only for you.

speaker: Hilda
content: Huck, think logically. I can let you pass, but you won't survive the journey back to DisCity. When he goes down the stairs.

speaker: Hilda
content: Surrender is your best option. Follow my lead.

speaker: Hilda
content: Is this how you want to reunite with your family?
Three.
Cold sweat and Casey's blood smear together as Huck drags her limp form, stumbling toward the stairs. He's focused on his escape.
Two.
Meanwhile, you're already in position.
One!
Swiftly, you snatch Marlo's discarded gun from the floor. But you don't aim at Huck, the dangerous, moving target. Instead, you fire at Marlo!

speaker: Hilda
content: Now!
Hilda's shout rings out almost simultaneously with the gunshot! In the split second Huck is distracted by Marlo's scream, she explodes into motion, lunging at him.

She crosses the short distance like a phantom, her right elbow driving with brutal precision into the soft tissue beneath his ribs. A strangled gasp escapes Huck as his vision tunnels. His grip fails.

In one fluid, vicious motion, Hilda wrenches the weapon from his hand, drives a knee into his lower back, and slams him into the floorboards. The cold, hard kiss of a gun barrel presses against his temple.

speaker: Hilda
content: Don't move. One twitch, and I'll make you wish you were dead.

Meanwhile, you step calmly past the chaos and send Marlo's pistol skittering into a distant corner with a precise kick.
He clutches his blood-soaked shoulder, glaring up at you with pure venom, but he's too weakened to do anything more.
Helene and Manphist stand utterly still, frozen by the lightning-fast reversal.
The hall stinks of dust and iron. Johnson's corpse, Casey's grievous injury, Marlo's bleeding shoulder, and Huck pinned beneath Hilda—together, they form a tableau from a nightmare.

Hilda kneels on Huck's back, her weapon unwavering. Her breath comes in quick, controlled puffs, but her eyes are razor-sharp. When her gaze flicks to yours, you catch a clear, unmistakable flash of approval.
Daylight gradually bleeds into the sky, yet the gloomy rain refuses to cease.

The chaos subsides into a grim aftermath. With Marlo and Huck bound and locked away, and Nolaine having taken Casey for emergency aid, Hilda dismisses the messenger guard. The hall suddenly feels cavernous and half-empty.
Then, you remember. The most urgent matter. Your eyes frantically sweep the room, landing just in time to see a slender, feminine hand retrieve the fateful envelope from its shadowy corner.

speaker: Helene
content: Hilda, you forgot this.
With elegant poise, Helene passes the letter to Hilda. A silent nod, and Hilda opens the envelope once more. Her face is an unreadable mask, giving no hint of the contents.
The opportunity to act has slipped away. All you can do is watch, your breath caught in your chest, as her eyes trace the final lines of the document.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...It appears the city-state's verification is conclusive, ${PlayerName}. I'm sorry for the previous skepticism.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now that your identity has been officially confirmed, I must formally apologize to you.
You force your expression to remain neutral, a mask held in place by sheer will. Every muscle in your face fights the shock screaming within.
What is happening? How can a letter from a metropole confirm your identity?
Your eyes lock onto the envelope in her hand. That's when you see it—a critical detail.
This envelope is different from the one you saw in the darkness. The original was grazed by a bullet, causing it to fall. This one is pristine. Unmarked.
The letter was switched.
But by whom?

Your heart hammers against your ribs, a frantic drumbeat against the chaos whirling in your mind. You scramble for an explanation, any thread of logic in this sudden turn of events.
Meanwhile, Hilda simply folds the "response letter" and tucks it into her coat. Her movements are unhurried, efficient, as if she's just filed a routine report. The matter, for her, is now settled.
Then, she turns and bows to you with solemn formality.

speaker: Hilda
content: From this moment, I will no longer entertain any doubt regarding your capabilities or your authority.

speaker: Hilda
content: And I must hope... that you can find it in yourself to overlook my earlier... lack of decorum.

speaker: Chief
content: Given the circumstances, your caution was warranted.

speaker: Chief
content: I have a long memory for slights, you know. Adequate compensation might shorten it.
(Paths converge)
She raises her chin, the ghost of a smile on her lips. Yet, in the subtle crinkling around her eyes and the gentle arch of her brows, her true feelings are quietly revealed.

speaker: Hilda
content: In that case, you are free to move about and rest. I will be interrogating Huck and Marlo, and will inform you at once of any new developments.

speaker: Hilda
content: You may keep Marlo's firearm. Secure it properly; it will serve you well for self-defense should you face danger again.
She places a hand over her heart and offers a crisp, formal salute before turning on her heel and striding away.
Only then do you exhale the tension you've been holding.
One hurdle now is cleared, but a critical loose end still hangs in the air, threatening to unravel everything...
Fortunately, the solution is clear. You've already pieced it together: of the handful of people who touched that letter, the most suspicious by far is "that person."
Once the attack begins, it will be too late. You must find her immediately.
To avoid raising any alarms, you calmly walk straight to your room.

speaker: Chief
content: The switch for the secret passage should be right around... here.
[Secret Passage]
The walls within are coated in ghostly fluorescent paint. You drop to a crouch—the floor is bare. No footprints.
They know about the passage, but they haven't come through. You've beaten them here.
There's still time.
[Hilda's Study]

Inside, heavy velvet curtains mute the unrelenting storm and the chaos down in the hall, creating an island of tense silence. Hilda is hunched over her desk, her entire focus locked on the Monolith prototype.

speaker: Hilda
content: Do you need something, ${PlayerName}?

speaker: Option
options: There's going to be a real attack.

speaker: Chief
content: I just got word. There's an attack coming in twenty minutes. I think all the guards are in on it. Their plan is to storm the manor, kill everyone, and take the Monolith. We need to get ready. Now.
She doesn't immediately accept your story, but she doesn't reject it out of hand either.

speaker: Hilda
content: What's your source?
You cross the room to Hilda's wardrobe, fling the doors open, and with a few practiced motions, pry away the false back panel.
A yawning, pitch-black passage is revealed. Within the darkness, a series of faint, fluorescent marks hover in the air. When you look at Hilda, her face is a mask of shock.

speaker: Hilda
content: Did you just say... the guards?

speaker: Chief
content: Think about it. If you could use them to stage a fake attack, why couldn't the mole use them to launch a real one?
The light catches half her face, revealing a stern profile. The faint smile is gone, her lips now a tight, severe line.

speaker: Hilda
content: How much do you know?
You take a deep breath and reveal what you've discovered.

speaker: Chief
content: The "attack" used non-lethal rounds. They deliberately avoided any angles that could cause real casualties. With that much gunfire, we didn't have a single injury? And it was just... "subdued." That's not believable.

speaker: Chief
content: It was more like an elaborate fireworks show. Designed to create the illusion of chaos.

speaker: Chief
content: Looking back now, certain details seem a little too convenient.

speaker: Chief
content: You knew Johnson had connections with a few here, so you loosened security around him to draw the mole out.

speaker: Chief
content: But you never expected it would involve innocent people. That it would lead to real casualties.
Finally, Hilda turns to you. Her movement is deliberate, unhurried. When her eyes meet yours, there is not a trace of hesitation in her gaze.

speaker: Hilda
content: Johnson's death was necessary. His actions alone warranted execution a hundred times over. He was the most obvious, weakest link in the mole's network. His stupidity and fear were a liability.

speaker: Hilda
content: I just made use of his corpse. It was an efficient way to flush out potential traitors. Nothing more.

speaker: Chief
content: Is that so? But I don't think that's who you are.
As you speak, you produce the roll of cipher paper, flashing it in her direction before placing it down on the table.

A flicker of naked panic in Hilda's gaze, swiftly mastered. She assesses you, the evidence, and the stakes in a heartbeat. The pretense is over. Now, she might as well hear you out before resorting to more permanent solutions.

speaker: Chief
content: You hate manufactured sacrifices. You despise involving civilians. You're loyal to the city-state, but you question its orders. Honestly, I wouldn't be surprised if you'd already altered classified documents given the chance.

speaker: Chief
content: You have your pride. You only eliminate targets you deem deserving. So admit it, Casey's death was never part of your design. It's a flaw in your otherwise perfect plan.

speaker: Chief
content: And I was angry. You knew who I was, and you still kept me in the dark. You used me, just like you used everyone else. If I hadn't been quick on my feet, I could have ended up like Casey.
Seeing her lips tighten involuntarily, you soften your tone.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not turning you in. Not now, anyway. I believe that even in a war, we need a line we don't cross. A sense of what's right.

speaker: Chief
content: But I will say this: one person can only do so much. If we had worked together from the start, maybe we could have avoided this tragedy.
At this point, her agitation suddenly stills. A calculated silence hangs in the air before she breaks it, her voice now measured and clear.

speaker: Hilda
content: To be honest, I never expected you to show up here. And you saw through my scheme far quicker than I projected.

speaker: Hilda
content: You could have remained silent. Or you could have moved against me in the chaos. Yet, you chose to help me.
Your proposal for an alliance hangs in the air. She meets it not with acceptance, but with a steely, knowing look, seamlessly pivoting to lay out her own shrewd assessment of the situation.

speaker: Hilda
content: This shows that despite your anger, you've made the most rational choice: aside from me, you trust no one else here. I remain your only viable ally.
Her words leave you utterly speechless.
She is right. The truth is, she isn't in your power; she's your only reliable ally. Any advantage you seemingly hold is purely theoretical.
In seeing this, both of you have proven yourselves a step ahead of Helene.
Having laid her cards on the table, Hilda extends her hand.
Time has taught you to decipher the subtle language behind her icy composure. And now, in her eyes, you see not just calm assessment and approval, but a faint, genuine glimmer of joy.

speaker: Hilda
content: Thank you for your honesty... and for your fair judgment.

speaker: Hilda
content: You have my word. I will not act unilaterally like that again.

speaker: Hilda
content: So, let us table the discussion of my... methods, and your objections to them. For now, we need a plan for the very real attack that is coming.

speaker: Hilda
content: That, after all, is the immediate priority.

You scout the passage behind the wardrobe again, calculating that a strike team of three or four will likely use it as a point of entry. Any more than that, and the front door remains their primary breach point.
With quiet efficiency, Hilda arranges a decoy from clothes and pillows before the desk, then directs you to use the furniture as concealment.
You've trusted no one else with this plan; the mole is still out there, and a single leak could be fatal.
And so, time passes quickly.

The expected explosion comes, rocking the annex building. Manphist's flustered shout echoes from below, immediately drowned out by the front door splintering open and the thunderous stampede of combat boots on the stairs—
(Sound effect: gunshots at the door)
Almost in sync with the assault on the door, you hear hurried, chaotic footsteps echoing from the depths of the wardrobe passage. They're here.
The room's door is kicked open with a violent crash. A storm of gunfire erupts instantly, shredding Hilda's decoy into a cloud of fabric and stuffing in a matter of seconds.
As the gunsmoke clears, the soldiers' grim realization dawns—they've been lured into a kill box. But the realization comes a heartbeat too late.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now!
Hilda's shots are precise, shattering wrists and sending guns clattering to the floor.
Yet, even with their hands broken, the guards charge forward, eyes bloodshot with frenzy. There's no choice left—
The last remaining survivor makes a desperate move, raising his hand to bite down on something hidden in his sleeve.

speaker: Hilda
content: Stop him! He's got a poison pill! We need him alive!
You summon all your strength and drive a powerful punch into the guard's jaw. His head snaps back, and he drops, unconscious.
You lunge forward, locking your hands around his throat and squeezing until his eyes roll back. He collapses to the floor, out cold.
(Paths converge)
A quick pat-down reveals the poison pill. You pry it from his clothes and toss it aside.
Rapid footsteps approach from outside the door.

speaker: Marlo
content: Heard gunshots! Are you two in one piece?!

speaker: L.L.
content: We're fine. What's happening with the fire outside?

speaker: Marlo
content: No idea, but you're safe, that's what counts. Those guards are all traitorous scum anyway. I'll go kill—
As he speaks, he bends down to retrieve the guns dropped by the two guards.
At this moment, you decide to...

options: Stop him from taking the guns

speaker: Marlo
content: Hmph. Appreciate it.
He strides out, a submachine gun in each hand and a small arsenal strapped to his body, radiating an aura of pure, predatory menace.
Moments later, the staccato roar of gunfire erupts from the corridor, punctuated by agonized screams that are swiftly cut short.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...No need to worry. Marlo will take care of it.
Hilda deftly reloads her weapon.

speaker: Hilda
content: These guards, including Shane, were all assigned from the city-state headquarters by the Intelligence leadership.

speaker: Hilda
content: As for who is really pulling their strings... we will find out during the interrogation.

speaker: Hilda
content: Let's go. We'll take him to the interrogation room first.
The last of the flames sputters and dies, and with them, the sounds of Marlo's massacre fall silent.

In the hazy, smoke-choked aftermath, you follow Hilda through the dim corridors, the acrid stench of burning saturating the air. She leads you to the hall that has been utterly transformed into a scene of chaos.
Here, the survivors have gathered.
Nolaine crouches by the doorway, a gun hanging limply in her hand. She stares with profound shock at the dozens of corpses littering the floor.

speaker: Nolaine
content: ...******* hell. That was brutal.
Before the sprawl of corpses, Marlo sits on the sofa, a god of slaughter soaked in blood.

speaker: Marlo
content: Report, ma'am. All 29 security guards who were disguised traitors have been eliminated.

speaker: Marlo
content: That old dog Huck tried to slip away in the chaos. I put him down with one shot, too.

speaker: Marlo
content: Not sure if the actual mole was among them, but if you interrogate that survivor, you'll get something useful.
His hand trembles as he fumbles for a cigarette. But his strength is gone; his fingers betray him, and it tumbles from his grasp, unlit.

speaker: Helene
