A final, icy tremor climbs your spine as the world dissolves. Yet, through the thickening fog, Hilda's voice remains sharp and perfectly clear.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now then, I want you to tell me very carefully... who are you, really?
The rainfall outside the window has thickened into a relentless downpour. You've been here longer than you realized.
Hilda's hostility has melted away. Though a trace of wariness remains, the pointed tests have ceased. Somehow, without a word, you have become genuine confidants.
As the second pot of black tea goes cold between you, you decline her offer to fill your cup and prepare to take your leave.

speaker: Hilda
content: Let me see you out through the front door.
But the moment she rises from the couch, a wrongness cuts through the calm.
She sways violently, her hands slamming onto the table to keep from collapsing to the floor.

speaker: Chief
content: Hilda... what's wrong?
You crouch to steady her, and a jolt of ice runs through you. Her skin is deathly cold to the touch. A violent, uncontrollable shiver has taken hold of her body.

speaker: Hilda
content: Nngh...
Then, a torrent of blood erupts from her lips, a shocking, brilliant crimson that soaks both your clothes.
(Red filter)
You freeze, stunned by this sudden turn of events.
What is happening? An attack from the mole? An accident? Or a sudden illness?
A terrifying, unprecedented thought strikes you: what happens if a LINK subject dies within their own consciousness?

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}...
Her hand claws at yours, gripping with a desperate, final strength. She pulls you closer, and with her last breath, she rasps one agonizing word into your ear—
Your eyes dart to the tea set. You both drank the same brew, and you feel fine. It isn't in the tea.
Your gaze flicks to a plate in the corner—today's unfinished dinner. Was the poison added there? Who prepared her meal?
Or was it contact-based? A toxin applied to a component of the Monolith prototype, seeping into a small cut on her finger...
Before your racing thoughts can find purchase, the air itself turns to stone. An immense, invisible force slams down, crushing the breath from your lungs.
Then, everything shatters into nothing.
[Restricted Area Laboratory]
Your eyes snap open.

A gasp rips through you, the suffocating shock of the memory fading just as the heart monitor's frantic beeping registers in your ears. You drag air back into your lungs, pulse hammering against your ribs.
Your eyes snap to the containment tank where Hilda lies motionless. She appears unchanged, yet gives the unnerving impression that she's fading, about to be consumed by the dark mist of Mania.
The only thing that steadies you is the containment tank's data screen, silently displaying all normal vital signs.

speaker: Chief
content: Schorl, what's going on? Can a LINK subject die inside their own consciousness?

speaker: Schorl
content: If the subject actively seeks their own demise, then yes, experiencing death within the consciousness space is possible.

speaker: Schorl
content: However, from our operational standpoint, the "death" of an interrogation subject is an extremely hazardous event. Should this recur, she faces a genuine risk of termination, and we would lose a vital intelligence asset. I must advise you to exercise greater caution in future sessions.

You remember the haunting indifference in Hilda's eyes. A woman who seemed to have already made her peace with death. The only crack in that stoic facade appeared when you discovered the cipher strip; that was the key that truly stirred her.
However, the immediate, brutal truth is that survival comes first. You must keep both of you alive—her, and yourself.

speaker: Chief
content: Understood. I'll keep trying. Her mind holds a wealth of intelligence we can't access anywhere else. For example, I've already identified several individuals who worked with her as Metropole spies. Many had infiltrated DisCity's financial sector and underground networks. You may want to look into whether they're still active.
As for other objectives, you'll have to play them by ear—gathering specific intelligence on Monolith, earning Hilda's trust, and potentially turning her.
For now, you hand Schorl the intelligence on Johnson from the dinner and settle back into the LINK device.
Hilda leaves the hall, leaving you and the others—each harboring private agendas—to occupy separate corners of the room.
You pace casually, using the moment to examine the traces of the attack while plotting how to extract the information you need.
Helene may be gone, but the hall itself still holds answers.
Cellar
[Cellar]
Footsteps echo, swallowed by the oppressive darkness of the tunnel.
Hey...? I'm here.
I saw the signal you hid. Where are you—?
In the suffocating quiet, every sound carries. A moment later, a series of sharp, metallic taps ring out from the pipes within the walls.
(Clank, clank, clank, clank—)
****. Always with the games.
Swallowing his frustration, he raises his own fist and begins to answer in kind, rapping a sequence against the pipe.
[Scene Change: Main Hall, Upbeat BGM]

speaker: Helene
content: ...Yes, spies come in many varieties. The most common are local assets. People living ordinary lives, only activated when needed.

speaker: Helene
content: Then there are the infiltrators, planted into specific departments. They require an elaborate cover and a full support system to maintain.

speaker: Helene
content: A man like Marlo is what we call "deep cover." Do you have any idea what it cost him? How many people he had to kill to earn his place in that gang?
With a slight sway, Helene sets her glass down and leans into your space, her movements softened by drink.

speaker: Helene
content: So yes, he's a bad person. I'm hardly surprised.
With a subtle shift of your weight, you evade her touch. Your face betrays nothing.

speaker: Chief
content: Sounds like you really hate him.

speaker: Helene
content: Of course. Isn't he the one who made me who I am today?
As if catching her own loss of composure, she grabs the wine bottle and shakes it. Nothing sloshes inside. It is empty.

speaker: Helene
content: Talking with you is so... refreshing, Officer. I'll go fetch another bottle...
She sways to her feet, but her movement freezes mid-step, her attention seized by something beyond the window.

speaker: Helene
content: Hey... wh-what's that?
[Exterior, Rain, Fire Effect]

speaker: Helene
content: Look! Is the annex on fire?!

speaker: Manphist
content: Oh my... It appears so... But in this downpour, and given the manor's brick and stone construction, it should have considerable fire resistance...

speaker: Nolaine
content: No! That's the depot with the fuel reserves—
BOOOOM!

A thunderous explosion tears through the air outside the window—gunpowder, oil barrels, it's impossible to tell. The shockwave is a physical force, slamming through the main building and hurling objects to the floor.

Before the deafening roar has even faded, a wave of heat and light follows. Flames surge, and thick, billowing smoke immediately begins to choke the air, rolling relentlessly toward the main building.

speaker: Manphist
content: Not again! Guards! Where are the guards?! Open this door at once! Let us out! This whole place could go up!
Manphist screams, throwing his weight against the locked door in a frenzy.
Then, a second blast erupts directly beneath your feet.
This is another attack! More brutal and dangerous than anything from this morning.

speaker: Guard
content: Everyone, stay calm! The attack is currently confined to the annex! Reinforcements have been dispatched. All main hall personnel, follow us to the shelter immediately!

speaker: Nolaine
content: That ******* mole! This time you won't get away!
With an angry roar, Nolaine charges through the doorway and into the smoke.
Helene's hand finds yours, her grip tight with panic.

speaker: Chief
content: You go with Manphist and the others. I'll find Hilda.
You wrench your hand from Helene's grasp without a second thought, racing up the stairs until you skid to a halt outside Hilda's door.
The corridor is a tunnel of fire, deserted and choked with swirling smoke.
You pound on the door, only to hear no answer. Instead, from within, you hear the unmistakable, metallic click of a gun being cocked.
Instinct screams that something is terribly wrong. You retreat, slipping cautiously into your own room next door.
[Study]
You make straight for the study, your fingers finding the hidden switch with practiced ease. The wall opens, revealing the secret passage.

speaker: Chief
content: ...!! What in the—
The narrow passage is illuminated by ghostly fluorescent arrows. In their eerie glow, you see a chaos of footprints scuffing the dust, and the air hangs thick with the acrid sting of gunsmoke.
A cold dread grips you. You plunge forward, racing toward Hilda's room.
[Slow Scene Change: Hilda's Room]

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Who's... there...
The room is a charnel house, choked with thick smoke and dancing flames.
Several guards litter the floor, their blood mingling in dark, spreading pools. A brutal gunfight has painted the scene with violence.

And there is Hilda. She lies on the cold floor, most of her clothing saturated with blood. Below her throat, a ghastly wound leaks crimson, viscous fluid. Every shallow, wet breath she takes bubbles horrifically.
Yet, her gun is still clenched in her fist, aimed shakily at the door.

speaker: Chief
content: Hilda!

You crash to your knees beside her, pressing torn cloth hard against the wound. Blood instantly soaks through, hot and relentless against your fingers. You can feel her life slipping away, like an unstoppable tide receding.
(CG: Death)

speaker: Hilda
content: I hear... ${PlayerName}...? Is that you? The lights... have all gone out...

speaker: Hilda
content: Listen... they found the secret passage... behind the wardrobe... in the manor...

speaker: Hilda
content: That gun from before... keep it close... when the time comes... don't hesitate...

speaker: Chief
content: Stop talking! I'll find something to stop the bleeding!
She tries to lift a hand to stop you, but the gesture dies as a feeble twitch.

speaker: Hilda
content: Don't... It's already too late...

speaker: Hilda
content: Heh... Never thought... you'd be the one with me... Not bad... Could've been much worse...
With a final, monumental effort, the one hand she can still move finds your collar and clutches it.
What are you trying to tell me?
(White Interaction Point)
A small key rests in her palm, radiating a stark, silver light. Without ceremony, she presses it firmly into your hand and gestures toward the Monolith.
Your gaze finds the device behind her. Its dark surface is broken only by a single, prominent lock. Even now, the machine stands like Death itself, cold and ruthless in the room's center.

You fit the key into the lock. The casing clicks open, revealing a breathtakingly complex web of multifaceted circuitry. Hilda points directly to the core component, her silent command clear: take it.
(White Interaction Point: Blood on Chest)

This is the fatal shot. The bullet shattered her brooch, robbing it of its full velocity, but still drove deep into her chest. It didn't exit; it lodged itself inside her. Now, with every ragged breath, she pumps more blood into the cavity of her own body. Saving her is impossible.
She knows it. The fight has already left her eyes.
(Continue with Multiple White Interaction Points)

speaker: Hilda
content: The Monolith... isn't finished... but the remaining data... is enough for the city-state's researchers...
Hilda's voice is a threadbare whisper, each word strained through a bloody froth.

speaker: Hilda
content: I entrust you... with the spark... beneath... the Monolith...
(Obtained Key 3)
Her voice is a fading whisper, but as your fingers close around the unfinished Monolith she entrusted to you, your own resolve hardens into something cold and sharp.

For all this time, that cipher strip has been an unbreakable lock. You've tried every method, every key, to no avail. But now... now you hold the key to the Monolith itself. If this creation of Hilda's can truly decode any cipher—
There's no time for sentiment. No time to wait for a natural end. With swift, deliberate movements, you take out the cipher strip and slide it into the Monolith's waiting slot.
Hilda's eyes widen in utter disbelief.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...${PlayerName}...

The facade crumbles. In a final, desperate act, her trembling fingers reach for you, not with strength, but with a plea. But the Monolith's work is already done. One by one, the encoded strip unspools into stark, undeniable truth, laying bare the reality she has been so desperate to bury.

June 7. The lockdown directive came in. Cut water and power. I checked the coordinates three times. They were targeting civilian sectors. I reported it. The response was just to follow orders.
This operation resulted in 11 casualties. I'm writing their names here. I have to.

June 9. Filed the raid report.
Operation successful. Another list of names to record.

August 11. Sent the preliminary "mole" report.
15 traitors purged. They were our own. The real mole is still out there.

I questioned it. Got reprimanded, again.
"Obey orders. Fulfill your duty. Don't concern yourself with anything else."
Duty, they say. Duty.
But is my duty just to relay death warrants and watch innocent people die?

September 21. Orders to transport real medical supplies. No cover story this time.
Good. For once, that's a relief.

October 2. Another operation against civilians. I objected.
My first time in solitary. I regret it. Not for speaking up, but because I'll be stuck here for days.
How much intel will I miss?

October 10. Out of confinement.

October 20. A major "error" happened today.
Maybe my hand still isn't steady from the injury. I pressed too hard, smudged the coordinates on the translation.
The strike missed by 5 degrees. Hit nothing but dirt. No casualties.
Our operation failed. And I felt... happy.
I think I'm losing it.
Your consciousness is slipping away. As you clutch the decoded text tightly, emotions surge within you.
So this is it. What she has been hiding all along is a loyalty shattered and remade—not by blind obedience, but by conscience.

Seeing her secret laid bare, Hilda's dying face contorts in despair, her eyes glistening with unshed tears. She doesn't know who you truly are; she believes the cold machinery of the city-state has uncovered her heart. But your answer is to clasp her hand, firmly, in your own.
The darkness presses in, a physical weight. Each breath is a struggle, a shallow gasp in the encroaching void.
Don't worry. Your secret is safe with me. I'll get you... get both of us out of here.
Following the vote, you disperse and return to your rooms alone.
[Study]
Back in the solitude of your room, you turn the facts over in your mind. Only three suspects remain: Manphist, Nolaine, and Helene. Should you... just kill them all?
You suddenly realize how pragmatic—and utterly cruel—this thought is.
A cold weight against your waist reminds you of Marlo's pistol.
You draw it, checking the magazine. Only a few rounds remain. If you plan to use it for protection, you'll need to find more ammunition.

options: Rest now and do it tomorrow
Go to Marlo's room for ammunition now

content: You slip out the door and make your way to Marlo's room.
[Hilda's Room]
Like Hilda's, it's a spacious master bedroom.
You begin your search, moving with deliberate caution.

speaker: Nolaine
content: Shh. Don't move.
You feel a cold blade pressed against your back.

speaker: Nolaine
content: I just went to your room. Didn't expect to find you here.

speaker: Nolaine
content: I know I'm not the mole, so it has to be one of the other three. So why bother figuring out which one when I can just kill you all?

speaker: Nolaine
content: So I took care of Manphist first. Then I went for Helene.

speaker: Nolaine
content: When I killed Helene, I found this.
A hand reaches over your shoulder, a blood-stained letter pinched between her fingers.

speaker: Nolaine
content: She kept this on her as a lucky charm. Pathetic, isn't it?

speaker: Nolaine
content: So it was you. You're the mole who infiltrated us!

speaker: Nolaine
content: Once you're gone, this is over. Hilda and I can finally get out of here alive!

speaker: Chief
content: That logic doesn't work. Killing everyone doesn't prove your innocence.

speaker: Chief
content: When you're the only one left... Hilda wouldn't see a savior. She'd see the most likely suspect.

speaker: Nolaine
content: No... that's not true! I'm her most trusted subordinate! She would believe me!

speaker: Chief
content: Do you really think she'd trust the person who slaughtered all the other people?

speaker: Chief
content: You'd have a better chance if you let me live. I can vouch for you.
You turn, a slow and deliberate motion. The blade bites deep, slicing through cloth and skin, but you refuse to flinch. Your eyes lock directly with Nolaine's, meeting her gaze with unwavering calm.

speaker: Chief
content: I believe you. Someone willing to go this far to ensure Hilda's survival... couldn't be the mole.

speaker: Chief
content: So please, trust me too.
The knife in Nolaine's hand begins to betray a tremor.

speaker: Nolaine
content: Hilda... has to live... Monolith... is the city-state's only hope...

speaker: Nolaine
content: I have to... I must protect her!! No matter what!!

You make a grab for Nolaine's knife. The hilt leaves her grip, but it's a feint. Using the momentum, she spins, wrist flicking to reclaim the blade in a fluid, deadly arc aimed at your ribs. Simultaneously, her other hand claws for the gun in your grasp.
Instinct takes over. You lock onto her arms, muscles straining as you wrench them away. A frantic, brutal twist, and then, the muffled, sickening thump of the trigger being pulled.

speaker: Nolaine
content: ...You... you... bastard...
She crumples. And as her body meets the ground, your gaze lifts to the doorway. Hilda stands there, frozen.
After all this time together, you've learned to read the subtle shifts beneath her icy composure.
Her eyes are wide, not just with shock, but a scalding disappointment. And beneath it all, a raw, unmistakable pain of betrayal.
The barrel of her gun rises, steadying on you.
Innocence is a lost cause. There is no proof, only the damning scene she witnessed. But you still have one decision to make—
Hilda's aim is steady. Yet, instead of fear, you find a strange calm.
You lower your own, close your eyes, and await her judgment.
(Fade to black)

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Tell me what happened.
(Black screen fades)
Your eyes open to find Hilda lowering her gun.
Her lips are a thin, hard line, and the usual coldness in her eyes has been forged into resolute determination.

speaker: Hilda
content: I believe you're not the mole, but you need to tell me what really happened.
You recount the night's events in detail, omitting only the letter held by Helene. The blood-soaked parchment is now illegible anyway, a secret forever lost.
When you fall silent, Hilda's gaze remains fixed on Nolaine's body.

speaker: Hilda
content: Could you help me with something?

speaker: Hilda
content: Help me prepare them for burial. After that... just go get some rest.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now, there really won't be any mole left.
Bang!
Blood erupts from Helene's chest.
Bang, bang—!
More gunshots rip through the air. High above, the fluttering pigeon stills, then drifts gently downward.

speaker: Helene
content: ...I don't want... to die...
With her last shred of strength, her hand stretches toward you. Her fingers scrape weakly at the cold ground, once, leaving only faint, desperate marks in the dirt.

speaker: Helene
content: Did I... make... the wrong choice... again...
[Black Screen]
A few minutes later, Hilda steps over to Helene's lifeless body.
As she retrieves the scroll from the fallen pigeon, her search reveals the letter, hidden on Helene's person. Your true identity is laid bare.
Afterward, Nolaine drags you into the interrogation room. The door closes. There is only darkness, and the promise of endless torture.

You choose Marlo. The more you think about it, the more his anger feels performative—too sudden, too convenient. It could very well be a trap. He might have already planned to kill Horne in the chaos.

speaker: Hilda
content: Mm, a logical deduction. I'll have a word with Marlo later.

speaker: Hilda
content: That will be all for today. Thank you for your cooperation, Mr. ${PlayerName}. You're free to go now.
female_content: That will be all for today. Thank you for your cooperation, Ms. ${PlayerName}. You're free to go now.

content: You step back into the corridor, drawing a deep breath to steady your nerves after the conversation with Hilda.
The corridor is silent and empty now. Through the window, a gentle rain mists the glass, carrying the sweet, petrichor scent of damp earth into the still air.

speaker: Edward
content: Officer ${PlayerName}! How did it go? I hope Hilda didn't give you a hard time.
...It seems you're not alone after all.

speaker: Chief
content: She just apologized for startling me. It was fine... Where is everyone else?

speaker: Edward
content: After what happened, no one wanted to stay in the hall. They've all moved to the dining hall in the annex. Here, let me take you there.

options: Were you waiting here for me?
No need, I can find my way there.

speaker: Edward
content: Of course I was. I was really worried about you, Officer.

speaker: Edward
content: Hilda's room is—gkkt. A place where people tend to lose their heads.

speaker: Edward
content: She calls it "questioning," but let's be honest, it's an interrogation. Rumor has it her closet doesn't hold clothes, but a full set of... professional tools.

speaker: Edward
content: Most people are terrified of being summoned there. It's a genuine relief to see you come out in one piece.

speaker: Option
options: You really don't need to act this way with me.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not some high-ranking official. I don't have the kind of power you might think.

speaker: Edward
content: Please, don't say that! In my eyes, you're the most capable and reasonable person I've ever met. My admiration is sincere.

speaker: Edward
content: Once I'm done here, I'm going to request a transfer from this backwater DisCity. I want to return to the metropoles and apply to join your Mania Countermeasure Center. When the time comes, maybe you could... mention my name?

speaker: Edward
content: I don't want to be a spy anymore. I want a job where I can be proud of who I am!
The raw sincerity on his face catches you off guard, leaving you almost lost for words.

speaker: Chief
content: Like I said, my influence is limited... but I'll remember what you've asked. If I get the chance, I'll put in a word for you.

speaker: Chief
content: But if you never wanted this life, why become a spy in the first place...?

speaker: Edward
content: Haha... Well, I've always been... unremarkable. To most people, I was practically invisible. Teachers would skip my name during roll call. I was always the one overlooked. For a long time, I thought that was just my lot in life.

speaker: Edward
content: Then one day, Mr. Manphist came to our school. And he... he picked me. Can you imagine what that feels like? For someone who's always been invisible to finally be seen? It was incredible. So I followed him to the agent academy and became a spy.

speaker: Edward
content: Mr. Manphist said I was a natural. That people just look right through me. I can be practically standing right next to them, eavesdropping, and they'd never know I was there. It let me accomplish things others couldn't.
In your mind, something suddenly clicks into place.
(The three photos flash past.)

<color=#fb9259>I was a natural. That people just look right through me. I can be practically standing right next to them, eavesdropping, and they'd never know I was there. It let me accomplish things others couldn't.</color>
You stare at Edward, frozen. He meets your gaze with a smile.
But it's all wrong. Gone is the humble, meek man from before.
Bam!
A nearby door crashes open. You try to run, but Edward slams into you from behind, driving the air from your lungs as you hit the floor.

speaker: Edward
content: Since you've seen through me... I suppose I have no choice left.
Something thin and sharp—a fishing line—whips around your neck. He yanks from behind, and it instantly slices into your flesh.
You thrash, but every movement only tightens the garrote. Your breath comes in ragged, useless gasps. You claw blindly behind you, reaching for Edward's arms, but your strength is already failing.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you... the mole...?

speaker: Edward
content: Oh, no. You've got it all wrong. I'm not the mole...
Edward pauses for a single, terrifying moment. Then he pulls harder. You can even hear a soft, sickening crunch in your throat.

speaker: Edward
content: But it told me I could be!
Warmth floods your neck. Blood.
The world grays out, details dissolving into a smear of nothing. Your final, gurgling pleas are a small, pathetic sound, lost against the corridor's chill and the rain's steady, mocking hiss.
Darkness takes you.
ENDING 6
Option B: No need, I can find my way there.

speaker: Edward
content: Oh... I see... My apologies, that was overstepping.

speaker: Edward
content: Of course, Officer ${PlayerName}. You're welcome to go on ahead...
He retreats half a step, a flicker of disappointment in his eyes, yet his polite smile remains.
But the moment you pass him, a sudden rush of air whips past the back of your head.
(Black Screen)
Thud!

speaker: Edward
content: ...Tch. Putting on airs, are we? You should have taken the easy way when offered.

speaker: Edward
content: Hand you over to those DisCity people, and I'm home free.
Your legs buckle. The ground rushes up to meet you, and as your vision tunnels into nothing, someone grips your ankles, pulling you into a dark, cold corner.

speaker: Chief
content: Surely you realize how vital an "anomalous power expert" is to the city-state right now. And you'd risk turning me into a vegetable for a hunch?

speaker: Chief
content: Think carefully. Can you afford to take that risk?
Hilda freezes mid-motion, her gaze turning inward in brief contemplation.
In the end, she puts the syringe down.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Then prove it to me.

speaker: Chief
content: What?

speaker: Hilda
content: Since you insist you're an anomalous power expert, demonstrate this so-called "expertise" of yours.
You want to present your evidence, to reason with her, but you already attempted that the moment you entered the LINK system... Here, your shackles hold no power.
You can only watch as she slowly removes her gloves. Each step she takes toward you is measured, deliberate, and final.

speaker: Hilda
content: What's wrong? Afraid? Shouldn't an "expert" have methods to regulate this anomalous power?

speaker: Hilda
content: You've been speaking with me all this time, yet you failed to detect the power I possess. That alone is suspicious. So if you have any way to prove yourself, use it on me. Now.

speaker: Hilda
content: Otherwise, you will die.
The red gloves come off, revealing her bone-white fingers. Delicate, gilt patterns trace their way across her skin as Mania—a flowing, liquid light—gathers in her palms.
The patterns resemble Aurum Secretum, yet they are alien, ones you've never seen.
Hilda doesn't care for your hesitation. She grabs your wrist and locks her fingers with yours, hard.
In an instant, black spikes erupt through both your palms. You feel the cool, rigid texture of her fingers a moment before the true agony hits: the violent invasion of her Mania into your veins.
You grit your teeth and endure.
A soft sigh escapes her. Her face is a mask, but her grip tightens.
A second, more brutal wave of Mania shatters through your hands. This time, it brings not just pain, but a cacophony of shrieking echoes that floods your mind, wracking your body with tremors.

speaker: Chief
content: Mmph...!
As your legs buckle, she catches you. Through the blinding pain, you see her gaze soften, then harden into unmistakable disappointment.

speaker: Hilda
content: See? You're still lying.

speaker: Hilda
content: You have no ability to control the anomalous power... When confronted with it, all you can do is endure the pain.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now then, I want you to tell me very carefully... who are you, really?
Clank.
The world swims. You collapse, overturning the basin of soaking documents. As crimson-stained papers drift down around you, your fading vision catches the writing Edward left behind—
(Flashback filter)
[In the car]

speaker: Edward
content: A spy's identity is usually a fabrication, of course. But to make a falsehood convincing... that requires a certain "technique."

speaker: Edward
content: My preferred method is what I call "double-layering." I present the target with an initial identity. Something simple, a little too clean, almost easy to see through. Then, I subtly guide them to become suspicious, to investigate on their own.

speaker: Edward
content: The more little discrepancies they dig up, the more they trust the "truth" they've uncovered for themselves. Set up the pieces just right, then... you're all set.
(Filter ends) [Black Screen]
So, Edward never intended the "anomalous power expert" to be your "true" identity. It was merely the first layer of a deception.
He must have known you were a fraud and that Hilda would see through it. His solution was to embed a second, backup identity directly into the files.
You can't tell if the bastard meant to set you up or save you. The only thing that matters now is the document before your eyes. You burn every word, every detail, into your mind.
Next time... you will absolutely...
You grip Helene's hand tightly as you both follow the guard evacuating toward the far end of the manor.

speaker: Helene
content: Wh-where are we going?!

speaker: Guard
content: Stop talking and keep up!
The world shudders without cease, and soon, the thick, choking smoke swallows the entire corridor.
The relentless thunder of explosions confirms it: the main building is rigged to blow.
Helene's hand is a vise of terror in yours, her nails biting into your palm.
Her progress is hobbled by her heels. The faint shapes of the group ahead gradually vanish into the gloom as the two of you stumble through a hellscape of crumbling stone.
Now is the moment. This is the perfect cover to steal the deadly letter from her grasp.
You feign an injury, dropping to the ground, but your plan backfires instantly. Helene directly trips over your body and stumbles past.

speaker: Helene
content: Aaahhh!
The sharp point of her heel digs viciously into your side. You hear a sickening crack as your ribs protest.
...Internal bleeding. Probably.

speaker: Helene
content: ${PlayerName}! My goodness, ${PlayerName}, are you all right?!
Her voice is frantic. She crouches down, her hands fluttering over your body as you gasp, fighting for air.
Just then...
(Red flash + gunshot)
Helene collapses. No cry, no final word. Just a silent, heavy thud against the floor.
You clutch the searing pain in your chest. Thick, acrid smoke and blooming flames swarm your vision.
Through the shimmering inferno, a dark silhouette stands firm, raising a gun toward you.

speaker: Raspy Voice
content: Long live DisCity!
(Black Screen)
(Red flash + gunshot)
The exhaustion from the fire, the fleeing, and the horrors you've witnessed has pushed you to your absolute limit, both in body and mind.
Tonight is not the night.
The military cot feels impossibly soft. Almost instantly, you are pulled down into a deep, dreamless sleep.

speaker: Unknown Voice
content: ...So your identity was fake all along.

speaker: Unknown Voice
content: Then you must be the mole. Die now!
(Sound of knife stabbing flesh + red flash)
Nolaine reads your intention, and her blade is the answer to your movement. It pierces you as you complete your turn.
(Stabbing sound + gunshot + red flash)
Together, you crumple, your blood mingling in separate, dark pools.

speaker: Nolaine
content: Haha... Hehe... You... really are... the mole...

speaker: Nolaine
content: ...Hilda... you're... safe... now...
Her draw is a blur of motion, a single, precise shot shattering your wrist before you even steady your aim.
As white-hot pain lances up your arm, you dimly recall how she has indeed demonstrated her exceptional marksmanship earlier today.
Of course... you never... stood a chance...
(Fade to red + Black Screen)

speaker: Hilda
content: I really hoped... it wasn't you...

speaker: Hilda
content: I see. The photograph does indeed show Huck passing an object to Horne. He is a plausible suspect.

speaker: Hilda
content: Moving forward, I will handle the situation with Huck "discreetly."

speaker: Hilda
content: That will be all for today. Thank you for your cooperation, Mr. ${PlayerName}. You're free to go now.
female_content: That will be all for today. Thank you for your cooperation, Ms. ${PlayerName}. You're free to go now.

content: [Scene Change: Corridor]
You step back into the corridor, drawing a deep breath to steady your nerves after the conversation with Hilda.
The corridor is silent and empty now. Through the window, a gentle rain mists the glass, carrying the sweet, petrichor scent of damp earth into the still air.

speaker: Edward
content: Officer ${PlayerName}! How did it go? I hope Hilda didn't give you a hard time.
...It seems you're not alone after all.

speaker: Chief
content: She just apologized for startling me. It was fine... Where is everyone else?

speaker: Edward
content: After what happened, no one wanted to stay in the hall. They've all moved to the dining hall in the annex. Here, let me take you there.

options: Were you waiting here for me?
No need, I can find my way there.

speaker: Edward
content: Of course I was. I was really worried about you, Officer.

speaker: Edward
content: Hilda's room is—gkkt. A place where people tend to lose their heads.

speaker: Edward
content: She calls it "questioning," but let's be honest, it's an interrogation. Rumor has it her closet doesn't hold clothes, but a full set of... professional tools.

speaker: Edward
content: Most people are terrified of being summoned there. It's a genuine relief to see you come out in one piece.

speaker: Option
options: You really don't need to act this way with me.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not some high-ranking official. I don't have the kind of power you might think.

speaker: Edward
content: Please, don't say that! In my eyes, you're the most capable and reasonable person I've ever met. My admiration is sincere.

speaker: Edward
content: Once I'm done here, I'm going to request a transfer from this backwater DisCity. I want to return to the metropoles and apply to join your Mania Countermeasure Center. When the time comes, maybe you could... mention my name?

speaker: Edward
content: I don't want to be a spy anymore. I want a job where I can be proud of who I am!
The raw sincerity on his face catches you off guard, leaving you almost lost for words.

speaker: Chief
content: Like I said, my influence is limited... but I'll remember what you've asked. If I get the chance, I'll put in a word for you.

speaker: Chief
content: But if you never wanted this life, why become a spy in the first place...?

speaker: Edward
content: Haha... Well, I've always been... unremarkable. To most people, I was practically invisible. Teachers would skip my name during roll call. I was always the one overlooked. For a long time, I thought that was just my lot in life.

speaker: Edward
content: Then one day, Mr. Manphist came to our school. And he... he picked me. Can you imagine what that feels like? For someone who's always been invisible to finally be seen? It was incredible. So I followed him to the agent academy and became a spy.

content: Mr. Manphist said I was a natural. That people just look right through me. I can be practically standing right next to them, eavesdropping, and they'd never know I was there. It let me accomplish things others couldn't.
