The moment the word "lives" leaves her lips, the General finally explodes into action! Her halberd flies from her grip like a furious dragon, ripping through the suffocating air with an ear-splitting shriek as it hurtles straight toward the curtained seat!

The next second, a cold gleam flashes from behind the gauze curtains, the fragrance of plum blossoms filling the air as invisible energy ripples outward like waves. This "internal force" seems as pure as that of the other martial heroes present, but the shackles detect more noticeable fluctuations amid the turbulent air...

speaker: Chief
content: S-Class?
The halberd never reaches the curtains, struck back mid-flight by a single petal shot from behind the veil.
Ma Ling catches her violently shaking halberd, her hand aching numbly.

speaker: Chief
content: She hasn't even shown herself, yet a single petal carries so much force... This manor master's power is on a completely different level from these "martial heroes." Could that codex really enhance special powers?

When has the mighty General Invincible ever endured such humiliation? Even as you process what just happened, she locks eyes with the Scholar, twists her body once more, and defiantly thrusts her spear forward!

The flying petals strike again, but the General seems to have expected this, twisting her waist to dodge aside. So the assault with her halberd was merely a feint. The real killing blow comes from behind her.
The silver needles between the Scholar's fingers have already been launched amid the earlier chaos.

In an instant, the silver needles pierce half an inch into the gauze curtains! Just as the attack is about to succeed, the next moment, tremendous energy erupts like a volcano, blasting forth from behind the veil.

The tightly sealed doors and windows burst open, as howling winds of the blizzard pour into the hall! Candles flicker throughout the room. Everyone shields their face from the sudden onslaught of snow.
When they manage to open their eyes again, they see that the silver needles have somehow reversed direction, hurtling back toward them with even greater speed and ferocity.

speaker: Xu Shen
content: Get back! The needles are poisoned!
Thanks to his timely warning, the silver needles hit the floorboards at their feet like lightning bolts.

This was clearly a killing strike meant to take lives. Everyone looks up toward the manor master's seat, where the glowing snow highlights that slender silhouette. Still seated, she seems poised, as if she didn't even move at all.

speaker: Xu Shen
content: The manor master's divine skills are truly unparalleled. It seems the rumors of your serious sickness are simply untrue... In that case, we shall humbly seek instruction from you as fellow martial artists. Please forgive any rudeness on our part.

speaker: Ma Ling
content: Enough talk! This is exactly why I came, to witness such marvelous weapons and martial techniques! She has slighted us so, and I'm not one who can endure such treatment! Then let me be the first to test just how strong you are!
With that, Ma Ling surges forward once more! This time it's no feint. She channels her immense energy, using her body as a shield to ram straight into the gauze curtains!
Seeing her courageous act, the others hesitate no longer.

Folding fan. Palm strikes. Hidden weapons. Even haunting strings of musical notes... Various attacks erupt simultaneously from every direction, converging into a deadly torrent that rushes straight toward the plain white gauze curtains.
Sensing danger, you start looking for cover, but notice Shuang'er frozen in place, her wide eyes staring blankly into the air.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't just stand there!

speaker: Shuang'er
content: ...Wow, my first time seeing so many masters! Invincible iron steeds cleave through a rain of silver; peacock plumes bloom, as harp notes make hearts quiver. What a gathering of great heroes...
Before she completes her sentence, you suddenly yank her under the table.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Ouch! What are you doing?

speaker: Chief
content: Trying to stay alive.
Sure enough, just as the wave of attacks is about to reach the curtains, a ring of pale green energy suddenly blooms from behind it, accompanied by a low rumble like muffled thunder.

All the incoming attacks are sent back along their original paths by this overwhelming, irresistible force, crashing into the surrounding walls with even greater intensity. The entire meeting hall shakes violently as utensils overturn and wine spills everywhere.

The table you're hiding beneath gets struck by the aftershock of a reflected palm strike, splitting open a half-foot crack. You and Shuang'er hunker down as low as possible, feeling the floor trembling continuously beneath you.

General Ma Ling, who bears the brunt of the attack, goes flying backward like a kite with a severed string, crashing heavily into the wall. Princess Ji's wheelchair gets pushed by the shockwave, sliding straight back before slamming into a pillar. The Scholar's and the Golden Brocade's faces turn deathly pale, each coughing up a mouthful of blood.

Only the Immortal Healer Yin Yansheng, who had slipped behind a massive pillar like a nimble fish the moment chaos broke out, now pokes half his face out. His eyes show no fear, but instead gleam with almost fanatical excitement.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: Marvelous... marvelous! This energy is unadulterated, intense, yet controlled. It clearly belongs to someone whose vitality has reached its peak, yet remains perfectly restrained!

The Healer looks ready to risk getting closer for another look, but just as he pokes his head out, a vicious palm strike comes from behind, whistling past his nose tip. With a sharp hiss, it leaves four gruesome claw marks, each an inch deep, in the tough sandalwood pillar.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: ...The blow feels bone-chillingly cold and embodies the savage gust of the mountains. This isn't from the girl behind the curtain...?

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: Wonderful, yet another new guest! Just how many treasures is this manor hiding today?
You look toward the hall's entrance upon hearing this, but there's no newcomer outside the door, only swirling snow everywhere.

speaker: Guest on the Beams
content: Hey, hey! Where are you looking? I'm up here... Tsk, I'm talking to you two hiding under the table!

speaker: Guest on the Beams
content: Got any more wine? I've drunk the entire jar while watching you all grappling around... Burp!

speaker: Guest on the Beams
content: Forget it, I can tell you two don't have any say around here. Hey, you, the manor master! Got any fine wine left? I need a couple of sips to wet my throat!
The entire hall falls silent. After that intense brawl, the heroes are still trying to catch their breath. At this moment, only the person behind the curtains can still respond calmly.

speaker: Jichuan
content: If you wish to drink, Mountain Lord, please help yourself.

speaker: Jichuan
content: It's just that my manor's wine has quite a bite to it. I'm afraid it might not suit an uninvited guest's palate.
[Animated CG: Flying Wine Cup]

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Oh, I don't care much about the wine's taste! As long as there are enough delicious snacks to go with it!

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: I can see you've terrorized them properly. The show probably can't go on now. How boring is that? Hey...

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Why don't you show yourself and spar with me? It'll be fun!
As the Mountain Lord speaks, she springs forward at the curtains. Her palm cuts the air, only to be deflected as the fabric ripples alive.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Now that's interesting!
She curves her fingers like claws, lunging once more toward the figure behind the curtains!
This time, the curtains remain still.
Because behind them...
There is no one.
[Meeting Hall]

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Ha! Your little voice-echoing trick with that fake shadow might fool these weaklings, but you can't fool my nose. I knew it from the start—there was never a "tenth person" here.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Well, since you've already gathered so many actors for this show... I'll stay to finish this wine! And I'm definitely sticking around for the entertainment!
Declaring that, the Mountain Lord picks up her cup of wine and drains it in a single gulp.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: You're indeed quite generous, little manor master. You heeded my request and brought in the best snack to go with the wine, haha!
Cheerfully, she sniffs the lingering aroma in her wine cup, then flips around and sprawls back onto the beams casually. But everyone can tell the "snack" she mentioned can't be anything pleasant.

Boom! A thunderous roar explodes from the mountain ridge, shaking the ground and swaying the building frame. The sky suddenly darkens, not from sunset nor clouds, but from the massive curtain of snow raised by the avalanche, like ten thousand white horses stampeding down from the mountaintop.

The entire sky is devoured by the rolling white waves. The sun vanishes rapidly behind the wall of snow. It's as if it has gone from day to night in the matter of just a few breaths. The manor seems to have plunged into a bottomless abyss of snow.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Since you all insist on claiming this power... then come and take it with your own hands.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I shall await you in the heart of this snowstorm. Come bearing your desires... treading upon blood.

Everyone barely manages to compose themselves from the shock of the avalanche before rushing outside the hall and climbing up to survey their surroundings. Everywhere around the manor is completely blocked by snow. As far as the eye can see, there are only thick white walls that have swallowed the paths, trapping the entire manor in an abyss.
You remember the couplet at the doors...

speaker: Chief
content: Hero bones, lone manor?
You catch a rusty stench drifting from the depths of the manor, cutting through the wind and snow.

speaker: Chief
content: It's the smell of blood.
[Small CG: Dead Body 1]

Jiewubei's corpulent body lies slumped beneath the guest room's folding screen, murky drool trickling from the corner of his mouth as the smell of alcohol fills the air. A half-finished jar of wine sits by his side, along with several dishes of meat that appear completely untouched.

But upon closer inspection, what fills those dishes isn't food at all. Piled there are the internal organs he spat out: heart, liver, spleen, lungs... all wrapped in mucus and streaks of blood, their shapes still faintly recognizable.
Beside Jiewubei, a note in crimson ink lies half-drenched in a pool of blood:

Red Plum Denunciation I Heavens' mighty gifts squandered at a feast. Can your gluttonous hearts discern the grease? Jade plates brim with oaths long broken; red plums shall witness you feast upon your own organs.
[Guest room]
Late at night, snow falls in silence.
You searched the entire manor but found no path down the mountain. Even more eerily, the manor master seems to have vanished without a trace.
The group turned the place upside down but found nothing, so they had no choice but to settle in the guest rooms for the night.
Schorl in your arms remains silent. The fire burns quietly in the brazier, casting light on Shuang'er as she sits hugging her knees.

You give the larger, softer bed to Shuang'er, but she simply stares wide-eyed toward the window in a daze. All the manor's guest rooms share the same layout, so the folding screen by the window is identical to the one in Jiewubei's room.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I... I can't sleep. Every time I close my eyes, all I see is Master Wubei... cut up into pieces, laid out on the table like some kind of dish...
The scene was simply horrifying. Even you hadn't witnessed anything like it in DisCity, let alone an innocent girl like Shuang'er. You use the gauze curtains as a divider to shield her from the view.

speaker: Chief
content: Stop thinking about that. Come closer to the fire. Once you're warmed up, you'll be able to fall asleep. Maybe by dawn, the snow will have gotten lighter.
You carefully check the door bolt once more.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't worry, I'm keeping watch. No matter how elusive that manor master is, she won't be able to get in here.
Shuang'er seems to relax a little and obediently moves to lie down on the bed.

This bed is so much bigger and softer than the kang bed back in Ping'an Town. This room alone could shelter dozens of the town's children from the snow. Yet she's in no mood to enjoy such a "luxurious" place.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Hey... this Northsnow Manor... is quite different from those famous places we've seen in martial world storybooks, right?

speaker: Chief
content: How is it different?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: In the storybooks, a master's retreat is usually a place where respectable elders greet guests amiably through ethereal mists and offer them martial arts teachings... A place where everyone drinks wine together under the moon, sharing tales of the martial world...
The fire crackles. Shuang'er curls up on the bed, wrapped in a thin blanket with only half her pale face visible.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Earlier, at the foot of the mountain... I was telling tales of Guo Liqing crushing villains with his palm strikes, and of Qi Aofeng breaching fortresses with his sword. The children's eyes lit up as they listened. We all thought a visit to these famous places would be such a wonderful, awe-inspiring adventure.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: But now lying here, what keeps haunting my mind is Master Wubei's final moments... and those heroes' ice-cold stares.

speaker: Chief
content: I actually think the martial world here isn't so different from the one in your storybooks. There are heroes, martial arts, conflicts, and banquets in your tales. The same things are all present here.
Shuang'er pokes her head out, looking somewhat surprised.

speaker: Chief
content: It's because in stories, we only keep the good parts. They glorify desire, hesitation, and the struggles of unfulfilled dreams, so people can focus on those honorable duels and heroic promises. After all, stories need to be satisfying and uplifting, right?

speaker: Chief
content: Even though certain parts of the stories are made up, the children still get all excited when they hear these tales. You... Ahem, we martial arts enthusiasts feel the urge to act virtuously ourselves after hearing such stories... All of that is real.
You add a piece of charcoal to the brazier, stirring up a few sparks.

speaker: Chief
content: If the blood-soaked martial world you saw today feels like this endless snowstorm, then think of the martial world you've always believed in as this fire.

speaker: Chief
content: They both exist here.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Are you saying we can still see the good side of the martial world?
She lifts her head, her eyes sparkling in the firelight.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes. Maybe... even better and more captivating than this fire! Something like... a delicious drumstick?

speaker: Chief
content: It's not the whole reality, but it's definitely part of reality. As long as we believe it exists, we can always find it here.
Shuang'er nods, then, as if remembering something, pulls out several small medicine bottles from her pocket. She counts the pills one by one against the light, then swallows them all.

You know she isn't in good health, but this is the first time you've witnessed her downing all the pills. This martial hero gathering and the rumors about the codex might truly be the opportunity she's long hoped for to transform her physical condition.

speaker: Chief
content: Whatever can help you achieve your dream of becoming a great hero is definitely out there somewhere, waiting for you.
Shuang'er stares at you for a long moment, then purses her lips, though the corners of her mouth quietly curve into the faintest smile.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: You... can be such a fool sometimes.
She finally relaxes, stretching out her limbs and embracing the gradually warming candlelight.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: The snow keeps getting heavier... I wonder if we'll even be able to go down the mountain tomorrow. I miss Auntie Wang's beggar's chicken. You know, when you hold that dish, it warms your palms and feels so real. You can tell just from the smell that it'll fill your belly...
She turns over to face the wall, and soon her breathing becomes long and steady. In the dim light, her frame seems especially small and frail.
You blow out the candle. The room falls completely silent.

Those things you said to comfort Shuang'er aren't lies. If the power of heroes truly works like that of seers, that regardless of innate talent, they can gain power through being admired by people and accumulating good deeds, then it would be tremendously beneficial for Northwild, Eastia, and any place suffering from disasters.

speaker: Chief
content: But if there really is such a foolproof method of cultivation, then what would be the point of the Aurum Secretum smuggling that we've been investigating?

You clearly remember the terrifying power that manor master unleashed at the banquet. She receives no admiration or offerings from the people, nor has she done any widely celebrated heroic deeds. Where does her power come from then? What exactly is she trying to accomplish by creating this prison of snow?

The codex, the divine techniques... Your thoughts drift to these mysteries as you fall half asleep. From the small bed nearby comes Shuang'er's mumbled sleep talk, intermittent and mixed with some soft gulping noise.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Drumstick... smells so good... Auntie Wang... I didn't steal the food... Who said they saw me do it?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: No, it didn't happen if there's no witness... Ah, you might think... the smell comes from the stove, but what if...

speaker: Shuang'er
content: ...The food has already been served at the table?
You suddenly snap awake and open your eyes in the darkness.

Since the start, no one has "seen" the manor master. That enticing "aroma," that "feast" hanging over everyone's heads, those manipulating hands waiting from behind the curtains... couldn't they actually have been present at the banquet?
[Somewhere in the Manor]
This night, no one at Northsnow Manor sleeps peacefully.
Shen Wanchou hasn't undressed at all. He paces back and forth restlessly beside the brocade-covered bed, his expensive cloud-patterned boots grinding messy tracks into the carpet.

The exquisitely carved glass lamp he brought sits on the desk, casting light on his brooding face. From time to time, he walks to the window and shoves the immovable frame, then glances with disgust at the brazier in the corner, provided by the manor and, in his view, utterly crude.

speaker: Shen Wanchou
content: What a heaven-forsaken place, and the snow never stops... Tch, they can't even afford to use silverbone charcoal? How stingy.
He yanks the bell-pull beside his bed to summon the servants, but gets no response. In his fury, he rips the decorative tassel off.

speaker: Shen Wanchou
content: Hmph, Manor Master Jiang, this treasure of yours better not be counterfeit. I would hate to have endured this awful blizzard for nothing.
[Somewhere in the Manor]

An eerie green light flickers in the darkness. Yin Yansheng sits cross-legged on a cushion. Before him spread his old turtle shell, which he always brings with him, and several polished ancient coins.
His gaunt fingers, dipped in a strange powder, draw twisted symbols on the floor. He mutters something under his breath while his cloudy eyes dart rapidly in their sunken sockets.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: An assault from the north while darkness lurks in the southeast... I see, this bloodshed is no new feud, but an old debt... Hehe, an old debt that was never fully repaid nor concealed, and now the snow has led it to us...
He suddenly snatches up the ancient coins, brings them close to his nose, and inhales deeply. His face shows both excitement and fear.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: This smell... I know it! Many years ago, in... in that graveyard. The same heavy snow, the same pungent stench of blood... No, no...

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: Back! All back! This manor... it's waiting to claim us...
[Somewhere in the Manor]
A solitary lamp flickers in the wind. The snow bears two long wheel tracks, and at their end, Ji Guining sits alone in quiet contemplation.

Before her sits a messy mound of snow with a broken branch stuck into it, serving as makeshift incense. She presses her palms together, bows her head, and quietly recites prayers. Her expression is filled with sorrow, tears glistening at the corners of her eyes.

speaker: Ji Guining
content: Jiewubei, if your spirit harbors any unresolved grievances, speak to me. How did the manor master claim your life from such a distance? Tell me, and I shall avenge you.
[Somewhere in the Manor]
"Clang! Clang!"
The rhythmic, piercing sound of metal scraping cuts through the silence of the night.
Ma Ling takes a wide stance, the heavy black halberd laid flat on her knee. She holds a whetstone in her hand, running it along the halberd's blade again and again.
With each drag of the whetstone, the muscles in her shoulders and back tense, ready to unleash an explosive blow at any moment.

speaker: Ma Ling
content: Don't you want to take my life? Then don't lurk in the dark like a coward! Come out and face me in a proper fight!
[Somewhere in the Manor]
The feeble candle flame casts Xu Shen's frantic silhouette on the wall, his shadow shaky and twisted.

His face is deathly pale, cold sweat beading at his temples and nose. His breathing comes in short, rapid gasps. His hands move hurriedly and jerkily to stuff his clothes into his bag. As he packs, he strains to listen for any noise behind the door. The slightest sound can make him jump.

Something suddenly occurs to him, and he lunges toward the candlelight, pulling out a piece of paper. The paper is badly crumpled, with several lines written on it. A copy of that blood-stained denunciation. He reads the text once more.

speaker: Xu Shen
content: This place isn't safe... I can't wait until dawn... Now, I have to leave now...

He clutches his belongings tightly to his chest and curls up in the shadows behind the door. His eyes are fixed unblinkingly on the window as if vengeful spirits might emerge at any moment to claim his life.
[Somewhere in the Manor]

Unperturbed by the fearful atmosphere beneath her, Xiaofeng has fetched herself another jar of wine and half a cold roasted chicken. Ignoring the freezing cold, she sprawls comfortably in the snow on the rooftop, watching the manor's unfolding drama with keen interest, her hands greasy and her face flushed from her drink.
Once she has tossed the last bit of chicken bone into her mouth and crunched it loudly, she sighs contentedly, raising her wine jar in a toast to the invisible stage below.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Fine wine for a fine spectacle! Another cup!
Lights gradually go out throughout the manor. In the darkness, a spider slips into the chaos...
You jolt awake in the bone-chilling cold.
The guest room is dimly lit in the early morning, with freezing wind constantly seeping through the window cracks. Your limbs are frozen and stiff, your throat dry and parched.
You sit up and look around. The room's furnishings remain undisturbed, and a few dark embers still glow in the brazier.
You instinctively look toward the bed across from you. But it's empty, the bedding carelessly pushed to one corner.
No response... The horrific scene with Jiewubei from last night instantly flashes across your mind.

speaker: Chief
content: No...
You throw off your covers and hurry over. You then discover Shuang'er hiding in the far corner of her bed, curled up in a ball.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: So cold... Don't... mm... don't take my blanket...
You clearly overreacted. Seeing Shuang'er drooling in her sleep, you finally breathe a sigh of relief and tuck the blanket she kicked off back around her.

speaker: Chief
content: After causing such a commotion last night, would the manor master really just let us sleep peacefully until dawn?

You check the guest room once more, and indeed find nothing out of place, yet that unsettling feeling that something is wrong refuses to fade. Just as you're lost in thought, a piercing scream echoes from the courtyard.
The snow has gotten even heavier than yesterday. By the time you trudge to the manor's front yard, the martial heroes have already gathered in a circle.

You push through the crowd and take in the scene before you. The manor's main entrance has been completely buried under snow overnight, but now, amid those heavy drifts, a guardian lion carved from snow has appeared out of nowhere.

The guardian lion crouches menacingly before the entrance, dark red liquid seeping from beneath its body. Around the lion, you notice a wicker basket, from which scrolls, stationery, and several pieces of plain clothing have spilled out.

speaker: Chief
content: These are the belongings of Xu Shen, the Scholar.

Red Plum Denunciation II Footprints stir the dust when the ink is still warm. How can a scholar's scrolls shroud a fleeing form? The guardian lion seizes your very soul. Red stains upon the steps, a plain coffin stands in the cold.
You follow the conspicuous, wide footprints in the snow all the way into the manor's pine forest, but the trail vanishes abruptly in a clearing.

The footprints are clearly shaped and deeply imprinted, yet they neither continue nor change direction ahead in the snow. Your target definitely didn't go far. They might even be using the terrain to hide somewhere nearby, watching you.
Suddenly, a sound comes from ahead to the left. The soft snapping of a dead branch broken by the weight of the snow.
You immediately look up and catch sight of a pine branch trembling gently. You steady your breathing and move closer toward that shadowy part of the forest.

speaker: Chief
content: You have fled here after someone just died in the manor. Are you too afraid to show yourself?
No one answers. But in the shadows to your right, a blurred silhouette streaks past the trees at incredible speed, stirring up a sharp whistle of wind.

speaker: Chief
content: I've already read the Red Plum Denunciation. With parts one and two complete, who is your next target?

You raise your voice with feigned casualness while you activate the shackles in your palm. You carefully weigh the risk of exposing your identity as you back against an old pine, using its trunk for cover. The sound of rushing wind grows more urgent, drawing closer.

speaker: Chief
content: All this skulking around... Are you scared of getting exposed? Or am I the third target?
Almost immediately, that sharp whistle of wind suddenly erupts behind you!
[Shackles]

You throw yourself against the tree trunk instantly, using the cascade of snow as cover before spinning around and unleashing the piercing spikes from your shackles. But as you turn, you finally get a clear look at your attacker.
Take this!
You snuff out the shackles narrowly. But through the swirling snow, a wooden stick is already being swung down square on your head.

speaker: Chief
content: Ouch...

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Huh?! What are you doing here?

speaker: Chief
content: I'm just about to ask you that. Shouldn't you be sleeping in your room? Why did you come here?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I was trying to! I was dozing off when I suddenly spotted a suspicious shadow moving past my window!

speaker: Shuang'er
content: When I went to check on you, you were gone! I was worried something might happen to a scrawny creature like you, so I rushed out to find and save you!
You touch your forehead. Surprisingly, it hasn't swollen up. You're not in the mood to debate who's actually scrawnier, given how weak that hit was, but you catch the crucial detail in her words.

speaker: Chief
content: A suspicious shadow? There was just an incident at the manor, and all the martial heroes were gathered in the front yard. What did this shadow look like?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Something big and... furry, moving really fast. It looked like... like a big cat? No, no, way bigger than a cat. Those legs were as thick as the diameter of a bowl...
Thick as the diameter of a bowl... Doesn't that match the size of the tracks you've been following?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Oh, right!
Her eyes suddenly light up as she points toward the snowy ground.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Just like this!
There in the snow lies a set of deep tracks left by a beast, the menacing marks clearly carved by some razor-sharp claws.

speaker: Chief
content: But the footprints ended right at this spot when I followed them here... Wait, something's wrong. Move!

Too late. The drift of snow beside Shuang'er suddenly explodes as a white figure leaps out! When you realize what's happening, she's already been swept away, carving a deep, messy furrow through the snow that stretches yards into the distance.
At the end of the furrow stands a massive, fierce white tiger.

The tiger is abnormally huge, its shoulders and back bulky like a mountain. It holds its head slightly lowered, gripping the back of Shuang'er's collar in its jaws, its razor-sharp fangs mere inches from her throat.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: What... what is this thing?!

speaker: Chief
content: Don't move... Keep your breathing steady. Don't provoke it.
You quickly examine the tiger's build and claws, comparing them with the wounds on the second victim and the tracks. Everything matches perfectly.

speaker: Chief
content: I didn't get a chance to tell you earlier. The Scholar is dead, and this second case might be connected to this white tiger. I'm still not sure if this creature here has anything to do with the manor master. So don't make any sudden moves.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Easy for you to say! I'd rather you hadn't told me that...

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Ma! Pa! Auntie Wang! Mountain God! Help me! I don't want to be eaten!

speaker: Chief
content: Quiet! The more you struggle, the fresher and tastier you'll seem, and the sooner it'll eat you.
The little rascal is right. My Meowy has quite the temper, and those claws are not used to handling delicate things. You'd better behave.

A languid, insouciant voice drifts near out of nowhere. You immediately snap to attention, eyes rapidly scanning the surrounding pine forest and snowy slopes, but there's not a soul in sight. You couldn't mistake that familiar accent, but...

speaker: Chief
content: Why would she be here?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I-I-I-I remember you! White Tiger Mountain Lord! Please let me go, good Mountain Lord! May your fortune be as vast as the East Sea and your life as enduring as the Southern Mountains...

You scan your surroundings warily, trying to pinpoint the source of the voice, but Xiaofeng doesn't show herself. Only that teasing voice remains, as if woven into the wind itself, drifting leisurely from every direction.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: It's no use flattering me. There's nothing but snow in this place. My Meowy is still having her growth spurt, and she's been starving. Now that she's finally found herself a nice piece of meat, how could I convince her to let go?

speaker: Chief
content: The Mountain Lord sounds like she has other demands.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Mmm, you get it! I always take a shine to clever ones like you. Alright, I pick you. Entertain me.

speaker: Chief
content: Entertain you? How?

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: The mountain path is completely blocked, and the boredom is killing me. I require some proper entertainment. Spar with me, just three rounds. You win, you can take this little beggar with you.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Wh-what kind of joke is this?! He, he can't do it! Can we play a different game, Mountain Lord? Please, I'm begging you...
female_content: Wh-what kind of joke is this?! She, she can't do it! Can we play a different game, Mountain Lord? Please, I'm begging you...

content: With each breath, the nape of Shuang'er's neck nearly brushes against the tiger's fangs. Her face is deathly pale, yet she strains to turn her head and manages to squeeze out a whisper.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: You can't win against her... We, we can't both die here... You go... Go find help...
There's no help coming. But if the second murder case is truly connected to this Mountain Lord, this might be your closest chance at the truth.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright, I'll entertain you.
Both Shuang'er and the Mountain Lord lurking in the shadows seem taken aback by your answer.

speaker: Chief
content: But I'm sure the Mountain Lord would prefer a fair game. Giving me back this girl you took from me hardly counts as a prize. If I win, I should get some other reward.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Oh? You wish to ask for something? Go ahead, I can be quite generous.

speaker: Chief
content: If I win, tell me everything you know about the Scholar's death.
The figure in the shadows takes a deep breath, clearly satisfied with what you've proposed.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: So you came here following the "copper smell." Well then, I certainly have plenty to tell you.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Come on, Meowy, time for a game!
The tiger's roar shakes the forest. The bet is on.

The white tiger crouches down, then moves so fast she becomes a blur. In an instant, she's already circled to your left, clawing the ground and sending up sprays of snow. Before you can turn around, she bounds to your right, a low growl rumbling in her throat, keeping you trapped within striking distance.
You sink into a half-crouch, shifting your weight to your lower body as your eyes track the tiger's every movement.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Hehe, look at my big kitty, getting all fired up at the sight of fresh prey. So fierce, just like her master!
The Mountain Lord remains hidden in the shadows. As for Shuang'er, the "prize" of this wager, she was tossed up onto a high branch by the tiger before the duel began, now hanging there in the air.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: What are you so smug about? You want to be entertained, yet you don't even dare show yourself! If you like skulking in the dark so much, perhaps you should call yourself the Rat Mountain Lord instead!
Shuang'er is struggling to climb down from the tree when several pine needles whoosh past her and land next to her sleeves. She immediately shrinks back up.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Well, the one doing the fighting isn't complaining! Stay put and keep quiet! What? Think that little rascal might lose?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Are you kidding me? D-do you know who he is? He's... he's the 18th generation disciple of a secret elite swordsman fellowship! He practices the Supreme Sovereign Domination sword technique! You... you should be shaking in fear!
female_content: Are you kidding me? D-do you know who she is? She's... she's the 18th generation disciple of a secret elite swordsman fellowship! She practices the Supreme Sovereign Domination sword technique! You... you should be shaking in fear!

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Oh, give it a rest. That's all you can come up with? Just watch, Meowy will soon obliterate that little rascal...

speaker: Both
content: Huh?
Once they're done bickering, they find that you have already vanished from the clearing.
You're not an idiot. No way you would fight a tiger head-on.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: What a fleet-footed runner... He didn't just abandon you and run off, did he?
female_content: What a fleet-footed runner... She didn't just abandon you and run off, did she?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: What do you know? This is called strategy.
Being hung so high up, from her vantage point, Shuang'er can see you dive into the densest thicket scattered with rocks.
Tigers excel at pouncing on prey on spacious terrain, so you deliberately choose an area full of obstacles.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: That's indeed quite clever, but surely a human can't match the speed of such a majestic beast.
As she says that, a bloodthirsty blow almost reaches your head! You frantically dodge the first strike, but an equally fierce second one quickly follows, aiming straight at your face.
You raise your sword sheath to block the attack, and with a resounding "bang," the impact sends you staggering back several steps, your hand going numb from the shock.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: What... Those are killing blows... What did we ever do to you to deserve this?

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: What's the fun if no blood is drawn? If you really want a reason... Well, you disturbed my sleep. Does that count?
Shuang'er wants to protest, but seeing you in such peril, her anxiety makes her swallow her words.
The white tiger's assault is so violent, forcing you to dodge repeatedly as her powerful claws tear several gashes in the front of your clothes.
But this is what you've been waiting for. As the tiger pounces through the air once more, you duck down and squeeze into the gap between two massive boulders.

Just as the tiger's head is about to get trapped in the gap, crisp rings of a bell cut through the air! The white tiger twists her body unnaturally in mid-air to change direction, and slams her massive paw down, pinning you heavily to the ground.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: A tiger-taming bell? What sort of martial master cheats against opponents like us?!

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: It's not against the rules. Besides, even if it is, I can't read. This round goes to me.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Hey, you on the ground. Do you have a problem with that?
The tiger halts and doesn't try to kill you, obviously holding back. You struggle free from her claws with only minor scrapes.

speaker: Chief
content: You waited until the last moment to use this unique skill. I had all the time to gain an advantage earlier. I shall not complain.
You give Shuang'er a reassuring look and brush the snow off your clothes.

speaker: Chief
content: Let's continue.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: You fought bravely. I won't be holding back in the second round.
The bell rings again, and the tiger stirs once more.

The tiger's attacks are clearly more methodical this time. Its movements are well positioned, while its claws strike with immense force. You recall Yin Yansheng's comment that this Mountain Lord's martial arts embodied the savage gust of the mountains, and you can see it right now.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Such finesse beneath the savagery... Be careful, it won't be so easy to handle this time.

You understand the situation just as well. All that dodging has already exhausted most of your stamina. This round can only be won through strategy. You suddenly change course, no longer running in straight lines, instead weaving quickly around several old pine trees.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Hmm, not bad, lad! I thought you ducked into the trees only to buy time, but you had this move planned out too. Too bad a tiger never misses its pre... Huh?
female_content: Hmm, not bad, lass! I thought you ducked into the trees only to buy time, but you had this move planned out too. Too bad a tiger never misses its pre... Huh?

content: She goes silent abruptly. Throughout the dense forest, rapid knocks echo from all directions, their sources impossible to pinpoint.

You had noticed earlier that many tree trunks were hollowed out by insects and would produce different sounds when struck. Now, hiding in the underbrush, you throw snowballs at the hollow trees. The thuds and cracks echo throughout the area, creating a distracting cacophony.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Was this planned too?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Oh! Tigers are blessed with sharp hearing and keen sight. In the first round, Meowy was a tough opponent when she was acting on her own. But this round, Meowy follows your bell instead, so she's relying on your ears and eyes, Mountain Lord!

speaker: Shuang'er
content: You've said it yourself, Mountain Lord. A human can't match a tiger's speed. And human senses are even worse! No matter what divine hiding skills you have, you're still just a mortal after all!

speaker: Chief
content: Keep explaining and she'll catch on. Stop chattering—give me the staff!
Upon hearing this, Shuang'er immediately tosses her staff down.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Too late. I've figured it out! Meowy, ignore my commands and find him!
female_content: Too late. I've figured it out! Meowy, ignore my commands and find her!

content: The bell stops ringing. The tiger pricks up its ears and pounces fiercely toward some rustling undergrowth. Yet it catches nothing, stumbling comically to one side.
Several pine branches tied to a long staff emerge from the bushes, swishing left and right before being hurled into the distance. Without a second thought, the tiger bounds after the swaying object.
A giant cat teaser you fashioned from Shuang'er's staff.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: A temptation no cat can resist. Even a big cat! Round two goes to us!

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Oh my dear Mountain Lord! After all, you're no match for the mighty alliance of Shuang'er and our young hero—mmmph?
A snowball plugs her mouth precisely.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: What a chatterbox. You're giving me a headache.

speaker: Mountain Lord
content: Do you really think me a mere mortal with dull senses? Today I'll show you little runts what it means to be the Lord of all mountain beasts!
The wind blowing through the forest suddenly stills, and snowflakes tremble to a halt in the air.
You have a bad feeling and grip your sword hilt with both hands, the shackles poised under your sleeve. That hearty yet domineering voice rumbles down from above like muffled thunder.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: First round, smooth, but far from enough power. Second round, plenty of clever tricks, all built on a weak foundation.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Do you want to know the result of the third round?

speaker: Chief
content: Can the Mountain Lord predict the future too?
She sneers, ignoring your provocation.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Third round...
The earth shakes violently, and the world spins! An invisible force hurls you off the ground, then an irresistible pressure crashes down like the sky has collapsed, slamming you hard into the snow!
[Big CG: Tiger Kneading]

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: You are bound to lose.
[Big CG: Tiger Kneading]

The Mountain Lord fights fiercely and squarely, her every move bold and sweeping. It's unlike the cunning traps and treacherous schemes you've seen these past few days. After careful deliberation, you decide not to release your shackles.
By the time the third round ends, you don't even have a chance to get back up.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: So, ready to accept the outcome of our bet?

speaker: Chief
content: You are indeed formidable, Mountain Lord. But do you remember what our actual bet was?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Of course. Best of three, right? If you win, you can ask me anything. If you lose, that little beggar stays to fill my Meowy's stomach...
As she speaks, she points toward the treetop.
[Exit CG]

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hey, where did she go?
Looking down, she sees Shuang'er is bear-hugging the tree trunk, having already climbed most of her way down breathlessly.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Huff... huff... I couldn't... escape while you were watching... but both you and Meowy... were busy just now... I must... seize the chance, right?
Xiaofeng's gaze turns back down at you, still pinned to the ground, and an unexpected hint of appreciation flashes through her eyes.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: A decoy, huh? That was your idea, wasn't it? I must say it's quite clever, but too bad...

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: I'm not letting that happen!
In the blink of an eye, she's already at the base of Shuang'er's tree.
Shuang'er is only a few feet from reaching the ground, but her escape route has been cut off.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: ${PlayerName}, do you... do you think... tigers can climb trees?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Funny you think I'll need to do that!
Xiaofeng throws a punch at the tree trunk, and the thick, sturdy tree shudders violently, cracking up in spiderweb-like patterns.
Shuang'er screams as she slides down, about to fall within Xiaofeng's reach.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I'm not becoming an appetizer! I'm going down fighting, you mangy tiger!

With nothing left to lose, Shuang'er uses her falling momentum to her advantage, spreading her arms wide and lunging straight at Xiaofeng. Just as Xiaofeng moves to capture her, Shuang'er suddenly throws her hand up in mid-air.

A handful of fluffy snow flies straight at her face, blinding Xiaofeng. She instinctively turns her head to dodge, and in that split second, Shuang'er manages to slip past her, landing with a thud in the thick snow.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Guess the mighty tiger does miss its prey sometimes! Heh!

Furious, Xiaofeng tries to bend down and seize her, but Shuang'er immediately pulls her head out of the snow and quickly grabs another handful, flinging it frantically. Somehow, the snow lands right in Xiaofeng's eyes.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hiss...

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Whoa, Look at that! ${PlayerName}, I beat the Mountain Lord! Am I about to become a martial master?!

speaker: Chief
content: Shut the **** up and RUN!
Shuang'er scrambles to get up, but this time she fails to escape. Xiaofeng's claws have already clamped around her wrist.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Not bad!... Heh, I admit, that was really entertaining.
Xiaofeng slowly wipes away the snow from her eyelids, letting Shuang'er struggle futilely.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: The angle of your aerial attack was quite cunning, and you indeed caught me off guard with that sneaky throw of snow... But even more interestingly...
Her grip on Shuang'er's wrist gradually tightens, and the flow of energy between her fingers becomes faintly visible.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: The Qi flowing through your body is a jumble, lass.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Ow... Let go of me, you mangy tiger! You're such a bad loser...
With her vital pressure point gripped, Shuang'er gasps sharply from the pain.
Xiaofeng's brow twitches almost imperceptibly, and the amusement in her eyes deepens.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: So, if I were to just... snap your wrist right now... do you think that would awaken your hidden talent and make you a martial master?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Heh... you can't scare me with such an empty threat! Your name is Xiaofeng, right? If you try anything, the folks in Ping'an Town won't let you get away with it!
Xiaofeng chuckles and suddenly relaxes her grip. She casually picks Shuang'er up before tossing her back at your feet.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Oh I wouldn't dare try. You're quite a fierce little thing. Way more savage than my Meowy.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, one would probably suffer from indigestion after having such a feisty little snack. Meowy deserves better quality cat food, Mountain Lord.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: That reminds me, I almost forgot we still have an unresolved contest. How about we call it a draw this time?

You and Shuang'er exchange a glance. Clearly neither of you wants to leave empty-handed after such a farce. Reading your thought immediately, Shuang'er suddenly clutches her chest and collapses heavily at Xiaofeng's feet.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Oh! But the White Tiger Mountain Lord has a reputation for being both mighty and reasonable! Surely you won't just walk away after bullying us common folk? In that case, when I get back down the mountain, I might have to tell everyone to reduce the offerings to the Mountain Lord from now on!

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Tsk... If you have a request, spit it out! Cut the dramatics.

speaker: Chief
content: According to our wager, if we win, you will tell us everything about the Scholar's death. Since it's now a draw, we only ask that you honestly answer one question. Would that be acceptable?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: I know what you want to ask.
Xiaofeng picks at her ear and leans back against Meowy with a smile.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: The man at the manor entrance—I didn't kill him.
The atmosphere suddenly grows tense. Her answer is far too direct.

speaker: Chief
content: ...That's it? You should know, Mountain Lord, that I'm not convinced by your answer. The fatal wounds on the Scholar's chest were obviously claw marks left by a fierce beast.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: What claw marks? Did Meowy go wandering around without me knowing again?

speaker: Chief
content: There were three parallel wounds on the Scholar's chest, each as long as an adult's palm, running down diagonally. They do match the wounds caused by a big cat's swipe, spaced roughly four fingers apart, penetrating deep into the flesh with the skin layers torn out...
As you speak, you begin to hesitate...

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: You're a bit slow on the uptake, aren't you? Are you only just catching on after three rounds of close encounters with a tiger?
Shuang'er still looks confused, so Xiaofeng snaps her fingers.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Come on out, little kitty!
She gently shakes the small bell on her wrist. Meowy responds to the sound, raising her paw to swipe at a nearby intact tree trunk, leaving a clear set of deep, fresh claw marks.

speaker: Chief
content: Tiger toes vary in length, so the depth and force of the marks should be uneven. But the wounds on the Scholar... they're too uniform. Did someone discover Meowy's presence and want to frame her?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Oh well, what can you do? Sometimes troubles will find a tiger who is minding her own business in the mountains. I suppose people are jealous of my power. Someone's afraid I'll mess up their plans. I get it, I get it.
If it's that manor master hiding in the shadows, why would she do this? Is it to divert attention, or does she have other intentions?
Somehow the specific shape and angle of those fake claw marks seem familiar to you...

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Why are you still dawdling? Just go find her and ask.
Xiaofeng clearly sees your concerns and has reached the same conclusion as you.
[Corridor]

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Can you two stop talking in riddles? Who exactly are you talking about? And are we seriously going with Xiaofeng? Do you really trust her? What if a fight breaks out and she just abandons us to save herself?
Shuang'er has completely lost respect for this Mountain Lord and is now calling Xiaofeng directly by her name.

speaker: Chief
content: During our duel, we tricked her plenty of times, and Xiaofeng clearly wasn't prepared for it. She was simply confident she could keep the situation under control even if we tried to pull anything.

speaker: Chief
content: At yesterday's banquet, she was the only one who saw through the manor master's trick, and she held her own in a direct confrontation with the manor master. If she really meant to harm these martial heroes, she wouldn't have to go through so much trouble. She seems more like a nosy spectator, though that's puzzling in its own way.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: ...But I just don't think she's a good person. Her tiger is already so fat, and she still wanted to use me as a snack!

speaker: Chief
content: The claw marks do seem suspicious, but that's still not enough to prove Xiaofeng is completely innocent. She might seem carefree and straightforward, but what if she's just playing dumb?

speaker: Chief
content: Since she's willing to take us to meet this so-called "suspect," let's go along and see. If she ends up luring us somewhere just to attack us again... when that happens, wait for my signal. You'll run, and I'll cover the rear.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hey, I can hear you, you know.
Xiaofeng waves at you from up ahead, signaling you to follow her toward the "suspect's" guest room. Behind her back, Shuang'er makes a face sneakily.

speaker: Chief
content: Whether it's Xiaofeng or the manor master, as long as this manor remains in lockdown, the culprit hiding in the shadows won't stop. Only by finding out the truth can we prevent more people from getting harmed.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: That's the spirit! Too bad now's not the time for rallying cries.
A flash of red darts past the corner of the corridor ahead. Xiaofeng stops in her tracks, and her tone becomes uncharacteristically serious.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Well, we got to know each other through our little scuffle, and I consider you my new friends. So, a gentle reminder: We're about to start playing a new game now.

speaker: Chief
content: What game?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Red Light, Green Light.

A sinister, cold presence spreads silently through the air. You suddenly realize the countless thin threads strung around the corridor pillars, under the eaves, and even between the shadows on the ground, weaving a web that surrounds you completely.

speaker: Chief
content: Did she set up traps in advance because she was expecting intruders? What happens if we touch them?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: How much longer are you going to keep guessing?

After examining the setup, Xiaofeng deliberately snaps one of the threads. A weapon comes flying out at them, whooshing through a gap without triggering any new mechanisms. Now even Shuang'er recognizes it.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: That's... General Ma's crowbeak dart!

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: What a coincidence, right? This is probably the person who tried to frame me by faking those claw marks.

speaker: Chief
content: The claw marks on the Scholar's chest are all fatal wounds, but he was killed by only one of them. The martial heroes gathered here use hidden weapons, poisons, or even sonic attacks, but only General Ma collects traditional weapons that could produce that kind of lethal cut.

speaker: Chief
content: That flash of red we saw earlier. It's probably her. Seems like she wasn't just trying to frame us. She also planned to use these traps to get rid of us after the exposure, before we could confront her directly.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Don't move an inch. Do you have a death wish?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: It's hard to stand still with your paw pressing down on me! If we snap another thread, we'll all be turned into pincushions.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: I just blocked plenty of those darts for you, and you won't let me borrow your shoulder for support? Besides, if I really wanted to hurt you, I could've just shifted when that arrow came earlier. You'd be clutching your knee and crying now.
You're stuck in the middle of their endless bickering. This situation has been going on for a quarter of an hour since you all got caught in the traps.

speaker: Chief
content: You two better switch your positions now.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Why?

speaker: Chief
content: I'm about to get... leg cramps...
The two carefully move away, finally allowing your stiff leg to relax. You feel slightly more comfortable in your new position, but the predicament you face hasn't improved in the slightest.
You attempt to force your way through a few steps, but only end up triggering even more mechanisms.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hmm, these traps must have cost a fortune. Icesilk reinforced with darkiron core is invisible in sunlight. Plus a network of pressure plates buried underfoot. Quite a fancy game for those with a morbid taste!
Xiaofeng doesn't seem nervous at all. Instead, she can't resist reaching out to pluck at the silken threads dangling before her eyes.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: You seem awfully familiar with this. You didn't set up these traps, did you?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Why would the carefree Mountain Lord know so much about these elaborate, devious contraptions? You're looking rather suspicious here.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hey now, you're being unfair! I'm simply knowledgeable and like to learn about these intricate little things you humans invent. How about this? To prove my innocence, let me try to "unwind" this thing a bit.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Just a warning, my methods are a bit on the rough side. Don't blame me if I slip up and turn everyone into porcupines!
She leans in closer with a mischievous grin, only to be pushed away by Shuang'er with a look of disgust.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Hmph, do you think we can't get out without you? I'm the most promising future hero of Ping'an Town after all! Come on, young hero, it's time for us to show what we're made of.

speaker: Chief
content: Us? You have a plan?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I may not know much about martial arts, but I know this saying: There's always a solution within three steps. Where all the thread patterns converge is the nexus of this system! Destroy it, and we can be free!

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Look, there's a groove at the top of that stele. That's got to be the key! But the threads are too dense along the way... I'll guide your movements.

You look to the left: Shuang'er, brimming with confidence but weighed down by a bag full of medicine bottles. Then to the right: Xiaofeng, grinning carelessly but not to be trusted to ensure your safety. You sigh, duck under a thread, and head in the direction Shuang'er indicated.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Move right three inches! Watch out for that horizontal thread.

speaker: Chief
content: There's more than one horizontal thread here.

You gather up the hem of your Eastian robe and slowly crouch down, lifting your head to watch those nearly invisible threads pass mere inches from your forehead. After painstakingly moving just three inches forward, you're about to straighten up when you hear Shuang'er gasp.
A sharp snap comes from behind your head as a thread breaks. A bronze battle ax immediately crashes down from above, hitting the ground right beside your feet.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Whoa, thank you. Now things just got a whole lot harder.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: It's all this mangy tiger's fault for interrupting me! Listen, let me start over: Bend backward, go between these two threads, then lift your foot...
You attempt to bend backward and get stuck halfway.

Despite making no big movements, you've already broken out in a thin layer of sweat. When the cold wind hits, your entire body stiffens. But you still focus on the next obstacle ahead as Shuang'er directed, hugging your arms close to your body as you begin to slowly lean backward.
But you stop in the middle.

speaker: Chief
content: Did you just say to bend backward while lifting my foot at the same time? Is that... even humanly possible?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Listen to me instead! Move three steps to the right, then drop into a horse stance! I've done the math. From that distance, you can dodge four traps at once. Much more efficient.

You can't hold this position much longer anyway, so you close your eyes, steel yourself, and take a step as Xiaofeng suggested. Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh! Three crossbow bolts fly just over your head, slicing off a few strands of hair.
Fortunately, you were crouched in the horse stance, or those bolts would have gone straight through your head. From this point on, you don't dare make another careless move.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: You mangy tiger, you nearly got someone killed! You can clearly see that all the threads on the right are connected to an underground crossbow!

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hey, I'm thinking ten moves ahead. And no one got shot, alright? This time it'll be fine. Take another half step left, push aside those two threads...

speaker: Shuang'er
content: Don't touch them. That floor tile is slightly higher than the others. There might be another trap underneath that's sensitive to pressure.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Don't you trust the judgment of the great White Tiger Mountain Lord? I've never made a wrong move during all my travels all these years!

speaker: Shuang'er
content: You just lost to us once today. Young hero, you should listen to me instead. I was the one who discovered the nexus. Trust my keen eyes.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: What good are keen eyes? Look at those skinny limbs. You're too scrawny to even be Meowy's snack. Aren't you embarrassed, shouting "I want to be a great hero!" in that squeaky little voice of yours all the time?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I'm just not lucky enough to have been born with a stronger body! Otherwise, I would've long since become the famous founder of the Tiger-Beating Staff techniques!

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Oh no, you're cursed with bad luck too? All the more reason not to listen to your instructions!
The two of them argue endlessly. Without anyone giving directions, you actually find yourself calming down and focusing your attention on the thread patterns before you.

After all, Ma Ling laid these traps in haste. Though the threads crisscross in a bewildering tangle, the underlying principle is actually quite simple. You discover that the key lies in the hidden triggers at each thread's end. By watching whether the endpoints go taut as you move, you can anticipate danger.
Perhaps you can break through the patterns on your own.
You take a step forward tentatively.
The threads hang quietly. Nothing happens.
Another step. Still safe.
Having taken several steps without incident, you grow even bolder. Before long, you've already drawn close to the nexus Shuang'er pointed out earlier.

Feeling a rush of relief, you duck down again to avoid another thread in front of you. But the moment your weight settles, the green tile beneath your foot sinks, and a series of mechanical clicks echoes from all directions at once.

Several poisoned crossbow bolts streak toward you in rapid succession. As you dodge, your shoulders and sleeves brush against even more threads. One trigger sets off the next, and soon the entire corridor's traps are activated.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Don't move! The poisoned bolts are a decoy. The real threat is coming your way!

Almost instantly, a muffled mechanical roar echoes from the far end of the corridor as a white ash spear comes hurtling straight at you. You twist aside just in time, but the spear doesn't stop, flying toward Shuang'er, trapped helplessly in the web of threads!
Xiaofeng lunges forward to intercept it, but the threads limit her range, and her fingertips miss the spear's tail by mere inches.
You have no time to think. You scan your surroundings, push off on your toes, and hurl yourself directly into the thickest cluster of threads.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: No! There's a chain of mechanisms there! You'll...
The floor beside you bursts open, shooting out iron caltrops and tripwires. Though they can't bring down the spear entirely, they manage to knock it off course by several inches.

The spear tip grazes past Shuang'er's ribs and embeds itself in a corridor pillar. Shuang'er is safe. But where you landed, the tiles are sinking, and a cloud of purple poison gas erupts from the cracks, instantly filling your vision.

The gas carries a pungent, sickly-sweet fragrance that floods your nose and mouth. Your throat burns, then your limbs seize up before going limp as wet clay. You can't summon the slightest bit of strength.
Everything before your eyes begins to sway and blur. Shuang'er's panicked cries and the lingering mechanical noise quickly grow muffled and distant, dissolving into a low drone.
Just before your vision fades to black, a frigid voice cuts through the fog.
Hold your breath...
Clang!
[Insert CG] Skyfall Manor Lord
A white flash from a blade cleaves through the air, instantly dispersing the poison gas in its wake and severing the countless icesilk threads.
The hidden weapons triggered at the other end of those threads are also instantly struck down and shattered like rotten wood.
Through the swirling snow and lingering mist, a slender figure in white descends gracefully.

She stands against the light, straight-backed like a pine tree, the sword in her hand a hazy shadow. In your dazed state, you think you glimpse winter plum blossoms blooming from the blade's edge... Are you hallucinating from the poison?

speaker: Frigid Voice
content: Gather your breath in your abdomen and guard your heart. Try to keep the poison from rising.
Her silhouette, her voice, even the technique of that sword strike just now. Everything matches perfectly with the person behind the curtains at the banquet yesterday.
It's the master of Northsnow Manor, <color=#fb9259>Jichuan</color>.
You're Ji... Cough, cough!

speaker: Jichuan
content: Hold your breath. Don't move.

Just opening your mouth makes your throat tighten up, sharp burning pain shooting straight to your lungs. Darkness floods your vision, leaving only blurred patches of color and light swaying before your eyes.
Jichuan has led you away from the poison gas and helped you sit down in the clearing behind the mid-lake pavilion.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Purple Haze burns when it meets blood and turns solid in your veins. If you speak now, the poison will follow your breath and attack your heart even faster. Do you have a death wish, young hero?

The way she calls you "young hero" feels strangely familiar. Before you can dwell on it, her palm is already pressed against your back, and a gentle yet irresistible flow of internal force begins to course through you.
You want to turn back to look at her, but her other hand gently presses down on your shoulder.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I told you not to move... If you do, the poison will spread even further.

speaker: Jichuan
content: The poison in your meridians has already passed three critical points. Delay another moment, and even I won't be able to save you. If you insist on not trusting me... shall I just let you be?
You finally settle down, controlling your breathing and focusing your mind as you sit still as told. The healing process is long and delicate.

Her internal force gradually merges with the Qi flowing through your body, drawing out the poison's chill little by little. You can even sense the rhythm of her breathing clearly. Light and controlled, each breath stirring the air and gently brushing against the strands of loosened hair by your ear.
Strangely, the shackles aren't disturbed by her power, nor do they resist it. A form of indescribable, subtle resonance quietly forms between you during this silent flow of energy.
You lose track of how much time passes, but gradually the tightness in your chest eases, and the burning pain in your throat mostly fades away. Finally, you can speak again.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...I was taken by a whim.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jiewubei and Xu Shen both died gruesomely. At the banquet, you spoke relentlessly. You seemed to be anticipating the bloodshed. Could someone so calculating be so easily "taken by a whim"?

speaker: Jichuan
content: What about you then? You protected Shuang'er when you were surrounded by those traps. Why was that?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's not from the same world as those martial heroes, just an ordinary girl who looks up to them. Perhaps you've possessed such extraordinary power for so long that you've forgotten ordinary people have no way to protect themselves from these schemes and conspiracies.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In that situation, I had to find the best solution. Saving her was my instinct in that moment.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Then... this is my instinct too.

You don't understand what she means. Perhaps you've never understood this manor master from the start. The flow of energy between you continues in silence, the poison being slowly drawn like delicate threads from your meridians and absorbed into her body.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I saved you... because you remind me of an old friend.

options: You have friends, even though you've lived in seclusion for years?

speaker: Jichuan
content: I did... when I was very, very young.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I was born with an incurable disease. As a child, I spent most of my days beside the medicine cauldron. I was a burden who could never inherit the manor. I hated the bitter taste and refused to take my medicine, always sneaking out to buy sweets instead... At the town entrance, I met a child around my age.

speaker: Jichuan
content: She was homeless, yet more spirited than anyone else. Even though we were complete strangers, she would stand in front of my scrawny body and swing her dusty little fists at the bullies.
You feel her internal force growing even gentler, like a spring stream melting ice, flowing warmly through your limbs and meridians.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Together, we made the dishonest butcher return every copper coin he'd overcharged to an old lady, chased off thugs who extorted money from peddlers, and returned a stolen rattle drum to a child from the town.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Back then, I knew little about martial arts, yet I felt... more truly alive than I ever have since.
${PlayerName}

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you healing me... because of that old friend?

speaker: Jichuan
content: I failed to keep the promise I made to her. Now, seeing you and Shuang'er... I hope you two can have a better ending.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What promise?

She doesn't answer. The snow falls silently, leaving only the gentle mingling of your breaths. Gradually, the poison recedes. You begin to gradually make out the pavilion corridor before you and feel the warmth of her palm against your back through your clothes.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Bear with me. The superficial poison is cleared, but the residue is still deep in your heart meridian. This final step requires me to guide it out with my Qi, to open your channels and break through the blockage.
You catch the suppressed trembling in her voice. Before you can react, she pushes forcefully with her Qi, and searing pain crashes over you like a tidal wave.

speaker: Jichuan
content: First your chest will feel frozen, then your limbs will go numb and tingly, followed by a burning sensation in your abdomen... Don't be afraid. These are all normal signs that the poison is being purged. If you feel weak, don't force yourself and just lean against my hand. I'll hold you up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I already have a lead on who killed the Scholar... And Jiewubei's murder on the first night... that wasn't you either, was it...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Don't use your internal force within three days after the detoxification. Avoid alcohol and cold foods. Soon after sunset, you should rest and regulate your breathing...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why won't you answer? You brought everyone here... What's your real purpose?

speaker: Jichuan
content: If you care about your own safety, after the detoxification is complete, just pretend you never saw me here...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you leave the Red Plum Denunciation? You're manipulating these martial heroes. What's your motive behind all this?
Ptuh! You both simultaneously cough up mouthfuls of black blood that splatter horrifyingly across the snow. But what follows is a sudden lightness and clarity washing over your entire body.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That codex of Snowquell Arts...
When you turn around, there's nothing behind you. Only two pools of black blood remain on the snow, like a pair of linked plum blossoms painted with ink.
The bitter wind howls past, sweeping away any lingering traces of her presence. Only the warmth from her palm remains, still burning vividly against your back.
You stand stunned in the snow. On a bare branch nearby, those two little birds appear again, pecking at each other irritably before flying off in opposite directions.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: What's on your mind?
Xiaofeng leaps out of nowhere, and before she's even steadied herself, her hand is already reaching over to grasp your wrist.

speaker: Department Head
content: Looks like someone beat me to playing nice. Hmm, too bad, this "mountain demon" you suspected of heartless murders was just planning to come and heal your injury.

speaker: Chief
content: With the fake claw marks and the traps designed to kill any witnesses, you're cleared of all suspicion in the Scholar's case. I believe we're both aware of that.

speaker: Chief
content: You're not the one I'm after.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Oh, so now you're cutting ties with me? How cruel!

speaker: Chief
content: Where's Shuang'er? Didn't she come out with you?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: She slipped away faster than a mountain sparrow. You'll have to look for her yourself. I need to go back and take a good, long nap.

speaker: Chief
content: Aren't we going to confront Ma Ling and ask her why she framed you?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: ...There won't be a need anymore.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: The General... already died in her own trap.
[Small CG: Dead Body 3]

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: So the righteous general and the protector of the people was nothing but an ambitious schemer underneath. She dug a trap for her enemies and ended up falling into it herself. I suppose... this was an outcome she deserved.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: The human world is indeed inferior to my mountains, where the order of survival is simple and honest!
With these casual musings, she shoulders her wine gourd and strolls away into the distance.
Behind the ornamental rocks, a figure in white stands quietly, watching it all unfold.

As the north wind sweeps by, her complexion appears several shades paler than the snow itself, a sign of the poison still coursing through her system. Yet colder than her ashen face is the gaze with which she watches the manor.

She clutches a scroll in her hand, eyes downcast as she watches the violence slowly subside. The martial world's true nature strips itself bare inch by inch against the bloodied snow, and the last glimmer of light in her eyes finally dies.
Before turning to leave, she raises her hands and ties the Red Plum Denunciation to a withered plum branch.

Red Plum Denunciation III Golden spears and iron steeds now all rust in graves. Arrowheads forged with blood still seek revenge unpaid. In a realm of decay, if a rotten trunk is to hold the sky, the world shall hear no songs of spring, only a muted cry.
[Guest room]

All is silent in the pitch-black night. Schorl remains unresponsive. Fortunately, such advanced technology is beyond the understanding of the people here in Northwild, so you've been able to carry it without raising suspicion.
You sketch several crude plum blossoms in the snow with a twig, each one representing a guest at the manor.

speaker: Chief
content: The first night, Jiewubei... died in his guest room. His death was gruesome. Killed by a strange poison that made him vomit his guts out.
You draw an X over Jiewubei's plum blossom.

speaker: Chief
content: Everyone assumed it was the manor master's doing at the time, meant to intimidate the heroes. Who would have thought the real killer was the timid-looking Xu Shen? Xu Shen received a threatening note that night and decided to flee the manor.

speaker: Chief
content: The next morning, Xu Shen was found buried within the snow guardian lion at the manor's entrance. Everyone thought it was an open provocation from the manor master. Judging from Xu Shen's wounds and the traces around the scene, all evidence pointed to Xiaofeng.

speaker: Chief
content: But it was in fact Ma Ling who murdered Xu Shen. She staged the crime scene to frame Xiaofeng, and even made excuses to disperse the group so she could set traps along the route and eliminate them all.
You cross out the plum blossom representing Xu Shen, then turn your gaze toward Ma Ling.

speaker: Chief
content: Known as the "General Invincible," Ma Ling always presents herself as bold and chivalrous, so it's shocking that she was capable of such acts. On our way to confront her, we accidentally triggered her traps, which even contained the rare poison "Purple Haze" that was used to murder Jiewubei.

speaker: Chief
content: The next morning, when we found Ma Ling, she had already died in her own maze of traps. Based on the time of death, the killer couldn't possibly have been the manor master or Xiaofeng.
You erase Ma Ling's plum blossom and look toward the Immortal Healer, Young Master Brocade, and the Princess.

speaker: Chief
content: Yin Yansheng is gloomy and eccentric. Shen Wanchou is greedy and cunning. Ji Guining is quietly calculating. If any of them wanted to murder Ma Ling, there's only one motive. To eliminate a competitor so they could be the sole owner of the manor master's codex of Snowquell Arts.

Your gaze finally falls upon the plum blossom representing the manor master. These three murders weren't her doing, but could she have been fanning the flames? And what was her reason for threatening everyone?
With such heavy snow, the mountain path won't be passable anytime soon. You can only leave an offline message on Schorl.

speaker: Communications
content: If contact with Eastia can be established, reinvestigate all related martial clans in Northwild. No one here can be trusted.

The moment the recording stops, a faint rustling sound drifts from the distance, barely perceptible, yet sending chills down your spine. You strain to listen, and the sound seems to be getting closer...
Clap! Someone slaps your back hard!
You startle in alarm, dodging to the side while your hand instinctively moves to your sword hilt. But then you see the person grinning with arms crossed. It's Xiaofeng.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: What are you wasting time on here? I could see that long face of yours from a mile away.
She leans in closer to take a look at the snowy ground in front of you.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Oh, making a drawing? Let me see... Wow, you've drawn a... a huge centipede!

speaker: Chief
content: ...It's a plum blossom. What are you doing in my room?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hey, we were as close as family just this morning. Don't be so cold. Guess what goodies I brought you?
Before you make a guess, she yanks out a small figure in yellow from behind her.

speaker: Wendy
content: Shuang'er? I've been looking for you for so long. Where did you run off to?

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I... hehe...
Her face is somewhat pale, and she shrinks back behind Xiaofeng guiltily.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Guess where I found her? In the kitchen!

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: She was crouching by the stove all by herself, clutching this huge roasted sweet potato and munching away! Caught her red-handed hogging the food.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: After you left me all alone in those traps! I didn't dare move a muscle, waiting for you guys to come rescue me... I waited so long I nearly froze into a snowman!

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: That can't be right! I remember I went back specifically to check, but I didn't see you there... Hey, what are you drawing?
Shuang'er starts drawing with a wooden stick next to your plum blossoms.

speaker: Shuang'er
content: I'm drawing a big dumb tiger, an awful, ungrateful tiger!

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hmph! You're not the only one who knows how to draw!
She shoves Shuang'er aside with her bottom, claiming the spot before lifting her foot to start sketching in the snow.

speaker: Xiaofeng
