With her eyes and ears now quiet, Ayiguo finds herself rather bored. She toys with little spider Number Eight in her hand, but her mind lingers on the encounter with that one.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Perhaps... that little one really is my <color=#fb9259>elixir of youth</color>?
Ayiguo traces the discolored markings on her arm. After that night, these signs have definitely faded.
Remembering the jolt of that eerie red light, she clenches her fists around this new lifeline in her endless existence, her eyes bright with a fierce excitement.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: I wish I could feel it again...

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Once, twice, what's the difference? Might as well make it a round number while I'm at it. Besides, Eastia's boring me to tears!

Ayiguo slips through the bustling crowds, dissolving into the ordinary streets and alleys of Eastia. Anyone who crosses her receives a casual dose of poison. This journey is simply a change of stage. Time to watch a new show unfold.
The martial world remains a noisy, chaotic mess. Today, a "peerless master" rises; tomorrow, a "champion of justice" falls in bitter defeat. Winning or losing, there is never any certainty.

Thieves plunder thieves, villains tear at each other's throats—none of it concerns this granny. Any good or bad blood she casually creates is just another idle stone placed in the river of her endless years.
What she seeks has always been crystal clear: to live long, to live beautifully, and to live exactly as she pleases.

CHAPTER 01: The Important Passenger on the Platform A whistle blares. An old-fashioned steam train stops at the platform. It's unusually lively inside the carriages today. The attendant, who's unfortunately on duty, finally gets a chance to take a breather from her hectic work. She leans against the train car for a quick break.
But then, out of the blue, a shadow is cast over her. The attendant scrambles to straighten up and greets them. "Good day, sir. May I see your ticket?" she says.
female_content: But then, out of the blue, a shadow is cast over her. The attendant scrambles to straighten up and greets them. "Good day, ma'am. May I see your ticket?" she says.

content: The passenger, dressed in a trench coat and wearing a narrow-brimmed hat, looks up, then hands over the ticket and identification to the attendant.
[Scene Transition - Train Corridor]

speaker: Attendant Allison
content: Let's see here... Yup, everything's in order! Please, board the train!
The young attendant glances at the name on the document.

speaker: Attendant Allison
content: Welcome aboard the Praeva Express—we wish you a pleasant journey, Mr. ${PlayerName}!
female_content: Welcome aboard the Praeva Express—we wish you a pleasant journey, Ms. ${PlayerName}!

content: [Background - Train Corridor]
Everything in the carriage is just right.

The lighting is soft, the carpet plush, and the air carries the scent of leather and hot tea. You step into the corridor, ticket in hand, and make your way forward, following the numbers in search of the room that should be yours.

This was never meant to be a journey worth remembering. After solving several high-profile murders in quick succession, your reputation has grown considerably. Many have requested your services since, and you've grown accustomed to traveling for work by now.
This trip is no different. Just as usual, you're traveling to solve some trouble for a stranger you've never met in some faraway place. They're covering the fare, and you booked your seat in advance.
And so, when the attendant closes her ledger and looks up at you, you never even imagined that there would be a problem.

speaker: Train Attendant
content: I'm terribly sorry, Mr. ${PlayerName}, but I'm afraid there are no vacant compartments left on the train.
female_content: I'm terribly sorry, Ms. ${PlayerName}, but I'm afraid there are no vacant compartments left on the train.

content: ...What?

You try every argument you can think of to persuade her, but no matter what you say, you can't secure a ticket. As the departure time draws closer, you have no choice but to abandon the case and return empty-handed—
I was supposed to investigate a case on the train though? How did I get kicked off before the story even started???
[Exit novel-like presentation. Enter Big CG 1 - Author A]
Oh dear, why are you looking at me? Aren't you going to keep reading?
A woman wearing a monocle is sitting across from you. She tilts her head slightly, resting her chin on her hand as she looks at the pages in your hands, smile on her face.
"The poor detective intended to board the Praeva, only to discover that the train was fully booked..."
What should he do? How will he board this train? And what will happen next?
female_content: What should she do? How will she board this train? And what will happen next?

content: Hehe, I wonder—
You can't help but curl your lip. You close the novel and point your finger at the "author" section.
As if the author doesn't know what happens in her own story.
Isn't that right, Ms. <color=#fb9259>Clementine</color>?
[Background - Clementine's Study]

20 minutes ago

A mansion in Eastside
20 minutes ago, you stepped into this study... or, it might be more accurate to say this dump of books.

Papers and books are scattered throughout the room, with even the towering bookshelves being crammed full. Among the classic literature, several books stand out with particularly eye-catching covers. Even from meters away, you can make out the sensational promotional quotes plastered all over them.

"Highly recommended by the new Speaker of the City Council, Max King! The most moving work of the year!" "Moved all of Eastside in N.F. 116! Even Quinn President can't stop singing praises!" "An unparalleled masterpiece with an ending you'll never see coming! A must-read of this year!"
...These publishers really will write just about anything for sales.
You lower your gaze a little more, and you notice all the books share the same author—<color=#fb9259>Clementine</color>.
Pardon the mess, Chief. I wasn't expecting company.
A pair of hands sets a cup of hot tea down in front of you. You follow the rising steam and find yourself coming face to face with the person who placed it there.
The woman looks at you, beaming. She's wearing a fitted trench coat with a striking butterfly pin fastened at her choker, looking more like a performer than an author.
I've heard some authors use pen names. What about you? Is Clementine your real name?

speaker: Clementine
content: It is, of course.

speaker: Clementine
content: I've heard much about the MBCC Chief, but this is our first time meeting face-to-face. Since you went out of your way to arrange this meeting...

speaker: Clementine
content: Could it be that you're also a fan of my work? Would you like an autograph?
There's laughter in her voice. She's clearly messing with you.

options: I'm afraid I don't read many novels.
Sure, why not? I'm already here.

content: I'm here today to confirm a few things with you.
Sure. But before I get that autograph, I need to confirm a few things with you.
The MBCC received an anonymous tip claiming that you've been concealing your status as a Sinner and using your Mania for personal gain.
Clementine's eyes widen, visibly surprised. Her brow furrows slightly, as if she's genuinely troubled.

speaker: Clementine
content: Hm? Was there an issue with my registration?

speaker: Clementine
content: It's embarrassing, but I must admit—back when I was young and reckless, I traveled everywhere to gather material for my books without ever considering the dangers. Fortunately, apart from the infection, I managed to come away from that time in my life unscathed. But then I got so caught up in writing that even after I learned the regulations had been relaxed, I completely forgot to register myself.

speaker: Clementine
content: I never intended to hide my identity. After all... "Famous Bestselling Author Revealed to Be a Sinner!" sounds like quite the headline, doesn't it?

speaker: Clementine
content: Oh, speaking of which, I have a new book coming out soon. Why don't we work together on this, Chief? We could turn it into a publicity campaign, and who knows, maybe the extra sales might just get us a few bucks—
She seems eager to share more of her marketing wisdom with you, but you cut her off.

A registration lapse wouldn't have been a huge problem. Ever since the parole regulations took effect, B-Class Sinners no longer require supervision under normal circumstances. But the allegations against you go far beyond that—
<color=#fb9259>Every time you publish a new book, a murder case bearing striking similarities to your story occurs in Eastside shortly after. Without exception.</color>

A pianist who murdered their agent the night before a performance. Brothers who turned on each other over an inheritance... And most recently, a serial killer hiding in a rural nursing home—just like in The Patricia Mystery.
Furthermore, you've emphasized the realism in your work on multiple occasions. You claim to have conducted rigorous research, and your stories draw inspiration from real life—
You pick up a book from the woman's desk. On the cover, a massive vintage train is barreling forward. Thick plumes of steam are billowing from its chimney, eventually coalescing into huge letters.
"<color=#fb9259>Murder on the Praeva Express</color>—a crime thriller so vivid, you'll feel like you're physically there at the scene. A murder mystery that will exceed all expectations."
Every one of your novels is followed by a new murder case... Are you predicting these deaths, or are they happening because of you?
Faced with your accusation, Clementine's smile falters ever so slightly.

speaker: Clementine
content: ...Those words are nothing more than a little marketing gimmick. Surely you don't think these works of fiction, meant for entertainment, actually affect reality, Chief?
After receiving the tip, the MBCC attempted to pull your records. But no matter how thoroughly we searched, we found nothing. Every database came up blank for your name.
The name "Clementine" doesn't exist in any official records.
When this novel does get published... who will be the next victim?
You narrow your eyes, studying Clementine's face intently, searching for any crack in her composure. But she simply rests her chin against her hand, tilts her head, and smiles.

speaker: Clementine
content: Now, now, Chief. I'm merely a novelist. I don't have that kind of power. Whenever I do reference real events, I need time to digest the material, to let it simmer before it becomes something on the page—

speaker: Clementine
content: Besides, I've always preferred <color=#fb9259>pure fiction</color> over stories that draw inspiration from reality.

content: What the hell is that useless Minos Chief doing? I should've known one tip-off wouldn't be enough. Good thing I sent my own people too...
Just like countless times before—report, pressure, silence. Even if he makes a mistake, it doesn't matter. The family will shield him.
He thought the last person who knew the truth had gone down with that sand ship. It's been so long now. Why won't she just leave him alone? Why can't she just stay dead?
The phone suddenly rings. It must be the assassin he sent to tail her. He answers immediately, but all he hears on the other end is labored breathing.
A sense of dread suddenly washes over him, but it's already too late.

speaker: Clementine
content: At long last... I've found you.
The door suddenly bursts open. The bodyguards are sent flying into the room. Before he can process what's happening, an iron grip closes in around his throat, slamming him to the ground.

speaker: Anxious Man
content: Grk... Argh—
He struggles to speak, but all that comes out are strangled, incoherent sounds.

speaker: Clementine
content: Do you remember me, Mr. Charles?

speaker: Clementine
content: Or should I use your old name instead... <color=#fb9259>Carl</color>?
The young children at the orphanage couldn't pronounce Charles properly, so they gave him a nickname that's easier to read—Carl.
And this very same Carl, who was once so kind, personally condemned them to hell.

speaker: Clementine
content: Once you swap our names, my story becomes the truth.

speaker: Carl
content: Clementine... I'm sorry... please, spare me... I didn't mean to...

speaker: Carl
content: We... we used to get along, didn't we? You'd even bring the children along to tell me stories, remember? I—
Clementine cuts him off.

speaker: Clementine
content: Shh...

speaker: Clementine
content: Listen. The clock just struck twelve.

Clementine tosses the gun to the ground, yet the man's expression only grows more terrified. He finds himself unable to move. The strength in his limbs is completely drained, and his eyes are fixated on that eerie, flowing light emanating from the butterfly necklace.
The light grows brighter and brighter, and she begins to speak. Her voice is soft and gentle, almost like she's reading a bedtime story—

speaker: Clementine
content: "The midnight bell chimes. Figures emerge from the darkness, stepping into the chamber. Their eyes unwavering, blades gleaming in their hands."

speaker: Clementine
content: "The first among them tightens her grip on the blade, its tip hovering just above the sinner's heart. She's waiting... waiting for the sinner to open his eyes and see who has come to claim his life."

speaker: Carl
content: It... it was an accident! I didn't want to run, b-but the fire spread too fast, I-I was terrified... You know I've always helped my uncle fund Redwood. I...I would never do this on purpose!

speaker: Clementine
content: "The sinner awakens in agony. He tries to scream, but a second hand clamps over his mouth. A third presses down on his shoulder. It was then that he realized the time had come for him to pay—"
Searing mania spreads across his skin. Under the grip of utter terror, Carl no longer sees Clementine as human. He only sees a monster standing before him.

speaker: Clementine
content: "The first stab—this for the innocent souls who perished in the flames."

speaker: Clementine
content: "They withered before they could bloom, trapped in the past before they ever had a future."

speaker: Carl
content: Wait, you want compensation, right? Money? Power? Anything you want, I can give you—
Through his blurring vision, the woman's figure warps and shifts.
The goddess of Justice descends. She weighs his sins upon her scales and brings down her blade to pass judgment.
"The second stab—this is for the souls who perished in WhiteSands before they got their revenge."
"They gave everything to fight injustice, seeking to reclaim justice with their own hands, only to be betrayed once more, buried beneath the sands."

speaker: Carl
content: No... No!
[Transition to Small CG - Assassinating the True Culprit 1]
[Small CG - Assassinating the True Culprit 2]

speaker: Carl
content: —ARGHHHHHHH!!!
Once, twice... The needle falls over and over. The butterfly beats its wings frantically, yet it cannot escape—for it has been pinned firmly to the ground.
"The seventh, and the eighth..."
"The blade falls again and again, blood splattering across the velvet wallpaper of the compartment. The sinner convulses and wails, yet he has still not paid in full."
"The ninth stab cuts through his skin and flesh. The tenth pierces between the ribs. The eleventh... splits open the heart..."
[Small CG - Assassinating the True Culprit 3]
Dark, putrid blood flows without end. The butterfly's struggles grow weaker and weaker, until all twelve needles have fallen. Then, at last, the taxidermy is complete.
"Twelve cuts of vengeance, twelve lives..."
"A blood debt paid in blood."
[Chief's Perspective]
MBCC vehicles rush through the curtain of rain, racing toward the estate on the outskirts of Eastside.
Emergency Alert: Banbury Estate under attack! M-value has exceeded threshold—confirmed presence of S-Class Sinner!
...We need to hurry.
At the edge of your vision, flames surge into the sky alongside a pillar of Mania. You can tell who's there.
[Background: Chaos, Sea of Fire Effect]
The fire rages. Tainted by Mania, the flames cannot be quenched by rain. They devour the Banbury estate inch by inch, burning away every last sin.

The woman emerges from the building and tries to take another step, but she stumbles. Only then does she notice the pain at her neck—the butterfly ornament has embedded itself into her body. With no more lives to feed on, it has begun devouring its host.
Mania surges in rhythm with her heartbeat, a fever pitch that invades her marrow and tears through her flesh. She can feel the pain. It's the same pain her family once endured in the flames.

speaker: Clementine
content: ...Right, she did warn me about this.
"Don't get too worked up when you take your revenge, or the butterfly will lose control and devour you too."

speaker: Clementine
content: Hehe... But how could I possibly hold back?

The blazing inferno continues to roar. No one is alive in the estate anymore, save for one figure standing amid the carnage, impossible to miss. A man in black, umbrella in hand, spots Clementine and bows his head in a greeting.

speaker: Man in Black
content: She sensed you activating your power, so she asked me to come and extend an offer.

speaker: Man in Black
content: You're far too talented to die here. Come and join her, while you still have the chance.
But Clementine simply shakes her head with a smile.

speaker: Clementine
content: ...I humbly decline. This is fine.
[CG - Vengeance]
Mania engulfs Clementine and everything around her, like a giant redwood burning in the night. She holds out her hand, watching the flames spiral up her arm before vanishing into the sky.
Those days of her past have grown far too distant—so much so that they feel like faded dreams, hazy and indistinct. Only that fire remains vivid in her mind.
Pain and rage pour from her pen, transforming into words. She can never return to the past, yet neither can she move forward.
Her enemy is dead. She has no regrets. If she had to say, then...
She places a hand on her chest, feeling the mark that connects her to ${PlayerName}. It's drawing closer, racing toward her.

speaker: Clementine
content: If...

speaker: Clementine
content: You're still willing to read my stories next time...
[WHITE OUT]
Perhaps... I'll be able to write a better ending then.
[Enter Flashback Sequence]
"You can find a place like this in Eastside."

"A peaked roof, a two-story wooden building. In the backyard stands an ancient tree that rustles in the breeze." "It isn't particularly spacious." "The red paint on the roof has already begun to peel, the windows always let in drafts, and the aging stairs creak with every step."

"But none of that mattered." "The peeling paint formed pictures if you looked close enough, and the broken windows let in the cool summer breeze." "If you bounded up the stairs laughing, even the creaking wood would sound like a cheerful tune."
"This is 28 Redwood Lane. This is our home."

An elderly woman and her husband opened the orphanage together. She had no children of her own, so every homeless child who came through their doors became hers. She would always tell them to grow like the redwoods—strong, steadfast, and true to themselves.

There were a pair of sisters at Redwood. The older sister fell in love with a man who came to work there as a handyman, while the younger chose to venture out into the world. She joined the finest sand ship fleet and would bring back the latest and most exciting gifts for the children from the satellite towns whenever she returned.

The man had a volatile temper, a frightening face, and always struggled to find the right words. His appearance drove many away, but the Redwood welcomed him regardless. There, he slowly learned to open his heart and eventually fell in love.
The children would run through the courtyard and around the old tree, their laughter echoing throughout the orphanage. Only one thing—one person—could settle them down.

speaker: Young Clementine
content: What would you like to hear? Are there any books on the shelf you haven't read yet?

speaker: Children
content: We've already read them all, Miss Clementine.

speaker: Children
content: That one! We want to hear the story you wrote last time!

Sometimes, the storytelling sessions would attract other listeners as well. Mrs. Jones would sit in the shade, knitting, and Allison would squeeze herself right in among the children. William, though he would keep his distance, still listened all the same.

Little heads huddled together, paying close attention as their most beloved and trusted Miss Clementine told them the stories she'd written. The children would laugh, gasp in wonder, and even wipe away a tear or two as the tales unfolded.
<i>Keep going. Keep telling your stories. The adventure goes on, and the tale never ends.
<i>Your smiles are my most precious treasure, and the words I write are my path to freedom. Keep writing, Clementine. Perhaps... becoming a novelist wouldn't be such a bad dream after all.
<i>If only... I could stay like this with you all, and keep writing forever...
[White Screen for 3 Seconds, Then Slowly Transition to Small CG - Holy Light Finale 1]
Clementine slowly opens her eyes.
She finds herself on a train bound for somewhere unknown. Brilliant light spills through the window, its warmth settling over her, making her strangely drowsy.
It's almost as if she's been walking for so very long, and has finally gotten the chance to rest.

speaker: Child's Voice
content: ...Clementine! Miss Clementine!

speaker: Child's Voice
content: You promised to tell us a story! Why'd you stop?
The voices come from somewhere unknown, yet they're so achingly familiar that her eyes begin to sting.

speaker: Clementine
content: ...Tell a story?

speaker: Child's Voice
content: Yeah! You stopped right at the best part last time—the detective was about to reveal who the real bad guy is!
Frozen memories begin to thaw and return. Yes... she had made such a promise, hadn't she?

speaker: Child's Voice
content: Are you okay, Miss Clementine?

speaker: Clementine
content: Don't worry about me... I just had a very, very long dream...

speaker: Clementine
content: There was a great fire in the dream, and you all went away, one by one. I searched for so long, but I couldn't find any of you...
She trails off. A warm hand comes to rest gently on her head.
[Small CG - Holy Light Finale 2]

One by one, translucent figures settle down around her. A kind face, a cheerful face , a stern face... Every single one is familiar. She may claim to have forgotten, but they have long been etched in her heart.
She hears a whistle in the distance. The train is about to depart, bound for that place of eternal joy and peace.

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: So... will you come with us this time?

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: Though... there's someone outside calling for you. Looks like he's trying really hard to bring you back with him.
female_content: Though... there's someone outside calling for you. Looks like she's trying really hard to bring you back with her.

speaker: Clementine
content: ...Is that so?
She made a promise to wait for someone to return.
But her limbs feel impossibly heavy, as though they have been filled with lead. Her eyelids weigh down, about to close at any second now. Even the strength to speak is slipping away from her.

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: In that case... you should just rest for a while.
[Background - Eastside Streets - Sunrise]
By the time you reach the scene, it's already over. All you see are countless dots of light scattered across the sky—the remnants of that goddess of vengeance—and half a torn page.
You reach out and catch it. It's the manuscript page Clementine scribbled on in front of you.
Some of the ink on the page fades from the heat, revealing the original line of text beneath—
"The train finally arrives at the station. One by one, the passengers disembark from the Praeva."
"The shadows that have shrouded their hearts for far too long have finally been lifted. After all these years, they can finally step into the light and walk toward the future—"
[Small CG - Holy Light Finale 3]

speaker: Mrs. Jones
content: Sleep well, child... You've been through so much...
Welcome home.
[ED]
Once upon a time...
...No, wait. I don't think this is the past.
Maybe... the distant future?
Hmm... that doesn't feel right either...
Ahh, whatever! Anyway, this is DisCity.
A place of desire, dreams, and hope...
[Scene Change: Bureau]

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: No wonder everyone says MBCC is blessed by fortune. Remote as it is, this place works miracles.

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: You know, it's funny... Data we couldn't coax out of our instruments back at the institute is just flowing in here. A few more readings like this, and we'll hit our annual targets ahead of schedule!
The research supervisor beckons to the students behind him, his face brimming with undisguised delight, yet the students themselves seem at a loss.

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: What's with the long faces? Oh, I know the successful experiment's got everyone buzzing, but let's not forget our manners. Hurry, Chief's waiting for us.
Still, no one stirs. The assistant standing nearby can no longer stomach the silence and, steeling himself, finally speaks up in a low voice.

speaker: Assistant
content: ...Supervisor, you told us before we came that there was a walking disaster living here. You said not to bring any of our latest prototypes...

speaker: Assistant
content: If that Summer girl catches wind of it, who knows what'll happen... Years of work could be gone.
Just thinking of that pink-haired girl who had blazed through the Ring Research Institute's record books two years ago was enough to make the supervisor's mouth twitch uncontrollably.

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: Tsk... ahem... Well, what about something else then? Tell me you didn't come completely empty-handed.

speaker: Assistant
content: We... we did bring something. It's in good shape. But it's also one of our experimental materials...

speaker: Assistant
content: Giving it to the Chief is fine, I just... without it, if something goes wrong with the experiment...

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: What's the probability of failure?

speaker: Assistant
content: Simulations put it at roughly <color=#fb9259>0.00000532%</color>.

speaker: Assistant
content: Then let's give it to them. That's a hundred times less likely than a pedestrian getting hit by a car in Eastside. It <color=#fb9259>won't</color> happen.
From his pocket, the assistant produces a coin-like object and slips it discreetly into the supervisor's waiting palm.

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: You'll have to forgive my students. Hopeless bookworms, the lot of them. Not an ounce of field experience between them. Terribly sorry for the awkward showing!

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: Now then! This is the Ring Research Institute's most prized achievement in recent months. Though I'll admit... compared to what a certain genius can whip up, it's little more than a trinket, haha... But please, accept it as a token of our goodwill!

options: I'm not gonna get captured for this later, am I?

content: He presses the coin into your palm with grave ceremony, his fingers trembling faintly from sheer, overflowing enthusiasm.

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: This is no ordinary coin; it's a core simulation medium, refined through countless sleepless nights and massive computational resources at the Ring Research Institute! It stands as a symbol of the unbreakable bond between our Institute and the Bureau.
[Scene Change: CG 1]
Here lives an office worker in DisCity, leading an utterly unremarkable life.
But he was once known as the Sinner Detention Expert, Black Ring Purifier, Syndicate Crime-Fighting Pioneer, and Eastside's Model Youth.
female_content: But she was once known as the Sinner Detention Expert, Black Ring Purifier, Syndicate Crime-Fighting Pioneer, and Eastside's Model Youth.

content: For him, such insincere pleasantries and evasive small talk have become nothing more than the most unremarkable routine.
female_content: For her, such insincere pleasantries and evasive small talk have become nothing more than the most unremarkable routine.

content: CG 1
Once you step out of the Bureau and confirm no one is around, you finally let out a heavy, bone-deep sigh.
Though DisCity has seen no abnormal activity of late, the joint project between the MBCC and the Ring Research Institute has been wearing you down to the marrow.

You have been stretched to your limit, caught between the construction crew lamenting, "Chief, we really can't tear down that load-bearing wall," and placating the Institute's persistent demands: "Why can't we install a miniature Ring substance collider here?"

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And of course, the real backbone of Bureau life is endless chores...

It took you a solid month, but you finally renovated one of the Bureau's above-ground laboratories to Ring Research Institute specifications. That, however, was just the beginning. Layers of bureaucracy and a web of competing interests have since bled you dry. You honestly think you'd rather wade into a Mania zone and face the Corruptors head-on.

If it had been the year you first woke up, you might still have felt a spark of excitement. After all, this was a collaboration with the Ring Research Institute, something most people would never get to touch in their lifetime.
But now, only one thought occupies your mind:

options: "...If only I could have something sweet to eat."

content: You fidget with the friendship commemorative coin the Ring Research Institute had pressed upon you, your fingers unconsciously unlocking your terminal. The screen lands on a food delivery page, and as your eyes skim the promotional text, something stirs faintly in your chest.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...It's been so long since I've ordered delivery. I've almost forgotten what food from outside the Bureau even tastes like. Just <color=#fb9259>this once</color> won't hurt, right?
It takes you a long moment to dredge up the Bureau's receiving address from memory, and after a brief hesitation, you settle on a milk tea at seventy percent sweetness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That'll do. Twenty minutes. Might as well call it a small celebration... for temporarily escaping overtime hell.
But even the most ordinary routines... need a little spice.
It could be sweet, bitter, sour... or perhaps, vibrant, colorful, and utterly unexpected.
[Scene Change: Car Interior]
In the driver's seat, a pair of hands wraps around the steering wheel, frozen in a vise-like hold.
No no no!! This can't be happening!! It was totally fine yesterday! How did it just break today?!

speaker: Car Navigation
content: Warning. Current speed: <color=#fb9259>80 kilometers</color> per hour. You are exceeding the speed limit. Please slow down.
I know, I know!! The brakes are literally dead! What am I supposed to do, yell at it to stop?!!!
Somebody do something!! I'm about to become a pancake on the streets of DisCity!! I haven't even delivered my three-thousand-word confession essay yet and I spent so long on it!!

speaker: Car Navigation
content: External equipment malfunction detected. Initiating autonomous driving protocol.
Watching the onboard AI finally take the reins of this chaotic situation, the person in the driver's seat feels her frayed nerves loosen ever so slightly.
Oh thank god... That was way too close. Like, way too close. Who knew turning yourself in came with a near-death experience?
No sooner does the tension ease than the navigation system crackles back to life, delivering a message she desperately wishes she had not heard.

speaker: Car Navigation
content: Connection failed. Braking system physically damaged. Autonomous driving unavailable.

speaker: Car Navigation
content: Driver, abandon vehicle immediately. Thank you for choosing our autonomous driving service.
The sheer panic sends the driver's mind into a momentary blank, and in her daze, her foot presses down on the accelerator again.

speaker: Car Navigation
content: Current speed: <color=#fb9259>100 kilometers</color> per hour. You are exceeding the speed limit by a significant amount. Please slow down immediately.
I said stop telling me that! Somebody help meeeee!!
[Scene Change: CG 1, 2, 3]
Barely five minutes after you tap the order button, just as you're making your way to the Bureau's delivery receiving point—
Car Sound Effect

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Since when does food delivery in DisCity arrive this fast?
Before the thought can even finish forming, before your fingers find the terminal to check the delivery person's location, blinding headlights flood your eyes.

Then the roar of an engine swallows everything. A car, its chassis vomiting sparks, cleaves through the MBCC gate with an almost surreal trajectory. The barrier pinwheels into the air, tracing an arc against the night.
Hey!! Out of the way!! Move, move, move!!!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Huh?
In this split-second, honed by countless brushes with death, your dynamic vision sharpens to an almost supernatural degree.
You see it with terrible clarity: the car tracing a flawless, inescapable ballistic arc through the air.
And its landing point is the very patch of ground beneath your feet.
In the chaos, the Ring Research Institute's commemorative coin is flung skyward at the same time, spinning into the night.
[Black Screen]
[Explosion, Screen Shakes]
[Scene Change]
You force your leaden eyelids open and give yourself a cursory once-over, checking that everything is still where it should be.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank goodness...
Not a mark on you. No lacerations, no bruises, no lingering imprint of the collision. Your body is, against all reason, perfectly whole; even your shackles obey without hesitation.
...Hold on! But that's exactly what's wrong.

A direct hit from a speeding car should, by all logic, have left you a corpse. So how are you still standing here without so much as a scrape...? Did you doze off at your desk and dream the whole thing?
You pinch your cheek. It stings. Not a dream, then.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...So where am I, exactly?
You lift your gaze. Above you is neither the familiar ceiling of the MBCC nor the harsh fluorescent glare of the Eastside hospital.
Instead... a dim, murky void stretches overhead.

Did it happen again? Summoned to some unknown space, just like before? Is someone about to pop up and announce, "Congratulations, you've been transported to another world!"? Because that would be exactly the kind of cliché straight out of those manga EMP is always reading.
Just as you're swiftly piecing the situation together, light footsteps echo from somewhere in the darkness, and a blinding light floods the space.
[CG: Murphy and Chief Meet]
A girl with a shock of fiery red hair stands silhouetted against the light, gazing down at you.
Your eyes meet. For a moment, the air seems to freeze.
Welcome to Otherworld, Chief!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wow, we're going with the most cliché setup possible?!
[CG Continues]
Welcome to Otherworld, Chief!
Hey!! Out of the way!! Move, move, move!!!
Scattered fragments begin surfacing in your mind: the world tumbling through your vision, a windshield bursting into shards, and that streak of red hair sweeping past you at the very last moment.
Without a doubt, the person now standing before you is the one responsible.

options: So where am I? The afterlife?

content: ...Uh... Y-yes! Yes, that! Haha... You got it!
I am the... the... the goddess <color=#e88490>Murphy</color>, who has guided you through your crossing!
The girl trips over her own words, utterly devoid of any goddess-like gravitas. You haven't been idle, though. Your shackles are already quietly engaged as you discreetly scan the area.
The shackles register a response. She's a Sinner. And whatever game she's playing, you need more intel before making a move...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So if you're a goddess, you shouldn't have any trouble answering a few questions, right?
She hesitates, just briefly, before her head dips and rises in a flurry of fervent nods.
The girl's gaze begins to dart around.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then I'll take your silence as a yes?
The moment she sees the shackles in your hand blazing with crimson light, the girl before you completely loses her nerve.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wait! I... I don't know the answer to that!!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What do you mean you don't know? You're a goddess. Shouldn't you, of all people, know this place?
Faced with a culprit who seems to talk around your question, you conclude that the shackles might just cut to the chase more effectively.

speaker: Murphy
content: I-I'm sorry! I was actually coming to MBCC to turn myself in... but then the atmosphere back there was just so perfect, and I couldn't help myself... I just really wanted to say those lines!

speaker: Murphy
content: Please, I'm begging you, go easy on me... Don't use those shackles...
She scrambles, yanking a wrinkled piece of paper from her pocket before, with a magician's flair, whipping out a steering wheel warped beyond recognition from behind her back.

speaker: Murphy
content: This is the evidence, and... this is my written confession.
As far as you can tell, there's good news and bad news.
The good news is that you came out of an all-out vehicular assault completely unscathed. The bad news... you honestly would have preferred waking up in a hospital bed.
Everything about this is beyond bizarre. You decide to go over the details one more time with the attempted-murder suspect standing right in front of you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So you're telling me you came here to turn yourself in?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Yes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And that car was yours?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Yes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And then you deliberately ran me over and dragged me... wherever this is?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Yes. Wait, no, no, no! It wasn't on purpose! But this place... I honestly have no idea where we are. Here, look, you don't believe me, right? See?
The Sinner before you raises a hand and points beyond this hazy, liminal space. The moment she does, the blur sharpens into clarity, and the silhouette of a town resolves before your eyes.
You roll your shoulders, testing your body, then rise and make your way toward the Sinner waiting at the threshold.

You're just about to close the distance when, as though struck by a sudden thought, her face contorts with alarm. She springs backward in a panic, putting a solid two or three meters between you in an instant.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, wait wait wait!!

speaker: Murphy
content: If you get too close to me, all kinds of <color=#fb9259>bad luck</color> is gonna hit you.
The moment her words escape her lips, you catch it: the shadow pooled at her feet trembles, just barely.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Bad luck?

speaker: Murphy
content: Like... small stuff, you know? Toothpaste falls on your foot when you brush your teeth in the morning. Flowerpot to the head the second you step outside. And if it's really bad... basically anything unlucky that can happen, will happen... Heh heh, yeah. That's just my life.
It's probably just a side effect of her Sinner ability. Powerful abilities often come with certain drawbacks; you've seen this sort of thing plenty of times among Sinners.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's fine. I've dealt with Mania way more ridiculous than this. Your bad luck shouldn't affect me, and besides, your ability might actually come in handy.
You brush the dust from your clothes. For someone who has weathered countless Sinner rampages and broken through multiple Black Rings, this degree of wariness feels more than a little unnecessary.

speaker: Murphy
content: Really? But I've got a feeling—
[Whoosh of incoming magic projectile]
[Sound of explosion, tremor]

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief! Are you okay?! See?! I told you bad things happen when you're near me!
A purple arrow of magic thuds into the ground right at your feet. Murphy, beside you, springs upward like a startled kangaroo, barely hanging onto the steering wheel.
As the dust clears, you glance down at the still-smoking crater near your feet, then lift your gaze to the distance.

At the far end of the street, wave after wave of magical creatures pour into the district, wreathed in glowing magic. Though their forms differ from the typical Mania monsters, the incantations they chant and the spells they unleash are devastatingly potent.
The scene is utterly surreal, as though a horde of goblins and slimes from some medieval fantasy had wandered into the ruins of a fairy-tale kingdom.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stay calm. This space might be under Mania's influence, but combat should work the same. Use your Sinner ability.

speaker: Murphy
content: Combat?! My biggest field accomplishment so far was running you over! I'm totally useless! Look, I say we split up and run. At least one of us might make it out that way!
On the verge of tears, she scrambles desperately to get away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about your ability? In a Mania environment like this, your power should be at its strongest.

speaker: Murphy
content: I can't! If I use my ability, we'll probably make things worse!

No time to react. The swarming creatures surge forward. Above them, blue magic circles flare to life, and an instant later, a relentless barrage of ice shards and fireballs comes crashing down on your cover.
[Rapid Explosions]

speaker: Murphy
content: Ahhh! Hot hot hot—! My hair! I almost went bald just now!
Murphy scrambles across the ground in a frantic, graceless roll. In her flailing, the broken steering wheel gets kicked loose and goes sailing straight toward the oncoming horde.

What follows is a trajectory that defies every law of physics. The steering wheel bounces off goblin shields three times in quick succession, then, at an angle that makes no rational sense, slots itself perfectly into the tip of the lead creature's staff.
[Sound of explosion, tremor]
The shockwave from the blast sweeps through, toppling an entire row of creatures in an instant. Murphy, still sprawled on the ground, stares blankly at the destruction she's just unleashed.

speaker: Murphy
content: Whoa... That actually worked?! Chief, did you see that?! Wasn't I amazing just now?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Didn't you just say we'd lose even harder?

speaker: Murphy
content: How about we just pretend that never happened...? Haha... ha... Anyway! If there's nothing else, I'll just be on my way—
Murphy pops upright and is already poised to bolt, but you seize her and haul her straight back.
The creatures just keep coming. Individually, they're hardly lethal, but as a swarm, they're becoming a real headache.
You need to wipe them out in one fell swoop. The thought crosses your mind, and your gaze slides over to Murphy beside you.
Watching Murphy flail and roll around helplessly in the middle of the monster horde, you come to the unmistakable conclusion that she's the last person you should rely on.
A volley of arrows rains down, and the creatures before you collapse in quick succession.
Someone else's here?
You lift your gaze. A voice reaches you before your eyes can find its source.

speaker: EMP
content: Ooh-hoo! The Archer Queen of Syndicate has arrived, now with the final piece of the set!

speaker: Letta
content: Kinda heavy... but... not bad!
...Situation assessment in progress. Preparing for combat engagement.
When Norma opens her eyes again, she is standing on a stone path.
On either side, shrubs grow thick and green. Low timber-and-stone houses bear iron signs, and a Gothic spire pierces the distance. It is nothing like the Bureau, let alone modern society.
Norma stands frozen, gazing down at the laptop in her hands. She nudges her glasses up and calls up her earlier movement log.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Four attempts to leave. Each time, I end up right back here.

speaker: Norma
content: The environment reads normal. Until I have a verifiable conclusion, panic is meaningless.

Not long ago, Norma arrived at the Bureau as a forensic specialist dispatched from the Public Security Bureau to lend support. She had only just deployed several environmental-data monitoring models when a powerful disturbance surged through the air. A glance up, a blink, and the world was reshaped into this.
She lifts her head and scans her surroundings. An elf in a pointed hat flicks a hand, and a fireball bursts to life on a roadside lamppost.

speaker: Norma
content: The energy conversion pathway is unclear. But the flame is real.
Norma blinks. The physical parameters that usually render clearly in her vision are now twisted by some unknown force in this world, spiking into grotesquely inflated values.
Soon enough, the screen erupts with searing error codes and warning pop-ups.

speaker: Norma
content: As expected, the <color=#fb9259>M-value</color> is the only outlier.
Norma lets her eyelids fall, untroubled. Nothing seems beyond salvaging just yet.

speaker: Norma
content: ...The monitoring models are still running. The local creatures show no hostile intent, or rather, no interest in me for now. I still have time for a more thorough analy—
Just as she prepares to continue debugging the program, a heavy thud rings out. A large, green, viscous mass drops from above and splats directly onto her laptop screen.
The force nearly knocks Norma off balance, but she keeps a solid grip on the laptop.
The blob writhes over the screen, smearing slime in its wake and emitting sticky, squelching noises. It seems harmless enough, but still, Norma feels her scalp prickle with revulsion.

speaker: Green Blob
content: Squish.
Right on cue, the laptop brings up fresh environmental data.

speaker: Norma
content: ...A slime... formed from Mania?

Norma has never encountered such a readout from the environmental monitoring model before. She's briefly thrown into bewildered silence, but she reins it in at once and settles into a cool, methodical analysis.

speaker: Norma
content: What kind of Mania field generates something like this?

speaker: Norma
content: And there are also... magical phenomena, slime-like creatures that actively approach humans, a town that looks pulled from a game...
Norma looks toward the distant town, then down at the seemingly adorable green blob that is, in truth, a Mania bomb. Her tone stays utterly flat.

speaker: Green Blob
content: Squish?

speaker: Norma
content: Communication isn't an option. But I still suggest you get off my laptop immediately.
It doesn't move off. Instead, it shuffles toward the middle of the screen, squarely obscuring the warning: "Advised to maintain distance from this creature."
Normally, Norma would follow protocol and stay clear of Mania.
But the Norma standing here is ready to probe for deeper, stranger laws.
She acts decisively, reaching out and grabbing the slime, her palm registering its cool, slick surface.

speaker: Norma
content: Conventional methods have all failed. Then... time for a different variable.

speaker: Norma
content: Initiating... fifth spatial exploration attempt.
Expressionless, Norma squeezes harder. The moment the green blob distorts, she triggers her ability, skipping past the physical values and forcing a direct touch on the Mania within.

speaker: Green Blob
content: Squiiiish!!!
The slime thrashes in her grip, convulsing through countless shapes, then—crack—it reverts to its raw Mania state, transforming into a spatial rift that swallows Norma whole.

speaker: Norma
content: The switch has a nice feel to it.
In the darkness, the corridor stretches on without end. Using the faint glow of her laptop screen, Norma runs her hand along the wall, only to find it rough and cold. Concrete.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Concrete. Modern construction. This is another space entirely?
She continues forward. Clack, clack, clack. Her footsteps echo through the empty corridor. But soon, Norma notices something amiss.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Wait. Someone's here.

A dark figure has been tailing her, always at a fixed distance—never too far, never too close. This is no ordinary pursuit. The shadow maintains an eerily exact interval, as though constantly calibrating its position against hers.
She breaks into a run.
The stone path. Lush shrubs. Wood-and-stone houses. The distant spire. Norma is back.

As she turns over her experience in that anomalous space, a thread of inspiration begins to unravel. She takes out her laptop and lays her recent movement data alongside the readings from the monitoring models she stationed nearby. The result is astonishing.

speaker: Norma
content: ...A second data set?! With my identity, my trajectory, duplicated and perfectly synchronized?

speaker: Norma
content: Could the models be compromised?
She shakes her head and launches into rapid typing. Across the screen, the scrambled numbers begin to fall into place.

speaker: Norma
content: I need more samples. With enough data... I can trace everything back to the <color=#fb9259>source</color>, even within a Mania field.
She lifts her hand, conjures a beacon with her ability, and drives it into the earth.

speaker: Norma
content: Beginning environmental analysis. Hopefully, the situation won't continue to deteriorate.
[Flashback: Dark Shadow in the Corridor]

speaker: Norma
content: So... that shadow back then. Who was it?
The words die on her lips as her computer blares an urgent alert.

speaker: Norma
content: ...There are others here?
Hey, stop, stop! Don't say that. Us Sinners don't get affected by luck that easily—Ow!
Norma follows the sound, edging closer with caution.

The fallen creatures lie strewn across the ground in a tangled heap. They don't vanish on the spot. Instead, like poorly made clay figurines, they slowly cave in on themselves, blackening and blistering, until nothing remains but an unidentifiable puddle of residue.
EMP reaches out and prods it a couple of times. Nothing happens.

speaker: Chief
content: These things... they're definitely not our usual Mania monsters.
They display a basic level of aggression... and yet, they're nothing like the creatures from before, the kind that would gleefully tear any living thing to shreds.
It's almost as if someone deliberately reshaped them into something less lethal, but infinitely more annoying.

speaker: Murphy
content: S-sorry! This is all my fault!
Just as you're about to pursue that line of thought, a timid, faltering apology sounds from behind you. You turn to find Murphy standing there, shifting awkwardly in place.

speaker: Murphy
content: It's gotta be my bad luck that caused all this! These monsters have to be because of my ability too...

speaker: EMP
content: Hey, stop, stop! Don't say that. Us Sinners don't get affected by luck that easily—Ow!
Before she can finish her sentence, her foot lands on a patch of melted slime, and she goes down hard, face-first into the dirt. While EMP flails on the ground, Letta steps forward from the side.

speaker: Letta
content: Chief didn't do anything to you, so heh... that makes you a <color=#fb9259>friend</color>.
You open your mouth to object, but it dies there as you notice Murphy, at your side, her eyes kindling with an unexpected gleam.

speaker: Murphy
content: F-friend!? Really!
But her excitement barely lasts a few seconds before she sinks back into her slump.

speaker: Murphy
content: Are you sure you wanna be friends with someone like me? Every time I go outside it starts raining, food gets stuck in my teeth when I eat... even stray dogs cross the street to avoid me! What if I end up attracting more monsters...

speaker: Whitestone Industries? Sure! I have so much to say about my company. Um...
content: This is a Mania field. The monsters appear because of Mania.

speaker: EMP
content: ...Ahem! Yeah, what she said! That just now was a pure coincidence. Pure coincidence!
EMP rubs her battered backside and starts acting tough, insisting she's fine. Meanwhile, you notice an unfamiliar face standing beside her.
The woman emerges from behind EMP with unhurried ease. Even after the chaos of the battle just now, not a single speck of dust mars her coat.
I'm <color=#fb9259>Norma</color>. Forensic analyst, Public Security Bureau.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...And why is the Public Security Bureau here?

speaker: Letta
content: See? I told you Chief would ask the same thing!

speaker: EMP
content: Hey, Lantern Girl, how about a little concern over here?! Shouldn't you be asking how we even got here in the first place?!

speaker: Letta
content: Because that question's boring. It's like listening to your Syndicate stories. Fun the first time, but after a while, I'd rather hear something new.

Typical EMP, as she can strike up a conversation with just about anyone. Contrast that with Letta, who's practically bouncing on her heels, seemingly unbothered by the situation. If anything... she looks almost excited.

speaker: Norma
content: I was deployed to MBCC as support staff for data analysis. During routine information gathering, an environmental anomaly occurred.

speaker: Norma
content: Five minutes ago, the monitoring models I set up inside the Bureau detected a sudden shift. M-values breached critical threshold instantly and are continuing to rise.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait, inside the Bureau? Are you sure?
Could that crash have dragged everyone from the Bureau into this place? You suck in a sharp breath and turn, your gaze landing on Murphy, who stands sheepishly at the back of the crowd.

speaker: Murphy
content: Uh... Chief, I couldn't have caused something this big, could I? I mean, my luck's bad, sure... but surely it wouldn't drag everyone else down with me... right?
...After seeing what Murphy's ability can do firsthand, you can't help but feel this outcome is entirely within the realm of possibility.

speaker: Norma
content: However, this situation was not caused by any individual. Every Sinner who came into contact with Mania has been pulled into this space.
Well, at least it's not the worst-case scenario. Ordinary people getting dragged into Mania would be a lot more trouble.
Thankfully, you had assigned the majority of your Sinners to field missions the day before. Only a handful remained inside the Bureau.
The analyzer lets out a warning ping. Norma glances down, her brow furrowing—barely, but it's there.
Within seconds, the waveform on the screen registers two spikes so close together they nearly overlap, and the source is nearby. She pauses for a moment, then quietly stows the terminal away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Any environmental changes outside the Bureau?

speaker: Norma
content: Environmental data analysis is still in progress. What I can confirm for now: the Mania spread remains small-scale. Additionally, the Sinners' abilities have... <color=#fb9259>deviated</color>, to varying degrees.

speaker: Norma
content: As you can see, every Sinner's ability has been altered to some degree. The changes could range from negligible to drastic.

speaker: Norma
content: Case in point: these three.

speaker: EMP
content: Ohhh, so that's what's going on. I was just in my room playing games, zoned out for like a second, and boom. This happened.

speaker: EMP
content: Guess I'm a real Archer Queen now. Can't shake this thing off no matter what I do.
EMP gives her hand a vigorous shake, but the bow stays firmly glued to her palm; she can't fling it off no matter how hard she tries. It might as well be a slingshot fused to her arm.

speaker: Murphy
content: Ah... Are you okay? Does it hurt? That looks like it hurts way worse than that time I accidentally super-glued my hand fixing the door handle...

speaker: EMP
content: Nah, it's fine. Just gotta get used to it. The lantern girl's got it worse than me.
Letta, on the other hand, is missing her ever-present lantern. It has vanished without a trace.

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... The lantern's gone. It used to come right back whenever I called it, no matter where I left it.

speaker: Murphy
content: I totally get that... Losing something you've had for so long...

Letta now wields an enormous lamppost, ripped from who-knows-where. Her original lantern is long gone; all that remains is the sturdiest chunk of the lamppost, slung over her shoulder like a makeshift bludgeon.

speaker: Letta
content: Not a big deal, though. This works fine. And... I actually kinda like it.

speaker: Murphy
content: Well... that does look way more powerful than a lantern...

It seems the deviation Norma mentioned extends over an alarmingly wide area. Everything tied to Mania has been warped by its influence. That would explain why the creatures from earlier were so weakened—the deviation is to thank for that.
So... the question now is, how do you get out of here? Or more precisely, how do you undo whatever this deviation has done to the Sinners?

speaker: Letta
content: Oh, and you should call me Lamppost Girl now.

speaker: EMP
content: Huh?! No way. Even though Hella turned into whatever she'd turn into, I'd still call her a Syndicate grey rat!

speaker: EMP
content: Oh yeah... speaking of Hella, you think the others from the Bureau got pulled in too? If we track them down, we might actually figure out what's going on!

options: Sounds like we're on the same page.

speaker: Norma
content: Theoretically, yes.

speaker: EMP
content: Then what're we waiting for? Let's move!
It seems even EMP can be reliable once in a while. Beside her, Murphy clenches her fists, looking ready to spring into action at any moment.

speaker: Norma
content: All right. You all go ahead.

speaker: EMP
content: Hey, hold up... What do you mean? You're not coming? And you still haven't told us what happened to your ability from the deviation!
Halfway through her step, EMP yanks her foot back.

speaker: Norma
content: <color=#fb9259>My ability did not deviate.</color>

speaker: Everyone
content: ...Huh?

speaker: EMP
content: So you were over there analyzing everything all serious, and the whole time nothing even happened to you?! No fair! I thought we were all in this mess together...

speaker: Letta
content: Actually... she's more like the family member keeping the patients company. She's just here to make us feel better.

speaker: EMP
content: That makes it sound even weirder!

speaker: Norma
content: Jokes aside. I need to return to the monitoring points I set up earlier and continue calibrating the models to pinpoint the source of the anomaly. I won't be accompanying you.
As she speaks, she pulls out a palm-sized terminal from her case, its casing still winking with indicator lights along the edges.

speaker: Norma
content: I'm leaving this portable analyzer with you. It will continuously monitor nearby Mania fluctuations. If you approach the anomaly source, or if it picks up any signals left by Bureau members, it will alert you.

speaker: Norma
content: Naturally. This is the most efficient approach. Once I've gathered sufficient data, I'll rendezvous with you.
Seeing that Norma's mind is already made up, you can only nod and accept the analyzer she hands you. Right now, information is what you need most.
Stay safe out there. Let's move.
The Sinners spring into action at once, all except Murphy, who remains frozen in place.

options: What are you spacing out for? You're gonna fall behind.

content: A flicker of surprise crosses Murphy's face; the last thing she expected was being told to follow.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wait for me!
She'd always believed that trouble, when it came, followed her like a curse—that people near her would either suffer for it or, at minimum, look at her with thinly veiled disdain.

But these people before her barely seem to register it. The monsters are bizarre, the world is bizarre, their own states are absurdly strange, and still they go about business as usual, cracking jokes on the side.
As if all of this is just <color=#fb9259>everyday life</color> to them.
...Maybe this time things could be different? Clinging to that thought, Murphy scrambles to your side.
And no one notices that in the lingering dark at the far end of the passage, something silently opens its eyes.
The path ahead is quieter than you expected.
Stone tiles stretch out beneath your feet, broken occasionally by metal inlays of a mismatched material, their edges scarred as if by intense heat.
You glance down, and a strange familiarity tugs at you. But there's no time to think. Around the corner, a sudden chaos of frantic footsteps rings out.
Close on their heels come a series of ricocheting thuds, the crackle of flames scraping the ground, and the raw, chittering noise of small contaminated entities jostling together.

speaker: EMP
content: Huh? You guys hear that...? What's all that noise?

speaker: Letta
content: Sounds like... when the servants chase me around at home.

speaker: Murphy
content: I think it's more like someone running for their life...
The words barely land before a familiar figure bursts out staggering around the corner.
Her helmet displays a wild scramble of emotion, and she's running so breathlessly she looks like she just clawed her way out of some massive disaster.
And most importantly, she really does have a whole swarm of things on her tail.

There are translucent slimes, bouncing and jiggling, the kind that look like one wrong step would drench your legs in goo. There are burning monsters wreathed in pale blue flames, sparks flying with every step.
The creatures chase with relentless, single-minded focus, clearly locked onto their isolated prey. And the instant that prey spots you, her eyes—no, her helmet—practically light up on the spot.

speaker: Demon looked at the bracelet on the ground in silence.
content: H-heeeeelp!

speaker: EMP
content: ...I feel like that's usually my line.

speaker: EMP
content: Those are just small fry. You could sweep 'em up with your laser easy. Why are you running like that?
EMP looks at Lynn with a puzzled expression.

speaker: Lynn
content: I... I wanna fight back too! But for some reason, no matter what I try, I just end up running away!
Lynn talks as she goes, circling around you in a restless orbit.

speaker: Letta
content: Oh! Now that's interesting! Way more interesting than my ability!

speaker: Lynn
content: Wh-what's so interesting about this?! I just wanna rest for a second... Wait, hold on!

speaker: Lynn
content: You look... really familiar?! I think I just saw you in the cave! You were standing right behind those monsters!
Lynn looks at Murphy and promptly slips behind you, quick as a startled rabbit.

speaker: Murphy
content: Huh...? I was? But I've been standing here the whole time! Could it be... are you sure you're not mixing me up with someone else?
You give Lynn a nod over your shoulder, and only then does she step out from behind you.

speaker: Lynn
content: Sorry... I must've been mistaken then...
The conversation is barely underway when the pack of slimy creatures behind you lunges forward, shrieking.
At the front, a slime vaults high into the air. Murphy spots it and instantly yells a warning.

speaker: Murphy
content: Run left first, then pause for just a second and cut right! Trust me! From experience, the slime won't be able to hit you if you do that!
Lynn takes the hint at once, but in the very next breath, a slime launches itself skyward with a wet splat, arcing straight toward her back.

speaker: Murphy
content: Huh?! That's not right! How did it—?! EMP, help her, quick!
EMP is faster than Murphy's warning, but her arrow cuts through the air only to swerve, veering clean past the slime.
She'd assumed Murphy was joking about her bad luck before. Now, watching her surefire shot sail wide, she can only stare, dumbfounded.

speaker: EMP
content: What the...?! How is that even possible?! My arrow just... curved. In midair. On its own!

speaker: Murphy
content: It's... It's okay! It'll work next time for sure! I'll bet tomorrow's breakfast on it. Guaranteed to hit!

speaker: Murphy
content: ...I mean, it's not like monsters are gonna start falling from the ceiling.
No sooner does Murphy speak than a wet noise rings out. A slime drops from thin air, looking utterly bewildered, and by sheer misfortune, lands square on Murphy's head.

speaker: Murphy
content: Um... okay, I know I'm unlucky. But hey, nobody else got hurt just now! So maybe the rest of the fight will go a little smoother...?

speaker: Letta
content: Oh... I think that's the one I sent flying earlier.

speaker: Murphy
content: I'm sorry... I'll just... stop talking now.
Seeing that the last few monsters are almost cleared out, Lynn has just breathed a sigh of relief when EMP flips forward and lands ahead, rolling her wrists loose.

speaker: EMP
content: Hehe, leave the cleanup to me!

speaker: EMP
content: Don't worry, Chief! I'm gonna make this look good! One shot and take 'em all out!
EMP launches herself high into the air, arcs of lightning coiling and dancing across the arrow in her grasp.

speaker: EMP
content: Watch this! You forced me to do this!

The slime at the front is pinned and bursts apart on the spot. The burning creatures have their cores pierced one after another, and even the monsters cowering at the very back are caught before they can react, skewered clean through in the same breath.
And yet something still nags at you, until your gaze lands on Murphy beside you, swept up in the fervor and openly cheering EMP on.

speaker: Murphy
content: EMP! You've got this! No wonder you're the Archer Queen of Syndicate!
Murphy freezes for a beat, then springs backward as though something just clicked in her mind.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Uh-oh.

speaker: Murphy
content: But... it's just cheering, right? That should be... fine...?
Before you can finish, the ground shudders beneath you. Then comes a second tremor. Then a third.
A pair of blazing golden eyes flare to life in the darkness. Moments later, a round silhouette comes rumbling out from the depths of the shadows.

speaker: EMP
content: Wh-what the hell is that thing?! Murphy! Don't you EVER cheer for me again!
Meow!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Spread out!
The words have barely left your mouth before the creature launches itself forward, its body propelled like a cannonball tearing free of its barrel.
[Vibration Effect]
It plows headfirst through a half-collapsed stone pillar, debris exploding across the ground. The group scatters in an instant, barely clearing the impact zone.
Letta's lamppost comes crashing down against its flank, the blow ringing out like a strike against thick metal plating. The creature is knocked slightly off course, but it does not stop.

speaker: Letta
content: Wow! It's seriously tough. Tougher than the diamonds in my family's collection even!

speaker: EMP
content: Now is so not the time to admire it!
The coin bank gouges a deep furrow into the ground as it grinds to a halt, its gaze snapping toward Murphy at the rear with unnerving intensity.

speaker: Murphy
content: Aaah! It's looking right at me! It totally thinks I'm the easy target!

speaker: EMP
content: This is bad. I can't find a single weak spot!

speaker: Murphy
content: Um... okay, since it's a coin bank, maybe its weakness is its center of gravity? Or...the usual spots on small animals? You know, like the ears, or under the arms...?
EMP swiftly maneuvers to flank it, loosing arrow after arrow at its ears, yet just as before, each shot fell agonizingly short.

speaker: EMP
content: Tch. Something's seriously wrong here...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Letta, take out its legs! Sweep low with the lamppost!
Letta answers, heaving the weighty lamppost up and ramming it into the ground. With a powerful twist, she sweeps it horizontal, forging a low barricade right across the center of the passage.

speaker: Letta
content: Round things always trip over stuff like this!
18 [Coin bank cries out - select a voice line from the coin bank's audio files]
The coin bank screeches, kicks off the ground, and barrels toward your group. Its front legs snag the lamppost right on cue, sending the whole thing hurtling through the air.

speaker: EMP
content: It worked?!
But a split second later, it ricochets back using its own momentum, crashing into the lamppost with enough force to rip it clean out of Letta's grip.

speaker: Lynn
content: That... that doesn't even make sense!
The coin bank skids in place, its gleaming golden eyes swiveling with calculating intent. Then it launches itself skyward, poised to come crashing down and flatten everything beneath it.

speaker: Murphy
content: No!!!
In that instant, the roar in Murphy's ears stretches into an endless, distorted drone.
(Flashback)

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Ugh... Why does this kind of thing always happen when you're around...

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Seriously. We barely ever get to hang out like this, and now... ugh. Way to kill the mood.

speaker: Murphy
content: <color=#fb9259>...Can we still hang out? After this?</color>

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Just forget it. Nothing good ever happens when you're here.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Forget it... Being around you just means bad luck. My mom told me to stay away from you.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Murphy... let's just call it off. What if you end up getting the other students hurt?

speaker: Murphy
content: <color=#fb9259>Get them... hurt...?</color>

speaker: Murphy
content: <color=#fb9259>No... They'll get hurt! I can't let that happen again!</color>
(Back to present)

She takes in the sight before her: Letta standing firm in her defense, EMP still loosing arrows without relent, Lynn running back and forth to pull the monster's attention away... and ${PlayerName}, who has never once given up on her.
They haven't shoved her aside. They haven't muttered a word about her cursed luck. Even at the most dangerous moment, they keep her sheltered behind them.

speaker: Murphy
content: We grow the finest wheat in all of WhiteSands, but the moment we signed that deal, we lost all say in the price! Every industry we try to build, we have to kneel and ask the metropoles for permission!

speaker: Murphy
content: I finally have people who treat me like a <color=#fb9259>friend</color> again... and I am NOT letting you hurt them!
You are just about to release your shackles when Murphy dashes forward, swift as an arrow flung from the bowstring.
Meow!
The moment it registers a new enemy, the rotund coin bank wheels around and comes rolling straight for Murphy.

speaker: Murphy
content: Even if it means burning up all my luck for the next twenty years. No, wait, what luck do I even have?! Fine! Then I'll stake every bit of bad luck from my entire life!

speaker: Murphy
content: Take this—
She has barely taken two steps before her left foot snags her right, sending her pitching forward into the ditch without so much as finishing her sentence.
But the fall saves her. The charging coin bank lost its mark in an instant.
Meooooow!!
And so, the very next second, right before everyone's eyes, it barrels past the ditch and crashes headlong into the shattered stone wall ahead with a thunderous boom.

With a series of earth-shaking rumbles, the coin bank, along with the broken rubble, tumbles into the deeper darkness below. The clattering din of its fall echoes downward, growing fainter and farther, until finally—clang—it lodges somewhere unknown.
The entire passage falls abruptly still. Only the patter of loose stones continues to fall. Murphy, covered in dust and dirt, pokes half her head out of the ditch.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Did I actually, you know... help?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In a way, yeah.

Just then, a piercing shriek of static splits the air above them. Crzzzt—bzzt—crzzzt— The noise erupts without the slightest warning, like a transmission signal forcing its way through, clawing desperately across some other layer of warped space.

speaker: Murphy
content: Huh...? What's that sound?

speaker: EMP
content: Sounds... kind of like...

speaker: Lynn
content: <color=#fb9259>The Bureau's broadcast?</color>
The next second, a halting yet deeply familiar voice squeezes its way out of the noise.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Chief... if you can hear this... please respond...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Repeat... if you can hear this... please respond...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nightingale?
[Scene Change]
In the candy forest, Norma stands beneath a tree laden with lollipops, watching in deadpan despair as a spring-legged monkey hops around nearby, clutching her monitoring model.

speaker: Spring Monkey
content: Screech! Screech!
Norma can only sigh inwardly at the sight. There's no sense in getting angry at a monkey.
After parting ways with the Chief and the others, she continues toward the other monitoring points to calibrate her data.
And so, after passing through a forest made of lollipops and swimming across a coffee-flavored lake, she arrives at the location of her monitoring model.

speaker: Norma
content: Locating it is simple enough. Retrieving it from the monkey, however, presents a logistical problem.

She makes a grab for it, only for the monkey to dance effortlessly aside, its spring legs propelling it a full three meters upward. She tries coaxing it with a candy banana; the monkey snatches the offering and bounds off still clutching the monitoring model, putting even more distance between them.

She even tries mimicking the monkey's gestures, making a show of offering to return something. The monkey waves toward the forest, and within a moment, seven or eight of its kind burst out and launch into a game of pass-the-parcel with her device.

speaker: Spring Monkey
content: Screech screech screech!!

speaker: Norma
content: ...At this point, I'm beginning to wonder which of us is the real monkey.
Watching her monitoring model get tossed from hand to hand, Norma adjusts her glasses. The monkeys grow increasingly gleeful; one even bonks a companion on the head with it.

speaker: Norma
content: The experience from before confirms that conventional methods are ineffective here. But ineffective doesn't mean I'm out of options.
She takes a step forward, weaving through the frenzied monkeys, and extends her hand toward the distorted sky draped in Mania—

speaker: Norma
content: I follow rules... but only when those rules are fair!

speaker: Norma
content: If this world operates on chaos, then... I'll rewrite the rules myself!

speaker: Spring Monkey
content: Ooh ooh ah ah—
Mania disperses outward in a sudden wave. The monkey troop scatters. A rift splits through the fabric of space, and Norma is swallowed into the other dimension once again.

She finds herself in the same familiar corridor, now traced with a few weak lights. To the naked eye, this place is merely an anomaly of overlapping data, but to Norma's perception, it reveals itself as something else entirely.

speaker: Norma
content: Last time, the data overlap was too severe for me to identify the full structure. But now I can confirm that this is the Bureau.

Through Norma's eyes, the space maps onto the Bureau with eerie precision. Only the wall signs are flipped, fire hydrants dangle from the ceiling, the Chief's office wears iron bars, and every Sinner's door gapes wide open.

speaker: Norma
content: A mirror image? But not a perfect one. There are discrepancies between the two spaces.
It is as though everything that should be in order has been deliberately nudged one notch out of place.

A glance from the corner of her eye, and there it is again, that indistinct yet familiar dark shape. Its form has altered. Even Norma cannot determine whether it is the same shadow she encountered earlier.

Thrust into another Mania-warped space once more, Norma finds this one marginally more structured than the last. The logic may be skewed, but it already feels far more bearable to her meticulous mind.
But this space clearly has no welcome for her. Some external force twists and strains, trying to expel her from its boundaries...
As expected, the Mania rift spits Norma out once again.
The pesky monkeys are gone. Her monitoring model lies amid cotton-candy-like blossoms. Norma swiftly calibrates it to collect data, then plants another beacon to stabilize this Mania-distorted area.

speaker: Norma
content: This data alone isn't sufficient. Combined with the readings from the <color=#fb9259>recorder</color> on the Chief's end, I should be able to reach some conclusions.
Once the data synchronizes, every stranded person is pinpointed. Apart from the Chief, all those swept into this Mania field are Sinners.
At least no innocent civilians blundered in. Norma cocks an eyebrow.

speaker: Norma
content: If my hypothesis holds, that anomalous space is undoubtedly the Bureau. The deviation in Sinner abilities, the weakening of Mania creatures—all of it stems from a source distorting the rules of reality.

speaker: Norma
content: Which raises the question... which space is the real one?
Norma taps at the keyboard, trying to locate the source of the distorted Mania field, but warning messages flash onto the screen once more.
With the beacon's help, Norma can now roughly correlate this world's numerical data with the Bureau's internal layout.

speaker: Norma
content: Dwelling on that question won't help... The priority is getting this information back.
She opens the communication terminal, but the screen still shows nothing but static.

speaker: Norma
content: Wait, there's another possibility...
She pulls up the Bureau map she requested when installing the monitoring models and compares it against the terrain of this anomalous space.

speaker: Norma
content: What if both spaces are real, interacting with and feeding back into each other?
On the screen, the two maps begin to overlap. She quickly locks onto a set of coordinates.

speaker: Norma
content: Found it. The way to transmit information.
After successfully transmitting the message, Norma lets out a heavy sigh. This space has all but shattered every rule she has believed in until now.

speaker: Norma
content: This is like... trying to calibrate a scale with a broken set of weights.

speaker: Norma
content: Even if the numbers add up, the process is utterly inelegant.

She slides her glasses back on, her gaze turning professionally cold behind the lenses. She scans the area. The beacons she'd tagged as stable are now humming faintly, their readings pulsing at erratic frequencies.
Her fingers fly across the keyboard as she hunts for the source of the rule-rewriting force. Amid the weaving threads of data, a minuscule but deeply oppressive black dot flickers by.
It's no Mania creature, no lingering Sinner energy. It's more like a pair of eyes... overseeing the entire chessboard.

speaker: Norma
content: Of course. Information flows both ways. Transmitting that message was bound to attract attention.

speaker: Norma
content: Since you're so eager to reveal your ugly side, I see no reason to keep indulging these absurd monkeys.
