Murphy stares at that silhouette, so identical to her own, her fingertips trembling faintly. She can feel it: this thing is bound to her.
It knows every thought buried in the deepest recesses of her heart. It knows precisely what she needs most. And yet...

speaker: Norma
content: Listen, Murphy. Biologically speaking, it really is similar to you.

speaker: Norma
content: Misfortune surrounds you constantly, but the shackles neutralize your M-value, keeping you locked in a dangerous but stable equilibrium.
[Flashback with supplementary details]

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Ring Research Institute has preliminarily confirmed that this abnormal expansion of the Mania field is linked to the influence of Sinner Murphy.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Accept me. I am you. From this moment on, I will carry all your misfortune. I will savor the endless suffering in your place!
As the M-value climbs ever higher within the space, the device in your hand sounds its alarm. The Mania hangs so thick in the air that even breathing becomes a strain.
It is Murphy who breaks the silence first.

speaker: Murphy
content: I want to take a gamble.

speaker: Murphy
content: On the chance that I might have something too... something that isn't just bad luck.
The Sinners nearby stand rooted to the spot, utterly dumbfounded, their eyes fixed on Murphy.

speaker: EMP
content: Wait... are you actually serious right now?! Lantern Girl, talk some sense into her! There's no way she wins this!

speaker: Letta
content: Aha... this is getting a little too interesting. Like, so interesting it's looped back around to not interesting at all.

speaker: Lynn
content: Murphy! Please... don't do something this dangerous!

speaker: Murphy
content: Yes.

speaker: Murphy
content: Crashing into you, getting chased by monsters, ending up down here... It's true. I'm always the one who messes things up first.

speaker: Murphy
content: But I... I still want to help everyone. I want to help my friends.
Misfortune Incarnate stands at a short distance, silently observing the scene before it. The smile on its face does not fade—if anything, it deepens.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Heh... what's this? Grasping at straws now?

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Sigh... You'd rather put your faith in these fragile, fleeting little things than accept the truth? You were born to stand with me. Only me.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: The one who's truly been with you all along... has only ever been me. Your misfortune.
Murphy closes her eyes, her fingers slowly clenching into fists. It is the gesture of someone who has, at last, steeled herself for a revelation that will tear her wide open.

speaker: Murphy
content: You're nothing but a monster this Mania field spat out, feeding off my bad luck.
Her words fall away, and she opens her eyes, meeting the monster's gaze without a trace of retreat. In the same breath, her hand comes to rest upon your shackles.

speaker: Chief
content: I won't lie... I don't know what's going to happen if we do this, Murphy.

speaker: Murphy
content: Then I... should at least get one chance to see what's really left of me.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't worry. We're all with you.

speaker: EMP
content: ...Tsk.

speaker: EMP
content: Fine. If Chief's in, I'm in.

speaker: EMP
content: But I'm calling it now! If things go south, I'm the first one out the door!

speaker: Letta
content: Count me in too!

speaker: Lynn
content: I... I'll help too!
So what if the worst should happen? Then let it. A few more days in this maddening Bureau is nothing.
—Not when you'll finish this Misfortune Incarnate together with your friends.

speaker: Murphy
content: You want to become me, to strip away my very existence.

speaker: Murphy
content: Then I'll tear every last bit of it away from myself... and <color=#fb9259>give it all back to you!</color>

As Murphy speaks, she extends her hand, and threads of black come streaming forth in endless ribbons. Misfortune Incarnate before her is delirious with glee, so impatient that it seizes Murphy's hand in a vice-like grip before she can offer it.
The violet-black mist thickens, wrapping nearly its entire form in a dense shroud. Its silhouette swells and shoots upward, and its smile warps into something utterly grotesque.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Haha... yes... that's it!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Acknowledge me! Accept me! Only together with me, can you be whole—

But its voice cuts short. It realizes, with a jolt, that its own power is draining away at a terrifying speed. The mist is rushing toward Murphy instead. It thrashes wildly to break free, only to find your shackles clamped down on it, unyielding.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: No... Why...?
It rips itself loose with a burst of force and looks down at its hands. Those hands that once passed for human now grow indistinct, regressing toward the primal form of Mania.

You've won the gamble. The Sinners wear sly grins; though not a single word passed between them, each seems more than happy to have joined Murphy in this reckless gamble: letting Misfortune Incarnate drop its guard and walk straight into her grasp.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: What did you do?!

options: Let me spell it out for you.

content: Murphy got her ability from that accident. Not for any other reason, but because of you.

Like all Mania, you had an obsession. You wanted Murphy to grow stronger, desperately, because that would make you stronger too. But it never happened. Murphy was too unlucky. Every chance to improve just slipped through her fingers.
But opportunity always finds a way. An accident happened, and Murphy's misfortune triggered a deviation here. The deviation can alter the form of any Mania, and you used that to break free.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: —!!

You got too greedy. Amping up the Mania wasn't enough; you wanted Murphy's body too. That's why you tried so hard to absorb her misfortune, to flood this place with Mania. You were looking for the perfect vessel. Your perfect vessel.
Too bad, you got outplayed. By the way... have you ever heard of communicating vessels?
EMP, never one for book learning, shakes her head first. You wave your hand at her, telling her not to cause any mischief.
One bottle's full of water. The other's empty. Connect the bottoms with a tube, and what happens?
Norma clearly knows. She gestures with her hand, drawing a flat, steady line through the air.

So now, the problem becomes simple. You both share the same vessel, which is misfortune itself. But the Mania stored inside is not equal. As the incarnation of Mania in this space, your reserves are practically endless.

If you hadn't let your guard down here, if you hadn't overlooked the shackles... everything would've gone exactly according to your plan. But anything that can go wrong will go wrong. You're no exception to that rule.
And my shackles are that tube. Your power is flowing uncontrollably from abundance to scarcity, until the balance between you two levels out. That's why your power is vanishing.
Murphy sways on her feet, and you rush forward to catch her. She is clearly overwhelmed, unable to contain this immense surge of power.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief... I did it...
With the power of misfortune now absorbed, the black tendrils have vanished from around Murphy. What remains is a subtle, near-invisible shimmer of warm gold.

speaker: EMP
content: ...For real?

speaker: EMP
content: Lantern Girl, when we get back, we're buying lottery tickets. We're definitely winning!

speaker: Letta
content: But I feel like scratch-offs would be more fun.
Beside the easy chatter of the others, Misfortune Incarnate now burns with a fury born of humiliation.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Impossible...!
The power of Misfortune Incarnate churns and swells once again. On the opposing side, Murphy meets it with equal ferocity, refusing to yield an inch.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...This time, I'm not running away!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Fine! Then I'll prove it myself. Without your misfortune, you are nothing!

The maintenance platforms, barely holding together moments before, now wrench themselves out of alignment all at once. Nearly every foothold lurches in the same breath toward the most treacherous angle.
Even the Mania that had been drifting formlessly through the air coalesces under its pull, sharpening into countless slender black spines that come raining down from every direction!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Do you see it now?! This is misfortune!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: It forces everything toward the worst possible outcome! And... no one can resist it!
At the very front, a single black spike drives straight for Lynn's face.
In the split second before it strikes, a warning sign, already loose, drops from above and to the side, slamming diagonally into the spike and deflecting it off its deadly path.

speaker: Norma
content: Lynn! Look out!

speaker: Lynn
content: Eh?!
The deflected spike whistles past her ear and buries itself deep into the wall behind her.
At the same moment, the metal plate beneath Letta's feet gives way, yet the fracture halts itself precisely at her heel, as if unwilling to take that final inch.

speaker: Letta
content: Hm... Time to give that pitch-black thing a taste of its own medicine. Let's see how it likes always falling just short!

speaker: EMP
content: Save the commentary, Lantern Girl!

speaker: EMP
content: This thing's trying to wipe us all out in one go!
She raises her bow and lets fly a rapid volley. Three arrows fan out across the air at distinct angles, every one of them aimed for the thickest knot of dark mist coiled upon its chest.
The black incarnation furrows its brow and waves away the arrows with a sweep of its hand. The two forces stand evenly matched, neither yielding an inch of ground.
With every step it takes, the platform splinters apart beneath its feet.
And Murphy steps forward as well. The two figures advance toward each other through the same crumbling space, unflinching.
[CG]

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Do you really believe you can match me? Dear Murphy?

speaker: Murphy
content: Guess I'll find out.

speaker: Murphy
content: I want to see if this world will show me any path... other than the worst one.
The battle rips through the entire space, dragging everything deeper down with it.
From the corridor to the broken bridge, from the broken bridge to the warped hall, and finally crashing into that first area, the one overturned by the car, now a ruin beyond recognition.
Still, neither side can seize victory. Both have spent every last method, and neither can muster even the ghost of a proper strike anymore.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: One day, that fear will come back to you. You will still run. You will still expect the worst to happen first.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: And when that day comes, I will return! I will return as your deepest nightmare!

speaker: Murphy
content: ...That's a problem for another day.

speaker: Murphy
content: At least right now, I know one thing for sure. There is another possibility besides misfortune!
The incarnation sneers coldly, offering no answer. It raises a hand and forces misfortune itself into solid form, ready to hurl it straight at all of you.
From the distance, the utterly ill-timed roar of an engine cuts through the air.
Vroom—vroom vroom—

speaker: EMP
content: ...Huh?

From the far end of the darkness, two crooked headlight beams flare to life. As though tracing a route that should no longer exist, the car has wound its way through a vast, meandering circuit—threading through shattered platforms, veering around collapsed door frames, smashing through the dangling rails—

speaker: EMP
content: You're kidding me?!

speaker: EMP
content: How did it even get back here?!
The car charges forward, just as it did at the very start, barreling straight toward its target. Only this time, that target is not you.

The black incarnation folds in midair, its body bent into a lurching, broken arc. Its shell, already split through with countless cracks, finally gives way under the impact, and the purple-black mist detonates outward.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: No—

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: This can't be!!
The car swerves drunkenly forward a short way, then screeches to a halt not far off. For good measure, the hood lets out a thoroughly undignified puff of smoke.

speaker: EMP
content: Holy ****.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: ...Why?
For the first time, it looks utterly lost.

speaker: Murphy
content: Because you've always believed... that luck only ever tips one way. Toward the worst.

With a thunderous boom, the dense purple-black mist rolls outward in all directions like a tide robbed of its center. And in kind, the misfortune and Mania that Murphy had temporarily taken into herself begin to scatter and fade.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Deep-level anomaly core confirmed eliminated. Reality restoration in progress... Wait, the underlying physical structure is collapsing!
As Mania disperses, a wave of vertigo comes crashing over you. You realize, with a jolt, that everything around you is inverted.
Thanks to the residue of Murphy's misfortune, the entire space now lies flipped, meaning every last one of you is plunging headfirst in free fall.
Until the very end, misfortune remains by your side.

speaker: EMP
content: A little warning next time?! I didn't even get to strike a cool pose—!

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... looks like it's a diving activity now.

speaker: Lynn
content: N-no, wait! There's... there's still a cushion layer below us... right?! Right?!

speaker: Norma
content: According to my analysis, there should be.
But set against everything you've endured to get here, this is hardly more than a trifle.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief?! Chief! All personnel, deploy every maintenance airbag and buffer net on the lower level immediately! We have to catch them, no matter what!

speaker: Everyone
content: AHHHHHHHHH—!
The howling wind swallows her voice almost whole. You lash out with the crimson shackles, sending them straight through the air to snatch Murphy—the one nearest to you—mid-flight.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief?!

options: Hold on tight! Don't let go!

content: After a fall that seems to stretch on forever, a soft white glow finally blooms below. It is the buffer netting and maintenance airbags, deployed automatically in the wake of the emergency repairs. In the next breath, everyone plummets into them with bone-rattling force.
Afterward, the Ring Research Institute spends two full days conducting a secondary sweep and structural reassessment of the Bureau's underground sector.

Faced with a report thick enough to bludgeon a person dead, Nightingale reads it through, falls into a long silence, and in the end merely sets the file down with care before turning to arrange new maintenance rotations and security shifts.
The incident is ultimately classified in a string of rigorous, officially worded conclusions.
But in the words of those who lived through it—

speaker: EMP
content: Okay, okay, listen, little mouse, you're not gonna believe this. We cleared this absolutely insane, ultra-hard secret dungeon. Under the Bureau.

speaker: EMP
content: And the place was completely cursed! Slimes, coin banks, you name it... Oh, and get this: there was this Mania thing, like, the embodiment of bad luck, and it totally had us on the ropes the whole time. Good thing I... I mean, good thing we pulled off some serious clutch plays, or we would not have made it out of there!

speaker: Hella
content: Pfft. A scrub's a scrub. You got your ass kicked, and you're still out here bragging about it.

speaker: EMP
content: Oh, right, forgot to mention, Chief was there too.

speaker: Hella
content: What?! That dummy had something this fun going on and didn't even tell me?!

speaker: Hecate
content: We were out on a field mission at the time.

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh, I don't wanna hear it! And anyway, couldn't you have just messaged me on the terminal? Obviously I would've rushed right back if I knew!

speaker: Hecate
content: Adjutant Nightingale said the comms were blocked by the Mania field.

speaker: Hella
content: Hmph. Next time something like this goes down, I'm definitely not missing it!

speaker: Hecate
content: Yeah. Next time.
[Scene Change]
In its post-incident review, the Ring Research Institute concluded that Murphy's "misfortune" was not eradicated, but rather brought into a more stable equilibrium.

Though drawn into the incident by misfortune, and though she came face to face with Mania, it was in reckoning with that Mania—and through it—that she finally found herself with something more than misfortune alone.

Of course, the institute supervisor who gifted away the experimental material was also suspended from his position. For the days ahead, he will serve as a member of the MBCC maintenance crew, helping repair the damage wrought upon the Bureau.
And so—
A long, long time later...
Oh wait, maybe... not that long after all.
For DisCity, managing to get through an entire week without incident is already an accomplishment worthy of the history books.
Anyway, on what seems like an utterly ordinary workday—though, in truth, not quite so ordinary—

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Mania response detected from Sinner Murphy! Move to detain!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Attention all units, Sinner Murphy's misfortune abilities remain active! Stay sharp!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: What?! The containment net short-circuited one second before deployment and tangled up three of our own people?!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Team One, pull back! Team Two, move in, now! Go, go!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Team Two? Team Two, report! ...What do you mean the tear gas all went off at once?! You can't even see what's happening on site?!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Sigh... Command, Sinner Murphy's current location unknown. Requesting immediate assistance from the MBCC Chief.
[Scene Change]
The reception office is unchanged, as it always has been. Since Kiki recovered from her injury, her life has remained much the same. Yet not entirely without change—
She has lately taken to growing four-leaf clovers, after receiving seeds sent by an old friend. The seeds, her friend claimed, came from another world and would bring good fortune.
Nightingale finishes the report at last. She lifts her gaze to ${PlayerName}, seated behind the desk with a shoulder still wrapped in thick bandages, and sinks into a long silence.
In the end, she merely sets the file down with care and exhales a sigh of quiet resignation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I've already rescheduled the maintenance and security rotations. As for your fieldwork requests, I'll be rejecting every single one of them until your injury is fully healed.
As for the red-haired figure who vanished from the reports—
Who knows?
Maybe this time, fate will actually show a little mercy, and let her stumble upon a stroke of luck, the truly good kind, around some corner where no one's watching.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wha—?! Why did the brakes break again?!

speaker: Murphy
content: Chieeeef! Heeeelp!

speaker: Tracy
content: Okay...
[Flashback]
(Scene change)

speaker: Joan
content: This is...?

speaker: Joan
content: What do you mean?
[Chief's portrait]

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief!
(Scene change)
[Flashback]
[Transition]

speaker: Joan
content: It's you?!

speaker: Jane
content: No, we haven't.

speaker: Eugene
content: Shh!
[Black Screen Transition]

speaker: Tracy
content: Oh.
(Scene change)
${PlayerName}
(Scene change)
That’s valuable information—hard to come by. Maybe we should consider an intel exchange.
[Bureau Corridor]

speaker: Phanuel
content: Mm.

speaker: Phanuel
content: No, we haven't.

speaker: Phanuel
content: No.
Hmm...

speaker: Chief
content: What are you getting at?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Purr?
Knock, knock.

speaker: Chief
content: Shh!

speaker: Phanuel
content: You won't.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Of course!

speaker: Phanuel
content: No, we haven't.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Mm.

speaker: Phanuel
content: No idea...
[Dark alley]

speaker: Phanuel
content: What is this?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why?
(Scene change)

speaker: Crowd
content: Yay!
(Scene change)

speaker: Eugene
content: Two...

speaker: Eugene
content: One!
(Scene change)
[Exit flashback]
[Exit flashback]

speaker: Jane
content: Found you.
[Exit flashback]

speaker: Joan
content: Darn it...
[Shackles Effect]
[Bar]
...The... ...sun... ...deformed...
...Demise... ...befell...

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Apostle of Ashes is invading from the northwest of the city and is now rapidly advancing within 20 kilometers from the Broken Frontline. All combat units are to assemble to intercept the enemy. It must not enter DisSea.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Its flames contain high-intensity Mania. Beware of contamination!

FAC troops are at the forefront. Rows of anti-Mania shields collide with the flames, yet the shields of blue light shatter as the underlying equipment melts. The enemy breaks through yet another line of defense.
Like a fiery bird, the Apostle flaps its wings and Mania flames envelop everyone in scorching heat, burning your skin. Prolonged combat under high temperature nearly dehydrates everyone.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: Where are Paradeisos' reinforcements? Out having a picnic?! That monster is about to enter DisCity. No amount of Hypercubes can save us then!

speaker: Schorl
content: ...It's not time yet. There's a more cost-effective solution.

speaker: Schorl
content: For the time being, hold the frontline. Paradeisos will give you the right instructions.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: Tsk... Squad three, retreat and regroup. Squad four, take over and hold out for as long as you can!

speaker: FAC Officer
content: Where are squads five and six?! Hurry up and get moving! Quick... Mmph!
With a loud thud, the sturdy wall of soldiers is breached. The soldier in front of you is blown away by the heat wave, crashing heavily to the ground and going silent.
You step forward to help up the soldier, who's still alive. The next second, a Mania storm engulfs you. You instinctively shield him with your body.
Furious shrieks pierce your eardrums. Flames consume your sanity. Clearly, you see a twisted eye of the beast drawing closer, like a gaping maw ready to swallow everyone whole.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Back off!
Red light pierces through the flames. A sharp wail bursts out as the Mania illusion is split apart. Suddenly, you see that evil giant bird impaled by shackles, struggling fiercely. You've caught it!
But the next second, it screams and the golden runes on its body suddenly ignite, forming strange patterns. The flames trace the thorns and follow the shackles, setting your entire body on fire!

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...An unseen human sorcery?

speaker: Nightingale
content: No! The Mania is corroding the shackles! Chief, it'll hurt you, let go!

Too late. The flames are burning all over your body, using the shackles as fuel and forcing a connection between you and the Apostle. You try to retreat from the battle, but your convulsing right hand is completely out of control.

The screams and fights blur in your ears. Steam from blood and sweat distorts your vision. In the searing daze, the Apostle in front of you disappears. The adjutant and your comrades are gone, leaving only...
The sun deformed, demise befell...
Before you get a response, breathing becomes difficult. The high temperature inside you is devouring your organs. The world grows brighter, hotter.
Hills burned and charred, lives ebbed and fell.
This time, you see it as clearly as you hear it. A burning humanoid figure is drawing near.
And behind her, ten suns hang in the sky. Searing heat, blazing flames, and various mirages of Wraith Beasts are destroying an unknown city.

A force different from the Hypercubes seeps in, accompanied by weird chanting. Patterned green light spreads, suppressing the black flames and binding the fiery bird. Both the high heat and illusions are gradually subdued.
And at the end of the light patterns, on the edge of the battlefield, several unfamiliar figures appear on the burning horizon.

speaker: Schorl
content: ...Reinforcements have arrived. It's time.

speaker: Schorl
content: Gather your forces, defeat the Apostle, and protect the MBCC's Chief.
You snap your eyes open. The temperature around you drops sharply and the sweat on your back turns cold instantly. You shiver.

Before you are not the high heat and flames in the nightmare, but the familiar ceiling of the MBCC lounge. The buzzing in your ears also gradually quiets down, and you slowly make out the repeating voice in the announcement.

speaker: Announcement
content: ...The expulsion operation has so far been a success. The S-Class Apostle has been suppressed and repelled, and the threat has been temporarily resolved. The FAC will also cooperate with the Ring Research Institute to remain on full alert and continue citywide searches.

speaker: Announcement
content: The battle is not yet over. The Apostle of Ashes is still alive. It has proven its destructive power and will not stop invading. All department members should rest well for the time being and prepare to face the enemy's next attack with your full strength.
Nightingale's voice comes from the PA system, ever so reliable and calm, but also more tired than usual. She was also injured in that battle.
The medical staff in the ward are also busy. Probably due to the heavy post-battle workload, everyone is in a hurry and no one notices you're awake.

You struggle to get up but fail. The burning pain from the blazing shackles lingers. The brief moment of clarity is quickly overshadowed by a headache. You collapse back into bed, stars bursting in your vision.

At that moment, a refreshing coolness spreads from the palm of your hand, soothing the restlessness within you as it flows along your arm. You realize someone has been holding your hand the whole time, and you hear her voice.
...You've just woken up. Don't push yourself right now.
Such a familiar voice. Have you heard it before?
A foreign fragrance wafts over, and you turn your head toward the direction of the voice.
A strange woman, wearing dark green clothes, is leaning on the other side of your bed, holding your hand.
Her eyes are gentle, and she looks at you openly. When you turn to look at her, she smiles slightly.

speaker: Woman in Green
content: How reckless of you to dare touch those demonic flames with your bare hands. Now that the shackles have been ignited, this fever won't break soon.

speaker: Woman in Green
content: You're sweating buckets and your brow is all wrinkled with the frown... Did you have a nightmare? What did you dream of?

She raises her hand to wipe the sweat from your forehead. She's surrounded by rising wisps of green smoke emanating a calming energy, the exact power that's soothing the heat within your body. This is a Sinner's power.
You only answer her with a question.

options: This is a healing ability. Who are you?

speaker: Woman in Green
content: Sinner... That's a kind of criminal here in your state, right? Going to arrest me? I thought the officials of DisCity would be more courteous.

speaker: Woman in Green
content: You don't remember me, do you... You DisCity officials surely know how to break my heart.

speaker: Woman in Green
content: I went through a lot of trouble to rescue you from that demonic being. I wish to at least be remembered for the deed.
The foreign fragrance on her grows more recognizable, same as the scent you smelled in your dream just now.

speaker: Woman in Green
content: I am <color=#fb9259>Du Ruo</color>, an envoy from the Eastian Alliance, a distinguished guest invited by Paradeisos to fight the calamity, and also the person who saved your life from the claws of the Sun Crow... I mean, the Apostle of Ashes.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: How about a little "thank you" to start with?

<color=#fb9259>Eastia</color>, the eastern part of the continent across the sea. After the fall of the Perishing Star, the surviving cities of Eastia formed an alliance to strengthen themselves. Hindered by natural disasters, communication with DisCity was difficult.

In N.F. 106, a new round of global calamities struck Eastia gravely, even severing the fragile Hypercube trade. The place was silent for several years, giving rise to rumors of its sinking in DisCity.

Until <color=#fb9259>January 31, N.F. 114</color>.

The envoys from Eastia arrive in DisCity, marking the first official contact between the two continents after <color=#fb9259>eight years</color> of estrangement. It is for confronting a sudden and severe Tide of Ashes.

A new calamitous apostle, <color=#fb9259>the Sun Crow</color>, has invaded DisCity.

19:23, February 1, N.F. 114.
Eastside City Council Meeting Hall,
Tide of Ashes Special Operation Meeting.

Inside the hall, you and the representatives of DisCity's council are seated on the west side, facing guests in Outland attire on the opposite side. Dressed in a light, smoky green robe, Du Ruo stands out even among the envoys. She sits across from you on the east side of the venue.
In the center of the meeting room, the Schorl from Paradeisos is reporting yesterday's battle results.

speaker: Schorl
content: The target, codenamed <color=#fb9259>Sun Crow</color>, invaded from the northwest of WhiteSands and got closer to the DisSea than any other Apostles of Ashes did in nearly three decades. It passed through three mandatory surveillance nets without triggering any alarms, an unprecedented occurrence.

speaker: Schorl
content: The Sun Crow is powerful and particularly intelligent, capable of consciously controlling Mania radiation to create interference and evade detection. It was repelled in the first encounter, but entering the DisSea is its instinct. It will definitely assault the Broken Frontline again.

speaker: Schorl
content: We know very little about the enemy. While strengthening our defenses and conducting searches, the most important task at this stage is to gather information. To this end, DisCity accepts the support of the Eastian Alliance to locate the Sun Crow and eliminate it once and for all.

speaker: DisCity Representative
content: We haven't cooperated with Outland states for a long time, as there has been no necessity. But... given the current special circumstances, we need Eastia's experience, since they are experts in dealing with that monster.

speaker: DisCity Representative
content: Please.

A man in white from the Eastian delegation stands up and bows to you formally. His face is hidden behind a bronze mask, but the bizarre Outland patterns on it are enough to draw attention and wariness from those around him.

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: The Sun Crow brings drought and devastation, and this is just the beginning. As an envoy of Eastia, I cannot sit back knowing such evil's at play.

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: That monster has plagued Eastia for years. We've fought it for decades, gaining expertise along the way. Last year's natural disaster broke its seal, allowing it to escape. Of course, Eastia would hunt it down wherever it may flee.

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: We've traveled thousands of miles here, hoping to help you all quell this disaster.
On the other side, Schorl aptly projects images of the Sun Crow being sealed in N.F. 106. This visual evidence is what convinced Paradeisos, you suppose.

speaker: DisCity Representative
content: You defeated it seven years ago? How many Hypercubes did it take to deal with an Apostle of Ashes of this magnitude?

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: I'll be frank. After the disaster in N.F. 106 disrupted our trade, Eastia's Hypercube reserves were nearly depleted. We could only rely on our own strength to defeat the Sun Crow.
The hall erupts in murmurs. Representatives of DisCity whisper among themselves, clearly skeptical that there exist other solutions to Mania disasters besides DisCity's unique Hypercubes.

You recall those strange green symbols you saw before passing out yesterday. They are unlike any FAC force fields or Sinner abilities you've seen, but they feel familiar, as if you've seen them somewhere before.

speaker: Ring Researcher Rep
content: We've reviewed yesterday's battle records. Indeed, you used some kind of sorcery to successfully suppress the Sun Crow Apostle. The effect was significant and entirely different from modern Hypercube technology.

speaker: Ring Researcher Rep
content: We've long heard about Eastia's special sorcery for controlling Mania. May I ask if it's a kind of Mania sorcery? Where did it come from, and how was it developed...

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: It's just some sorcery passed down among Eastia's seers that permits minor restrictions on the Sun Crow's actions.

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: What truly helped us overcome the calamity and defeat the evil was an ancient myth that has been passed down in Eastia for millennia.
He bows respectfully.

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: The Perishing Star falls, calamities descend... Our ancestors had long foretold the era of great disasters and recorded the true method to subdue demons in legends.
There's another stir among the audience. This statement sounds overly absurd, leaving people both incredulous of everything they've heard and eager for further explanation.

speaker: DisCity Representative
content: ...The fall of the Perishing Star occurred just over a century ago. Did Eastia foresee the calamity before then? What method could they have suggested to resist the Apostle of Ashes thousands of years ago, back when humanity hadn't even discovered gunpowder?

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: Eastia has always been home to gifted individuals, whom we call seers. They are capable of spiritual communication and are the interpreters and scribes of myths. I'll let her take over the introduction.
You look toward Du Ruo. Noticing your gaze, she turns to smile at you, but doesn't begin to speak.
Instead, she turns to the door of the meeting hall. A childlike voice comes through, reciting words that take you by surprise.
The sun deformed, demise befell. Hills burned and charred, lives ebbed and fell...
It's the poem from your dream! You cannot forget that suffocating feeling brought by those inexplicable, ominous words. Just then, the door suddenly opens...
A shape darts past the front row. Obscured by the heads in front, you can't see it clearly. The next second, it leaps onto the podium. It's actually a child?!

It could be because of her bizarre outfit, or the captivating poem. Or perhaps the calm demeanor of the Eastian envoys convinces everyone that this is no accident. No one stops the child, and she straightens her clothes and then bows deeply in greeting.

speaker: Girl in Eastern Attire
content: I am <color=#fb9259>Yanyan</color>, the seer of Sunsink City. Seers communicate with the spirits, decipher scriptures, repel demons, and comfort the masses. What I've just recited is the <color=#fb9259>Ode to Sun</color>, a millennium-old myth from Eastia.

speaker: Yanyan
content: It details the origin of the Sun Crow calamity and the method to eradicate it. Yanyan has committed every detail to memory, specifically…

speaker: Yanyan
content: Ages past, there emerged from the sun a giant bird known as the Sun Crow. It embodied both deity and evil, wielding unrivaled fiery might.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Humans must worship it respectfully, or else, if the Sun Crow got angry, disaster would follow its flight, casting misfortune upon all in its path. In other words…

speaker: Yanyan
content:
Poison uncured, from plants impure. Dragon's frenzy, bane of the sea.
Minds invaded, by foul spirits. Ten suns in sky, lest crops survived.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Came a tough time when harvests were poor and offerings grew meager. Feeling neglected, the Sun Crow was furious and inflicted three great calamities on the populace as punishment. Eventually, ten suns rose in the sky at once, threatening to burn everything down. And then...
She spreads her arms in a gesture of praising the sun.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Brave champion sang, sunward quest began. Crimson bow taut, white fletchings shot.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Amid the people's despair, a hero came. This nameless champion snapped a branch from the sky-reaching blessed tree, took the Dragon's Vein from East Sea, wove an unburnable Wraith Spirit fletching, and ultimately crafted an Almighty Bow capable of piercing the sky from miles away.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Finally, surrounded by the people, and in front of the grand altar...
The girl steps onto the desk of the meeting hall, posing as if drawing a large bow with her hands. She sounds very passionate though she's only holding a small wooden slingshot.

speaker: Yanyan
content: The hero drew the Almighty Bow, aiming at the sky, and brought down the nine suns one by one, leaving only the Sun Crow remaining. In fear and rage, it cawed as it fled, "You short-lived mortal! I shall return when you are dead!"

speaker: Yanyan
content: The hero laughed back, "Bring it on then! Another hero will rise after me, with another Almighty Bow! The legend has begun. When you return, you'll be no deity, just a hapless bird destined to be shot down! Ha! Ha! Ha!"
The child's high-pitched howl echoes in the silent hall. The girl strikes a final pose, then stands straight to signal the end of the grand play, and gives another deep bow.

speaker: Yanyan
content: That was a quick summary of the Ode to Sun. Now that we know how to fight the Sun Crow, time to get moving!
The current atmosphere doesn't allow for jokes. The idea of using ancient mythology to combat Mania is unbelievable enough, and this girl's animated performance only adds to the shock.

speaker: Councilor A
content: What does this have to do with eliminating the Apostle of Ashes? And why is a child allowed in such an important meeting?

speaker: Yanyan
content: Hey, isn't it clearly stated in the myth? Go snap off a branch from the blessed tree, take the Dragon's Vein from the East Sea, weave a Wraith Spirit fletching, and finally craft an Almighty Bow powerful enough to shoot down the Sun Crow from thousands of miles away!

speaker: Councilor B
content: Stop talking nonsense. What East Sea, Dragon's Vein, blessed tree... Such things don't exist in DisCity.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Myths are profound metaphors. They are puzzles given to us by the gods. It's okay if ordinary people don't understand. Leave the interpretation to those who have a gift for spiritual communication. That's exactly the job of seers in every generation. That's what I do!

speaker: Yanyan
content: Yanyan is the current seer for Sunsink City, and I will lead everyone to seek the oracles and follow the myth's instructions to craft the Almighty Bow for the Sun Shot. Once the Almighty Bow is made and the Sun Crow is shot down, everything will come to a perfect conclusion!
She pats her chest confidently, but no one would trust a child's promise. The hall is filled with rising doubts.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: This is a waste of time. I'm heading back to the front line.
Amid the chaos, someone left his seat. It's the FAC operation commander for this Apostle of Ashes campaign.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: The Apostle's destination is DisSea. When it got into the 20-kilometer range last time, the resulting Mania resonance already spread to three Black Ring ruins.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: I set aside all my tasks to come to this meeting to find a way to combat the Apostle of Ashes, not to listen to some Outland brat's nonsensical babble. Is this what the frontline soldiers sacrificed their lives for?

speaker: Yanyan
content: Hold on! Yanyan is serious. I've been working hard on my seer training, and I've already mastered the art. Look!
She spreads her palm and musters enough strength to create a small spark in her hand. It leaps up and twists into a strange rune before it disappears.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: She's a Sinner?!
That's a sorcery, and it's very similar to the Mania flames of the Sun Crow Apostle. You've seen similar symbols on that giant bird.

Before a bigger clamor breaks out, a figure of green and white steps onto the podium, taking Yanyan's hand. The flames are extinguished instantly. Du Ruo shields Yanyan behind her placidly, facing everyone in the audience.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Well, even two neighboring towns in Eastia can have vastly different customs, let alone DisCity which is worlds away. We must communicate in a common language.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I am the scholar of the delegation. My area of expertise is Eastian mythology, and I have also studied some of DisCity's scientific theories. I am aware that the ways we perceive the world differ greatly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Let me be the "interpreter" here.

Du Ruo raises her hand. You're surprised to see the incense burner she held now float in mid-air, emitting faint green smoke that swirls around her palm. She's openly displaying her abilities as a Sinner in front of everyone.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: In Eastia, there are a small number of highly intuitive and talented individuals who can comprehend the unknown and gain the psychic power to become <color=#fb9259>seers</color>.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Here in DisCity, they might be called Sinners and are to be captured and strictly monitored by a certain Chief. But in Eastia, seers are greatly respected, especially as a key force against natural disasters when Hypercubes are scarce.
Du Ruo gives you a smile, but a skeptical voice appears from the audience.

speaker: DisCity Representative
content: We also have experts on Sinners here. Of course we know the potential power of this child and your seers.
He implies something more. Both seers have used their powers, and an analysis of their abilities has already been quickly generated and distributed to every DisCity attendee.
Based on their M-values, one is A-Class, and although the other is S-Class, she has a Catalyst Tendency. They couldn't possibly have the power to confront the Apostle of Ashes.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Do you really? As early as last August, Yanyan foresaw the Sun Crow's arrival at DisCity. That's why we've crossed the sea to be here. Had we come just a little later...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The Sun Crow would likely have broken through your defenses yesterday...
An undeniable fact. The hall falls back into silence.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Our myths have been passed down for millennia. It's true that some of the ambiguous descriptions must have led to far-fetched interpretations. But there are indeed claims that have been verified.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: When the Sun Crow loses control, disasters follow wherever it goes. <color=#fb9259>Poison uncured from plants impure</color>, <color=#fb9259>bane of the sea</color>, and <color=#fb9259>minds invaded by foul spirits</color> correspond to the three strange phenomena. As the officer just mentioned, the three Black Ring ruins are already showing signs.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: After the Three Calamities, the Sun Crow will strengthen quickly and eventually burn down the entire city. Time is running out, and if we waste more of it on suspecting each other...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Do you wish to witness <color=#fb9259>the ten suns hanging in the sky</color>? And experience the apocalyptic disaster that destroyed our homeland and wreaked havoc across all of Eastia?

speaker: DisCity Representative
content: Are you threatening us?

speaker: FAC Officer
content: ...Please continue. This kind of practical intelligence is what we need. Please lend us your strength to stop the disaster.
The FAC officer returns to his seat, watching Du Ruo intently. She responds with a smile and a bow, and she resumes her calm and gentle demeanor.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Thank you, officer, but I'm only a non-combat mythologist in our delegation. The main force against the Sun Crow will be the sealers and the seer, who will guide us through the myth. They are the ones who need DisCity's special assistance.
Her gaze moves past the crowd to the silent Schorl in the corner.

speaker: Schorl
content: Certainly. The Sun Crow has a unique invisibility. Its approach to the DisSea this time already caused no small disturbance within the city, and it will surely follow the Apostle of Ashes' instinct to return to the DisSea. We must not let our guard down.

speaker: Schorl
content: In the past year, the city faced many changes that led to huge consumption of resources. The production of Hypercubes has not returned to normal either. The previous high-cost defense methods are no longer suitable for this operation. We need a safer and more efficient plan, hence cooperation with Eastia is necessary.

speaker: Schorl
content: From today on, please have the delegation's sealers assist the FAC in fortifying the defenses and locating the Sun Crow. All operations concerning the bow-making or the myth required by the envoys will be fully supported by the MBCC.
Du Ruo turns back to give you a meaningful look.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Of course, I'm relieved to know that Chief will be there. Are you taking us to your residence... Excuse me, um, the Bureau?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: We'll have a lot of important matters to discuss for the upcoming operations.

You look at Du Ruo, but your gaze inadvertently flits to the 9th Agency operative standing silently against the east wall, behind everyone. He's watching the envoys, and upon noticing your gaze, he tips his hat slightly in acknowledgment.
You don't need his reminder to remember the "real instructions" received before the meeting.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're not sending me just to help them, are you? You and your boss don't believe in that myth or the so-called envoys. What is my real task?

speaker: 9th
content: We indeed need their help, but we must also be vigilant of their ulterior motives.

speaker: 9th
content: After all, it's been eight years since we last saw our friends from the Outlands. Those myths and sorceries are beyond logic. If there really is an ulterior motive behind them, especially during this Apostle crisis... It'd be too dangerous.

speaker: 9th
content: So, while assisting them, please also keep an eye out, Chief. I will stay in touch with you.

options: Looks like I can't say no

content: After receiving a positive response, she gives you that evaluating look again with her amiable eyes.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Well, I look forward to our cooperation, Chief...

It's been almost a year, and we've finally caught up with it. The Sun Crow has grown much stronger than before. Here, it's known as the Apostle of Ashes, and the disasters it brings are called the Tide of Ashes. There are probably many of its kind here. But unlike in Eastia before, this time the Sun Crow has a very clear purpose... It wants to enter the DisSea, or rather, BR-000.

I can only get so much information here. But from the first encounter, it's clear that the Apostle of Ashes resonates significantly with the Black Rings. The Apostle's power was noticeably strengthened as it approached the DisSea, and its proximity also caused an obvious resonance in the DisSea and the Black Rings of DisCity. What will happen if it enters the DisSea? DisCity is very wary of this. They've prepared many counter-strategies, and they view the crisis in an entirely different way. Although information is limited... a chance must lie somewhere.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this what you meant by... "collaborative effort"?
The Bureau's VIP lounge has been decorated in an Eastern style, with wisps of smoke curling through the air.
Du Ruo leans back on the soft couch, looking as comfortable as if she were at home, flipping through a report in her hands.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Your subordinates are diligent. I merely mentioned that Chief agreed to provide me with a comfortably furnished room, and look how nicely they've spruced up the place.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The directive from above is for the MBCC to seek a method to eliminate the Sun Crow at your guidance. You said we'd have many things to discuss. Such as?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Eastia has practical experience in dealing with the Sun Crow but lacks theoretical conclusions. The research here is the perfect supplement for reference. I'm trying to cram down as much knowledge as I can.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: As for discovering unusual phenomena and crafting the Almighty Bow, Yanyan is more reliable than I am. She will show you the way.
She glances at your displeased expression and laughs. She covers her mouth with her hand and coughs softly, in spite of her complexion all rosy and healthy.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Excuse me. I have been buried in books for years and neglected my physical health. It's already a stretch for me to have traveled here, not to mention the adjustment to the new environment and exposure to the sun...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I'd only be a burden if I insisted on going with you... So, with a heavy heart, I'm entrusting the exciting task of crafting the Almighty Bow to you and Yanyan.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: If you encounter any interesting incidents or rumors along the way, do share them with me so I can study them further. Let me contribute to the great cause of bow-making in my own way. Best of luck, see you!
Then she lies back down, switching to a more comfortable position.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Oh, want to hang out a bit more? Then why not tell me about your nightmare? I can give you an analysis now. Maybe I'll discover something new.
She suggests with a teasing smile. But for the first time, the scholar closes the book in her hands and looks you straight in the eyes...
Those eyes are much more honest than their owner, glinting with a solid desire. Since the first meeting, she's seemed very interested in your dreams.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll tell you what I dreamed about, and you'll tell me the truth about those sun-shooting myths.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The "cultural differences between the two cities" are a vague excuse, I don't buy it. I'll feel like you're hiding something if you don't spell everything out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You wouldn't want any rifts in this cooperation, right, Miss Ambassador?
Du Ruo narrows her eyes as she looks you up and down, then begins slowly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: It's normal to have reservations. I'm not bothered by your suspicions toward me, Chief. If one day you find that you can truly trust me, I will tell you all my stories.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: But with the disaster looming now, try not to overcomplicate things.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then let's talk about that dream when you tire of these mind games.
You hold each other's gaze and simply wait for the other person to answer first. Suddenly, the door opens and a girl stumbles in.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Du Ruo, Du Ruo! Yanyan had another psychic dream! I dreamed there were ten suns in the sky and plenty of demons and monsters in the fire! One of them was a giant bird with human eyes and wearing a mask. It held my head in its beak and tried to eat me!

speaker: Yanyan
content: That must be the Sun Crow! But in the dream, a hero came and shot it down with an arrow! Du Ruo, you're the best at interpreting dreams. Can you tell if this is a good omen?
Yanyan gestures around the lounge dramatically. Though her description is all over the place, you realize... her dream is exactly the same as yours?
The dream interpreter simply props her chin on her hands languidly, observing your reaction.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Oh, did you have the same dream, Chief? Yanyan is the chosen seer who receives oracles through her psychic dreams. How do you explain your dream then?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Oh my, you two aren't long-lost siblings, are you?
female_content: Oh my, you two aren't long-lost sisters, are you?

speaker: Yanyan
content: Did you also dream of the same big bird, Chief? Cool! It must be a good omen then, because we're setting off to craft the Almighty Bow together today!
Yanyan has already jumped up to grab your arm. Her palms are abnormally hot, reminding you of the fiery bird in your dream. You pat the girl's head and turn to Du Ruo.

options: Do you have anything else to tell me?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: A scholar is neither omniscient nor omnipotent. I'm always on the path of seeking the truth... Let's talk again when you return. You and Yanyan will get along well.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: After all, you had the same dream. Maybe it really is a good omen.

Her expression has already changed and she's stashed away her curiosity about you. Du Ruo picks up the documents and lies sideways on the couch, seeming concentrated on her reading and reluctant to be disturbed.

Black Rings, Corruptors, the DisSea... Even DisCity doesn't have a definitive explanation for everything. They hypothesize that the Apostles of Ashes originate from the highly concentrated collective human subconsciousness. They are projections from the psychic dimension into the material world. This aligns with the notion of "divine and demonic entities". As the collective subconscious is erratic and unstable, so are the manifestations of the Apostles of Ashes. It can be inferred that during the era of disasters, the Apostles that are most likely to survive this unusual selection process are those that induce the most fear, despair, and negative impressions.

According to seers' psychic records, besides attacking humans, calamitous demons, aka Apostles of Ashes, also engage in mutual predation. It now seems this is not for power but to eliminate competitors and ensure their own survival. Their desire to enter the DisSea may possibly stem from the same reason. The Ring Research Institute considers this an instinct of the Apostles and uses this affinity for the DisSea as a criterion to distinguish this "species" from ordinary Corruptors. Moreover, this tendency is specific to BR-000 and not other Black Rings. Near DisCity, this instinct even overrides all their other characteristics.
Having collected plenty of interesting information, you organize the facts and decide to bring them back to Du Ruo in the Bureau first. You also need some rest to recover your strength.

Ever since the shackles came into contact with the Sun Crow, your body has never fully recovered and you've been having this persistent low-grade fever. The exertion of the past half-day has worn you out, and once you get back, you soon fall asleep in your office.

In the dream, something is scorching your skin. Whispers of Mania and roars of a beast drill into your ears. Some chaotic, lacerated consciousness is forcefully tearing through, trying to invade your mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mmph!

Flames lash out at you, and the sharp golden eye of a fierce bird captures all your attention. Sparks spatter onto your body, causing unbearable pain, but fear swallows you whole before you can react.

Is this a dream? You don't have time to think as you struggle to cower away instinctively. But the monster screeches and lunges forward, pinning you to the ground with its sword and claws beside your ears. Trapped, you are forced to look at its true form.

That is not a beast. It has the shape of a human, a woman bathing in fire whose body is covered in red feathers. She sits atop you like a hunter on its prey, leaning down close to your face, the intense heat of the fire suffocating you as she draws nearer.
She opens her mouth near your neck, and her whispers mixed with the crackling of burning debris numb the back of your ears.

You try to struggle, but unable to release the shackles in the dream, you remain imprisoned in the cage of flames. The charring smell surrounds you as the world gets incinerated, as if this isn't a dream, but a true purgatory.
And death is beckoning to you.

The flames recede and her face leans even closer. Half of it is covered by an ominous cluster of contamination, like she's wearing a bent mask. The other half is indistinct against the backlight, leaving only that golden eye visible, clear and sharp.
That's not a human eye, but it's not menacing as a demonic beast's either. It's simply staring at you, like... a golden sun.

As you think that, the lapping flames gradually lose their heat, no longer causing the burning pain, but acting like a barrier protecting you in this inferno. The raging Mania outside is entirely consumed by the flames enveloping her body.
She locks eyes with you without any other movement, only repeating the chaotic whispers over and over again. That inhuman pupil seems eager to convey a thousand emotions to you.
But you can't comprehend them. The distance between you is not just a matter of inches, but an insurmountable difference.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Who... are you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What are you trying to tell me?
Chief... Chief...
Chief is awake!
A small hand is slapping your cheek, and you wake up to see Yanyan's face instead of the monster's. She looks at you with concern.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Your cheeks are all red, and you're panting... Are you having a fever? You're scaring me.
Maybe it's because you slapped them so hard? You only remark inwardly, then raise your hands to move the girl aside.

options: I'm fine, it was just a dream.

speaker: Yanyan
content: You had a dream again...?

speaker: Yanyan
content: Did you dream of a woman wearing a mask and extraordinary clothes, with flames all over her body... She leaned very close to look at you, embrace you, and try to talk to you?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Oh, did you have the same dream, Chief? Yanyan is the chosen seer who receives oracles through her psychic dreams. How do you explain your dream then?
You're still pondering when the girl claps her hands joyfully and jumps up.

speaker: Yanyan
content: You had the same wonderful dream as Yanyan did! You also dreamed of <color=#fb9259>the Great Seer</color>!

speaker: Yanyan
content: Yes! In Sunsink City... Oh, back then it was still called Sunset Town. The Great Seer was the most powerful person in Sunset Town. We were only able to repel all evil spirits and overcome natural disasters thanks to her leadership!

speaker: Yanyan
content: She always wore a mask and her pretty seer robes. She would stand on the high altar accompanied by her long sword and flames, performing the ritual dance to drive away evil spirits and pray for blessings. What a beautiful sight!

speaker: Yanyan
content: Actually, I dreamed of her just now when I was dozing off in the car too. Hehe, maybe because tackling the Sun Crow is too hard, the Great Seer even came specially to comfort me... It's been a long time since I had such a beautiful dream...
Mask... Long sword... Flames... Woman... You indeed dreamed of the same things again.
But can you call that hellish scene a beautiful dream? That being, burned to the point it no longer looked human... You could hardly see it as a beautiful and gentle woman.

options: What did the Great Seer say to you?

speaker: Yanyan
content: Hmm... She told Yanyan to go to some sea... and she told me I could do it. Although I didn't hear the rest clearly, but... she must be encouraging me.

options: What she told me was different.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Huh? Well... Du Ruo is better at interpreting dreams! Let's go find her!
She takes your hand and runs outside. You consider for a second and don't stop her.
Never mind that strange dream. At Du Ruo's request, you've specifically brought back a lot of information for her. You wonder if the scholar has figured anything out yet.

speaker: Staff A
content: Watching the High Tower Black Ring collapse from the helicopter... Man, how do I put it... I couldn't imagine the person who did such a big thing was our Chief. I mean, our skinny Chief with those heavy dark circles from all the overtime, who we see every day!

speaker: Staff B
content: Who'd have thought? When the second Black Ring erupted, they said Chief was dead. I thought I'd never see him again!
female_content: Who'd have thought? When the second Black Ring erupted, they said Chief was dead. I thought I'd never see her again!

speaker: Staff B
content: Eek! Chief!
You walk over to find a few loudmouths from the Bureau chattering to Du Ruo, and they scurry off the second they see you. The scholar nods at you with a smile, her expression full of amusement.
You steady your emotions and smile at Yanyan.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll ask her about the dream. Go play somewhere else, Yanyan. But don't listen to those stories. Read the actual reports.

options: I'm braver in real life than in the stories.
Don't get your hopes up. I'm not that bright.

content: Getting your permission, the girl bounces about joyfully. She's already forgotten about the dream and is now captivated by those tales of Chief's Great Adventures spun by those two.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Then I'll be off! Tell me how my dream differs from yours later. I really want to know too!
She runs off gleefully, leaving you and Du Ruo alone.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Bummer, my field research was just getting interesting. "Skinny Chief Strikes Back and Mad Shackles vs. Mania." How fascinating!

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Never mind, you're my priority. Finally willing to let me interpret your dream?

options: I'm not here to talk about the dream.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We agreed to talk about that only when we can finally face each other honestly. But the things you've done...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Refusing to go out using different excuses. Being vague about everything. Sending me away to "gather information" and then snooping around in the Bureau. You're making it hard to trust you, you know.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Are you upset because I neglected your investigation results, or are you indeed here to interrogate the Outlander?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need an explanation. I can't work with someone suspicious.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: To think that one would doubt the truthfulness of a scholar's words... Not gonna let this slide if I say nothing, are you?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Sigh... Alright, alright.
She actually straightens up and looks at you earnestly, the humor in her tone all gone.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: My homeland is not like DisCity. Eastia is ever the victim of disasters, and our people struggle to survive. My studies in mythology, frequent overseas journeys, and information gathering in DisCity are all to grasp these unpredictable disasters. For example...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: In N.F. 112, Eastia faced a massive Tide of Ashes. Several cities were destroyed and vast lands sank beneath the sea. That would later be known in DisCity as the Sinking of Eastia.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: In N.F. 113, just when we barely suppressed the Sun Crow Apostle, it suddenly broke free from its seal, catching us off guard and severely damaging the newly revived Sunsink City.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: These are the two most recent disasters which even our seers did not foresee. Yet, in DisCity, I found some interesting clues.
She looks at you, the warmth in her eyes cooling slightly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: In August N.F. 112, on the brink of the sinking of Eastia, a certain Chief awoke from a slumber. In March N.F. 113, after he was attacked and fell into a coma, the Sun Crow broke its seal and went berserk thousands of miles away. I'm sure you're smart enough to connect the dots...
female_content: In August N.F. 112, on the brink of the sinking of Eastia, a certain Chief awoke from a slumber. In March N.F. 113, after she was attacked and fell into a coma, the Sun Crow broke its seal and went berserk thousands of miles away. I'm sure you're smart enough to connect the dots...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: It's just a speculation. I have no solid proof.
She smiles and steps closer smoothly to whisper in your ear. Is it your imagination, or is there indeed a hint of hostility in her voice?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Your people are the center of the world and the center of Mania. Your every unconscious action might trigger a disaster that affects everyone, and yet you've been reluctant to see it.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Think about what you've done and who is really the one to be doubted and hated?
With that, you find the two of you locking eyes, standing merely a foot apart. Without waiting for your answer, Du Ruo's smile fades as she looks away and stands up to go, leaving you there alone.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Chief? Hehe, you're still here. Tell me the result of the dream interpretation. I'm dying to know the good news!
You're still collecting yourself.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Yeah! I saw Du Ruo come out just now covering her mouth and giggling all the way. It's rare to see her so happy. There must be some good news, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Giggling?

Dammit! You finally realize Du Ruo has dodged your question. You hurry out to the corridor, but the suspect is long gone. Those nonsensical words were just a bluff to scare you. That trickster played you again!
Frustrated, you make to chase after her, but Yanyan grabs your sleeve again.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Wait, wait! Du Ruo asked me to tell you something.
Another arrangement made by that woman. You quiver and swallow hard. Who knows what she is planning to play on you this time?

options: ...What does she want you to tell me?

content: Seemingly oblivious to your wary and puzzled look, Yanyan breaks into a big smile and hugs you tightly.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Thank you for always being with me, believing in me, and showing me all the fun things. ${PlayerName}, no matter where you're from, Yanyan adores you, even if you believe in those strange blue and red crystals!

speaker: Yanyan
content: Let's go! The mission isn't over yet. I have to work hard. I'll definitely defeat the Sun Crow. I'll protect Chief and DisCity, your homeland!
The straightforward declaration of affection following Du Ruo's roundabout threatening bluff throws your thoughts into complete disarray. Tongue-tied, you come up with only one conclusion...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These two Outlanders are both intimidating in their own ways. Can't let my guard down with them, not even a little!
Remembering ${PlayerName}'s shocked expression at her threat, Du Ruo chuckles lightly and strolls through the Bureau's long corridor.

His great deeds and miraculous shackles aside, that one is indeed beloved by those around him. He's also truly naive and kind, and almost too honest. Even that kind of lie could make him pale with shock.
female_content: Her great deeds and miraculous shackles aside, that one is indeed beloved by those around her. She's also truly naive and kind, and almost too honest. Even that kind of lie could make her pale with shock.

content: Outside the scholar's room, an agent from the 9th Agency leans against the wall. Seeing Du Ruo, he removes his hat in greeting. Du Ruo smiles and returns the gesture before entering the room alone.
Her smile fades as she flips through the documents ${PlayerName} brought back, recalling what Yanyan just said.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Then I'll be off! Tell me how my dream differs from yours later. I really want to know too!

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Two different psychic dreams...

The characteristics of Eastian seers can be deduced from comparison with the research on Sinners. Black Rings have only appeared within DisCity, and the "Mania contamination" they produce is unique. Sinners born from them are thus more diverse and strange, their minds unstable. Such severe contamination does not exist in Eastia. Seers are born when their innate psychic gift awakens, likely induced by Mania disasters. The awoken ones are also more likely to resonate with the "deities" that awakened them and possess similar Mania properties. This is known as "channeling".
Those two cuties brought back a lot of interesting information. I'll be waiting for the Ring Research Institute's analysis report...

06:23, February 3, N.F. 114.
Keylan Square Black Ring Ruins,
FAC Monitoring Station Break Room.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: Has the Sun Crow Apostle not shown up yet? When will this operation finally end...

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: All this superstitious stuff Chief and that little trickster are fussing over, do you buy it?

speaker: FAC Soldier B
content: Well, actually, I don't dislike her. I used to think Easterners were pretty strange, always looking like they were up to something. But it seems like that girl is really trying hard to help.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: Whoa, so their trick actually works on you? Maybe that's why they sent that girl, so we'd lower our guard. I say we can't trust the Outlanders before they explain the purpose of their sorcery.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: Okay, I'll admit I don't hate her either... Even Chief is nice to her, isn't he? That's the clever hero who beat the Black Ring we're talking about. He can't be wrong.
female_content: Okay, I'll admit I don't hate her either... Even Chief is nice to her, isn't she? That's the clever hero who beat the Black Ring we're talking about. She can't be wrong.

speaker: FAC Soldier B
content: Those two are exhausted from their work today. Let them sleep for a bit. We've got it covered here.
BR-004 Ruins Outpost Break Room.
Before the fever breaks, you're having a strange dream again.
<color=#dg1f1f>Danger...</color>
It's that voice again.
An ominous heat gradually envelops your body. You recoil instinctively, but she grabs you firmly.
<color=#dg1f1f>Wake up...</color>
<color=#dg1f1f>...The Sun Crow is coming!</color>
You gradually begin to understand the words spoken by that blurry hoarse voice. Or perhaps, you're starting to grasp the genuine emotions in the anxious cries.

options: Who are you? The Sun Crow? Or...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What exactly do you mean by danger?
<size=45><color=#dg1f1f>That child... Danger... Save her!</color></size>
A blast of blazing flames hits you, knocking you out of consciousness.
Snapping your eyes open, you don't see Yanyan. However, the air around you is abnormally dry and hot. It's Mania.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is bad...
You burst out of the break room. Yanyan hasn't gone far, but... something seems wrong with her.

speaker: Yanyan
content: I don't know, I'm so scared... I've been trying so hard...

speaker: Yanyan
content: If it fails, it's all Yanyan's fault... I don't know what to do...
The girl mumbles to herself, walking forward obliviously in the open space scorching like the inside of an oven.
Hearing your call, Yanyan, now a few meters away, does not turn back and even keeps going further.
You try to go up to her, but the closer you get, the more uneasy you feel. The grass where Yanyan passes dries up and catches fire, the air twisting with steam.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yanyan, can you hear me?
She trembles, clearly hearing something, but doesn't turn to look at you. Mania is spilling out of her, and the girl casts her gaze into nothingness.

speaker: Yanyan
content: ...Great Seer, is that you? Have you finally come to find me?

Yanyan fumbles forward, as blinding golden light continuously strips away her consciousness, taking over her body. She is channeling now, but the Mania entwined around her comes from something you're more familiar with... It's the Sun Crow!

options: Wake up! The Great Seer isn't here!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whatever it is that's luring you, you must not fall for its trap!
You reach out to touch Yanyan, but immediately recoil at the shocking heat of her body. Indeed, it's as hot as the Apostle in your memory.
Already worn out by the bow-making preparation, Yanyan grows paler, but she's still conversing with the voice in her spiritual world.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Great Seer, I've missed you, and I've got so many questions for you. I... there's too much I still need to do, but I don't know how.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yanyan, stop!
She can't hear your voice anymore.

speaker: Yanyan
content: I only need to offer my power to the Sun Crow? I see... I'm coming, I'll listen to you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't go! It's a trap!

speaker: Yanyan
content: The Great Seer is always right...

The mark signaling the channeling begins to flicker, and Yanyan's strength is being rapidly drained. But hindered by the melting heat, you cannot get closer. The voice in your dream warns you once again.
<color=#dg1f1f>Stop it! Danger!</color>
The wake-up call seems to push you forward, helping you tear through the barrier of heat and grab hold of Yanyan.
The backlash of the shackles is incessant, and you are drenched in cold sweat. Releasing the shackles, your right arm is covered in bulging veins, trembling uncontrollably.
On the other end of the shackles, the red glow of contamination on Yanyan's body finally starts to flicker unsteadily.
The monster possessing Yanyan is declaring its ownership, but you refuse to let go.
Your vision starts to blur, possibly due to the heat of the steam or your fading consciousness. You can only force yourself to stay awake with the pain in your palm.
But you cannot last long. Eventually, you black out...
We've found Chief and that girl!
In your coma, you hear the sound of armor approaching. Apparently, the Hypercube shields are right beside you, protecting you.
As you ask, you see Yanyan lying in the arms of another person in white armor, smacking her lips.

speaker: FAC Soldier B
content: The envoy is fine. Thankfully, you intervened in time. But you're not in the best shape. Please take care of yourself first, Chief.
Right. You just used the shackles, and they caught fire again after touching the Wraith Spirit possessing Yanyan, just like when you first drove away the Sun Crow.
So that thing really was the Sun Crow Apostle. Did it invade Yanyan's mind by taking advantage of her psychical nature?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm fine. I feel much better now. Take Yanyan back first, she...
Look at the state you're in before you worry about Yanyan.
A cold hand presses against your forehead, and everything calms down again. It's that familiar scent of incense. As you tilt your head up, you finally see who is holding you.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Yes, it's me again.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Stop being so harsh toward yourself. It makes my heart ache to see a saint like you suffer.
Her composed smile somehow calms you down a lot, and you're surprised that Du Ruo, who's usually reluctant to go out, came promptly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The materials for the Almighty Bow are all safe. Relax and just rest. You both have worked hard.
Du Ruo waves the incense burner in her hand, covering the small camp with green smoke, healing the injuries of you, the soldiers, and Yanyan.

22:30, February 3, N.F. 114.
Minos Bureau of Crisis Control.

Cradling the bow, Yanyan curls up in a corner of the room. She wraps the carving knife with her special ability, engraving the bow body bit by bit while filling the patterns with small flames. Apparently, this is how the sorcery works.
Since having gathered all the materials for the Almighty Bow, she has maintained this posture without ever getting up.

speaker: Yanyan
content: It's okay. It will work... Everything's gonna be fine.
Eyes shadowed by heavy dark circles, she mumbles to herself as her hands continue the bow-crafting process mechanically.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're pushing yourself too hard, you'll be exhausted before the sun shot. The FAC hasn't localized the Sun Crow yet, we still have time.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Only a little bit more to go. It's almost done. There will be no problems... I can't, make mistakes again...
Not noticing your approach, she keeps working without looking up, her hands moving faster and faster. Finally...

speaker: Yanyan
content: Ah!
In her haste, the carving knife cuts Yanyan's finger, and blood drops onto the bow. She quickly pulls up her sleeve to wipe it.
She keeps wiping and wiping, as if the stained spot could never be cleaned.
You take the bow wordlessly and make a show of wiping it a few times before setting it aside. Then, you grab Yanyan's hand to check the wound.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Oh, look how clumsy I am... I've only got one final step left but I can't even do the engraving properly. How can I be a great seer like this...
She tries to shrug it off, but her shoulders remain drooped and she bows her head low to avoid your gaze. You both plunge into a brief silence.
Finally, she speaks first.

speaker: Yanyan
content: You know, Chief, I'm actually very afraid of natural disasters. When I was a child, the great drought brought by the Sun Crow dried up the fields, and its little monsters hurt people everywhere... I still remember how Grandma's house was set ablaze. It was terrifying...

speaker: Yanyan
content: But back then, there was a very powerful seer in Sunset Town. The Great Seer was a wonderful person. She could always predict when disasters would come. She was always fighting against natural disasters and protecting us, warding off evil spirits.

speaker: Yanyan
content: When Grandma and I were struggling to survive, she led us to our new shelter with her divination and performed a ritual dance to bless us. She told Grandma and I and everyone that we would all see the most beautiful sunset.

speaker: Yanyan
content: The Great Seer kept her promise. She was so powerful and reassuring, always inspiring everyone with her smile. Everyone trusted her fully. In the end, she led us to shoot down the Sun Crow.

speaker: Yanyan
content: I too wish to stop disasters like the Great Seer. I want to tell Grandma, my fellow townspeople victimized by disasters, and everyone who is scared like me, that everything will be alright, because the seer is here.
The Fusang Branch, the String of East Sea, and the Mystic Fletching. Yanyan looks at these symbols laden with great wishes and bows her head lower and lower.

speaker: Yanyan
content: ...But Yanyan can't do it as well.

speaker: Yanyan
content: My channeling skills aren't strong enough. I often misinterpret the Wraith Spirits. I haven't read enough scriptures. I don't know the oracles by heart. I even made a fool of myself.

speaker: Yanyan
content: I know the people of DisCity don't believe in Yanyan. Those myths sounded so captivating in the Great Seer's words, but they become foolish coming from me... I've been nothing but trouble on our journey to gather materials.

speaker: Yanyan
content: The Great Seer is no longer with us. She left the human realm which she painstakingly guarded in my care. What if I can't protect it... What if the disasters return, what then...
She hugs the unfinished bow and arrow dejectedly, too guilty to meet your eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've done very well already. You deciphered the myth and gathered all the materials for the Almighty Bow in just a few days. It's proof that you're more than capable. We all support you.

speaker: Yanyan
